title: [homeassistant] fix(tools): support response-returning services (?return_response)
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant/pull/7 by @jcrabapple. The `hermes-homeassistant` repo moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit applied under `homeassistant/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## What this fixes

`ha_call_service` can't call Home Assistant services that return data, such as `weather.get_forecasts` and `calendar.get_events`. Home Assistant rejects a plain POST to those services:

```
HTTP 400 {"message": "Service call requires responses but caller did not ask for responses. Add ?return_response to query parameters."}
```

Ordinary services reject `?return_response` in the other direction ("Service does not support responses"), so the flag can't simply be sent on every call.

## Change

- `_api_json` gains `return_response` (POST only, default off). The call goes out plain, and it's retried once with `?return_response` only when HA's 400 body asks for it. Ordinary services still send exactly one plain request.
- `_parse_service_response` handles both HA reply shapes: a bare list of changed states (plain call) and `{"changed_states": [...], "service_response": {...}}` (`?return_response`). It returns the service data under a new `response` key. `affected_entities` keeps its current shape.
- `_async_call_service` enables `return_response`.

This restores behavior that existed as a local patch on the old in-core `tools/homeassistant_tool.py`. That patch was lost when Home Assistant moved into this plugin.

## Tests

- `tests/test_return_response.py` runs a local aiohttp server that reproduces HA's behavior for both service kinds. Without the fix, 2 of 3 tests fail (the forecast retry and the dict-shape parse). The ordinary-service test passes both ways, as it should.
- Full suite: 66 passed, 2 skipped (`PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent checkout> python -m pytest`).
- Verified live against Home Assistant 2026.10: `weather.get_forecasts` on `weather.home` returns a 7-day forecast, and `homeassistant.check_config` sends one plain request with no `response` key.

title: [homeassistant] feat: operator entity allow/deny lists, optional cap, targeted list queries, registry-backed area filter
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant/pull/3 by @sanastasiou. The `hermes-homeassistant` repo moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit applied under `homeassistant/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

Moved here from NousResearch/hermes-agent#119189, as suggested when it was closed: Home Assistant left core in NousResearch/hermes-agent#132469 and the code that PR changed now lives in this plugin.

## What it adds

- **Operator entity filters** (all opt-in; unset keeps today's behaviour):
  - `HASS_ENTITY_DENYLIST`: comma-separated entity_id prefixes or globs that `ha_list_entities` always excludes. A final veto (wins over the allowlist): `ha_get_state` refuses to read a matching entity and `ha_call_service` refuses to control it, both before any network call.
  - `HASS_ENTITY_ALLOWLIST`: same format; when set, listing, reading and control are restricted to matching entities.
  - `HASS_MAX_ENTITIES`: optional cap on `ha_list_entities` results. Unset means no cap; a per-call `max` overrides it. A result cut by a cap is marked `truncated` with a note on how to narrow the query.
- **Targeted queries** on `ha_list_entities`: `name` (substring of friendly names / entity IDs), `entity_ids` (exact list, supersedes the other filters) and `max`.
- **Registry-backed `area` filter**: areas are resolved through the area/device registries over WebSocket, so entities match even when their names do not mention the room. The registry pull runs under one bounded deadline, empty results are cached, and an auth failure is logged as a warning; if the registry is unreachable it falls back to friendly-name matching. Entities carry `area`/`device` when known.

Patterns match exact IDs, family prefixes (`.` and `_` interchangeable at the boundary) and shell-style globs.

## The lists also block control (added on top, commit e8c3081)

Per maintainer ruling, the allow/deny lists are not just a discovery filter: when either is set, `ha_call_service` refuses before anything is sent:

- **Named entities are checked.** `entity_id`, and in `data` the keys `entity_id`, `target.entity_id`, `*_entity_id(s)`, `entities`, `snapshot_entities`. One denied entity, or (allowlist set) one entity outside it, refuses the whole call. The error names the entity and the pattern that blocked it.
- **Targets the lists can't check are refused.** `area_id` / `device_id` / `floor_id` / `label_id` targets and `entity_id: all` resolve on the Home Assistant server; the model is told to target explicit entity IDs (`ha_list_entities` with `area` finds them).
- **No target is refused**, since an entity service with no target can act on the whole domain (`light.turn_off` turns off every light). Exceptions: `notify.*` / `persistent_notification.*` act on no entity and pass; `script.<name>` is checked as the entity `script.<name>`. Scenes, scripts and automations are entities, so `scene.turn_on` / `automation.trigger` are filtered by their `entity_id`.
- **No lists set: unchanged.**

README (env table, filter section with the exact rule, Security section), `plugin.yaml` and the tool description say so; the restricted Home Assistant user/token advice stays as defense in depth.

Tests: `TestCallServiceOperatorFilters` (deny blocks explicit/list/`target` control; allowlist refuses outside, no-target, area/device/floor/label and `all`; allowed entity, named script and `notify` still pass; no lists = unchanged). Over `f186f69a`: 2 failed, 124 passed. On `e8c3081`: 126 passed, 2 skipped.

Live check, real plugin code against a local fake Home Assistant REST server (counts the POSTs it receives):

| call | lists | before (f186f69a) | after (e8c3081) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `lock.unlock lock.front_door` | deny `lock.*` | sent, unlocked | refused, 0 POSTs (`pattern 'lock.*'`) |
| `switch.turn_on switch.heater` | allow `light.*` | sent | refused, 0 POSTs |
| `light.turn_on light.kitchen` | allow `light.*` | sent | sent |
| `light.turn_off` (no target) | either list | sent | refused, 0 POSTs |
| `light.turn_off` `area_id: kitchen` | either list | sent | refused, 0 POSTs |
| `notify.mobile_app_phone` | either list | sent | sent |
| all six | none | sent | sent (unchanged) |

## Port notes

- `tools.py`: the logic is the original PR's, carried over verbatim with a 3-way merge. The only differences from it are this plugin's packaging (`register_tools(ctx)`, local `tool_error`).
- `plugin.yaml`: the three variables are declared under `optional_env`.
- `README.md`: documents the new parameters and the operator filters (the PR documented them in core's website docs).
- Tests: the PR's additions to core's `tests/tools/test_homeassistant_tool.py` are ported to `tests/test_homeassistant_tools.py`. Core's registry-based `TestRegistration` tail is not ported, since `tests/test_plugin_registration.py` covers registration here.

## Testing

Against current hermes-agent `main` (131b005c), in a clean venv:

```
PYTHONPATH=/path/to/hermes-agent python -m pytest tests -q
106 passed, 2 skipped
```

Also run in shuffled order (random seed) several times, all green. The new tests fail against the plugin's previous `tools.py`.

`test_schemas_identical_to_core_tools` skips on current core as designed. With an older core that still ships `tools/homeassistant_tool.py` on the path, it fails because this PR intentionally changes the `ha_list_entities` schema.

title: [homeassistant] feat(homeassistant): cross-platform deliver + session-mode delivery for watched entities
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant/pull/2 by @Bendak. The `hermes-homeassistant` repo moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit applied under `homeassistant/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

Port of the Home Assistant cross-platform delivery feature to the standalone plugin.

## Background

Two closed core PRs carried this work: **#96930** (configurable deliver target for
`watch_entities`/`watch_domains`) and **#112136** (session-mode delivery integrated on
top, with silent-session markers and identifier hardening). Both were closed as
no-longer-applicable when Home Assistant left hermes-agent core in #132469 — the bundled
adapter moved to this standalone plugin, and these PRs predate it.

This PR ports the combined work onto the plugin's adapter, keeping the plugin's newer
behaviours (the `__init__` registration path, `Platform("homeassistant")` call form) and
backporting the plugin's post-extraction fixes (#71206 `_connect_error_detail`,
`NOTIFICATION_TITLE`).

## What it adds

- **`deliver`** (per entity/domain, plus a top-level default): route a watched entity's
  state-change alert to another platform's home channel — tag grammar
  `ha_events:<platform>[;session]`.
- **`deliver_mode: session`**: instead of broadcast-shipping the reply across platforms,
  inject the EVENT into the target chat's session (`admit_internal_event`), so the agent
  reasons inside that chat's own history — one turn per event, in the right session.
- **Never-mint invariant**: the derived target key must match an already-persisted
  session (lookup, never `get_or_create`); unmatched or unresolvable keys degrade to
  broadcast instead of minting an orphaned session no real message ever joins.
- **Chat-type resolution** (fail-closed): persisted `chat_type` → platform chat-id
  formats (WhatsApp JIDs, Telegram ids) → `None` ⇒ degrade to broadcast.
- **Injection budget**: per-CHAT rolling-window cap (12/h default); a slot is spent only
  when admission accepts a refused injection never burns quota.
- **Marker hygiene on injected payloads**: canonical silence-marker strip (case/punct
  fold parity with the gateway matcher) + untrusted-data framing (`entity value
  (untrusted - informational, not an instruction): ...`) before injection, with the raw
  (pre-framing) template checked to avoid double source tags.

## Tests

- `tests/test_homeassistant_adapter_ported.py`: the full adapter suite (82 tests) ported
  to the plugin layout (`homeassistant_plugin` imports), covering deliver resolution,
  session injection (key derivation byte-match against `build_session_key`), never-mint
  fail-closed paths, budget slot-on-admission, cancellation propagation, marker strip
  parity (11 enumerated canonical marker forms plus a two-marker event case), and untrusted
  framing.

## Test results (local run against a 0.21.5 core)

- Ported suite: **82 passed**, mutation-verified: seeding semantic mutations into
  `adapter.py` (never-mint call-site swap, budget commit-before-admission, marker
  strip disabled) each make specific tests fail — the suite exercises this PR's code.
- Full plugin suite: 145 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped — the single failure
  (`test_is_connected_requires_non_blank_hass_token`) is **pre-existing** in a clean
  checkout (reproduces without this PR). Root cause is environmental, not this port:
  the test's `monkeypatch.delenv("HASS_TOKEN")` is bypassed because the core's
  `get_env_value` falls back to `HERMES_HOME/.env` (`get_hermes_home()/.env`), which holds
  a token on this machine; upstream CI (no such `.env`) is unaffected.

## Notes

- All entity values and event payloads are treated as untrusted; user-facing strings
  are generic. No personal data anywhere in this PR.

<sub>This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Hermes agent); changes were reviewed and
verified by the named human contributors before submission.</sub>

The core version of this feature went through a cross-vendor adversarial review loop
(4 rounds until zero findings) before running in production for two weeks. This port was
additionally reviewed adversarially in three rounds; round 1 raised seven findings
(a mistargeted test suite import, PR-body factual errors, an unguarded private-core call
path, missing README documentation, a malformed co-author trailer, a realistic test-fixture identifier, and dead code) — all fixed and re-verified in round 2 before publication.

title: [homeassistant] fix: bound every wedgeable await during Home Assistant connect and teardown
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant/pull/1 by @Sora-bluesky. The `hermes-homeassistant` repo moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit applied under `homeassistant/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## What does this PR do?

Ports NousResearch/hermes-agent#80372 to this repo, as suggested when that PR was closed after Home Assistant moved out of core.

The adapter could go silently deaf (NousResearch/hermes-agent#67470): several awaits on the connect and teardown paths have no bound, so a hung auth handshake or a wedged WebSocket or session close leaves the adapter stuck while the gateway still reports it as running. On `main` here these are the three `receive_json()` calls in `_ws_connect` (`adapter.py:159`, `:163`, `:167`), `obj.close()` in `_close` (`:180`) and the listen-task wait in `disconnect` (`:193`).

- `_ws_connect()` builds the session into a local, bounds `ws_connect` and every handshake send and receive with `_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` (30 s), and runs the bounded close on the local socket and session on failure, timeout or cancellation. `self._session` and `self._ws` are only set once the handshake has succeeded.
- Every explicit close on the WebSocket connect and disconnect paths goes through `_run_bounded_close()` (`_DRAIN_TIMEOUT`, 5 s). The `async with` sessions in `send()` and `_standalone_send()` are not changed. A close that does not finish in time is logged and abandoned, and its task stays referenced until it ends.
- `disconnect()` cancels the listen task through `_cancel_task_bounded()`, so a task that ignores cancellation cannot hold teardown.

There is no watchdog or stall detection in this PR, only the bounded waits.

## Related Issue

NousResearch/hermes-agent#67470 (closed there when the adapter moved). Port of NousResearch/hermes-agent#80372.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)

## Changes Made

- `adapter.py` (+144/-30): the #80372 diff merged three-way onto this repo's adapter. The one overlap, the new module constants next to `NOTIFICATION_TITLE`, keeps both sides. `_connect_error_detail`, `Platform("homeassistant")` and the registration in `__init__.py` are untouched.
- `tests/test_homeassistant_network_reconnect.py` (new): the 15 tests from #80372 with the import switched to `homeassistant_plugin`. One of them, `test_cancel_task_bounded_abandons_uncancellable_task`, now watches the helper with `asyncio.wait` and releases its uncancellable task in a `finally`, so a regression fails the test instead of hanging it.

## How to Test

1. `PYTHONPATH=/path/to/hermes-agent python -m pytest tests -q`: 78 passed, 2 skipped here (Windows 11, Python 3.11, hermes-agent `main` at `8b66a51036`).
2. With `adapter.py` put back to `main`'s version, the new file fails 15 of 15.
3. With the bounded wait in `_cancel_task_bounded` replaced by a plain `await task`, `test_cancel_task_bounded_abandons_uncancellable_task` fails in about 2 s instead of hanging.
4. `ruff check adapter.py tests/test_homeassistant_network_reconnect.py` is clean.

Not exercised against a live Home Assistant instance; the tests drive fake sockets and sessions.

## Checklist

- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched this repo's existing PRs (none open)
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this fix
- [x] I've run `pytest tests -q` and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11

title: send_message: register a target parser so homeassistant:<notify_target> resolves
body:
Carried over from NousResearch/hermes-agent#40507 by @nftpoetrist (closed there when Home Assistant moved out of core in fb9fc8a3ddc).

`send_message` with `homeassistant:mobile_app_my_phone` still drops into channel-directory resolution and fails: at ba30cb0 `__init__.py:55-71` registers no target parser. Core now has a generic `parse_target_ref_fn` hook on the platform registry entry, so the fix is to register one here that treats `homeassistant:<notify_target>` as an explicit target. Credit to @nftpoetrist for the diagnosis and original patch.

title: [Feature]: Add custom Spotify playlist cover uploads
body:
## Problem or use case

The bundled Spotify plugin can create and modify playlists, but it does not expose Spotify's official custom playlist cover endpoint. Its default OAuth scope also omits `ugc-image-upload`, so users cannot complete this playlist-management workflow through the existing integration.

## Proposed solution

Extend the existing `spotify_playlists` tool with an `upload_cover` action that:

- accepts a playlist ID and an HTTP(S) or base64 data image URL;
- resolves and validates the image through Hermes' existing image-source safety path;
- converts the image to JPEG and keeps the Base64 request body within Spotify's 256 KB limit;
- sends `PUT /playlists/{playlist_id}/images` with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`;
- includes `ugc-image-upload` in the default Spotify OAuth scopes; and
- documents that existing users must re-authenticate before the new scope is available.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `spotify_playlists` exposes an `upload_cover` action and `image_url` input.
- [ ] Supported images are uploaded as Base64-encoded JPEG bodies no larger than 256 KB.
- [ ] Authentication retries preserve the raw image body and content type.
- [ ] Local filesystem paths are rejected by this action.
- [ ] The default Spotify OAuth scope includes `ugc-image-upload` alongside playlist modification scopes.
- [ ] User documentation covers usage, scope requirements, and re-authentication.
- [ ] Regression tests fail on the current default branch and pass with the implementation.

## Alternatives considered

A separate tool would add unnecessary model-tool surface for behavior that belongs to the existing playlist tool. Direct API calls also require users to handle Hermes' Spotify OAuth state themselves.

## Feature type

Other — extension to an existing bundled plugin tool.

## Contribution

I would like to implement this and submit a pull request.

title: Spotify: discoverability polish — surface integration in 'hermes setup', doc HA interop
body:
Two small tidy-up items identified while rolling out the Spotify integration. Low-priority but straightforward; bundle together or ship separately.

## A — `hermes setup` first-run wizard should list Spotify

Context: `hermes setup` (the initial guided setup a brand-new user runs) has a tool-category picker. Currently Spotify doesn't appear there — it's only reachable via `hermes tools` after setup completes. Same gap exists for Home Assistant and RL Training.

**Why now:** Low severity because most users run `hermes tools` eventually. Still a discoverability miss — a new user who would have enjoyed Spotify may never find out it exists unless they go looking.

**Scope:** Whatever pattern the first-run wizard uses for existing opt-in integrations (probably just adding an entry to the setup picker's opt-in list). If this needs new plumbing for 'opt-in integrations in first-run', that's a broader UX project — file a separate issue.

**Non-goal:** Don't make Spotify default-on in first-run. Stay opt-in.

## B — Home Assistant interop docs note

Context: Spotify Connect already exposes HA-controlled speakers (Sonos, Echo, Nest, etc.) as Spotify devices automatically via the `spotify_devices` tool. The user doesn't need a Hermes-side HA↔Spotify bridge because Spotify itself handles the bridging at the device layer.

**What to add:** ~5-10 lines in `website/docs/user-guide/features/spotify.md` (new subsection under 'Using it' or within troubleshooting) explaining:

- If you have Home Assistant managing speakers that support Spotify Connect, those speakers appear in `spotify_devices list` automatically
- Target them by name via `spotify.default_device_name` (issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#19) or by passing `device_id` explicitly
- No extra config needed — this is Spotify's native behavior, not a Hermes feature

**Why it's worth documenting:** Users with HA assume they need a Hermes-side integration to route Spotify to HA-managed speakers. They don't, and saying so saves them a configuration rabbit hole.

## Acceptance

- A: Spotify appears in first-run setup picker; toggling it on runs the same wizard that `hermes tools` does
- B: Docs page has a clear 'Home Assistant-managed speakers' subsection

Both are docs/UX polish — no core code changes expected beyond the first-run picker registration for A.

title: Dashboard: Spotify remote-control widget (Tier 1, Free-compatible)
body:
Simpler companion to issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#20 (Web Playback SDK widget). Ships faster, works for Free users, controls an existing Spotify client rather than becoming one.

## What this is

A dashboard plugin showing a small transport bar — album art, track + artist, progress, play/pause/skip/volume. Polls `spotify_playback get_state` every few seconds for updates. Buttons call the existing Spotify tools directly (no SDK, no browser-as-device).

## What this ISN'T

Not a Spotify client. No audio plays in the browser. This widget controls whatever Spotify is already running elsewhere — your phone, desktop app, Sonos, etc.

Issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#20 (Web Playback SDK) IS a client. Strictly more capable but Premium-only and heavier.

## Why both tiers make sense

- **Tier 1 (this)**: ~200 LOC dashboard plugin, works on Spotify Free, useful to everyone, ships in a weekend.
- **Tier 2 (#15182)**: ~400 LOC + SDK integration, Premium-only, useful to everyone with Premium who wants a self-contained in-browser player.

Users get strict upgrade when both ship. Tier 1's UI stays identical; Tier 2 adds 'this tab is a device' functionality underneath.

## Requirements

- Dashboard plugin under `plugins/` (new directory, follow `plugins/example-dashboard/` / `plugins/strike-freedom-cockpit/` pattern)
- Server-side poll: every 3-5s, dashboard backend calls `spotify_playback get_state` and pushes result over the existing dashboard WebSocket
- Client-side UI: album art, track title, artist, album, progress bar that ticks locally between updates
- Transport buttons wired to `spotify_playback` actions (play, pause, next, previous, seek via click on progress bar, volume slider)
- Device indicator: shows which device playback is on. Dropdown to transfer via `spotify_devices transfer`
- 'Not authed' state: when `get_provider_auth_state('spotify')` returns empty, widget shows a button linking to setup docs
- Play-action behavior matches the device resolution in issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#19 (use `spotify.default_device_name` if set, otherwise let Spotify pick active device)
- No regression if the dashboard plugin isn't loaded — widget is opt-in per dashboard layout

## Premium gating

On Free accounts, read-only actions still work (get_state, recently_played). Transport buttons should render as disabled or show a 'Premium required' tooltip rather than throwing 403s on click. Detect by checking the `product` field on `/me` once at load.

## Open questions

- Polling interval: 3s feels responsive but racks up API calls. 5s is more polite. Start at 5s, drop to 2s when the widget has focus (document.hasFocus).
- Album art: cache client-side? Spotify's URLs are CDN-stable.
- Small-form factor: widget should look reasonable at 300px wide too. Progressive disclosure — album art only, then + track info, then + transport.

## Scope estimate

- Backend: ~50 LOC (poll loop, WS push, tool dispatch for button clicks)
- Frontend: ~150 LOC (React/similar widget matching dashboard conventions)
- Total: ~200 LOC across the plugin

## Acceptance

- Widget loads in dashboard, polls state
- Shows 'not authed' state gracefully when Spotify isn't configured
- Transport buttons work on Premium, degrade visibly on Free
- Progress bar ticks locally, doesn't jitter when poll arrives
- Transferring device via dropdown updates the state on next poll

## Non-goals

- Playlist browsing (agent's job)
- Library management (agent's job)
- Queue management beyond 'show current queue'
- Multi-user device handling

title: Spotify: gateway slash commands (/play, /pause, /skip, /nowplaying, /queue)
body:
Expose Spotify control as slash commands in messaging platforms (Discord, Telegram, etc.) so users don't need a full agent turn for common actions.

## Depends on

- **Issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#19** — `spotify.default_device_name` config knob. Without a reliable target device, slash commands hit 'no active device' too often to be worth shipping. See the end of that issue for the full rationale.
- Or (alternatively) issue NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#20 — Web Playback dashboard widget. Once the dashboard is a Spotify Connect device, slash commands have a guaranteed target whenever the dashboard tab is open.

One of the two must ship first. Slash commands after.

## Proposal

Add 5 gateway-only slash commands:

| Command | Action |
|---------|--------|
| `/play [query]` | Play a track/album/artist. No query = resume current. |
| `/pause` | Pause playback. |
| `/skip` | Skip to next track. |
| `/nowplaying` (alias: `/np`) | Show current track, progress, device. |
| `/queue <query>` | Add matched track to queue. |

All five run in whichever gateway platform is active (Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc.) and respond with a terse formatted line rather than raw tool JSON:

```
/nowplaying
▶ Miles Davis — So What (Kind of Blue) · 3:42 / 9:22 · Kitchen Sonos

/play blackbird acoustic
▶ Now playing: Blackbird (Acoustic) — Beatles · Kitchen Sonos

/pause
⏸ Paused on Kitchen Sonos

/skip
⏭ Skipped · next: Freddie Freeloader — Miles Davis
```

## Visibility gating

Current `CommandDef` supports `gateway_config_gate: str` (a single config dotpath). That's fine for simple flags but doesn't fit 'toolset enabled AND Spotify authenticated' which is two-factor runtime state.

**Extension proposal:** add `gateway_availability_fn: Callable[[], bool]` to `CommandDef`. `_is_gateway_available()` calls it if present. Falls back to `gateway_config_gate` then the `cli_only` default. ~20 LOC in `hermes_cli/commands.py`.

For Spotify the check is:
```python
def _spotify_gateway_available() -> bool:
    # toolset enabled somewhere + Spotify authed
    from hermes_cli.auth import get_provider_auth_state
    state = get_provider_auth_state('spotify') or {}
    return bool(state.get('refresh_token'))
```

This way users without Spotify configured never see these commands in help, Telegram bot menus, Slack subcommand lists, or autocomplete — zero clutter. Dispatch still works if someone types them manually, returning a helpful 'Spotify isn't configured' error.

## Where the handlers live

Don't add 5 individual handlers scattered across `gateway/run.py`. Instead:

- `plugins/spotify/gateway_commands.py` — module exposing 5 handler functions that each call the underlying Spotify tool and format the result
- `gateway/run.py` — one dispatch block that routes `/play`, `/pause`, `/skip`, `/nowplaying`, `/queue` to the handler module

Keeps the Spotify-specific logic in the plugin directory where it belongs, and the gateway just has a thin import + dispatch.

## Acceptance

- Commands appear in Discord/Telegram help ONLY when Spotify is authenticated
- `/nowplaying` returns a single formatted line, not JSON
- `/play miles davis` from Discord plays on the user's default device (or the dashboard tab if NousResearch/hermes-pantheon#20 is the route we took)
- `/pause` and `/skip` work on Free accounts only if we gate with a clear error ('Spotify Premium required')
- Commands dispatched while Spotify isn't authed return 'Spotify not configured — run `hermes auth spotify`'
- No regression on existing slash commands; `gateway_availability_fn` is additive

## Non-goals

- Search pickers / interactive result selection. `/play X` just plays the top search result. More complex flows are the agent's job.
- Playlist management. Use the agent.
- Per-user device targeting in multi-user gateways. v1 uses the bot's configured default device.

title: Spotify: add spotify.default_device_name config knob
body:
Small quality-of-life improvement to reduce 'no active device' friction for Spotify users.

## Problem

Every Spotify playback action (play, pause, skip, queue add, etc.) targets Spotify's current 'active' device. If nothing is active, the call returns `403 Forbidden — No active device found` and the user has to open Spotify on some device before retrying.

Users with an always-on device (Sonos, Echo, smart speaker) hit this needlessly often. Their speaker is always online and ready, but Spotify doesn't consider it 'active' unless something's playing or recently played on it.

## Proposal

Add `spotify.default_device_name` to `config.yaml` (string, default empty).

When set, the Spotify tools resolve the name to a `device_id` at call time (via `spotify_devices list`, match on `name` case-insensitively) and pass it as `device_id` to any playback action that didn't get one explicitly.

```yaml
spotify:
  default_device_name: "Kitchen Sonos"
```

## Where it plugs in

- `plugins/spotify/tools.py`: before each playback call that accepts `device_id`, if `args.get('device_id')` is empty, look up the configured default and substitute.
- `skills/media/spotify/SKILL.md`: update the 'no active device' failure-mode section to mention this as the recommended mitigation.
- Docs: add to `website/docs/user-guide/features/spotify.md` under a new 'Default device' subsection.

## Why not just always target the last-used device?
Spotify's Web API already does that. The problem is that 'last-used' can be a phone that's now off. An explicit user-configured name sidesteps the ambiguity.

## Acceptance

- `spotify.default_device_name: "Kitchen Sonos"` in config.yaml
- User runs `hermes` in a fresh tab with nothing playing anywhere
- Agent calls `spotify_playback play` with no `device_id` → tool resolves 'Kitchen Sonos' → music plays there
- If the named device isn't currently online, return a clear error ('configured default device "Kitchen Sonos" is offline — available: ...') rather than silently falling back to Spotify's guess
- Explicit `device_id` in the tool call always wins over the config default

## Relation to other issues

Unblocks gateway slash commands (`/play`, `/pause`, etc.) — see the separate issue on that. Also improves agent UX independently.

title: Dashboard: Spotify Web Playback widget (browser becomes a Spotify Connect device)
body:
Follow-up to the Spotify integration rollout (#15121, NousResearch/hermes-agent#15130, NousResearch/hermes-agent#15135, NousResearch/hermes-agent#15154, NousResearch/hermes-agent#15174, NousResearch/hermes-agent#15180).

## The goal

A dashboard plugin that makes the browser tab itself a Spotify Connect device. Audio plays out of the browser. The agent can control it directly via the existing `spotify_devices` and `spotify_playback` tools — no new backend code, it just shows up as a device the agent can target.

## Why this tier (vs. a remote-control widget)

A simpler "remote control" widget would just poll `get_currently_playing` and show album art + play/pause buttons that call the existing tools. Useful, but it only controls a Spotify client you're already running elsewhere (phone, desktop app, Sonos).

The Web Playback SDK approach is strictly more capable: the browser IS the client. You don't need Spotify open anywhere else. The agent can say 'play X' from a fresh cron session and audio comes out of the dashboard tab that's already open. This is the natural home for a Hermes user who lives in the dashboard anyway.

## Requirements

- **Premium only.** Spotify's Web Playback SDK refuses to initialize on Free accounts. Widget should detect and show a clear message, not break silently.
- **Token handoff from `auth.json` to browser.** The dashboard is a Hermes plugin with server-side access to `~/.hermes/auth.json`. It needs to hand the Spotify access token to the browser for SDK init, and handle refresh (the SDK calls a user-provided callback when the token expires — that callback should hit a dashboard endpoint that returns a fresh token, refreshing via our existing `_refresh_spotify_oauth_state` if needed).
- **Device registration.** The SDK emits a `ready` event with a device_id. Widget should expose that device in the UI ("This tab is registered as 'Hermes Dashboard' — agent can target it").
- **Control surface.** Standard transport bar (play/pause/skip/seek, volume slider, current track + album art). Progress bar ticks locally between SDK state updates.
- **Agent-triggered playback.** When the agent calls `spotify_playback play` with `device_id` = this tab's id, the SDK handles it. Nothing special from our side — it just works because the browser is a real Connect device.
- **Graceful degradation.** If the tab loses focus / network / SDK connection, reconnect automatically. Don't leave zombie devices in the user's Spotify Connect list.

## Reference

- [Web Playback SDK overview](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-playback-sdk)
- [SDK quick start](https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-playback-sdk/tutorials/getting-started)
- Existing Hermes dashboard plugin pattern: `plugins/example-dashboard/`, `plugins/strike-freedom-cockpit/`
- Existing Spotify client module: `plugins/spotify/client.py` (has refresh logic we should reuse)
- Existing auth: `hermes_cli/auth.py` `_refresh_spotify_oauth_state` and `get_provider_auth_state("spotify")`

## Scope estimate
- Dashboard plugin: ~400 LOC (SDK bootstrap, token refresh endpoint, transport UI, device state sync)
- No changes to the core Spotify integration
- Opt-in — only users who load the dashboard plugin pay for it

## Non-goals
- Playlist/library browsing UI. The agent handles that through tools. Widget stays focused on "what's playing + transport controls."
- Offline playback. SDK doesn't support it.
- Replacing the existing remote-control tools. The transport buttons in the widget should call the same `spotify_playback` tools so an external agent can drive the UI too.

## Acceptance
- User opens dashboard → sees Spotify widget showing login state
- Clicks login → PKCE flow completes → tab shows 'Hermes Dashboard' as active device
- Agent 'play miles davis' → music plays in the tab
- Skip/pause buttons in the widget work and the agent sees the state change via `get_currently_playing`
- Free users see a clear 'Spotify Premium required for in-browser playback' message

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): normalize foreign tool IDs before native replay
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/132 by @efron. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Problem

Switching a conversation from another provider back to the subscription DirectSDK can fail even though Claude works in a fresh session. Foreign tool-call IDs such as the synthetic `terminal:42` are passed through to `tool_use.id` and `tool_result.tool_use_id`; Anthropic rejects them with HTTP 400 because they do not match `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$`. Hermes then classifies the request as "request format rejected" and activates an unnecessary provider fallback.

## Change

Normalize incompatible tool IDs at the outgoing history boundary, after canonical frame/replay construction:

- Preserve every already-valid ID, including native Claude IDs.
- Generate deterministic SHA-256-derived IDs for incompatible strings.
- Reserve all valid IDs first and resolve generated-name collisions, so distinct calls cannot be merged accidentally.
- Rewrite both the call ID and every matching result reference consistently.
- Leave source history, tool arguments, result bodies, and valid signed native replay blocks unchanged.

This is a transport-only fix. It does not change authentication, tools, model routing, telemetry settings, or persisted sessions.

## Validation

- **Red on current main:** the colon-ID regression fails against `4bc79c78031d1a042b5d8a7314ceea283db5c5e2` because the emitted ID is still `terminal:42`.
- **Green with this change:** full upstream suite on Python 3.14.7: **216 passed, 9 subtests passed**, with no failures or skips.
- Seven synthetic boundary regressions cover invalid IDs, valid-ID preservation, distinct-ID collisions, reserved native-ID collisions, deterministic ordering, signed native replay, and payload/source immutability.
- Live subscription DirectSDK checks with `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`, replaying only synthetic foreign-ID history, returned `OK` in four independent plugin installations. These used the DirectSDK client directly, with no fallback path, API-key authentication, or execution of real tools.

Offline reproduction command (with a Hermes core checkout and its test dependencies available):

```sh
HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1 \
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=/path/to/hermes-agent \
python -m pytest -q tests/test_directsdk_foreign_tool_ids.py
```

Only implementation and synthetic tests are included. No user configurations, logs, conversation data, or credentials are attached.

After merge, catalog-pinned installations will need the normal release/catalog-pin update to receive the fix.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(admission): keep the open turn's start readable after a long tool loop (#122)
body:
Fixes #36. Other issue references in the preserved original description belong to the archived source repository.

Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/130 by @MakerFounder. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

Historical report: NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#122.

## What

After a tool loop longer than the cache lookback, the next turn's first call read only system + tools from cache and wrote the whole conversation again. The relay now keeps one more message breakpoint where the finished turn's thinking starts, so the next turn reads that prefix.

## Why it happens

Following #122's diagnosis:
- Once a user message carries more than tool results (the next turn, or a `/steer` row), cache entries written after the finished turn's first thinking block stop matching.
- Anthropic's cache lookup walks back at most 20 blocks from a breakpoint.
- After a loop longer than that, the single recurring breakpoint cannot reach the last entry that still matches. The read falls back to system + tools.

On one user's real logs (plugin 0.3.3 / `4bc79c7`, `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`, about 10 days), 39 calls lost more than 20K previously cached tokens without the context shrinking. That was 4.86M re-written tokens, about 46% of all cache writes. 22 of them were turn starts that fell back to about 21K (system + tools).

## How

`admission.py::_keep_turn_mark`, called from `pin_message_breakpoint`:
- **Where the mark goes.** The open turn starts at the latest user message with more than tool results. The mark goes on the last cacheable block of the user message right before that turn's first assistant message with thinking. That is usually the turn's opening frame, or a `/steer` row. An earlier request of the turn already wrote an entry there as its recurring breakpoint.
- **When it is added.** Only when that block is more than 20 blocks before the recurring breakpoint, counted per block without the API's merging of tool runs, so an error only marks early. A shorter loop, or one without thinking, is unchanged.
- **Breakpoint budget.**
  - Every `cache_control` in the body is counted, recursively, including a top-level marker and markers nested in tool-result content. The count never exceeds 4.
  - Native 2.1.285 places three, so the extra mark is the fourth.
  - At the limit (2.1.287+ marks two message blocks), a native mark between it and the recurring breakpoint moves there instead. Otherwise nothing changes.
- **Never touched.** The extra mark copies the TTL of the next mark after it, so native's TTL order holds. System and tools marks are never touched, content never changes, and a payload that does not parse is forwarded as is.

The README paragraph on breakpoint placement is updated.

## Evidence

**Tests.** There is a new `tests/test_admission_turn_start.py` (18 tests). It covers:
- a long loop with thinking, both layouts;
- short loops;
- a thinking-free loop;
- a `/steer` row after 11 rounds;
- parallel rounds of 4 calls × 6;
- the 4-breakpoint limit, including nested markers and no spare slot;
- TTL order;
- one request through the real `Admission` relay.

On `4bc79c7`, 12 of the first 16 fail. The 4 that pass are the unchanged-behaviour guards. The 2 nested-marker tests fail on the first commit and pass on the second.

| Base | Per-call | `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1` |
|---|---|---|
| This branch | 227 passed | 227 passed |
| Merged with #99 + #123 | 263 passed | 263 passed |

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly onto #99 and #123. The baseline on `main` is 209.

**Wire eval.** `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` now runs 2 tool rounds, 2 user turns, a 14-round loop with thinking, and the turn after it. On the final turn it asserts a breakpoint on the loop's opening frame, more than 20 blocks from the recurring one, on a prefix an earlier request wrote. With the real Claude Code 2.1.285 it passes on this branch. On `4bc79c7` it fails with `no breakpoint on the loop's opening frame`.

**Live**, on a real subscription:
- Setup: `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`, effort low, Claude Code 2.1.285, Hermes v0.21.6+171, one long-lived `hermes-acp` process per run.
- Turn 1: a 400-line ledger (about 13K tokens), then 14 one-call echo steps.
- Turn 2: one more echo.

First call of turn 2, from `agent.log`:

| | cache read | write |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`4bc79c7`) | 17,740 / 32,669 (54%) | 14,699 |
| this branch | 30,816 / 32,715 (94%) | 1,667 |

30,816 is exactly call #1's read + write, i.e. the turn's opening frame.

## Limits

- **Observed, not documented.** That entries after the first thinking block stop matching at a new turn comes from #122's captures and the live run above. Anthropic's docs say prior thinking stays cache-valid on Opus 4.5+. So the finished loop is still re-written from its first thinking block at each turn start: 1,667 tokens above, more on long thinking-heavy loops, but no longer the whole conversation.
- **Not live-verified.** `/steer`, parallel rounds and warm mode with the mark present are covered offline only. The one live warm run had no thinking in turn 1, so it shows no regression rather than the mark at work.
- **Overcounting is safe.** A literal `cache_control` key inside a tool input or schema is counted as a breakpoint. The only effect is that the mark is skipped.
- **TTL.** With a 5-minute TTL, a very slow early loop can let the opening entry expire before the mark first appears, more than 20 blocks in.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(admission): support CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY for dedicated upstream relay proxying
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/129 by @MematiBas42. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Summary
Add `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY` environment variable support to route the relay's upstream connection (`https://api.anthropic.com`) through a dedicated HTTP CONNECT proxy without forcing process-wide `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` on the host Hermes process.

## Motivation
In environments where Claude/Anthropic datacenter traffic must egress via a specific residential/proxy IP while other Hermes gateway tools and services (messaging bots, web scrapers, local endpoints) should keep their default routing, setting a global `HTTPS_PROXY` introduces unwanted side effects and unnecessary bandwidth consumption.

This allows configuring a dedicated proxy solely for the DirectSDK admission relay.

## Changes
- `admission.py`: Check `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY` before falling back to environment proxies.
- `plugin.yaml`: Declare `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY` under `optional_env`.
- `README.md`: Document the variable under the Proxies section.
- `tests/test_admission_proxy.py`: Add unit test verifying that `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY` takes precedence over `HTTPS_PROXY`.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(accounting): report usage as subscription-included with list_price_usd
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/128 by @bartcollet. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Problem

`get_usage_cost()` recorded the native `total_cost_usd` as `status='estimated'`, `source='provider_cost_api'` — labelling a provider invoice. On a Claude subscription (Max) the out-of-pocket cost of this usage is $0; the native figure is the LIST-PRICE equivalent, an allowance gauge. Recording it as estimated provider cost inflated every spend consumer that sums `estimated_cost_usd` by the full session cost.

## Change

On the valid-list-price path (`costBasis='list'`, finite, non-negative), `get_usage_cost` now returns `amount_usd=0`, `status='included'`, `source='subscription_included'`, `label='included'`, with the native figure on the new core `CostResult.list_price_usd` field — the companion core change (fork branch `feat/subscription-included-list-price` on `bartcollet/hermes-agent`) persists it as `list_price_equiv_usd`, separate from spend.

Compatibility: on a core `CostResult` without the field the constructor raises `TypeError` and the fallback returns the same included/$0 result without the gauge — no crash, no dependency on the core change to stop mislabelling spend. The unknown paths (missing `modelUsage`, non-`list` `costBasis`, non-finite or negative amounts) are unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/test_directsdk_usage_cost.py` (new): list-price → included/$0 with the gauge; zero list price still included; unknown paths stay unknown.
- `tests/test_directsdk_discovery.py`: the native-alias metadata test now pins included/$0 + `list_price_usd` instead of an estimated list price.
- Full plugin suite (`python -m pytest -q`, `HERMES_AGENT_REPO` pointed at a core checkout carrying the companion change): 212 passed, 9 subtests passed.
- Against a pre-change core the profile still returns included/$0 via the `TypeError` fallback (probed directly); only the gauge assertions need the companion core change.

## ⚠️ Pitfall

`total_cost_usd` is the list-price equivalent, NOT an invoice: never sum it into spend. It rides `list_price_usd`/`list_price_equiv_usd` precisely so `estimated_cost_usd` stays truthful at $0 for subscription usage.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(setup): settle a due login before  and reap an orphaned refresh lock
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/124 by @LevSky22. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## What does this PR do?

On a gateway where the subscription login sits idle between uses, selecting this provider (or loading the picker) after the access token's 8 h expiry made every following request fail with:

```
Native API error: Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. This is usually transient; retry in a minute, and if it persists close other Claude Code processes or sign in again
```

Hermes then falls back to the next provider. Waiting does not help; only deleting `<config>/.oauth_refresh.lock` by hand does.

**Cause.** `setup_status()` runs `claude auth status` on every provider selection and picker load (`discover_models()` calls it first). Every Claude Code command starts the OAuth refresh at init when the stored token is inside its 5-minute window, and `auth status` exits before that refresh lands. That's anthropics/claude-code#95822, still open. The abandoned refresh leaves the empty `.oauth_refresh.lock` directory behind, and Claude Code never reclaims it despite its `stale: 60000` setting. That's anthropics/claude-code#95236, also open, and it isn't Windows-only. If the abandoned POST reached the server, the refresh token has also been rotated without the CLI saving the new pair. The next refresh then gets `invalid_grant`, which forces a re-login. On an idle login nearly every selection hits this, because the token has always expired by the time the user switches.

**Fix.** Before a setup probe runs `auth status`, it first runs `claude -p /usage`, the workaround tested in #95822. `/usage` is a local command that needs a valid token, so it waits for a due refresh to be saved before exiting, and it sends no Messages request. Before setup probes and native requests, the plugin also removes an orphaned empty refresh lock older than Claude Code's own stale window.

**Trade-off for you to decide.** The plugin cannot tell whether a refresh is due without reading `expiresAt` from the credential store, and the README says it never opens its credential files. So this always runs `/usage`. That costs about 0.6 s and one account request per selection or picker load, and the setup section's "never Anthropic" became "no Messages request". An earlier revision of this branch read only `expiresAt` from `.credentials.json` and ran `/usage` only when a refresh was due, which kept the probe at ~0.3 s for a valid login. Happy to switch back if you'd rather relax that rule than add the request.

**Security note.** This touches login handling. The plugin still never opens, copies, refreshes or prints a credential file; Claude Code does the refresh itself. The only filesystem write is `rmdir` of an *empty* `.oauth_refresh.lock` directory in the CLI's config dir, and only when it's older than 60 s. A live holder bumps the mtime every 5 s, and `rmdir` refuses a directory with contents. Nothing new is logged.

## Related Issue

No issue in this repo. Upstream causes: anthropics/claude-code#95822 and anthropics/claude-code#95236. I searched issues and PRs, all states, and found no duplicate. In this repo I searched for `auth status`, `oauth_refresh`, `refresh lock`, `refresh token`, `stale lock` and `setup_status`. In hermes-agent I searched for `oauth_refresh.lock`, `auth status refresh` and `another Claude Code process is refreshing`.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `directsdk_setup.py`:
  - `settle_login()` runs `claude -p /usage` (same child env as the other probes, so `claude_code_telemetry` is respected; `/usage` still fetches with the telemetry flags set), bounded by the probe timeout. `setup_status()` calls it before `auth status`, and the status answer still comes from `auth status`, so a logout is never masked.
  - `reap_orphaned_refresh_lock()` does the lock cleanup described above.
  - `_config_dir()` resolves the CLI's config dir the way Claude Code does: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude` with Node's `os.homedir()` rules (%USERPROFILE% on Windows even when a Git Bash or MSYS shell sets `HOME`).
- `directsdk.py`: the native request path reaps an orphaned lock before spawning, which also covers a request that was cancelled mid-refresh.
- `README.md`: the setup flow (step 2) and the authentication notes describe both.
- Tests:
  - New file `tests/test_directsdk_oauth_refresh.py`.
  - The shared fake CLI in `tests/test_directsdk_setup.py` answers `-p /usage`.
  - `tests/test_directsdk_telemetry.py` counts the extra discovery child, and its existing assertions check that child for the telemetry flags.

## How to Test

1. **Reproduce the bug** on a Linux file credential store: let the login's `expiresAt` pass, then select the provider. On `main`, an empty `.oauth_refresh.lock` is left in the config dir and the next request fails with the error above.
2. **Check the fix** on this branch:
   - after step 1, no lock is left;
   - the stored `expiresAt` moves about 8 h ahead;
   - the next request answers.
3. **Planted lock:** run `mkdir ~/.claude/.oauth_refresh.lock && touch -d '-2 minutes' ~/.claude/.oauth_refresh.lock`. On this branch the next request answers and the directory is gone.
4. **Run the suite:** `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=<hermes-agent checkout> python -m pytest -q`. Each test in the new file maps to one failure mode:
   - an expired login is renewed before `auth status`;
   - a logged-out CLI still reports logged out;
   - a failed renewal still reports the CLI's login, and a hung one returns within the probe timeout;
   - an orphaned lock is reaped; a live lock, or one with contents, is kept;
   - the config dir follows the CLI's home rules on Windows and elsewhere.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass. **Ran this repo's command against hermes-agent v0.21.5: 216 passed, 2 failed.** The failures are `test_directsdk_discovery.py::test_missing_claude_is_reported_on_every_path` and `::test_resolve_honors_the_env_dict_not_the_process_path`. They fail identically on `main` there, because the environment has a system-wide `/usr/local/bin/claude` that the install-prefix probe finds.
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). **N/A here:** this repo has no `scripts/check`. I ran hermes-agent's `scripts/check-windows-footguns.py` on the changed files instead; my changes add no findings.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Debian 13 container, Python 3.13, Claude Code 2.1.283, Max subscription, file credential store)

  - On macOS the Keychain store is unaffected: `/usage` works with any store.
  - I couldn't run macOS or Windows locally; the CI matrix covers them.

## Screenshots / Logs

Live check on the Linux gateway, after installing 356fe41 (this branch's first commit) with `hermes plugins install … --ref`, no rebuild. The second commit only changes the Windows home-dir rule and test encodings:

```

PASS valid: credential file untouched
PASS due: logged in
PASS due: renewed expiry saved
PASS due: no lock left

PASS orphan: Opus served it through the plugin
PASS orphan: lock reaped

```

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(setup): stop native's own session-title request from taking the turn's admission (#116)
body:
Fixes #78. Other issue references in the preserved original description belong to the archived source repository.

Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/123 by @100yenadmin. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

Historical report: NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#116.

## What
Adds `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1` to the flags the plugin always sets on a child (`ALWAYS_QUIET`, next to `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` and `DISABLE_FEEDBACK_COMMAND`). That stops native's own session-title request, which can take the one upstream request the relay admits for a step.

## Why
In Claude Code 2.1.286, native skips the title request when non-essential traffic is off, when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` is set, or when the entrypoint is `sdk-cli` (what `-p` sets when none is inherited) with no `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION`/`CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID` and the server flag `tengu_quizzical_thimble` on (its default).

So it can fire when:
- the Hermes process carries a `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` other than `cli` or `sdk-cli`, or `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` or `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`, which a gateway started from another Claude Code or Agent SDK process can inherit; or
- that server flag is off for the account.

Before #111, every spawn set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`, which kept it off. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` stops native's session-title generation without turning off the feature-flag fetch (#86).

## Tests
- `test_native_never_sends_its_own_session_title_request` (setup probe and turn, setting default and off, with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py` and `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_VERSION` inherited) checks that the child gets the variable. It fails on main and passes here.
- The test clears an inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE` first, so a developer's own environment can't make it pass.
- Full suite: 213 passed (macOS, Python 3.11).
- Offline check with the real Claude Code 2.1.286, the plugin's relay and a fake loopback upstream, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py`, 4 user turns:
  - main `4bc79c7`: a title request reached the relay first on every turn, and the real turn was denied each time;
  - this branch: no title requests, nothing denied.
- Re-checked on Claude Code 2.1.292: the same results on main and on this branch. Merged with #99's warm mode, there are no title requests and warm reuse holds.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(setup): skip install prefixes under a relative HOME
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/117 by @grantjayy. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Problem
`_install_prefixes` joins `HOME` (or `USERPROFILE`) with `.local/bin`, `.claude/local`, `bin` and the other home prefixes. When `HOME` is empty or relative, those paths resolve against the current working directory. `_resolve` can then run a `claude` binary that sits under the directory Hermes was started from, for example `./relative-home/.local/bin/claude`.

## Solution
Only an absolute home directory contributes home prefixes. PATH lookup, an explicit command, `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` and the system prefixes are unchanged.

## Validation
- New `test_relative_home_does_not_discover_cwd_binary` (empty and relative `HOME`).
- Red on `main` (31b591f): the `relative-home` case resolves the planted binary.
- Green on this branch.
- Full suite with `HERMES_AGENT_REPO` at hermes-agent: 210 passed, 9 subtests passed (macOS).

## Risk
None known. A user with a relative `HOME` loses only the home-prefix fallback; PATH still works.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(setup): an API-key or cloud login is not a subscription login
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/115 by @100yenadmin. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Problem

`claude auth status` reports `loggedIn: true` for every way Claude Code can authenticate, including the ones that don't use a subscription:

| Native auth | `authMethod` / `apiProvider` |
|---|---|
| Claude subscription | `claude.ai` / `firstParty` |
| `claude setup-token` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` | `oauth_token` / `firstParty` |
| Console API key (stored, or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) | `api_key` / `firstParty` |
| `apiKeyHelper` | `api_key_helper` / `firstParty` |
| Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry | `third_party` / `bedrock`, ... |

`setup_status` reads only `loggedIn`, so setup and model discovery pass a Console-key or cloud login as a working subscription. The request-path guard only sees environment variables. A key stored by the CLI itself is not caught, so requests would bill API usage instead of the plan.

## Fix

In `setup_status`, a login with `authMethod` `api_key`, `api_key_helper` or `third_party`, or any `apiProvider` other than `firstParty`, is not logged in. Its `detail` says why and how to switch:

> Claude Code would sign in with an Anthropic API key, which bills API usage instead of your Claude subscription. Run `claude auth login` with your Claude account (and unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in Hermes' environment if it is set), then select this provider again.

- On a TTY, Hermes' setup gate then runs the CLI's own `claude auth login`.
- Discovery falls back to the pinned table, as it does for a logged-out CLI.
- `claude.ai` and `oauth_token` logins are unchanged. An unknown future `authMethod` is still accepted, so only known API-billing logins are rejected.

## Verification

- **Real CLI (Claude Code 2.1.286):** `auth status` gives the values in the table for a dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`, a dummy `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and a claude.ai Max login. `setup_status` against the real CLI with the dummy key returns `logged_in: False` and the detail above. Without it, it returns `logged_in: True`, `Claude Max`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_directsdk_setup.py` gains a parametrized case for each billing login. All four fail on main and pass here. A setup-token case guards against over-blocking.
- **Suite:** 213 passed locally (macOS).

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code; independent Codex review).

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(directsdk): opt-in warm native session (#97, #83)
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/99 by @100yenadmin. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## What

An opt-in **warm native session** (`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1`, default off). Today every `create()` spawns `claude -p --max-turns 1` and replays the whole history. With warm mode on, one native process stays alive per conversation instead. The default path is unchanged: with the flag off, it runs main's code.

**Hermes still owns every step.** Each `create()` is one model step. Native `tool_use` comes back as Hermes `tool_calls`, and Hermes runs its own hooks, approvals and tools. Anything that doesn't line up falls back to the existing full replay.

It targets the two per-call costs that main's fixes do not reach:
- #97: thinking is re-derived on every tool round.
- #83: a fresh `claude -p` is spawned on every call.

Updated 2026-10-05:
- Rebased onto `31b591f`.
- The Windows cancel fix that was part of this PR landed separately as #107.
- #33/#77 are fixed on main, and warm steps go through those same admission rewrites, described below.

## How
- **Parking tool calls.** Hermes tools are exposed as an SDK-type MCP server over the stream-json control protocol:
  - `--mcp-config {"mcpServers":{"hermes":{"type":"sdk",...}}}`, `--allowedTools mcp__hermes`, `dontAsk`, no `--max-turns`.
  - Native sends each call as `control_request{mcp_message, tools/call}`.
  - The plugin parks the call until the next `create()` brings the Hermes `tool` result, matched by `toolUseId`.
- **Docs.** A README section, "Warm native session (opt-in, experimental)", covers the flag, the reuse rules and the two tuning variables. The "Ownership and replay" text now says the parked-session absence applies outside warm mode.
- **Admission.** `Admission.rearm(timeout, queried)` admits exactly one upstream request per step, under that step's own timeout.
  - The anchor is set to the frame native will replay next: Hermes' frame on a user turn, or, on a tool round, native's stored copy of the MCP results in native's call order.
  - Main's tool-result restoration (456fdb0), first-turn caching (#77) and single recurring breakpoint (#33) therefore apply as they do per call.
  - A frame that can't be restored is reported as `native_admission.unrestored`, as per call.
  - In every measured warm step: 1 upstream request, 0 denied.
- **Same answers as per call.**
  - A refusal is `content_filter` with its reason and no tool calls.
  - Failures carry the HTTP status Hermes routes on.
  - A tool name outside the inventory, or a bare offered name, goes to Hermes. Native never parks those calls, so that session is not reused and the next step replays.
- **Finding the session by history, not by client.** Hermes builds request-local clients, so the pool is module-level.
  - Reuse requires a unique exact-prefix match.
  - The key covers: native carrier hashes, model, system prompt, tools, generation fields, the resolved command, native auth env, the `claude_code_telemetry` flags, `DO_NOT_TRACK` and the proxy route.
  - The conflicting-auth guard runs on every step. The per-call launch env lives in `_native_env()`, shared by both paths.
- **Fallback.** Any of these kills the session and does the existing full replay: an ambiguous match, edited or compacted history, a prompt/tool/model change, a cancel, a dead process, or unexpected output.
  - A warm launch or session that fails before its upstream request serves that step per call, provided nothing was streamed and the step wasn't cancelled. Auth and backend refusals stay errors.
- **Lifecycle.**
  - `cancel()` also kills a parked session owned by that client.
  - Idle sessions are reaped after `..._WARM_IDLE_SECONDS` (default 600).
  - An LRU cap limits retained slots (`..._WARM_POOL`, default 8). A full pool takes the per-call path, and so do tool-less calls.

## Evidence

Setup: Opus 5.5 `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`, `--reasoning high`, Claude Code 2.1.286, Max, Hermes `f42f579`, isolated HERMES_HOME, rebased code.

**Controlled A/B.** A chained task: six terminal tool calls, 7 steps. Strictly interleaved, fresh nonce per run, n=3 per mode, all correct.

| | per-call (main) | warm |
|---|---|---|
| wall | 43.2 s | 22.8 s (−47%) |
| per-step latency (steps 2+) | 7.38 s | 2.68 s |
| thinking tokens | 2,305 | 492 (−79%) |
| output tokens | 3,285 | 1,451 (−56%) |
| uncached input | 465 | 14 |
| cache-read share (writes counted) | 95.2% | 95.8% |
| upstream requests per step | 1 | 1 (0 denied) |

- Per-call thinking is about 320–850 tokens on every tool round (#97). Warm thinks once, then 0–60 per step.
- Main's #77/#33 fixes already cut per-call uncached input from 1,354 to 465 tokens since the first version of this PR. The latency, thinking and output gaps did not change.
- In two of the three per-call runs the model batched steps, so those runs had 5–6 steps. Compare totals, not per-step figures. The one 7-step per-call run took 45.3 s against 21.3–25.7 s warm.

**Quality A/B.** A seeded multi-file bug-fix task, graded by its tests plus hidden cases, interleaved, n=3 per mode:
- 3/3 pass in both modes.
- Warm wall: 20.5 s vs 37.0 s (−45%).
- This fixture family needs little thinking in either mode. It shows no loss here; it does not prove quality on reasoning-heavy work.

**Live check on the final head.** The A/B above ran one commit earlier, before warm steps went through main's restoration and breakpoint pinning. On this head:
- **The plugin driven directly against real Claude Code 2.1.286 in warm mode:**
  - A parallel tool round whose results Hermes returned in reverse call order reused the session. Restoration succeeded (no `unrestored`), with 1 upstream request and the correct answer.
  - The next user turn reused the session and read the previous step's cache entry.
  - A history that no longer matched rebuilt by replay (`rebuild:prefix`). The tool round after it reused again.
- **Through `hermes chat`:** the chained task (7 steps, 1 cold then 6 reused) was correct, and a fresh bug-fix seed passed.

**Re-checked on Claude Code 2.1.292** (2026-10-09):
- The direct-plugin live check above, run again on this head, gave the same warm modes (cold, reused, reused, `rebuild:prefix`, reused), no `unrestored`, 1 upstream request per step, and the next turn read the previous step's cache entry.
- Offline, native now also sends `thinking.display: "updates"` and one more line in its injected environment context. The relay passes both through.

**Gateway soak** (before the rebase). One `hermes gateway run` on loopback, with 3 concurrent conversations × 2 tool turns:
- 3/3 correct, one native per conversation, no crosstalk.
- Turn 2 reused its session across gateway turns.
- The idle reaper killed all 3. With pool cap 2, the retained pool never exceeded 2.
- 0 processes left after shutdown.

**Tests.** 28 deterministic warm tests use a fake native and a fake loopback upstream, with no live calls. The fake native appends to every request the per-request context reminder and cache marks that Claude Code 2.1.287+ sends from a fresh process. A real warm native process sends that trailing context only on its first request, including the first one after a rebuild (checked on 2.1.292). They cover:
- the history-selection and lifecycle regressions from review;
- each main change listed above: restoration, breakpoints, refusal, status, tool names, telemetry/proxy/`DO_NOT_TRACK` identity, per-step timeout, and the shared cwd;
- the per-call fallback after a warm failure before admission, in both stream modes, and a native behind a launcher process (as with a Windows venv Python).

The full suite passes locally with 240 tests in both default and warm modes (macOS, Python 3.11, hermes-agent `f42f579`). One upstream test changed by one line: `test_directsdk_telemetry`'s `_base_env` drops the warm flag, because its fake native only speaks the per-call protocol.

**Review.** The change had an independent read-only cross-model review (Codex) over five rounds. Every blocking finding was fixed with a test that failed first and then passed. On this rebase it caught two problems:
- warm steps skipped main's restoration and breakpoint pinning;
- `DO_NOT_TRACK` was missing from the reuse identity.

Its verdict on this head: ready.

Updated 2026-10-06 (`3676d61`): fixes for both findings in andrexibiza's review (the per-call fallback above, and the launcher-safe PID check in the isolation test). Codex re-reviewed the change: no findings.

## Limits
- Experimental and opt-in. Validated on Claude Code 2.1.286 and 2.1.292; the control-protocol details are version-sensitive.
- Needs #123, or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_TERMINAL_TITLE=1`, wherever native's session-title request can turn on (#116). Without it, that request takes a step's admission and the session is rebuilt every turn. With #123 merged in, warm reuse holds (checked offline on 2.1.292).
- Not tested on Fable, Telegram/Desktop end to end, Windows live, or the subscription meter (only API-reported tokens).
- `/steer` and compaction always rebuild.
- Parallel results are anchored in native's call order. If a Claude Code version replays them in another order, restoration skips that frame: it is reported as `unrestored`, Hermes' results still reach the model, and caching falls back to native's own marks.

Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code orchestrating, Codex reviewing). The measurements are from real runs; raw logs are available on request.
