title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): remind Claude to check the skills index on each new user turn
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/89 by @GodsBoy. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

Fixes #90

## Problem

On a Hermes install that switches between this provider and openai-codex, Hermes skills load far less often on Claude. Over 30 days of real sessions on one install:

| Provider | User turns | Turns that load any skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude-subscription-directsdk (Opus 5.5) | 1,795 | 16.2% |
| openai-codex (gpt-6.1-sol) | 5,921 | 50.3% |

The gap is there before any compaction and widens after it. Hermes' prompt says "Before replying, scan the skills below ... you MUST load it with skill_view(name)", and Claude stops acting on it once the index is far behind a long conversation.

## What it is not

- **Not the prompt transport.** The system prompt reaches the wire intact. Captured offline, it is byte-identical to the GPT session's prompt apart from the model-gated tool-use-enforcement block core adds only for GPT-family ids.
- **Not the `mcp__hermes__` tool prefix.** Stripping it on the wire gave the same rate as baseline (16/28 vs 16/28).
- **Not reasoning effort.** See below.

## Fix

When the tool inventory contains `skill_view`, the queried frame of a fresh user turn gets one trailing text block:

```
<system-reminder>Before replying, scan the available skills in your instructions. If one matches or is even partially relevant to this message, load it with skill_view(name) first.</system-reminder>
```

- Tool-result rounds, including steering rows appended after a tool result, are sent unchanged. So is any inventory without `skill_view` (title generation, compression, auxiliary calls).
- It is per-request context, like native's own date and email annotations. Hermes history never contains it, and the caller's messages are not mutated.
- Admission is handed the frame without it, so `pin_message_breakpoint` keeps the cache breakpoint on host content and the next request replays an identical prefix.

## Evidence

**Live A/B, Opus 5.5, real subscription.** I replayed 18 real post-compaction Hermes contexts (60K to 160K tokens, full tool-call history, real system prompt and tools) at real user turns, twice each:

- 10 cut points come from Claude sessions.
- 8 come from GPT sessions where GPT loaded a skill.

| Arm | Skill loaded on first response |
| --- | --- |
| Baseline | 13/36 |
| `effort=high` | 14/36 |
| Reminder | **26/36** |

Paired per replay, the reminder gained 13 turns and lost none (exact McNemar p = 0.0002). By pool:

| Pool | Baseline | Reminder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude-session contexts | 4/20 | 12/20 |
| GPT-session contexts (GPT: 16/16) | 9/16 | 14/16 |

On short contexts the effect is smaller (19 to 23 of 28), which fits the cause: the index loses salience with distance.

**Cache (patched plugin, real subscription).** On a 125K-token post-compaction context, the next tool round read 125,325 of 125,599 prompt tokens from cache (99.8%). The breakpoint stayed on host content in both requests.

## Tests

`tests/test_directsdk_skills_reminder.py` has two invariant tests:

- The reminder reaches native only on a fresh user turn with `skill_view` available, after Hermes' own blocks, and the caller history is not mutated.
- The relay pins the breakpoint on the host block, not the reminder.

Both fail on `main` and pass here. I reproduced the CI job locally (Python 3.14, hermes-agent `main` at 7200e0f5, `python -m pytest -q`): 42 passed, 1 failed. The one failure, `test_directsdk_replay.py`, is the pre-existing #79 (fix in #69); unmodified `main` gives the same failure with 40 passed.

## Update: name skills that compaction pruned

A second commit extends the same reminder. In a real Opus 5.5 session, compaction stubbed a loaded skill and listed another under `## Pruned Skills`. Claude kept drafting for about 90 minutes without reloading either, even with the reminder on every turn, and reloaded them only when the user asked. The generic "scan the skills index" rule does not contradict Claude's belief that the skill is still loaded. Naming the skill does.

On the same fresh user turns, new `pruned_skills.py` reads the frames Claude is about to see in one ordered pass. It finds skills that compaction pruned (core's `[SKILL_PRUNED: ...]` marker, or a main-file `skill_view` result replaced by a compaction stub) and that no later `skill_view` reloaded or reported as missing. When there are any, the reminder gains one sentence:

```
Compaction removed the full text of these previously loaded skills: creative/brand-voice, social-posting. If any still applies to this conversation, reload it with skill_view(name) before replying.
```

- Names match by leaf (`creative/brand-voice`, `plugin:brand-voice` and `brand-voice` are one skill), are deduplicated, capped at the eight most recently pruned plus "and N more", and restricted to a plain name charset so pasted text cannot inject into the reminder. The marker regex gap is bounded, so pasted runs of the prefix stay linear.
- Markers inside other tools' output and `file_path` reference views are ignored. A later prune counts again.
- Gating, placement, history and cache behaviour are unchanged. With nothing pruned, the reminder is byte-identical to the first commit.
- Core's marker and stub helpers are private, so their wording is mirrored rather than imported, and a test feeds core's own output through the parser. A wording change in core fails CI instead of silently disabling detection.

Tests: `tests/test_directsdk_pruned_skills.py` (9 tests) plus 2 end-to-end tests in `tests/test_directsdk_skills_reminder.py`. The two end-to-end tests fail on the first commit and pass on this one. Full suite locally against hermes-agent `main`: 53 passed, 1 failed, the same pre-existing #79 replay failure.

This extension has not had a separate live A/B. It builds on the reminder measured above.

## Follow-up after merge

This changes what reaches the model, so per `AGENTS.md` the catalog pin in `NousResearch/hermes-agent:plugin-catalog/claude-subscription-directsdk.yaml` needs a bump before `hermes plugins update` delivers it.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: opt into host streaming to avoid buffered-call timeouts
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/55 by @rborkow. `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Summary
Opt this streaming-capable process client into Hermes host streaming with `profile.supports_streaming = True`.

**Depends on https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/124566. Draft until that host capability lands.** The host-routing regression test intentionally requires the patched host; it will fail against current unpatched Hermes main. Attribute assignment keeps plugin import compatible with older hosts, which continue their existing non-streaming behavior.

## Why
Hermes currently forces all `external_process` profiles onto the non-streaming path. This client then buffers its native stream until completion, hiding healthy progress from the host stale-call watchdog. A real observed host deadline was 240 seconds. The companion core PR makes streaming an explicit provider capability, while preserving ACP and legacy defaults.

## Verification
- Added host-routing regression: fails without this opt-in on patched Hermes, passes with it.
- Full plugin suite against patched Hermes: **37 passed** on macOS, including existing transport cancellation coverage.
- Companion core focused suite: **62 passed, 4 skipped**.
- Isolated live Opus 5.5 `[1m]` two-call tool round through host dispatch: real fixture read, exact receipt returned, streamed text callbacks, native replay metadata and usage preserved. Short smoke test only; not a four-minute live generation/cancellation proof.
- Independent code review passed after correcting the core dataclass compatibility issue.

## Related proposals / rollout
Checked existing proposals before submitting. #42 detects a genuinely silent upstream; #38 enables summarized thinking display. Neither changes the unconditional host non-streaming gate, so they are complementary rather than replacements.

Merge the core capability first. After this plugin change merges, update the Hermes plugin-catalog pin so catalog-installed users receive it. No production installation was modified by this work.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: request summarized thinking display so reasoning reaches Hermes (4.7+ defaults to omitted)
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk/pull/38 by @mister-ideas. The standalone plugin repo moved into this monorepo, so these are the same commits applied under `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, with authorship kept (Vincent Attali, @100yenadmin). Rebased onto current `main` on 2026-10-23.

Closes #45

## What

Adaptive-thinking requests now send `thinking: {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}` instead of `{"type": "adaptive"}`.

## Why

On Claude 4.7 and later, `thinking.display` defaults to `"omitted"`. Every thinking block comes back as `"thinking": ""` plus a signature, so no `thinking_delta` text streams and Hermes' reasoning panel stays blank for this provider. Hermes core already asks for `"summarized"` for the same reason (`agent/anthropic_adapter.py::_thinking_kwargs`), and the plugin's AGENTS.md asks it to mirror that file on thinking policy.

## Changes

- `directsdk.py` `request_body()`: add `'display': 'summarized'` to the adaptive thinking block.
- `directsdk.py` final message: `reasoning_content` is set only when the turn also has text or a tool call. With summarized display, a thinking-only turn would otherwise reach Hermes as a reasoning-only `stop`, which Hermes promotes to the final answer, ending the tool loop mid-task. Left empty, Hermes' empty-response recovery nudges the model on. The signed thinking still replays through the carrier. Guard designed by @100yenadmin; the early stop was reproduced by @rganz in three of three multi-step runs (#40).
- Tests: the adaptive assertions in `test_directsdk.py`, `test_directsdk_models.py` and `test_directsdk_reasoning_off.py` expect the `display` field; a parametrized test pins it on every pinned adaptive route and its `[1m]` spelling; `test_directsdk_admission.py::test_a_thinking_only_turn_reaches_hermes_without_reasoning` pins the guard (thinking-only turn: no reasoning; turn with text: reasoning kept; signed block still in the carrier).
- `CHANGELOG.md`: Fixed entry.

Haiku 4.5 (no `thinking` block), reasoning-off (`{"type": "disabled"}` or the lowest effort where thinking cannot be disabled) and the effort mapping are unchanged.

## Rebase notes

- `tests/test_directsdk_models.py` conflicted with main's wider Haiku route lists (`haiku-5-5`, `haiku-4.5`, ...): kept main's lists with the new `display` assertion.
- Main's newer `tests/test_directsdk_reasoning_off.py` asserted the bare `{'type': 'adaptive'}`; updated in the first commit.

## Verification

- Red on main: the PR's test files over `main`'s plugin code give 16 failed, 433 passed (the 12 route params, the request-shape contract, the Haiku 5.5 test, the reasoning-off effort test, and the thinking-only guard's no-text case).
- Green on head: full plugin suite, 449 passed + 9 subtests (Python 3.14, hermes-agent `main` installed the way `tests.yml` does).
- Real service (from the original PR and #45): on Claude Code 2.1.305 with `claude-opus-5-5`, effort high, the plugin's current request gets 0 thinking characters and the summarized request gets a readable summary (measured by @shaggy2626; @mstrangeguy confirmed the same on Opus 5.5). Native passes `thinking.display` through `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY`, and the plugin's extra body replaces native's own `display: "updates"` (wire check by @100yenadmin on 2.1.292).

## Follow-up

This changes thinking policy, so the catalog pin in `NousResearch/hermes-agent:plugin-catalog/claude-subscription-directsdk.yaml` has to move after merge before `hermes plugins update` delivers it.

title: Text after a tool result arrives in one burst (the API sends it that way, not the relay)
body:
**What happens**
With Opus 5.5 through this plugin, the assistant text that follows a tool result reaches Hermes
all at once instead of streaming. The same prompt without tool history streams normally.

**Measured** (plugin `31b591f`, Claude Code 2.1.292, macOS, direct `Client.create(stream=True)`;
second call has `tool_use` + `tool_result` in history; timestamps from request start)

| run | text chunks out of `create()` | spread | `text_delta` bytes arriving at the admission relay (`Capture.feed`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| after tool result | 105 | all at 6.9 s | n/a |
| after tool result | 91 | all at 6.2 s | n/a |
| after tool result | 93 | 6.0 to 6.1 s | all in one read at 6.0 s |
| after tool result | 84 | 5.7 to 5.8 s | all in one read at 5.7 s |
| same follow-up, no tool history | 113 | 3.1 to 8.7 s | n/a |
| same follow-up, no tool history | 98 | 1.7 to 6.5 s | 39 distinct reads, 1.6 to 6.5 s |

The relay (`read1` + `flush`) forwards bytes as they come, and the plugin yields every
`text_delta` immediately. When text follows a tool result, the bytes already arrive in one piece
from upstream. So the hold sits in the request Claude Code sends or in the API's handling of it,
not in this plugin's code.

**Why it matters**
Clients that render streamed text (the Hermes WebUI, a native iOS client) see a silent pause
and then a wall of text after every tool call. Most agent turns use tools, so most text arrives
this way.

**Questions**
- Is this known for native Claude Code with replayed tool history (an API-side behaviour,
  a request flag, or Claude Code buffering the request)?
- If it can't be fixed upstream, is it worth documenting, so clients know they need to pace
  text themselves?

Repro script available (stdlib + the plugin, monkeypatches `admission.Capture.feed` for
timestamps only, no plugin changes).

title: Per-profile Claude login: the plugin reads only the process env, so a multiplexed gateway cannot serve two accounts
body:
## Problem

Hermes 0.21.6 serves every profile from a single multiplexed gateway process and refuses a
second gateway on the same host ("Exactly one gateway per host serves every profile", per-user
host lock; the escape hatch is an explicit `gateway run --force`). The plugin resolves the
Claude login from the **process** environment only:

- `directsdk.py:607-609` — `config = env.pop('CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR', None)`;
  `if config: env['CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR'] = config`
- `__init__.py:215` — `env_vars=()`
- `__init__.py::_subscription_token()` — `os.environ.get('CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN', '')`, else
  `read_claude_code_credentials()`, which itself honors `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` from the process env

Hermes never passes a per-profile environment into that plugin:

- `ProviderProfile.create_client(**client_kwargs)` is called without `env=`
  (`agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py::_provider_supplied_client`,
  `agent/auxiliary_client.py::_resolve_external_process_branch`)
- `hermes_cli/auth.py::resolve_external_process_provider_credentials()` returns only
  `{provider, api_key, base_url, command, args, source}` — no env
- `process_command_env_vars` is resolved with `os.getenv` in
  `hermes_cli/auth.py::_external_process_spec()`, i.e. also process-global

Profile `.env` files do not close the gap: a served profile's `.env` is never loaded into the
host gateway process's environment, and `auth.claude_config_dir` (the key a `hermes model`
config surface suggests) is read by nothing in the current tree.

Net effect: every profile served by one gateway runs on whichever login `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
names at process start. Two profiles that must run different Claude subscriptions cannot.

## Measured on a live host (Windows)

- Gateway PID environment: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=C:\Users\<user>\.claude`
- Profile `muaz` is configured for a different login (`auth.claude_config_dir:
  C:/Users/<user>/.claude-muaz`, a separate CLI login for an organizational seat) and
  nevertheless ran every turn on `C:\Users\<user>\.claude` — verified by reading the served
  profile's turn logs (`provider=claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`) and the gateway
  process environment.
- Both logins are valid and logged in; only the selection is impossible.

## Requested change

Add a per-profile setting to `config_schema`, honored on every spawn the way
`claude_code_telemetry` already is (README: "read for the active profile on every spawn"):

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental:
      settings:
        claude_config_dir: C:\Users\<user>\.claude-muaz
```

Precedence: explicit per-profile setting > `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` >
inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` > CLI default.

Because plugin settings are per-profile, this works under a single multiplexed gateway with no
core change. An `optional_env` entry for the same value would also help the `hermes model`
picker and auth paths, which run outside the gateway.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate of NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#43 (account-bound quota-reserve admission) or NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#46 (organizational LLM
  gateway). This is only about *selecting which login / config dir a given profile uses*.
- Core-side, the same "per-profile value unavailable under multiplex" class is tracked for
  terminal scope (`NousResearch/hermes-agent#101659`) and launch-only env keys
  (`NousResearch/hermes-agent#135628`). I am not asking core to pass env here — a per-profile
  plugin setting is the smaller change and keeps the transport's env contract unchanged.
- The alternative today is running the second profile as a `gateway.standalone` process started
  with `--force`, which the host-lock design otherwise discourages.

title: Long healthy calls and real stalls look the same to Hermes: the stale timeout can only limit the whole call
body:
**Setup:** plugin 0.3.3 (`4bc79c7`), Hermes v0.21.6+145 (main `d687605`), Claude Code 2.1.283, `claude-opus-5-5` with adaptive thinking at high effort, Slack + Zulip gateway.

**What happens:** Hermes runs external-process providers without streaming (`agent/turn_api_call.py::_should_stream` returns False for `auth_type: external_process`). The call goes through `_NonStreamRequest`, whose stale check is wall-clock time since the call started (`agent/chat_completion_nonstream.py`, `if elapsed > wd.stale_timeout`). The README already says so: the stale timeout "limits the whole call, not a silence". The plugin itself sees every native stream event and resets its own read-idle timer on them, but none of that reaches Hermes. So one number has to cover both "longest healthy call" and "how long a stall may hold the turn", and those are far apart.

**Our numbers (5 days, about 11,500 calls):**

- Per call: p50 9.5 s, p90 44 s, p99 150 s, max 727 s. 266 calls produced more than 10K output tokens.
- One research thread made three healthy calls of 45-47K output tokens each (almost all thinking, each ending in a tool call) that took 437-509 s. At about 95 tokens/s, a call over about 55K output tokens would pass 600 s.
- Before we set `stale_timeout_seconds`, the implicit 240 s timeout (contexts over 100K) killed one healthy 315K-context call twice in a row, and the turn fell back to another provider, whose replies reached users.
- With `stale_timeout_seconds: 600`, one real stall (no output at 177K context) held the turn for the full 600 s before the kill. The retry on the same model then finished normally in a couple of minutes. The relay's 180 s upstream idle check didn't fire, so presumably bytes (pings) were still arriving.

So the timeout is either short enough to kill healthy long-thinking calls, or long enough that a stall costs the user ten minutes.

**Request:** give Hermes a progress signal it can time silence against. Two ways we can see:

1. The plugin records the time of the last native stream event that shows model progress (`content_block_start`, and deltas of any type: text, thinking, signature, `input_json`), not pings. Hermes's non-stream watchdog reads it the way it already reads Codex event times (`_codex_watchdog_snapshot` and the event-idle kill), and kills on progress silence instead of total time. This probably needs a small core hook.
2. Let this provider stream in core. `Client.create(stream=True)` already yields text and reasoning deltas, and the streaming path already times silence since the last chunk. Tool-call input would need to count as activity too, since many long calls end in a tool call.

One caveat: with `thinking.display` left at its default (`omitted` on these models), a long thinking phase may produce no content events until the signature, so either option works best together with NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#38. Even summarized thinking can arrive in bursts (as noted in NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#125), so a progress-silence timeout would still need to be generous, for example 180-300 s, but that is a lot better than a 600 s+ total cap.

title: Prompt cache: after a tool loop with thinking, the next user turn re-writes the whole conversation once that loop is longer than ~20 blocks
body:
**Setup:** plugin `31b591f`, Claude Code 2.1.283, Hermes gateway (Slack + Zulip) and CLI,
`claude-opus-5-5` (adaptive thinking, `context_management: clear_thinking keep: all`), subscription
login, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h`, shared native cwd in place.

**What happens:** cache entries written by calls *after* a thinking block inside a tool loop are never
read again once the next user turn starts. The next turn's first call falls back to the newest entry
written *before* that turn's first thinking block. When the loop is short, that entry is within the
API's ~20-block lookback, so only the previous turn is re-written. When the loop is longer, nothing is
in range, the read falls back to the tools+system mark, and the whole conversation is written again.

**Capture (one session, Claude Code request bodies captured between native and the relay; the relay's
`restore_queried_turn` + `pin_message_breakpoint` re-run offline on them):**

| Turn | What | First call of the next turn |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15 sequential `echo` tool calls, thinking blocks on calls 7 and 14 | read 9,240 (tools+system only), wrote 1,676 = all of turn 1 |
| 4 | thinking, 1 tool call, answer | read 10,958 = the entry written by turn 4's *first* call; turn 4's second call's entry (11,114) unused |
| 6 | 3 tool calls, **no thinking blocks** | read 11,425 = the entry from turn 6's last call: full hit |

The upstream bodies of the last call of turn 1 and the first call of turn 2 are byte-identical
through the last tool_result (blocks 0–35 of 36/40, the relay had marked block 35), and system, tools
and every top-level field are identical too. The entry at block 35 exists (that call wrote 110 tokens
on top of a 10,804 read), is 1 block behind the new breakpoint, and still misses. So the mismatch is
server-side and starts at the first thinking block of the finished loop. Content can't fix it, but
breakpoint placement can limit it.

**Live gateway impact (6 Oct 13:00 → 8 Oct 00:30, turn-start calls 3–60 min after the previous call,
from `agent.log`):**

| Calls in previous turn | full hit | partial | miss (tools+system only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–3 | 32 | 1 | 0 |
| 4–7 | 33 | 3 | 2 |
| 8–9 | 2 | 5 | 1 |
| 10–11 | 3 | 1 | 7 |
| 12+ | 13 | 4 | 29 |

Typical miss: `in=193K cache=27K write=165K`. About 60% of all cache-write tokens on our gateway
re-write content that was already cached (about 10.7M tokens on 7 Oct, roughly 20% of the day's
usage).

**Suggested fix:** use the spare breakpoint (native uses 2 on system plus the one message mark) to
keep a second message mark on the last cacheable block *before the current turn's first assistant
message that carries a thinking block* (or simply on the turn's opening user frame). That prefix
recurs on the next turn whatever the loop length, so a turn start re-writes at most the previous
turn's loop instead of the whole thread.

Possibly related to NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#38 (different pattern: there, cache_read stops growing within a turn).

title: Login health is invisible to Hermes: call outcomes are never recorded in the credential pool, so a revoked Claude login is only found when agents fail
body:
## Summary

Login health for this provider is invisible to Hermes' normal credential surfaces. Codex, xAI and other pooled providers record each real call's outcome in `auth.json` (`credential_pool` entries with `last_status` / `last_status_at`), so `hermes auth`, dashboards and alerting built on it see a revoked or broken login as soon as an agent hits it. This provider keeps its login in the Claude Code CLI's own `.credentials.json` and never reports call outcomes back to Hermes, so a login that Anthropic has revoked (or a refresh that fails) is only discovered when a user notices an agent failing.

## Environment

- Plugin `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.0 @ `ef73726`
- Hermes v0.21.5, Linux, multi-profile gateway (several profiles share one `~/.claude` login; another host runs a profile with its own `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`)

## What we see

- No `credential_pool` entry or status for this provider ever appears in `auth.json`, so `hermes auth`-style status and anything reading the pool show nothing for Claude profiles.
- The only local signal is the CLI's `.credentials.json` (`claudeAiOauth.expiresAt` / `refreshTokenExpiresAt`). That tells you when a token will expire, not whether Anthropic still accepts it.
- `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` is raised correctly on `authentication_failed` (directsdk.py ~L640), but the failure lives only in that request's error. Nothing persists it, and an idle profile never raises it at all.

## Current workaround

We run an external probe every 6 hours that makes one tiny real call per distinct login file through Hermes (`hermes -p <profile> chat -q "Reply with exactly OK" --oneshot ...`) and alert on failure. It works, but it spends subscription usage, has to group profiles by login file so they don't race the same refresh token, and lives outside Hermes.

## Proposed fix

Record the outcome of every real call where Hermes already looks for credential health:

1. After each request, mark this provider's credential **ok** on a successful upstream response, and **dead/needs re-login** on `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` or an upstream 401/403 that is an auth failure (not 429/5xx, which should stay transient as today).
2. Key the status by the resolved config dir (`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` → `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` → `~/.claude`), not by profile, so profiles sharing one login share one status. Store status and timestamp only, never token material.
3. Optionally, expose the offline `claude auth status` result from `directsdk_setup.py` as the initial status, so a missing login shows before the first call.

If the plugin API has no supported way for an `external_process` provider to write pool status, that hook is probably needed in hermes-agent first; happy to open the matching issue there if you'd rather track it in core.

## Why it matters

On unattended gateways (Basecamp/Telegram agents, cron jobs) a revoked Claude login currently shows up as silent agent failures. With the status recorded, existing `hermes auth` output and any monitoring on `auth.json` would catch it the same way they already do for every other provider, and external probes become unnecessary.

title: Prompt cache: native rewrites its injected messages[1] system reminder between request 1 and 2, so cache_read freezes at the first mark (hermes-agent#133866)
body:
Mirror of NousResearch/hermes-agent#133866 (P0 there). Summary and the full triage with receipts: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/133866#issuecomment-6019120619

## Symptom (reporter, Hermes `781334ee`, plugin `31b591f`, Claude Code 2.1.291-era, Sonnet 5 [1m], subscription)

One user turn, 20 tool rounds: `cache_read` freezes at exactly what request 1 marked (26,692 tokens) from call NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#2 onward; `in` and `cache_creation` grow every call; by call NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#20 the request re-writes 97k tokens. Same in an unrelated session (freeze at 25,175). Older sessions reach 250–365k tokens/request.

## What the wire shows (offline, real CLI 2.1.291, plugin head `31b591f`, the plugin's own loopback peer)

`pin_message_breakpoint` does its job: the message breakpoint advances every round ((0,0) → (3,0) → (5,0) → (7,0)) and the bytes through the previous breakpoint replay identically; `system` and `tools` are stable. `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` passes 6/6.

What the relay cannot see: between request 1 and request 2 native rewrites its own injected `role: system` message at `messages[1]`:

```
req1 messages[1].content == [{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder># Environment…</system-reminder>\n\n<system-reminder>You are powered by…</system-reminder>\n\n<system-reminder>Today's date is …</system-reminder>"}]
req2 messages[1].content == "<system-reminder># Environment…</system-reminder>\n\n<system-reminder>You are powered by…</system-reminder>"   # plain string
req2 messages[-1]       == {"role":"system","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<system-reminder>Today's date is …</system-reminder>"}]}
```

`req1[1].text == req2[1] + "\n\n" + req2[-1].text` → True. Same words, different block shape and position. `messages[1]` sits after request 1's breakpoint (`messages[0]`), so the "span through the last assistant replays byte-identical" check is satisfied while an earlier message is still edited.

## Why this would freeze `cache_read` at request 1's mark

Anthropic's preserved-thinking rules bind each thinking block to the whole prefix before it (`system`, `tools`, every earlier message). "Edit … any earlier `system` message" is **Invalid for every later thinking block**; where enforced the API drops that block and every later one, and "the cached prefix changes from that block's position onward on that request" (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#what-counts-as-an-edit and the "Dropped thinking blocks" row of https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#what-invalidates-the-cache). The first thinking block is in `messages[2]`, immediately after the edited message, so from request 2 on only `tools + system + messages[0]` reads from cache. `admission.py` already records this signature without a cause ("measured no cache hit even though they replay byte-identical (#33, cause unknown)").

Not proven live: I have no subscription on this host. The docs scope the binding check to Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 and newer accounts; the reporter is on Sonnet 5. Confirmation: relay one two-round turn with `anthropic-beta: thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` + `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block"` and look for `input_transformations[].reason == "prefix_binding_mismatch"` on request 2. Either way the `messages[1]` rewrite is a prefix change and worth removing.

Related: NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#77 fixed the request-1-only account-email block in `messages[0]` by reordering; the `messages[1]` rewrite is the same class one message later. NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#40's "thinking never reaches the model" has the same mechanism as a candidate (dropped blocks are what the recall test observed).

## Fix direction

- `admission.py`: make native's injected `role: system` context byte-stable across requests (split request 1's combined block into the request-2 shape, or strip the volatile reminders on every request, identically every time).
- Add the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta with `drop_block` in the relay and surface `input_transformations` through `native_admission` so a prefix edit is visible in `agent.log` instead of a silent miss.
- `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py`: assert every shared message (not only the span through the previous breakpoint) is identical between consecutive requests; today's eval is green on the broken shape.

Repro script (loopback, no credentials): run the plugin's `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` harness with a history of one user turn + tool rounds and compare `wires[0]["messages"][1]` with `wires[1]["messages"][1]`.

title: Native session-title side request can take the single admission: first reply arrives as {"title": ...}
body:
## Summary

On a fresh conversation, the user-facing reply is sometimes replaced by a session-title JSON object such as `{"title": "Greek language response assistance"}`. The reply is short (about 13–19 output tokens), uses no tools and ends with `finish_reason=stop`. Hermes stores it as a real assistant message. In our case it went out to Telegram as the answer.

## Environment

- Plugin: `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` at `31b591f` (catalog install, 2026-10-05)
- Claude Code (native): 2.1.284
- Hermes Agent 0.21.5 (gateway, Telegram platform), Linux
- Model: `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`

## What we observed

- It happens only on the first user turn of a session, and most often with short messages ("axiom άλλαξε φωνή", "axiom καλημέρα").
- `/new` does not prevent it, because the very first turn of a new session is the one affected.
- The same prompt through `hermes chat -q` was not affected in our runs before the workaround. This may just be timing.
- Hermes' own title generator is not involved. `auxiliary.title_generation` is routed to a different provider, and Hermes stored a separate, correct session title at the same time.

## Likely cause

Native Claude Code sends its own session-title side request when the first user frame arrives. In the 2.1.284 bundle this is `generateSessionTitle` / `querySource: "generate_session_title"`, sent with `outputFormat: json_schema {title: string}`, no tools. It is triggered from the first user frame when `shouldQuery !== false`. The same process also sends the real turn request.

The admission relay accepts exactly one upstream request per Hermes call (`gate.used`). Whichever request reaches `/v1/messages` first takes the admission. When the title request wins, the relay captures the title response as the turn's assistant message. Native's real turn is then denied with `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED` and treated as handled.

We have not proven which request arrives first in each case. The symptom pattern fits this race: short title-shaped output, first turn only, no tool calls.

## Local workaround (verified)

In `Handler.do_POST`, before taking the admission, we read the body. If it is a native title request (no `tools`, `output_config.format.type == "json_schema"` and the schema `properties` is exactly `{title}`), we answer 400 without setting `gate.used`. The body is then reused for the real request. Native ignores the failed title call, because `generateSessionTitle` catches the error and returns null.

After the change, each new session logged one refused title request, and the real reply came through normally on Telegram and CLI.

A cleaner upstream fix may be to stop native from sending the title request at all for `-p` stream-json sessions (if a setting or env var exists for that), or to have the relay recognise and drop side requests in general rather than only this one shape.

Happy to share the diff if useful.

title: Reasoning from earlier tool rounds does not reach the model: each round re-derives its analysis, about 10× the thinking tokens of a native Claude Code session
body:
## Summary

In a multi-step tool loop through the plugin, the model's thinking from one round is not part of its context in the next round. The thinking blocks are stored by Hermes and replayed by the plugin, and they are present in the request the admission relay forwards, but the next request's input grows only by the visible tool call and result. A continuous native `claude -p` session on the same task grows by the full thinking. The visible effect is that every round re-derives its analysis: on a long agentic task with `effort: xhigh`, rounds of 10,000 to 49,000 thinking tokens (3 to 8 minutes each) where a native session thinks about 1,000 tokens per round.

## Environment

- Plugin `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.0, Hermes Agent v0.21.5 (upstream `c8301ea6`), Claude Code CLI 2.1.288, Linux.
- Model `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`, `agent.reasoning_effort: xhigh` (lower efforts not measured).
- Kanban worker sessions over an SSH terminal backend; nothing else unusual.

## Evidence

**1. A/B on one four-step task** (step 2 asks for a hand factorisation of two numbers before the next tool call, so it needs real thinking; steps 1, 3, 4 are `echo` calls):

| | output of the thinking round | input growth to the next round |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes + plugin | 2,139 tokens | +156 tokens |
| `claude -p ... --effort xhigh --allowedTools Bash` (one session) | (in the run's 2,661 thinking tokens) | +2,809 tokens |

Through the plugin, the two trivial `echo` rounds after the thinking round produced 839 and 815 output tokens each.

**2. Replay is happening.** With summary-only logging added to a copy of the plugin:

- `prepare_history()`: every assistant message has a carrier, `projection(message) == expected` is true for all of them, and the native blocks (including one `thinking` block each) are restored.
- `admission.pin_message_breakpoint()`: the outgoing body carries those thinking blocks in the earlier assistant messages (`[0, 1, 1]` thinking blocks for the three replayed assistant messages), `context_management.edits = [{"type": "clear_thinking_20251015", "keep": "all"}]`, `thinking = {"type": "adaptive"}`, `output_config.effort = "xhigh"`.
- The stored thinking blocks have `"thinking": ""` and only a signature (display defaults to omitted, see NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#45).

**3. A real long run** (53 model calls, 61 tool calls): tool time 11 s in total, model time 94 min.
27 calls took 96 % of it at about 20,600 output tokens each (531,541 of 546,872 output tokens were reasoning), at a steady ~103 tokens/s. After a call with 27,470 output tokens, the next input grew by 833 tokens. For comparison, a native Claude Code session on the same model and effort averaged 1,013 output tokens over 1,184 calls (none above 14,000), and its input grew by about the output after
long calls.

## What I think is going on

The thinking is replayed, but the model does not get it back as context: either the server treats the replayed assistant messages as earlier turns and drops their thinking despite `keep: all`, or something in how the native CLI ingests stream-json history changes how those blocks are treated. A long-lived native process per Hermes session (as suggested in NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#42) would avoid the replay altogether.

## Reproduction

The four-step prompt from evidence 1, once through a Hermes profile on this plugin (`hermes -p <profile> chat -q "<prompt>"`, compare `in=` of consecutive "API call #" lines in `agent.log`) and once through `claude -p "<prompt>" --model 'opus[1m]' --effort xhigh --allowedTools Bash --output-format stream-json --verbose` (compare the input usage of consecutive assistant messages).

title: Claude loads Hermes skills far less often than other providers, worst after compaction
body:
### Summary

With this provider, Claude loads Hermes skills far less often than other providers on the same install, with the same system prompt and the same skills. It gets worse deep into a session and after compaction.

### Evidence

30 days of real sessions on one Hermes install (Telegram, WhatsApp, CLI):

| Provider | User turns | Turns that load any skill |
| --- | --- | --- |
| claude-subscription-directsdk (Opus 5.5) | 1,795 | 16.2% |
| openai-codex (gpt-6.1-sol) | 5,921 | 50.3% |

I replayed 18 real post-compaction contexts (60K to 160K tokens) at real user turns on Opus 5.5 through this plugin. Claude loaded a skill on 13 of 36 turns. Raising reasoning effort to high gave 14 of 36. Where GPT had loaded a skill at that exact point (16 of 16), Claude managed 9 of 16.

### Ruled out

- The system prompt reaches the wire intact, with the same skills index and the same "MUST load it with skill_view(name)" rule as on GPT.
- The `mcp__hermes__` tool prefix: stripping it on the wire left the rate unchanged.
- Reasoning effort (above).

### Cause

The skills rule sits at the top of a long system prompt. Deep into a conversation, Claude stops acting on it unless it is restated near the turn being answered.

### Environment

- Claude Code 2.1.287, plugin `main` at ef73726, Hermes main, Linux.

Fix with the full A/B and cache verification: NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#89

title: Per-request claude.exe spawn adds ~2-4 s fixed latency to every API call (Windows)
body:
## Summary

Every API call made through the DirectSDK provider spawns a fresh native `claude` process (plus the inert MCP helper and a loopback relay). On Windows this adds a fixed ~2–4 s (regression estimate ~4.6 s) per call, independent of prompt size or cache state. With several calls per agent turn, this dominates end-to-end latency.

## Environment

- Windows 11, measured 2026-09-30
- Microsoft Defender real-time protection **disabled** during measurement (so this is not AV scanning overhead)
- `claude.exe` from `@anthropic-ai/claude-code/bin/claude.exe` (~242 MB binary)

## Observations

1. `directsdk.py` (around line 548) spawns a new process per request:
   `claude -p --max-turns 1 --no-session-persistence ...`
   together with `inert_mcp.py` (a Python process, ~0.6 s startup on its own) and a loopback relay — on **every** API call.
2. `claude.exe --version` alone takes **2.1–4.0 s** on this machine, i.e. the bare process startup cost before any request work.
3. Linear regression over **742 calls** from `agent.log`:
   - fixed overhead ≈ **4.6 s per call**
   - ≈ **22.7 ms per output token**
4. Calls per agent turn: median **4**, p75 **12** → roughly **12–50 s of pure startup overhead per agentic turn**.
5. Prompt cache hit rate is ~**99%**, so the overhead is not prompt processing — it is process spawn/initialization.

## Request

Please consider a persistent / warm mode, e.g.:

- **Long-lived native process**: keep one `claude` process alive using stream-json input with multiple turns, resetting conversation context per request; or
- **Pool of pre-spawned processes**: spawn the next worker in the background while the current request runs, so the startup cost is off the critical path.

Alternatively / additionally:

- Allow **skipping the MCP relay / `inert_mcp.py`** when no MCP tools are needed for a request, which would remove at least the Python helper startup (~0.6 s) and the relay setup.

Happy to provide more timing data or test a branch.

title: Feature proposal: opt-in account-bound quota-reserve admission and usage receipts
body:
## Problem / maintainer decision requested

A Claude subscription may be shared between manual use and several autonomous Hermes processes. A user can want automation to stop before exhausting either the five-hour or weekly allowance, without disabling the account entirely.

Would you prefer this as **opt-in configurable per-account admission policy in the plugin**, or as **supported admission/completion hooks so an external policy/pool plugin can implement it without patching `directsdk.py`**? The second option may keep the transport smaller. If an existing supported composition already covers the full lifecycle, guidance on that would be preferable to adding a redundant API.

This is a feature/design request, not a report that the plugin's cache repair is missing. It does not require a change to native authentication, entitlement enforcement, upstream destination, model routing, or default behavior for users who do not opt in.

## Behavior to support

- Configurable cutoffs for the selected account's five-hour and weekly meters, plus applicable model-specific limits. Each window independently blocks admission; one resetting cannot override another still-blocking window.
- In strict reserve mode, missing, stale, malformed, throttled, or otherwise unverifiable required usage means **no admission for that account**, not zero utilization. A validated inactive window is distinct from missing data. Observation freshness and rate-limit/backoff behavior need an explicit contract; uncontrolled metadata polling can itself cause throttling.
- Evaluate at the actual inference boundary and bind the decision to the identity native will use. Creating two deferred streams must not let a later selection change the first one's account. `Client(env=...)` and the existing provider factory should be considered before introducing a new identity API. We found the mutable-selection race in an external pool wrapper, not in an upstream pool implementation.
- Coordinate concurrent automation sharing an account across processes. Any lease must cover check → dispatch → stream completion/cancellation and the native child's lifetime, rather than end when a lazy generator is constructed or its parent dies. Cross-platform behavior must be explicit.
- Return a typed, non-authentication policy refusal so the host can stop/wait or choose an already-authorized alternative. Do not retire valid credentials, silently authorize a paid fallback, or replay an inference already dispatched because cleanup failed.
- Provide optional, secret-free admission/completion receipts using an opaque account label and request ID, with cache-read/write/input/output usage and terminal outcome. Canceled or crashed calls without complete usage must remain unknown/unfinalized—not disappear or count as zero.

An extension contract would need to establish who owns the account binding, when a lease is acquired/released, and what happens if policy evaluation or receipt delivery fails. It must preserve the existing one-upstream-request-per-host-call, replay/cache, streaming and cancellation invariants. Existing single-request HTTP admission and quota-policy admission are different concerns; the proposal should not weaken the former.

## Scope and limits

This is **headroom-oriented admission**, not a guaranteed reservation of an exact percentage: provider accounting can lag, next-request cost is opaque, and manual activity can happen concurrently. Token counts or API list-price equivalents cannot establish subscription utilization.

The initial scope would be requests routed through this provider, including main/auxiliary, sync/async and streaming paths. It should not be advertised as controlling unrelated native CLI invocations, other hosts, or deliberate credential/raw-binary bypasses. Broader coverage would need its own explicit integration.

We have a local implementation exercising these concerns, but it contains deployment-specific policy and OS-specific process/locking assumptions; it is not proposed as an upstream-ready code dump. Account identities, machine paths, chosen cutoffs, deployment wrappers and local operational procedures would stay outside a generic contribution. No credentials or prompt bodies should be passed into telemetry callbacks. Native remains responsible for credential refresh; a successful refresh is not a quota decision.

## Suggested qualification for a follow-up PR

Synthetic, secret-free regressions for independent window cutoffs, legitimate inactive windows, unknown/throttled telemetry, immutable identity under interleaved deferred streams, cross-process exclusion, parent-only death, immediate group cancellation, and successful native completion with a lingering child. Include reporting of interrupted/unmeasured attempts and prove unchanged default behavior, replay/cache preservation, and one upstream request per host call.

Happy to contribute a narrow implementation after the preferred boundary is agreed. The intent is to reduce downstream patching, not add an account-management framework to this transport. Any eventual admission change would also need the catalog-pin/release follow-through described in `AGENTS.md`.

title: ClaudeCodeLoggedOut fires with correct env, empty native stderr, and sub-1.5s failure — only inside a real Hermes gateway process, never in any standalone reproduction
body:
## Summary

We hit persistent `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` failures (the error added in NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#23) when running this
provider as primary/fallback inside a real, long-running Hermes gateway process (launchd-supervised
on macOS, messaging surface, cron ticking multiple profiles). Every standalone reproduction we
built — bare CLI, exact production CLI flags, this plugin's own `Client` class directly, concurrent
calls, calls under artificial heavy system load, calls with a full-size system prompt + 34-tool
manifest, and the async `_acreate`/`asyncio.to_thread` dispatch path with a saturated shared
executor — succeeded cleanly every time. The failure only ever reproduces inside the actual gateway
process, and we've been unable to find what's different about it after an extensive investigation.

This may be the same underlying issue as NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#47 or NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#17 (gateway/bot-surface class of bugs), but neither
report's enumerated causes match what we found, so filing separately with the new evidence in case
it helps narrow things down.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: updated `c4a5deef` → `59004a62` same session (~11.4k commits, well past
  `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.4"`)
- Plugin: `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`, installed via `hermes plugins install
  claude-subscription-directsdk` (pinned catalog SHA)
- Claude Code CLI: current as of 2026-09-26 (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`)
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon), gateway run as a `launchd` LaunchAgent
  (`RLIMIT_NOFILE` soft-capped at 4096 via the plist, `LimitLoadToSessionType: Aqua, Background`)
- Auth: isolated `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at a separate, dedicated
  `claude auth login` session directory (Claude Team plan seat), kept apart from any other login on
  the machine. Baked directly into the launchd plist's `EnvironmentVariables` so it can't be dropped
  by any config-reload path.
- The org's own `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`-presence conflict (this plugin's own guard) was hit and fixed
  separately by scrubbing that key from this one provider's env before the check — unrelated to
  this report, mentioning only so it's not mistaken for the same issue.

## Symptom

```
error_type=ClaudeCodeLoggedOut ... summary=Claude Code is installed but has no usable login in the
environment Hermes runs it in. Run `claude auth login` as the user Hermes runs as, set
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (from `claude setup-token`) in Hermes' environment, or point
CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR at a logged-in config directory, then try again.
(native: Not logged in · Please run /login)
```

Fires on the first attempt of essentially every real turn through the live gateway, retries 3x
(all fail identically), then correctly falls back to the configured fallback provider. Service
continuity is preserved by the fallback, but the primary model is effectively unusable.

## What we ruled out, with real tests, not just plausible reasoning

1. **`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` conflict** (this plugin's own conflict-check, `directsdk.py` ~line 470) —
   real, and unrelated to this report; we scrub the 4 conflicting `ANTHROPIC_*` vars from this one
   provider's env dict before the check, in our own patch. Not the cause of the symptom below.
2. **Env-var delivery** — added temporary instrumentation directly in `Client._run` logging
   `HOME`/`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` at the exact moment of the call. Confirmed
   correct on 3/3 live failures. Later expanded to a full `os.environ` diff (190 keys in the real
   gateway vs. 17–50 in every standalone test, including a maximally clean `env -i` shell) —
   nothing suspicious found; all plugin-relevant vars correct every time.
3. **Concurrent multi-process access to the shared config dir** — ran up to 8 concurrent real
   calls through the actual `Client` class (real admission relay, real per-request loopback ports,
   same shared config dir) — all succeeded. Also tried 2 concurrent calls sharing **one** `Client`
   instance (same cached working directory via `_workdir()`) — also succeeded.
4. **The admission relay mechanism itself** — single and concurrent calls through the real relay
   succeed; ruled out as a variable on its own.
5. **System/CPU load** — the gateway machine ran `loadavg_1m` 9–13 during real failures. Ran the
   same standalone reproduction under artificial load up to `loadavg_1m 10.47` (matching/exceeding
   the real conditions) — still succeeded, 8/8.
6. **Request size/complexity** — every earlier test used a trivial single short message with no
   tools. Rebuilt a full-size request (~15KB synthetic system prompt, 34 tool schemas matching the
   real gateway's tool count, 5-turn conversation history) — single and concurrent, under load —
   still succeeded.
7. **The async dispatch path** — `create()` branches on `asyncio.get_running_loop()`; every test
   above had used the *synchronous* branch. Rebuilt the test using the real `_acreate`/
   `asyncio.to_thread` path, deliberately saturating the default shared thread-pool executor with
   40 unrelated blocking tasks first — still succeeded, 4/4.

## What we found instead, live, in the real gateway (never reproducible standalone)

- **Native's stderr is completely empty on every failure** (0 lines captured, via temporary
  `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` + a drain thread added directly in `Client._run`). There is no hidden
  diagnostic text anywhere in the process we spawn.
- **Every failure completes in well under 1.5 seconds** (0.48–0.70s observed across 3 real
  failures), consistent with `admission.used == False` — i.e. native fails via what looks like a
  purely local check before attempting any network or relay contact at all. This is far faster
  than any real network round-trip we saw in a successful call (typically 1–7s).
- Two calls in the same real burst (main response + an auxiliary call) started only **~10ms
  apart** — tighter than anything our own thread-pool-based concurrency tests produced, though
  a shared-Client-instance variant with similar timing still didn't reproduce it standalone.

## Existing issues checked first

Searched all 49 issues/PRs (open and closed) before filing. Closest related, neither an exact
match:

- **#16** (provider profile unavailable on bot/gateway surface) and **#17**/**#23** (the
  `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` error class itself) — same general "works on desktop/CLI, fails on
  gateway/bot surface" shape, but NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#17's own root-cause enumeration (different user/HOME/config
  dir) doesn't hold here — we confirmed all three correct, live, repeatedly.
- **#43** (per-client native cwd deleted by Hermes' 24h scratch prune, long-lived clients fail
  with ENOENT) — same *class* of bug (a long-running gateway misbehaving in a way no fresh
  standalone script reproduces, surfacing as a misleading auth-shaped error). Doesn't fit here:
  it requires a client older than ~24h with an idle, pruned scratch dir; every one of our
  failures happened within minutes of a fresh gateway restart, and our credentials live in a
  separate, non-pruned directory (`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR`), not the ephemeral
  per-client cwd.

## Question for maintainers

Given native fails near-instantly with zero stderr output and `admission.used == False`, is there
a known **local-only** precondition Claude Code checks before ever reaching for the network (e.g.
credentials file staleness/format, a lock/session marker in the config dir, a timestamp-based
"last verified" cache) that could plausibly behave differently on a first real invocation inside a
freshly-spawned, launchd-supervised process versus a manually-invoked shell — something that isn't
env, isn't concurrency, isn't load, and isn't request shape? We're out of angles we can test without
attaching a debugger/strace to native's own process during a live failure, which is why we're
filing this now rather than continuing to guess.

Happy to run further tests against a specific hypothesis if one exists — we have the isolated repro
environment already set up and can reproduce the live-gateway conditions on request.

title: Thinking is never shown on Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Fable: adaptive requests omit `thinking.display`, so every thinking block arrives empty
body:
## Summary

`request_body()` enables adaptive thinking with `{"type": "adaptive"}` and no `display` field. On Claude 4.7+ models `thinking.display` defaults to `"omitted"`, so the API returns thinking blocks with `"thinking": ""` and only a signature. No `thinking_delta` text is ever streamed, `reasoning_content` stays empty, and the Hermes reasoning panel (desktop, TUI, CLI with `display.show_reasoning: true`) never shows anything for this provider.

Hermes core already handles this in `agent/anthropic_adapter.py::_thinking_kwargs`:

```python
return {"thinking": {"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"}, "output_config": {"effort": adaptive_effort}}
```

Its docstring says: *"On 4.7+ `thinking.display` defaults to "omitted", hiding the reasoning Hermes shows in its CLI, so "summarized" is requested to keep the activity feed populated."* The plugin doesn't do the same, which goes against the AGENTS.md rule to mirror `anthropic_adapter.py` on thinking policy.

## Evidence

- Plugin at `602393b` (current main), Hermes desktop, `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`, `agent.reasoning_effort: medium`, `display.show_reasoning: true`.
- In `state.db`, 15 of 17 DirectSDK assistant messages carry `reasoning_details[].messages[].content[] = {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": "…"}`, and all 17 have empty `reasoning_content`.
- With `'display': 'summarized'` added (see linked PR), a direct `directsdk.Client().chat.completions.create(model='claude-opus-5-5[1m]', stream=True, extra_body={'reasoning': {'enabled': True, 'effort': 'medium'}})` streams `reasoning_content`: `"391 factors as 17 times 23, confirming it's composite."`. So native forwards `thinking.display` from `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY` to the API. This is unlike `output_config.effort` (#34).

## Expected

Thinking summaries stream as `reasoning_content` and appear in the Hermes reasoning panel, as they do with the core `anthropic` provider.

## Scope

- Only the adaptive branch changes. Haiku 4.5 (`NO_ADAPTIVE_THINKING`) still sends no `thinking` block, and disable or `effort: none` still sends `{"type": "disabled"}`.
- Signed-thinking replay isn't affected: the signature is unchanged, and summarized text is what the API expects to be echoed back.
- This is separate from NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#34/#35 (effort) and NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#22 (Opus 5.5 disable).

title: Support subscription-authenticated Claude Code through an organizational LLM gateway
body:
## Deployment use case

We have a real internal deployment that needs this capability.

Our organization routes model traffic through an internal gateway ("Seatbelt") used for access control, user attribution, observability, and policy enforcement. The gateway is authenticated independently with organization-specific headers, currently a TrueFoundry token plus a Maat identity token.

For the Claude subscription path, the intended architecture is:

Hermes
  -> Claude Subscription DirectSDK
  -> official claude -p
  -> DirectSDK request-scoped Admission relay
  -> organizational gateway (Seatbelt)
  -> Anthropic

The gateway is intended to be transparent to Claude authentication:

- the user logs into the official Claude CLI with their own subscription seat;
- the native `Authorization` bearer and Claude identity/capability headers emitted by `claude -p` are preserved unchanged;
- the gateway does not synthesize Claude Code identity;
- the gateway does not replace or rotate the OAuth bearer with pooled subscription credentials;
- gateway authentication and user attribution are carried separately via headers such as `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`.

This is specifically intended to use Anthropic's documented subscription-through-gateway model.

## Current blocker

DirectSDK correctly rejects inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, but then its Admission relay necessarily uses `https://api.anthropic.com` as its upstream.

We do not want to weaken the generic `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` guard, since an accidentally inherited value could redirect native OAuth credentials to an unintended endpoint.

## Proposed shape

PR NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#18 adds an explicit opt-in:

`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_UPSTREAM=https://seatbelt.example.internal`

while leaving the existing generic auth/backend override guard intact.

Gateway-specific authentication can remain separate, e.g. through `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`.

The Admission relay already supports an arbitrary HTTPS upstream internally, so the missing capability is simply a supported way for the normal provider path to select a trusted organizational gateway explicitly.

Related: NousResearch/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#18

title: external_process provider profile unavailable on bot/gateway surface → "(none configured)" agent_init_failed (works on desktop)
body:
## Summary

The `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` provider works correctly for **desktop / interactive** sessions but fails at agent init for **bots** (the `tui_gateway` / messaging surface) with:

```
Could not find the 'claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental' CLI command '(none configured)'. Install it.
(layer: runtime, code: agent_init_failed, retryable: true)
```

`claude` **is** installed and authenticated — the same subscription drives desktop sessions fine, and `claude -p "..."` returns output normally. So this is not a missing binary or a login problem; it's the provider **profile** not being available on the bot surface.

## Environment

- Hermes: **0.21.4** (the plugin's minimum `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.4"`)
- Plugin: **claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental 0.3.0**
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon); `terminal.backend: docker` sandbox
- Claude Code CLI: 2.1.x on host, logged in via `claude auth login` (file-based `.credentials.json`)
- `plugins.enabled` includes the provider; it is the default model.

## Diagnosis

Traced to provider-profile resolution in `hermes_cli/auth.py::_external_process_spec`:

```py
from providers import get_provider_profile as _get_provider_profile
profile = _get_provider_profile(pconfig.id)   # returns None on the bot surface
...
command_env_vars = tuple(getattr(profile, "process_command_env_vars", ()) or ())
command = (next((v for v in (os.getenv(var, "").strip() for var in command_env_vars) if v), "")
           or str(getattr(profile, "process_command", "") or ""))
return command, args, base_url, shutil.which(command) if command else None, command_env_vars
```

When `profile is None`:
- `command_env_vars` -> `()`
- `command` -> `""`
- `resolve_external_process_provider_credentials` then raises with `command='(none configured)'` **and no env-var hint**.

The absence of the `" or set CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND"` hint in the user-facing message is the tell: it proves `command_env_vars == ()`, i.e. the **profile object itself is missing**, not merely the binary. If the profile were present, `process_command='claude'` (from the plugin's `__init__.py`) would make `command` non-empty and the message would read `'claude'`, not `'(none configured)'`.

The plugin registers its profile at **import time** (`register_provider(profile)` in `__init__.py`, with `process_command='claude'`, `process_command_env_vars=('CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND',)`).

- **Desktop surface:** plugin discovery runs — logs show `hermes_cli.plugins: Plugin discovery complete: N found, M enabled` and later `run_agent: ... client created from provider profile` for this provider. Profile resolves, sessions work.
- **Bot / `tui_gateway` surface:** the provider registry is not populated when `get_provider_profile` runs during agent build, so it returns `None`.

This lines up with the note already in `hermes_cli/plugins.py`:

> Ensures plugins are discovered on first invocation so callers in processes that never explicitly call `discover_plugins()` (gateway platform events, TUI slash workers, query mode, cron) still fire callbacks registered by user plugins (tracking #64178).

The **hook/middleware** delivery path was hardened for this (via `_delivery_manager()`), but **external_process provider-profile lookup** on the credential path appears to have the same discovery gap.

## Reproduction

1. Enable `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` (`plugins.enabled`), set it as the default model. Install + log in to Claude Code.
2. Open a normal **desktop session** -> works, streams, tools run.
3. Create a **bot** (BOTS tab) using the same provider -> send any message.
4. Result: `agent_init_failed` with `... CLI command '(none configured)'` on every attempt.

Note: **Retry does not rebuild the agent** — `tui_gateway/prompt_turn.py` re-emits the cached `session["agent_error"]`, so the same frame repeats without a fresh provider-resolution attempt.

## Expected

Bot / gateway / cron agent builds should resolve provider profiles from enabled plugins the same way desktop sessions do — i.e. ensure the plugin registry is populated (join/await `discover_plugins()`) before `get_provider_profile` is called on the `external_process` credential path.

## Workarounds verified

- Desktop / normal sessions work fine on the subscription provider.
- Setting `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` (absolute `claude` path) and `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` (file-based creds dir) fixes desktop, but **not** bots — the bot path fails earlier, at profile lookup, before command/env resolution is ever reached.

title: [memory-wiki] fix: prioritize user topics over tool and system noise
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-memory-wiki/pull/3 by @tillstriegel. `hermes-memory-wiki` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `memory-wiki/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Summary
Prioritize what the user actually discussed over execution noise in Memory Wiki topics.

- Derive subjects from every user turn, with session titles as secondary evidence and an intentional title-only fallback. Exclude unverified previews, tool/system/developer text and tool-call metadata from topic creation/scoring.
- Preserve explicitly discussed identifiers (including snake_case/dotted tool names), packages, commands, paths and plain-language phrases. Read text blocks from structured message content without interpreting image payloads or metadata as prose.
- Rank user-supported topics first across subjects and daily logs; machine repetition cannot create topics or boost scores/order. Message counts remain factual activity metadata.
- Prefer user snippets. Assistant text can provide matching context for existing topics, not introduce new ones. Filter noisy daily work items and deduplicate repeated assistant support.

## Verification
- Baseline: 21 tests passed.
- Final: 38 tests passed with `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=<hermes-agent-checkout> <hermes-python> -m pytest tests/ -o 'addopts=' -q`.
- Synthetic SQLite SessionDB + FastAPI coverage for overview, subjects/query/detail, days/day detail and read-only database guarantees; noisy-role/repetition, later user turns, explicit tool names, empty/title-only sessions, ranking limits, multimodal text and empty/punctuation-only assistant regressions.
- `npm run check` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Independent defect-first exact-diff review; findings repaired and regression-tested before publication.

## Checks / CI state
- This repository has **no CI configured**: `GET /repos/NousResearch/hermes-memory-wiki/actions/workflows` returns zero workflows, and the exact head below reports zero check runs and zero commit statuses (`statusCheckRollup: []`). There is no upstream check for this head that is passing, failing or pending — none exists, and none is claimed here. Required-check/branch-protection state could not be read with the available token (the branch-protection endpoint returns 404 for a non-admin collaborator), so it is reported as unverified rather than absent.
- All verification for this exact head is local, reproduced by the commands in the `Development` section of `README.md` at head `9ae86a3d8005688e0c299b0e28f655e760d68f64`: 38 passed, `npm run check` clean, `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` clean, working tree clean.

## Scope and limitations
Backend relevance, tests and documentation only. No cache/loading/UI changes; independent of the separate performance PR and based directly on upstream `main` (single commit on top of `9bc3913`, no commits from `perf/search-cache-feedback`). Diff is exactly four files: `README.md`, `dashboard/memory_wiki_core.py`, `tests/test_memory_wiki_core.py`, `tests/test_topic_relevance.py`.

Extraction remains deterministic English-oriented regex/keyword heuristics, not semantic topic understanding. Existing bounded history and truncation limits remain (sessions leaving the loaded window are out of scope). No LLM/network ranking, new dependencies, settings, or API response-key changes. No live session data is included. Not merged, installed or activated.

title: [memory-wiki] perf: cache subject searches and show loading/error feedback
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-memory-wiki/pull/2 by @tillstriegel. `hermes-memory-wiki` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `memory-wiki/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Summary

- Reuse complete subject indexes in a bounded, profile/database-isolated process-local cache, before query filtering and truncation. Invalidate on database/WAL metadata changes, with five-second expiry as a fallback. Concurrent cold requests share work.
- Move database aggregation off the async event loop, capturing the request home before worker dispatch.
- Show immediate accessible search status during debounce and requests, distinguish failures from empty results, abort obsolete SDK requests, and ignore late responses. Rebuild the tracked dashboard bundle.

Topic extraction, scoring, ordering, API shapes and limit-dependent history scopes are unchanged. This PR is limited to search performance and feedback, not relevance improvements.

## Verification

- Fresh `npm ci`: passes, zero reported vulnerabilities.
- Python suite: 35 passed, 1 expected failure (pre-existing host integration limitation below).
- Rendered React DOM/jsdom tests against the actual bundle: 2 passed, covering debounce/loading, errors, empty results, stale replies, cancellation, clearing and unmount.
- Frontend build and bundle syntax check: pass.
- Cache tests cover hits, filtered matches beyond the unfiltered top limit, WAL session/message updates/deletes, inserts, replacement/removal, expiry/bounds, concurrent requests, detached results and overlapping A→B→A request contexts.
- Real host plugin discovery/auth test passes. Independent defect-first review of the complete diff found no introduced actionable defects.
- AST comparison confirms extraction/scoring/snippet/finalization functions are unchanged.

## Reproducible synthetic benchmark

Run `python scripts/benchmark_search.py` using the Hermes test environment. It creates only synthetic data: 600 sessions with 12 messages each; the existing search scope remains 500 sessions. Five queries are checked over five repeated batches, with exact baseline/current output parity.

| Measurement | Baseline | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First/cold query | 762 ms | 821 ms |
| Repeated-query median | 743 ms | 29 ms |

These are local backend/API-function timings, not browser latency or a production workload benchmark. The improvement is warm-cache only; cold work is slightly slower. Results vary with hardware and activity.

## Limitations

- Overview, subject-detail and day aggregation remain uncached, though off the event loop.
- A simple shared lock serializes cold searches across profiles. Cache bounds are eight entries and 16 MiB serialized payload; Python object overhead is additional. Expired entries are purged on the next search.
- The host checkout used for integration tests does not inject selected profiles into plugin SDK URLs or scope plugin routes by `?profile=`. A strict expected-failure test reproduces this on the untouched baseline too. Cache isolation for correctly scoped request contexts is verified; this PR does not claim to fix the host dashboard profile switcher.
- UI behavior was exercised in rendered DOM tests, not live-browser or screen-reader testing.

No installed-plugin changes, host-core modifications, restart, deployment or merge are part of this PR.

title: [telegram-business] fix: harden Telegram Business draft approval
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-telegram-business/pull/2 by @vitorpy. `hermes-telegram-business` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `telegram-business/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Summary

Harden Telegram Business “secretary mode,” where incoming customer messages are drafted for the connected account owner, who must explicitly **Send**, **Edit**, or **Discard** each reply.

This implementation is deliberately fail-closed and concurrency-safe:

- atomically claim Send/Edit/Discard actions in SQLite before customer delivery
- enforce expiry at action time, not only during cleanup
- snapshot immutable owner user/chat/revision on every draft
- increment a durable owner revision on every ownership change, including A→B→A
- transactionally supersede unresolved drafts after ownership reassignment
- revalidate owner revision, active state, and reply permission immediately before delivery
- serialize Business connection updates with final validation, network delivery, and terminal transition inside the plugin’s single manager process
- prevent known pre-delivery retries from resurrecting obsolete drafts or Edit captures
- keep ambiguous delivery failures terminal because Telegram offers no send idempotency key
- migrate existing plugin databases transactionally, recover interrupted/partial migrations idempotently, and fail closed for unresolved legacy rows lacking trustworthy ownership snapshots
- prevent stale legacy cleanup from overwriting a terminal state committed by another SQLite connection
- close the plugin database if manager startup fails before publishing the singleton

## Why

A naive Telegram callback implementation allows duplicate callbacks and mixed Send/Edit/Discard actions to race. It can also deliver stale content after a newer customer message, retry an older Edit into the wrong capture, or authorize against a reassigned connection owner.

The durable state machine, conditional claims, owner revision snapshots, atomic retry release, and edit-generation CAS close those paths while preserving at-most-once delivery.

## Test plan

- `/usr/bin/python -m pytest -q` — **97 passed**
- isolated Python 3.11 run — **97 passed**
- `PYTHONWARNINGS=error::ResourceWarning /usr/bin/python -m pytest -q` — **97 passed**, no unclosed SQLite warnings
- `/usr/bin/python -m compileall -q __init__.py manager.py state.py tests`
- `git diff --check`
- real Hermes Python 3.11 + `python-telegram-bot 22.6` import, A→B→A, and database-reopen smoke test
- added-line credential/injection/eval/deserialization/formatted-SQL scan
- exact-HEAD, partial/interrupted-schema, migration rollback, and idempotent reopen tests
- independent SQLite-connection claim/release orderings, including terminal newer drafts
- deterministic owner reassignment, stale debounce/generator, and direct/edited dispatch interleavings
- blocking customer-send tests for duplicate and mixed callback races

## Recovery semantics

- Edit capture is intentionally process-local. Startup terminally supersedes `awaiting_edit` rows whose in-memory capture cannot be reconstructed; the owner can act on a fresh draft instead.
- An interrupted `sending` row remains terminal/stuck rather than being retried because delivery may already have happened.
- Final network-send serialization is process-local by design: the plugin wires one `BusinessModeManager` into one Hermes Telegram gateway process. SQLite state transitions remain safe across independent connections.

These choices prefer a closed draft over wrong-recipient or duplicate delivery.
