title: [blender] docs: install from the Hermes catalog until the next release
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-plugin-blender/pull/4 by @alt-glitch. `hermes-plugin-blender` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `blender/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

The README's install command now works on released Hermes. Fixes #3.

The README told users to run `hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-plugin-blender`. That installs this repo's latest commit (plugin 0.2.0), whose `plugin.json` lists several install locations per OS. Only Hermes main reads a list (NousResearch/hermes-agent#134050), so every released Hermes refuses the install on every OS with `app.win32.location is required`.

- The primary command is now `hermes plugins install blender`, the catalog entry, which pins 0.1.0 and installs on released Hermes.
- One sentence explains that installing from this repo installs 0.2.0 and needs a Hermes release that includes #134050.
- Removed the sentence saying catalog installation "becomes available only after its catalog entry is merged". The entry is published, so the sentence was wrong.

## Live verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Released Hermes on Windows, `hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-plugin-blender` | `app.win32.location is required`, exit 1 |
| Same machine, `hermes plugins install blender` | installs 0.1.0 at catalog pin `d1929b59`, exit 0 |

Related: NousResearch/hermes-agent#134485 lets a plugin declare the Hermes version it needs, so a future mismatch says "run hermes update" instead of a parse error.

title: [accent-picker] fix: render preset swatches horizontally
body:
Ported from https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-desktop-accent-picker/pull/1 by @lorzl. `hermes-desktop-accent-picker` moved into this monorepo (see the [README](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#already-used-one-of-these)), so this is the same commit(s) applied under `accent-picker/`, authorship kept. Review continues here.

---

**Original description:**

## Problem

The 8 preset swatches in the statusbar accent picker render in a single vertical column instead of one horizontal row.

## Root cause

The swatch container used the Tailwind utility class `grid grid-cols-8 gap-1`. The Hermes desktop app builds its Tailwind CSS from the app's own source only — the plugin lives in `~/.hermes/desktop-plugins/`, outside the build's scan path. The app's source uses `grid-cols-6` but never `grid-cols-8`, so that class has no CSS at runtime.

The container therefore got `display: grid` (from the `grid` utility, which IS emitted) but no `grid-template-columns`, collapsing to a single column — every swatch on its own row.

## Fix

Replace the Tailwind utility class with an inline CSS grid that does not depend on which utilities the host app happens to have generated:

```
display: grid;
grid-template-columns: repeat(8, minmax(0, 1fr));
gap: 4px;
```

Both files are updated to stay in sync:

- `src/picker.tsx` — the TypeScript source
- `plugin.js` — the shipped, uncompiled artifact the desktop actually loads

## Test plan

- Confirmed the 8 swatches now sit in one horizontal row.
- No behavioral change: clicking a swatch still calls `setAccentOverride(hex)` exactly as before.

title: Drafts replies to the owner's own outgoing Business messages (no sender check in handle_business_message)
body:
## Summary

The plugin drafts a reply to **every** text `business_message` in a connected chat, including messages written **by the Business account owner themselves**. When I (the owner) write to a contact from my own Telegram, the bot DMs me a "suggested reply" to my own message, as if the contact had written it.

Telegram delivers both sides of a Business chat to the bot: the contact's incoming messages *and* the owner's outgoing ones (plus messages the bot itself sent on the owner's behalf). `handle_business_message` never checks who the sender is.

## Environment

- `hermes-telegram-business` installed from this repo (behaviour confirmed by reading `main` @ `98c60afc`)
- Hermes Agent `v0.21.5+3779.g8f897d2`, Telegram gateway in polling mode
- Bot connected via Telegram → Settings → Business → Chatbots with access to private chats and "reply on your behalf" enabled

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install and enable the plugin, connect the bot as a Business chatbot (`/biz` shows the connection as active).
2. From the owner's own Telegram app, send a text to any contact in a connected chat.

**Expected:** no draft. Drafts should be produced only for messages sent by the other party.

**Actual:** the bot DMs the owner

```
💬 <owner name> wrote:
  > <the owner's own message>
📝 Suggested reply:
  <a reply to the owner's own message>
[✓ Send] [✎ Edit] [✕ Discard]
```

## Root cause

`manager.py` @ `98c60afc`, `handle_business_message` (L228): after checking `is_enabled`, `auto_draft` and `paused_chats` (L241–L255), it goes straight to extracting text and scheduling the debounced draft (L258–L270). The only sender-related field used is `message.chat.id`. `message.from_user` is never compared with the connection's `owner_user_id`, and `message.sender_business_bot` isn't consulted (0 occurrences in the file). The docstring states the assumption: *"`from_user` (the customer)"*, but for outgoing Business messages `from_user` is the owner.

## Side effects beyond the extra draft

- **Owner messages replace pending drafts for the customer.** The debounce key is `{conn_id}:{customer_chat_id}` (L270), so if a contact writes and the owner answers manually within `debounce_seconds`, the draft for the contact's message is cancelled and replaced with a draft replying to the owner.
- **Approved sends can trigger new drafts.** A message the bot sends on the owner's behalf (✓ Send) comes back as a `business_message` from the same chat with `sender_business_bot` set. With no sender check it gets drafted again, which wastes LLM calls and invites loops.
- LLM tokens are spent on every message the owner sends in any connected chat.

## Suggested fix

In `handle_business_message`, after the connection is loaded and before any text or debounce handling:

```python
# Only draft replies to the *other* party. Skip messages the owner wrote
# themselves and messages the bot sent on the owner's behalf.
if getattr(message, "sender_business_bot", None) is not None:
    return
sender = getattr(message, "from_user", None)
if sender is not None and str(getattr(sender, "id", "")) == str(conn.get("owner_user_id")):
    return
```

Suggested tests:

- an owner-sent `business_message` (`from_user.id == owner_user_id`) → no draft is scheduled, and an in-flight debounce for that chat is **not** cancelled;
- a message with `sender_business_bot` set → no draft;
- a customer message → still drafted (regression).

Optionally, an owner message could instead be used as a signal that the customer has been answered, e.g. discard the pending draft for that chat.

## Related

hermes-agent#42400 discusses classifying Business message origins (`bot_echo` vs owner-manual vs inbound) for the core gateway. The same classification is needed here.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): accept Hermes tool names of 51-64 characters
body:
## What breaks

`request_body()` raises `ValueError('Tool names must be unique ASCII identifiers of at most 50 characters')` for any tool name over 50 characters. That fails the whole provider call, not just the one tool.

Hermes core names MCP tools `mcp__<server>__<tool>` and clamps them to 64 characters (`tools/mcp_tool_schema.py::mcp_prefixed_tool_name`). Its comment notes these names routinely exceed 64 before the clamp. So any agent with one long MCP tool name cannot use this provider at all.

The 50 limit exists because native sees each tool as `mcp__hermes__` + name, and the API allows 64.

## Fix

- Names of 50 characters or fewer are unchanged: request body, manifest and replayed history are byte-identical.
- Names of 51–64 characters reach native under a stable 50-character alias: the first 41 characters, `_`, then 8 hex digits of sha256(name). Native sees `mcp__hermes__<alias>` (63 characters).
- A call on the alias maps back to the original Hermes name. This covers both the prefixed name and the bare one native sometimes returns (#62). The stored native block keeps the prefixed alias, so replay and carrier restore are unchanged.
- An alias that collides with another offered name raises `ValueError` naming both. Over 64 characters, invalid characters and duplicates are still rejected.
- `request_body()` now returns a `{hermes_name: native_name}` dict in place of the name set. Membership checks behave the same.

## Tests

New `tests/test_directsdk_tool_names.py` (18 tests). It covers:
- alias determinism and length;
- a literal byte-identity check for short names (body, manifest, history);
- rejection cases and both kinds of collision;
- history replay;
- an end-to-end run through the fake native, streaming and non-streaming, prefixed and bare. The Hermes call carries the original name, and the second request restores the native carrier.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| New tests on `main` | 17 failed, 1 passed (the expected `ValueError`s) |
| New tests on this branch | 18 passed |
| Full suite | 227 passed |
| Full suite with `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1` | 227 passed |

Not run against live Claude Code with a 63-character MCP name. Native's view of an aliased tool is the same length as today's 50-character names.

## With #29 (warm mode)

The warm MCP path matches tool calls by name, so it needs the same reverse lookup once both land. I'll do that port on whichever lands second.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] ci: run the offline evals against a pinned Claude Code
body:
## Why

The directsdk plugin depends on exactly what the real `claude` binary puts on the wire: admission, breakpoint pinning, signed replay. Those can change between Claude Code releases. For example, 2.1.287 started marking two message blocks, and 2.1.292 sends `thinking.display: "updates"`. The unit suite uses a Python fake native, so it can't see such changes. The plugin already ships two offline evals that run the real binary against a loopback peer, with no credentials and no inference, but CI never installs `claude`, so they never run there.

## What

- **`tests.yml`:** one generic step after the unit suite. If a plugin ships `evals/ci.sh`, run it (Linux and macOS). No other plugin is affected, and any plugin can opt in the same way.
- **`claude-subscription-directsdk/evals/ci.sh`:**
  - installs a pinned `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` from npm into a temp prefix (`CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`, default `2.1.292`);
  - runs `evals/directsdk_admission.py` (11 protocol modes, one upstream request each) and `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` (cached prefix replays byte-identical round to round).
- **README:** one paragraph in Verification.

The pin keeps a new Claude Code release from turning unrelated PRs red. Bumping it is how a release gets qualified.

## Local run

`bash claude-subscription-directsdk/evals/ci.sh` on macOS with a fresh npm install of 2.1.292: exit 0. Both evals pass on `main`.

Cost: one npm install (~1 min) plus about 1 min of evals per macOS/Linux job. Whether the step should be required is your call.

Follow-ups this enables: #22's extended `cache_wire` check (turn-start mark) would then run in CI too. So would further offline cells, such as checking every shared message for #38, or the side-request admission check for #39.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat: per-profile claude_config_dir setting picks the Claude login (#34)
body:
Fixes #34.

## What

A per-profile plugin setting, `claude_config_dir`, selects the Claude login that native runs on. It is read for the active profile on every spawn, the same way `claude_code_telemetry` is, so profiles served by one multiplexed gateway can use different Claude subscriptions:

```sh
hermes config set plugins.entries.claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental.settings.claude_config_dir ~/.claude-work
```

Precedence for the native child's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` follows the issue: nonempty setting > `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR` > inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` > CLI default.
- The chosen value gets `~` expansion only. There is no existence check: a missing login already surfaces as native's authentication error.
- `os.environ` is never changed.

## How

`directsdk_setup.apply_config_dir(env)` is the one place the choice is made. It has three callers:
- the request spawn (`directsdk.py`, replacing the old env-only block);
- `claude auth status` (`setup_status`);
- model discovery (`discover_models`).

The settings lookup is factored out of `telemetry_enabled()` into `_setting(key, default)`, so both settings read the profile the same way. Telemetry behaviour and its tests are unchanged, except that the manifest test now selects its field by key.

Not covered, and documented in the README: the plan-limits / account-usage snapshot (`_subscription_token()`). It uses core's `read_claude_code_credentials()`, which reads only the process `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and the default macOS keychain entry. Following the setting there would mean reimplementing core's credential lookup.

## Tests

New `tests/test_directsdk_config_dir.py` (18 tests):
- each precedence level;
- `~` expansion, and whitespace falling through;
- the override variable never reaches the child;
- two profiles in one process getting different dirs;
- end to end through the fake native (the child sees the profile's dir);
- auth status and model discovery;
- the manifest key.

| | Result |
|---|---|
| New tests on `main` | 18 failed |
| New tests on this branch | 18 passed |
| Full suite | 227 passed |
| Full suite with `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1` | 227 passed |

Unit and fake-native only. There was no live two-account run.

## With #29 (warm mode)

Warm's launch identity already includes `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (`_WARM_LAUNCH_KEYS`, computed from `_native_env()`). Merging means calling `apply_config_dir(env)` in `_native_env()`; a pooled session then never crosses logins.

title: fix(directsdk): stall watchdog kills the native call on model-progress silence
body:
Fixes #35.

## The bug

A native call that stalls looks healthy to every timer that exists today:

- The plugin's read-idle deadline (`directsdk.py` `receive()`) resets on **every** native event, and a stalled upstream can keep pinging while producing nothing - so it never fires.
- Hermes' non-stream stale-call watchdog (`agent/chat_completion_nonstream.py`) only knows wall-clock time since the call started, so it cannot tell a healthy long thinking call from a stall.

The reporter's numbers make the cost concrete: with the provider-level stale timeout at 600s, one real stall (no output at 177K context) held the turn for the full 600s; lowering it kills healthy 437-509s calls that are still streaming thinking.

## The fix

The plugin tracks **model progress** separately from liveness, as the issue's option 1 describes, and enforces it itself - no core change needed:

- `_is_progress()` classifies native events: stream deltas of any type (text, thinking, signature, `input_json`), block/message starts and stops, and assistant/system/user/result frames are progress; **pings and keepalives are not**.
- `receive()` resets the progress clock only on progress events, and kills the native call (`p.kill()`) when none arrives for `stall_timeout_seconds`.
- The kill raises `TimeoutError('Claude request stalled: no model progress for Ns')` - a timeout to Hermes, so it retries or falls back at the stall bound instead of holding the turn.

`stall_timeout_seconds` (default **300**, `0` disables) is read per spawn from the profile config, exactly like `claude_code_telemetry`, so a multi-profile gateway honors each profile and a change applies on the next call:

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental:
      settings:
        stall_timeout_seconds: 300
```

Healthy long calls are unaffected: their deltas keep resetting the clock. This pairs well with the provider-level `stale_timeout_seconds` for the wall-clock side (documented in the README update).

## Tests

`tests/test_directsdk_stall.py`, against fake native processes (no network):

- a ping-fed stall (pings every 50ms, no progress) is killed with `no model progress` well before the 25s read-idle limit - **fails on main pre-fix** (the stall survives on pings)
- real text deltas every 500ms over 2.5s survive a 1s stall limit (progress defers the kill)
- `stall_timeout_seconds: 0` keeps the old behavior: a 2s ping run then completion is not killed

Full plugin suite: 204 passed, 8 skipped (includes these); no existing behavior changed when the watchdog is disabled or untriggered.

title: fix(directsdk): carry the login identity into the child env; capture native stderr
body:
Fixes #44 (the confirmed part; the rest becomes diagnosable).

## What the issue established

`ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` fired only inside a real gateway process, never standalone, and the reporter exhausted env, concurrency, load, request shape and the async dispatch path as causes. Two things from the thread are actionable:

1. **A confirmed local precondition** (@100yenadmin): Claude Code's local login check reads the process identity - `env -i HOME PATH claude auth status` reports `loggedIn: false` while adding `USER` flips it to `true`, instantly, with empty stderr and no upstream request. A supervised gateway (launchd background, containers, cron) or a filtered env dict can omit `USER` even when the machine has a working login.
2. **A diagnostic gap**: native's stderr went to `DEVNULL`, so the reporter had to patch the plugin to learn the stream was empty.

## The fix

**Identity carried into the child env** (`_with_login_identity`, applied right after the Windows essentials): `USER`/`LOGNAME` on POSIX - from the configured env, else the parent process, else `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_name` - and `USERNAME`/`USER` on Windows. Derived before every spawn; the configured env always wins over the derivation.

**Native stderr captured and surfaced**: spawn now uses `stderr=PIPE` with a bounded (`deque(maxlen=40)`) off-thread drain, and the first lines ride `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut`, `Native request failed` and invalid-stream errors via `_stderr_tail`. The drain thread is joined in the existing cleanup; no FD is closed on a caller thread.

This does not claim to explain the reporter's remaining launchd case - it removes the one **confirmed** local precondition and makes any remaining gateway-only failure carry native's own diagnostic text.

## Tests

`tests/test_directsdk_identity.py`, fake native processes, no network:

- an identity-free child env now completes (`OK`) where pre-fix it raised `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` - red pre-fix, green post-fix
- a logged-out failure now carries native's stderr (`keychain locked`) in the raised error - red pre-fix, green post-fix

Full plugin suite: 203 passed, 8 skipped.

title: homeassistant plugin: cron delivery fails (HTTP 500) — standalone sender uses legacy notify.notify with target
body:
## Summary

Cron delivery with `deliver: homeassistant` fails on current Home Assistant builds with `500 Internal Server Error`, because the standalone cron sender (`adapter.py`, `_standalone_send`) POSTs to the legacy grouped service `/api/services/notify/notify` with a `target` payload. On HA 2026.x, any call to `notify.notify` that passes a `target` returns:

```
500 Internal Server Error
Server got itself in trouble
```

The same message delivered via the concrete per-device service (`POST /api/services/notify/mobile_app_<device>`) succeeds with HTTP 200 and the push arrives on the companion app. The live gateway adapter's `send()` is unaffected (it uses `persistent_notification/create`), so gateway restart notifications still appear — which makes this confusing to diagnose.

## Environment

- Hermes homeassistant plugin 2.0.1 (`_standalone_send`, adapter.py ~line 345)
- Home Assistant current 2026.x (container install)
- iPhone companion app; `notify.mobile_app_*` services registered and healthy
- Cron config: `deliver: "telegram,homeassistant"` — the Telegram leg succeeds, only the HA leg fails

## Reproduction (with a valid long-lived token)

```bash
# Fails: 500 on every target spelling
curl -X POST "$HASS_URL/api/services/notify/notify" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HASS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "probe", "target": "matts_iphone"}'          # -> 500
curl ... -d '{"message": "probe", "target": "mobile_app_matts_iphone"}'  # -> 500

# Works: 200, push arrives
curl -X POST "$HASS_URL/api/services/notify/mobile_app_matts_iphone" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $HASS_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "probe", "title": "Hermes probe"}'           # -> 200
```

The legacy `notify` integration is deprecated upstream in Home Assistant; the grouped service with `target` is the broken path.

## Suggested fix

In `_standalone_send`, call the concrete per-device notify service derived from the chat id first, keeping the legacy call only as a fallback:

```python
url = f"{hass_url}/api/services/notify/notify"
payload = {"message": message, "target": chat_id}
# Recent HA builds return "500 Server got itself in trouble" for the legacy grouped
# notify.notify service when a ``target`` is passed. Prefer the concrete per-device
# service (notify/mobile_app_<device>) and only fall back to the legacy grouped call.
slug = chat_id.split(":")[-1].strip()
if slug.startswith("mobile_app_"):
    candidates = [slug]
else:
    candidates = [f"mobile_app_{slug}", None]  # None = legacy grouped call with target
last_error = None
try:
    async with HomeAssistantAdapter._new_session() as session:
        for service in candidates:
            send_url = url if service is None else f"{hass_url}/api/services/notify/{service}"
            send_payload = payload if service is None else {"message": message}
            async with session.post(send_url, headers=_auth_headers(token), json=send_payload) as resp:
                if resp.status in {200, 201}:
                    return {"success": True, "platform": "homeassistant", "chat_id": chat_id}
                last_error = f"Home Assistant API error ({resp.status}): {await resp.text()}"
    return send_error(last_error or "Home Assistant send failed")
except asyncio.TimeoutError:
    ...
```

This is applied locally on my install and verified end-to-end (manual cron fire delivered successfully afterwards). It also keeps behaviour for other `notify.*` platforms (webos tv etc.) via the legacy fallback.

Happy to open a PR against `main/homeassistant` if useful.

title: [homeassistant] fix: close the superseded connection when connect() is re-entered
body:
## What

`[homeassistant] fix: close the superseded connection when `connect()` is re-entered`.

## Why

`connect()` is not one-shot: the gateway's reconnect watcher re-enters it with
`is_reconnect=True` while the previous connection is still live. On that path the old code
called `_ws_connect()` (which overwrites `self._session`/`self._ws`) and then overwrote
`self._rest_session` and `self._listen_task`, without closing or cancelling anything it
replaced. Two things leak on every reconnect:

1. **The two `aiohttp.ClientSession`s are orphaned.** Nothing references them any more, so
   they are only cleaned up when GC collects them — until then aiohttp logs
   `Unclosed client session` / `Unclosed connector`, and their sockets and file descriptors
   stay open. Where this was found the gateway log held 183 `[Homeassistant] Connected to …`
   against 187 `[Homeassistant] Disconnected` lines, i.e. the watcher normally completes a
   teardown before re-dialling, so the leak is **latent** rather than one per reconnect: it
   fires whenever `connect()` is re-entered without a finished teardown (a second watcher
   tick, a teardown that raised, the lost-connection path), and the log did show
   `Unclosed client session` errors on the days with reconnect churn. The isolated test above
   is what pins the mechanism down; the log says how often it can bite.

The clearest sighting, from the log on the machine where this was found:

```
2026-10-12 14:01:31 WARNING hermes_plugins.homeassistant.adapter: [Homeassistant] Reconnection failed: 502, message='Invalid response status', url='wss://mmhome…'
2026-10-12 14:02:17 ERROR   asyncio: Unclosed client session
client_session: <aiohttp.client.ClientSession object at 0x…>
```

`_ws_connect()` assigns `self._session` before it dials, so a handshake that *fails* (here a 502 from
the proxy) leaves that session unreferenced with nothing closing it on the failure path. With this
patch the next `connect()` closes it via `_cleanup_ws()`; #6 additionally closes the freshly-created
session inside `_ws_connect()`'s own failure path. The two cover different halves of the same leak,
which is why they are complementary.
2. **Two `_listen_loop` tasks run against one adapter.** The superseded listener keeps
   reading its own (still-open) websocket and dispatching events, so a single HA
   `state_changed` event can produce duplicate agent turns.

## How

Close and cancel the superseded connection before dialling again, reusing the existing
teardown path (`_cleanup_ws()` + `_close()`), and drop the stale listener before starting
the new one:

```python
await self._cleanup_ws()
await self._close(self._rest_session)
self._rest_session = None
if self._listen_task is not None and not self._listen_task.done():
    self._listen_task.cancel()
    try:
        await self._listen_task
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        pass
    except Exception:  # a dying listener must not block the reconnect
        logger.debug("[%s] stale listener exited with an error", self.name, exc_info=True)
self._listen_task = None
```

18 lines in `connect()`. A first connect has nothing to close, so that path is unchanged.

## Relationship to #6

Complementary, not a duplicate. #6 ("bound every wedgeable await during Home Assistant
connect and teardown") bounds the *teardown awaits* and makes `_close()` bounded, and it
rewrites `_ws_connect()` to hold the new socket in locals — but its `connect()` still assigns
`self._session = session` / `self._ws = ws` at the end without closing the previous pair, so
the reconnect orphaning described here still happens on top of #6. This patch and #6 touch
different lines of `connect()`/`_ws_connect()` and should merge cleanly in either order;
whichever lands second should re-run both suites.

## Tests

`tests/test_homeassistant_connect_reconnect.py` (new, offline — connection primitives stubbed,
no real HA instance):

* `test_reconnect_closes_superseded_sessions` — both superseded sessions are closed, the
  superseded listener is done, the live one is a new task;
* `test_repeated_reconnects_do_not_accumulate_sessions` — 3 reconnects leave exactly the live
  connection's two sessions open;
* `test_cold_connect_then_disconnect_closes_everything` — the cold path still tears down.

Verified on this commit:

```

tests/test_homeassistant_connect_reconnect.py::TestConnectReconnectLifecycle::test_repeated_reconnects_do_not_accumulate_sessions FAILED
2 failed, 1 passed        # against main, before the fix

66 passed, 2 skipped      # full plugin suite from homeassistant/ with the fix
```

(The new tests fail on `main` and pass with the fix, which is the point of adding them.)

title: [homeassistant] A HASS_URL without http(s):// fails forever with only the URL as the error
body:
## Problem

If `HASS_URL` (or `platforms.homeassistant.extra.url`) is set without a scheme, for example `HASS_URL=ha.example.com`, nothing tells you what is wrong:

- **Gateway adapter:** `_ws_connect()` only swaps an existing `https://`/`http://` for `wss://`/`ws://`, so the WebSocket URL becomes `ha.example.com/api/websocket`. The log shows only

  ```
  ERROR ... [Homeassistant] Failed to connect: ha.example.com/api/websocket
  INFO gateway.run: Reconnect homeassistant failed, next retry in 300s
  ```

  The gateway keeps retrying every 5 minutes indefinitely. In my case it ran for over a week (more than 1,800 attempts) before I noticed, because the error names no cause.
- **Tools** (`ha_get_state` etc.) and **cron delivery** (`_standalone_send`) build their request URLs the same way and fail with just the URL as the error, e.g. `Home Assistant send failed: ha.example.com/api/services/notify/notify`.

Adding the scheme (`HASS_URL=https://ha.example.com`) fixes everything immediately.

## Expected

Per the "fail loud at integration boundaries" guideline in hermes-agent's CONTRIBUTING.md: reject the URL where it is read, with a message that names the setting and the fix, and don't retry a config error that only an edit can fix.

## Environment

Plugin version 2.0.1 (same code on `main`), Hermes Agent v0.21.7, Linux.

I've opened a PR with a fix and tests.

title: [homeassistant] fix: reject a URL without http(s):// with a named cause
body:
Fixes #65.

## What this does

A Home Assistant URL without a scheme (e.g. `HASS_URL=ha.example.com`) used to fail with only the URL as the error, and the gateway retried it forever. It is now rejected where it is read, with a message that names the setting and the fix:

> Home Assistant URL 'ha.example.com' has no http:// or https:// scheme. Set HASS_URL (or platforms.homeassistant.extra.url) to the full URL, e.g. https://ha.example.com or http://homeassistant.local:8123

## Changes

- `homeassistant/tools.py`: new `url_scheme_problem(url)`; `_get_config()` raises `ValueError` with that message, which the existing `_dispatch` turns into the tool error.
- `homeassistant/adapter.py`:
  - `connect()` checks the URL before opening the WebSocket and sets a **non-retryable** fatal error (`homeassistant_url_scheme`), so the reconnect watcher drops it instead of retrying every 5 minutes.
  - `_standalone_send()` (cron delivery) returns the same message.
- Tests for all three paths. Without the fix, the four new tests fail with the old opaque errors.

I chose rejecting over silently prepending `https://`. That follows the "fail loud at integration boundaries" rule in hermes-agent's CONTRIBUTING.md, and guessing would pick the wrong scheme for plain-HTTP LAN installs.

## Testing

```
cd homeassistant
HERMES_HOME=$(mktemp -d) PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q
67 passed, 2 skipped
```

Run against hermes-agent v0.21.7 on Linux. The empty `HERMES_HOME` matters: without it, `test_is_connected_requires_non_blank_hass_token` picks up a real `HASS_TOKEN` from `~/.hermes/.env` and fails on `main` too.

I also confirmed the root cause end to end on a real instance: the same token connects and authenticates once the scheme is added.

## Note

#64 also edits the start of `connect()`. This check sits just before its `try:`, so whichever merges second may need a trivial rebase.

| PR #45048 @zhuxungit: tracing reliability | ALREADY_FIXED (`_LANGFUSE_CLIENT_LOCK` double-checked init in `_get_langfuse`, plus atexit finalize). The fixed-trace-id/EvalOps env knob is a separate feature and is not ported | — |

## Changes
- `_start_root_trace` opens the root with `client.start_observation(...)` (no current-span contextvar is pushed), still inside `propagate_attributes`. `_end_root` now only ends the span. `TraceState.root_ctx` stays as an always-None field so existing and parallel-lane `TraceState(...)` constructors keep working.
- The root's `propagate_attributes` kwargs are kept on `TraceState.propagated`. `_start_child_observation` re-enters `propagate_attributes(**state.propagated)` around each child's creation. Entry and exit happen on the same thread, so this does not reintroduce the cross-context detach that holding the context open across hooks (#81732's approach) would.

body:
The default `sanitized` capture mode no longer sends opaque secrets under credential-named JSON keys, bare `Bearer` tokens, or `user:pass@` base URLs to Langfuse. Redaction now fails closed. The per-type cost breakdown also adds up to the trace total on context-tiered models.

- `_redact_secrets` now uses `agent.redact.redact_for_egress`. This is core's scrub for text leaving the machine: it forces redaction, adds a sweep for leftover opaque `Bearer` tokens, and fails closed. The old `try/except` returned the raw value if the redactor raised.

title: [langfuse] Background export on live turns; mark failed/abandoned calls ERROR/WARNING
body:
A slow or dead Langfuse backend no longer delays a finished turn (cron watchdog case), and failed or abandoned LLM/tool calls now land as `ERROR`/`WARNING` observations instead of looking like successes.

Langfuse backlog lane **export**: covers flush behaviour, error states, failed-API traces and stale per-turn state. It decides 6 hermes-agent items (open issues/PRs that targeted the old core `plugins/observability/langfuse/` path).

| hermes-agent item | Verdict | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| issue #87468 flush() has no timeout, cron hang | PORTED | 674c3c2 |
| PR #134284 @xiaoxipanda export live-session traces in the background | PORTED (base) | 674c3c2 |
| PR #87471 @liuhao1024 bounded flush with a deadline | SUPERSEDED by #134284 (credited) | 674c3c2 |
| issue #81731 failed/abandoned calls never marked ERROR/WARNING | PORTED (LLM-request part already fixed by `on_api_request_error`) | 664e8c2, 44493cd |
| PR #83774 @airclear close failed api traces | ALREADY_FIXED (Langfuse hunk) + CORE_HALF_STAYS | — |
| PR #45326 @rdguidry localhost default base URL; reap stale state | reaper ALREADY_FIXED; localhost default NEEDS_DECISION | — |

## Changes
- **674c3c2** (author xiaoxipanda, co-author liuhao1024): `_finish_trace` no longer calls `flush()`. `on_session_finalize`, which `on_session_end` also calls once per turn, now flushes only for `reason="shutdown"`. Ended spans go out through the SDK's background exporter. On process exit (CLI `chat -q` and `-z` both send `reason="shutdown"`) the plugin still flushes and shuts the client down; atexit `_finalize_all_traces` is unchanged. README hook table updated, with an export-timing note.
- **664e8c2** (author sylbae): any generation or tool observation still open when its turn ends never got its response/result, so it closes as `level=ERROR` with a status message. A retry attempt superseded in `pre_api_request` closes as `WARNING`. `_end_observation` takes `level` and `status_message`.
- **44493cd** (author Enough1122): `post_tool_call` `status` is now mapped to a level: `error`→`ERROR`, `blocked`/`cancelled`→`WARNING`. `status_message` is set to the error type.

## Live evidence
Real `hermes chat -q` turns (Gemini flash-lite) on a throwaway HOME with the catalog-installed plugin. Plugin code swapped between main and this branch.
- **#87468, Langfuse host that accepts the POST and stalls 60s.** On main, the reply box opened at +2.99s but `pong` printed at +8.08s. The turn was blocked ~5.1s in `flush()`, which equals the SDK's HTTP timeout. On this branch, the box opened at +2.82s and `pong` printed at +2.92s. The wait moves to process exit (shutdown flush), which is expected.
- **Delivery unchanged.** Normal recorder, prompt with two tool calls: main and branch both log `Hermes turn` 2, `LLM call` 2, `Tool: terminal` 1, `Tool: read_file` 1, shipped on exit.
- **#81731 tool status, live turn.** `read_file /nonexistent/xyz.txt` fails ("File not found"). On main the recorder shows `ERROR` 0. On this branch it shows `ERROR` 1, inside the `Tool: read_file` span, plus 2 `tool_error` strings; the `terminal` span stays at DEFAULT.
- **#81731 unanswered and superseded calls.** Direct calls into the real plugin module with the real langfuse 4.15.2 SDK and the local recorder: an interrupted turn (open LLM call + open tool), then a superseded retry. On main: `ERROR` 0, `WARNING` 0. On this branch: `ERROR` 2, `WARNING` 1, with "Turn ended before…" and "Retried: no response…" status messages.
- **#83774, live turn with an invalid Gemini key on main** (non-retryable 400): the recorder already shows the generation at `ERROR` (status_code and retryable present in metadata), and the `Hermes turn` root closed and exported.

title: [langfuse] Loud credential failures, custom-endpoint keys, SDK v4 trace I/O and service.name
body:
Langfuse now warns when keys are templates or missing, accepts keys from custom endpoints, and ships trace-level input/output plus a real `service.name`. Each of these was silently broken in the plugin as pinned (SDK 4.15.2).

## What changed

| hermes-agent item | Verdict | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| PR #64309 (@Solitud1nem): reject right-prefix template keys (`pk-lf-...`) | PORTED | 8fc614c |
| issue #51399 + 15 duplicates: placeholder key fails silently | fixed by 8fc614c, f0a628d, 3d562c6 | — |
| PR #72487 (@EvanProgramming): prefix guard only on Langfuse Cloud hosts | PORTED (Langfuse half; core half no longer has a target) | f0a628d |
| issue #72484: custom-endpoint keys rejected by prefix | fixed by f0a628d | — |
| PR #98635 (@liuhao1024): warn once when credentials are missing | PORTED | 3d562c6 |
| issue #98631: placeholder public key + unset secret, zero log output | fixed by 3d562c6 | — |
| issue #94710: plugin calls v3 `update_trace` on SDK v4 | FIXED (`set_trace_io`) | c2f4be6 |
| PR #94752: pin SDK to v3 | SUPERSEDED by c2f4be6 (a v3 pin would clash with the plugin's `langfuse==4.15.2` pin) | — |
| issue #58322 / PR #58264 (@AXEG0): `service.name=unknown_service` | PORTED (slim redo, co-authored) | ea9994c |
| issue #59026, PRs #59032 / #99909 / #49458: SDK missing after venv rebuild | ALREADY_FIXED: the plugin installs its SDK into its own environment from `pyproject.toml` (`langfuse==4.15.2`), and `_build_client` warns with a reinstall hint when the SDK is missing | — |
| PR #64236: export consent gate | needs a product call (the parent will decide); not built | — |

How the two key checks fit together: the template check (`...`, `***`, bare prefix, `placeholder`, `your-`, `xxx`, …) runs for **every** host. The `pk-lf-`/`sk-lf-` prefix is required **only** when the base URL is `langfuse.com` or one of its subdomains. That match is on a dot boundary and ignores a trailing DNS dot, so `evil-langfuse.com` doesn't count as Langfuse Cloud. A pasted `pk-lf-...` is caught on self-hosted setups too, and operator-issued keys on a custom endpoint are passed through to the endpoint, which authenticates them.

`service.name` is only a default. `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`, or `service.name` in `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, still wins. The config key, setup wizard and fail-closed behaviour from #58264 are not carried over, because the standard env var already gives per-agent naming.

## Live evidence

title: [langfuse] one trace per turn: stop session-wide trace collapse
body:
Each Hermes turn now gets its own Langfuse trace. Before this, gateway, ACP and API-server conversations were merged into one trace per session. Session grouping stays as it was.

## Items

| hermes-agent item | Verdict | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| #110582 (dandomin) scope trace IDs by turn | PORTED (base) | 17a82c1 |
| #125639 (marten-lucas) scope trace id per turn | SUPERSEDED by #110582 port (same fix, credited as co-author) | 17a82c1 |
| issue #32005 same trace ID for all turns in a session | PORTED (fixed by 17a82c1) | 17a82c1 |
| issue #29776 traces collapse when task_id == session_id (ACP) | PORTED (fixed by 17a82c1) | 17a82c1 |
| issue #71556 /v1/responses random session_id, not gateway_session_key | ALREADY_FIXED in core: `/v1/responses` now resolves `X-Hermes-Session-Key` to the live session row (`api_server_openai_routes.py` "previous_response_id chain > declared X-Hermes-Session-Key > fresh id"), so the plugin's `session_id` is already stable | – |
| #71608 (Slobaka, mixed) prefer gateway_session_key | ALREADY_FIXED (see #71556). Its core half only forwards a kwarg for Langfuse and does not stand alone | – |
| #125666 (marten-lucas) group by approval-context session key | NEEDS_DECISION (not built): the key it reads is per-request on API-server streaming (`run_id` / `completion_id`) and stays the same across `/new` on messaging platforms | – |

## Fix

`_start_root_trace` built the trace seed as `f"{session_id}::{task_id or task_key}"`. Gateway, ACP and the API server pass `task_id == session_id`, so `create_trace_id(seed=…)` returned the same id for every turn. The seed now uses `turn_id`, then `api_request_id`, and only after those the old task/key scope. `trace_context.session_id` is unchanged, so Langfuse still groups the turns under one session. The test asserts the two roots get distinct trace ids. It fails on main (2 failed) and passes with the fix (101 passed).

## Live evidence

The probe ran a real `hermes gateway run` with api_server on 127.0.0.1:18511 and a local OTLP recorder, using real Gemini flash-lite turns. It sent two `/v1/responses` requests with the same `X-Hermes-Session-Key`. The decoded OTLP spans were:

Before (monorepo main plugin): one trace id for two different turns.
```
46b538ddd5b17bba0c976f61906c3bbd | Hermes turn | session.id= 6af5ee81-… | turn_id= …:cc57db84
46b538ddd5b17bba0c976f61906c3bbd | Hermes turn | session.id= 6af5ee81-… | turn_id= …:c2250459
```
After (this branch swapped in): a distinct trace per turn, with the same session.
```
d311756b9d911e74de4b0bfd31aad0ca | Hermes turn | session.id= 537de222-… | turn_id= …:9a9e11fe
6b7bbbf0b7efc05f19e886623c4b8496 | Hermes turn | session.id= 537de222-… | turn_id= …:fb264206
```
The before run also shows that core already gives both same-key requests one session.id, which is why #71556 is closed as already fixed.

Checks: plugin tests 101 passed, `hermes plugins validate langfuse` passed, `plugin_guard.scan_plugin` reports safe.

Credit: @dandomin (#110582, author), @marten-lucas (#125639, co-author), @jojorgen (same seed fix proposed on #32005, co-author).

Closes after merge (parent will do it): hermes-agent #110582, #125639, #32005, #29776, #71556, #71608. #125666 is waiting on a product decision.

title: [spotify] fix: play bare track lists on desktop clients
body:
Spotify's desktop client (1.3.1.234 and 1.3.3.264, September/October 2026) accepts `PUT /me/player/play` with `{"uris": [...]}` (204) but plays nothing and stops whatever was playing. Requests that carry a context still play. Reported on the Spotify community forum: https://community.spotify.com/forum/en/discussion/7552922

**Change:** when `play` gets `uris` and no `context_uri`, the plugin looks up the first track (`market=from_token`, so relinked tracks resolve), plays it inside its album with `offset.uri`, and queues the remaining tracks. `context_uri` requests are unchanged. The result reports `started`, `context_uri` and `queued`.

**Trade-off:** after the queued tracks finish, the first track's album keeps playing instead of playback stopping.

**Tested:** new unit tests (`tests/test_spotify_play.py`); full suite passes against current core. Live on Windows desktop client 1.3.3.264: the old request reproduced the silent stop; the new path started playback from an inactive device and queued the rest.

title: [langfuse] Port the stranded hermes-agent Langfuse backlog: per-turn traces, no detach errors, visible failures, safer keys and redaction
body:
Ports every still-valid fix from the hermes-agent Langfuse backlog (stranded when Langfuse moved out of core in hermes-agent#137131) into `langfuse/`, with each contributor as commit author; it folds the six lane PRs #67, #68, #69, #70, #71 and #72 into one branch so the shared `__init__.py` merges once.

## What changes for Langfuse users

- **One trace per turn** in a session, still grouped under one Langfuse session (was: every turn of a session in one trace). Sampling (`HERMES_LANGFUSE_SAMPLE_RATE`) now samples turns.
- **No more `Failed to detach context`** errors: the root observation opens detached, so a turn finishing on another worker thread detaches nothing.
- **Child observations carry the session, tags and profile** (were bare).
- **Failures are visible**: failed/blocked tools and unanswered or superseded LLM/tool calls close as ERROR / WARNING.
- **Finished turns no longer wait on `flush()`**: the SDK exports in the background, process exit flushes (a stalled Langfuse host no longer delays replies).
- **Key checks**: template keys (`pk-lf-...`) and missing keys warn instead of failing silently; the `pk-lf-`/`sk-lf-` prefix is enforced only on `*.langfuse.com`, and a wrong prefix on a self-hosted/custom host warns but still exports.
- **Trace-level input/output** exported again via SDK v4 `set_trace_io` (the v3 `update_trace` call failed on every turn).
- **`service.name=hermes-agent`** instead of `unknown_service`, without leaking `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` into child processes; an operator's own `OTEL_*` still wins.
- **Attribution**: `metadata.profile`, tags `platform:<name>`, `trigger:cron|interactive`, `cron-job:<id>`, kanban task/run ids on worker traces; Responses API tool/reasoning/compaction input items keep their fields.
- **Sanitized mode masks more**: secret-named keys in parsed tool JSON (incl. numeric values), URL credentials (`user:pass@`, `?api_key=`) in content and the endpoint URL, bare `Bearer` tokens; a redactor error withholds content instead of sending it raw.
- **Cost**: the per-type breakdown is priced at the context-tier rate, so it adds up to the total.

## Validation

| Check | main (d48cfa8) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin suite | 101 passed | 143 passed (every new test red on main; reverting each fix turns ≥1 test red) |
| `hermes plugins validate` / install scanner | pass / safe | pass / safe |
| Live: 2 `hermes chat` turns (2nd resumes 1st), local Langfuse ingestion stand-in, real Gemini | 1 trace for both turns | 2 traces, same `session.id` |
| `service.name` on exported resource | `unknown_service` | `hermes-agent` |
| Child spans with session/tags/profile | 0 / 5 | 5 / 5 |
| Failing `read_file` span level | unset | `ERROR` |
| Trace input/output on roots | 0 / 0 | 2 / 2 |
| `Failed to detach context` in agent.log | 4 | 0 |
| `env | grep -c OTEL_` from the terminal tool | n/a | 0 |
| Test secret in exported bytes | 0 | 0 (`access_token=***`) |

Each lane also live-verified its own items (API-server `/v1/responses` per-turn traces, `hermes cron run` tags, a 60 s stalled host: reply after ~5 s on main vs 0.1 s, invalid-key turns, wrong-prefix keys on 127.0.0.1). Independent review of all six lanes: no blockers; its two majors (self-hosted prefix regression, env leak) and URL-credential redaction gap are fixed here.

title: [homeassistant] fix: cron delivery reaches the phone again (calls the target's notify service)
body:
Cron messages delivered to Home Assistant (`deliver: homeassistant`) reach the phone again.

- The cron sender called the grouped `notify.notify` service with a `target`. Current Home Assistant answers that with a 500, and its docs say `notify.notify` only picks "the first notify action Home Assistant can find". The README already documents the target as a notify service name (`mobile_app_my_phone`), so the sender now calls `notify.<target>` directly.
- It falls back to the old grouped call only when Home Assistant reports the service doesn't exist (400) or the target isn't a service name. Any other error is reported with the service that returned it.

Validation: new `tests/test_homeassistant_standalone_send.py`, 4 of 5 tests fail on `main` and all 5 pass here; Home Assistant suite 68 passed; install scanner `safe`; `hermes plugins validate` passes. Not yet tried against a live Home Assistant instance.

Fixes #62. Thanks @atomicsapien for the report (credited as co-author).

title: blender: walk a fresh computer through add-on setup, and show the build as it happens
body:
## What changed

- `blender/skills/blender/SKILL.md` gains a short **First run on a new computer** section. The model checks softly (tools listed, then `get_objects_summary`). On a connection error it opens https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/ (in the Hermes desktop app with `desktop_preview`, elsewhere as a link) and walks the user through four steps: Blender 5.1+ open, drag the page's **Drag and Drop into Blender** button in twice (first drop adds the Blender Lab repository, second installs the add-on), allow online access, and start the bridge (**Auto Start**, or **Start MCP Bridge Server**, `localhost`:`9876`). It checks again each time the user says done. It never installs Blender or the add-on.
- Scene workflow gains one rule so the user can watch a build: `get_screenshot_of_window_as_image` after each change, copied over one fixed file that the preview pane reloads, and one `render_viewport_to_path` at the end.
- `references/setup.md` quotes the page and add-on labels instead of "may require two drops".

## Why

Sid ran the desktop onboarding twice with the Blender first task on a fresh Windows PC. When the add-on side was not set up, the skill failed or asked vaguely. On a fresh computer it must lead the user through setup, starting from the official page with the drag-and-drop install button.

## Verified against

- https://www.blender.org/lab/mcp-server/: button text, "you will need to do it twice", Blender 5.1 minimum, download / Install from Disk.
- Add-on source at `2cea8d566dde07fbac28a61d698909d69724e853`: preference labels Host / Port / Auto Start (default on), the **Start MCP Bridge Server** operator, "Server is running" / "Server is stopped", the error "Online access must be enabled in the system preferences", defaults `localhost` / `9876`, and the tool names and parameters of `get_screenshot_of_window_as_image` and `render_viewport_to_path`.
- Blender manual: Edit > Preferences, System > Network > Allow Online Access, Add-ons > add-on Preferences.
- `hermes plugins validate ./blender` passes.

No version bump: this is a skill-text change, like d3b8f33. The catalog pin is the release.

## Maintainer verification

Independently reviewed in the approved six-PR union (base `a4e311e`, core `5e908370`): 348 tests passed, 2 skipped; DirectSDK 252, Home Assistant 74, Spotify 22. Negative controls reproduce the affected DirectSDK and Home Assistant failures on baseline. Actual current-core Home Assistant target resolution also passes. All four affected plugins scan `safe` on current core and release v0.22.0; this is local scanner evidence, not an install-scanner CI job. No new paid-provider, device, or graphical-app E2E run was performed in this review.
