title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: fail closed when Claude Code is missing or logged out
body:
`ClaudeCodeMissing` (503) and `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` (401) mean native can't run where Hermes runs it. A retry won't help, and Hermes' default verdicts for those statuses walk the fallback chain. A user who picked this provider for their subscription then gets the turn answered by `fallback_providers[0]`, often a paid API, with exit code 0 (NousResearch/hermes-agent#132337).

`classify_api_error` now returns `auth_permanent` with `retryable=False, should_fallback=False` for both. The check is by class name because the Hermes loader and the flat test path import `directsdk` as two different modules.

This needs NousResearch/hermes-agent137928. On current Hermes the 401/403 escalation in `route_classified_error` ignores `should_fallback`, so this hook alone still falls back. Measured with `hermes -z` on v0.21.5, a fake `claude` answering "Not logged in", and a local fallback stub that counts requests:

| Change | Requests at the fallback |
| --- | --- |
| neither | 11 |
| this PR only | 11 |
| core PR only | 11 |
| both | 0, and the turn ends with the login hint (exit 2) |

Tests: a new `test_missing_or_logged_out_claude_code_fails_closed_without_fallback`. The full plugin suite passes against Hermes v0.21.5 (229 passed).

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: intermittently returns internal session_title JSON as the chat reply
body:
### Summary

`claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` intermittently returns the **internal `session_title` JSON payload** (`{"title": "..."}`) as the actual assistant reply to the user, instead of a real conversational answer. This happens on sequential (non-concurrent) turns within the same session, is not tied to any specific message content, and persists across a full gateway restart.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.7+500.g8f81791 (2026.9.24)
- Plugin: `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` v0.3.3
- Model: `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`
- Platform: Telegram gateway (systemd user service)
- `auxiliary.title_generation.enabled: false` at the time of the failures below (ruled out Hermes's own title generator as the source — see "What I ruled out")

### Reproduction (one session, sequential turns, each one fully completed before the next was sent)

| # | User message | Assistant row actually persisted |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Hola` | `¡Hola, Sergio! ¿En qué te ayudo?` ✅ |
| 2 | `Puedes ayudarme a organizar mis conversaciones` | `{"title": "Organizar mis conversaciones"}` ❌ |
| 3 | `Hola` | `¡Hola, Sergio! Sí, puedo ayudarte a organizar tus conversaciones con Hermes: buscarlas, renombrarlas, archivarlas o depurar las viejas. ¿Qué quieres hacer? ...` ✅ |
| 4 | `Wisp, caricatura infantil, novelas` | `{"title": "Wisp, caricatura infantil y novelas"}` ❌ |
| 5 | `Esas necesito` | `{"title": "Solicitud de esas cosas necesarias"}` ❌ |

Earlier in the same debugging session, the exact same request text ("Quiero limpiar las sesiones basura...") was retried 3 separate times (new sessions, gateway restarted in between) and got the JSON leak all 3 times, while unrelated short greetings sometimes succeeded — so it is not deterministically tied to specific wording, and not fixed by restarting the gateway (which spawns a fresh local `claude` CLI subprocess).

The leaked payload is byte-for-byte the schema Hermes's own `agent/title_generator.py` uses internally:
```python
_TITLE_RESPONSE_FORMAT = {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {"name": "session_title", "strict": True, "schema": {
        "type": "object", "properties": {"title": {"type": "string"}},
        "required": ["title"], "additionalProperties": False}},
}
```

### What I ruled out

1. **Hermes's own auto-title feature.** Set `auxiliary.title_generation.enabled: false` and confirmed in-process (importing `agent.title_generator` directly against the live config) that `_auto_title_enabled()` returns `False` and `maybe_auto_title()` bails before building any request. The leak still occurred afterward, so Hermes's title generator is not issuing the request that leaks.
2. **A one-time pipe desync that a restart clears.** Restarted `hermes-gateway.service` (fresh local subprocess) and the leak still occurred on the very next few turns, mixed with successful turns.
3. **Content-triggered behavior.** Reproduced with completely unrelated short messages ("Wisp, caricatura infantil, novelas", "Esas necesito") that have nothing to do with session/title management.

### Suspected root cause

`agent/title_generator.py`'s `title_upgrade_must_wait_for_turn()` only treats `provider in ("custom", "lmstudio", "local")` (or `custom:*`) as "self-hosted" (`_is_self_hosted_provider()`), and therefore assumes any other provider "multiplexes requests independently." `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` is **not** in that allowlist even though its `base_url` is `process://claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` — a single local subprocess, exactly the kind of single-slot server the existing guard (#117296) was built to protect. Whenever a title-generation call (or any other `response_format: json_schema` auxiliary call sharing the same local subprocess) *was* in flight — including from earlier in the day before I disabled `auxiliary.title_generation` — it looks like the shared local subprocess/client can end up serving a stale/queued title completion into a later, unrelated main-turn request on the same `shared=True` client, and this persists in a way a simple process restart doesn't reliably clear.

### Suggested fix

Add `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` (and ideally any provider whose `base_url` starts with `process://`) to `_is_self_hosted_provider()` in `agent/title_generator.py`, so `title_upgrade_must_wait_for_turn()` correctly defers/serializes any auxiliary JSON-schema call against this provider instead of assuming it multiplexes independently like a hosted API.

### Impact

Using a Claude Pro/Max subscription through this plugin is currently unreliable for real conversations: roughly half of my sequential test turns on one session returned the internal title JSON instead of an answer, with no visible error to the user — it just looks like the bot "replied with the chat title" instead of answering.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(directsdk): opt-in warm native session (replaces #29)
body:
Replaces #29: the same change, rebased on current main (`a4e311e`) with the fixes from review and testing on #29. #29's head is a NousResearch branch that now conflicts with main, and pushes from a fork can't update it. The full design notes and the original evidence are in [#29's description](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/29). Issue numbers there refer to the old `hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk` repo.

## What
An opt-in **warm native session**, default off. It is turned on by `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1`, or per profile by the `warm_session` setting.
- **Per call (main):** every `create()` spawns `claude -p --max-turns 1` and replays the whole history.
- **Warm:** one native process stays alive per conversation. With the flag off, main's code runs unchanged.

Hermes still owns every step:
- Each `create()` is one model step.
- Native `tool_use` comes back as Hermes `tool_calls`. Hermes runs its own hooks, approvals and tools; native parks each call on an SDK MCP server until the next step brings the result.
- Anything that doesn't line up falls back to the existing full replay: an ambiguous history match, edited or compacted history, a prompt, tool or model change, a cancel, a dead process, or unexpected output.

## Since #29
| commit | change |
|---|---|
| `554749c` | #29's change, rebased. `_native_env()` now calls main's `apply_config_dir(env)` (#59), so a profile's `claude_config_dir` reaches its warm native. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` was already in the warm reuse identity, so sessions never cross logins. |
| `d9f03e9` | (MakerFounder) Large tool results stay out of native's MCP persistence. Before, a result over 50,000 characters reached the model as a ~2.4 KB `<persisted-output>` stub. |
| `7e34d14` | (MakerFounder) Per-profile `warm_session` setting. A routed profile's `.env` never reaches the plugin in a multi-profile backend or gateway, so the env flag alone can't turn warm mode on there. |
| `3ca35d6` | A tool round over ~195,000 characters replays, because native's per-message result budget would rewrite it. A session parked on a long tool call is kept up to `WARM_PARKED_IDLE_SECONDS` (3600) instead of being reaped as idle at 600 s, and the pool evicts user-idle sessions first. |
| `3da2cd9` | Warm re-applies the first-turn reorder on later requests: the cache regression found on #29 (below). |
| `57cab95` | #26 (native's session-title request off). Without it, that request can take a step's admission, and warm sessions rebuild every turn. |
| `aa4f5da` | Drops an inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`. Started from a Claude Code or Claude desktop session, Hermes passed `claude-desktop` to native. Native then sent a summary request after every final answer; the relay denied it, and the denial discarded the warm session. Live: before, `denied=1` on each end-of-turn step and the next turn cold; after, `denied=0`, and the next turn reused the process. |

## Testing on #29
[HeshamaMohamed's A/B](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/29#issuecomment-6150547566): `hermes chat`, `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`, Claude Code 2.1.296, a chained 9-tool round, n=3 per mode and size, all answers correct.

| input per step | per-call median wall | warm median wall | per-call step 2+ | warm step 2+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ~57k | 76.5 s | 48.5 s | 5.7 s | 2.7 s |
| ~140k | 86.9 s | 51.7 s | 6.3 s | 3.0 s |
| ~273k | 100.2 s | 62.8 s | 6.6 s | 3.8 s |

It also found that warm wrote the whole first turn twice. The #77 reorder put native's first-turn reminder after Hermes' frame on request 1, but a live process replays message 0 in its original order on request 2. `3da2cd9` records request 1's reorder, with a hash of native's message 0, and re-applies it on later requests while the hash matches. That keeps warm steps and fresh-process replays on the same cached prefix. (Skipping the reorder on warm also fixes step 2, but then any fresh-native replay of the conversation rewrites the whole first turn.)

Live, n=2 per arm: Opus 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.292, a ~54k-token first turn with two tool calls, then a second user turn on a fresh native.

| arm | turn 1 step 2, read / write | turn 2 step 1, read / write | median cache write per run |
|---|---|---|---|
| #29 | 0 / 54.3k | 53.5k / 0.7k | 108.8k |
| skip the reorder on warm | 54.2k / 63 | 0 / 54.2k | 108.8k |
| this PR | 53.5k / 0.8k | 53.5k / 0.7k | **55.3k** |

## Tests
- Suite: 293 passed with warm off and with `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_WARM=1` (macOS, Python 3.11).
- New tests:
  - The fake native now keeps its first-turn reminder in live history, as the real process does.
  - A regression test asserts that message 0 is identical across a first turn, a tool round and a new user turn on one process, and that each request replays the previous request's prefix. It is red on #29's code.
  - Two #59 tests: the config dir reaches the warm native, and changing it rebuilds instead of reusing.
  - The env test now covers the entrypoint drop; it is red without the fix.

## Merge order with the other open directsdk PRs
- **#22:** conflicts textually with `3da2cd9` in `admission.py`.
  - Resolved on [`warm-fixes-for-29-with-22`](https://github.com/100yenadmin/hermes-official-plugins/commits/warm-fixes-for-29-with-22): 311 passed in both modes.
  - #22's wire eval passes on Claude Code 2.1.292 per call, and also with warm mode forced on (1 cold step, 19 reused).
- **#30, #32, #57:** they don't reach warm sessions as written. I'll port each one onto whichever side lands second (details in [this comment on #29](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/29#issuecomment-6106572268)).

## Limits
- Experimental and opt-in. Validated on Claude Code 2.1.286, 2.1.292 and 2.1.296; the control-protocol details are version-sensitive.
- Not tested on Fable, Telegram or Desktop end to end, Windows live, or the subscription meter (only API-reported tokens).
- These always rebuild, once each: `/steer`, compaction, edited history and a background-review fork.
- Each retained session is one native process (~100+ MB), up to 8 per pool.

Refs #29

title: fix(directsdk): silence the harmless broken-pipe traceback from native's pre-flight probe
body:
## What

Native (Bun's HTTP client) sends a throwaway warm-up probe (observed as a GET/HEAD to an
`/api/hello`-style path) ahead of the real `/v1/messages` POST on every turn. `Handler`
only implements `do_POST`, so `http.server`'s default dispatch answers the probe with a
501 via `send_error()`; native never reads that body and disconnects immediately, so the
write raises `BrokenPipeError`/`ConnectionResetError` while `send_error()` is still
writing it. `socketserver.BaseServer`'s default `handle_error()` then dumps a full
traceback to stderr, which is console noise in every single Hermes CLI chat using this
provider:

```
----------------------------------------
Exception occurred during processing of request from ('127.0.0.1', 37228)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File ".../http/server.py", line 483, in handle_one_request
    self.send_error(HTTPStatus.NOT_IMPLEMENTED, "Unsupported method (%r)" % self.command)
  File ".../http/server.py", line 555, in send_error
    self.wfile.write(body)
BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe
----------------------------------------
```

The 501 itself is expected and harmless to the real request — the archived
hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#17 already settled that the request still
succeeds regardless of the probe's answer. The only actual bug is the scary-looking stderr
dump for this exact, harmless, every-turn race.

## Fix

`_Server(HTTPServer)` overrides `handle_error()` to swallow only
`BrokenPipeError`/`ConnectionResetError`; anything else still falls through to the real
traceback, so a genuine `Handler` regression is never hidden.

## Testing

- `tests/test_admission_broken_pipe.py` (new): reproduces native's probe-then-RST shape
  with a raw socket + `SO_LINGER(1,0)` to force an RST before the response is read, asserts
  stderr stays empty, and asserts the relay still serves the real `/v1/messages` POST
  afterward. A second test proves the suppression is narrow: an unrelated `RuntimeError`
  injected into `process_request` still prints.
- Verified **red on `main`** / **green on this branch** for the new test.
- Full existing admission/directsdk suite (209 tests across the other 17 test files) passes
  unchanged on this branch.
- One unrelated, pre-existing test
  (`test_directsdk_admission.py::test_refusal_after_a_tool_call_reaches_the_user`) hangs in
  my local sandbox; it reproduces identically with this diff stashed out (i.e. on `main`),
  so it's an environment artifact in my sandbox, not a regression from this change — left to
  CI's clean environment to confirm.

## Context

Filed against the new home per the repo's own description ("Moved to
NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/claude-subscription-directsdk"); the original report
lived at the now-archived hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#17.

## Maintainer verification

Independently reviewed in the approved six-PR union (base `a4e311e`, core `5e908370`): 348 tests passed, 2 skipped; DirectSDK 252, Home Assistant 74, Spotify 22. Negative controls reproduce the affected DirectSDK and Home Assistant failures on baseline. Actual current-core Home Assistant target resolution also passes. All four affected plugins scan `safe` on current core and release v0.22.0; this is local scanner evidence, not an install-scanner CI job. No new paid-provider, device, or graphical-app E2E run was performed in this review.

## Infographic

![Plugin fix](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae65b6/Q8C17tVsaBPc1YoigbwZX_7j1UnXgH.png)

title: REA: reverse-engineer programs from Hermes (new official plugin)
body:
Hermes gets an official REA plugin that connects the pinned reverse-engineering server and its workflow skill in one install.

[REA](https://rea.tools) ([morluto/rea](https://github.com/morluto/rea), MIT) inspects native binaries, .NET assemblies, JavaScript/Electron applications, Android packages and other artifacts. This packages the upstream server, not a new implementation.

## Package

- `rea/mcp.json` pins `npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 mcp`; no `@latest` or setup-generated duplicate server.
- The upstream workflow skill is adapted for Hermes tool discovery, evidence paging, session reuse, and explicit confirmation before action tools. Native pseudocode is treated as inferred decompiler output, not original source.
- Native analysis gets a 900-second Ghidra startup deadline and a 1000-second Hermes per-server call budget. The explicit engine-environment recipe preserves both deadlines and the reviewed package pin.
- README, MIT/upstream attribution, card art and the monorepo index entry are included.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Updated package against merged Hermes core | `hermes plugins validate`: passed; install scanner `safe` |
| Earlier release scanner (v0.22.0) | `safe`, zero findings; scanner source verified against the release commit |
| Earlier clean install and discovery | installed/enabled; 172 registered REA tools including generated prompt helpers; schemas remain deferred |
| Earlier real Hermes JavaScript turn | model discovered and invoked REA analysis and evidence-inspection tools |
| Blind static analysis of official WinSCP 6.7 portable binaries | console launcher imported in 30.05 seconds; GUI default failed at 330.62 seconds, then imported in 663.24 seconds with the longer engine deadline |
| Independent source check after recording binary findings | confirmed launcher command, shared-memory/event IPC, registry subkey and automatic INI selection; source-only details were kept separate |
| Real Hermes/model native turn via Nous | first Ghidra query completed in 579.7 seconds; 14 REA calls, including follow-up decompilation/caller checks; results read back from the isolated session database |
| Native coverage | 28,701 procedures and 30,432 Ghidra-defined strings in the GUI executable; static Linux-hosted analysis only; the Windows targets were never executed |

The integrated run exposed Hermes' separate 420-second outer deadline. Core fix [NousResearch/hermes-agent#138491](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138491) is now merged as `f974222e69278b856b1b75053774e10014c4797b`, with fresh CI and 140 focused tests passing after rebase. Its executor regression also fails when deadline propagation is removed, while unrelated tools retain their shorter deadline.

The successful model probe's usage-based estimate was $0.02694368; all qualification probe sessions together were estimated at $0.06332388. Vendor-billed amounts were not exposed. Raw trajectories remain private.

## Admission and limits

- **Release compatibility verified:** v0.22.1 resolves to `297552a9d646119871391d202509822cd86330df` and contains core timeout fix `f974222e69`. The final package validates and scans `safe` against an export of that release. A real local-source install into an isolated home succeeds; release-code discovery registers 172 tools, preserves the 1000-second call / 900-second startup settings, and successfully lists all six REA prompts. This is a release loader/MCP smoke, not a rerun of the native model benchmark. Catalog minimum: `>=0.22.1`.
- **Maintainer approved the current disclosed action-tool policy:** 12 operations can run commands, drive applications/devices or overwrite chosen output files. The current candidate keeps the explicit skill-level confirmation instructions; it does not provide an enforced per-tool approval gate. Setting server-wide `trust: untrusted` would gate 165 of the 170 upstream tools because of REA's annotations, including ordinary inspection, so that behavior has not been silently enabled.
- No speedup or guaranteed progress UI claim. The model did not consistently announce the first-query wait. Ghidra still reports uncertain types and unnamed functions.
- Native Windows/macOS execution and action-tool consent adherence were not qualified. CI validation on those operating systems is not native-engine E2E evidence.
- The maintainer approved this plugin and [hermes-agent#138225](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138225). The catalog entry must be re-pinned to the final plugin merge before it lands. The alternative core-MCP proposal, hermes-agent#136423, was closed at the maintainer's request with a pointer here.

## Infographic

![REA plugin](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae4ee7/6QzEY86udBwLV2u0iUD4J_ZPclXXV6.png)

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] /usage reports "no Claude Code login found" when auth.adopt_external_logins is false
body:
**Plugin:** `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.3 (catalog sha `682b22d`), Hermes v0.21.7

### What happens

With `auth.adopt_external_logins: false`, `/usage` and `hermes usage` print:

```
📈 Claude plan limits
Provider: claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental
Unavailable: no Claude Code login found (run `claude` and log in)
```

while the same Claude Code login (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, valid, `claude auth status` OK) keeps serving every chat turn through the plugin.

### Why

`_subscription_token()` (`__init__.py`) reads the login through core's `agent.anthropic_credentials.read_claude_code_credentials()`. That function returns `None` whenever `auth.adopt_external_logins` is false — by design, so that core never seeds/refreshes the borrowed grant.

But the plugin doesn't borrow the grant for core: native Claude Code owns it, and `_subscription_token()` is explicitly read-only (its docstring already avoids `resolve_anthropic_token` for exactly the refresh-race reason). So the opt-out disables the usage readout without protecting anything.

`adopt_external_logins: false` is what `security.md#borrowed-cli-logins` recommends when the CLI runs alongside Hermes — which is always the case with this plugin. So the docs' recommended setup and `/usage` are currently mutually exclusive.

### Expected

`/usage` works with `adopt_external_logins: false`: the plugin reads the credentials file (and Keychain on macOS) itself, read-only, honouring `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `claude_config_dir`, without going through the adoption gate.

### Workaround

Turning adoption back on, which reintroduces the refresh race the switch exists to prevent.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(admission): keep native's per-request context stable across per-call replays (#40, #36)
body:
## Problem

In per-call mode each request starts a fresh native Claude Code process that replays Hermes' history. Diffing per-block hashes of consecutive upstream requests (Claude Code 2.1.299, Opus 5.5) shows two things native does on every replayed request:

1. **The date moves.** It strips `\n\nToday's date is YYYY-MM-DD.` from the end of its environment system message and sends `Today's date is YYYY-MM-DD.` as a trailing `role: system` message.
2. **The reminder moves.** On a new user turn, it puts its plain-text context reminder ahead of the newest user frame.

Neither appears in the next request, which has two effects:
- Each step's signed thinking is replayed without the context it was generated against, so Opus re-derives it (#40).
- The cache entry written at the previous turn's last step is not a prefix of the next turn's first request. The lookup falls back to the opening frame, so at every user turn the conversation is written to the cache again (#36).

## Fix

`stable_request_context` runs in the relay after tool-result restoration and before `pin_message_breakpoint`:

- **Date line:** a trailing system message that is exactly native's date line goes back to the end of the environment message, where native's opening request had it. A string stays a string. Other trailing text is left alone, because moving text that varies per request into the environment message would change the prefix from message 1 on every request.
- **Reminder:** on a new user turn after an assistant message, plain-text blocks before the newest queried frame are dropped, but only when that whole frame occurs exactly once. Native's own tool-result steps already omit this reminder.
- **Cache markers:** markers on removed blocks move with `setdefault`, so the breakpoint count never grows.
- **Left alone:** opening requests, tool-result continuations, assistant blocks (thinking, signatures, tool calls), top-level system/tools, and any unexpected shape all pass through unchanged.

## Evidence

**Live 4-turn bench (advisory; list-price equivalents from upstream usage, not subscription-meter readings).** Opus 5.5, effort high, 4-user-turn task, 20 s between turns. An equivalent relay transform behind a bench-only flag, compared with unfixed per-call on the same seeds (n=2):
- cache misses at user-turn boundaries: 3/3 → 0/3 per conversation;
- thinking tokens: 3.2k / 5.9k → 0.7k / 1.8k;
- list cost: 0.68× unfixed per-call, which is 0.78× headless Claude Code on the same seeds;
- after the move, the environment block's hash equals the opening request's, so the restoration is byte-exact.

**Live 10-turn bench with this PR's function** (advisory, same price basis). This PR's exact `stable_request_context` ran on a bench branch that also logs usage. Two tasks (incremental coding, reasoning over data files) × 2 seeds, 10 user turns each, all graded passes:
- cache misses at user-turn boundaries: 36/36 → 0/36 (unfixed per-call re-wrote 28–54k tokens per conversation);
- list cost: 0.76× unfixed per-call on the same task and seed;
- vs headless Claude Code: 1.03× the run in the same batch, 0.96× an earlier run (Claude Code itself varied 7% between them).

**Tests.** `tests/test_admission_stable_context.py`, 29 tests, run offline against a loopback upstream through the real relay. Cases:
- date move with string and list environments; non-date trailing text left in place; no duplicate date;
- marker transfer;
- reminder drop, including a frame whose first block equals the reminder; resegmented or duplicate frames left alone;
- tool-result continuations; opening requests; malformed payloads; idempotence;
- two consecutive per-call requests sharing a byte-identical prefix through the earlier step's prompt.

With the call site removed, that last relay test fails. Full plugin suite on current main: 301 passed (macOS).

**Not proven here:** subscription-meter impact (the numbers above are list-price equivalents), real user workloads, and Claude Code versions other than 2.1.299. If a later CLI changes the date-line format, the move simply stops firing and requests go out as today.

## Relation to other PRs

- **#22:** complementary. It keeps the open turn's start readable after a long tool loop. This PR removes the reason the previous turn's entry stops matching.
- **#99:** describes the same user-turn miss on Windows / Claude Code 2.1.285. Its proposed layout moves the date line back into the environment message and drops the reminder, which is what this PR does on current `main`.
- **#100:** independent and complementary (a stable `--session-id` for the scratchpad line). It touches `directsdk.py`; this PR touches `admission.py`, so they don't conflict.
- **#79:** closed. The warm-session bypass is removed (`381704d`); the transform now runs on every relayed request.

Refs #40, #36

title: Warm mode: after a session restarts, its next user turn re-writes the previous turn's tool loop to the cache
body:
**Setup:** warm mode from #79 (head `20098b7`), Claude Code 2.1.299, Opus 5.5 at effort high, pinned Hermes `71d34bad`. The test is a 10-user-turn bench with 20 s between turns. To force a restart at every turn, the warm idle limit was set to 5 s ("E" in the #79 summary).

**What happens:** when a warm session's native process is replaced, the first request of the next user turn re-writes the previous turn's whole tool loop to the cache, although that loop is still cached. A kept-alive warm session (C) doesn't do this.

After #79's `20098b7`, a restart happens only in these cases:
- a reply comes after the one-hour idle limit;
- the pool evicts the session (LRU);
- Hermes restarts.

So this is narrower than before, but it still costs a full re-write each time.

**Measured (list-price equivalents from upstream usage; 2 tasks × 2 seeds):**

| Warm session | Boundary misses | Re-written per conversation | Cost vs `claude -p` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kept alive (C) | 0/36 | 0 | 1.005× |
| Restarted every turn (E) | 36/36 | 30–60k tokens | 1.28× |

**Where the prefix breaks:** I compared per-block hashes of the previous turn's last request with the next turn's first request.
- **In all 36 E boundaries,** the first divergent block is the same 604-char user text block (same hash every time). It's the plain-text context reminder that #83 drops in per-call mode.
  - **Placement:** in 32 cases it sits ahead of the restarted turn's frame, where the dead process's native put it. In the 4 first boundaries it sits behind the conversation's first frame, where the relay's first-request move (#77) put it.
  - **On replay:** the new process replays that frame without the block.
- **Why a kept-alive session is unaffected:** native adds the block to the first user frame its process queries.
  - **Kept-alive session:** that is the conversation's first frame. #77 moves the block behind it and it stays there (in 227 of C's requests).
  - **Restarted session:** the frame is the restarted turn's, and the next restart drops the block from it. Everything after that point, i.e. the previous turn's tool loop, is then written again.
- **On the first boundary,** the replay also carries a 977-char `role: system` message after the first frame, which the live process didn't send.

**Why #83 doesn't cover it:**
- #83 skips relays whose `first_turn` is a dict (the warm path).
- Dropping the block only at the turn start wouldn't be enough here. The restarted process keeps the block in its live history, so its later tool steps still carry it ahead of that frame (173 requests in E).

**One possible direction (not tested):** on every request from a warm process whose first query was not the conversation's first frame, move this block behind the conversation's first user frame, where a kept-alive session has it. A restarted session would then send the same prefix as a live one.

**Not established:** whether that is the only divergence after a restart (I've only compared up to the first divergent block); real idle-hour restarts, as opposed to the 5 s simulation; and Claude Code versions other than 2.1.299.

Refs #79, #83, #77, #36

title: fix(directsdk): support /usage when adopt_external_logins is false (#82)
body:
Resolves #82.

### Summary of Changes

1. **Direct read-only credential retrieval**:
   In `_subscription_token()`, when Hermes core`s `read_claude_code_credentials()` returns `None` (which happens intentionally when `auth.adopt_external_logins: false` to stop core from borrowing/refreshing the grant), fall back to `_read_directsdk_credentials()`.
   `_subscription_token()` is strictly read-only for plan usage limits and never refreshes or writes credentials, so reading the existing Claude credentials does not trigger any refresh race.

2. **Per-profile config directory support**:
   `_read_directsdk_credentials()` now honours the active profile`s `claude_config_dir` setting and `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR`, resolving the limitation previously documented in `README.md`.

3. **Keychain handling**:
   On macOS, macOS Keychain is read when no custom config directory is configured. When an explicit custom config directory is configured, Keychain is skipped to avoid cross-account contamination.

4. **Documentation & Changelog**:
   Updated `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

5. **Tests**:
   Added comprehensive unit tests in `test_directsdk_account_usage.py` covering:
   - `/usage` with `adopt_external_logins: false`
   - `/usage` with per-profile `claude_config_dir` setting
   - `/usage` with `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR`
   - Keychain fallback and custom directory isolation

title: AttributeError: 'Admission' object has no attribute 'unrestored' on every chat completion
body:
### Summary

Every chat completion made through the plugin raises `AttributeError: 'Admission' object has no attribute 'unrestored'`, which surfaces as a 502 to the caller.

### Environment

- Plugin: claude-subscription-directsdk (installed from NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins, commit a4e311e)
- Claude CLI: 2.1.299
- Python: 3.11 (Hermes venv)
- OS: Linux (Docker)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install the plugin fresh from the official repository.
2. Configure it as a chat provider (any model, e.g. claude-sonnet-5).
3. Send any chat completion through it.

### Expected

A normal completion response.

### Actual

The request fails with:

```
AttributeError: 'Admission' object has no attribute 'unrestored'
```

raised at `directsdk.py` line ~779, inside the usage-normalization block:

```python
if admission.unrestored:
```

### Root cause

`Admission.__init__` (admission.py, `__init__`, ~lines 133-158) initializes `used`, `denied`, `request_id`, `status`, `failure`, `capture` and `error_body`, but never `unrestored`. A repo-wide search finds the attribute read exactly once (directsdk.py:779) and assigned nowhere. The README documents `native_admission.unrestored` as part of the response usage payload (introduced with the warm-session feature in PR #29), so the initializer appears to have been missed when that feature landed.

### Suggested fix

Initialize the attribute in `Admission.__init__`:

```python
self.unrestored = 0
```

This is on the hot path for every completion (the `native_admission` usage dict is built unconditionally), so the plugin cannot serve any chat request until this is fixed. A local one-line patch restores service immediately.

I searched existing issues/PRs for `unrestored` — only PR #29 mentions the attribute by name; no existing report covers the crash.

title: docs(directsdk): re-check subscription metering on Max with Opus 5.5
body:
Docs only. This updates the README's "Subscription usage" section with a re-check on a Max plan with Opus 5.5 and Claude Code 2.1.299.

**ELI5:** Your plan's 5-hour meter fills up at the same speed whether the requests come from this plugin or from `claude -p`. Interactive Claude Code fills it more slowly for the same work. The README says ~1.7x from a Pro / Sonnet 5 test; on Max with Opus 5.5 I measured at least ~2.3x. Anthropic sets that weighting on its side; the plugin can't change it.

**Changes:**
- **Heading:** the hard-coded "~1.7x" is dropped, since the ratio depends on the plan and model.
- **Sonnet 5 token figure:** "~0.6x the tokens" is now labelled as the Sonnet 5 comparison it came from.
- **New paragraph:** the Oct 14–15 readings, plus per-task token cost on Opus 5.5.

**Method:**
- I measured the list dollars spent between consecutive 0.01 meter steps, inside stretches of one kind of traffic. The plugin cost $2.70 per step and `claude -p` $2.87 / $2.44.
- The TUI figure (≥ $6.65 per step) rests on about one step, so it's stated as a floor.

Details, tables and caveats are in the summary comment on #79.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Warm mode: an empty tool result breaks the cached prefix (native rewrites it to a placeholder)
body:
**What happens.** When a Hermes tool returns an empty string in warm mode (#79), the kept-alive Claude Code process sends it upstream as `[{"type": "text", "text": ""}]` on the next request. On every request after that it rewrites the same result to the string `"(mcp__hermes__<tool> completed with no output)"`. The cached prefix therefore breaks once inside the turn. A restarted native replays the empty block again, so it misses a second time, against the placeholder the kept-alive one now holds.

**Scope.** It's rare. Hermes tools almost never return an empty string: none of the 131,827 tool results in one heavy Hermes profile's session database are empty. The cost is one re-write of the conversation per occurrence. Whether the real API accepts the empty block was not tested.

**Evidence.**
- A modified copy of the offline rehearsal (`evals/directsdk_cache_continuity.py`, on the fork's `eva-final` branch), in which one tool result (turn 2, round 2) is empty. It ran with real `claude` 2.1.299 against a synthetic API, on the plugin at `d218f63` (#79 + #83 plus fixes).
  - Kept alive: 1 mismatch, at the second request after the empty result, when native swaps in the placeholder.
  - Idle restart: 2 mismatches.
  - The same scenarios without an empty result: 0 mismatches (the standard rehearsal).

**Possible fix.** When the warm spawn builds its replay, substitute native's own placeholder for an empty result: `(<native tool name> completed with no output)`. The kept-alive mismatch comes from native's own rewrite, which the plugin cannot change.

**Not established:** whether other Claude Code versions use the same placeholder text.

title: Fix DirectSDK request cancellation and owned process cleanup
body:
Cancelling a request during body/history preparation could still start Claude after cancellation, an accepted local connection could stall the relay before its headers were complete, and a CLI that stopped reading stdin could bypass the receive timeout. On POSIX, reaping an exited launcher before cleaning its process group could also leave descendants behind.

Register requests before preparation, mark every registered cancellation token before dispatching cleanup, and unregister failed async submissions. Track relay sockets from handler setup, give stdin a dedicated writer with cancellation and idle deadlines, and retain the POSIX launcher until its owned group has been signaled or confirmed absent. Cleanup attempts continue after individual failures and report errors and pending owners; async cleanup waits keep the event loop responsive.

The patch changes only `directsdk.py`, `admission.py`, two regression files, and a bounded synthetic CLI fixture. It does not change routing, cache policy, account selection, or telemetry policy.

Validation on macOS / Python 3.14, with plugin base `c2a95963c442f3f23e4bc6fe0da898e1dd1fb63d` (v0.3.3) and isolated Hermes core `63d0b94120027d487c9a5235b9ec64b696af1b26`:

- Existing baseline: 209 passed plus 9 subtests.
- Final complete suite: 267 passed plus 9 subtests; all 58 focused lifecycle cases passed.
- Recorded red/green reproductions cover preparation cancellation, incomplete headers, blocked stdin, exited owned launchers, cleanup failures, batch cancellation, and rejected executor submission. Independent review found the last two gaps; their three additional reproductions failed before correction and passed afterward.
- Tests used temporary HOME/config directories, synthetic environments and Python CLI processes, mocked credential readers, an external-I/O guard, and bounded execution. No real Claude, account login, model calls, or subscription use. Final full run tracked 169 subprocesses with no live-process rescue and no extra threads at worker exit. Three relay fixtures already leaked in the baseline suite were closed by the isolated supervisor.
- Independent review and whitespace/secret/path checks passed. Local machine logs and prior investigation artifacts are excluded. A local merge-tree check against upstream `3a102d9a387983e9c95bf84379d08fa2492b1de8` was conflict-free.

Limits: POSIX group ownership requires usable `waitid`/`WNOWAIT`, default `SIGCHLD`, and an exclusive waiter for the private launcher. Unsupported configurations fail before spawn. Standalone `Admission.close()` still has no overall deadline; transport cleanup bounds each caller wait and explicitly reports pending resources, which does not guarantee those operations have completed. Linux, Windows, Windows descendants after launcher exit, and live Claude behavior have not been qualified locally; cross-platform tests are left to CI. Consumer pauses after completed output, assistant block-list history, config-reader mapping, and escaped telemetry-loader exceptions remain deferred; this PR makes no fix claim for them.

Initial upstream CI: [tests run 38711403810](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/actions/runs/38711403810) finished with `action_required` and zero jobs. GitHub explicitly reports that the workflow is awaiting approval from a maintainer. This is an approval blocker, not a passing CI result.

REA cannot be installed on Hermes v0.22.2, the current stable. That release was rebuilt from the 0.22 release branch and lacks the per-server MCP deadline (hermes-agent #138491, main-only, ships in v0.23.0). Its loader rejects `plugin.json` with:

title: rea: restore the 1000 s per-server timeout when a Hermes release with per-server deadlines ships
body:
## Restore the 1000 s per-server timeout once a Hermes release carries it

#90 (`69ea758`) dropped `extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.servers.rea.timeout: 1000` from `rea/plugin.json`. Hermes v0.22.2, the current stable, was rebuilt from the 0.22 release branch without the per-server deadline support (NousResearch/hermes-agent#138491, main only), so its loader refused the whole package with `server declaration 'rea' has unknown keys ['timeout']`. Until the timeout comes back, REA calls run under the normal 300 s MCP deadline, and the first native (Ghidra) query on a large binary can time out. In the WinSCP GUI test the import took 663 s.

**Trigger:** the first published Hermes release, patch (0.22.x) or minor (0.23.0), whose tag contains #138491. A patch counts only if that fix was backported to its release branch. Check the tag's tree, not the version number (that mismatch is what broke this):

```bash
git show vX.Y.Z:hermes_cli/agent_plugins.py | grep -n '"timeout"'   # must list it in the allowed server keys
git merge-base --is-ancestor f974222e69278b856b1b75053774e10014c4797b vX.Y.Z && echo has-fix
```

**To do when it ships:**
- [ ] `rea/plugin.json`: re-add `"extensions": {"com.nousresearch.hermes": {"servers": {"rea": {"timeout": 1000}}}}`.
- [ ] `rea/README.md` ("Native analysis wait budget", Requirements) and `skills/reverse-engineer-anything/references/connection-and-recovery.md`: restore the 1000 s budget text and name the release it needs.
- [ ] hermes-agent `plugin-catalog/rea.yaml`: re-pin `sha` + `image` to the new plugin commit and set `requires_hermes: ">=<that release>"`, so older releases get a clean "requires Hermes X" message instead of an install error.
- [ ] Live check: install by name on that release, then make a first native query on a large binary that runs past 300 s.

Related: NousResearch/hermes-agent#139201 (catalog re-pin), NousResearch/hermes-agent#139225 (future releases ignore unknown server keys with a warning instead of refusing the plugin).

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Replayed carrier usage trips Claude Code's local "Prompt is too long" gate right after compression
body:
### What happened, and what did you expect?

A directsdk session grows to ~160K tokens, Hermes compresses it (estimate after: ~90K), and the very next request fails with `Native API error: Prompt is too long`. Hermes then reports "server rejected as too large ... only ~90K tokens" and stops. No request reaches the API: the admission relay is never used, and the error arrives ~0.3 s after spawn. Expected: the compressed request is sent and succeeds. It does (see below) once native's local check is fed correct data.

**Cause**
- Claude Code gates every request locally. It takes the `usage` on the last assistant message in history (input + cache_creation + cache_read + output), adds a byte estimate of all messages after it, and returns a synthetic "Prompt is too long" once that reaches `contextWindow - min(maxOutput, 20000) - 3000` (177K for a 200K Sonnet window). The plugin disables auto-compact, so nothing recovers.
- `prepare_history` replays `carrier['messages']` verbatim, so every restored assistant frame keeps the `usage` of the request that produced it. This is still the case at `claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py` on 69ea758.
- Compression keeps the protected tail, so the last assistant frame still reports the pre-compression size (158,258 here). Anything sizable after it pushes native's count past the gate. Here that was Hermes' "STILL IN PROGRESS" restatement of the active request, which carried a large skill payload (~34K tokens): 158K + 34K ≈ 192K > 177K.

**Evidence**
We replayed the stored post-compression history through the plugin against a loopback fixture:
- Unchanged: blocked locally, 0 upstream requests.
- With `usage` removed from the replayed assistant frames: native sends the request (418,578-byte body).
- Against the real API that request returned 200 with 109,790 prompt tokens. A rerun read 109,600 tokens from cache, so the wire request is byte-identical: `usage` is local metadata only.
- A pre-compression 158K-token history also still passes with `usage` removed, so the gate does not start firing early.

**Suggested fix**
In `prepare_history`, drop `usage` from the restored native assistant messages (`native.pop('usage', None)` on the deep copy). Native then estimates from the history it actually holds, its gate stays meaningful, and the prompt cache is unaffected. An alternative is to keep `usage` only on frames after the newest compaction boundary, but the host does not expose that boundary to the plugin.

We run that change today as an in-memory wrapper around `prepare_history` (a gateway hook), so the plugin files stay untouched.

### Versions

```text
Hermes 0.21.5 (2026.9.24), config_version 49
claude-subscription-directsdk 0.3.0 (installed from the old repo, ef73726); same code path on hermes-official-plugins 69ea758
Claude Code 2.1.284
model claude-sonnet-5-5 (200K), compression.threshold 0.8, protect_last_n 20, protect_first_n 3
```

### Logs

```text
agent.conversation_compression: context compression started: session=cron_..._003011 messages=124 tokens=~160,234 model=claude-sonnet-5-5
agent.conversation_compression: context compression done: session=20261015_003638_fed778 messages=124->96 rough_tokens=~92,923 awaiting_real_usage=true
agent.conversation_loop: Repaired 1 message-alternation violations before request
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=RuntimeError provider=claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental model=claude-sonnet-5-5 summary=Native API error: Prompt is too long
agent.conversation_loop: Provider context rejection not explained by request size (~90,879 of 200,000 tokens); skipping compression: native api error: prompt is too long
```
Reproduced on 4 runs (10/14 16:49, 10/15 00:36 and 00:42, plus every scheduled run since 10/8).

title: [buzz] WebSocket idle timer kills healthy connections every 300s on quiet DMs — agent shows "offline" in Buzz UI
body:
# [buzz] WebSocket idle timer kills healthy connections every 300s on quiet DMs — agent shows "offline" in Buzz UI

**Plugin:** buzz (platforms/buzz/adapter.py)
**Version observed:** shipped with hermes-agent v0.21.7 (3569e846) and still present in v0.22.2 (d923a5eb)
**Impact:** agent presence flaps to "offline" in the Buzz client every ~5 minutes during idle periods, despite a fully healthy connection. Messages flow correctly the whole time; only the presence badge lies. Also generates ~12 reconnects/hour against the Buzz relay for no reason (we observed `rate-limited: too many concurrent requests` from the relay side as a knock-on).

## Repro
1. Connect the buzz platform (WebSocket transport).
2. Stop chatting for >300s.
3. Log shows exactly every 300s: `Buzz: WebSocket disconnected; retrying in 1.0s: no WebSocket frame for 300s; assuming the connection went silent`
4. Buzz UI presence badge goes/stays "offline". While actively chatting, zero disconnects (verified: 41 min clean during an active conversation, then exact-300s churn once idle).

## Root cause (verified by code reading)
Two independent facts combine:

1. `_ws_read_loop` uses `websocket.__aiter__()` and treats "no yielded frame in 300s" as a dead socket (`_WS_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 300.0`). The websockets library's `__aiter__` yields **only data frames** — its own keepalive ping/pong control frames are consumed internally and never reach the iterator. So a healthy-but-quiet connection is indistinguishable from a CLOSE_WAIT zombie.

2. The 20s `_ws_discovery_loop` (which looks like it should keep the socket warm) does **not send any WebSocket frames**: `_rediscover_and_subscribe` → `_discover_dms` shells out to the **buzz CLI as a subprocess** (`_run_cli(["dms", "list"])`). Nothing on the ws gets written unless a message is dispatched or a new conversation is adopted.

Net: with no inbound chat traffic, *nothing* produces inbound data frames, the 300s bound fires unconditionally, and the adapter churns a healthy connection. The comment block says the intent was a last-resort bound for relays that never surface closes (#98097) — but as written it fires on every quiet period, not just dead ones.

## Suggested fixes (any one)
- Cheapest: in `_ws_discovery_loop`, send a lightweight data frame each sweep — e.g. re-issue the kind-44100 membership REQ or a `COUNT`/`REQ` with `limit: 0`. A relay `EOSE` reply is a data frame and resets the idle timer. (NIP-44 relays answer these; ours demonstrably does for message REQs.)
- Better: track socket liveness from the library's own keepalive — a successfully answered `ping_interval=20` means the transport is alive; only force-reconnect when a ping *times out* (`ping_timeout=20` already surfaces this as an exception) instead of counting data-frame idleness.
- Or: reset the idle clock in a wrapper around `recv()` that observes `pong` frames via `websocket.pong`-aware transport hooks (websockets ≥ 12 exposes `recv()` control-frame filtering, but connection-level liveness is what we actually want).

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.22.2, Linux (Debian 13), gateway as systemd user service.
- Chronic: same 300s pattern present pre-update on v0.21.7.
- Knock-on observed: `Buzz: WebSocket disconnected; retrying in 1.0s: rate-limited: too many concurrent requests` — the 5-min churn reads as abusive to the relay.

Happy to test a patch or provide fuller logs.

title: fix(directsdk): drop replayed usage so compression does not trip native's local size gate (#92)
body:
## What breaks

Reported in #92 by @ARKrentals. A long session hits Hermes' compression threshold and gets compressed. The very next request then fails with `Native API error: Prompt is too long` after about 0.3 s, and Hermes stops the turn with "server rejected as too large ... only ~90K tokens".

That request never reaches Anthropic. Claude Code refuses it locally.

## Why

Claude Code checks every request before sending it. It takes the `usage` on the newest assistant message in history, adds an estimate of everything after it, and answers "Prompt is too long" itself once the total passes the window.

`prepare_history` replays our stored native assistant turns verbatim, so each one keeps the `usage` of the request that produced it. Compression keeps the recent tail. The newest kept assistant turn therefore still reports the pre-compression size (158K in the report), and a sizable message after it pushes the total over the limit.

## Fix

The replayed copy drops `usage`. The stored carrier keeps it, so nothing changes in Hermes' history or accounting. The fix is the reporter's suggestion, with credit.

## Evidence

This was run with the real Claude Code **2.1.299** against a loopback peer: no credentials, no inference. Turn 1's peer reports a large input size. Turn 2 replays that turn and adds a ~40K-token user message.

| Model (window) | Turn-1 reported input | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-haiku-4-5 (200K) | 170,000 | **0 requests sent, `Prompt is too long`** | 1 request sent, OK |
| claude-haiku-4-5 (200K) | 5,000 (control) | 1 request sent | 1 request sent |
| claude-sonnet-5[1m] (1M) | 975,000 | **0 requests sent, `Prompt is too long`** | 1 request sent, OK |

- **The request is unchanged.** On the 200K control and the fixed run, the upstream `messages` hash identically (`47dc19d3…`), so `usage` was never part of what is sent. The reporter saw the same against the live API: 109,600 of 109,790 prompt tokens were read from cache on a rerun.
- **The cache is unaffected.** `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` against the real 2.1.299 on this branch passes: 20 requests, every cached prefix replayed byte-identical.
- **Unit test:** the new `test_replayed_carrier_drops_native_usage_...` fails on `main` (1 failed, 3 passed in `test_directsdk_replay.py`) and passes here.
- **Full plugin suite:** 253 passed.

Merges cleanly with the open PRs #57, #58, #61, #77, #79, #83, #85 and #87.

Fixes #92

title: X Chat (encrypted X DMs) as an official plugin (moved from hermes-agent#68930)
body:
X Chat (X's end-to-end encrypted DMs) becomes an official plugin in this repo instead of a bundled core platform: `hermes plugins install xchat`.

Moved from NousResearch/hermes-agent#68930 per Teknium's decision; that core PR closes in favour of this one.

## Changes
- `xchat/`: the three commits from hermes-agent#68930 imported with authorship (adapter, X API client, Chat XDK crypto wrapper, `hermes xchat setup|register|status`, 51 tests), plus one packaging commit:
  - manifest name `xchat` (the catalog name), homepage, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`: every `PlatformEntry` field and `register_cli_command` the plugin uses exists in that release's tree (checked v0.21.5, v0.22.0, v0.22.2)
  - `chatxdk==0.4.1` (published 2026-07-20) + `httpx` declared in `pyproject.toml`, so the plugin install prepares them with consent. The core `tools.lazy_deps.ensure()` call is gone: on current core that is a retired shim that always raises, so the in-core version would never have loaded the SDK
  - `cli.py` drops its import of the private `hermes_cli.colors` module (validate flagged it under catalog rule 9) for a ten-line local helper
  - the docs page becomes `xchat/README.md` with install lines; tests load the dir as `xchat_plugin` through a conftest matching the other platform plugins
- `assets/xchat.jpg` card + root README entry

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest -q` in `xchat/` against core `origin/main` (py3.14, chatxdk 0.4.1) | 54 passed |
| `hermes plugins validate xchat` | passed, no private-import warning |
| Install scanner (`tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin`) on core main AND v0.22.2 | `safe` on both |
| Real install: `hermes plugins install file://<clone>#xchat --enable --yes-deps` in a scratch HOME on core main | installed, deps env built, `hermes xchat status` dispatches through the real CLI parser |
| Real Chat XDK in the installed plugin's own env, through the plugin's `XChatCrypto` | keygen, blob export and fresh-session re-import, identity/signing binding verify (tampered record rejected), conversation-key wrap for 2 participants, encrypt + sign, encrypted media round-trip, MIME sniff all pass |

## Live run against a local X Chat stand-in (no X developer account available)

A real `hermes gateway run` with this plugin installed via `hermes plugins install`, a real model (claude-haiku-5.5 via Nous Portal), and a local stand-in for X's chat API: simulated users run X's official `chatxdk` for keys, encryption and signatures, wire events are built the way X's backend builds them, and every request is validated against X's published OpenAPI spec (0 violations either leg). Each verdict is what the simulated user's own Chat XDK client decrypted and signature-verified.

| Scenario | PR head before (f224471) | This PR now (4bb2249) |
|---|---|---|
| First DM, opening a new conversation | no reply (swallowed as backlog) | replied, verified |
| Follow-up | replied | replied, natively threaded |
| Inbound image → vision | "I don't see an image" | "Red" (correct) |
| User's threaded reply | replied, no quote context | replied with the quoted message |
| Bot sends an image (`MEDIA:`) | failed: "no conversation key cached" | delivered; user decrypted a valid PNG |
| Access token expires mid-session | refreshed, rotated tokens persisted | same |
| Gateway restart, 2 DMs sent while down | each answered once | each answered once |
| `hermes send xchat:<conversation>` | "Could not resolve" | delivered |
| `hermes send xchat:<new user id>` (key handshake) | delivered, verified | delivered, verified |
| Events read in 30 idle seconds | 110 | 0 (10 conversation-list reads instead) |

X bills chat events per resource returned. The old polling re-read each conversation's newest 50 events every cycle, which at $0.01 per event comes to roughly $180 an hour at the default 10 s poll for one idle conversation if X re-bills repeat reads. X does not document whether that happens for chat events.

What the stand-in cannot prove: X's real server behaviour beyond its spec (field quirks, paging internals), billing for the conversation-list read, and anything only X's backend enforces. A real-account smoke test is still owed before calling this production-verified.

Other checks: suite 54 passed against core main; the plugin still registers on v0.21.5 (the new target-parser field is only passed where the core supports it); install scanner `safe` on main and v0.22.2.
