title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: a Hermes auxiliary one-shot pays no never-read cache write
body:
**What happens.** Hermes' auxiliary calls (compression summaries, session titles) send one user turn and no tools. Native marks that turn for its 1-hour prompt cache, and the relay moves the mark to the end of the frame. Every such call therefore writes its whole input at the 1h cache-write price, 2× input. No later request ever reads it:
- each summary has a different transcript;
- an LCM-style summarizer also puts a per-call nonce in the system message.

**Change.**
- **Marking:** the profile's `build_api_kwargs_extras` marks Hermes' auxiliary calls with a top-level `hermes_auxiliary=True`.
  - The hook knows them because `call_llm` reaches it without the conversation context the chat path always passes (`session_id`), or with an explicit `task`.
  - `request_body` accepts the kwarg and never forwards it.
- **One-shot:** a marked call with no tools and a single user frame is a one-shot. For a one-shot, the relay drops native's `cache_control` marks inside `messages` before its usual pass.
- **Unchanged:** system and tools marks stay, so a stable system prompt is still cached across calls. Chat turns are unchanged, including a chat whose toolsets are all disabled.
- **Safety:** content is never changed, and a payload that doesn't parse forwards as is.

**Measured** (Claude Code 2.1.299, Opus 5.5 `[1m]`, subscription login). Two consecutive LCM-X leaf summaries of ~10K tokens, sent through Hermes `call_llm(task="compression")`. Costs are list-price equivalents from native's own usage.

| | Written to 1h cache | Read | Per summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | ~9,560 tokens | 0 | $0.089 |
| this PR | ~605 tokens (native's system marks) | 0 | $0.054 (−39%) |

**Tests.**
- **Unit** (`tests/test_admission_one_shot.py`):
  - message marks go, while system and tools marks and all content stay;
  - unmarked or unparseable payloads forward byte-identical;
  - the hook marks only calls made without `session_id`.
- **Eval** (`evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py`, CI, real Claude Code) now ends with two single-turn requests:
  - the unmarked one, a tool-free chat turn, keeps its message mark;
  - the marked one has no message mark and keeps native's system marks.
  - It fails without the fix.
- **Suites and evals:** full suite passes (276). `evals/ci.sh` passes against 2.1.292.
- **Live check** through Hermes' real `call_llm` path (Hermes 0.22.2): marked, ~605 written, $0.054.

**Merges cleanly** with #83 and #100: the change sits away from the lines those PRs touch.

**Not covered.** How the subscription plan weights cache writes against its usage windows is not established.

title: fix(rea): forward REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON to the MCP server
body:
`inspect_recorded_crash` and `inspect_binary_layout` return `provider_unavailable` for every Hermes user today.

## Summary

Hermes starts stdio MCP servers with a filtered environment (`PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `LANG`, ... via `_build_safe_env`), so `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` never reaches REA, even when it is set in the shell and in `~/.hermes/.env`. REA's pwntools-backed tools then report `provider_unavailable`.

`mcp.json` now forwards it in the server env as `"REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON": "${REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON}"`, which Hermes resolves from the profile's `.env`. Unset, REA reports the same `provider_unavailable` as before. README says where to set it.

## Validation

`inspect_recorded_crash` on a real x86-64 core, called through the plugin's MCP server (hermes-agent main, Python 3.14):

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` in `~/.hermes/.env` and the shell | `provider_unavailable` | Evidence returned |
| `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` unset | `provider_unavailable` | `provider_unavailable` (unchanged) |
| `hermes plugins validate rea` | pass | pass |

In my sandbox `npx` can't reach the registry from Hermes' filtered MCP environment, so these runs launched the same REA 6.4.0 from a checkout (`node scripts/rea.mjs mcp`); the env entry under test is identical.

title: feat(rea): add a crash-triage skill (core dump + binary to root cause)
body:
Follow-up to the X thread with @teknium1: crash triage as a REA use case. Needs #97 for REA's core tools to work under Hermes.

## Summary

`skills/crash-triage/` takes the agent from a Linux core dump and the binary that crashed to a root cause and a paste-ready bug report:

- reads the crash with `inspect_recorded_crash`
- places the program counter with `inspect_binary_layout` plus `scripts/core_mappings.py`, a stdlib helper that decodes the core's NT_FILE note (REA returns it as raw bytes)
- uses gdb in core-file mode for a backtrace if present
- classifies the crash and writes a report that separates recorded, computed and inferred facts

It does not run the crashed program, even when asked to "reproduce" it: it proposes the exact command and waits for approval of that command, and in an unattended run only reports it. Hermes doesn't prompt before terminal commands, so the skill states this up front.

Skills only: no new tools, hooks or dependencies. Adapted from [crashlens](https://github.com/mingleiw/crashlens) (MIT); notice added to `rea/LICENSE`.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `hermes plugins validate rea` (main, Python 3.14) | pass; `load_agent_plugin` finds both skills, no diagnostics |
| Real Hermes session (directsdk provider, Opus), NULL deref on a worker thread | picked the skill on its own, called `inspect_recorded_crash` via `tool_call`, correct report citing the Evidence ID |
| 7 core types, core + binary only: NULL in libc, stack overflow, assert, SIGFPE, use-after-free function pointer, read-only write, multi-threaded | 7/7 correct root cause |
| "Reproduce the crash to confirm", agent allowed to run `./app` | without the skill 3/3 ran it; with it 0/5, all proposed the command |
| `core_mappings.py` vs gdb on PIE, non-PIE and in-libc crashes | same function+offset |

Not covered: AArch64 cores, C++/Rust/Go binaries.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: first call of a new user turn after a thinking answer still re-writes the conversation (real-API measurement)
body:
## What happens

On current `main` plus the stable-session-id fix, the first request of a new user turn misses the cache when the previous turn ended with a thinking answer. The read falls back to tools + system + first turn, and everything after is written again. Within a tool loop, every request reads the previous one fully.

The README notes that the synthetic loopback tests establish wire continuity, not vendor cache hits. These numbers are vendor cache hits.

## Measurement

Setup:
- Real Hermes loop (core 0.21.5), plugin in an isolated `HERMES_HOME`.
- Opus 5.5 `[1m]`, Claude Code 2.1.285, Windows 11.
- Turn 1: a read-only question answered after one tool call. Turn 2: a code change with several tool rounds.
- Request bodies dumped after `pin_message_breakpoint`.

| | Call 3 (turn 2 opens) read / input | Written |
|---|---|---|
| `main` + session-id fix | 9,559 / 17,903 | 7,959 |
| Alternative layout below (built on 0.3.0) | 16,402 / 17,449 | 1,043 |

- **Bytes:** in both layouts the bytes up to the previous request's breakpoint are identical in the next request (checked block by block).
- **Message breakpoints on `main`:** call 2's is on the newest `tool_result`. Call 3's is on the last block of turn 1's assistant answer, right after its thinking block. Turn 2's new user frame comes after it, then native's reminder and the trailing `role: system` date message.
- **In both layouts:** every other call read the full previous request.

On a long chat this miss happens once per user turn and re-writes the whole conversation each time.

## Alternative layout that hit in the same scenario

The alternative mirrors how native lays out its own sessions (captured from Claude Code 2.1.285 against a loopback API). Native keeps the date in its environment message near the top, and its single message breakpoint sits on the request's last block, which the next request replays. Behind the relay, the request becomes:

1. The newest user frame exactly as Hermes queried it, with native's reminder dropped. Today that reminder is only the account-email context; dropping it also keeps the email off the wire.
2. Native's trailing per-request `role: system` text (today's date) folded into its environment message after the first user turn. That message then changes once a day, as it does in native's own sessions.
3. The single message breakpoint on the last queried block, so the request ends at the breakpoint and the next request extends it.

With that layout, every call in the run above read the whole previous request (about 2 uncached tokens per call), including the turn opening after thinking. It matches what Claude Code itself shows for the same task.

This was one run per layout, and the alternative was measured on the 0.3.0 relay rather than ported onto current `main`. Happy to port it, add loopback tests, and repeat the measurement with more runs if this direction is acceptable. It overlaps `_keep_turn_mark` ([`4ac82ed`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/commit/4ac82ed00e2897001a15a2086907b09f64fe204b)) and the restoration path, so I'd rather agree on the approach first.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(directsdk): keep one native session id per conversation
body:
## Problem

With feature flags on (the `claude_code_telemetry` default), Claude Code adds a per-session scratchpad line to its environment message, the system message right after the first user turn:

```
Scratchpad directory: <TEMP>\claude\<cwd-slug>\<session-uuid>\scratchpad — always use it for temporary files …
```

The plugin starts a new native session for every request, so the UUID was different on every call. Because that message sits near the top, every request's cached prefix stopped at tools + system + first turn, and the rest of the conversation was written to the cache again on every round.

Native shows the line when the `tengu_scratch` flag is on (read from the 2.1.285 bundle: `scratchpadDirectory` is set when `qS()` is true, and `qS()` checks `x("tengu_scratch")`). With `claude_code_telemetry: false` no flags are fetched and the line is gone, which is why the problem only shows with the default setting.

## Fix

Start native with `--session-id`, derived from the conversation's system prompt and first frame (SHA-256, formatted as a UUIDv4). Every request of a conversation replays both unchanged until compaction, and compaction is a cache boundary anyway. Client rebuilds keep the same id. Different conversations get different ids.

## Evidence

The same two-turn agentic task was run through the real Hermes loop (core 0.21.5) with the plugin in an isolated `HERMES_HOME`:
- Opus 5.5 `[1m]`, Claude Code 2.1.285, Windows 11, `claude_code_telemetry` left at its default.
- 7 requests each run; request bodies were dumped after `pin_message_breakpoint`.

| Call | `main` read / write | With this fix read / write |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5,709 / 3,848 | 5,709 / 3,850 |
| 2 | 9,557 / 7,093 | 9,559 / 7,094 |
| 3 | 9,557 / 7,839 | 9,559 / 7,959 |
| 4 | 9,557 / 8,369 | 17,518 / 633 |
| 5 | 9,557 / 17,580 | 18,151 / 9,218 |
| 6 | 9,557 / 18,703 | 27,369 / 4,070 |
| 7 | 9,557 / 19,372 | 31,439 / 592 |

- **Scratchpad session ids:** on `main`, the 7 dumps carried 7 different ids. With the fix, all 7 carried one id.
- **Cache writes over the run:** 82,804 → 33,416 tokens. The gap grows with conversation length, because on `main` every call re-writes everything after the first turn.
- **Remaining miss at call 3:** this is the first call of the second user turn, after a thinking answer. It is a separate issue (#99), and it also happens with telemetry off.

## Tests

- Added `tests/test_directsdk_session_id.py`, in the style of `test_directsdk_workspace.py`, with a fake native that logs its `--session-id`. It checks:
  - one conversation keeps one id across rounds and across a rebuilt client;
  - different conversations get different ids.
- The new test fails on `main` (2 failed) and passes with the fix.
- Full plugin suite against core 0.21.5: 261 passed, 8 skipped, 5 failed. The same 5 fail on `main` in this environment: four `test_refusal_after_a_tool_call_reaches_the_user` cases (they need a newer core than 0.21.5), and `test_missing_claude_is_reported_on_every_path` (Claude Code is installed on the test machine). CI against current core should show this more cleanly.

## Notes

- Background-review forks and the main turn share a system prompt and first frame, so they get the same id and may run concurrently. With `--no-session-persistence` nothing is written per session except the scratchpad directory. This was not exercised under concurrency.
- An alternative would be stripping the scratchpad line in the relay. A stable session id keeps native's content unchanged, which fits the relay's "never edit content" approach better.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(directsdk): opt-in session mode, one Claude Code session per chat (replaces #79)
body:
## Summary

This adds an opt-in **session mode**. Each Hermes chat keeps one Claude Code session alive, the way Claude Code and Anthropic's Agent SDK (`ClaudeSDKClient`) run. Per-call mode stays the default. Machines without the RAM for even one session use per-call automatically.

This PR replaces #79, which was closed for three reasons: the process-pool surface, coupling to the control protocol across CLI versions, and memory per chat. Each one is addressed below with measurements. It builds on #83, now merged: session mode's restart fix uses #83's `stable_request_context`.

**Size, honestly:** the product code is +910/−128 lines (`directsdk.py`, `admission.py`, `directsdk_setup.py`, `plugin.yaml`), larger than #79. The extra lines are the RAM-sized pool, the restart fix and the per-call fallbacks below. On top of that: +422 for the offline rehearsal eval, +1,738 for tests, +39 for docs.

### ELI5

Anthropic keeps no memory between requests. Every request carries the whole conversation, and the prompt cache only makes re-reading a prefix it has already seen cheap. So the model never "holds" a session. What differs between the two modes is only which program builds each request on your machine:

- **Per-call:** for every model request, including each tool step, the plugin starts a fresh Claude Code, replays the conversation into it, and waits for it to exit. A fresh process lays some things out differently on each start (the date line, a reminder, a per-session ID behind a server flag), and the relay patches each one back (#83, #100). When a new difference appears, nothing fails. The cache just stops hitting and the conversation gets re-written at full price.
- **Session mode:** one Claude Code per chat builds every request, as it does in Claude Code itself, so the layout stays the same because it's the same process. After an idle limit, an eviction or a gateway restart, the session is rebuilt by replaying Hermes' history. That restart path sends the same prefix a kept-alive session would have sent, so the cache keeps hitting.

### When to use which

| | Per-call (default) | Session mode (opt-in) |
|---|---|---|
| Idle RAM | none | one Claude Code per active chat, until the idle limit or eviction |
| Local time per model request | process start + replay + exit (measured below) | ~0.03 s |
| Exposure to Claude Code layout changes | every request | only on a restart |
| What a broken CLI interface does | n/a | the step runs per-call; two failed launches in a row switch session mode off for the process |

## Measurements

**Setup:**
- Opus 5.5 `[1m]` at effort high, Claude Code 2.1.299, one Max account, macOS.
- Synthetic seeded tasks with graders.
- **Costs:** list-price equivalents computed from upstream `usage`, not subscription-meter readings.
- **Ratios:** against headless Claude Code (`claude -p`) on the same seeds. Claude Code's own run-to-run noise on these tasks is about ±10%.

**Cost and cache (10 user turns, two tasks × two seeds; ratios against the mean of 5 Claude Code runs):**

| Mode | Cost vs Claude Code | Cache misses at user-turn boundaries |
|---|---|---|
| Per-call before #83 | 1.26× (n=8) | 36/36 |
| Per-call with #83 (main now) | 0.98× (n=8) | 0/36 |
| Session, kept alive | 0.98–1.01× (two builds, n=4 each) | 0/36 |
| Session, restarted before every turn | 0.97× (n=4) | 0/36 |

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Cost vs headless Claude Code (10 turns, lower is cheaper)"
    x-axis ["per-call before #83", "per-call (main)", "session alive", "session restarted"]
    y-axis "ratio" 0 --> 1.4
    bar [1.26, 0.98, 0.98, 0.97]
```

On cost, then, session mode and today's per-call tie. The difference is speed and how each one fails.

**Live check on this branch's exact head** (real API, a 4-turn coding task, Claude Code 2.1.299):
- **Kept alive:** 13 consecutive request pairs, 0 cache misses.
- **Restarted after every turn** (1 s idle limit): 3 restarts, 12 pairs, 0 misses. Each restart's first request read the whole previous prefix from the cache.
- **Headless Claude Code on the same task:** 0 misses.

The restarted row in the table above was measured on an earlier build of the same restart fix; this check confirms it on this branch.

**Speed (wall time without pauses, 10-turn reasoning task):**
- Claude Code took 204 s, per-call with #83 345 s, and session mode 175–199 s.
- The per-request logs attribute 85–100% of per-call's gap to time spent outside the upstream call: ~2.2 s per request over 68 requests. Request counts, tokens and uncached prefill were the same across modes.
- A separate per-call A/B (3 seeds) measured 1.18 s of local time per request. About 0.6 s of it comes after the answer is complete: Claude Code flushes telemetry before it exits, and per-call waits for the exit. #102 makes per-call return at the answer instead. Exporting `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` would also shorten the exit, but in Claude Code it turns off feature flags too, so it isn't the fix.

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Local time per model request, outside the upstream call (s)"
    x-axis ["per-call", "session"]
    y-axis "seconds" 0 --> 1.4
    bar [1.18, 0.03]
```

**Memory:**
- An idle session native measured 114–166 MB physical footprint (216–309 MB RSS), growing with history. Live sessions on a long chat reached ~355–400 MB RSS.
- A per-call native holds 114–136 MB footprint, but only while its request runs.
- So the cost of session mode is that memory, held for each idle chat.

## What this PR does about each concern on #79

**1. Pool surface**
- Per-call and session mode now share one launch, replay and response path (`native_command`, `replay_history`, `tool_calls`, `_response`). #79 duplicated these.
- There is one setting, `session_mode`, plus an optional `session_pool`. #79's pool and idle knobs are gone; the environment keeps an override for the switch and a test-only idle override.
- The pool is sized from physical RAM: `min(session_pool, floor(RAM / 4 / 400 MB))`, with `session_pool` defaulting to 8. Below one slot (under 1.6 GB of RAM, or `session_pool` 0), the plugin uses per-call and logs why once.
- A full pool, or a session that fails before admission, serves that step per-call. Nothing is ever sent upstream twice.

**2. Control-protocol coupling**
- Session mode uses the interface Anthropic's Agent SDK uses for its long-lived `ClaudeSDKClient`: `--input-format stream-json`, `initialize` and `mcp_message` control requests, and an `sdk`-type MCP server. In the Claude Code changelog, none of the ~40 changes to that interface across 2.1.x is marked breaking.
- Tool results are paired by the `claudecode/toolUseId` key, which is Claude Code's own and not part of the SDK. Without it, the plugin pairs by tool name and exact JSON arguments, as native parses them. A batch with identical calls is rebuilt by replay instead of guessed.
- Two failed launches in a row switch session mode off for the process, so a CLI that changes the protocol degrades to per-call. A launch counts as working as soon as it reaches admission.
- `evals/ci.sh` now runs an offline cache-continuity rehearsal on CI's pinned CLI:
  - **Covers:** per-call, and session mode kept alive, restarted, forked onto another model, and model-swapped.
  - **Setup:** a fake key and a loopback upstream.
  - **Asserts:** every request byte-extends the previous one.

**3. Memory**
- The pool is sized from RAM (above), and idle sessions are reaped after an hour, the cache's lifetime.
- With the restart fix, a reaped session costs no cache, only a replay on the next turn. The idle limit is therefore purely a RAM-versus-latency choice. #79 originally moved it from 10 minutes to 1 hour only because restarts used to re-write the cache.
- On one real Hermes agent's turn gaps, a 10-minute limit would hold about a third of the idle sessions an hour holds, with 31% of turns restarting instead of 17%. I can lower the default if you prefer.

**Also:**
- **Externally reaped processes:** a session native collected by someone else counts as exited. An example is the Kanban dispatcher's `waitpid(-1)` from your review of #89. The session is retired and replayed, and the turn never fails. A test reaps the child externally.

## Tests

- **Suite:** the full suite passes with session mode off and on (423 each, macOS).
- **Rehearsal:** all 8 scenarios × 6 turns have 0 prefix mismatches on CI's pinned Claude Code 2.1.292 and on 2.1.299, each with an API-key login and an emulated subscription login (96 checked turns per version).
- **New behaviours, each failing with its code reverted:**
  - the RAM-sized pool;
  - the two-failure switch-off, counted from admission;
  - tool-result pairing without the ID: identical and out-of-order calls, and exact JSON as native parses it (`true` vs `1`, integers past 2^53);
  - external reaping.
- **Per-call:** behaviour is unchanged, guarded by the existing per-call tests.

## Not proven here

- Windows and Linux. The session measurements are macOS-only, and the Windows RAM probe has not run outside CI.
- Real user workloads, and subscription-meter impact. All costs above are list-price equivalents.
- Answer quality differences. Every graded task passed in every mode, so the tasks don't separate them; identical request bytes give the model identical input.

Refs #79, #83, #99, #100, #89

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): return per-call answers at Claude Code's result, not at its exit
body:
## Summary

In per-call mode, return the answer to Hermes when Claude Code reports it, instead of waiting for Claude Code to exit. Claude Code then finishes shutting down in the background.

## Why

Through the unmodified plugin, Claude Code (2.1.299, default `claude_code_telemetry` setting) emits its `result` event 11–20 ms after the relay has the complete upstream answer. It then spends another 0.63–0.73 s before it exits, flushing telemetry. `Client._run` reads stdout to EOF and calls `p.wait()`, so every model request, including each tool step, waits out that shutdown.

Exporting `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` shortens the exit too, but in Claude Code it also turns off feature flags, so it isn't a fix the plugin should apply.

## What changes

- **Fast path:** on `result`, the request returns immediately only when all of these hold; every other case keeps today's EOF, wait and exit-code checks unchanged:
  - the relay admitted the request and got a complete 200 answer;
  - `message_stop` was seen, with no native error and no denied retry;
  - the answer is not a refusal;
  - the result is a clean `success`, or `error_max_turns` with tool calls (the usual tool-step boundary).
- **Hand-off:** under the request lock, the request drops its process and relay before returning, so a later `cancel()` or `stream.close()` can't kill a native that is only shutting down.
- **Drain:** a daemon thread waits up to 10 s for native to exit, then kills it. It keeps draining stdout and stderr so native never blocks on a full pipe, and closes the relay only after native has exited. A late native request still gets the relay's `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED` denial, never an upstream call. An `atexit` hook kills anything still draining.
- **Trade-off:** on the fast path the exit code is not read. The answer is already complete at that point, and a native that will not exit is killed by the drain.
- **Kanban:** a foreign `waitpid(-1)` that collects a draining native (your review of #89) is harmless. The drain never reads the exit code, and `kill_process_tree`'s `poll()` guard does not signal a reaped group.

Product code: +91/−13 in `directsdk.py`. This touches the same per-call tail as #101 (session mode), so the two conflict textually; I'll rebase whichever lands second.

## Measurements

**Live A/B through Hermes:**
- **Setup:** real API, per-call, a 4-turn coding task, Claude Code 2.1.299.
- **Arms:** main against this branch, alternating (ABBAAB), 3 seeds each.
- **Local time:** Hermes' call latency minus the upstream request's own duration.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Local time per request, median | 1.18 s | 0.53 s |
| Local time per request, mean | 1.91 s | 0.98 s |
| Local time per request, p90 | 3.08 s | 1.87 s |
| Requests | 31 | 37 |
| Cache misses at tool steps | 0/19 | 0/25 |
| Graded tasks passed | 3/3 | 3/3 |

- **Wall time and cost per run don't compare:** the model took different paths per seed, so the request counts differ. Cost per request was the same ($0.020 vs $0.019).
- **Turn-open misses:** both arms show main's known misses at user-turn boundaries (6/9 and 7/9). #83 fixes those; this PR doesn't touch them.

## Tests

- **New tests (6), fake natives through the real relay, each failing without the fast path:**
  - result then a 30 s sleep: returns in under 1 s, and native is killed at the grace period;
  - a tool step with `error_max_turns` and exit 1, returned without reading the exit code;
  - a foreign reaper looping `waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)` during the drain;
  - `stream.close()` / `cancel()` after the final chunk leave the drain alone, and before `result` they still kill;
  - each ineligible case (non-success, native error, unused or denied admission, refusal, incomplete or non-200 capture, missing `message_stop`) keeps today's path;
  - the `atexit` hook kills a draining native.
- **Suite:** 278 passed (macOS). No existing test's expectation changed.
- **Offline evals:** `evals/ci.sh` passes on CI's pinned Claude Code 2.1.292 and on 2.1.299.
- **Unrelated flake:** `test_a_real_handler_bug_still_prints` now waits up to 5 s for the handler's traceback instead of sleeping a fixed 0.3 s. A Windows runner on this PR printed only half of it in time.

## Not proven here

- Windows. The kill path there is the existing `taskkill /T`, unchanged, but this branch hasn't run it outside CI.
- The `atexit` hook covers normal interpreter exit, not `os._exit` or an unhandled SIGTERM.

Refs #89

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: short model names 404 and fall back
body:
## What happens

`/model sonnet-5-5` stores the short name as the session route. `native_model()` in `claude-subscription-directsdk/model_catalog.py` only rewrites the bare family aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`), so the CLI is invoked with `--model sonnet-5-5` and answers `HTTP 404: model: sonnet-5-5`. A 404 is a hard failure, so Hermes abandons the provider and falls back to the next one in the fallback chain. The same applies to `sonnet-5.5` and the equivalent spellings of `opus` and `haiku`.

Observed on 2026-10-16: 15 calls to `sonnet-5-5` each failed three times and fell back to `grok-4.7`. The full ids (`claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`) worked on the same subscription throughout, so this is not a credit or rate-limit problem. The `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED` error that rides along is the gate refusing the CLI's own retries of the failed call, not a separate fault.

## Fix

A short name that names a pinned route should resolve to it: add the missing `claude-` prefix and swap a dotted version separator for the hyphenated spelling the catalog uses. A name that matches nothing should still pass through, so an unknown route fails at the CLI instead of being guessed at. `accepts_thinking_disable()` and `supports_adaptive_thinking()` need the same resolution, or a short name gets the wrong thinking policy.

I have this implemented and tested against the archived repo (4 passed in `tests/test_directsdk_models.py`, including the fake-CLI argv check for `sonnet-5-5`, `sonnet-5.5`, `opus-5-5` and `haiku-5.5`). That repo is archived and read-only, so the pull request could not be opened there. The branch is `fix/short-model-alias` on `thejoshbq/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk`; the diff against this monorepo's `claude-subscription-directsdk/model_catalog.py` is the same change. Happy to re-raise it as a PR here if that is more useful.

title: fix(directsdk): make stall watchdog sound for omitted-thinking calls
body: Rebase of #60 onto main with the watchdog made sound for omitted-thinking models: pings count as progress only while a thinking block is open, so healthy silent thinks survive while pure ping stalls are still killed. Adds omitted-thinking test.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: short model names (sonnet-5-5, opus-4.8, haiku-4.5) resolve to their pinned routes
body:
## What users see

`/model sonnet-5-5` (also `sonnet-5.5`, `opus-5-5`, `haiku-4.5`, and so on) reaches Claude Code exactly as typed. Claude Code answers `HTTP 404: model: …`, and Hermes drops the provider and moves down the fallback chain. Only bare aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`) and full ids worked.

## Fix

`model_catalog._route_base` maps a short name to its pinned route before `native_model()`, `accepts_thinking_disable()` and `supports_adaptive_thinking()` look it up. It swaps a dotted version separator for the hyphen and adds the missing `claude-` prefix when the result names a pinned id or an alias. A name that matches nothing still passes through unchanged, so an unknown route fails at the CLI rather than being guessed.

- Commit 1 is @thejoshbq's fix from #103, with authorship kept. It was written against the archived standalone repo; the version bump in `plugin.yaml`/`pyproject.toml` is dropped here.
- Commit 2, ours: `haiku-4-5` / `haiku-4.5` still went through verbatim, because the `claude-` form of that name is an alias, not a pinned id. The resolver now checks both tables. Tests cover `haiku-4-5`, `haiku-4.5` and `opus-4.8`, and there is a changelog line.

## Evidence

- **A/B, unit:** this branch's `tests/test_directsdk_models.py` run over `main` fails 3 of 4 tests (argv check for the short names, plus the Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 thinking-policy checks). The full plugin suite on this branch passes: 302 tests, core origin/main `0ab43d4f`, py3.14.
- **Live, real Claude subscription, Claude Code 2.1.299:** `model='haiku-5-5'` on `main` gives `ClaudeAPIError` with `first upstream attempt: status 404`. The same call on this branch answers `ok`.

Fixes #103

Co-authored-by: Josh Boquiren <thejoshbq@proton.me>

title: fix(directsdk): cancellation, bounded relay/stdin I/O, launcher group cleanup (slim redo of #89)
body:
Slim redo of #89 by @shanelic (Co-authored-by kept on the commit). #89 is +1287/-47 and conflicts with main. It also adds an ownership check that fails successful turns inside a gateway. This PR keeps the five bugs its tests reproduced on main and drops the cleanup-error machinery: +91/-16 in `directsdk.py` and `admission.py`, plus #89's lifecycle test file and fixture CLI.

What users get:
- **A cancel during request preparation now stops the call.** Before, the request was registered only after its history was built, so a cancel during that phase was missed and Claude Code started anyway.
- **Cancelling one async call no longer kills the others.** An async `CancelledError` used to call `self.cancel()` on the shared client; it now cancels only its own request.
- **The relay can always shut down.** It applies its timeout and abort from the moment a connection is accepted (#89's `setup`/`finish` hunk, verbatim). A partial request line or partial headers can no longer block `Admission.close()`.
- **A child that stops reading stdin can't hang the turn.** Each stdin write has a timer that cancels the request at the timeout.
- **An exited launcher's child processes get killed.** The group kill now checks the leader with `waitid(WNOWAIT)` instead of `poll()`, and the reader kills the group before reaping it. If the leader was already reaped by someone else, the plugin skips the group kill instead of failing the turn.

Why not #89 as written: core's Kanban dispatcher runs `os.waitpid(-1, WNOHANG)` every tick and collects any exited child. #89 raises "group leader was reaped outside its owner" when that happens. #89 also refuses to spawn when a SIGCHLD handler is installed.

Evidence (core origin/main, scratch py3.14):

| check | main | #89 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| plugin suite + #89 lifecycle tests | lifecycle tests: 16 red | green on its old base | 323 passed |
| reaper probe (spawn, `waitpid(-1)` takes the leader, then owner wait/poll/cancel) | ok | wait/poll/kill raise, cancel → `ClaudeCleanupError` | ok |
| 40 × `_create` with a 0.5 ms `waitpid(-1)` reaper | 40/40 | 35/40 (5 answers turned into errors) | 40/40 |
| real Claude Code 2.1.302 vs a loopback upstream, reaper on | answers | — | answers 2/2 |

Dropped from #89: `test_owner_failure_regressions.py`, plus the `[wait]`/`[poll]` variants of the launcher test, which assert #89's `_OwnedProcess` API. `os.waitid` is missing on macOS before Python 3.13; there the old `poll()` guard stays.

title: fix(directsdk): /usage asks Claude Code for plan limits instead of reading its login (#82)
body:
Fixes #82. Supersedes #85 by @korowant (Co-authored-by kept on the commit).

**What users see:** with `auth.adopt_external_logins: false`, `/usage` on this provider said "no Claude Code login found" while chat worked fine. The plan-limits snapshot also ignored the per-profile `claude_config_dir`.

**Why not #85's approach:** #85 reads `.credentials.json` or the macOS Keychain from the plugin and sends that bearer itself. It does this exactly when the user turned off Hermes reading the CLI login. Catalog rule 11 says the plugin must not hold the CLI's token.

**This PR:** ask Claude Code. Its `get_usage` control request (`{"subtype":"get_usage","skip_behaviors":true}` on a one-shot `claude -p --input-format stream-json`) returns the same `/api/oauth/usage` body, fetched with the login it already holds. The plugin never touches the token.
- The call follows the per-profile `claude_config_dir`, the same as every native spawn.
- It runs behind an unused admission gate, so no inference can leave.
- It finishes in about 1.5 s, inside core's 10 s hook deadline.

Each failure returns an `Unavailable:` reason instead of raising: no subscription login, an older CLI without `get_usage`, a timeout, or quiet mode. Claude Code skips the fetch when `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` is set, which is what `claude_code_telemetry: false` sets; `/usage` says so.

Evidence:

| check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| live `/usage` through core's `fetch_account_usage`, real Claude Code 2.1.302, real Pro login dir via `claude_config_dir`, `adopt_external_logins: false` | `Unavailable: no Claude Code login found` | `Current session: 98% remaining (2% used) …` / `Current week: 100% remaining …` |
| `get_usage` behind the admission gate | — | gate used: False (no inference request) |
| quiet traffic flag (`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1`) | — | `rate_limits: null` → reason line |
| plugin suite (core origin/main, py3.14) | 302 passed | 302 passed |

The tests fake only the CLI subprocess. Every core credential reader is patched to fail the test if it is called.

title: X Chat: message yourself to talk to Hermes, and say which account it runs as
body:
You can now talk to Hermes on X by messaging yourself, and every surface now says plainly that Hermes runs as the X account you connect.

Hermes runs as whichever X account's token you give `hermes xchat setup`. Until now it dropped every message sent from that account, so "message yourself" (the natural way to use your own account) did nothing at all. Nothing on the card, README or setup screens said that Hermes would be acting as your account either.

## Changes

- **Self-chat works, on by default.** In your chat with yourself, the messages you type reach Hermes and get answered. Hermes keeps a record of every message it sends (gateway replies, cron, `hermes send`) in `~/.hermes/xchat/sent_message_ids.json`, so it never answers its own replies or deliveries. Messages you send from your account in your other chats are still ignored. `XCHAT_ALLOW_SELF_CHAT=false` turns self-chat off.
- **Your account is allowed.** Setup adds the connected account to `XCHAT_ALLOWED_USERS`. The adapter also reports it to the gateway's allowlist, so installs set up before this change (allowlist naming only friends) start answering the self-chat too.
- **Setup says what is going on.** It explains the two setups (your own account, or a separate one made for the agent) and prints `Hermes will run as X account @handle (id)`.
- **Docs.** The README opens with a "Which X account does Hermes use?" table. The plugin description, env var descriptions and the repo README card all now say "the account you connect" instead of "the bot account". The card also shows how to ignore strangers silently instead of sending them pairing codes from your account.
- A new conversation started with yourself wraps its key once instead of twice.

The catalog card text in hermes-agent changes in a companion PR, which also re-pins the plugin to this commit once this merges.

## Validation

Live A/B: a real `hermes gateway run` with the plugin installed through `hermes plugins install`, a real model (Nous, Haiku 5.5), and a local X Chat stand-in built on X's own `chatxdk`. Every request was validated against X's published OpenAPI: 0 violations. Your own X app is simulated as a second registered device of the same account. Each verdict comes from what that app, or the friend's client, decrypted and verified.

| Scenario | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| You message yourself: "reply PINEAPPLE" | no reply | `PINEAPPLE`, signature verified |
| Hermes's own reply comes back around | n/a | not answered (self-chat stays at 1 exchange) |
| You DM a friend from your app | Hermes stays out | Hermes stays out |
| `hermes send xchat:<you>-<you>` (cron) while the gateway runs | delivered, not answered | delivered, not answered |
| An allowlisted friend DMs | answered | answered |
| Setup output | no account shown | `Hermes will run as X account @hermes_standin_bot (…)`, allowlist gets the account |

- Plugin suite: 55 passed. The new test (owner message answered, own reply and a cron delivery from another process never answered, self-chat off clears the allowlist hook) fails on main and passes here.
- `hermes plugins validate xchat`: passed. Install scanner: `safe` on core main and on v0.22.2.
- Not tested: real X. As before, this is the stand-in run only. It also assumes the real X Chat returns self-chat messages from your phone with the account's own sender id, which is how X's protocol identifies the sender.

## Infographic

![xchat self-chat](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaebc01/3Hbauu02XO79gKofwWoHv_kpDqL88t.png)

title: feat(rea): crash-triage supports stripped binaries
body:
Follow-up to #98. The crash-triage skill now works on stripped production binaries with no source: it checks that the binary is the one that crashed, names functions from the unwind tables, and walks back from the crash site to the caller that produced the bad value.

## Summary

- **Build ID check** (`core_mappings.py`): compares the binary's GNU build ID with the one in the core's copy of its ELF headers. On a mismatch it places no addresses in the binary, and the skill stops and asks for the right build. A renamed copy is found by build ID.
- **Stripped binaries**: names the function around each address from `.eh_frame_hdr`, which survives `strip` (`sub_11d4+0x1f`), labelled as derived, not a symbol. A function whose FDE end can't be decoded is bounded by the next function's start; nothing past the last one is guessed.
- **Walk back to the caller**: place the caller frame (return address − 1), disassemble it with `objdump --start-address/--stop-address` (reads the file only), read the code before the call, and confirm from the core's memory. When REA has a decompiler provider, `procedure_pseudo_code` is selected by `image_base + (start − link_base)` (the helper prints `link_base`), which works with the pinned rea-agents 6.4.0.
- The report gains a Build ID row.
- Standard library only. No new tools, hooks, dependencies or `mcp.json` changes.

## ⚠️ Known gap: REA's Ghidra tools can't be reached through this plugin

This affects the whole rea plugin, not only this skill: every Ghidra-backed REA tool (decompile, procedure analysis) is unavailable when REA runs from this plugin in Hermes.

**Why**
- Hermes starts MCP servers with a filtered environment, so `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` from the user's shell or `~/.hermes/.env` never reaches REA.
- rea-agents 6.4.0 (the pinned version) finds Ghidra only through `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`. It doesn't fall back to a `ghidraRun` on PATH (`rea doctor`: "GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is not set").
- Forwarding it the way #97 forwards `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON` doesn't work: when the variable is unset, Hermes passes the literal `${GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR}`, and REA validates it as an absolute path at startup. REA then refuses to start, so users without Ghidra would lose every REA tool:

    ```
    $ GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR='${GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR}' npx -y rea-agents@6.4.0 mcp
    REA configuration is invalid: GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR must be absolute.
    ```

  This PR tried that in its first commit and reverted it.

**What this PR does about it**: the skill doesn't depend on Ghidra. It walks back to the caller in the `objdump` disassembly and uses REA's pseudocode only when a decompiler provider responds.

**Possible fixes (maintainers' call)**
1. Have Hermes drop an env entry whose `${VAR}` stays unresolved, instead of passing the placeholder through. That fixes every optional variable for every portable plugin.
2. Ask REA to treat an unexpanded `${...}` value as unset, or to find Ghidra on PATH. REA's docs describe PATH discovery, but the pinned 6.4.0 doesn't have it.
3. Have users set it per profile today with a `mcp_servers.rea` entry in `config.yaml`. That replaces the plugin's pinned server, which the README advises against.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `hermes plugins validate rea` | passed, security scan safe |
| Helper on 7 stripped cores (NULL, stack overflow, abort, SIGFPE, rodata write, threads, use after free) | build IDs match; frames agree with crashlens (`sub_11d4+0x1f`, caller `sub_11f8+0x7a`) |
| Renamed binary / mismatched build / libc address / non-PIE binary | found by build ID / no addresses placed, warning / libc offset / link base `0x400000` |
| Live Hermes session (`hermes -z`), stripped use-after-free, no source | root cause named in the caller (free at 0x1239, chunk reuse, call through the stale pointer at 0x126e), confirmed from stack and heap in the core; build ID match and `.eh_frame` names reported; ASan rerun proposed, program not run |

Not proven here: the decompiler path (see Known gap above). AArch64 cores are still untested.

title: fix(langfuse): record the served model on the generation
body:
The generation is started with the requested model. `on_post_llm_call` already reads `response_model` (commented as "the model that actually served the request"), but only uses it for cost estimation. The observation keeps the requested model, so a trace cannot show which model answered when a router, alias or fallback serves a different one.

**Change**
- `_end_observation` accepts `model` and passes it to `observation.update()`. Langfuse SDK 4.15.2 `LangfuseGeneration.update(model=...)` supports this.
- `on_post_llm_call` passes the served model to the generation's final update. When it differs from the requested model, the request is kept in metadata as `requested_model`.
- With no `response_model`, nothing changes.

**Tests**
- 3 new tests in `TestModelAttribution`: the served model replaces the requested one and `requested_model` is recorded; with no response model there is no model update and no metadata; with identical models there is no `requested_model`.
- Each change was shown to bite: removing the `model` pass-through fails 2 tests, and removing the metadata line fails 1.
- 3 existing test fakes of `_end_observation` now accept `**_`, so they tolerate the new keyword.
- `python -m pytest -q` in `langfuse/` against hermes-agent core: 146 passed (143 on `main`). `hermes plugins validate ./langfuse` passed.
- Not run: CI on macOS and Windows.

title: REA: bump to rea-agents 6.7.0 (37 new tools; debugger/Frida tools on the confirm list)
body:
## What users get

The REA plugin moves from rea-agents 6.4.0 to **6.7.0**: 37 new tools, none removed or renamed, plus three releases of upstream fixes (Evidence retention when analysis or cleanup fails, JavaScript resolution and value flow, APK resource accuracy, browser and Electron capture cleanup, setup and config fixes). New in plain terms:

- **Read more file types without any extra engine:** Go build info (`inspect_go_binary`), Rust cargo-auditable dependencies (`inspect_rust_binary`), Electron fuses (`inspect_electron_fuses`), Flutter and Dart AOT build facts, HarmonyOS package graphs, WASM interface comparison. `inspect_sqlite_database` needs Node 24.15+ or 26+.
- **Bring-your-own engines:** packet captures (TShark), signal recordings (sigrok), WASM (WABT), GNU objdump, Ghidra byte-signature search, and the **Kuna** decompiler as a native provider.
- **Debugger and instrumentation bridges:** Frida (attach, spawn, inject scripts), persistent GDB and Rizin debugger sessions, Cutter/Rizin commands. These run or change targets, so they go on the skill's confirm-before-execute list (below).
- The bundled `reverse-engineer-anything` skill is synced from upstream v37 to v42: new target routes, summary-first paging views, Kuna, Fiddler and browser-scenario guidance. Our Hermes sections (connection, confirm list, recovery guide) are kept, and upstream's `setup`/`doctor` steps stay stripped.

Engines unchanged: node `^22.19.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`. 6.6.0 was tagged upstream but never published to npm.

## New tools and the confirm list

Annotations come from the real 6.7.0 server's `tools/list`. **Bold** = added to the skill's ask-first list (and to the README's "What runs on your machine").

| Tool | ro / destr / openWorld | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **instrument_with_frida** | F / T / T | Runs a caller-authored Frida script against a selected process (local or remote) |
| **start_frida_session** | F / F / T | Attaches Frida to a process or spawns one (paused) |
| **load_frida_script** | F / T / T | Injects JS into the target; can change memory and behaviour |
| **resume_frida_session** | F / T / T | Resumes a paused, spawned target, so it runs |
| **unload_frida_script** | F / F / T | Removes instrumentation from a live target |

Two more additions:

- **observe_native_calls** is now on the list. It launched the active Mach-O under LLDB in 6.4.0 as well; we missed it in the original list.
- 14 existing tools had `destructiveHint` raised to true in 6.7.0: the ADB mutators, `capture_process_scenario`, Hopper/Ghidra annotation writers, and `observe_native_calls`. The ADB and capture tools were already listed. The annotation writers only change REA's own session database, so they stay off the list.

Not done: Hermes still does not enforce per-tool approval. The list is model guidance, as before, and the README says so.

## Probe: real server, stdio `initialize` → `tools/list`

| | 6.4.0 | 6.7.0 |

| serverInfo | rea 6.4.0 | rea 6.7.0 |

npm publish times: 6.4.0 2026-10-11T04:02Z · 6.5.0 2026-10-14T12:56Z · **6.7.0 2026-10-18T08:12:05Z**.

No new `mcp.json` env forwarding: an unset `${VAR}` reaches the child as a literal string, and I did not verify how each of these handles a non-absolute value.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| Install scanner, core `origin/main` (6f572e1) | `safe` (findings: 2× `hermes_env_access`, the documented `.env` prose; same as the current pin) |
| Install scanner, latest stable `v0.22.2` | `safe` |

| Same on a v0.22.2 tree | installed, enabled; 209 tools discovered |
| Live Hermes turn (core main, Nous, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`) | 1 turn, 4 API calls: `tool_search` → `skill_view` → `tool_describe` → `mcp__rea__inspect_go_binary` (0.06 s) on fzf v0.74.5 linux_amd64 (publisher checksum OK, sha256 `c8d3ac08…293e8`, never executed). Reported go1.27.2, `github.com/junegunn/fzf v0.74.5`, 6 deps with h1 hashes, Evidence `ev_02ff8a84…`; all independently matched against the binary's buildinfo bytes. **$0.169** (provider models-API estimate; 27.3k in / 972 out) |
| tests.yml equivalent | `rea/` ships no `tests/`; CI runs validate only (passes above) |

## Hold

6.7.0 was published to npm at **2026-10-18T08:12Z**. Under the 3-day release-age practice (Hermes applies the same rule to catalog dependencies), this PR is held until **2026-10-21T08:12Z**. The catalog re-pin (`plugin-catalog/rea.yaml`, whose description also says `rea-agents@6.4.0`) follows the merge as a separate PR.

title: fix(langfuse): include the assistant role in generation outputs
body:
Generation outputs contain `content`, `reasoning`, and `tool_calls` but omit `role`, so chat viewers cannot identify the assistant and may label a tool-only response as `item 1`.

Add `role: "assistant"` to the full-message serializer, legacy text response, and summary-only fallback. The role comes from the hook's assistant semantics because normalized provider responses may omit it. Retain the existing reasoning and tool-call extensions, including the shared objects used to backfill tool results.

Regression coverage exercises all three output paths (including two parallel tool calls), checks the payload passed to the Langfuse observation, and verifies that the final trace output retains the assistant role.

Validation:
- New regression cases: 4 failed before the fix, 4 passed afterward.
- Full Langfuse plugin suite: **147 passed** on Python 3.14 with Langfuse SDK 4.15.2 (`HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1` for the isolated test runtime).
- Plugin manifest validation passed; it reports existing private-core-import warnings.
- `git diff --check` passed.

title: fix(directsdk): stop long tool calls looking like stalls to the Hermes stale watchdog
body:
## What does this PR do?

On its streaming path, Hermes decides a call is stale from the gap between chunks. While the model writes a tool call, Claude Code streams `input_json_delta` events and no text. The plugin read those events and yielded nothing, so the host saw silence for the whole generation, cancelled a healthy request when it hit the stale budget, and the conversation loop replayed it.

Now the plugin yields an empty chunk for every native stream event that has no text or thinking to show: `input_json_delta`, `signature_delta`, and block starts and stops. Pings stay silent. A ping tells you the connection is open, not that the model is working, and if it counted as progress, a stall that keeps pinging could never be cancelled. Final responses don't change.

This is the other half of NousResearch/hermes-agent#124566 and #31, which send this provider down the streaming path where chunks count as liveness. They fix long text and thinking, but not tool calls, because the plugin had nothing to emit for those. On current `main` this PR does nothing on its own, since the non-streaming path discards chunks. It needs both of them: I ran it with NousResearch/hermes-agent#124566 but without #31, and the host still didn't stream.

Not covered: I only tested against a synthetic child, so the event shapes come from Anthropic's streaming docs and not from a captured live session. Neither layer caps the wall-clock time of a streaming request, so a child that emits events forever is never killed. A real stall is still retried up to `HERMES_STREAM_STALE_GIVEUP` times (default 5). I left the cap and the retry classification alone because both change behavior for everyone. Per AGENTS.md this also reaches users only after the catalog pin moves, and I haven't opened that PR.

## Related Issue

Refs #35 and NousResearch/hermes-agent#125095. I didn't write `Fixes`, because closing either one also takes hermes-agent#124566 and #31.

#60 and #104 add a stall kill inside the plugin, and both also treat pings as non-progress, which matches this PR. They change the same part of `directsdk.py`, and my patch doesn't apply as-is on either current head, so whichever lands second will probably need a rebase. This PR doesn't depend on them.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py` (+6): in the `stream_event` handling, yield an empty chunk for any event other than `message_stop` or `ping` that has no text or thinking delta.
- `claude-subscription-directsdk/CHANGELOG.md` (+1): one line under 0.3.1, Fixed.
- `claude-subscription-directsdk/tests/test_native_progress_liveness.py` and `tests/fixtures/progress_cli.py` (+170): six tests against a synthetic stream-json child. No Claude import, credentials or network.

## How to Test

1. From `claude-subscription-directsdk/`, with hermes-agent checked out beside this repo: `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=../../hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest tests/test_native_progress_liveness.py -q`. All six pass. With `directsdk.py` from `main`, `test_tool_argument_progress_is_visible_before_the_final_chunk` fails with "tool-call argument generation produced no chunk the host can see".
2. Run the whole plugin suite the same way, without the file name. Against hermes-agent `5480918`, `main` gives 335 passed and this branch gives 341.
3. End to end, with the real `AIAgent` and the real plugin loaded through provider discovery, against a synthetic child that stays busy for 7 s, with a 3 s stale budget:

| hermes-agent | plugin | child | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | `main` | text, cron | `TimeoutError` at 3.09 s |
| `main` | `main` | text, cli | cancelled at 3.03 s |
| + hermes-agent#124566 | + #31 | text, cron | completes at 7.23 s |
| + hermes-agent#124566 | + #31 | tool-call arguments, cron | cancelled at 3.47 s |
| + hermes-agent#124566 | + #31 + this PR | tool-call arguments, cron and cli | completes at 7.08 s |
| + hermes-agent#124566 | + #31 + this PR | silent, cron | cancelled at 3.70 s |
| + hermes-agent#124566 | + #31 + this PR | pings only, cron | cancelled at 3.41 s |

For the "+ hermes-agent#124566" rows I merged that PR's head, `3cf49b0`, into core `main` (clean merge). For "+ #31" I added its one line, `profile.supports_streaming = True`, by hand. No child process survived any run. The harness needs a core checkout that has hermes-agent#124566 merged, so it isn't part of this PR. I can attach it if it would help.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) (and this repo's own `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which is the one that applies here)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate (in this repo: #31, #60 and #104 are related and listed above, and none of them does this)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits): one commit, four files
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: 341 passed in the plugin suite, run from `claude-subscription-directsdk/`
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs): this repo has no `scripts/check`. Its equivalent gate is `hermes plugins validate ./claude-subscription-directsdk` (CONTRIBUTING step 3), which passes. The private-core-imports warning it prints is the same on `main`.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Debian 13, Python 3.14.7. I haven't run macOS or Windows; CI does.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings), or N/A: added a CHANGELOG line. The README's note about the non-streaming watchdog stays correct until hermes-agent#124566 and #31 land.
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys, or N/A: no config keys changed
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows, or N/A: no architecture or workflow change
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility), or N/A: the tests start the fixture with `sys.executable -I` and an empty PATH, the way `test_lifecycle_regressions.py` does, and use no `os.kill`, process groups or other POSIX-only calls
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior, or N/A: no tool changed

title: fix(spotify): serve the loopback callback over https
body:
## The problem

Spotify deprecated insecure redirect URIs in November 2025 and the developer dashboard now refuses to save `http://127.0.0.1:43827/spotify/callback` ("this redirect URI is not secure"). `hermes spotify login` could not complete any more: `_validate_redirect_uri` only accepted `http`, and the loopback listener was plain HTTP.

The loopback flow itself still requires an IP literal (RFC 8252), so the only way through is to serve TLS locally.

## The change

- `_validate_redirect_uri()` accepts `https` alongside `http`, and `DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI` becomes `https://127.0.0.1:43827/spotify/callback`. Apps already registered with the `http` URI keep working.
- New `_loopback_tls_context()` generates a self-signed certificate for `127.0.0.1` once (SAN `IP:127.0.0.1, DNS:localhost`, key mode `0600`) under `$HERMES_HOME/cache/spotify-loopback/` and reuses it, so the browser shows the normal "not private" warning instead of refusing.
- `_wait_for_callback()` wraps the socket it already bound; the callback handler and core's serving loop are untouched, and browser handshake noise is dropped rather than printed.
- `cryptography` added to `pyproject.toml` (Hermes core already ships it), README updated, version bumped to 2.1.0.

## The trap this hit

Hermes calls `truststore.inject_into_ssl()` at startup, which replaces `ssl.SSLContext` with a subclass that verifies the **peer** certificate. On a server socket there is no peer certificate yet, so the first `wrap_socket(server_side=True)` raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_unverified_chain'`. `_server_ssl_context_class()` uses the stdlib class (truststore keeps it as `_original_SSLContext`) when the shim is active — that bug is also why this needed testing through the real CLI rather than the repo venv.

## Verification

- `pytest` in `spotify/`: **30 passed** (4 of the new tests fail on `main`, all pass here).
- `hermes plugins validate ./spotify`: passed.
- End to end against the real Spotify API: login completed through the https loopback with a tunnel, and `GET /me` returns the account afterwards.

title: feat(meshy): official Meshy 3D plugin (MCP + Desktop viewer, animation, formats, progress, preview videos)
body:
Adds **Meshy** as an official portable plugin: Hermes can make, texture, rig, animate and 3D-print models through Meshy's own MCP server, asking before every credit-spending call. In Hermes Desktop, models render in chat and in a gallery tab with animation playback and a download menu for each file type. Generations show live progress, a status-bar chip shows your credits, and messaging users get a short preview video. Every option lives in **Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Meshy**.

## Infographic

![Meshy plugin](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaef50b/8l7JnwjCakkfr1W-PLEPb_ILIArnEs.png)

## What ships (`meshy/`, v0.4.0)

- `mcp.json`: Meshy's first-party server, `npx -y @meshy-ai/meshy-mcp-server@0.6.4` (stdio, exact pin, MIT). `MESHY_API_KEY` comes from the profile `.env`. `cwd` is `${PLUGIN_DATA}`, so downloads land in the plugin's data directory, never in Hermes' working directory.
- `plugin.json`: `trust: untrusted`. 21 of the 28 tools spend credits or write files; only the 7 read-only ones run without a prompt. It also declares the settings form.
- `skills/meshy-3d/`: workflow skill with Meshy's routing rules (cost confirmation, never re-create an uncertain task, pick the format first), plus:
  - **Pick the detail level**: the agent asks what the asset is, not for a triangle number. Smart Topology sized per asset (characters ~15k, NPCs 5–15k, weapons ~3k, props ~1.5k; mobile about half); Standard full detail for close-ups, renders and printing; Standard plus a remesh or a Blender copy when you need both. For MMOs, crowds and mobile it offers distance copies and smaller textures through the Blender copy. The comparison below measured the Smart vs Standard trade.
  - **Format by destination**: GLB for web, Godot and Blender, FBX for Unity, Unreal and Maya, STL for printing, USDZ for Apple AR, with unit scale and texture-packing notes for each engine.
  - **Delivery by platform**: Desktop gets a 3D card. Telegram, Discord and the rest get the thumbnail, the file as an attachment (size caps stated, signed link plus its expiry when the file is too big) and a preview video. The CLI gets the path plus the signed link.
  - **Optional Blender handoff** (`scripts/blender_handoff.py`): when Blender is installed, the skill offers an "optimized copy for game testing" (no additional Meshy credits). Blender runs in the background on an empty scene and never touches your own files. It reduces triangles only to a budget you approve, packs the textures and exports `.blend` plus GLB or FBX; `--lods 0.5,0.25,0.1` adds distance copies and `--max-texture 2048` shrinks oversized textures (frog, live: 7,964 / 3,981 / 1,592-triangle copies; a 1024 texture took the GLB from 3.9 MB to 1.0 MB). It then reopens both outputs to confirm they load, and flags rigs, animations and shape keys. It says plainly that decimation isn't clean retopology.
  - **Preview video** (`scripts/render_preview.mjs`): a 360° turntable, or the animation clip for rigged models, at 30 fps as H.264 MP4. It renders on the CPU with Hermes' bundled Chromium and ffmpeg (no GPU or Blender) and gets sent as a native video upload.
  - `scripts/glb_stats.py`: real triangle and vertex counts from the downloaded file, because Meshy's task JSON doesn't include face counts.
- `desktop/plugin.js` (built from `src/`, stock three.js 0.180):
  - **Inline 3D cards** with a **Download** menu: every file type Meshy produced for the task, saved beside the .glb at no credit cost.
  - **Animation playback**: play/pause, a clip picker, loop and a scrubber, in the chat card and the gallery.
  - **Gallery tab**: local models plus recent generations, with the same Download menu.
  - **Live progress chip** while a generation runs.
  - **Credit chip** in the status bar.
  - Rendering runs only while you interact, so 1M-triangle models don't pin the GPU.
- `dashboard/plugin_api.py`: serves the viewer, so the renderer never reads files or holds the key. It reads only model and image files under home or the plugin output folder, with symlinks resolved, and fetches remote files only from `https://assets.meshy.ai`. `tests/test_plugin_api.py` covers both guards; each test fails if its guard is loosened.

## Settings ▸ Plugins ▸ Meshy

| Setting | Default | CLI equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| Meshy API key | — | `hermes config set MESHY_API_KEY msy_...` (`.env`, never `config.yaml`) |
| Credit balance in the status bar | on | `plugins.entries.meshy.settings.show_credits` |
| Inline 3D cards in chat | on | `….inline_viewer` |
| Auto-rotate in the gallery | on | `….auto_rotate` |
| Recent generations shown | 24 | `….gallery_limit` (1–60) |
| Default detail level | ask | `….default_detail` (ask / game / mobile / detailed) |
| Blender optimized copy | ask | `….blender_handoff` (ask / always / never) |
| Blender executable | (auto-detect) | `….blender_path` |

A save applies at once, and a new key restarts the Meshy MCP server with it.

An independent review of `aefc972` found 4 P1 and 4 P2 defects; all fixed and re-run with the reviewer's own repro scripts. A second independent review of the fix commits found no P1; its two partial fixes and small items are closed in `d550e89` (preview names include the clip position, a failed Blender move reports what was saved).

| Finding | Fix | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Preview video: a GLB clip named `../../x` overwrote a file outside the videos folder | clip/file names become a slug; default output must stay in `cache/videos/meshy` | reviewer's escape probe: sentinel unchanged |
| Concurrent provenance POSTs (and asset-index updates) lost records | one lock + per-writer atomic temp file for both stores | new test covers both: red on old code, green now |
| Two tasks shared one download folder (8-char UUIDv7 prefix) | `meshy_output/<full task id>` | same test |
| Background-profile completion saved to the active profile | the backend accepts a record only if the chat that made it is in its own state.db (409 otherwise); Desktop re-offers refused ones after each profile/connection switch | unit test with a real sqlite state.db (foreign chat → 409); live Desktop resize recorded under its chat |
| Switching clips with loop off paused the new clip at ~0.1 s | only the current action's `finished` ends playback | reviewer's Chromium probe: plays on |
| Blender `--force` wrote through a hard link to the source | `samefile` refusal | reviewer's Blender probe: source unchanged |
| A refused LOD step left files while saying "nothing saved" | outputs staged privately, published only when every step succeeds | reviewer's probe: no files; frog run still writes all 4 |
| Recent-generations model lost Next / Download / Made from | URL sources carry the task id | live Desktop: both present |

## Smart Topology vs Standard, both at 15k triangles (measured, 75 credits)

Same prompt or image each time, real API calls. Both routes were asked for 15,000 triangles, so the triangle counts match **on purpose**: the comparison is how each route spends the same budget. Counts are from the downloaded GLBs, because Meshy's task JSON reports none. "Shared verts" welds UV and normal seams. The raw vertex count in the viewer (19k vs 27k on the frog) mostly reflects how many texture seams each route cut, not geometry.

| Model | Route | Credits | Triangles | Shared verts | Parts | Good tris (median shape) | Slivers | Non-manifold edges |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ornate sword | Smart | 5 | 14,860 | 7,908 | 11 | 0.59 | 9.2% | 71 |
| Ornate sword | Standard + remesh | 20 | 15,337 | 7,666 | 1 | 0.60 | 8.3% | 15 |
| Frog warrior (image) | Smart | 15 | 15,929 | 7,948 | 8 | **0.70** | **4.5%** | **0** |
| Frog warrior (image) | Standard + remesh | 30 | 15,513 | 7,704 | 1 | 0.59 | 6.8% | 80 |

- **Frog:** the two meshes are almost the same shape; the median surface gap is 1.3% of the model's height. Smart's triangles are better shaped and it has no broken edges, but it comes back as 8 separate parts. At normal viewing distance they look the same, and Smart costs half as much. Meshy's image-to-3d task record doesn't echo `model_type`, so the only evidence the routes differed is the credit charge (15 vs 30) and the part count.
- **Sword:** the two runs produced different designs (different seeds), so this is a look at detail, not a matched pair. Standard keeps the carved runes and scrollwork; Smart smooths them away and leaves 1,154 open edges across 11 parts.
- **Takeaway:** the triangle target sets the count on both routes, and price doesn't depend on it. Smart gives cleaner triangles for characters where the texture carries the detail. Standard keeps fine carved detail on hard-surface pieces. The skill now routes by use for this reason.

![sword](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/6e6cf125808d0cbe0878b0a52fe6a87b/raw/20-sword-smart-vs-standard.png)
![frog](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/6e6cf125808d0cbe0878b0a52fe6a87b/raw/21-frog-smart-vs-standard.png)
![frog wire](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/6e6cf125808d0cbe0878b0a52fe6a87b/raw/22-frog-wire.png)

In a real agent turn ("low-poly treasure chest for my mobile game"), the agent quoted Smart Topology, about 8,000 triangles and 5 + 10 credits before the paid call. It then reported 7,768 actual triangles from the file.
![detail confirm](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/6e6cf125808d0cbe0878b0a52fe6a87b/raw/23-detail-confirm.png)

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `hermes plugins validate` (catalog CI, macOS / Linux / Windows) | passed |
| Plugin tests (`meshy/tests`) | 9 passed (2 contract tests through real core); each guard test fails when its guard is loosened (the parallel-provenance test fails on the pre-fix code) |
| MCP discovery + real call | 28 tools; balance call returns live credits |
| Interactive CLI, Desktop agent turns | approval prompt or card before every paid call; models render inline; chip tracks spend |
| Download menu, live | GLB/FBX/OBJ/STL/USDZ saved with byte sizes matching Meshy; bad format, bad task id, preview-only formats and paths outside home all refused |
| Animation, live | rigged knight: play, pause, clip switch, loop off and the gallery recorded on video |
| Blender handoff, live | portable Blender 4.5 LTS: gauntlet 1.75M → 50k triangles with packed textures; outputs reopen in a fresh Blender process |
| Preview video, live | real agent turn → `MEDIA:` reply → real gateway (Telegram SDK, stand-in server, strict media mode) → one `sendVideo`, byte-identical |
| Viewer guards | `/etc/passwd`, `.env`, symlink to `.env`, relative path, non-Meshy and lookalike hosts, `.exe`: all refused |

Meshy balance across every live run: 28,000 → 27,800.

## Requires

hermes-agent with NousResearch/hermes-agent#141478 and NousResearch/hermes-agent#141533, both merged. Two open core PRs improve it further, and the plugin works without them:
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#141970: cards whose attributes contain a raw URL render. Until it lands, the skill uses local paths.
- NousResearch/hermes-agent#141985: live MCP progress events. Until it lands, the progress chip polls every 4 s.

## Not covered

- Real Discord or Telegram sends (no bot credentials). Telegram went through its real SDK against a stand-in server; Discord's video upload wasn't exercised.
- Preview video and Blender detection on macOS and Windows: the code paths exist but weren't run.
- In one Desktop turn the agent quoted the cost and then went straight to the paid call. Hermes' approval card stopped it, which is the guard this plugin relies on (`trust: untrusted`).
- Catalog entry (data-only hermes-agent PR) follows once this merges, pinned to the merged SHA.

title: rea: forward GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR once a Hermes release drops unset ${VAR} env entries
body:
REA's Ghidra-backed tools (decompile, procedure analysis) can't be reached through this plugin today. Hermes passes MCP servers a filtered environment, so a user's `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` never reaches REA. Forwarding it from `rea/mcp.json` as `"GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR": "${GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR}"` breaks REA for everyone without Ghidra on current releases: Hermes passes the literal `${GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR}`, and REA refuses to start (`GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR must be absolute`). Found by @mingleiw in #109.

Core fix: NousResearch/hermes-agent#141379 (merged as `5fc490e2b3`). An env entry that is entirely an unset `${VAR}` is now left out of the server's environment, so the forward is safe once users run a release that has it.

**Trigger:** the first stable Hermes release whose tree has the fix. Check the tag's tree, not commit ancestry:

```
git fetch --tags
git show <tag>:tools/mcp_tool_config.py | grep -n "unset\|_drop_unset\|placeholder"   # the drop of a whole-value unset ${VAR}
```

(Compare against the merged code in #141379 to pick the exact line to grep for.)

**Then:**
- [ ] Add `"GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR": "${GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR}"` to `rea/mcp.json` `env`.
- [ ] Raise `requires_hermes` to `">=<that release>"` in `plugin.json` and the catalog entry.
- [ ] README and skill: Ghidra tools work when `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` is set in `~/.hermes/.env` (or the profile's `.env`); remove the "can't be reached" note.
- [ ] Live-verify: with it unset, REA starts with all tools; with it set to a real Ghidra install, one decompile call works.
- [ ] Re-pin `plugin-catalog/rea.yaml`.
- [ ] Also check whether rea-agents 6.7.0 (#111) finds Ghidra on PATH by itself; if so, note that in the README too.

title: fix(spotify): accept locale-prefixed open.spotify.com share urls
body:
Port of NousResearch/hermes-agent#102858, which teknium1 closed when Spotify moved out of core and asked to have reopened against the plugin repo.

`normalize_spotify_id` reads the url path by position. A share link copied from a non-English web player has a locale segment ahead of the type (`/intl-de/track/<id>`, `/intl-pt-br/album/<id>`), so the locale is read as the type:

- with `expected_type` (every playlist, album and save call in `spotify_tools.py`): `SpotifyError: Expected a Spotify track, got intl-de.`
- without it: returns `"track"` as the id, and the failure shows up later as a bad API call

`normalize_spotify_uri` gets both, since it delegates to `normalize_spotify_id`.

The fix drops a leading `intl-*` segment before the positional read. I matched on the prefix because that is how Spotify's router behaves, checked today:

```
/intl-de/track/<id>     302 -> /track/<id>
/intl-pt-br/track/<id>  302 -> /track/<id>
/intl-zzz/track/<id>    302 -> /track/<id>
/notalocale/track/<id>  404
```

A two-letter pattern would miss `intl-pt-br`. hermes-agent's desktop embed matcher (`apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/embeds/providers/spotify.ts`) already uses the same `startsWith('intl-')` rule.

Tests: two new cases in `spotify/tests/test_spotify_client.py` covering a plain `intl-de` url, `intl-pt-br`, a `?si=` tracker, the untyped call that used to return `"track"`, and a wrong type that still has to raise. Run against current hermes-agent main on Python 3.14, the same setup as CI: 26 passed, and `hermes plugins validate ./spotify` passes. With the guard reverted, the 4 new cases fail with `Expected a Spotify track, got intl-de.` and the other 22 still pass.

Not checked: macOS and Windows, which only CI covers.

title: fix(spotify): page through playlist items with an items action
body:
Fixes #11 (reported by @seong85).

`spotify_playlists` advertises `limit` and `offset`, but `get` calls `GET /playlists/{id}` with only `market`, so both are dropped. That endpoint returns the first 100 items embedded and takes no paging params. The issue shows this: every `get` call came back with `.../items?offset=0&limit=100` no matter what was passed, so tracks past 100 were unreachable.

This adds an `items` action that calls `GET /playlists/{id}/items` with `limit`, `offset` and `market`, using the same `_page_params` helper the albums `tracks` action already uses. Spotify's reference for that endpoint gives `limit` as 1 to 50, default 20, which matches `_limit`'s existing clamp. `get` is unchanged. The `limit` and `offset` descriptions now say which actions read them, so the model can tell to switch to `items` past 100.

`_page_params` moved up next to `_playlist_path` so it is defined before its first use. It is not otherwise changed.

Tests: new `spotify/tests/test_spotify_playlists.py`, using the same fake-client pattern as `test_spotify_play.py`.
