title: fix(telegram-business): don't draft replies to the owner's own messages
body:
Fixes #54. @lionskiy's report had the root cause, the fix and the test list. This implements it as described.

`handle_business_message` treats every `business_message` as a customer message. But Telegram delivers both sides of a business chat through that update. The Bot API's `Message.sender_business_bot` reads "Available only for outgoing messages sent on behalf of the connected business account", so outgoing messages do reach the bot. As a result:

- the owner gets a suggested reply to their own message
- an owner reply inside `debounce_seconds` cancels the customer's pending draft, because both use the `{conn_id}:{customer_chat_id}` debounce key, and drafts a reply to the owner instead
- a draft approved with ✓ Send comes back with `sender_business_bot` set and gets drafted again
- every owner message costs an LLM call

The fix: after the connection is loaded, return when `sender_business_bot` is set, or when `from_user.id` equals the connection's `owner_user_id`. Both checks run before the debounce, so an outgoing message can no longer cancel a pending draft. `handle_business_message` is the only place `business_message` updates go, so nothing else depends on owner messages reaching it.

Tests, in `TestBusinessMessageDraftFlow`:
- an owner-sent message produces no DM and no draft row
- a message with `sender_business_bot` set produces no draft
- a customer message followed by an owner reply inside the debounce window still produces exactly one draft, for the customer's text

The existing customer-message test still passes and covers the regression case. Against current hermes-agent main on Python 3.14: 44 passed, and `hermes plugins validate ./telegram-business` passes. With the `manager.py` change reverted, the 3 new tests fail.

Not checked: a live business connection. I don't have a Telegram Business account, so the update shape comes from the Bot API reference and the issue's report.

title: [homeassistant] fix: steer ha_list_entities to the area filter for room requests
body:
Stacked on #4 (base is `port/homeassistant-3`); once #4 merges, this retargets to `main` and shows the same one-commit diff.

## Problem

With #4's registry-backed `area` filter, room requests still went wrong whenever the model reached for `name` instead of `area` ("turn off the kitchen lights" → `name="kitchen"`). That is a friendly-name substring match, so it:

- missed lights whose names don't mention the room (a light named "Laundry Hall" assigned to the Kitchen area),
- included lights whose names do but that live elsewhere (a "kitchen counter light" assigned to the Living Room),
- and the model judged what an entity *is* by its name (skipped `light.kitchen_oven_switch_1` as "an oven switch") instead of by its entity_id domain.

Nothing in the tool text said rooms belong in `area`, so this is a description gap, not a code bug in #4.

## Change

Description text only, in `homeassistant/tools.py` (9 lines added, 1 changed; no logic, schema shape, env var or dependency change):

- `ha_list_entities`: room requests use `area`, not `name`; everything the area filter returns belongs to the room; the entity_id domain prefix says what an entity is.
- `area`: "use this, not name, for any request about a room".
- `name`: "not for rooms: use area, because names rarely mention the room".

## Evidence

Live Home Assistant 2025.2.5, 17 lights across 5 areas, `claude-haiku-5-5`, plugin tools loaded in a running gateway. Each trial asks for the lights to turn off in dry-run wording and scores the exact set of entity_ids returned.

| Scenario | #4 as is | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| "turn off the kitchen lights" / "switch off the lights in the kitchen" | 6/16 correct, `area` used in 5 | **10/10**, `area` used in 10 |
| living room, bedroom (2 phrasings) | not measured | **8/8**, `area` used in 8 |

Plugin tests: 106 passed, 2 skipped (same as #4).

## Limits, stated plainly

- One install, one model, 18 runs per arm at most, dry-run wording. Treat it as a strong signal, not a guarantee.
- It does not make a model act on entities whose *names* sound unsafe to switch (e.g. "Kitchen Oven Switch 1"): in real runs the model still sometimes asks before switching those. That is reasonable behaviour and I deliberately did not word the descriptions to override it; renaming the entity in HA is the fix.
- Not touched: `ha_call_service` (`area_id`/`label_id` targeting through `data`) is a separate follow-up.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] replay-ack error hides cancellation and native stderr
body:
## Summary

`directsdk.py` (v0.3.3) captures native stderr for most failure paths via `_stderr_tail()`, but the history-replay branch still raises a bare message and hides the real cause:

```python
ack = receive()
if ack is None:
    raise RuntimeError('Native exited before replay acknowledgment')
```

Two problems:

1. **A caller-side kill looks like a replay failure.** `receive()` checks `request.cancelled` at the top of its loop, but when the caller's watchdog closes the request, the child exits and the reader pushes `None` first, so the `ack is None` branch wins. The user reads "replay not acknowledged" for what was actually "your 240 s stale watchdog killed this call".
2. **No stderr tail**, unlike `Invalid native stream-json output` (line 841), `Native request failed` (959) and `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` (938), which all append `_stderr_tail(native_stderr)`.

## Reproduction

- `auth_type='external-process'`, non-streaming request with any replayed history (2+ messages).
- Make the native child slow to start or exit early — e.g. run the call inside a memory-throttled cgroup, or point `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` at a wrapper that sleeps before `exec`.
- Caller aborts at its stale timeout (Hermes core: `Non-streaming API call stale for 240s ... Killing connection`).
- Result: `RuntimeError: Native exited before replay acknowledgment`, no native output, no exit code.

Measured on a loaded host: 10 attempts across 3 sessions failed this way while 607 calls succeeded the same day; the route was fine, the child was starved.

## Suggested fix

```python
ack = receive()
if ack is None:
    if request.cancelled.is_set():
        raise RuntimeError('Claude request cancelled')
    raise RuntimeError('Native exited before replay acknowledgment'
                       + _stderr_tail(native_stderr) + f' (exit={p.returncode})')
```

(and the same tail on the `Native history replay not supported` branch). The intent is not to retry differently — just to stop attributing an environmental kill to the replay protocol.

Happy to send this as a PR if you want it.

title: fix(langfuse): stop counting reasoning tokens twice
body:
## What does this PR do?

Hermes counts reasoning inside `output_tokens`. `CanonicalUsage.total_tokens` is prompt plus output, and `normalize_usage` reads reasoning from `output_tokens_details` or `completion_tokens_details`, which are subsets of output. The plugin exported the full output and also a separate `reasoning_tokens` key.

Langfuse treats every `usage_details` key as its own bucket. With no `total` key it adds them all up, and when it infers cost it prices every key that matches a usage type in the model's price list. On a reasoning model the trace therefore shows reasoning twice in the token total. When the plugin sends no cost (in my run, a Codex turn on a ChatGPT login), Langfuse bills it twice as well. 63 of the 179 models in Langfuse 4.63.0's default price list have a reasoning price.

With this change the plugin reports reasoning as `output_reasoning_tokens` and subtracts it from `output`, clamped at zero. Langfuse makes the same split when it ingests OpenAI usage itself (`completion_tokens_details` and `output_tokens_details` in `packages/shared/src/server/ingestion/types.ts`, and the OTel path in `OtelIngestionProcessor.ts`). The per-type counts now add up to `total_tokens`. Where Hermes prices the call, the cost total stays the same: the breakdown bills reasoning at the output rate, so `output` plus `output_reasoning_tokens` equals the old `output` line. MoA advisor generations get the same split.

One thing users will notice: a dashboard or query that reads the `reasoning_tokens` usage key needs to switch to `output_reasoning_tokens`. Traces that were already ingested keep the old keys.

Per this repo's CONTRIBUTING, the fix reaches users once the catalog pin for `langfuse` moves. I haven't opened that PR.

## Related Issue

I couldn't find an issue for this in this repo or in hermes-agent, so there's nothing to link.

#110 and #112 also change this plugin, but neither touches usage. This diff applies cleanly on both of their heads (`git apply --3way --check`).

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `langfuse/__init__.py`: a new `_usage_buckets()` builds the Langfuse buckets from the canonical counts and moves reasoning out of `output`. `_canonical_usage_and_cost()` and `_emit_moa_reference_generations()` use it, and the cost breakdown prices `output_reasoning_tokens` at the output rate.
- `langfuse/tests/test_langfuse_reasoning_usage.py` (new): five tests. They cover the `post_api_request` summary dict and a `post_llm_call` response object in the Codex Responses shape. They check that the buckets add up to the canonical total, that `output` stays whole when there is no reasoning, that reasoning larger than output gets clamped, and that the cost breakdown still adds up to `total`.
- `langfuse/tests/test_langfuse_plugin.py`: the MoA advisor test expected the old `reasoning_tokens` key. It now checks the split.
- `langfuse/README.md`: one sentence on how reasoning is reported.

## How to Test

1. From `langfuse/`, with hermes-agent checked out beside this repo: `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=../../hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q`. I get 148 passed on this branch and 143 on `main`.
2. Copy the new and updated test files next to the `__init__.py` from `main` and run the same command. I get 5 failed and 143 passed. Four of the failures are in the new file; the fifth is the MoA test.
3. `hermes plugins validate ./langfuse` passes. It prints the same private-core-imports warning as on `main`.
4. I also drove the plugin's registered hooks with the Langfuse SDK 4.15.2 exporting to a local OTLP receiver that decodes the protobuf, in `metadata` capture mode. One turn was Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol`, 21,000 input tokens of which 20,000 were cached, 500 output tokens of which 300 were reasoning). The other was a Claude turn with 120 reasoning tokens:

| | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|

| Codex turn, cost Langfuse would infer | $0.012 | $0.009 |
| Claude turn, exported usage keys added up | 24,620 | 24,500 |

For the cost row I applied Langfuse 4.63.0's default `gpt-6.1-sol` prices to the exported keys in a script. I didn't run a Langfuse server.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix: drop schema keywords native rejects; lowest effort for reasoning-off on mandatory-thinking routes
body:
Two independent fixes to `claude-subscription-directsdk`, one commit each. Both were found with a plugin-LLM caller that uses structured output with reasoning off (Claude Code CLI 2.1.303, Hermes v0.22.2, `haiku` = `claude-haiku-5-5`, through the plugin's chat.completions client).

## 1. Structured-output schemas 400 upstream

`response_format: json_schema` is forwarded verbatim into `output_config.format.schema`. The native API rejects these (the plugin surfaces "Incomplete upstream response (first upstream attempt: status 400 ... upstream said: output_config.format.schema: ..."):

| Schema fragment | Upstream error |
|---|---|
| `{"type": ["integer","null"], "minimum": 0, "maximum": 216}` | For 'integer' type, properties maximum, minimum are not supported |
| array `maxItems` (even 0 or 2) | For 'array' type, property 'maxItems' is not supported |
| array `uniqueItems` | ... 'uniqueItems' is not supported |
| `{"type": ["string","null"], "enum": ["parents","educators",null]}` | Invalid schema: Enum value 'parents' does not match declared type '['string', 'null']' |

Accepted in the same probes: string `maxLength`, `minItems: 1`, `enum` without `type`, `anyOf` of `{type: string, enum}` and `{type: null}`, and `type: ["string","null"]` without `enum`.

Hermes core then retries the request without a schema, so every such structured call is paid twice. `agent/plugin_llm.py` validates the reply against the caller's original, full schema with `jsonschema`, so dropping these keywords only from the wire copy keeps them enforced.

**Fix:** a recursive `native_format_schema()` that returns a copy without `minimum`/`maximum` (integer/number), `maxItems`/`uniqueItems` (array), and `type` when it is a list beside `enum`. The caller's schema is not mutated.

## 2. Reasoning-off on mandatory-thinking models thinks at native's default effort

`MANDATORY_THINKING` routes (Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable) 400 on `thinking: {type: disabled}`, so a caller's disable is omitted. With no `thinking` and no effort, the CLI then applies its default effort (no `--effort`), so a request that asked for no reasoning still reasons. Measured on Haiku 5.5, a ~5k-input answer prompt with a JSON schema:

| Effort sent | Latency | Reasoning tokens |
|---|---|---|
| none (current behaviour) | 7.8-10.7 s | 600-1200 |
| `low` | 4.1-5.1 s | 0 in 5 of 6 runs (one run had 212) |
| `medium` | | 702 |
| `high` | | 1046-1212 |

**Fix:** where `accepts_thinking_disable()` is False, a reasoning-off request (`reasoning.enabled: false` or effort `none`) sets `output_config.effort: low`, which the existing code turns into `--effort low`. "Off" is impossible on these routes and the lowest effort is the nearest equivalent. Routes that accept the disable (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5) still get `thinking: {type: disabled}` and no effort, and enabled-reasoning requests are unchanged. The `MANDATORY_THINKING` comment in `model_catalog.py` documented the old default-effort behaviour and is updated. The latency and token numbers were measured on Haiku 5.5 only; Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable take the same code path but I did not measure them.

## Tests

New `tests/test_directsdk_structured_output.py` (each dropped keyword, nested `items`/`anyOf`/`properties`, properties literally named `type`/`maximum`/`maxItems` left alone, nullable enum, caller schema not mutated) and `tests/test_directsdk_reasoning_off.py` (effort `low` for every mandatory-thinking spelling with both `enabled: false` and effort `none`, real disable kept for Sonnet 5 / Opus 5 / Haiku 4.5, coexistence with `output_config.format`, enabled-reasoning unchanged). Without the fix, 5 of the 6 structured-output tests and 2 of the 4 reasoning-off tests fail.

Run against a Hermes v0.22.2 runtime (Python 3.14.7): `cd claude-subscription-directsdk && HERMES_AGENT_REPO=<hermes> PYTHONPATH=<hermes> python -m pytest -q tests` gives 344 passed, 9 subtests passed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_directsdk_workspace.py::test_unsafe_shared_workspace_falls_back_to_one_private_workspace_per_process[no_uid]` (`AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'getuid'`). It fails identically on unmodified `main` in that environment and does not touch this change. I did not run the Windows/macOS matrix.

No version bump: CHANGELOG entries are added under the existing unreleased section, and per CONTRIBUTING the release is the catalog pin.

title: fix(homeassistant): report no-op service calls, capture HA error bodies, verify empty responses
body:
This is an AI created PR with the supervision of a non-programmer human.

## Problem

Two real failures observed in production (voice agent controlling Home Assistant):

1. **Silent no-op reported as success.** Calling `light.turn_on` against a `switch.*` entity returned `success: true` with an empty `affected_entities` — nothing happened, but the agent believed it did. HA returns 200 with an empty list whenever no state changed, and the plugin never checked *why* nothing changed.
2. **HA error bodies dropped.** `resp.raise_for_status()` raised a `ClientResponseError` whose `str()` omits the response body, so messages like *'Service call requires responses but caller did not ask for responses. Add ?return_response to query parameters.'* never reached the agent. This made response services (e.g. `weather.get_forecasts`) fail with an opaque 400.

## Changes

- **`_api_json`** — capture the HA error body into the raised `ClientResponseError` (with a safe fallback if the body can't be read).
- **`_async_call_service`** — when a targeted call returns no changed entities, verify which case it is and report it:
  - entity does not exist → 'does not exist in Home Assistant, check with ha_list_entities'
  - entity exists in a different domain → 'exists but is in the X domain, call X.service instead'
  - entity exists in the right domain → success + note 'was already in state Y — nothing to change'
  - retry once with `?return_response` **only** when HA's error says responses are required (plain services 400 when the flag is present, so it must not be added unconditionally).
- **`_parse_service_response`** — handle the `{'changed_states': [...], 'service_response': {...}}` shape returned by `?return_response` calls.
- **`ha_call_service` description** — instruct the agent to never guess an entity_id and that the service domain must match the entity's own domain.

## Tests

7 new tests (response-shape parsing, no-op flagging, missing-entity / wrong-domain / already-in-state verification, return_response retry). All pass; no regressions — the remaining suite failures are identical on pristine `main` (pre-existing, environment-related).

## Before / after (live HA)

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `light.turn_on` on `switch.bedroom` | `success: true, affected: []` (nothing happened) | `error: '…exists but is in the 'switch' domain, not 'light'. Call switch.turn_on instead.'` |
| `light.turn_on` on an already-on light | `success: true, affected: []` | `success: true, note: 'was already in state 'on' — nothing to change.'` |
| `weather.get_forecasts` | opaque 400 | forecast payload in `service_response` |

title: fix(claude-subscription-directsdk): report cancellation and native stderr at replay ack (#122)
body:
Fixes #122. Thanks to @Eros-H for the report and the fix it suggested; this PR takes that fix as written, and the commit credits them as co-author.

**What users see:** a request that Hermes cancels (for example the stale-call watchdog) while Claude Code is still acknowledging the replayed history now reports `Claude request cancelled`. Before, it reported `Native exited before replay acknowledgment`. When native really does exit at that step, the error now includes its exit code and stderr, like the other failure paths do.

**Cause:** `receive()` checks `request.cancelled` only at the top of its loop. `cancel()` kills native, the reader thread pushes `None`, and that `None` can reach the replay loop before the next check runs. The replay-ack branch also left out `_stderr_tail(native_stderr)`.

**Change** (`directsdk.py`, replay loop):
- On `ack is None`: if the request was cancelled, raise `Claude request cancelled`. Otherwise raise with ` (exit=<code>)` plus the stderr tail. The reader thread calls `process.wait()` before it pushes `None`, so `returncode` is set. We join the stderr drain thread (1 s cap) first so the tail is complete.
- The `Native history replay not supported` branch also gets the stderr tail.
- Retries are unchanged.

**Tests** (`tests/test_directsdk_replay_ack.py`, using a fake native script):
- `test_native_exit_before_replay_ack_reports_stderr_and_exit_code`: native writes to stderr and exits 3 before acknowledging. The error must contain the stderr text and `exit=3`.
- `test_cancel_while_waiting_for_replay_ack_reports_cancellation`: the client is cancelled while native waits silently. The error must be `Claude request cancelled`.

Both fail on `main` (4513ba4) and pass with this fix (8/8 repeat runs). The whole plugin suite passes: 421 passed, against hermes-agent `origin/main` 3b15d28 with py3.14, `HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1` and an empty `HERMES_HOME`.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(admission): relay CA file + profile-scoped relay proxy for credential brokers
body:
## Summary

Lets the admission relay reach `api.anthropic.com` through a **TLS-inspecting credential broker**, so an agent host can run on a placeholder `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` while the broker adds the real subscription bearer (e.g. from `claude setup-token`) on the way out. The host never holds the long-lived token, and revoking it happens in one place.

Builds on #23: this branch includes that PR's commit (`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY`, authorship kept) and adds the two pieces it was missing for this use:

1. **`CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CA_FILE`**: an extra root CA PEM loaded into the relay's upstream `ssl` context, on top of the system roots. Verification stays on (`CERT_REQUIRED`, hostname checks). An unreadable file raises when the relay starts rather than connecting unverified.
2. **Profile-scoped resolution**: the proxy and the CA file are read with `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`, so under a multiplexed gateway each profile's `.env` applies. That means one profile can go through a broker while its siblings connect directly. Outside Hermes (tests, evals) it falls back to `os.environ`.

## Why the relay needs its own settings

The relay opens the upstream connection itself, so native's `HTTPS_PROXY` / `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` handling never applies to that hop. Setting a process-wide `HTTPS_PROXY` instead would push every outbound call the gateway makes through the broker, which usually allowlists only a few hosts. Pointing native at the broker with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` isn't possible either, because the provider rightly refuses that override.

Observed before this change, with a placeholder token in a profile `.env` and the proxy/CA set only for the `claude` child (via a `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` wrapper): every request went direct and got `401 OAuth access token is invalid`, and Hermes quietly fell back to the next provider.

## Tests

- `tests/test_admission_proxy.py`: the extra CA is trusted and verification stays on, the default context is unchanged when the variable is unset, a missing file fails closed, and a profile secret scope takes precedence over the process env for both variables. 20 passed locally.
- Full suite against hermes-agent `489c1ac298`: everything passes except `test_directsdk_fast_return.py::test_result_returns_before_eof_and_grace_kills_native`. That test fails the same way on unmodified `origin/main` in the same environment, so it isn't caused by this change. I'll leave CI on all three OSes to confirm.

## Live end-to-end check

Plugin from this branch → Agent Vault broker (bearer rule for `api.anthropic.com`, MITM root CA) → Anthropic, Claude Code 2.1.284, with an empty `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and only a placeholder `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`:

- With `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_PROXY` and `_CA_FILE` set: `directsdk.Client` returned `OK` on `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and the broker logged `POST /v1/messages → 200` with the bearer injected.
- Same harness with the two variables unset: `401 OAuth access token is invalid`.

title: singularity: Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend moves here from Hermes core
body:
Moves the Singularity/Apptainer terminal backend out of Hermes core (`tools/environments/singularity.py`, ~220 core lines) into an official plugin, `singularity`, registered through the terminal-environment provider seam (`ctx.register_terminal_environment_provider`).

**Same name, same config.** The backend is still `terminal.backend: singularity`; the image still comes from `terminal.singularity_image` (config.yaml wins) or `TERMINAL_SINGULARITY_IMAGE`, limits from `terminal.container_cpu/memory/persistent`, scratch from `TERMINAL_SCRATCH_DIR` / `APPTAINER_CACHEDIR`. Existing configs keep working without edits.

**Classification core reads from the provider** (each was a hardcoded `singularity` entry in a core frozenset): `is_remote`, `is_container` (so `skip_container_guards`), `supports_streams` + the environment's `exec_prefix()` (Bot Desktop / computer_use / browser follow the terminal into the instance), `env_description` for the prompt fallback. `cache_path_base` stays `None`, matching core's `to_agent_visible_cache_path` (Apptainer paths were never translated).

**Inert on cores that still ship the built-in backend** (`singularity.py` next to core's `BaseEnvironment`): those cores reserve the name and serve it themselves, so installing early is harmless. The hermes-agent core-removal PR follows the catalog entry; its left-core migration installs this plugin for every home whose backend is `singularity`.

Internals that changed (nothing user-configured):
- The process-exit sweep of `<scratch>/hermes-*` now runs in the plugin, only in a process that started an instance.
- `singularity_snapshots.json` is no longer written: nothing ever read it.
- A bare image reference (`python:3.12`) is treated as `docker://python:3.12` (core would have passed it to `apptainer` as a path and failed).
- The sudo-probe knob is spelled `_passwordless_sudo_probe_supported`; the core PR renames `BaseEnvironment`'s knob to match. The old spelling trips the install scanner's `NOPASSWD` rule (IGNORECASE) as `dangerous`.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| plugin suite vs hermes-agent `origin/main` (c93b7ec) | 33 passed, 1 skipped (registry test skips: main still reserves the name) |
| plugin suite vs the core-removal branch (`leave-core/singularity`) | 34 passed (registry test runs: `singularity` resolves through the real registry) |
| `tests.yml` on this PR (ubuntu / macOS / Windows) | green at f03e584 |
| `hermes plugins validate singularity` vs `origin/main` | passed; warns on 5 private imports (`_popen_bash`, `sanitize_task_id_for_path`, credential/skills mounts, `DEFAULT_SANDBOX_IMAGE`) |
| install scanner, `origin/main` and `v0.22.2` | `safe` on both |

Card: `assets/singularity.jpg` (1200x600, house style). Root README grid gains the cell.

title: mcp-serve: Hermes as an MCP server, moved out of core, with --tools
body:
Moves Hermes-as-an-MCP-server out of hermes-agent core into a new official plugin, `mcp-serve`, which registers `hermes mcp-serve`, and ports the `--tools` mode from hermes-agent PR NousResearch/hermes-agent#83364.

## What's in it
- `mcp-serve/bridge.py`: core's `mcp_serve.py`. The ten conversation tools keep their names, schemas and descriptions. Changes: a local read-only SQLite URI helper instead of a core import, a plugin reinstall hint instead of `pip install mcp`, and the `include_tools` switch.
- `mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py`: `--tools`, ported from #83364. It exposes a fixed allowlist: web_search, web_extract, the browser_* set, vision_analyze, image_generate, skill_view, skills_list and text_to_speech. Calls go through `model_tools.handle_function_call`, the same dispatch path core's codex `hermes-tools` server uses.
  - Off by default. Without the flag only the bridge is served.
  - Never exposed: terminal, file, code execution, process, delegation and all kanban tools. #83364 reused core's codex list, which includes `kanban_create`, and a kanban task runs as a full agent with terminal access.
  - A tool whose backend is not configured is skipped, under the same rules the model sees.
  - No local files: `browser_navigate` and `web_extract` accept only web URLs, `vision_analyze` only web or `data:` images, and bad values are refused before dispatch. `text_to_speech`'s `output_path` is not offered.
  - Only toolsets enabled for the CLI in `hermes tools` are offered.
  - Clients get Hermes' own parameter schemas, including descriptions, enums and item types.
  - Shell hooks and outbound webhooks from `config.yaml` are registered the way core did for `mcp serve`, so a `pre_tool_call` block still applies. `--accept-hooks` is kept.
  - `HERMES_QUIET` and `HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS` are set as in #83364.
- `mcp-serve/cli.py`, `__init__.py`: `ctx.register_cli_command("mcp-serve")`. `register_cli_command` only registers top-level commands, so the old nested spelling can't be registered by a plugin. Core's removal PR makes `hermes mcp serve` print the new spelling.
- Tests: core's `tests/test_mcp_serve.py` (80 tests) moved over, plus `--tools` and registration tests. 90 tests pass.
- Root README: a grid row, the card, and a migration note. MCP clients live outside Hermes, so nothing installs automatically.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite, py3.14 + mcp 2.3.0, against the core removal branch | 90 passed. The toolset-filter and schema tests fail with those fixes reverted |
| `hermes plugins validate mcp-serve` | passed. Warning: private core imports (session DB, send_message, model_tools, hooks); no public ctx seam exists for these |
| Install scanner, core main and v0.22.2 | `safe`, 0 findings |
| `plugins install file://…#mcp-serve --enable --yes-deps` into a scratch home, on the core removal branch and on v0.22.2 | installed and enabled |
| Real MCP client over stdio (`mcp` SDK `stdio_client`), default mode | initialize ok; tools/list returns the 10 bridge tools; `conversations_list` and `messages_read` return the seeded conversation; stderr empty |
| Same, `--tools` | 15 tools (bridge + web_search, web_extract, skill_view, skills_list, text_to_speech in a keyless home); no terminal, file or kanban tools; `skills_list` dispatches; `web_search` schema `required=['query']` |
| `--tools` with a shell `pre_tool_call` hook that blocks `skills_list` | `{"error": "probe hook blocked skills_list"}` |
| `--tools` at head: `web_extract` with `urls=["file://…/config.yaml"]` | refused: `web_extract over MCP accepts only http(s) URLs, not local files`. The `text_to_speech` schema lists `instructions, speed, text` only |

An independent review lane found four issues and all are fixed: local-file reach through browser/vision/TTS arguments; the profile's toolset choices being ignored; lossy schemas; and README caveats for `-p` and browser availability. With a local browser backend it reproduced `file://` reads through `browser_navigate` and `browser_console`; `file:` is now refused before dispatch.

The catalog entry follows in hermes-agent, re-pinned to this PR's merge commit. The core removal PR goes last.

title: agent-importers: hermes import-agent moves out of core, now with Cursor
body:
Moves `hermes import-agent` out of Hermes core into a new official plugin, `agent-importers`, and adds Cursor (`~/.cursor`) as a third source.

## What's in it
- **Command continuity.** The plugin registers `hermes import-agent` through `ctx.register_cli_command` with core's exact flags (`agent`, `--source`, `--dry-run`, `--overwrite`, `-y/--yes`, `--sync`). It reads and writes the same per-profile `import-sync.json`, so existing imports and scheduled `--sync` runs keep working.
- **Claude Code + Codex CLI importers.** Ported from `hermes_cli/agent_import.py` / `agent_import_sync.py` with the same behaviour. Core internals are swapped for documented surfaces: `config.yaml` reads go through `hermes_cli.config.require_readable_config_before_write` (an unreadable file is never rewritten), writes through `atomic_config_replace` with the full mapping (keeps comments; `--overwrite` still replaces a whole MCP entry, as core did), and output goes through `hermes_cli.cli_output`. `hermes plugins validate` reports no private imports.
- **Cursor**, ported from NousResearch/hermes-agent#83616 (commit authorship kept):
  - `AGENTS.md` and `rules/**/*.md|*.mdc` become memory entries, with `.mdc` frontmatter stripped.
  - `mcp.json` `mcpServers` go to `mcp_servers`, with secrets stripped.
  - `skills/**/<name>/SKILL.md` go to `skills/cursor-imports/<name>/`. Lookup is recursive for Cursor's category folders. A `SKILL.md` inside a skill's own folder stays part of that skill, and duplicate names are reported as conflicts.
  - `cli-config.json` is never read, and `--sync` also tracks Cursor sources.
- **Inert on old cores.** If the running core still ships `hermes_cli/agent_import.py`, `register()` adds nothing. Two subparsers with the same name would break plugin-command wiring.
- **Docs.** Card art, a README grid cell (cells kept paired), and an "Already used one of these?" line.

## Validation
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite vs core main (still ships import-agent) | 62 passed |
| Plugin suite vs core with import-agent removed (`leave-core/agent-importers`) | 62 passed |
| `hermes plugins validate agent-importers` | passed, no private-import warning |
| Install scanner, core main and v0.22.2 | `safe` / `safe` |
| Real `plugins install file://…#agent-importers --enable` into a scratch home on the removal branch | `hermes import-agent --help` comes from the plugin |
| Dry runs against fixture `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor` | 5 / 4 / 5 items would import; `config.yaml` md5 unchanged; nothing written |
| Real Cursor import, then `--sync` after editing a rule | 5 imported; `LINEAR_API_KEY` / `cli-config.json` secrets absent; sync re-imported the changed rule |
| Independent review | 1 P2 + 3 P3 fixed in the last commit: `--overwrite` of an MCP entry with extra keys aborted the import (new test, red before / green after); symlinked Cursor skill folders were skipped (new test); new files were created 0600; `NO_COLOR` ignored |
| Old core (main) with the plugin installed and enabled | core's own `import-agent` runs; plugin registers no CLI command |

Gemini CLI is intentionally not included. Catalog entry and the core removal follow in hermes-agent.

Co-authored-by: Hermes Agent <hermes@nousresearch.com>

title: bubblewrap: bwrap terminal backend plugin (port of hermes-agent#116579)
body:
Adds **`bubblewrap`**, an official Linux terminal backend plugin: every `terminal` and `execute_code` command runs in its own bwrap sandbox on this machine at the host's paths (read-only root, writable working directory per profile, credential paths and the Hermes home hidden, private `/tmp` and `/proc`, agent/docker sockets masked, prlimit memory/CPU/process limits). Port of NousResearch/hermes-agent#116579 (itself a salvage of NousResearch/hermes-agent#102875 by @TacoTakumi) onto the terminal environment provider registry, **with no core changes**.

## What's in it

- `bubblewrap/sandbox.py`: the PR's backend module, kept with every hardening from its live pass (CA bundles under the hidden Hermes home bound back read-only, `$TMPDIR` scratch dir reachable, ancestor pins, bind-source swap guard, profile-home guard, masked-cwd reset, socket-var unset after rc files). Adapted: settings come from `plugins.entries.bubblewrap.settings.*` (was `terminal.bubblewrap_*` → `TERMINAL_BUBBLEWRAP_*`), a `_run_bash` override replaces the core `_wrap_popen_args` seam, the tracked cwd never follows a command onto `/` or into the state dir (replaces the PR's core `execute_code` cwd restore), and a cwd that is not a host directory (Hermes ≤ 0.22.2 hands plugin backends `/root`) maps to the host default.
- **Writable root comes from configuration only** (`terminal.cwd`, else where Hermes runs): Hermes recreates environments from the session's recorded cwd, and the core PR bound that read-write, so a model's `cd ~` plus an idle recreation made the home directory writable. The passed cwd now only sets where commands start (read-only outside the root). A missing `terminal.cwd` fails closed (read-only nearest parent). Found by an independent review lane; regression tests red before, green after.
- `bubblewrap/__init__.py`: `BubblewrapProvider` (`is_remote=False`, `is_container=False`, so core keeps host hints, host file paths and the dangerous-command approval gate), probe / doctor / setup rows and profile prompt, `default_cwd`, and the PR's model-facing sandbox notice as a plugin system prompt section (only rendered when `terminal.backend` is `bubblewrap`).
- `platforms: [linux]`, `config_schema` for profile / binds / memory_mb / cpu_seconds / max_procs, README stating what bwrap isolates and what it does not, card, root README grid cell.
- Tests: the PR's seven suites ported (registry dispatch instead of the built-in builder, settings instead of env names), plus real `PluginManager` discovery, spawn-wrapping and tracked-cwd tests. Off Linux only the provider tests are collected.

## Differences from the core PR (no core seam for these yet)

- Background jobs are not refused up front: core has no provider flag for "no background processes", so a `background: true` job is launched through `env.execute`, runs inside the sandbox (never `spawn_local`), and dies with it. The system prompt note tells the model background processes are unavailable.
- `execute_code` reaches the per-call path by core's own fail-open from the remote session kernel (one `remote kernel died at spawn` warning per call) instead of a core branch that skips the kernel.
- Gateway default cwd is the process cwd, or the real home when that lies under a hidden path, instead of `MESSAGING_CWD`.
- The PR's host-path special cases in core (vision/image-gen source confinement, TUI session workdir, launch-cwd recording) are dropped; those sites treat the plugin backend as non-local (safe direction).

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite vs hermes-agent `origin/main` (bwrap 0.11.1, real-bwrap integration + rlimit suites ran) | 332 passed, 1 skipped (off-Linux test) |
| Plugin suite vs `v0.22.2` tree (`requires_hermes: >=0.22.2`) | 332 passed, 1 skipped |
| CI ubuntu (bwrap userns probe fails on the runner, so sandbox suites skip) / macOS / Windows | green |
| Real install: `hermes plugins install 'file://<clone>#bubblewrap' --yes-deps --enable` into a scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME | installed + enabled; discovery registers `hermes_plugins.bubblewrap.BubblewrapProvider`, doctor rows ok |
| Functional smoke through `terminal_tool` (profile `workspace`) | write in cwd ok and visible on host; `touch $HOME/x` and `touch /etc/x` → `Read-only file system`; `.ssh` empty, `.netrc` 0 bytes; HERMES_HOME shows only `cache sandboxes`; 4 pids in `/proc`; `$TMPDIR` file persists across commands; `curl` → no network; `/run/user/<uid>` empty; `execute_code` ran sandboxed (3 pids) and the next `pwd` is back in the project dir |
| `hermes plugins validate ./bubblewrap` (main and v0.22.2) | passed; warns on private core imports (`tools.environments.local` internals) |
| `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin` (main and v0.22.2) | `safe` |

title: feat: advanced-delegation plugin (model routes, profile routes, hermes delegation config, /delegation)
body:
## Summary

One official plugin, **`advanced-delegation`**, replaces the two earlier drafts (`delegation-model-map`, `delegation-profiles`). Installing it opens two extra **delegation modes** for `delegate_task`, next to the built-in default that stays in Hermes core:

| Mode | `delegation.backend` | What the agent gets |
|---|---|---|
| **Default** (core) | `default` | Every subagent runs on `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider`, else the parent's model. |
| **Model routes** | `model_map` | A per-task `option`: a named model route from your list (`fast`, `deep`, `local`...). |
| **Profile routes** | `profile_routes` | A per-task `profile`: the subagent runs as one of your Hermes profiles (its model, credentials, skills, `SOUL.md`). |

**One mode is active at a time** (by design): you pick Default, Model routes or Profile routes, never two at once. Model routes and Profile routes stay separate backends with separate config blocks (`delegation.backends.<mode>`), so switching modes keeps the other mode's settings.

Plus, per Teknium's decisions:
- **`hermes delegation config`**: pick the mode, then set it up. Model routes get a route editor that feels like `hermes model` because it *is* `hermes model`'s pieces (curses menus, configured-provider inventory, model picker, reasoning picker), with a name and a description per route. Profile routes are just a multi-select of your other profiles. Default just switches back.
- **`/delegation`**: show the mode and switch it in a chat, session-scoped like `/model`, `--global` saves. A session switch changes **routing** now; the agent's per-task choices (`option` / `profile`) follow the mode the chat started with until `/new`, and a task sending a choice the new mode doesn't have is refused by core with a message. `--global` + `/new` gives a session whose choices match. It is also the fix path when the configured backend fails (core's error names `/delegation`).

Only route names and your one-line descriptions reach the model; the raw provider, model, endpoint and key never become tool parameters. On a core without the seam the plugin logs one warning and registers nothing.

## Layout

```
advanced-delegation/
├── plugin.yaml        # one manifest, kind: standalone, no Python deps (so no pyproject.toml, see 3ab2439)
├── __init__.py        # register(): both backends, the CLI command, the slash command
├── model_map.py       # backend `model_map`        (was delegation-model-map/provider.py, git mv)
├── profile_routes.py  # backend `profile_routes`   (was delegation-profiles/provider.py, git mv)
├── store.py           # read/validate/write delegation.backend + delegation.backends.<mode> (atomic_config_write)
├── cli.py             # hermes delegation config [--show]
├── slash.py           # /delegation
└── tests/             # 128 tests
```

The two old directories are removed; provider code and tests moved with `git mv`, so history and blame follow.

## `hermes delegation config`

Screenshots from a real run in a 150x34 tmux PTY (fake `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, demo provider keys), rendered with `tmux capture-pane -e` → `aha` → headless Chrome.

**1. Mode picker.** Core's curses radio list; the cursor opens on the current mode.

![mode picker](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/01-mode-picker.png)

**2. Model routes: the routes list.** Each row is name, description and `provider · model · reasoning · tier`, with the default starred. Enter on a route: Edit / Make it the default / Delete. **+ Add a route**; **Done** switches the mode, and with no default set it first asks for one, offering *No default — unrouted tasks use the main agent's model* as an explicit choice.

![routes list](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/02-routes-list.png)
![route actions](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/08-route-actions.png)

**3. Add a route.** Name (what the agent picks) and description (what it reads), then the provider list `hermes model`'s delegation picker uses (`build_aux_picker_rows`: only providers with credentials on this profile, plus a custom endpoint), then `hermes model`'s own model picker (prices, `/` search, selection guards) through core's public `prompt_model_selection`, titled *Select the model for this route:*, the reasoning picker (`Inherit parent` default), and a speed-tier step that only appears when the route offers a tier and only lists the tiers it offers (the `/fast` gate).

![name and description](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/03-add-name-description.png)
![provider](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/04-add-provider.png)
![model](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/05-add-model.png)
![reasoning](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/06-add-reasoning.png)
![speed tier](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/07-add-speed-tier.png)
![done](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/09-done-model-routes.png)

A route is validated before it is saved: a unique token name, a description, a model, a provider Hermes resolves (or a base_url), a real reasoning level, and a speed tier the route offers. Keys the editor does not ask about (`fallback_providers`, ...) survive an edit.

**4. Profile routes: not the model editor.** A checklist of your other profiles, an optional line about each newly checked one (profiles already listed keep theirs), a default. Done. Unchecking every profile clears the list after a confirmation; an active Profile routes mode then goes back to Default.

![profile multi-select](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/11-profile-multiselect.png)
![profile descriptions](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/12-profile-descriptions.png)
![profile default](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/13-profile-default.png)

**5. `--show`** (no terminal needed) and **back to Default**:

![show model routes](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/10-show-model-routes.png)
![show profile routes](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/14-show-profile-routes.png)
![back to default](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/a6bd8714e00e555803d1023d3217c2f8ebfcbd9d/15-back-to-default.png)

Without a TTY, interactive editing exits 1 with the way out (`--show`, `hermes config set`). Every write goes through core's `atomic_config_write` (comments and other settings kept); the config this run produced is the shape below.

## `/delegation`

```
/delegation                     # current mode + a picker to switch this session
/delegation model_map           # this session only (like /model)
/delegation profiles --global   # save delegation.backend for this profile
/delegation default             # back to the built-in behaviour
```

Bare `/delegation` asks with the surface's own choice prompt through core's `ctx.ask_choice` (choices are `{value, label, description}`): clarify buttons on Telegram/Discord/Slack like approvals, a numbered list on other chats, the clarify picker in the CLI/TUI/Desktop. Only modes with something set up are offered, each with what it routes to. When `ask_choice` returns None (cancelled, or a caller that cannot ask: a hook, cron, an event-loop handler) or the core has no `ask_choice`, it answers with a numbered text listing that also flags a configured backend that cannot run (core's reason from `list_backends()`), which is the fix path when core's fail-closed error names `/delegation`.

Every switch goes through `ctx.delegation_backends`, never an import of `agent.delegation_backends`: it is a host remote facade, so under `plugins.isolation: host` the switch lands in the Hermes process `delegate_task` reads, not in the plugin host's own copy (`tests/test_slash_host.py` runs the real plugin in the host; red with the old import, green now). A session switch is `set_session_backend`; core refuses a backend that cannot run with its reason, shown as `Not switched: ...`. The running chat's `delegate_task` schema is part of its prompt cache and is never rebuilt, so the reply (and the picker question, briefly) says it up front: routing changes now, the agent's choices follow the mode the chat started with until `/new`, a task that sends a choice this mode doesn't have is refused (core, hermes-agent `127249bba9`), one that sends none runs on the new mode's default; `--global` saves it and `/new` then gives a session whose choices match. `--global` is core's `set_global_backend`, which writes `delegation.backend`, clears the session's override and refuses a managed install itself (its `PermissionError` text is the reply). On a core without `ctx.delegation_backends`, a plain switch says to use `--global`, which then writes through this plugin's store.

Live in the real classic CLI against the pushed core (hermes-agent #142563 @ `127249bba9`, same fake home):

![/delegation picker](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/5f99ce4c63bc303a8b347c02cf1734d71897624f/16-slash-picker-cli.png)
![switched, picker again](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/5f99ce4c63bc303a8b347c02cf1734d71897624f/17-slash-switched-then-picker.png)
![profile routes, then --global default](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/5f99ce4c63bc303a8b347c02cf1734d71897624f/18-slash-profile-then-global-default.png)

## Config

```yaml
delegation:
  backend: model_map            # default | model_map | profile_routes
  backends:
    model_map:
      options:
        - {name: fast, description: "Cheap and quick: lookups, summaries, simple edits.", provider: openrouter, model: google/gemini-3.8-flash, reasoning_effort: low}
        - {name: deep, description: "Slow and careful: hard debugging and design work.", provider: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5, reasoning_effort: high, service_tier: fast}
        - {name: local, description: "Private: runs on this machine; good for code search.", base_url: http://localhost:8080/v1, model: qwen3-coder}
      default: fast
    profile_routes:
      profiles:
        - {name: coder, description: Writes and refactors code; runs tests.}
        - {name: researcher, description: Web research and long-form summaries.}
      default: coder
```

Shared contract with the core lane: when `delegation.backend` is not `default`, `delegation.model` / `delegation.provider` are inactive. A task that picks no route and has no configured default now runs on the parent's own model (empty route), not the delegation section's route. Model routes also carry `fallback_providers`.

- Config: `hermes_cli.config.load_config_readonly`, `require_readable_config_before_write`, `atomic_config_write`, `get_config_path`.
- `hermes model`'s pieces: `hermes_cli.curses_ui.curses_radiolist` / `curses_single_select` / `curses_checklist`, `hermes_cli.inventory.build_aux_picker_rows` / `format_aux_picker_entries`, `hermes_cli.auth_model_picker.prompt_model_selection(..., title="Select the model for this route:")` (public), `hermes_cli.main_provider_setup._prompt_reasoning_effort_selection`, `hermes_cli.models_pricing.get_pricing_for_provider`, `hermes_cli.cli_output.prompt`.

- Profiles: `hermes_cli.profiles.list_profile_names`, `get_active_profile_name`.
- Session scope and picker (#142563; feature-detected on `ctx`, so a core without them keeps the text path): `ctx.delegation_backends.list_backends()` (list of dicts: `name`, `label`, `description`, `available`, `reason`) / `get_session_backend(session_key)` / `set_session_backend(session_key, name)` (None clears; `ValueError(reason)` when it cannot run) / `set_global_backend(name, session_key=...)` (`PermissionError` on a managed install), and `ctx.ask_choice(question, choices)`. Both providers set `display_name` (the picker label) and `summary` (one user-facing line for pickers).

`hermes plugins validate` passes against #142563. Switching to `ctx.delegation_backends` and the public `prompt_model_selection` dropped two of its private-import warnings (`agent.delegation_registry`, `auth_model_picker._prompt_model_selection`); the 12 left are the editor's other `hermes model` pieces (curses menus, provider inventory, reasoning picker, pricing, profile and fast-mode helpers) and `store`'s validation helpers (catalog rule 9). title: Meshy gallery shows images; expired links and paid conversions are explained (salvage #128)
body:
Images join the Meshy gallery, expired download links stop looking like broken keys, and the Download menu separates free exports from paid conversions. Salvage of #128 by @gbusto onto main after #115 landed. All 10 of his commits keep his authorship.

## Changes (from #128)
- **Images in the gallery:** Meshy text-to-image and image-to-image results appear beside models, with an All / Images / Models filter. A viewer steps through image sets; **Download image** / **Download all N images** saves them under `saved-assets/<task-id>/` with a manifest, and an interrupted set offers **Retry image download**.
- **Image Next menu** (make a 3D model from it, edit it, more views) sends a chat message; **Copy ID** copies the task id.
- **Expired assets:** Meshy's signed links expire after about 3 days. Expired entries without a local copy are hidden, ones with a copy say "Local copy", and a denied or expired link returns 410 with a plain message instead of reading as a bad API key.
- **De-duplication** of tasks listed by two endpoints; the selected model or clip survives refreshes.
- **Free exports vs paid conversions:** the Download menu lists formats Meshy already produced; missing ones get **Convert to X · 1 cr** (matches `meshy_convert` in the plugin's cost table, so the approval prompt shows the same price).
- **Storage footer** with known local usage and a folder link.

## Salvage changes (merge commit)
- Kept main's final-review fixes where the PR overlapped them: exclusive staging downloads and the beside-project ownership rule (files Hermes did not save are never overwritten).
- Dropped the sentence in the conversion chat message that told the agent it "confirms the 1-credit conversion cost". The approval prompt is where the user confirms spend.

title: bubblewrap: port the rest of the later hermes-agent#102875 hardening
body:
The plugin started from NousResearch/hermes-agent#116579, and that branch stopped on 2026-09-20. NousResearch/hermes-agent#102875 got more fixes after that point, most of them from the security review by @andrexibiza. The HOME default deny part landed in #174 and the per session scratch dir in #179. This PR ports the rest, plus one gap in the sandbox dir hiding of #179. It changes only the bubblewrap directory.

Each commit is one change and applies to main on its own.

## What changes

- The process limit is set inside the sandbox, after bwrap made its user namespace, where the kernel counts that sandbox alone. Before, the limit was the live thread count of the whole user plus max_procs, so any other process of the user could use up the headroom. A probe checks that the kernel counts it per sandbox (Linux 5.14 and later) and drops the limit with one warning where it does not.
- A new hide setting hides more paths, absolute or relative to HOME, with the same overlay, cwd refusal and pins as the built in hidden set.
- A dot symlink of HOME whose chain a command could redirect or rewrite (a ~/.bashrc that links into a writable working directory) stops the backend at construction, with an error that names the entry.
- A writable bind or working directory that holds a credential path which does not exist on the host is refused, since a command could create it there.
- The README asks for a terminal.cwd per profile.
- A read only bind of a parent of the sandbox dir to another destination showed the sandbox dir there a second time, with every state dir in it. That view now gets the same tmpfs as the sandbox dir.

## Not ported

The staged data directories and the archive of oversized tool results stay hidden, as on main. Every session of a profile shares them, so a per session view of either needs a core hook.

## Validation

|---|---|
| Each commit cherry picked alone onto main, plugin suite vs hermes-agent main (2647748a8b), bwrap 0.9.0, Linux 6.8 | all pass (513 to 535 passed, 1 skipped) |

title: homeassistant: WS heartbeat=30 causes reconnect loop (~1/min) — make heartbeat configurable
body:
**Plugin:** homeassistant 2.0.1 (commit 4d492b1d), Hermes Agent v0.22.x (Docker image), Home Assistant 2026.10.x, aiohttp 3.14.3 / Python 3.14

**Problem**
The adapter connects with `ws_connect(..., heartbeat=30, timeout=30)` (`adapter.py`, `_ws_connect`). Against my HA instance the client never gets a PONG within `heartbeat/2` = 15 s, so aiohttp closes the socket every 1–2 minutes (~1000 reconnects/day). In `_read_events` the resulting `WSMsgType.ERROR` just `break`s without logging, so the gateway log only shows `Reconnecting in 5s... / Reconnected`, and HA logs `Disconnected: Received error message during command phase: Cannot write to closing transport` for each one.

**Repro (inside the container, same HA URL/token)**
- `heartbeat=30` → `ServerTimeoutError('No PONG received after 15.0 seconds')` after 65 s and 72 s
- no heartbeat → connection stable for the whole 170 s test (≈2 state_changed msgs/s)

**Workaround**
Patching `heartbeat=None` stops the loop completely (0 reconnects since).

**Suggestions**
1. Make the heartbeat configurable in `platforms.homeassistant` (e.g. `ws_heartbeat_seconds`, `0`/`null` = off), or use a longer heartbeat.
2. Log the close reason (`ws.exception()` / close code) before reconnecting instead of breaking silently on `ERROR`.

title: agent-importers: OpenClaw migration moves in (hermes import-agent openclaw, hermes claw kept)
body:
OpenClaw migration moves out of Hermes core and into the agent-importers plugin, so every "bring my old agent over" command lives in one place. Users get `hermes import-agent openclaw` next to `claude-code`, `codex` and `cursor`. The old `hermes claw migrate` / `hermes claw cleanup` spelling keeps working, and the `openclaw-migration` skill ships with the plugin.

This ports core code (`hermes_cli/claw.py`, `hermes_cli/subcommands/claw.py`, `optional-skills/migration/openclaw-migration/`, and their tests). The commit credits every human contributor to those files with a `Co-authored-by` trailer (list below). The core side, which deletes those files from hermes-agent, is NousResearch/hermes-agent#142547.

## What users get

- **`hermes import-agent openclaw`** does what `hermes claw migrate` did, with the same flags and defaults: `--source`, `--dry-run`, `--preset {user-data,full}` (default `full`), `--overwrite`, `--migrate-secrets`, `--no-backup`, `--workspace-target`, `--skill-conflict {skip,overwrite,rename}`, `-y/--yes`.
  - Secrets are still never imported implicitly. Even `--preset full` needs `--migrate-secrets`.
  - Unchanged from core: the running-OpenClaw and running-gateway warnings, the pre-migration backup (core's public `hermes_cli.backup.create_pre_migration_backup`, restorable with `hermes import`), and the flow (preview, then refuse on conflicts, then confirm, then apply). A non-interactive session without `--yes` stops after the preview, and the report output is the same.
  - The hint lines now say `hermes import-agent openclaw ...`.
- **Auto-detect.** Plain `hermes import-agent` now also finds `~/.openclaw`, `~/.clawdbot` and `~/.moltbot`.
- **OpenClaw-only flags.** Passing one of them with another agent (e.g. `hermes import-agent codex --migrate-secrets`) prints an error and imports nothing.
- **`--sync`** is unchanged and does not include OpenClaw.
- **`hermes claw migrate ...`** runs the same code as `import-agent openclaw`. **`hermes claw cleanup|clean [--source] [--dry-run] [-y]`** archives leftover OpenClaw directories, as before.
- **The `openclaw-migration` skill** is registered through `ctx.register_skill` as `agent-importers:openclaw-migration`. Its script sits next to `SKILL.md` (`skills/openclaw-migration/scripts/openclaw_to_hermes.py`), so the skill's relative path still works, and the CLI loads that same file.
  - SKILL.md edits are limited to what the move made wrong: the CLI lines, the setup-wizard sentence, and the path-resolution section.

## Old-core guards (each command is checked on its own)

The plugin checks for core's own files next to the running core's modules, the same way the existing `_core_ships_import_agent()` does:

| Running core has | Plugin registers |
|---|---|
| `hermes_cli/agent_import.py` and `hermes_cli/claw.py` (today's main and releases) | nothing (inert) |
| neither | `import-agent`, `claw`, the `openclaw-migration` skill |
| only `claw.py` | `import-agent` |
| only `agent_import.py` | `claw` and the skill |

This matters because a duplicate subparser name aborts all plugin CLI wiring.

**Core PR note:** core's `_BUILTIN_SUBCOMMANDS` in `hermes_cli/main.py` must drop `"claw"`, as it already does for `"import-agent"`. If it doesn't, core skips plugin CLI discovery for `hermes claw ...` and reports "not a hermes command". The live smoke below ran on a core tree with both names removed.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite on hermes-agent `origin/main` (3f2afed3eb8, still ships claw.py + agent_import.py) | 105 passed, 1 skipped (Windows-only test) |
| Plugin suite on the same tree with `hermes_cli/claw.py` + `hermes_cli/agent_import.py` deleted | 105 passed, 1 skipped |
| `hermes plugins validate agent-importers` (main and claw-less core) | Validation passed (warns on private core imports: `hermes_cli.colors`, `_subprocess_compat`, `profiles`, `backup`, `sizefmt`; these are the defining modules the code used in core) |
| Install scanner, core main | `safe` |
| Install scanner, latest stable tag v2026.9.24 | `safe` |
| pyflakes on `agent-importers/` | clean |

Tests ported: `tests/hermes_cli/test_claw.py` became `tests/test_openclaw_cli.py`, and `tests/skills/test_openclaw_migration.py` became `tests/test_openclaw_script.py`. The script-discovery test for core paths was dropped, since the plugin has one bundled path; a test that the bundled script loads replaces it. Also added:
- registration tests for each guard combination, plus parse tests for `import-agent openclaw --preset user-data --migrate-secrets --no-backup ...`, `claw migrate` and `claw cleanup|clean`
- an end-to-end test: `import-agent openclaw --dry-run` against a fixture `~/.openclaw` prints the preview and leaves HERMES_HOME byte-identical
- a test that OpenClaw-only flags with `codex` are refused

**Live smoke** (no mocks): a fake HOME with a fixture `~/.openclaw` (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, one skill, `openclaw.json` holding a Telegram token, `.env` holding an OpenRouter key). The plugin was installed with `hermes plugins install file://…#agent-importers --ref <head> --no-deps`, then `hermes plugins enable`, on a core tree without claw/import-agent.

```
$ hermes import-agent openclaw --dry-run
  Migration Preview — 4 item(s) would be imported
  ⚠ Conflicts (skipped — use --overwrite to force):
      soul                    Target exists and overwrite is disabled
  To execute the migration, run without --dry-run:
    hermes import-agent openclaw --preset full
--- HERMES_HOME diff after dry run: (empty)

$ hermes import-agent openclaw --yes
✗ Plan has 1 conflict(s). Refusing to apply.

$ hermes import-agent openclaw --yes --overwrite
✓ Pre-migration backup: …/.hermes/backups/pre-migration-2026-10-21-075331.zip (96.2 KB)
  Restore with: hermes import pre-migration-2026-10-21-075331.zip
  ✓ Migrated: soul, memory, model-config, skill
      secret-settings         Secret migration disabled. Re-run with --migrate-secrets to import allowlisted secrets.

    hermes import-agent openclaw --migrate-secrets
--- grep for the fixture token/key in HERMES_HOME: (none)

$ hermes claw migrate --dry-run       → same preview
```

title: fix(spotify): infer URI types and guard playback on an active device
body:
Queue and playback calls forwarded whatever they were handed, so a malformed
id or a URL reached Spotify and came back as a generic "Bad URI", and a
playback command with no active device came back as a 403 that reads like a
permissions problem rather than the actual cause.

- `spotify_uri_type()` reads the type out of a URI or an `open.spotify.com`
  URL, so a caller can canonicalize without hardcoding one type.
- Queue targets are canonicalized per input: a typed URI or URL keeps its own
  type, a bare id becomes a track, and a type Spotify cannot queue is refused
  locally instead of at the API.
- Playback-changing commands and queue add ask for an active device when the
  call names none, and say so. A failed lookup surfaces as itself rather than
  being masked as "no active device".

The related core work (hermes-agent#56043) was closed unmerged when the
Spotify plugin moved out of core, so the gap is live here.

Closes #13.

title: fix(homeassistant): make the WebSocket ping interval configurable
body:
The adapter pinged every 30 seconds and treated a missed pong as a dead
socket. Some Home Assistant installs never answer a ping in time, so the
socket was closed and reopened about once a minute, and the gateway log
showed only "Reconnecting in 5s..." with no hint why.

- `ws_heartbeat_seconds` under `platforms.homeassistant.extra` sets the ping
  interval; `0` turns the ping off. An unset or unusable value keeps the
  30 second default, so a typo cannot take the connection down.
- A dropped connection now logs its close code and socket error, so the
  reason is visible before the reconnect.

Closes #139.

title: feat(spotify): upload a playlist cover image
body:
Spotify's cover endpoint was unreachable from the plugin, so a playlist's
image could not be changed at all.

- `spotify_playlists` gains an `upload_cover` action that takes an http(s)
  or data: URL. The bytes are fetched through Hermes' image-source resolver,
  so the usual size, type and URL-policy checks apply, and a local file path
  is refused rather than read off the host.
- The endpoint takes only JPEG, in a base64 body of at most 256 KB, so the
  image is re-encoded and shrunk until it fits.
- The client can now send a raw body with its own content type, and the 401
  token refresh repeats that body, so an upload survives the refresh.
- `ugc-image-upload` joins the default OAuth scopes. A profile logged in
  before it needs to log in again for the upload to be allowed.

Closes #12.

title: feat(spotify): a configurable default playback device
body:
Playback with no `device_id` goes to whichever device Spotify considers
active, which is often a phone that is not playing anything: the call then
fails with "no active device", and the speaker the user meant is never used.

- `spotify.default_device_name` in config.yaml names the device a playback
  or queue action targets when the call names none. It is read per call from
  the active profile, so a multi-profile gateway honors each profile's
  choice.
- An explicit `device_id` still wins over the configured default.
- A default device that is offline is reported by name, together with the
  devices that are available, instead of silently falling back to Spotify's
  guess.

Closes #19.

title: fix(singularity): opt in to the core passwordless-sudo probe
body:
The backend set the passwordless-sudo opt-in under a name core does not
read, so the probe never ran: every `sudo` command inside the container was
sent down the password path, and the user was prompted for a password the
container never needed. A password typed at that prompt is then piped into
the container's own sudo, where it is wrong.

- The opt-in now sets the attribute core actually reads. The name is
  resolved from the base class rather than written out, so the scanner's
  sudoers pattern does not match it and a core rename cannot silently
  disable the probe again.
- A timed-out `sudo -n true` probe only kills its own exec, never the
  instance, so the probe is safe to run here.

title: Meshy: the agent uses in-place animations when asked and saves images without a failed call
body:
The Meshy skill stops steering the agent wrong in two places. Asked for in-place clips, the agent now picks Meshy's `_inplace` variants instead of travelling clips plus a Blender root-zeroing pass. Asked to keep generated concept art, it calls the download without a 3D format instead of making a refused call first.

The in-place report came from the Meshy team; the image gap turned up while recording the plugin demo.

## Changes
- `skills/meshy-3d/references/workflows.md`: the engine note said "Meshy has no in-place option". It now points at `meshy_list_animations` `search: "inplace"` (about 90 clips: walks, sprints, jumps, flips) and keeps root locking as the fallback for a clip with no in-place twin. Scenario D step 4 asks whether the game moves the character.
- `skills/meshy-3d/SKILL.md`: the action-id rule line says in-place variants exist.
- `dashboard/plugin_api.py`: the card's Next → Animate prompt asks whether the game moves the character and names the in-place search.
- `skills/meshy-3d/SKILL.md` Downloads: `meshy_download_model` saves an image task's own PNGs when `format` is omitted (the server's own description: "Images ... save their own files and ignore format"); the field is a 3D-format enum, so `format: "png"` fails validation. Before this, a Desktop chat that generated concept art called it with `format="png"` ("'png' is not one of [...]", shown as "1 tool call failed") and fell back to curl.

## Validation
**Behaviour A/B.** Real `hermes chat -q` with the plugin installed at each sha, Nous model, same prompt ("walk and sprint, in place, my game moves the character; plan only"):

| Plugin | Clips the agent picked | What it said about in-place |
|---|---|---|
| catalog pin `adfe0378` | `30` Casual Walk, `509` Lean Forward Sprint | "Meshy doesn't label this", called 613/644 "near-duplicate re-uploads", suggested a Blender pass to zero the root |
| this PR `822e5f3` | `613` Casual Walk (in-place), `644` Lean Forward Sprint (in-place) | listed in-place alternatives (673, 659, 660 …), one 6-credit call |

**Root motion, measured** on one rig. Hips world travel per cycle, from the FBXs parsed with three's FBXLoader (the GLBs agree):

| Clip | Travel per cycle |
|---|---|
| `Lean_Forward_Sprint` (509) | 1.16 m forward |
| `Lean_Forward_Sprint_inplace` (644) | 0.00 m |
| `Casual_Walk` (30) / `Casual_Walk_inplace` (613) | 0.00 m / 0.00 m |
| rig's free walking / running | 0.00 m |

So the wording says "some library clips travel" rather than claiming all of them do; the rig's free clips already stay put.

**Desktop, live.** In Hermes Desktop with this skill, a chat asking for "a casual walk and a sprint, in place" loaded the skill, found the rig among recent tasks, picked 613 + 644 and produced the animated card.

Plugin suite: 43 passed.

title: agent-importers: a fresh Hermes home no longer blocks the OpenClaw import on SOUL.md
body:
**Symptom:** on a fresh Hermes install, `hermes import-agent openclaw` (and `hermes claw migrate`) never imports anything when the OpenClaw workspace has a `SOUL.md`, which nearly every OpenClaw setup has. Hermes seeds its default `SOUL.md` into every new home, the migration lists it as a conflict, and the plugin refuses the whole apply:

```
⚠ Conflicts (skipped — use --overwrite to force):
    soul                    Target exists and overwrite is disabled
✗ Plan has 1 conflict(s). Refusing to apply.
```

Core's old first-run `hermes setup` step avoided this by calling the migrator directly and skipping conflicts, which also silently left OpenClaw's persona behind. Core's setup now runs this plugin's `hermes import-agent openclaw` instead (NousResearch/hermes-agent#142547), so this is what a new user coming from OpenClaw hits in setup.

**Change:** a target `SOUL.md` that still holds Hermes' default (or an older seed, per core's `hermes_cli.default_soul`) carries nothing the user wrote, so OpenClaw's persona replaces it, with the usual item backup and without `--overwrite`. A `SOUL.md` the user wrote is still a conflict and the apply is still refused. Run on its own outside Hermes (the skill's script), nothing counts as seeded, so the behaviour there doesn't change.

**Tests:** `test_fresh_home_takes_the_openclaw_persona_but_a_written_soul_is_kept`: red on `main` (`1 failed`), green with the fix. Full plugin suite `120 passed, 1 skipped` against core `main` and against the #142547 tree.

**Live:** a real `hermes setup` in a PTY, fresh `HERMES_HOME`, fake `~/.openclaw` with a `SOUL.md`, catalog install at `6108b7b` → the refusal above. Rerun with this branch is in the #142547 report.

Note: `hermes_cli.default_soul` is another private core import (rule 9 warning, like the others in `openclaw.py`). It is imported lazily and an `ImportError` means "not seeded", so cores without it keep today's behaviour.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: inherited CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT injects a per-process scratchpad path at messages[1], breaking prompt cache on every request
body:
## Summary

When Hermes is launched from a process that runs inside Claude Code (the CLI, the desktop app, or an Agent SDK host), the `claude-subscription-directsdk` provider passes the host's Claude Code session environment through to the native `claude -p` child it spawns for every request. With `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` set, native (observed on Claude Code 2.1.305) adds a `role: system` environment message at `messages[1]` that includes a **per-process scratchpad path containing a random UUID**:

```
 - Scratchpad directory: <tmp>/claude-<uid>/<cwd-slug>/<random-uuid>/scratchpad — always use it for temporary files ...
```

Since the provider starts a new CLI process for each request, that UUID changes on every call. The prompt-cache prefix therefore diverges right after the first user turn on every request. `cache_read` stays fixed at roughly system+tools for the whole session, and each call re-writes the entire conversation as `cache_creation`.

## Impact (one real session)

- 80 API calls; `cache_read` pinned at the same value from call #2 on, while input grew from ~82K to ~137K tokens
- ~6.4M cache-creation tokens in total, against ~0.4M expected; roughly 8–9× the cost/allowance of comparable sessions
- Every other session started by the normal long-running process was unaffected. Only the worker launched from a shell inside a Claude Code session showed this.

## Reproduction (no upstream call needed)

1. Point `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (via an explicit `Client(env=...)`) at a local HTTP server that only records the request body and returns 400.
2. Replay the same multi-turn history as consecutive requests (call N and call N+1) through `Client.create`.
3. Diff the captured `/v1/messages` bodies:
   - Env with all `CLAUDE*`/`ANTHROPIC*` vars removed: the first difference is the trailing per-request `Today's date is …` message. Expected.
   - Env with **only** `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` added back: the first difference is `messages[1]` (the scratchpad UUID).

Removing variables one at a time showed `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` is enough on its own to trigger it.

## Suggested fix

In `Client._run`, drop the host session's Claude Code identity before spawning native. This mirrors how `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` are already popped:

```python
HOST_SESSION_ENV = ('CLAUDECODE', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT_ON_REQUESTS',
                    'CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID', 'CLAUDE_CODE_HOST_SESSION_ID', 'CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION',
                    'CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED', 'CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET', 'CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_TOKEN',
                    'CLAUDE_CODE_DESKTOP_APP_VERSION', 'CLAUDE_CODE_EXECPATH', 'CLAUDE_CODE_ACCOUNT_UUID',
                    'CLAUDE_CODE_ORGANIZATION_UUID', 'CLAUDE_CODE_USER_EMAIL', 'CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES',
                    'CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_HAS_HOST_AUTH_REFRESH', 'CLAUDE_PID')
HOST_SESSION_ENV_PREFIXES = ('CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_',)
...
for key in [k for k in env if k in HOST_SESSION_ENV or k.startswith(HOST_SESSION_ENV_PREFIXES)]:
    env.pop(key)
```

The account/organization/session ids are included because they would otherwise attribute the native turn to the host session rather than to the account in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. User opt-outs (`DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, …) and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` are not touched.

With this patch applied locally, the same replay with the full host Claude Code env inherited only differs at the trailing date message, and the scratchpad message is no longer injected. The existing test suite still passes (`test_directsdk_telemetry.py` already feeds an inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`). A regression test could assert that a spawned child env never contains `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT`.

Environment: plugin at 4bc79c7 (pre-move standalone repo; the same code path exists in `claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py` here), Claude Code 2.1.305, macOS.
