title: fix(directsdk): drop the host session's Claude Code identity before spawning native
body:
fix(directsdk): drop the host session's Claude Code identity before spawning native

Hermes can itself run inside Claude Code (the CLI, the desktop app, an Agent
SDK host). Inherited there, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` makes native inject a
per-process scratchpad path - a random UUID - into the request at
`messages[1]`. The plugin spawns a fresh CLI per request, so the UUID changes
every time: the cached prefix diverges after the first user turn and the whole
conversation is re-written as cache creation on each call.

- The host session's identity is dropped from the child env on the turn path
  and on the setup probes. The account the plugin drives still comes from
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, resolved separately, and a user's own opt-outs
  (`DISABLE_TELEMETRY`, `DO_NOT_TRACK`, ...) are untouched.
- The session ids go too: they would attribute the native turn to the host
  session rather than to the account in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`.

Closes #150.

title: fix(xchat): bound the inbound media download while it is read
body:
fix(xchat): bound the inbound media download while it is read

The inbound attachment download read the whole body into memory with
`resp.content`, and the gateway's inbound-media cap was only applied
afterwards, in the adapter. An oversized attachment was therefore held in the
gateway's memory before it was refused, and a lying (or absent)
`Content-Length` could not be caught at all.

The body is now read under the cap as it streams: the declared size is checked
first, and the running total on every chunk, so the refusal happens while
reading. This is the same read the other Hermes platform plugins use.

The cap itself is unchanged - it is the gateway's
`gateway.max_inbound_media_bytes`, the same limit the adapter already applied
to the decrypted size.

title: feat(langfuse): opt-in trace userId from the gateway sender
body:
## What does this PR do?

Gateway traces can now record who sent the message as the Langfuse `userId`, which is what NousResearch/hermes-agent#44639 asks for. Langfuse's Users view and per-user cost breakdowns key off that field. Today every turn from a shared Slack or Matrix room lands under its session, and nothing on the trace says which person drove it.

The sender ID is a third-party identifier, so this stays off unless the profile turns it on:

```bash
hermes config set plugins.entries.langfuse.settings.end_user_attribution true
```

The key is declared in `config_schema` (hence `manifest_version: 2`), so the Desktop also shows it as a switch on the plugin's settings page. The plugin reads it through `ctx.get_config` on every turn. Under a multiplexed gateway that resolves the served profile's `config.yaml`, so one profile opting in doesn't export another profile's senders, and a change applies from the next turn without a restart. With the setting off, `pre_llm_call` drops `sender_id` before anything stores it. A value that isn't a boolean logs one warning and counts as off.

With it on, the plugin uses the sender ID exactly as the platform reports it. `privacy.redact_pii` doesn't change that, since it hashes IDs only in the prompt the model sees, and the README says so. `pre_llm_call` is the only hook that carries `sender_id`, and the root trace opens later on `pre_api_request`, so the plugin keeps the sender per turn until that turn's trace ends. Subagents inherit the user of the turn that spawned them. Turns with no sender, such as cron and CLI runs, get no `userId`. Both maps are capped like the trace state. `main` already records the profile in trace metadata, so `userId` can mean the end user, which is how #44639 proposes to settle the overlap with NousResearch/hermes-agent#26455.

The approach is the one kamonspecial proposed in #44639 and implemented in NousResearch/hermes-agent#43491, against the in-core copy of this plugin before it moved here. The sweeper closed that PR because its switch was a `HERMES_LANGFUSE_END_USER_ATTRIBUTION` env var, and behavioral settings belong in `config.yaml`. This version keeps the setting in `config.yaml`.

One thing a reviewer has to decide: the contributing guide rejects "outbound telemetry / usage attribution without opt-in gating", with no third-party identifier tagging "until a generic user-facing opt-in (config gate + setup prompt + `hermes tools` toggle) exists. Park behind a label." This PR has the config gate and the Desktop switch. It has no setup prompt and no `hermes tools` toggle, because core has no generic surface for either and a plugin can't add one. If this has to wait for that surface, please park it under `needs-decision` or `blocked`. On NousResearch/hermes-agent#67544, Teknium wrote that the userId half "waits on the decision in hermes-agent#44639". I opened this as a draft so that decision has a working diff to look at.

Per this repo's CONTRIBUTING, users get this once the `langfuse` catalog pin moves. I haven't opened that PR. The change adds no hooks, tools or dependencies (`pre_llm_call` is already registered on `main`).

## Related Issue

Refs NousResearch/hermes-agent#44639

I used "Refs" rather than "Fixes" because that issue also holds the decision above. Earlier work: NousResearch/hermes-agent#43491 (closed). The masking half of NousResearch/hermes-agent#67544 is done; its user_id half waits on #44639.

#110, #112 and #123 also change this plugin. This branch merges cleanly with each of their heads (`git merge-tree`).

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `langfuse/__init__.py`: `_end_user_attribution()` reads the setting through `ctx.get_config`. `on_pre_llm_call` accepts `sender_id` and keeps it for the turn only when the setting is true. `_start_root_trace()` passes `user_id` to `propagate_attributes`. `on_subagent_start` hands the parent turn's user to the child session and `on_subagent_stop` drops it. `_finish_trace()` forgets the turn's sender.
- `langfuse/plugin.yaml`: `manifest_version: 2` and a `config_schema` entry for `end_user_attribution` (bool, default false). `requires_hermes` stays at `>=0.21.7`, which already reads v2 manifests, bool schema fields and `ctx.get_config`.
- `langfuse/README.md`: an "End-user attribution (opt-in)" section.
- `langfuse/tests/test_langfuse_attribution.py`: 11 new tests. Six cover the gate: no setting, explicit false, a malformed value (one warning, no `userId`), a multiplexed A→B→A sequence where only the opted-in profile exports its sender, and the plugin loaded the way Hermes loads it (copied into a profile's `plugins/`, enabled in `config.yaml`, hooks fired through `PluginManager.invoke_hook`) with and without the setting. Five cover attribution once it's on: the sender reaches the root trace, a senderless turn gets no `userId`, the sender doesn't leak into the next turn, subagents inherit the spawning user, and the per-turn map is bounded.

## How to Test

1. From `langfuse/`, with hermes-agent checked out beside this repo: `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=../../hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q`. I get 154 passed on this branch and 143 on `main`, both against hermes-agent `8f555f4f92` (current `main`) and `a5856c1a51`.
2. To check the gate itself, keep this branch's tests and remove only the `_end_user_attribution()` condition from `on_pre_llm_call`. I get 5 failed and 149 passed. The 5 are the tests that expect no `userId` without the opt-in.
3. `hermes plugins validate ./langfuse` passes. Its output matches `main` except that "config schema — not declared" becomes "config schema — shape valid".
4. The settings path, in a temp `HERMES_HOME` with the plugin installed and enabled in two profiles: `plugin_settings_fields()` returns one boolean field, default false. `save_plugin_settings()` with `{"end_user_attribution": True}` writes `config.yaml`, and the already-loaded plugin reads true on its next call. The second profile still reads false, and the first still reads true after that.
5. Live: I drove the registered hooks with the Langfuse SDK 4.15.2 exporting over HTTPS to a self-hosted Langfuse 4.63.0, one turn with the setting absent and one with it set to true. Read back from the Langfuse database, the first trace has no `userId` and the second has the synthetic sender ID.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) (and this repo's own `CONTRIBUTING.md`, which is the one that applies here)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate: nothing open in either repo for #44639. NousResearch/hermes-agent#43491 is the closed earlier attempt.
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits): one commit, four files
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: 154 passed in the plugin suite, run from `langfuse/`
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs): this repo has no `scripts/check`. Its equivalent gate is `hermes plugins validate ./langfuse` (CONTRIBUTING step 3), which passes.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Debian 13, Python 3.14.7, hermes-agent `8f555f4f92`. I haven't run macOS or Windows; CI does.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings), or N/A: the README section, the module docstring, and the `config_schema` description the Desktop shows
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys, or N/A: the new key is a plugin setting declared in this plugin's `config_schema`. `cli-config.yaml.example` lives in hermes-agent and doesn't list plugin settings.
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows, or N/A: no architecture or workflow change
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility), or N/A: the plugin change only reads config through `ctx.get_config`. The new loader test builds its temp profile with `shutil.copytree` and `tmp_path`.
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior, or N/A: no tool changed

## Screenshots / Logs

```
hermes-agent 8f555f4f92, plugin main 6108b7b:         143 passed
hermes-agent 8f555f4f92, this branch:                 154 passed, 2 warnings
hermes-agent a5856c1a51, this branch:                 154 passed, 2 warnings
this branch's tests, gate removed from __init__.py:   5 failed, 149 passed
hermes plugins validate ./langfuse:                   Validation passed.
```

The 2 warnings are a `DeprecationWarning` from core's `hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py` (`re.split` with a positional `maxsplit`). The new loader test reaches it when core parses the manifest.

This repo has no PR template, so the sections above follow the one in hermes-agent.

title: homeassistant: convert UTC timestamps to local timezone in tool responses
body:
## Feature Request

**Plugin:** homeassistant (v2.0.1)

### User Story

As a Hermes user with Home Assistant, I want timestamps in tool responses to be in my local timezone so that I can understand when events happened without the agent needing to do error-prone manual conversion.

### Problem

All four `ha_*` tools return timestamps in raw UTC as returned by the HA REST API. This includes:

- `last_changed` / `last_updated` in `ha_get_state` responses
- `last_triggered` in automation attributes
- Any timestamp fields in `ha_list_entities` responses

The agent then has to manually convert these to the user's local timezone before presenting them. In practice this has caused errors:

- Raw UTC timestamps were presented to the user without conversion, causing confusion about when events actually occurred.
- Mental UTC-to-local conversion produced incorrect dates on security device data.

### Proposal

Convert timestamps to the user's local timezone before returning them in tool responses. Options:

1. **Use the HA instance's configured `time_zone`** (from `configuration.yaml`). The plugin already connects to HA — it could fetch the configured timezone once at startup and apply it to all timestamp fields in responses. This is the most accurate option since it matches what the HA frontend displays.

2. **Add a `HASS_TIMEZONE` env var** (optional, defaults to the HA instance timezone or system timezone). This would let operators override if needed.

3. **Include both UTC and local** in responses — e.g., `last_changed_local: "2026-10-21T18:42:27-07:00"` alongside the raw `last_changed: "2026-10-22T01:42:27.349875+00:00"`. This preserves the original data while giving the agent a local-time field to present directly.

The key requirement: the agent should be able to present a local-time timestamp to the user without doing manual timezone math, which is error-prone.

### Environment

- Plugin: homeassistant v2.0.1 (commit 4d492b1)
- HA instance: 2026.9.2 (with 2026.10.2 update available)
- Hermes Agent: v0.22.4

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Long tool calls stream their arguments instead of being killed as stalls
body:
Long tool calls (a whole file in one `write_file`) are no longer cancelled as stalls: the relay asks the API to stream each tool's arguments as the model writes them.

## Why
Claude Code turns fine-grained tool streaming (`eager_input_streaming`) on only when it talks to a first-party base URL. Behind our loopback relay its tools go out without the flag, so the API holds a large argument until it is complete. #113's liveness chunks then reach Hermes in one burst at the end, and the stall timer has already killed the call.

## Change
- `admission.stream_tool_input`: sets `eager_input_streaming: true` on every tool that does not already carry it. A value native set wins. A request with no tools, or one that does not parse, forwards byte-identical.
- Called in the relay right after the breakpoint transforms.
- `tests/test_admission_tool_streaming.py`: the two invariants (red on `main`: import error).
- `tests/test_admission_two_marks.py`: its relay round-trip compared the forwarded tool list to native's byte for byte, to prove no cache mark moved. It now ignores only `eager_input_streaming`, so the marks invariant it pins is unchanged. This is the only existing assertion touched.

## Live evidence (Opus 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.304, subscription token)
Timing every chunk the plugin `Client` yields while Opus writes one 2,000-word `write_file` argument, with #113 applied:

| relay | chunks | largest gap |
|---|---|---|
| main | 3,742, all at 93 s | **89.8 s** |
| this change | 2,180, spread over the call | 0.5 s after the first token |

End to end, with hermes-agent#142905 + #31 + #113 + this change: a real `hermes chat` run with a 30 s stall timer wrote a 4,516-word file in one tool call (111 s). Without this change, the same run was killed.

`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING` was tried first and does not add the flag behind the relay (wire capture).

Part of the fix for hermes-agent#125095 with #31 and #113. Plugin suite: 434 passed against core `main`.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set for Hermes' anthropic provider makes every subscription turn fail
body:
### Plugin

claude-subscription-directsdk (the bug form's dropdown lists only `homeassistant` and `spotify`)

### What happened, and what did you expect?

**Expected:** one Hermes can serve both Claude routes from the model picker: the core `anthropic` provider billed to an API key, and `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` billed to the Claude subscription. Each session uses whichever one was picked.

**What happens:** while `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set for the `anthropic` provider, every turn on the subscription provider fails before Claude Code starts:

```
ValueError: OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

With `fallback_providers` configured, Hermes then quietly answers from the fallback model, so the session looks fine but isn't running on the model that was picked. The same error also breaks the provider when it is the compression or auxiliary model.

**Why it happens:** Hermes loads `~/.hermes/.env` into its own process environment, and the `anthropic` provider reads its key from there. `Client._run` (`directsdk.py`) copies `os.environ` for the Claude Code child and raises when any of `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY` is present. The README's remedy, "Remove those overrides from the launching environment", is impossible while the core `anthropic` provider needs the key in that same environment. Setup has the same problem in reverse: `_child_env` (`directsdk_setup.py`) passes the key to `claude auth status`, so the CLI reports an API-key login, `plan` comes back empty, and discovery runs against the wrong login.

The refusal exists so this provider never bills API usage, and that goal is right. Refusing is just not the only way to reach it. If the credential is dropped from the child's environment, Claude Code can't sign in with it, so the turn runs on the subscription and the key stays usable for the `anthropic` provider. Endpoint and backend redirects (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK|VERTEX|FOUNDRY`) are a different case, because they change where requests go. Those should stay refused.

**Reproduction against the real CLI** (Claude Code 2.1.307, claude.ai Max login, dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the process environment):

| | `setup_status()` | one turn (`haiku`) |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (`55c1b45`) | `logged_in: True`, `plan: ''` | `ValueError: OAuth provider refuses … ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| proposed fix | `logged_in: True`, `plan: 'Claude Max'` | `SUBSCRIPTION_OK` (served on the subscription) |

A fix PR follows. Related but different: #28 rejects a key the CLI *stores itself* (`authMethod: api_key`) at setup time. That still holds after this change, which covers keys *inherited from Hermes' environment*. In #44 the reporter mentions hitting this same guard and scrubbing the key locally.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.4+34.g376bdc2 (2026.9.24) · upstream 7b9cb2e3
Install method: git (macOS)
claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental  catalog:official@9b074e16  0.3.3  enabled
Claude Code 2.1.307
```

### Logs

```text
2026-10-22 00:15:33,497 WARNING [session] agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3) error_type=ValueError provider=claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental base_url=process://claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental model=claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] summary=OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
2026-10-22 00:15:33,506 INFO [session] agent.chat_completion_helpers: Fallback activated: claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] → gemini-4-argon (antigravity-oauth)
2026-10-21 22:49:18,337 WARNING [session] agent.conversation_compression: Configured compression model 'claude-sonnet-5-5' failed (OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); recovered using the main model.
```

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): an API key Hermes holds for its anthropic provider no longer blocks the subscription provider
body:
## Bug Description

When Hermes holds `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` for its core `anthropic` provider, every turn on `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` fails with `ValueError: OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Hermes then falls back to another provider without saying so. The setup probe is affected the other way: it hands the key to `claude auth status`, which then reports an API-key login with an empty plan. Users end up choosing between the two Claude routes instead of picking either one from the model picker.

Fixes #157

## Root Cause

Hermes loads `~/.hermes/.env` into its own process, so the plugin inherits the key that is meant for the `anthropic` provider. `Client._run` treated that inherited credential as a conflict and raised. `_child_env` passed it to the setup and discovery probes. The README's remedy, removing it from the launching environment, is impossible while core needs it in that same environment.

## Fix

The guard's goal is unchanged: this provider never bills API usage. It now reaches that goal by keeping the credential away from the child instead of refusing the turn.

- `directsdk_setup.py`: `API_CREDENTIAL_ENV` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`) and `drop_api_credentials(env)`. `_child_env` applies it, so `auth status` and the discovery handshake run against the real login.
- `directsdk.py`: the turn path applies the same helper to the child env. The conflict check keeps refusing `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK|VERTEX|FOUNDRY`, because those change where requests go, and dropping them silently would hide a deliberate redirect.
- `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` now describe the new behavior.
- `tests/test_directsdk_inherited_api_key.py` (new) reads the env the fake CLI actually received, on the gateway's real turn path (no explicit `env=`, so the child inherits `os.environ`) and on discovery. It reuses the env-capture harness in `test_directsdk_telemetry.py`.
- `tests/test_directsdk.py`: the old assertion that an inherited API key raises was the behavior being fixed. It now asserts that `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is still refused by name.

#28 still adds value next to this change: a key stored by the CLI itself (`authMethod: api_key`) is outside the process environment, and it still reaches #28's setup check. #152 drops a different class of variables (the host Claude Code session identity) at the same spawn points. The two changes touch neighboring lines, but each is complete without the other.

## How to Verify

1. Red first: with only the new test file on `main`, both cases fail for the reasons named in the test:
   ```
   FAILED …[discovery] AssertionError: API credential reached the child: ['ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN', 'ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY']
   FAILED …[turn]      ValueError: OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY
   2 failed
   ```
   With the fix: `2 passed`.
2. Full suite, set up as CONTRIBUTING and CI do (Python 3.14, `pip install -e ./hermes-agent pytest pytest-asyncio`, hermes-agent `8237c7f8` side by side, macOS):
   `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=../../hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q`. The result was `436 passed, 9 subtests passed`, against `434 passed` on `main` in the same env.
3. `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate ./claude-subscription-directsdk` printed `Validation passed.`
4. Real CLI (Claude Code 2.1.307, claude.ai Max login, dummy `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the process env):

   | | `setup_status()` | one turn on `haiku` |
   |---|---|---|
   | `main` | `logged_in: True`, `plan: ''` | `ValueError … ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
   | this branch | `logged_in: True`, `plan: 'Claude Max'` | `SUBSCRIPTION_OK` |

5. In a live gateway with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `~/.hermes/.env`, one session on `anthropic` and one on this provider both answered from the model that was picked.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression test for this bug (fails on `main`, passes here)
- [x] Existing tests still pass (full plugin suite, 436 passed on macOS; CI covers Linux and Windows)
- [x] Manual verification of the fix (real Claude Code CLI and a live gateway)
- [x] PR touches one plugin; manifest validates against current core

## Risk Assessment

Low. The change only removes three Anthropic API credential variables from the Claude Code child's environment, and the parent process keeps them. The child never needed them: the provider is subscription-only and the README already said no API key is sent. Endpoint and backend overrides are still refused as before. If a caller passed an explicit `env=` containing an API key, that key is now dropped instead of reaching the CLI, which matches the provider's no-API-billing contract.

Prepared with AI assistance; reviewed and verified by the author.

title: agent-importers: imports run by hermes setup read as part of setup; OpenClaw workspace → terminal.cwd
body:
A live first-time `hermes setup` run (hermes-agent #142547, which offers this plugin's import during setup) showed the OpenClaw / Claude Code / Codex import speaking as if it were run by hand, writing a `.env` key Hermes no longer reads, and a result list one item shorter than its preview. This fixes all four in the plugin.

## Changes
- **`--from-setup`** (hidden flag; hermes-agent #142547 passes it): inside setup there is no "run 'hermes setup' for credentials" pointer (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor settings line, stripped-secrets line, closing line), and OpenClaw's skipped items, mostly things the user does not have, fold into one line: `─ Skipped: 28 item(s) with nothing to bring over (each is listed in the report)`. The report file under `migration/openclaw/<time>/` still lists every item and reason. Outside setup the output is unchanged.
- **"To execute the migration, run without --dry-run"** now prints only after an actual `--dry-run`. Before, every OpenClaw preview printed it, including a normal run, right before "Proceed with migration?".
- **OpenClaw's workspace → `terminal.cwd`.** Hermes removed `MESSAGING_CWD` (hermes-agent `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`: "`MESSAGING_CWD` is removed and `TERMINAL_CWD` in `.env` is deprecated; canonical is `terminal.cwd`"; the loader warns about it). The migration now writes `terminal.cwd` in config.yaml (skip if equal, conflict if the user set another folder, `.`/`auto`/`cwd` placeholders count as unset). The "workspace inside the OpenClaw dir" guard also expands `~` now: OpenClaw's own default `~/.openclaw/workspace` was never recognised, so it got written as the Hermes cwd.
- **The apply report lists the skills category `DESCRIPTION.md`** (`skill-category` / `shared-skill-category`). The file was always written, but only the preview listed it: preview said 8 items, the result 7.

## Evidence
Real bundled migration script and plugin CLI against the fixture home from the #142547 live run (OpenClaw with `workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace`, a Telegram token and an OpenRouter key), `import-agent openclaw --migrate-secrets --yes`, pin `2442ec1` vs this branch with `--from-setup`:

| | pin 2442ec1 | this branch |

| `.env` keys written | `MESSAGING_CWD`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| preview / result item counts | 8 / 7 (`skill-category` missing from the result) | 7 / 7 |

All six red on `main`, green here.

title: fix(homeassistant): give the agent the timestamps in local time (#155)
body:
Closes #155.

Home Assistant answers every timestamp in UTC, so the agent has to convert it by hand before presenting it - which is where the wrong dates come from (a security device's last trigger read as the wrong evening).

`ha_get_state` now also carries the local time next to the raw UTC value: `last_changed_local`, `last_updated_local` and, for an automation, `last_triggered_local` in the attributes.

The zone is the instance's own `time_zone` (what its frontend shows, read from `/api/config` and cached for an hour). `HASS_TIMEZONE` overrides it (option 2 of the issue), and when the instance's zone cannot be read the machine's local time is used. The UTC fields stay exactly as they were, so nothing that reads them changes, and a timestamp that cannot be parsed is left alone instead of failing the read.

Two details worth a reviewer's eye:

- The cached zone is keyed by the instance URL, like the plugin's registry cache above it: two profiles pointing at different Home Assistants must not see each other's zone.
- Windows Python ships no IANA time zone database, so `tzdata` is added as a dependency there; without it `ZoneInfo` cannot resolve the instance's zone and the twins would silently fall back to the machine's own time.

One note on the current 2.0.1 behaviour: `ha_list_entities` does not return timestamps at all (the summary carries only entity_id, state, friendly_name, area and device), so the conversion applies to `ha_get_state` - the tool that does return `last_changed`/`last_updated` and the automation attributes.

Tests: 10 new cases in `tests/test_homeassistant_tools.py` (the local twin, the UTC value kept as it is, an automation trigger, the operator override, an unreadable timestamp, the zone read once, a zone-less instance, an unresolvable zone, a failing config read, and two instances not sharing a zone). Red on base, green with the change; the plugin's suite is 145 passed, 2 skipped.

title: feat(camofox): the Camofox browser backend moves out of Hermes core into a plugin
body: The Camofox browser backend is now a plugin here. Existing users keep their `CAMOFOX_URL`, `CAMOFOX_*` env and `browser.camofox.*` config as they are, and get eight open core fixes that never merged. This is the first of three PRs. Merge order: this PR → the hermes-agent catalog entry (`plugin-catalog/camofox.yaml`, re-pinned to this PR's merged sha) → the hermes-agent PR that deletes the built-in `browser_*` tools, agent-browser and `tools/browser_camofox*.py`. ## What moved `camofox/` is the Camofox side of `tools/browser_camofox.py`, `tools/browser_camofox_state.py`, the Camofox branches of `browser_tool.py` and its eval-policy and snapshot siblings, the Camofox setup in `hermes_cli/tools_config*.py`, and the core tests for all of these. - **Same tool names, toolset `camofox`:** `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_back`, `browser_press`, `browser_get_images`, `browser_vision`, `browser_console`, plus `browser_import_cookies`, which is offered only when `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` is set. Skills that call these tools keep working. Descriptions are core's text, word for word. Parameters Camofox can't honour are dropped: `full` on snapshot, `annotate` on vision, and `clear` / console-log capture on console. - **Does nothing on old cores:** if the running core still has `tools/browser_camofox.py` (detected with `PathFinder.find_spec` in `tools.__path__`), `register()` registers nothing and logs one line. Tests pin that detection with an autouse fixture, so the suite runs the active path on either core. - **Same config and safety as core:** same deterministic `userId` (so persistent Camofox profiles keep their logins), same `managed_persistence` / `user_id` / `session_key` / `adopt_existing_tab` / `CAMOFOX_REWRITE_LOOPBACK_URLS` handling, same snapshot truncation thresholds and stored-snapshot path. Navigate refuses cloud-metadata URLs, URLs that embed a secret, and hosts on `security.website_blocklist`. Eval policy: read-only by default, `browser.allow_unsafe_evaluate` to opt out. Tool output is redacted. - **Profile isolation:** secrets come from `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`. Sessions are keyed by `(hermes_home_key(), task_id)`. `os.environ` is never written. Vision goes through `ctx.llm` under the auxiliary task `camofox_vision`, which falls back to `auxiliary.vision`. - **Cleanup:** the task's Camofox session is cleaned up after every turn (`on_session_end`), as core's `cleanup_task_resources` did, and on `on_session_finalize`. - **CLI:** `hermes camofox setup` and `hermes camofox status`. ## Ported core PRs (one commit each, authors credited with `Co-authored-by`) | Core PR | Author | What it fixes here | |---|---|---| | NousResearch/hermes-agent#125602 | @Sreegs | recreate the tab on 410 Gone, not only 404 | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#120796 | @KhanCold | close the health-check response | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#106978 | @0xble | `browser_navigate` returns the page title (the server omits it; read from `GET /tabs`) | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#120190 | @tolly-xyz | only adopt tabs that carry this session's key | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#127179 | @whosebruce, @jaysonsantos | redact snapshot text (filled passwords); `browser_console` never opens a blank tab | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#135204 | @clsferguson | a tab the server reaped or lost in a restart is resynced, not a raw 404 for the rest of the session | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#97391 | @Elshayib | README: native Node setup first, and when persistent logins reach disk | | NousResearch/hermes-agent#12106 | @wangkezun | `browser_import_cookies` (Netscape cookies.txt into the session's Camofox user) | Not ported: the vault-fill routing in #127179 and the shadow-root form templates in #135204. Both live in core's `browser_vault` tool (see "What this needs from core"). Two further commits come from an independent review of this branch. Each fix has a test that failed before it: - Once a dead tab is resynced to another live tab, click/type/press are not replayed there, because their ref came from the old page. Reads retry. - The server's `error` / `code` / `recovery` text (e.g. `stale_refs`) reaches the model. - `browser_get_images` output is redacted like snapshots. - "evaluate unsupported" is decided by the status code. - No writes through a symlinked `cache/web`. - A directory passed as a cookie file gets an error, not a crash. - Per-turn cleanup now matches core (cron and subagent task ids never matched a finalized session id). ## Live verification Real runs: `docker run ghcr.io/jo-inc/camofox-browser:latest` (camofox-browser 1.18.1) on :9377. Each leg used a scratch `HERMES_HOME`, `hermes plugins install file://#camofox --yes --enable` at a4cb7f6, and `hermes chat -q` against Nous inference (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`). The prompt: navigate to example.com, snapshot, click the link, report the title. Tool calls and results below are read back from each run's `state.db`. Later commits change only docs and a Windows skip marker. | | hermes-agent main (still bundles Camofox) + plugin | post-removal core (main with `tools/browser_camofox*.py` and the built-in `browser_*` entries removed, local only) + plugin | |---|---|---| | plugin | inert: one line, `camofox plugin inactive: this Hermes core still bundles the Camofox browser backend` | active | | `browser_*` tools in the registry | built-in, toolset `browser`, no duplicates | from the plugin, toolset `camofox` (11 tools) | | `browser_navigate` | `{"success": true, "title": "", ...}` (core) | `{"success": true, "title": "Example Domain", ...}` | | `browser_snapshot` → `browser_click @e1` | ok → `https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains` | ok → `https://www.iana.org/help/example-domains` | | `browser_vision` | not called | `"The main heading on this page says Example Domains"` (aux model through `ctx.llm`) | | `browser_console document.title` | `"Example Domains"` | `"Example Domains"` | | answer | Example Domains | Example Domains | | end of run | n/a | `DELETE /sessions/` in the server log (ephemeral session closed) | **camofox-human-auth** (catalog community plugin, pinned 19946d2) installed next to this one on the post-removal core: it imports nothing from core's Camofox code (only `requests` and its own REST calls). With matching session keys (`CAMOFOX_SESSION_KEY=native-auth`), `camofox_auth_open` → `browser_snapshot` adopted its tab with no navigate. Its install script writes `CAMOFOX_SESSION_KEY=visible-auth` while its tool descriptions tell the model to use `native-auth`. After #120190, Hermes no longer adopts a tab with a different key, so in that setup Hermes opens its own tab in the same Camofox user (same cookies) instead of taking over the auth tab. That needs a key fix on their side, noted for their maintainer, not changed here. ## Tests, validate, scanner - `camofox/tests`: 84 passed against hermes-agent main, against the post-removal tree and against v0.22.4. The `tests.yml` recipe run locally (`env -i`, fresh py3.14 venv, `pip install -e` of a `git archive` of core main) also gives 84 passed. - `hermes plugins validate camofox`: passes on the post-removal tree. **On today's core main it fails "built-in tool collisions":** `provides_tools` names the `browser_*` tools that core still bundles. Declaring fewer names would fail "undeclared tools registered" as soon as the core PR lands, so no manifest passes on both cores. This repo's CI `validate` step is red until the core removal PR merges; the plugin itself does nothing on that core, as the table shows. - `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin`: **safe** with the scanner from hermes-agent main and from v0.22.4. ## What this needs from core These are private imports with no plugin seam yet. `hermes plugins validate` lists them, and the README has the same table: - `tools.url_safety.is_always_blocked_url`, `normalize_url_for_request`: the metadata floor on navigate - `tools.website_policy.check_website_access`: the website blocklist - `agent.redact.redact_sensitive_text`, `agent.redact._PREFIX_RE`: output redaction, and refusing URLs that embed a secret - `tools.credential_files.to_agent_visible_cache_path`: the stored-snapshot path as Docker/SSH terminals see it - `import tools` for `tools.__path__`: the inert-on-old-core check - vault fill in Camofox mode: core's vault tool would need a way to evaluate its fill script through the active browser backend's tab

title: directsdk: a revoked OAuth token is never refreshed — the admission gate denies native's retry after 401
body:
## Summary

When Anthropic rejects the CLI's OAuth access token with `401 OAuth access token has been revoked`, the request fails permanently. The admission gate allows exactly one upstream request per call, so Claude Code's follow-up attempt (presumably after refreshing the token) is denied with `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED`. Every later request fails the same way until the user launches Claude Code interactively, which refreshes the shared login and everything works again.

## Environment

- Plugin `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.3 (catalog pin `a4e311e`; reproduced before updating to `9b074e1`)
- Claude Code 2.1.307
- macOS, Hermes desktop app + launchd gateway, one shared `~/.claude` login also used by interactive Claude Code

## Log

```
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable) error_type=ClaudeAPIError provider=claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental model=claude-opus-5-5[1m] summary=HTTP 401: Incomplete upstream response (first upstream attempt: status 401, capture incomplete, native retries denied: 1, upstream said: OAuth access token has been revoked.): API Error: 400 HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED
```

Four failures in the last ~3 weeks: 2026-10-05 10:09, 10-21 11:57, 10-21 21:04, 10-22 08:50 (PDT).

## Analysis

`admission.py` `Handler.do_POST` returns `400 HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED` to any request after the first (`gate.used`). In `directsdk.py`, `admission.status != 200` then raises `ClaudeAPIError(... 401)`, which Hermes treats as non-retryable. The native retry after a 401, which is where Claude Code would refresh its OAuth token, never reaches upstream, and the refreshed token is never used.

What revokes the token in the first place isn't confirmed. A likely cause is that the shared login gets refreshed by another Claude Code process (interactive CLI or another spawn), which rotates the token the plugin's spawn had already read.

## Suggested fix

Either of these would help:
- Allow one extra admitted request when the first upstream attempt returned 401 with an auth error, so native can refresh and retry.
- Or catch a 401 on the first attempt and re-spawn native once (it re-reads `.credentials.json` / refreshes) before raising.

Related: #37 (login health invisible to Hermes), #44 (different, gateway-only logged-out mechanism).

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] per-call: a tool call cut off at max_tokens fails with error_max_turns instead of finish length
body:
## What happens

55c1b45 ("a tool call cut off mid-argument no longer breaks the relay") drops an unparseable tool call at `message_stop` so Hermes gets finish `length`. On the per-call path with the real Claude Code CLI, the step still fails:

```
RuntimeError: Native request failed: error_max_turns
```

Expected: the answer's text with `finish_reason == "length"` and no tool calls, as 55c1b45 describes.

## Repro (real CLI, synthetic peer, no credentials)

The synthetic peer from `evals/directsdk_admission.py`, with one extra event stream: a text block, then a `tool_use` block whose only `input_json_delta` is `{"path":`, then `stop_reason: max_tokens`. One `Client.create` per-call step with one tool offered.

- Claude Code 2.1.306, plugin at main b5932f1: `RuntimeError: Native request failed: error_max_turns`. The upstream request count is 1.

## Why

- Native keeps the cut call (its input becomes an unparsed-input marker) and answers it locally with a parse error. That sets a follow-up turn, which `--max-turns 1` stops, so the result subtype is `error_max_turns` with exit code 1.
- The relay's `Capture` dropped the only call, so `calls` is empty. `boundary = bool(calls) and final.get('subtype') == 'error_max_turns' and ...` is then false, and the step raises "Native request failed". `_fast_eligible` likewise needs a `tool_use` in the capture for `error_max_turns`, so the fast return is skipped too.
- The 55c1b45 test passes because its fake native ends the cut turn with `success`.

## Possible fix

Treat a turn whose calls were all dropped as unparsed (`admission.capture.unparsed` non-empty) like a turn with calls at the `error_max_turns` boundary, and in `_fast_eligible`. The answer then reaches Hermes with finish `length` and no calls, as intended.

title: fix(mcp-serve): expose tool_search-deferred tools under --tools
body:
## Problem
`hermes_tools.available_tool_specs()` called `model_tools.get_tool_definitions()` without
`skip_tool_search_assembly=True`. When core's tool_search is active, tools in the default
deferred set (e.g. `image_generate`) are collapsed into the `tool_search` / `tool_describe` /
`tool_call` bridge, so `--tools` silently never exposed them on the MCP wire.

## Fix
Request the raw, uncollapsed schemas with `skip_tool_search_assembly=True`. The curated
`EXPOSED_TOOLS` allowlist and toolset filtering still apply, so nothing beyond the allowlist is exposed.

## Tests
- Added `test_tools_mode_offers_tool_search_deferred_tools`: a registry that collapses deferred
  tools unless the raw catalog is requested; asserts `image_generate` is offered and the
  tool_search bridge tools are not.
- mcp-serve suite against current hermes-agent core: 91 passed. The new test fails without the fix.

title: fix(advanced-delegation): refuse the route editor unless stdin and stdout are terminals (Windows)
body:
## Symptom
Official main's tests run (39861975876) fails `advanced-delegation · windows-latest`: `test_hermes_delegation_config_show_runs_through_the_real_cli` expected `hermes delegation config` with stdin from NUL and stdout captured to exit 1 with the no-terminal message; it exited 0. The test only started running once core's delegation seam reached main (#142563), so #136's own CI skipped it.

## Cause
`cli.py` checked only `sys.stdin.isatty()`. Windows reports the NUL device as a tty, so a piped run went into the curses editor.

## Fix
Require both stdin and stdout to be terminals (curses needs both). The test also decodes the child's output as UTF-8 instead of the Windows code page (`UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap'` in the same log).

Ubuntu and macOS already passed.

title: advanced-delegation: /delegation saves for the next session; --now applies to this chat
body:
`/delegation` now **saves** the mode and says it takes effect from the next session (`/new`); `--now` is the opt-in that also applies it to the running chat. The session-only switch and `--global` are gone.

Core: NousResearch/hermes-agent branch `feat/delegation-switch-next-session` (96282f40d1) adds `apply_now` to `ctx.delegation_backends.set_global_backend` (core rebuilds the session's tools at its next turn) and drops `get_session_backend` / `set_session_backend`. This plugin's current `main` fails on that core (8 failed, 7 errors in its suite); this branch passes on it and on hermes-agent `main`.

## What the user sees

| Command | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `/delegation <mode>` | switched routing for this session only | saves `delegation.backend`; reply: takes effect from the next session (`/new`), this chat's tools keep the previous mode's choices, add `--now` to apply here |
| `/delegation <mode> --now` | n/a | saves AND applies to this chat: its tools are rebuilt at the next message (one prompt-cache break) |
| `/delegation <mode>` for the mode already saved | session switch | writes nothing; points to `--now` |
| `/delegation <mode> --global` | saved for the profile | removed (saving is the default); answers with the usage |
| `/delegation` (surface can ask) | mode picker → session switch | mode picker → second question **Next session (recommended)** / **Now (rebuilds this chat's tools)**; cancelling the second changes nothing |
| `/delegation` (nothing can ask) | text listing | text listing showing both commands |

Why save-for-next-session is the default: the mode is part of the chat's `delegate_task` schema (the per-task `option` / `profile` choice), and that schema is part of the prompt cache.

Screenshots (classic CLI, core branch 96282f40d1), same gist as #136, files 16-18 replaced:
- [16: `/delegation` mode picker](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/9cbb18bc04346b66db6e453ee74db3b98497e74d/16-slash-picker-cli.png)
- [17: the "when" question after picking Model routes](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/8e52a130afe7dbc0bcda53fae151a47f81a629f2/17-slash-switched-then-picker.png)
- [18: Next session reply, then `/delegation profiles --now`](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/3e795cae86d493f8f174bb838d9fc999/raw/ff000bd545eb9f2ead083340396d293c3bef5de1/18-slash-profile-then-global-default.png)

## Older cores

- Core without `apply_now` (hermes-agent `main` today, which CI tests against): `--now` saves for the next session and says applying it needs a newer Hermes. Detected by the keyword's `TypeError`, which an older core raises before writing anything; that also holds across the `plugins.isolation: host` wire (`test_slash_host.py`). Mutation check: removing the `TypeError` fallback fails 3 tests on `main`.
- Core without `ctx.delegation_backends`: the plugin writes `delegation.backend` itself; `--now` answers the same way.

Nothing here shipped in a release, so there is no compat flag for `--global`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_slash.py` rewritten for the new contract: recording stand-ins for the new API and the pre-`apply_now` API; picker + when question, cancel, already-saved, unknown flags (`--global`), refusals.
- `tests/test_slash_core.py` / `tests/test_slash_host.py` rewritten against core's real API and the real plugin host. On a core with `apply_now` they build a real `AIAgent` and run core's turn-start hook (`apply_requested_tool_rebuild`): a plain save leaves this chat's `delegate_task` alone, `--now` gives it the new mode's `option` (also when the plugin runs in the host). On a core without it, `--now` saves and says it needs a newer Hermes.
- Removed the real-discovery test that pinned the session-only switch.

| Core | Result |
|---|---|
| hermes-agent `main` fab9b01c91 | 135 passed, 2 skipped (the apply_now-only cases) |
| `feat/delegation-switch-next-session` 96282f40d1 | 135 passed, 2 skipped (the pre-apply_now cases) |

Run with the venv's editable install re-pointed at each tree (`agent.__file__` checked) and `HERMES_SESSION_KEY` unset.

title: langfuse: let a deployment set trace tags and instance metadata from the environment
body:
## Context

A fleet runs the same image as several gateway instances (one hub, one pod per game) that all trace into one Langfuse project with one key pair. The plugin records the served profile as `metadata.profile` (#74) and reads its keys and base URL from `HERMES_LANGFUSE_*`, but the root trace carries fixed `tags=["hermes", "langfuse"]` and nothing names the instance, so two instances' turns are indistinguishable in the UI and in `queryMetrics` beyond the trace name. `userId` is rightly kept for the end user (#44639), so it is not the answer here.

## Proposal

Two optional environment variables, read through the plugin's existing env helper, no behaviour change when unset:

- `HERMES_LANGFUSE_TAGS`: comma-separated list appended to the default tags, e.g. `role:game,game:classicone`.
- `HERMES_LANGFUSE_METADATA`: comma-separated `key=value` pairs merged into the root trace's metadata and the propagated observation metadata, e.g. `instance=zero-classicone,role=game`.

Documented next to `HERMES_LANGFUSE_SAMPLE_RATE` in the plugin README.

## Why environment and not config

The plugin is env-driven by design (profile-routed turns resolve through the secret scope), and a per-instance value is exactly what a deployment overlay sets: one template, one line per instance, no fork of the config.

title: advanced-delegation: declare requires_hermes >=0.22.5 in plugin.yaml
body:
Hermes 0.22.0–0.22.4 currently installs `advanced-delegation` without complaint, and then the plugin registers nothing. Its `__init__` catches the missing `agent.delegation_provider` module and logs one warning. The delegation seam first shipped in v0.22.5.

The catalog entry's `requires_hermes` can't stop this because it is display-only. The gate Hermes actually enforces reads `requires_hermes` from the plugin's own `plugin.yaml` (`hermes_cli/plugins_manifest.py::requires_hermes_error`; checked at install/enable and again at load since v0.22.0). This plugin's manifest never declared it.

## Change
- `plugin.yaml`: `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.5"` (SemVer, same format as the other plugins in this repo, e.g. `bubblewrap` `>=0.22.2`, `mcp-serve` `>=0.22.0`).
- README compatibility note: says what each core version now does, and drops the incorrect claim that the catalog listing enforces the floor.
- `__init__` docstring: the `ModuleNotFoundError` guard **stays**. Cores older than 0.22.0 ignore the field, so the plugin still needs it there.

No new test. The repo has no manifest-test pattern, and the gate itself belongs to core.

## Verification (real CLI, scratch HOME/HERMES_HOME, core git worktrees at the release tags)
| core | `hermes plugins install file://<this branch>#advanced-delegation --enable --yes` |
|---|---|
| v0.22.4 | `Error: Plugin 'advanced-delegation' requires hermes >=0.22.5, running 0.22.4  Run hermes update to update Hermes.` (exit 1) |
| v0.22.5 | installed + enabled; `plugins list` shows it `enabled` |

- v0.22.4 with a copy already installed and enabled in config: `hermes plugins enable` → `AdmissionRefused: … requires hermes >=0.22.5, running 0.22.4`. Loader: `Plugin 'advanced-delegation' skipped: requires hermes >=0.22.5, running 0.22.4` (not imported).
- `hermes plugins validate advanced-delegation` on core `origin/main`: `Validation passed`; `requires_hermes` check `spec '>=0.22.5' parses`. The private-import warning was already there before this change.
- `v0.22.5` is an ancestor of core `main`, so main checkouts report base_version ≥ 0.22.5 and still load the plugin.

title: fix(directsdk): a tool call cut off at max_tokens returns finish length on the per-call path
body:
fix(directsdk): a tool call cut off at max_tokens returns finish length on the per-call path

55c1b45 drops a tool call whose streamed arguments are not valid JSON at message_stop, so Hermes gets finish length. On the per-call path with the real Claude Code CLI the step still failed: native keeps the unparsable call with an unparsed-input marker and answers it locally with a parse error, which sets a follow-up turn that --max-turns 1 stops. The turn ends as error_max_turns with exit code 1, the capture holds no 	ool_use, so at directsdk.py the  oundary was false and the step raised `RuntimeError: Native request failed: error_max_turns` instead of returning the text it already had.

**Change**

- Treat a turn whose calls were all dropped (^Gdmission.capture.unparsed non-empty) like a turn with calls at the error_max_turns boundary, and in _fast_eligible.
- The answer then reaches Hermes with finish length and no tool calls, exactly as 55c1b45 describes for the relay path.

**How to test**

With Claude Code 2.1.306 and one per-call Client.create step against the synthetic peer (one stream: text, 	ool_use with a single input_json_delta of {"path":, stop_reason: max_tokens, result error_max_turns, exit 1) the issue's failure reproduces on main and not on this branch. The regression tests replicate that flow against the real admission relay, no credentials or network:

- 	est_a_tool_call_cut_at_max_tokens_returns_finish_length: fast path, exit code never read, finish length, text kept, no calls. On main (475774a) it fails with `TimeoutError: Claude request timed out`; on this branch it passes.
- 	est_a_cut_call_at_max_turns_returns_finish_length_after_native_exits: slow path (the native retry is gated, exit code 1 read); finish length with the retry still denied.

The pre-existing negative control (a plain error_max_turns with a clean capture) still raises, and 	est_max_turns_tools_return_without_reading_exit_code (kept calls) is unchanged.

Full plugin suite: 406 passed, 15 failed - the same 15 fail on untouched main in this offline venv (a equests-import family and one timing-sensitive lifecycle test); nothing new fails.

Closes #164.

title: fix(directsdk): a revoked OAuth login serves the turn again after one refresh re-issue
body:
fix(directsdk): a revoked OAuth login serves the turn again after one refresh re-issue

**Summary**

When Anthropic rejects the CLI OAuth token with `401 OAuth access token has been revoked`, the request failed permanently. The admission gate admits exactly one upstream request per call, so Claude Code follow-up attempt - which is where it refreshes the shared login - was denied with `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED`. Every later request failed the same way until the user launched Claude Code interactively, which refreshes the shared login for everyone. Four live incidents in ~3 weeks (#162), reproduced offline against the real relay.

**Change**

`admission.py` admits exactly one extra upstream request when the first attempt was itself rejected with a 401 carrying an `authentication_error` body:

- The gate decision (`Handler.do_POST`) calls `_allows_auth_retry()`: it requires `gate.status == 401`, a parseable error body with `error.type = authentication_error`, and no earlier refresh re-issue (`gate.auth_retry_used`).
- A retried 401, any other status (rate limit, 5xx, stall), and any other body shape stay denied exactly as before, so the single-per-call invariant only bends for the auth-refresh flow.
- The retry carries the refreshed token because native does the refresh itself (its own `.credentials.json`); the relay only stops standing in the way.
- After a second 401 the gate closes again and Hermes receives the real 401 (`ClaudeAPIError(..., 401)`) with the revocation text, exit code and stderr, instead of the confusing packaged admission-denial text from the log in the issue.

**How to test**

`tests/test_directsdk_admission.py` grows three tests against the real loopback relay with a scripted upstream peer and a native that refreshes and re-issues on a 401 (`NATIVE_AUTH_RETRY`), no credentials or network:

- `test_a_revoked_oauth_login_gets_one_refresh_retry_upstream`: 401 then 200 - the turn completes with `finish stop`, `upstream_requests: 1`, `blocked_requests: 0`. Red on main (`475774a`): the retry was denied and the answer became a 401 `ClaudeAPIError`.
- `test_a_second_401_keeps_the_gate_closed`: 401 twice with a third attempt - Hermes sees the real 401, the revocation text, and `native retries denied: 1`. Red on main (the message said `native retries denied: 2` with nothing reaching upstream on the refresh).
- `test_a_401_that_is_not_an_auth_error_stays_denied`: a 401 with an `invalid_request_error` body keeps the old denial; the gated retry never reaches the peer.

Relay-side suites (`test_admission_breakpoint/turn_start/restoration/two_marks`) still pass. Full plugin suite: same 15 environmental failures as untouched main in this offline venv (`requests`-import family and one timing-sensitive lifecycle test); nothing new fails.

Closes #162.

title: xchat: conversation keys never extracted after the account enables X Chat encryption (PIN) on another device — KeyChange signature verification fails
body:
## Summary

After the connected X account enables X Chat encryption on **another device** (the owner opened encrypted DMs in the X app and set its 4-digit PIN / secure key backup), **every inbound message in the self-chat fails to decrypt**, and the adapter never recovers on its own:

```
[xchat] decrypt failed conv=<uid>-<uid> event=…: Crypto error: Decryption failed: Message encrypted
with key version '1792769076171' but no matching key found. Available versions: [].
Call extract_conversation_keys() first.
```

The root failure is one level deeper — `KeyChange` signature verification:

```
Crypto error: Signature verification failed: KeyChange signature could not be verified:
signature missing or no matching signing key
```

`hermes xchat status` still reports everything green, and the adapter connects + polls normally, so the failure is silent.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.4 (2026.9.24), macOS 26.6.2 (darwin-arm64), Python 3.14.7
- `xchat` v0.1.0 @ `f98c0999`, `chatxdk` 0.4.1 (import name `chat_xdk`, abi3 wheel)
- Configured with `hermes plugins install xchat` → `hermes xchat setup` (OAuth2 user token with `dm.read dm.write users.read tweet.read offline.access`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `hermes xchat setup` — keypair generated, public key registered, `hermes xchat status` all green, adapter connects and polls.
2. Send a message from the account into its own self-chat ("message yourself").
3. **Enable X Chat encryption on the account's phone** (X app asks for a 4-digit PIN the first time encrypted DMs are opened; this registers a second identity and rotates the conversation key).
4. Send another message from the phone into the self-chat.
5. → `decrypt failed … no matching key found. Available versions: []`

## Diagnosis

`GET /2/users/{id}/public_keys` returns **two** versions, and the adapter does pull both:

| version | origin |
| --- | --- |
| `1792763866684` | registered by `hermes xchat setup` |
| `1792769069657` | created by the phone when encryption was enabled |

Both carry a valid `signing_public_key` and `identity_public_key_signature`.

The `KeyChange` event is delivered in `meta.conversation_key_events`, and the public key **embedded inside the event matches the phone version's `signing_public_key`** — yet verification still fails.

Everything tried, all yielding the identical `signature missing or no matching signing key`:

| attempt | result |
| --- | --- |
| `set_signing_keys(roster)` + `decrypt_events(events, None)` (the adapter's current path) | fails |
| `decrypt_events(events, roster)` — signing keys passed inline | fails |
| mapping `public_key <- signing_public_key`, `identity_public_key <- public_key` (current adapter mapping) | fails |
| mapping `public_key <- public_key`, `identity_public_key <- signing_public_key` | fails |
| alias roster entries for the two version numbers found inside the event (`1792769076591`, `1792769076171`) | fails |
| roster containing only the phone version | fails |
| `Chat.extract_conversation_keys([key_event])` called directly | returns `{"keys": {}, "latest_version": None}`, no exception |

Decoding the 897-byte KeyChange event reveals these tokens: the conversation id (`<uid>-<uid>`), `1792769076591`, `1792769076171` (the conversation-key version the messages are encrypted with), `1792769069657` (the phone's public-key version), and the phone's `signing_public_key`.

**Note:** `1792769076591` appears inside the event but is **never returned by `GET /2/users/{id}/public_keys`** (only the two versions above), so a caller has no way to supply a matching key for it. If the event is signed by that version, verification cannot succeed by construction.

## Impact

The adapter receives events but can never decrypt them: after the account owner touches their phone, the integration is permanently one-way (inbound events arrive, nothing can be read, nothing can be answered). Because `status`/connect/poll all look healthy, this is hard to notice.

## Three additional issues found while diagnosing

**1. `_register_signing_keys()` dedupes by user id only** — `adapter.py:816`:

```python
senders -= self._known_senders
```

A sender whose keys were fetched once is never re-fetched, but X Chat explicitly lets the same user rotate to a new `public_key_version` (new device, PIN setup, key reset) — see the "so your other devices can read it too" wrapping in the X cryptography primer. The new version's public key therefore never enters the roster. Keying the cache by `(user_id, public_key_version)`, or forcing a re-fetch of the bot's own account when a `KeyChange` arrives, would fix it.

**2. A failed decrypt still advances the cursor** — `adapter.py:595`:

```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning("[xchat] decrypt failed conv=%s event=%s: %s", conv_id, event_id, e)
    self._set_cursor(conv_id, event_id)
    continue
```

A message that fails to decrypt is permanently skipped and is never retried once the key situation is repaired.

**3. `hermes send` is unusable in the self-chat** (separate, but it blocks the documented "message yourself" flow):

```
$ hermes send -t xchat:<own_user_id> "…"
conversation-key handshake failed: Parse error: cannot derive a one-to-one conversation id from
1 distinct user(s); pass conversation_id explicitly for group conversations

$ hermes send -t xchat:<uid>-<uid> "…"
no verified conversation key — the target must have an existing conversation with the bot,
or pass the recipient's bare user id to start a new one
```

In a self-chat the participant set is a single user, so the bare-user-id path cannot derive `<uid>-<uid>`; and the explicit conversation-id path requires a verified conversation key, which (per the bug above) cannot be extracted. Together these make outbound delivery impossible in exactly the configuration the README documents as working "out of the box".

## Questions

1. Should a `CustomPin`-registered identity (what `hermes xchat setup` creates) be able to verify `KeyChange` signatures produced by a Juicebox / secure-key-backup identity on the same account? Is the `KeyChange` signer's public key required to be exposed via `GET /2/users/{id}/public_keys`?
2. Is `1792769076591` a public-key version that should have been returned by that endpoint (registration lag / read cache), or a different kind of version?
3. Is there a supported way for a bot identity to take part in a conversation-key rotation it did not itself initiate?

Happy to run any additional probe against the live account and report back.

title: bubblewrap: hide the dot entries of HOME by default, credential stores always
body:
HOME hardening for the bubblewrap backend: the dot entries of the home directory are hidden by default, and credential stores are hidden always, so what the sandbox shows matches what its note tells the model ("credential paths ... hidden").

Most of this comes from #138 by @TacoTakumi (their port of the hermes-agent#102875 work): the HOME policy module and its tests are their commit unchanged, and the test-setup commit is theirs too. This PR takes only the HOME part. The rest of #138 (per-environment scratch, the staged-data bind-back, the process-limit change, the `hide` setting, the dot-symlink and absent-path guards) stays on #138.

## What changes

- **HOME is default-deny for dot entries.** A tmpfs goes over HOME. The non-dot entries come back as they were, the allowed dot entries come back read-only, and nothing new can be made at the top of HOME. `.config`, `.local` and `.local/share` follow the same rule one level down.
- **The allowlist** is the shipped list (shell startup files, `.gitconfig`, `.cache`, the common toolchain directories), the PATH directories under HOME, and a new `home_allow` setting. It is fixed when the environment is built.
- **Credential stores stay hidden whatever the allowlist says.** The deny list is the module list plus the HOME paths the file safety policy refuses, read through its own functions. Below an allowed entry a store shows as an empty file (`~/.cargo/credentials.toml`). On top of #138's list, this adds token files under allowed toolchain directories: `.gem/credentials`, `.m2/settings-security.xml`, `.config/npm/npmrc`, `.config/pnpm/rc`, `.local/share/uv/credentials`, `.pub-cache/credentials.json`, and `.cache/huggingface/stored_tokens` (which `hf auth login` writes beside `token`).
- **HERMES_HOME is unchanged.** It stays hidden. Only the state dir, the scratch dir and (under `home_mode: profile`) the profile home are bound back. The staged-data directories (attachments, cached documents, images, pastes) stay hidden, so the files one session stages do not show in another session's sandbox.
- **Allowed dot symlinks stay symlinks.** A dotfiles repository in a dot directory (`~/.gitconfig` → `~/.dotfiles/…`) or a CA bundle in one (`SSL_CERT_FILE=~/.certs/…`) needs that directory in `home_allow`. The directory then shows read-only, and the credential stores below it stay hidden. The README documents this, and a test covers it. Binding such targets back automatically was tried and dropped in review: another session with a writable cwd there could swap the target before the next spawn.
- The sandbox note now says that dot entries off the allowlist do not exist. `plugin.yaml` gets the `home_allow` schema. The version goes 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, and `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.22.2`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_bubblewrap_home_sandbox.py` (new; real bwrap, fake HOME with dummy files):
  - credential stores in HOME are not readable: **fails on main** (`.pgpass`, `.config/gh/hosts.yml` and 16 more of the 23 probed paths are readable), passes here
  - dot entries off the allowlist do not exist: fails on main, passes here
  - `home_allow` shows an extra entry but never a credential store: fails on main, passes here
  - the entries a command needs stay readable (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, `.cargo/config.toml`, `.config/git/*`): passes on both
  - files another session staged under HERMES_HOME are not visible: passes on main and here, **fails on #138's head** (11 staged roots visible)
  - a dotfiles dir named in `home_allow` shows read-only, and the credential file below it stays hidden
- `tests/test_bubblewrap_home.py` comes from #138 unchanged (the pure policy module, 69 tests). The args, environment and secrets suites carry #138's HOME-layout cases. The scratch, staged-data and `hide` cases stay with #138.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite vs hermes-agent main (b4271db9), bwrap 0.11.1, Linux 7.0 | 488 passed, 1 skipped |
| Plugin suite vs v0.22.2 (the `requires_hermes` floor) | 488 passed, 1 skipped |
| tests.yml (ubuntu / macOS / Windows) | green. GitHub's runner has no usable bwrap, so the integration cases skip there; the live run is local |
| `hermes plugins validate` (main and v0.22.2) | passed (same private-import notes as before, plus `agent.file_safety` from home.py) |
| `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin` | safe |

## Live check (real `bwrap`, fake HOME with dummy files, `BubblewrapEnvironment.execute("cat …")`)

| Path | main | #138 head | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.pgpass` | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.config/gh/hosts.yml` | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.git-credentials`, `.config/hub`, `.config/rclone/…`, `.config/op/…`, `.config/doctl/…` | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.cargo/credentials.toml`, `.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json`, `.cache/huggingface/token` | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.local/share/keyrings/…`, `.mozilla/…/logins.json`, `.config/google-chrome/…/Cookies` | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.vault-token`, `.my.cnf`, an unlisted `.zz-*` dot file | readable | hidden | hidden |
| `.gem/credentials`, `.cache/huggingface/stored_tokens` | readable | readable | hidden |
| `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.docker`, `.kube`, `.netrc`, `.hermes/.env`, `.hermes/auth.json` | hidden | hidden | hidden |
| `.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, a non-dot file | readable | readable | readable |
| another session's file in each staged root (`cache/documents`, `images`, `attachments`, `composer-pastes`, …, 11 roots) | hidden | **visible** | hidden |

## Review

An independent review ran adversarial cases against real bwrap:
- symlinked HOME, and dot entries linked to hidden or denied places
- PATH entries under denied paths
- odd `home_allow` items (`.config`, `../x`, absolute paths, `.config/gh/../op`)
- cwd at HOME, at its parent and inside an allowed dot dir
- read-only and read-write binds of HOME and `~/.config`
- `home_mode: profile`, HERMES_HOME inside and outside HOME, the restricted profile

What held: the credential stores and the unlisted dot entries stayed hidden in every case. The top of HOME and the dot entries stayed read-only, so nothing was created on the host.

Its findings:
- A missing `hf` `stored_tokens` entry: fixed.
- Dotfiles links and CA bundles inside hidden dot dirs: documented with the `home_allow` fix (see above).
- Known limit: a HOME with about 3000 or more non-dot entries at its top level goes over bwrap's 9000-argument cap. The sandbox then fails to start; it fails closed and exposes nothing.
