title: fix(directsdk): answer native's session-title side request locally before the admission gate
body:
fix(directsdk): answer native's session-title side request locally before the admission gate

**Summary**

On a fresh conversation the user-facing reply is sometimes replaced by a session-title JSON object such as `{"title": "Greek language response assistance"}`. Claude Code sends its own session-title side request next to the first turn (the 2.1.284 bundle: `generateSessionTitle`, `outputFormat: json_schema {title}`); the relay admits exactly one upstream request per call, so whichever request arrived first kept the admission. When the title won, the relay treated its tiny title response as the turn's assistant message and denied the real turn. The reporter saw it on Telegram; `/new` does not avoid it because the first turn of every session carries the race.

**Change**

- `admission.py::is_title_request()` recognises exactly that shape: no `tools`, `output_config.format.type == "json_schema"`, and the schema properties are exactly `{title}`.
- `Handler.do_POST` reads the body before touching the gate and answers a recognised title request with 400 (`HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_TITLE`) without setting `gate.used`; native catches the error and returns no title. The real turn keeps its admission.
- A body read failure now answers 400 instead of landing inside the forwarding `try`; `Content-Length` is optional.

This is the reporter's verified local workaround adopted into the relay; it refuses the request rather than switching it off at native, which keeps native's normal behaviour when no title is produced.

**How to test**

- `test_is_title_request_recognises_only_the_side_request_shape`: positive shape plus four negatives (tools present, non-json body, extra schema properties, text format).
- `test_a_title_request_never_takes_the_turn_admission`: end-to-end through the real relay with a native that sends a title request first and a peer that answers title-shaped requests with `{"title": "Greek"}`. On main (`475774a`) the title request is admitted (immediately visible: its status becomes 200 and two upstream requests happen, so the reply is the title object); on this branch the title gets 400, exactly one upstream request happens, the answer is the turn's text and `blocked_requests` is 0.
- Relay-side suites: 122 passed. Full plugin suite: 420 passed, 15 skipped, 1 failure - the timing-sensitive `test_blocked_stdin_has_deadline_and_cancellation[True]` that also fails on untouched main on this machine (CI covers it).

Closes #39.

title: docs(directsdk): note the post-tool-result streaming cadence and whose job pacing is
body:
docs(directsdk): note the post-tool-result streaming cadence and whose job pacing is

The measured finding in #33 is that text after a tool result reaches the relay late and in one burst from upstream (all deltas in a single read at ~6 s), while the same turn without tool history spreads evenly, and the relay/provider forward every delta as it arrives. Nothing in the plugin is buffering.

This adds one paragraph to the transport section so clients (Hermes WebUI, native apps) know to pace display themselves and future reports do not get chased as a plugin stall. Refs #33.

title: fix(homeassistant): enforce complete service-policy checks
body:
## Summary
- Validate the entire domain and service identifier before checking the blocked-domain list or dispatching. A terminal line feed no longer passes the `$`-anchored pattern through `match()`.
- Include the service-selected `script.<name>` in the entity-policy checks for every custom script service call, even when the payload also names other entities. Keep the existing built-in script-service exceptions and unfiltered behavior.

## Tests
- New synthetic regression cases on the unmodified base: **14 failed, 19 passed**, covering terminal line feeds and omitted custom-script targets.
- Full Home Assistant plugin suite after the fix: **168 passed, 2 skipped** on Linux with Python 3.12. The skips cover macOS-only diagnostics and compatibility with a core-bundled Home Assistant module that is no longer present.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate homeassistant`: passed, with the existing `gateway.restart` private-import warning.
- `ruff check --no-cache homeassistant/tools.py homeassistant/tests/test_service_policy.py`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The tests use synthetic policies and mocked service dispatch. No Home Assistant instance was contacted, and these results establish local pre-dispatch enforcement rather than provider-side execution semantics. The offline test environment used the Python fallbacks of the HTTP dependencies.

## Delivery
This changes the standalone plugin only. After merge, a catalog-pin update and a subsequent plugin update are still needed to distribute the fix.

title: bubblewrap: sandbox hardening: validated binds and per-session scratch
body:
Sandbox hardening for the bubblewrap backend: validated binds and per-session scratch. Follow-up to #174.

## What changes

**Validated binds.** Every bind whose host path comes from configuration or the environment goes through one helper, `binds.bind_refusal`, once when the environment is built:

- the CA bundle variables (`SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`, `HERMES_CA_BUNDLE`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `GIT_SSL_CAINFO`, `PIP_CERT`)
- the Hermes scratch directory (from `HERMES_HOME`)
- the profile home (`HERMES_HOME/home` under `terminal.home_mode: profile`)
- the `binds` setting's sources

The helper resolves the path once. It refuses a path that is missing, and for the CA bundles and the scratch dir one that is not a regular file (or a directory where one is expected); a `binds` source may be any existing path, sockets, FIFOs and device nodes included. It refuses a path that lies in a directory any sandbox of this profile can write to: the working directory (this environment's, the configured `terminal.cwd`, and those of the other sandboxes the process built), read-write binds, the profile home, the shared scratch dir, or the sandbox dir. A `binds` source bound at its own path directly under one of those is still accepted, since it is a mount point. For the CA bundles, the scratch dir and the profile home, it also refuses a path that resolves into a credential store, into a hidden dot entry of HOME (#174), or into the Hermes home. Inside the Hermes home, only the Python environment Hermes runs from (where certifi's bundle lives) and the plain profile home are allowed.

The argv uses the resolved path, never the name as written. A refused read-only `binds` entry or profile home stops the environment build with a configuration error naming it, as the existing read-write bind, cwd and sandbox-dir checks do. Any other refused path is skipped with one warning and the sandbox still runs. Unset or missing CA variables change nothing and log nothing.

**Per-session scratch.** `HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch` was bound read-write into every sandbox, so one session's scratch files were visible to every other session's sandbox. Now each sandbox gets its own directory, `hermes-bwrap-session-<digest>` inside the shared scratch dir on the host, mounted at `HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch` itself. That is the path Hermes names in its system prompt and points `TMPDIR`, `TMP` and `TEMP` at, so writes there keep working and land in the session's own directory. It is writable with the working directory and read-only under `restricted`.

- The name comes from the terminal session and the Hermes process. When Hermes rebuilds a session's environment after the 300 s idle timeout, the new sandbox finds its earlier files. Another session, or another CLI process (they all use the task id `default`), gets its own directory.
- Hermes' 24 h scratch pruning removes it once it is unused, and each spawn refreshes it.
- Staged files stay hidden per session, as #174 set up.

The scratch design comes from #138 by @TacoTakumi: a private dir per sandbox, the `TMPDIR` handling and the refresh against pruning. #138 carries it in one commit together with the staged-data bind-back, which would share staged files across sessions, so a cherry-pick would have brought that in too. This PR ports only the scratch part, credited with `Co-authored-by`. The session-keyed name (so the directory survives the idle rebuild) is new here.

**Sandbox dir.** When `terminal.sandbox_dir` lies outside the hidden set, each sandbox now sees only its own state dir there (a read-only tmpfs with that one entry), not the shell snapshots and `execute_code` files of other environments. Such a sandbox dir must not hold the working directory, HOME or a bind destination, or the build stops with an error. The default `HERMES_HOME/sandboxes` was already hidden.

**Other changes.** The sandbox note tells the model the scratch directory (`$TMPDIR`) is the sandbox's own. The README documents the bind rules, the scratch layout and the sandbox dir. A CA bundle kept in the Hermes home, outside its venv, has to move (the README suggests `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates`). One kept in a dot directory needs that directory in `home_allow`. The version goes from 1.1.0 to 1.2.0, and `requires_hermes` is unchanged.

## Changes since 6f7b630 (review follow-up, commit a08c936)

| # | Change | Test (fails on 6f7b630, passes now) |
|---|---|---|
| F2 | `binds` entries may name unix sockets, FIFOs and device nodes again, as on main; the file/dir rule covers the CA bundles and the scratch dir only | `test_binds_may_name_a_unix_socket_and_a_fifo` (6f7b630: connection refused, socket not bound) |
| F3 | A read-only `binds` entry the validator refuses stops the build with a `ValueError` naming the entry, instead of being skipped (which left a "protect this path" bind writable) | `test_read_only_bind_deep_in_the_writable_directory_is_not_left_writable` (6f7b630: no error, file writable) |
| F4 | The session's scratch dir is mounted AT `HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch` instead of an empty read-only view, so the prompt-named path and `$TMPDIR` are the same writable, private place; `restricted` stays read-only | `test_a_sandbox_writes_to_the_scratch_path_hermes_names` ×2 (6f7b630: EROFS) |
| F1 | The profile home is resolved once at construction, goes through the same bind rules (a link into a directory a sandbox can write to is refused), and every spawn binds the resolved directory | `test_profile_home_linked_into_the_writable_directory_is_refused` (6f7b630: dummy `~/.ssh` key readable after a swap), `test_profile_home_is_bound_from_the_directory_it_resolved_to` (6f7b630: follows a re-pointed link) |
| F5 | The writable set the checks use covers every sandbox of the profile: the configured `terminal.cwd` and the writable dirs of every sandbox the process built (per Hermes home), plus the sandbox and scratch roots | `test_a_bind_another_sandbox_of_the_profile_can_swap_is_refused` (6f7b630: dummy hidden dot-entry token readable through sandbox B after A swaps the source) |
| F6 | A sandbox dir outside the hidden set is a read-only tmpfs inside each sandbox with only that environment's state dir bound back | `test_a_sandbox_sees_only_its_own_state_under_the_sandbox_dir` ×2 (6f7b630: lists and reads other environments' snapshots) |
| F8 | README: the private dir name (`hermes-bwrap-session-<digest>`), what "session" means (CLI, cron and subagents share their parent's), operator binds may be sockets/FIFOs; the empty-view directory and its 0700 nit are gone with F4 | — |
| F7 | Unchanged and documented: a CA bundle in the Hermes home outside its venv is not bound | — |

Adjusted existing tests: the read-only bind steering test now expects the build to stop; the "ro form constructs" case keeps the at-its-own-path form and expects an error for the other; the scratch tests follow the new mount (other sessions' files invisible, writes to the shared path land in the session's dir); the Hermes-home listing test and the profile-home argv test follow the new mounts; the builder signature test lists `profile_home` and `sandbox_root`.

## Tests

The real-bwrap files use a fake HOME that holds dummy placeholder files and, like the existing real-bwrap files, skip where bwrap cannot run:

- `tests/test_bubblewrap_host_binds.py`
- `tests/test_bubblewrap_scratch.py`

The scratch tests run twice: once with the Hermes home under HOME and once with it elsewhere. The new tests above were run against the 6f7b630 plugin code: 12 failed, each for the reason listed; all pass on a08c936.

## Normal use on a08c936

Real bwrap 0.11.1, `network` profile, fake HOME and HERMES_HOME with dummy secrets, `TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`/`HERMES_SCRATCH_DIR` exported the way Hermes does at boot, environment made through the provider:

| Command in the sandbox | Result |
|---|---|
| `git init`, `git add`, `git commit` in the cwd | ok (1 commit) |
| `curl https://github.com` | 200 |
| Python `urllib` https (`pypi.org`) | 200 |
| write `HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch/probe.py` (the prompt-named path), run it | ok (`42`) |
| write and read `$TMPDIR/note` | ok, `TMPDIR` = `HERMES_HOME/cache/scratch` |
| `mktemp`, `python3 -c 'tempfile.mkdtemp()'` | ok, under the scratch path |
| `cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 HERMES_HOME/.env` | hidden |
| On the host afterwards | the files are in `cache/scratch/hermes-bwrap-session-…`; nothing landed in the shared dir |

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite vs hermes-agent main (`e04614a`), bwrap 0.11.1 | 513 passed, 1 skipped (6f7b630: 506 passed, 1 skipped) |
| Plugin suite vs v0.22.2 (the `requires_hermes` floor) | 513 passed, 1 skipped |
| `ruff check --select F,E9 bubblewrap` | clean |
| tests.yml (ubuntu / macOS / Windows) | see checks. GitHub's runner has no usable bwrap, so the integration cases skip there; the live runs are local |

title: bubblewrap: say exactly where the file tools run (1.2.1)
body:
The bubblewrap prompt note and README said the file tools run on the host. That is true by default, but it was not the whole picture: the note did not say what follows from it, and it was wrong when Hermes runs with `HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ=0`.

## What is true (hermes-agent main 2647748a8b)

`tools/file_tools.py:372` wraps the backend in `ShellFileOperations(terminal_env)`, and `_exec` (`tools/file_operations.py:239`) runs commands through `env.execute`, which on this backend is the bwrap sandbox. But every file tool first checks `_native_read_enabled()` (`tools/file_operations.py:912`). That check is `sys.platform != "win32" and isinstance(env, LocalEnvironment)` (`tools/file_operations_lint.py:255`), and `BubblewrapEnvironment` subclasses `LocalEnvironment`. So by default:

| Tool | Host fast path | Live result (default) | Live result (`HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ=0`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read_file` | `_read_file_native` (`file_operations.py:834`, `:928`), in-process `open()` | read the hidden `~/.zz-dummy/secret.txt` and a read-only path outside the cwd | hidden: `File not found`; outside: read (visible read-only) |
| `write_file` | `_native_io.atomic_write` (`file_operations.py:583`, `file_operations_native.py`) | wrote into the hidden dot dir and outside the writable set | `Read-only file system` for both |
| `patch` | `_read_exact_bytes` native read (`:350`) + the native write above | patched both dummies | hidden: `Failed to read file`; outside: `Read-only file system` |
| `search_files` | `_path_exists_probe` (`file_operations_search.py:519`), `_run_rg_native` (`:424`, `subprocess.Popen` on the host) | listed and matched the hidden files | hidden: `Path not found`; outside: matched (read-only is still readable) |

Meanwhile `terminal` in the same session got `No such file or directory` for the hidden file and `Read-only file system` outside the cwd. `search_files` falls back to `find`/`grep` without ripgrep, and that fallback and a few helper probes go through the sandbox. Hermes' write denylist still applies on the native path: `write_file` to `~/.ssh/...` is refused. `read_file` on a dummy `~/.ssh` file and on the scratch `HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` succeeds.

Another gap the old note did not mention: the sandbox mounts its own private scratch dir at the `$TMPDIR` path. Live, a file a command wrote to `$TMPDIR` was `File not found` for `read_file`, and a file `write_file` put at `$TMPDIR` was missing for `cat` in the sandbox.

Run: scratch `HERMES_HOME` with this plugin installed via `hermes plugins install NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins#bubblewrap` (main 35d24e4), `terminal.backend: bubblewrap`, a fake `HOME` with dummy dot-dir files, tools driven through `model_tools.handle_function_call`, bwrap 0.11.1.

## Change

- Prompt note: names the default case (the file tools run in the Hermes process on the host and can reach paths that are hidden or read-only for commands) and the `$TMPDIR` split (hand files over through the working directory). With `HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ` off it says they run through the sandbox, using the same parse as core.
- README: a per-tool table of what runs on the host, the denylist that still applies, the `$TMPDIR` split, and the core switch.
- Root README card: names the four tools.
- Tests: a provider test for both note variants (fails on main), plus a live bwrap integration test, parametrized on the switch, that pins the claim (`write_file` outside the writable set succeeds natively and is refused through the sandbox). It runs locally only; CI has no usable bwrap. The integration fixture now also clears the file tools' cache, as core's own cleanup does. Without that, a shell-path file op reused a previous test's dead sandbox.
- Version 1.2.0 → 1.2.1 in `plugin.yaml`. `pyproject.toml` goes from 1.1.0 to 1.2.1 because #179 left it behind.

Local: `516 passed, 1 skipped` (real bwrap, `env -i`, TMPDIR outside `~/.hermes`); `hermes plugins validate bubblewrap` passes.

Core follow-up (not in this PR): the native fast path is gated on `isinstance(env, LocalEnvironment)` (`tools/file_operations_lint.py:255`, used by `tools/file_operations.py:912`, plus the `isinstance` checks in `tools/file_operations_search.py:66,300,435,661`). A sandboxing subclass cannot opt out without the process-wide env switch.

title: ElevenLabs Sound Effects: generate sound effects from a text description (new official plugin)
body:
Adds **ElevenLabs Sound Effects** (v1.2.0) as an official plugin. It has one tool, `elevenlabs_sound_effect`, which turns a text description into an audio file through the [ElevenLabs Sound Effects API](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/capabilities/sound-effects). It also bundles a sound-design skill with a local post-processing script. In Hermes Desktop, each generated sound shows up as an inline **sound card**, and there is a **sound library** tab.

[![Demo: ElevenLabs Sound Effects in Hermes Desktop (1:42, sound on)](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/11c3fd6f2c9901a337fe5141d030cd11/raw/poster.jpg)](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/11c3fd6f2c9901a337fe5141d030cd11/raw/elevenlabs-sound-effects-demo-1440p60.mp4)

**Demo video, with sound:** [elevenlabs-sound-effects-demo-1440p60.mp4](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/11c3fd6f2c9901a337fe5141d030cd11/raw/elevenlabs-sound-effects-demo-1440p60.mp4) (1:42, 2560×1440, 60 fps, AAC). It was recorded live in Hermes Desktop built from `main` (3403b92c4b6), with Claude Sonnet 4.6 driving real ElevenLabs generations, so every sound you hear is real. The audio was captured from the app's own output, and every stretch where a sound plays runs at 1.0× speed. Only the waits are sped up, and those carry a badge. It shows an impact, a 6 s rain loop with gapless loop audition, a 0.5 s UI click, **Next → 3 variations** landing in the same chat and the sound library. The app is framed on a dark backdrop with each caption in the band below it, so no caption covers the UI being shown, and a caption only appears once the thing it describes is on screen.

## What it does

**Tool (agent half)**
- `elevenlabs_sound_effect(prompt, duration_seconds?, loop?, prompt_influence?, model?)` calls `POST /v1/sound-generation` with the profile's `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`. That is the same key core's ElevenLabs voice uses. It is read per call through `agent.secret_scope`, so a multiplexed gateway serves each profile its own key.
- The file is saved to `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/generated/audio/sfx_<slug>_<timestamp>_<id>.<ext>` and never overwrites an earlier one.
- The result **always** carries the plain `MEDIA:` line, which every surface plays. It also carries:
  - the billed amount and a `sound_id`;
  - the **real length** of the returned audio (`length_seconds`, read from the bytes), next to `requested_duration_seconds`;
  - a `length_note` when the two differ. Loops come back longer than asked (1 s → 1.5 s), and billing follows the request.
- Settings live in `config_schema`: `sound_model` (v2 or v3), `output_format` (mp3, opus or wav variants), `api_base_url` (data-residency endpoints), plus the key as a `secret` row. They are read per call. In Desktop they are under Capabilities → Plugins → gear; elsewhere, use `hermes config set plugins.entries.elevenlabs-sound-effects.settings.<key>`.
- Anything that would waste a billed call is refused before the request goes out:
  - an empty prompt, or one over 450 characters;
  - an out-of-range `duration_seconds` or `prompt_influence`;
  - a length written into the prompt without `duration_seconds`;
  - a setting outside its declared choices.
- Unanswered calls are not retried blindly. Vendor errors come back as readable tool errors that never echo the key.
- Downloads are streamed under a 50 MB cap with a 180 s overall deadline. The tool is deferred (found through `tool_search`). The only dependency is `httpx`.
- Billing measured on the real API: about 10 credits per second when `duration_seconds` is set, and a flat ~50 when it is not. This round's turns billed 2.5 s → 25, 6 s → 60, 0.5 s → 5, 1 s → 10.

**Skill + script (`skills/elevenlabs-sound-design/`)**
- Covers prompt writing (from ElevenLabs' guide), loops and how to verify them, picking a format by destination, and the sound-pack workflow.
- Delivery is one rule for every surface: put the sound's `media_tag` on its own line. Converted or processed files go on extra lines after the original, never instead of it.
- `scripts/sfx_tool.py` (stdlib + ffmpeg) provides `probe`, `process`, `loopfix`, `loopcheck` and `pack`. Every run prints one JSON line, on success and on every failure.

**Desktop half (inside `@hermes/plugin-sdk`, opt-in)**
- **Sound card through Desktop's tool-media renderer seam** (hermes-agent `567569267a`, `TOOL_MEDIA_RENDERER_AREA`).
  - Desktop maps a reply's `MEDIA:` path to the tool call that produced it. For `elevenlabs_sound_effect` it lets this plugin draw the card instead of the built-in player. Desktop only accepts the claim because this package registered that tool.
  - The card shows: the prompt; length (with the requested length when ElevenLabs returned a different one); loop, model, format and billed-credits chips; a clickable waveform with playhead; Play; a playback clock; a gapless **Loop** audition; **Download** (original, or MP3/WAV/OGG converted by the plugin backend); **Reveal**; **Library**; and **Next**.
- **Built-in player whenever the card can't play the sound:**
  - a failed call, or a file that isn't one of this tool's sounds;
  - a record the active profile doesn't have;
  - a file the backend refuses to serve (for example, hard-linked by a backup tool);
  - an audio load that fails.
- **Older Desktops** (no `TOOL_MEDIA_RENDERER_AREA`) load the plugin and play every sound in the built-in player. The area is feature-detected through a namespace import, because a named import of a missing export would fail to load.
- `::elevenlabs-sfx{id=…}` directive cards from pre-seam chats still render. Nothing emits that line any more.
- **Next** offers 3 variations, shorter, longer, make it loop, and try the other model.
  - Each row's cost is worked out from this sound's own bill.
  - Each row sends a chat message to the card's own chat (`composer.submit(sessionId, …)`). The message names the tool and uses only arguments the schema accepts, and it asks the agent to reply with the result's `media_tag`.
- **Sound library** (⌘K → "ElevenLabs: open sound library", or the card's Library button) lists every generation in the active profile from the per-generation provenance record. It has:
  - per-format totals, a format filter and search;
  - waveforms for the newest rows;
  - play, Reuse prompt, Open chat, Download and Reveal on each row.

  It is event-driven, with no polling.
- **Remote Hermes:** audio and downloads stream through the plugin's backend route, never a local path. Reveal is replaced by a note naming the host when the backend is remote.
- No account-wide ElevenLabs UI (balance or usage), by design.

## Screenshots

These are from real Hermes Desktop built from `main` (3403b92c4b6) over CDP, with real ElevenLabs sounds and the plugin installed the user way.

## Game sound sets (c7b7dc3)

These additions are for game audio. ElevenLabs' `/v1/sound-generation` has no seed, batch or channel option ([API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-sound-effects/convert)), so the additions are local to the skill's script, and each take is still one call.

- **`process --mono`** downmixes to one channel *before* trimming and levelling, so the loudness is set and measured on the mono file that ships. Positional sounds (footsteps, hits, doors) are point sources an engine attenuates and pans.
- **`pack --variations`** treats the files as takes of one sound:
  - names them `name_01`, `name_02`... (one base name, numbered, the way engine random containers expect takes);
  - records each take's `integrated_lufs`;
  - reports `variation_set` and `loudness_spread_lu`, plus a `loudness_note` when the spread is over 1 LU, since takes at different loudness stand out when the engine picks at random.
- **Skill:**
  - a "Game sound sets" recipe: same prompt, prompt influence 0.2-0.3, level and downmix each take, `--variations`, then the engine's random picker (Unreal Sound Cue Random node or MetaSound, Unity 6 Audio Random Container, Godot 4 `AudioStreamRandomizer`; Unreal's Sound Wave Looping flag for loops);
  - a mono-vs-stereo column in the format-by-destination table;
  - a note that restricted keys need the **Sound Effects** permission.

  The README mirrors the flags and the permission.

**Verified with real ffmpeg (no credits spent):**
- A 2-channel clip through `process --mono --trim --loudness -18` came out with `channels: 1` at -18.0 LUFS.
- Three takes 20 dB apart, packed with `--variations`, gave `footstep_gravel_01..03.wav`, `loudness_spread_lu: 20.2` and the note.
- Each take levelled to -18 LUFS, then re-packed: spread 0.0 and no note. `manifest.json` carries the same fields.

**Tests:** two new script tests (mono downmix holds the loudness target; variation naming, spread and note, then the levelled re-pack). Plugin suite: 48 passed (pytest) and 18 passed (`npm test`).

## This round: rework onto the tool-media renderer seam (933c882 → 021c2c6)

- **Seam instead of handshake** (933c882). The tool always returns `MEDIA:`. The Desktop half registers the renderer for its own tool. **Deleted:** `desktop_card`, `POST`/`DELETE /card-ready`, the `tool.start` sighting listener, the sightings file with its lock and owner tokens, the `session_surface` gate, and the skill's "use desktop_card" step. The commit adds 301 lines and removes 614.
- **Theme bug found live** (2980a3a). The card and the library rows styled themselves with `var(--color-border)`, `--color-card`, `--color-ring` and `--color-destructive`. Desktop compiles those Tailwind tokens inline (`@theme inline`), so they don't exist as CSS variables. On `main` the card had no border or background, and the waveform's played colour was unset. Everything now uses the documented `--ui-*` plugin variables, and a test fails on any other variable.
- **Polish** (2980a3a):
  - card: framed, filled Play as the primary action, playback clock, playhead, peaks scaled to the loudest bucket, readable chips, actions grouped on the right, labelled Library button;
  - library: centred column, waveforms on the newest rows, date beside the prompt.
- **Review fixes** (6655b1f, fb05e05, 7a88cd5):
  - The card hands the sound back to the built-in player instead of showing a dead Play button.
  - `/audio` says *why* a file isn't served: another hard link, or replaced by a symbolic link.
  - Versions agree everywhere.
  - Handshake-era tombstone tests are gone.
  - Removed the `file.resolveUrl()` fetch path, which failed live (Desktop's `hermes-media:` scheme refuses `fetch`).
- **Skill** (c9ca52d). Recording the demo found the model delivering only a converted OGG, which hid the card. The skill now always delivers the original sound's `media_tag` first.
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.0"` is unchanged, so the plugin installs and plays sounds on every release from 0.22.0. The card itself needs a Desktop with tool-media renderers: `567569267a` is on `main` and no stable tag yet (only `v0.22.5+canary.*`), so it ships in the next release after v0.22.5. The README says so.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin pytest (real `PluginManager` discovery and registry dispatch, the plugin backend over FastAPI, provenance per profile, returned-length parsing incl. fuzz, https rule, symlink/hard-link refusals with their reasons, script subprocess contract) on a fresh `git archive` of core `main` 3403b92c4b6 and on `v0.22.0` | 46 passed on each |
| Node tests: real `src/plugin.tsx` bundled against a stub SDK **with and without** the seam (renderer claims exactly `elevenlabs_sound_effect`, card vs built-in-player choice, older Desktop loads with no renderer, directive kept); `--ui-*`-only theme variables; fallback decision; sound-id extraction (object, JSON string, file name, failed call); clock; Next costs and arguments | 18 passed; `tsc` clean; `desktop/plugin.js` rebuilt and committed, rebuild byte-identical |
| Red on the old head 133ba73 (the current tests copied onto the old sources) | Node: all 3 plugin tests fail (no renderer registered; `--color-*` variables) and `sound.test.mjs` fails on the missing helpers. Python: the refusal-reason test fails. Head mutations each turn their test red: the seam guard forced to `if (true)` (older-Desktop test), the fallback predicate, the `/audio` reason. Removing the card line is a deletion: the result's `MEDIA:` contract is tested, and per the review there is no tombstone test for the removed path |
| `hermes plugins validate` on `main` | passed, no private-import warning, desktop surface clean |
| **Live Desktop (main 3403b92c4b6, Xvnc + CDP, plugin installed with `hermes plugins install file://…#elevenlabs-sound-effects --enable`)** | Desktop half **off**: built-in `<audio>` player, 0 cards, no raw text. Turned **on** in Capabilities → Plugins: the **same reply** renders the card through the seam (0 `<audio>`). Next → 3 variations: message lands in the same chat, 3 new cards. A hard-linked sound shows the built-in player while its siblings show cards |
| Live CLI (`hermes chat -q`, same sandbox) | plain `MEDIA:<path>` line, no card text |
| Live Telegram stand-in (real `hermes gateway run --force` from a core `main` export, real model) | `sendAudio` with the generated MP3 (sha256 equal to the file on disk), no card or directive text |
| Independent review of the whole plugin (2980a3a) | 0 P1, 1 P2 (card could hide a playable sound behind a dead Play button), 5 P3 → fixed in 6655b1f, fb05e05 |
| Re-review of the fix delta | 0 P1, 0 P2, 2 P3 (skill card claim unconditional; symlink refusal worded as "gone") → fixed in 7a88cd5 |
| Demo video audio | `ffprobe`: h264 2560×1440 60/1 + AAC 48 kHz stereo, 1:42. The door impact measures 1.85 s above −50 dB in the final MP4 and 1.85 s in the source MP3 (0% difference); the envelope correlation is highest at 1.00× (0.989, vs ≤0.946 at 0.8×–1.25×). The 6 s rain loop plays for 15.39 s in both the raw take and the final, and its envelope repeats every 6.00 s. Speed-ups only cover waits and carry silence. |
| ElevenLabs spend this round | 275 credits (live legs 80, demo takes 195, including 20 for the re-recorded CLI leg) |

Earlier rounds (handshake era, 4 reviews plus re-reviews) are in this PR's history. Their fixes that still apply (input validation, length parsing, script contract, the remote-backend paths, Next addressing) are unchanged.

**Not covered:**
- A live run on a 0.22.x stable Desktop. The no-seam path is covered by the bundled-against-stub test, and the stable SDK has no `TOOL_MEDIA_RENDERER_AREA` export.
- Windows/macOS live runs (CI only).
- A Desktop connected to a remote Hermes on another machine.
- A card in a split-view tile from another profile. It asks the active profile's backend, gets no record, and falls back to the built-in player after that request.
- A `ReadyCard` render test with a real React renderer (the fallback decision is tested as a pure function).
- In the demo, ElevenLabs returned one of the three variations near-silent (max −51.9 dB), so that play was cut from the video. The tool reports such clips as successful.

## After merge

A data-only catalog PR on hermes-agent pins `plugin-catalog/elevenlabs-sound-effects.yaml` to the merged SHA (#143744, currently on hold).

title: Meshy: audit fixes (long jobs, task cards, remote Desktop, all saved formats, previews)
body:
Fixes the Meshy plugin audit (2026-10-23) plugin-side findings 1-6, 9-15, backend hardening, item 8's plugin half (per-chat card actions, feature-detected for hermes-agent #143776), the progress chip's API fan-out, and documents today's core approval changes (hermes-agent #143780, #143787). Version 0.5.0.

## Infographic

![Meshy fixes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf971c/ugz8bFKnpuvCU4MrZSkS9_VjHdCWEH.png)

## Changes
- **Long jobs (1):** `plugin.json` `servers.meshy.timeout: 1500`. Creative Lab waits up to 2 × 600 s, which outlasts core's 300 s default, and 3 timeouts trip the server breaker. `timeout` is a known declaration key on v0.22.3 (catalog floor) and v0.22.5 (latest stable). v0.22.2 already refuses this manifest over `costs`.
- **Task cards (2, 3):** `/task`, `/active` and `/models` find every task type the tools create: convert, resize, uv-unwrap, print repair/split/multicolor, text-to-motion, Creative Lab. A card's next poll costs one Meshy call, and an unknown id is cached as a miss.
  - Cards stop polling on a permanent 4xx (rejected key → 403; Meshy's own 403 reason) and on a 404 after a 90 s early window, with a Retry button. Outages back off and keep polling.
  - A task with no GLB (Convert → FBX/STL) opens in its best format. A BLEND-only task keeps its download menu.
- **Previews (4, 5):** `render_preview.mjs` launches Chromium with `--password-store=basic` (plus `--use-mock-keychain` on macOS). Every failure, including an offline first run, ends in the one `{"ok":false}` JSON line.
- **Chat apps (6, 12, 14):**
  - The skill sends the thumbnail as `MEDIA:<HERMES_HOME>/cache/images/…` instead of markdown, which the streaming path drops.
  - On messaging, the agent answers "started, ~N min" and wakes itself with a background `notify_on_complete` sleep (`references/messaging.md`).
  - Stale text fixed: Telegram cap is 50 MB and Discord's is 20 MB. A bare path is not uploaded for 3D files. The key page is meshy.ai/developers/keys. The README lists all 8 settings with `hermes config set`.
- **Desktop (9, 10, 13):**
  - The credit chip, settings and gallery follow profile and connection switches.
  - On a remote backend, "View a 3D model file…" uploads the bytes (`POST /upload`; ctx.rest upload, with a JSON fallback for older Desktops). Reveal says where the file is instead of silently failing, and the gallery heading names the backend machine.
  - Saved FBX/OBJ(+MTL)/STL/USDZ/3MF are listed, counted and viewed with three.js's own loaders; BLEND is listed without a preview. Bundle: 653 → 763 KB. Desktop surface lint: 0 findings.
- **Card actions in their own chat (8, plugin half):** Next, Convert, image Next and Reuse go to `composer.submit(sessionId ?? null, …)` with the id captured at render. Gallery buttons use the Made-from chat (`openSession` first when it isn't open). The gallery opens docked right. Hosts without `sessionId` keep the exact old call.
- **Regenerate (11):** keeps the original `ai_model`/`model_type`, quotes that model's price, and drops the "new seed" wording.
- **Blender (15):** after decimation, faceless vertices and edges are removed and source points/lines are kept. Heavy at 1M → 15k: .blend 20.5 MB / 1,022,499 verts → 7.2 MB / 30,262; the GLB is byte-identical.
- **Backend hardening:**
  - Task, clip and session ids use fullmatch.
  - Every redirect hop is re-checked: assets stay on assets.meshy.ai, and the API key never leaves the API origin.
  - Declared and counted size caps leave nothing on disk.
  - Symlinked sidecars and folders are refused, and disk and shape errors come back as JSON instead of raw 500s.
- **Progress chip, no fan-out:** the status-bar chip used to poll `GET /active`, which listed 17 Meshy routes every 4 s while a Meshy tool ran or a task was in flight, plus 68 calls of grace on every window load. Now it watches only the task ids its own tool events name: the id a create call returned, or the id a status call waits on. It polls `/active?tasks=kind:id,…`, which is one Meshy read per task on its own route, and nothing when no task is running.
  - A task leaves the watch list on any final status, when its route still doesn't know it after 90 s, or after an hour.
  - One task's failed read (a plan-gated 403 or an outage on its route) never stops the chip: that task keeps its last row and retries on its own backoff (3 s → 60 s) while the others keep the 4 s pace. Only a refused key (401, or a 403 on the generic routes every plan reads, cached route or not) fails the whole poll, which then stops until the next Meshy call. A route that refuses or does not know the task falls back to the cached lookup.
  - The route a create call recorded wins; a status call's `task_type` (Meshy accepts a wrong one) only replaces an unknown kind.
  - Each task is polled only while the profile and connection its event came from is in front (event tags, connection included; an untagged event belongs to the scope in front). Switching back resumes it.
  - Chip reads have their own global cap, separate from the probe slots (no deadlock, no unbounded fan-out across windows).
- **Gallery and Made-from, per-product errors:** `/models` lists ~29 product routes and failed the whole gallery when one answered 403 (a plan-gated product such as Creative Lab), while a 5xx on one route vanished without a word. Now only a refused key fails it (401, or 403 on both generic routes every plan reads); every other failed product comes back in `failed` (`{task_type, error}`) and the rest still list, with one small notice per distinct reason in the gallery. Every list failing (Meshy down) still shows one error. `/details` (the Made-from panel, and the session the gallery's chat buttons send to) no longer fails on a plan-gated 403 or an outage on the task's route: it keeps the recorded lineage and returns `remote_error`, shown as one line. The other endpoints were checked for the same shape: `/status`, `/formats`, `/actions`, `/task` and `/save` read one record; `_task`'s lookup fan-out already keeps going past one route's failure.
- **Errors (P3):** `/status`, `/models` and `/actions` said "rejected the API key" for any 403. They now show Meshy's own reason ("Meshy refused the request: ip_not_authorized …"). `/status` also returns `error_code`, so the credit chip reads "refused" even when Meshy's text says "rejected".
- **Live-pass fixes:**
  - A window without WebGL shows a message in the viewer instead of taking the whole card down.
  - The theme's `color-mix()` stage background is applied; three.js used to warn "Unknown color".
  - Gallery rows say "1 credit".
- **Approvals and full creative control (README, skill):** what "Allow once", "for this session" and "Always" cover on builds after v0.22.5 (session = that tool for the chat; Always = `command_allowlist` `mcp:meshy/<tool>`) versus v0.22.5 and older (that call only). No tagged release contains #143780/#143787 yet.
  - `/yolo`, `--yolo`, `HERMES_YOLO_MODE` and `approvals.mode: off` skip the trust prompt; the spend limit still asks (Once/Deny).
  - Raising or removing the limit takes a same-name `mcp_servers.meshy` override with `spend_limit: 0` or a number. Checked against core main: the override replaces the plugin's whole entry, including `trust: untrusted`, `cwd` and the 1,500 s `timeout`. Only the declared costs and the 200-credit limit carry over, so the example repeats `timeout: 1500` and keeps `trust: untrusted` with a comment.
  - `${PLUGIN_DATA}` is not expanded in `config.yaml`. The README says where a download without `save_to` then lands (the folder the server was started in, fixed until it restarts) and how to pin a folder (`cwd: ${userHome}/Meshy`).
  - Unattended runs refuse paid calls only with the default settings. With `approvals.mode: off`, `--yolo` or an Always answer, cron and `chat -q` spend up to the spend limit without asking, and `spend_limit: 0` removes the cap. README and skill say so (checked with core's real gate and no approver: default 0 calls, YOLO 8 then refused at ~200 credits, `spend_limit: 0` 100/100).
- **Real-API pass fixes (a6659fb, b1c6f26, 4451b0f):** found by running this PR against the real api.meshy.ai with a real model on Desktop, a real `hermes gateway run` + Telegram stand-in, and `chat -q`:
  - A create the model makes with `response_format: "json"` (the server then returns `{"result": "{\"task_id\": …}"}`) was invisible to the progress chip and to Made-from. On Desktop the model chose json for 3 of 3 card Convert rows. `taskIdFrom` now reads `task_id` from nested JSON, and from an escaped pair when the result is wrapped in a notice block.
  - One card for an unknown task id made 136 Meshy reads in ~5 s (4 concurrent `/task` calls × 34 routes) and drew real 429s. Lookups of the same (key, task) now run one at a time, and later callers reuse the first verdict: 34 reads, no 429 (real-API A/B below).
  - Made-from showed "convert (from the original <the task itself>)". The MCP server names a prompt-less project after its type; that name is no longer shown as a prompt, and a project's first task keeps its own project prompt without a self-link.
  - Messaging skill: in 2 of 2 runs the model called `meshy_get_task_status` right after the create (server default `wait: true`) and held the chat for the whole job. After the first wording fix, the next run used a foreground `sleep` instead. Step 4 now leads with the messaging rule, calls a foreground sleep the same fault, and spells out the exact `terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` wake. 2 of 2 runs pass at 4451b0f (streaming on and off).
  - Thumbnail recipe: the path is printed with `realpath` and copied verbatim. The model had shortened it to a `~/.hermes/…` path that does not exist. `render_preview.mjs` is run from skill_view's `skill_dir`; one run had guessed another install's copy.
  - Streaming is off by default on current Hermes (`streaming.enabled: false`), so the docs no longer call it Telegram's default.
  - Copy: a malformed id now says "not a Meshy task id". The OBJ row no longer promises a texture that an untextured preview does not have.

## Desktop screenshots (REAL api.meshy.ai)

title: blender: open Blender itself and install the add-on on one yes (0.3.0)
body:
The Blender agent now opens Blender itself when a task needs it, instead of telling the user to open it, and installs the MCP add-on after a single yes.

## Infographic

![Hermes Agent Blender plugin 0.3.0: opens Blender itself, online for one session, asks before the add-on](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aaf973e/JTTsxIpYskYuAW1ESOQD9_Ex2XBy7l.png)

## Before / after

Same prompt ("What objects are in my Blender scene right now?"), Blender closed, add-on installed, saved online-access preference off, real `hermes chat -q` with claude-sonnet-5.5 on Linux (Blender 5.2.3 LTS):

| | Result |
|---|---|
| 0.2.0 (catalog pin `ad20043d`) | "open Blender, enable the MCP add-on, and start its server ... Tell me once that's done" |
| 0.3.0, first commit | Starts `blender --online-mode` in the background, waits for the bridge, answers "Camera, Cube, Light ... this is Blender's default startup scene, give me a path if you meant a saved file" (52 s, no question asked) |
| 0.3.0, PR head (after review) | Checks `blender --command extension list` first, starts `blender --online-mode` with `persist_on_release: true`, answers "I opened it with online access for this session. It's showing the default startup scene" + Camera/Cube/Light (42 s, no question asked) |

### Recovery cases (second review, fixed in 1167e83 + 70f61eb)

Same harness, real `hermes chat`, isolated Blender config:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Add-on **enabled**, saved online access **off** (Blender's default), Blender closed | Agent runs `blender --background --online-mode --command blender_mcp --help`, sees `usage:`, opens Blender and reads the scene without asking |
| Add-on installed but **disabled**, Blender closed | Agent sees it with the same check (`Unrecognized command`) before launching (`extension list` still says `[installed]`), asks once with the no-password disclosure, opens nothing without a yes |
| Same, user answers "yes, enable it" | Enables it (Python one-liner, no `--online-mode`, so online access is never saved), opens Blender, reads the scene; saved `use_online_access` still `False` |
| Another program holds **port 9876** | Agent names the process and PID from `ss -ltnp`, does not stop it, does not open Blender (Blender's window prints nothing about the port, so the check is now direct) |
| Happy path, re-run twice | Unchanged: opens Blender, reads Camera/Cube/Light |

The skill now resolves Blender once from the plugin's own detection list (adds `~/Applications`, macOS Steam, Linux snap and Steam) and uses that installation for the check, the install and the launch (macOS `open -a "<Blender.app>"`).

## Changes (skill + docs, no code)

- **Opens Blender itself.** On a refused connection the skill checks for a running Blender and for the add-on (`extension list`); when none runs it starts one detached (`persist_on_release`, so session teardown never closes the user's work) (Linux `blender`, flatpak, macOS `open -a Blender --args`, Windows `Start-Process`), always with `--online-mode`, retries `get_objects_summary` for up to 30 s and tells the user in one line. A named `.blend` is opened by path; otherwise it says it is looking at the startup scene. No display (SSH, server): headless `blender --background --online-mode --command blender_mcp`.
- **Never a second Blender.** A running Blender with no bridge means the add-on is missing or Blender was opened without online access: the skill checks `blender --command extension list` and asks the user to quit (so it can reopen with `--online-mode`) or start the bridge.
- **Online access without touching preferences.** The add-on only starts its bridge with online access; `--online-mode` grants it to that Blender session alone, so the saved **Allow Online Access** preference stays as the user set it.
- **Add-on install on one yes.** It offers once per session, saying the bridge has no password (any local program can drive Blender while it is open), to install the pinned v1.0.3 extension (the one matching the pinned server) with `blender --command extension install-file -r user_default -e`, while Blender is closed, after checking the zip's sha256 (`a7a9da81…0707`); `curl.exe` on Windows. The drag-and-drop walkthrough stays as the fallback. Blender itself is never installed.
- `references/setup.md`, `README.md`, `VERIFICATION.md` (new Linux table), `plugin.json` 0.2.0 → 0.3.0.

## Measured on Linux (isolated Blender user config, saved online preference off)

| Launch | Bridge on 127.0.0.1:9876 |
|---|---|
| `blender` | never (40 s) |
| `blender --online-mode` | up in 3 s |
| `blender --background --online-mode --command blender_mcp` | up in 0.5 s |

`hermes plugins validate blender`: passed, security scan `safe`.

Independent reviews (no review bot on this repo): first review, no blockers, every should-fix in 28492f9; second review found the three recovery gaps above, fixed in 1167e83; its re-review caught that the add-on check needs `--online-mode` under default preferences, fixed in 70f61eb and re-run live (add-on check before launch, `persist_on_release`, read Blender's output instead of asking the user to quit an agent-opened Blender, consent wording, hash check, `curl.exe`, per-OS executable named once, stale `plugin.json` description). The catalog disclosure update rides the re-pin PR.

## Depends on

A core fix so the agent can load this skill at all: the skills index lists plugin skills under a `plugin` heading and models call `skill_view("plugin:agent-plugin-…:blender")`, which current releases answer "not found" (seen live on both runs at the old pin). Core PR: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/143784. Until a release carries it, some turns will not load this skill; the skill change itself is harmless on older cores.

Not covered live: macOS and Windows launch commands (written from the platforms' standard launchers, not run here), flatpak/snap/Steam on Linux.

title: fix(directsdk): route the relay through an explicit organizational gateway
body:
fix(directsdk): route the relay through an explicit organizational gateway

**Summary**

`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is refused when inherited (a stale value can point an OAuth token at the wrong endpoint), so an organization with an internal LLM gateway had no supported way to place it between the relay and Anthropic - the admission relay always forwarded to `api.anthropic.com`.

**Change**

- `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_UPSTREAM` names the gateway explicitly; the relay forwards there and the CLI's own `Authorization` bearer plus Claude identity headers stay untouched.
- The inherited-`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` guard is unchanged.
- Gateway authentication stays separate via `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, which native already sends through the relay.
- A value Admission cannot use (plain http outside loopback) fails at spawn with the existing `Native upstream must be HTTPS...` message rather than mid-turn.

**How to test**

- `test_an_explicit_gateway_upstream_wins_over_an_inherited_base_url`: the env carries both a dead `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the gateway variable pointing at a loopback peer; the peer gets exactly one request and the turn answers. Red on main (`15e3fa0` era, run against a main worktree: `ClaudeAPIError`) - green here.
- `test_an_unusable_gateway_upstream_is_refused_upfront`: plain-http value surfaces `ValueError: Native upstream must be HTTPS or a loopback HTTP fixture`. Red on main (the variable is ignored and the turn proceeds).
- `tests/test_directsdk_admission.py` + `test_directsdk_fast_return.py`: 38 passed, 1 skipped.

README documents the variable and the `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` split; CHANGELOG has the entry. Also adds `.coverage` to the spotify `.gitignore` (it was untracked noise from the coverage work).

Closes #46.

title: fix(directsdk): record login health in the credential pool
body:
fix(directsdk): record login health in the credential pool

**Summary**

A revoked Claude login is only discovered when an agent fails. Pooled providers record each call's outcome in `auth.json` (`last_status` / `last_status_at`), so `hermes auth` and alerting see a dead credential immediately; this provider keeps its login in the CLI's `.credentials.json` and reported nothing, so unattended gateways failed silently.

**Change**

- New `login_health.py`: `record(env, ok)` writes one pool entry for provider `claude-subscription-directsdk` with `last_status` `ok` or `dead` and an ISO timestamp. No token material is copied.
- Keyed by the resolved login directory (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` as `apply_config_dir` left it, else `~/.claude`), so profiles sharing a login share one status (the issue's requested keying).
- Wired at the three outcome points: a successful turn marks `ok`; a native `authentication_failed` (no usable login) and an upstream 401/403 mark `dead`. 429/5xx stay transient ? unchanged.
- Best effort: any failure inside the writer is swallowed; a turn never fails because of it.

**How to test**

`tests/test_login_health.py` (5 tests) spies `hermes_cli.auth.write_credential_pool`:

- entry identity/status/no-token shape, default-dir fallback, and the swallow-on-error contract;
- end-to-end through the real relay with a fake native: a 200 turn records `ok` keyed by the config dir, a 401-only upstream records `dead`.

`test_login_health.py` + `test_directsdk_admission.py`: 39 passed. The two wiring tests are red on main (nothing is written there).

Closes #37.

title: feat(directsdk): opt-in skills nudge on the final user frame
body:
feat(directsdk): opt-in skills nudge on the final user frame

**Why**

#41 measures Claude loading Hermes skills far less often than other providers on the same install (16.2% of 1,795 turns vs 50.3% of 5,921), worst deep into a session and after compaction. The system prompt carries the rule identically on both providers; Claude simply stops acting on it when it sits far away in a long prompt. Wire-identical reprompts and the `mcp__hermes__` prefix were ruled out in the issue.

**What**

A `skills_nudge` setting (bool, default **off**) appends one short `<system-reminder>` to the final user frame, after every other request rewrite in `Handler.do_POST`:

- only the final frame grows, so the change lands in the uncached tail, and replayed history frames stay byte-identical;
- unparsable or shape-unknown payloads forward untouched; the setting is read per spawn and defaults to off, so nothing changes until a profile opts in;
- declared in `plugin.yaml` (with the Desktop/CLI switch), documented in the README, and changelogged.

**Tests**

`tests/test_directsdk_skills_nudge.py`: pure-function coverage (string content, block list, garbage, unknown shape, empty history) plus two end-to-end turns through the real relay: on, the forwarded body's last frame carries the reminder; off, it does not. 43 passed across the nudge/admission/core suites.

Draft: the issue's A/B and cache verification (`hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#89`) is real-account work that cannot run on this host, so the default-off stance stands until that evidence lands.

Refs #41.

title: fix(directsdk): name the resolved CLI and login dir when the login is missing
body:
fix(directsdk): name the resolved CLI and login dir when the login is missing

**Summary**

#47 reports `(none configured)` on the bot surface while the same login drives desktop sessions. The logged-out error currently reads the same regardless of caller, so nothing in it shows what the gateway actually resolved.

title: perf(directsdk): skip the inert MCP helper when a request has no tools
body:
perf(directsdk): skip the inert MCP helper when a request has no tools

**Why**

#42 measures a fixed 2?4 s per call on Windows and names three costs. One of them is cheap to remove now: `inert_mcp.py` is a Python process (?0.6 s startup) started on *every* call, including calls that carry no tool schemas at all.

**What**

With an empty tool manifest the helper is no longer mounted and no `tools.json` is written; `--strict-mcp-config` still receives `{"mcpServers": {}}`, so native cannot discover ambient servers. Tool-carrying requests are byte-for-byte unchanged.

This takes the tool-less slice (titles, summaries, classification) out of the regression the issue describes, without touching the two bigger items (warm process / pool), which stay follow-ups.

**How to test**

`tests/test_directsdk_mcp_skip.py`: a fake native records the `--mcp-config` value and whether `tools.json` exists beside `system.md`:

- no tools ? `{"mcpServers": {}}`, no manifest. **Red on main** (`24d49a4`, the helper is always mounted), green here.
- with tools ? the `hermes` server is mounted and the manifest exists (no narrowing).

Suite: 12 passed across the skip/core/fast-return files (1 skipped, the known timing test deselected).

Draft: partial credit toward #42; the warm-process/pool design is separate.

Refs #42.

title: fix(xchat): a KeyChange refreshes its sender's public-key roster
body:
fix(xchat): a KeyChange refreshes its sender's public-key roster

**Root cause**

Signing keys are fetched only for *unknown* senders (`senders -= self._known_senders`), and `_register_signing_keys` is only given the page's *messages*. When another device enables X Chat encryption it registers a second identity and signs the resulting `KeyChange` with the **new** version's signing key ? but the sender is already known, so that key never reaches the XDK roster. The SDK rejects the change with `no matching signing key`, no conversation key is extracted, and every following message fails with `no matching key found` until restart.

**Fix**

- Decode each `KeyChange` blob for its `sender_id` (`_key_event_senders`, best-effort) and refresh exactly those senders regardless of `_known_senders`; keys are still fetched for all message senders as before.
- Deduplicate the pushed roster by `(user_id, public_key_version)`, so repeated key changes do not grow it, and keep pushing the full roster because the SDK store is replaced wholesale.

**Tests**

`tests/test_xchat_adapter.py`:

- `test_a_keychange_refreshes_a_known_senders_roster`: sender known with v3, phone registers v4 and sends a KeyChange ? roster becomes {3, 4}. **Red on main** (`24d49a4`: roster stays {3}), green here.
- `test_the_roster_does_not_grow_on_repeat_keychanges`: two polls, one version ? still one entry. Red on main only because the refresh never happens.

`test_xchat_adapter.py` + `test_xchat_api.py`: 53 passed.

Draft: the reporter's live X account cannot be driven from this host; the offline fakes exercise the adapter path, and the SDK-level ordering the issue describes (`set_signing_keys` before `decrypt_events`) is pinned by the existing batch test.

Closes #173.

title: blender: install Blender itself after one yes, instead of refusing the plugin (0.4.0)
body:
When a task needs Blender and none is installed, the agent now asks once and installs it, instead of the plugin refusing to install and the skill linking a download page.

## Infographic

![Blender plugin 0.4.0: Hermes installs Blender after one yes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafab1f/fe-j4QKszf6Dyt7rv3GnN_WL98urgN.png)

## What changes for the user

- **Before:** `hermes plugins install blender` refused without Blender ("blender is not installed. Install blender 5.1 or newer, then try again."), and with Blender older than 5.1 the skill only linked https://www.blender.org/download/.
- **After:** the plugin installs anywhere. When a task needs Blender and none (or only one older than 5.1) is found, the agent asks once, naming the download size, the folder, that no admin rights are needed, and that the add-on's local server on port 9876 has no password. On yes it installs Blender and the add-on, opens Blender and carries on. On no, it links the download page.

## Changes

- `plugin.json` 0.4.0: the `app`/`requires` server declaration is removed, so the install no longer depends on Blender being present. Its other readers now treat Blender as available or unknown: tools are no longer hidden when Blender is missing or older than 5.1, tool search and the Desktop server status give no Blender-specific reason, and the catalog and onboarding card drop the "needs Blender" badge. That is the intent: the skill handles a missing Blender.
- `SKILL.md`, new *Installing Blender*: newest `Blender<x.y>/` folder on download.blender.org, the file for this machine (`linux-x64.tar.xz`, `macos-arm64.dmg`, `windows-x64.zip`, `windows-arm64.zip`; none exists for Intel Macs or Linux on ARM, so it says so), checked against that release's `.sha256` list, unpacked in scratch and moved into place, never over an existing Blender and without admin: Linux `~/.local/opt` (plus a `~/.local/bin/blender` link only when no `blender` command exists), macOS `~/Applications`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Blender Foundation` via the built-in `tar`. One yes covers Blender and the add-on.
- The *Find Blender* list includes those install folders, and checks the version with `--version` now that nothing checks it at install time.
- Scene work only through the plugin's tools: when a session started without them, the agent gets Blender ready and asks for `/reload-mcp` or a new chat. Without this rule, one live run read the add-on's source and sent code straight to port 9876, around Hermes's MCP layer.
- README, `references/setup.md` and `VERIFICATION.md` updated to match.

## Live verification

Ubuntu x86_64, the user's installed `hermes`, a fresh `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME` with no Blender, real model turns, results read back from the session's own `state.db`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Install 0.3.0 | Refused: `blender is not installed` |
| Install 0.4.0 | Installed and enabled |
| "What objects are in my Blender scene?" | `get_objects_summary` cannot connect, no Blender found, one question, nothing installed |
| "Yes, go ahead" | Blender 5.2.3 `linux-x64.tar.xz` matches `blender-5.2.3.sha256`, unpacked to `~/.local/opt`, add-on v1.0.3 hash matches and installs, `blender --online-mode` opens, `get_objects_summary` returns Camera/Cube/Light |
| Blender present, add-on missing | One question, add-on install, launch, scene read through `get_objects_summary` |
| Session started without the Blender tools | Blender opened, then asks for `/reload-mcp`; nothing sent to port 9876 |

Not run on a real machine yet: the macOS `.dmg` and Windows `.zip` install steps.

title: blender: find Blender installed from the Microsoft Store instead of offering a second copy (0.4.1)
body:
The Blender skill now finds Blender installed from the Microsoft Store (and any `blender` on `PATH` on Windows) instead of offering to download a second copy.

Reported in NousResearch/hermes-agent#141761 by @fneuch: with Blender 5.2.2 from the Store, the plugin install was refused. Since 0.4.0 the install no longer checks for Blender, so that refusal is gone, but the skill's *Find Blender* list still missed the Store package and would have offered a fresh 400 MB install.

## Infographic

![Blender plugin: Hermes installs Blender after one yes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aafab1f/fe-j4QKszf6Dyt7rv3GnN_WL98urgN.png)

## Changes

- `SKILL.md`, *Find Blender*, Windows: adds `blender` on `PATH` and the Store package via `Get-AppxPackage BlenderFoundation.Blender` (its `Version`, and `blender.exe` in its `InstallLocation`). The package name is the family the reporter saw (`BlenderFoundation.Blender_ppwjx1n5r4v9t`).
- `VERIFICATION.md`: the Store is no longer listed as a place the skill does not look; the lookup is marked as not yet run on a real machine.
- `plugin.json` 0.4.1.

## Not verified

No Windows machine with the Store package was available, so the lookup is not run live. If it misses, the skill still asks before installing anything, and the user can name the existing path.

title: test(homeassistant): assert HASS_TOKEN at the layer that owns it (fixes #5 CI)
body:
Fixes the failing test in #5 — `TestConfigIntegration::test_env_override_creates_ha_platform` — which fails on all three CI runners with:

```
>       assert ha.token == "env-token"
E       AssertionError: assert None == 'env-token'
```

## Root cause

The preceding assertions pass: the `homeassistant` platform is created and enabled by `load_gateway_config()`, and `extra["url"]` is seeded from `HASS_URL`. Only `ha.token` is `None`.

Core no longer copies `HASS_TOKEN` into `PlatformConfig.token` — that credential row left with the Home Assistant extraction (NousResearch/hermes-agent#132469). The plugin's adapter now reads the token from the environment itself (`config.token or _get_scoped_secret("HASS_TOKEN", "")`), so the test was asserting a contract core deliberately dropped.

## Fix

Keep the platform and `extra["url"]` assertions; move the token assertion to the layer that owns it now — construct the adapter and assert `_hass_token`. One hunk, test-only, no production code changes.

## Validation

- Ported file: **82/82 passed**.
- Full plugin suite with a clean `HERMES_HOME` (mirroring the CI runner, which has no `.env`): **145 passed, 2 skipped** — the Ubuntu/Windows CI shape with the single failure removed.
- Python 3.14 against the current `hermes-agent` checkout.

## Merge notes

Base is `port/homeassistant-2` on purpose: merging this lands the fix directly in #5, and the CI matrix re-runs on that PR. The `main` branch does not contain the ported suite yet, so a standalone PR against `main` would have nothing to fix.

*This PR was drafted with AI assistance (Hermes agent), reviewed and verified by the account owner.*

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Claude Code's own project memory gets mistaken for a prompt-injection attack mid-conversation
body:
### Plugin

homeassistant

### What happened, and what did you expect?

## Summary

When this plugin bridges a Hermes session through the Claude Code CLI, Claude Code's own auto-attached project context (its MEMORY.md, a userEmail note, wrapped in <system-reminder> tags) sometimes rides along into the Hermes conversation as if it were part of the user's message. Hermes then can't tell the difference between "legitimate local context Claude Code attaches to itself" and "a user trying to smuggle in fake system instructions" — and reasonably treats it as a possible attack, even though nothing malicious happened.

## Simple example

1. User sends Hermes a normal one-line question over Telegram, e.g. "Is this repo well-maintained?"
2. Hermes's own gateway log shows that exact short line arrived clean without extra content.
3. But by the time the message reaches the model, it's prefixed with something like:
	```xml
	   <system-reminder>
	   Contents of .../memory/MEMORY.md (user's auto-memory)...
	   [bulleted list of unrelated project notes]
	   </system-reminder>
	   <system-reminder>
	   userEmail: someone@example.com
	   Claude Code attached this context automatically; it isn't part of the user's message.
	   </system-reminder>
	```
4. The model (correctly, from its point of view) says "this looks like someone trying to inject fake system authority into my context" and spends the rest of the conversation trying to convince the user it's compromised., when really it's just seeing Claude Code's own legitimate local session data bleeding in from the wrong layer.

## Suggested fix direction

Either the directsdk relay should strip/filter Claude Code's own auto-attached project-memory and userEmail blocks before they reach Hermes's turn history, or Hermes should be told (via some marker) that this specific content came from the native Claude Code child process itself, not from the user, so it's never treated as untrusted user-authored text in the first place.

## My personal experience

Since switching to the claude-subscription-direct-sdk plugin, my hermes installation all the time thinks it's compromised or that I'm trying to test its safeguards and on every single message I send it comments on the injected Claude Code block, and sometimes refuses to respond to me due to that.

I think I may have read somewhere that this injected block is intentional?
What are recommended ways to stop this from happening?
