title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] fix(directsdk): keep Claude Code's memory and account context out of the user's turn
body:
Claude Code's own memory and account context reached Claude inside the user's first message, so Claude took it for a prompt-injection attempt (#195). The native child now runs without its auto memory and CLAUDE.md files, and the relay drops the context native prepends to the first user turn.

## Root cause

Two layers, both on `main`:

1. **Native loads its memory.** `directsdk.py:821` starts native with `--setting-sources ''`. That turns off the user, project and local CLAUDE.md files, but not auto memory: per Claude Code's memory docs, auto memory and the managed CLAUDE.md load whatever the setting sources are. Native's user-context builder puts `claudeMd` (here `Contents of …/memory/MEMORY.md (user's auto-memory, persists across conversations)`) and `userEmail` into `<system-reminder>` blocks on the first user turn.
2. **The relay kept those blocks.** `admission.py` `_frame_first` (was lines 141-156, from #77) moved the text native prepends to the opening request *behind* Hermes' frame. Nothing was dropped, so Claude read them as part of the user's message. On later turns, `stable_request_context` already drops the same prepended text (#40/#36, merged in #83). That is also why the reporter, on 0.3.2 from before that change, saw it on every message.

Real-CLI wire capture on `main` (Claude Code 2.1.310, offline: fake OAuth token, loopback peer, body as it leaves the relay, scratch config dir seeded with an auto-memory note and an account email):

| model | first request, `messages[0]` |
|---|---|
| `claude-opus-5-5` / `claude-sonnet-5-5` | Hermes frame, auto-memory reminder (contains the `MEMORY.md` note), userEmail reminder |
| `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` | Hermes frame, then env, model-id, auto-memory, userEmail and date reminders |

Later-turn and tool-step requests carried neither block on `main`.

## Fix

- `directsdk.py`: the child env gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1` and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1` (both in Claude Code's env-var reference). Hermes owns memory and instructions. A user's `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=0`, which forces auto memory on in Claude Code, is overridden.
- `admission.py` `_frame_first`: on the opening request (no assistant message yet), the plain-text blocks native prepends before Hermes' queried frame are **dropped** instead of moved. This follows the same rule `stable_request_context` already applies to later turns. It is anchored on data we own: the frame must occur exactly once, everything before it must be plain text, and native's wording is never matched. A cache marker on a dropped block moves to the frame with `setdefault`. `pin_message_breakpoint` no longer returns the untouched payload when the opening request has no marks but the turn changed.
- The first turn now goes out exactly as every later request replays it, so #77's contract (call #1's cached prefix recurs at the head of call #2) still holds. `test_first_request_caches_a_prefix_the_second_request_replays` passes unchanged.

After the fix, the same capture shows `messages[0]` = the Hermes frame alone on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 4.5, with no memory and no email anywhere in the body. `evals/directsdk_admission.py` and `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` both exit 0 against Claude Code 2.1.310.

**For review:** on the legacy Haiku 4.5 layout, native also prepends its environment and model-id reminders to the opening request, and those are dropped now. Later requests still carry them at the top of the first turn. Request 1 already differed from request 2 there before this change, so caching is unaffected. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS` also skips an organisation's managed CLAUDE.md. Claude Code's docs list that as a supported way to start a session.

## Tests

New `tests/test_directsdk_native_memory.py` (fake native that records its env; real `Admission` relay against a loopback peer, with native's 2.1.310 opening layout). `test_admission_first_turn.py`: the test asserting native's context is kept after the frame now asserts it is dropped with one marker on the frame.

RED, the new and updated tests run against `main`'s `admission.py` and `directsdk.py`:
```
FAILED tests/test_directsdk_native_memory.py::test_native_is_told_not_to_load_its_memory_or_claude_md   (assert '0' == '1')
FAILED tests/test_directsdk_native_memory.py::test_first_turn_reaches_claude_without_native_memory_or_email[environment]
FAILED tests/test_directsdk_native_memory.py::test_first_turn_reaches_claude_without_native_memory_or_email[context]
FAILED tests/test_directsdk_native_memory.py::test_first_turn_reaches_claude_without_native_memory_or_email[none]
FAILED tests/test_admission_first_turn.py::test_first_turn_is_sent_as_later_requests_replay_it_with_one_marker
5 failed, 5 passed
```
GREEN on this branch: `10 passed`. Full plugin suite: `454 passed, 9 subtests passed` (py3.14 venv, core `origin/main` 571a5911).

Fixes #195

title: mcp-serve: --tools lets vision_analyze read a local file named without a scheme (pic.png)
body:
### Plugin

mcp-serve

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Under `hermes mcp-serve --tools`, the README promises that `vision_analyze` takes "only web or `data:` images (no local paths)". The guard in `hermes_tools._is_web_url` treats any value without a scheme as a bare host (it exists so `browser_navigate` can take `localhost:8080`). It refuses only values that start with `/`, `~`, `\` or `.`, so these values reach the tool:

- `image_url="secret.png"`
- `image_url="screenshots/secret.png"`
- `image_url="Documents/../.ssh/id_ed25519.png"`

Core's `vision_analyze` sends any scheme-less source to `tools.image_source.resolve_image_source`. That function reads the value as a file path ("Everything else is a filesystem path, including bare relative names like \"pic.png\""). On the local terminal backend, it reads the file from the MCP server's working directory, which is usually the client's project directory. An MCP client can then send local images to the vision provider, which the tool surface says it refuses.

Expected: `vision_analyze` over MCP refuses any `image_url` without an explicit `http:`, `https:` or `data:` scheme, with the same "not local files" error that `/abs/path` and `~/x.png` already get.

Repro with the plugin test fixture (`mcp-serve/tests/test_hermes_tools.py`):

```python
server = bridge.create_mcp_server(event_bridge=bridge.EventBridge(), include_tools=True)
_call(server, "vision_analyze", {"query": "q", "image_url": "secret.png"})
# dispatched to handle_function_call instead of returning {"error": "... not local files ..."}
```

### Versions

hermes-official-plugins main (e746f4c), mcp-serve 1.0.0, hermes-agent main (4dcef215cf), Python 3.14, Linux.

### Logs

N/A. The call is dispatched without an error.

title: fix(mcp-serve): refuse scheme-less vision_analyze sources under --tools
body:
Under `--tools`, the URL guard treats any value without a scheme as a bare host, so `browser_navigate` can take `localhost:8080`. `vision_analyze` uses the same rule. Core's image resolver reads every scheme-less source as a file path, so `image_url="secret.png"` or `"screenshots/secret.png"` read a local file. The README says `vision_analyze` takes no local paths.

## Changes

- `_URL_ARGS` gets a third field, "bare hosts allowed". It stays on for `browser_navigate` and `web_extract`, which never read local files, and is off for `vision_analyze`.
- `_is_web_url` takes `allow_bare` (default `True`). When it is off, a value without an `http:`, `https:` or `data:` scheme is refused with the existing "not local files" error.
- README: the `vision_analyze` line says the scheme is required.

## Tests

Two new cases in `test_tools_mode_refuses_local_files_before_dispatch`: `secret.png` and `screenshots/secret.png`.

- Without the `hermes_tools.py` change: `pytest -q tests/test_hermes_tools.py` gives 2 failed, 10 passed (both new cases are dispatched).
- With it: 12 passed. The full `mcp-serve` suite gives 92 passed against hermes-agent main on Python 3.14. `hermes plugins validate mcp-serve` passes.

Fixes #197

title: feat(homeassistant): cross-platform deliver + session-mode delivery for watched entities
body:
Supersedes #5 (and #194, which carried the CI fix aimed at #5's branch).

## Why a new PR

#5's head branch `port/homeassistant-2` was cut on Oct 10, and its `.github/workflows/tests.yml` predates the uv-based install. Any PR based on it dies at *Install hermes-agent and the plugin's dependencies*: `browser-harness==0.1.13` pins `pillow==12.3.0` while core pins `Pillow==13.0.0`, and only uv reconciles that through `[tool.uv] override-dependencies`. That is exactly what happened in #194 — all six matrix jobs failed before pytest started (including `spotify`, which that PR did not touch).

This PR is the same port, rebased onto current `main` so it runs main's workflow, plus the test fix from #194.

## Background

Two closed core PRs carried this work: **#96930** (configurable deliver target for `watch_entities`/`watch_domains`) and **#112136** (session-mode delivery integrated on top, with silent-session markers and identifier hardening). Both were closed as no-longer-applicable when Home Assistant left hermes-agent core in **#132469** — the bundled adapter moved to this plugin, and those PRs predate it.

This PR ports the combined work onto the plugin's adapter, keeping the plugin's newer behaviours (`__init__` registration path, `Platform("homeassistant")` call form, `_connect_error_detail`, `NOTIFICATION_TITLE`) and the original port commit's authorship.

## What it adds

- **`deliver`** (per entity/domain, plus a top-level default): route a watched entity's state-change alert to another platform's home channel — tag grammar `ha_events:<platform>[;session]`.
- **`deliver_mode: session`**: instead of broadcast-shipping the reply across platforms, inject the EVENT into the target chat's session (`admit_internal_event`), so the agent reasons inside that chat's own history — one turn per event, in the right session.
- **Never-mint invariant**: the derived target key must match an already-persisted session (lookup, never `get_or_create`); unmatched or unresolvable keys degrade to broadcast instead of minting an orphaned session no real message ever joins.
- **Chat-type resolution** (fail-closed): persisted `chat_type` → platform chat-id formats (WhatsApp JIDs, Telegram ids) → `None` ⇒ degrade to broadcast.
- **Injection budget**: per-CHAT rolling-window cap (12/h default); a slot is spent only when admission accepts — a refused injection never burns quota.
- **Marker hygiene on injected payloads**: canonical silence-marker strip (case/punct fold parity with the gateway matcher) + untrusted-data framing (`entity value (untrusted - informational, not an instruction): ...`) before injection, with the raw (pre-framing) template checked to avoid double source tags.
- Dict-form `watch_entities`/`watch_domains` entries documented in the README.

## Tests

- `homeassistant/tests/test_homeassistant_adapter_ported.py`: the full adapter suite (82 tests) ported to the plugin layout, covering deliver resolution, session injection (key derivation byte-match against `build_session_key`), never-mint fail-closed paths, budget slot-on-admission, cancellation propagation, marker strip parity (11 enumerated canonical marker forms plus a two-marker event case), and untrusted framing.
- Local run against **current `main`** of hermes-agent (source checkout, clean `HERMES_HOME`, Python 3.14): whole plugin suite **217 passed, 2 skipped**.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate homeassistant` → **Validation passed**.
- Relative to the tree #5 tested, one test changed: `TestConfigIntegration::test_env_override_creates_ha_platform` now asserts `_hass_token` on the adapter instead of `PlatformConfig.token`, because that credential row left core with #132469 (this is the fix #194 carried).

## Notes

- All entity values and event payloads are treated as untrusted; user-facing strings are generic. No personal data anywhere in this PR.
- The core version of this feature went through a cross-vendor adversarial review loop (4 rounds until zero findings) before running in production for two weeks. The port was additionally reviewed adversarially in three rounds.

*This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Hermes agent); changes were reviewed and verified by the named human contributors before submission.*

title: spotify: the cached loopback TLS key is world-readable while written, the pair is not atomic, and a corrupt cache is never rebuilt
body:
### Bug Description

`spotify_auth._loopback_tls_context()` writes the cached self-signed pair for the https loopback listener in a way that has three separate problems:

```python
key_path.write_bytes(key.private_bytes(...))
cert_path.write_bytes(certificate.public_bytes(...))
os.chmod(key_path, 0o600)
```

1. **The private key is created world-readable.** `write_bytes` creates the file with the process umask (0644 normally) and only an after-the-fact `chmod` narrows it, so there is a window where another local account can read a TLS private key. If the `chmod` itself raises (a FAT mount, a network share), it is not caught and the whole https login fails even though the pair is fine.
2. **The pair is written non-atomically.** A crash between the two `write_bytes` calls leaves a `cert.pem` without its key, or a truncated file.
3. **A corrupt cache is never repaired.** The guard is `if not (cert_path.exists() and key_path.exists())`, so once a truncated pair exists both files are "present" and `load_cert_chain` fails on every login until someone deletes `$HERMES_HOME/cache/spotify-loopback/` by hand. The failure surfaces as a bare `ssl.SSLError` from the callback thread.

### Expected Behaviour

The key is created owner-only, both files appear atomically, and a cached pair that no longer loads is regenerated once instead of wedging login.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `printf '' > $HERMES_HOME/cache/spotify-loopback/cert.pem` and the same for `key.pem` (or truncate them).
2. Run the loopback https flow.
3. `ssl.SSLError` from `load_cert_chain`, on every attempt; the files are never rewritten.
4. Inspect the key mode after a clean generation: `0644` between creation and the chmod.

Environment: `main`, Windows 11 (mode window also applies on POSIX), plugin `spotify`.

title: fix(spotify): write the loopback TLS pair owner-only, atomically, and rebuild it when corrupt
body:
## What does this PR do?

Closes #200. Three defects around the cached self-signed pair the https loopback listener uses:

1. **The private key was created world-readable.** `write_bytes` creates the file with the process umask (0644 normally) and only an after-the-fact `chmod` narrowed it — a window where another local account could read a TLS private key. The `chmod` was also uncaught, so a filesystem without POSIX modes (FAT, a network share) failed the whole login.
2. **The pair was written non-atomically.** A crash between the two writes left a `cert.pem` without its key, or a truncated file.
3. **A corrupt cache was never repaired.** The guard was "both paths exist", so a truncated pair was accepted forever and `load_cert_chain` raised a bare `ssl.SSLError` on every login until the cache was deleted by hand.

The pair is now written through `_write_owner_only()` — `os.open(..., 0o600)` so the mode is set at creation, then `os.replace()` so a reader never sees a half-written file — and the `chmod` that remains for umask-honouring filesystems is best-effort. `load_cert_chain` failing on a cached pair regenerates it once and retries, so a leftover bad pair cannot wedge login.

## Tests

- `test_the_cached_key_is_owner_only` (POSIX), `test_no_partial_write_is_left_behind`, `test_a_corrupt_cached_pair_is_regenerated` — the last one is red on base (`ssl.SSLError` from `load_cert_chain`, no rewrite).
- The plugin's suite: `40 passed, 2 skipped`; ruff clean.

## Note

The regeneration is deliberately limited to the https loopback listener's own cache: a key/cert swap only concerns this pair, and the pair carries no user data, so rebuilding is safe. The friendly `spotify_tls_unavailable` message for a missing `cryptography` package is unchanged.

title: dispatch: bring your own sandbox — any platform becomes a terminal backend through a short program you write
body:
Any infrastructure becomes a Hermes terminal backend through a short program the user writes: Hermes runs it to spawn, exec in, pause and delete one sandbox per session.

## Why Vendor sandbox backends keep arriving as core PRs and getting closed: E2B three times (NousResearch/hermes-agent#18348, NousResearch/hermes-agent#34492, NousResearch/hermes-agent#90226), Tenki (NousResearch/hermes-agent#64190), Alibaba AgentRun (NousResearch/hermes-agent#24087), CubeSandbox (NousResearch/hermes-agent#47614), Kubernetes (NousResearch/hermes-agent#37591, NousResearch/hermes-agent#84962 open), QEMU (NousResearch/hermes-agent#137936 open). Since NousResearch/hermes-agent#94400 they can ship as plugins, but each still has to be a Python package against the provider seam. This plugin covers that whole class with one contract: a 30-line shell script is a working backend, and nothing new lands in core. ## What it does `terminal.backend: dispatch` + `plugins.entries.dispatch.settings.program: ~/.hermes/dispatch.sh`. Hermes runs ` [argv...]`: | Operation | When Hermes sends it | The program must | |---|---|---| | `spawn` | first command of a session, or the next one after a pause | create the sandbox, or start the existing one with that id (idempotent) | | `exec` | every command, file sync and probe | run `argv` inside with stdio connected, exit with its status | | `pause` | idle reaper (`TERMINAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS`) and session close | stop it, keep its disk | | `delete` | throwaway sessions (`container_persistent: false`) and explicit teardowns (`force_remove`, used by the prompt-time backend probe) | remove it | - **Same sandbox across pause/resume.** A persistent session's id is `hermes-`, so resume lands in the same sandbox and two profiles never share one. - **Skills and credential files sync in** over the exec job (one `tar` stream through `FileSyncManager`, as the SSH backend does), back out on cleanup. - **Secrets never on argv.** Skill / `terminal.env_passthrough` values go in the program's environment with only their names in `HERMES_SANDBOX_ENV` (the Docker example forwards them with `docker exec -e NAME`); profile-scoped names the active scope lacks are unset inside, same as SSH. - **Bot Desktop, `computer_use` and the browser follow** the terminal into the sandbox (`supports_streams`, `exec_prefix` = ` exec `). - **Approval prompts stay on by default.** A dispatch program might run commands on this host, so `skip_container_guards` is false until the user sets `disposable: true`. No guard theater: this is the existing approval system, not a new boundary. - `hermes doctor`, `hermes setup` and the dashboard picker report a missing or non-executable program. - Ships `examples/docker.sh` (30 lines) and `examples/kubernetes.sh` (pod + PVC, 44 lines). No Python dependencies. ## Live verification (real `hermes chat -q`, real model, real Docker) Scratch `HOME`/`HERMES_HOME`, `origin/main` core (`749cb638ff4`), plugin installed with `hermes plugins install file://#dispatch`, `examples/docker.sh`, `image: debian:13-slim`, Nous Portal `google/gemini-3.8-flash`. Evidence read from the probe home's `state.db`: | Step | Result | |---|---| | `hermes doctor` | `✓ Dispatch program (/…/plugins/dispatch/examples/docker.sh)` | | Turn 1: `hostname; head -2 /etc/os-release; echo HOME=$HOME; pwd; ls ~/.hermes` | `be7b7f4a607b` (container), `Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie)`, `HOME=/root`, cwd `/root`, `cache credentials skills` (sync base created) | | Session 2, turn 1: `hostname; echo resumed-ok > note.txt; ls -a ~/.hermes/skills` | `467f1f913f44`, bundled skills present inside the sandbox (bulk tar sync) | | Wait past `TERMINAL_LIFETIME_SECONDS=20` | log: `Cleaned up inactive environment for task: session:…`; `docker ps`: `hermes-4a16d14eb38c9d8e Exited (143)` (paused) | | `hermes chat --resume -q 'hostname; cat note.txt'` | `467f1f913f44` / `resumed-ok`: same container resumed, file intact | | Prompt-time backend probe | spawned and deleted (`force_remove`); before that fix it left a stopped `hermes-…` container behind, caught by this run | Tests (`HERMES_AGENT_REPO=… PYTHONPATH=… python -m pytest -q`): 3 passed. The environment test drives a real fake dispatch program (a Python script keeping each sandbox as a directory) through spawn → exec → pause → resume-by-id → delete, plus a failed `spawn` surfacing the program's stderr. Sabotage check: forcing `delete` on every cleanup, or a fresh id per persistent environment, turns it red. ## Source and comparison Inspired by Amp's **Self-Hosted Orbs** (2026-10-22, https://ampcode.com/news/self-hosted-orbs, docs https://ampcode.com/docs/orbs/self-hosted): `amp orb provider ./dispatch.sh` connects out to Amp and dispatches `spawn` / `pause` / `delete` jobs (via `ORB_OPERATION`, `ORB_ID`, `ORB_IMAGE`, `ORB_SNAPSHOT_ID` env vars) to a user program, which boots `amp orb bootstrap` inside the machine; that process dials back to the thread. | | Amp self-hosted orbs | This plugin | |---|---|---| | Who runs the agent | Amp's cloud; the orb dials back over outbound HTTPS | Hermes on the user's machine; no inbound or outbound service | | How commands get in | an `amp orb bootstrap` daemon inside the machine | an `exec` operation in the same program, so any image with `bash` works, no agent daemon to install | | Lifecycle | spawn / pause (idle, archive) / delete (thread deleted) | spawn / pause (idle reaper, session close) / delete (throwaway, explicit teardown) | | Snapshots | `ORB_SNAPSHOT_ID` project snapshots | not yet; `pause` keeps the disk per session | | Credentials | `ORB_TOKEN` passed in | skill/env-passthrough values by name; skills + credential files synced in | | Approvals | n/a (orbs are disposable) | prompts on until `disposable: true` | ## Not covered / follow-ups - **Catalog listing:** after merge, a hermes-agent PR adds `plugin-catalog/dispatch.yaml` pinned to the merge SHA so `hermes plugins install dispatch` resolves (the README already uses that command, as the other entries do). - Core drops `probe_only` before calling plugin providers (`tools/terminal_tool_backends.py::_build_plugin_env` swallows it in `**_`), so the prompt-time OS probe still runs one file sync on this backend before its `uname`. Harmless (one tar stream), but a one-line core forward would let every plugin backend skip setup for the probe. - Kubernetes example: written to the documented `kubectl` contract, not run against a live cluster here. The Docker example is what the live run above used. - No macOS live run (CI's macOS lane runs the suite).

title: bubblewrap: CI green again after core moved its exit-status capture inside the eval
body:
The bubblewrap ubuntu lane is green again on current Hermes core: the nightly run on `main` (20048e6) and every open PR's run fail on one test.

- `TestStateDir::test_wrap_command_unsets_the_socket_variables_in_front_of_the_command` asserted the wrapped script contains `echo hi'`, the closing quote of core's `eval '<command>'`. Core now puts its PIPESTATUS capture inside that eval (hermes-agent `812c4bb0449`, `c98e8dc63a4`), so the command is followed by a newline instead of `'`.
- The test's point is that the socket `unset` comes before the command inside the eval. It now checks exactly that, and that the local wrapper still starts `eval 'echo hi` without the unset.

| | `main` test | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `"echo hi'" in wrapped` (current core) | False → `ValueError: substring not found` | not asserted |
| `index(unset prefix) < index("echo hi")` | | True |
| `"eval 'echo hi" in local wrapper` | `"eval 'echo hi'"` False | True |

Checked against `origin/main` core (749cb638ff4) by building the wrapped script with `LocalEnvironment._wrap_command`, as `BubblewrapEnvironment._wrap_command` does after prefixing the unset. The full bubblewrap suite cannot run on this host (its sandbox-dir guard refuses any temp dir under `$HOME`), so CI's ubuntu lane is the proof. Seen while CI ran on #207.

title: test(bubblewrap): match the socket unset inside core's eval, not its exact quoting
body:
## What broke

The bubblewrap job has been red on `main` since 2026-10-25, and on every PR, e.g. #181. One test fails: `test_wrap_command_unsets_the_socket_variables_in_front_of_the_command`, with `ValueError: substring not found`.

Cause: hermes-agent `2b7ab937113` (2026-10-24, "keep shell exit codes when recording pipelines") now wraps a command as `eval '<cmd>\n\n__hermes_rc=$? …'` instead of `eval '<cmd>'`. The test looked for the exact closing quote, `"echo hi'"`, so it failed even though the plugin's behaviour is fine.

## Fix (test only)

The test now asserts what it is actually about: the socket `unset` sits inside the same `eval`, directly before the command (`eval 'unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK GPG_AGENT_INFO DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS; echo hi`). The local wrapper still runs the command bare, with no `unset`. This passes with both the old and the new core wrapping. Plugin code is unchanged.

## Verification

This PR's CI `bubblewrap · ubuntu-latest` job is the proof. Locally the suite can't build its sandbox, because the test temp dirs land under `$HOME`, which the backend refuses as `terminal.cwd`.

title: bubblewrap: ask the user before making another folder writable during a session
body:
## Problem

The bubblewrap backend fixes its writable set when it builds the environment: the working directory (`terminal.cwd`, else the launch directory) plus the `binds` entries with `readonly: false` (`build_bwrap_args` in `bubblewrap/sandbox.py`). Per the README's *Working directory* section, a `cd`, by the model or through a Desktop/TUI workspace, moves where commands start, and they run read-only there.

A common session starts in one project and then needs a change in another. Today that leaves three options:

- add the second folder to `binds` with `readonly: false`, which makes it writable for every session of the profile, permanently;
- set `terminal.cwd` to a shared parent such as `~/Projects`, which makes every project writable in every session;
- start a new session in the other folder, which loses the conversation.

Each one widens the boundary or breaks the session to serve a one-off need.

## Proposal

Make the writable set a per-session value that grows only with the user's approval.

### 1. Ask when a command starts outside the writable set

Before a command runs, the plugin compares its working directory with the session's writable set. When the directory lies outside it, Hermes asks the user, with the same choices as dangerous-command approval:

- **once**: this command runs with the folder writable;
- **session**: the folder joins the session's writable set;
- **always**: the folder joins the profile's writable set (persisted like the permanent approval allowlist);
- **deny**: the command runs read-only there, as today.

The user decides at the moment the access matters, with the folder in view, and the model gains write access only through that answer.

The trigger is the working directory alone. A command can still write elsewhere without changing directory (`echo x > ~/Projects/other/file`), and guessing paths from command text is unreliable, so such a write fails read-only as today. The model-facing sandbox notice tells the model to `cd` into the folder first, which raises the prompt.

Sessions without a person to answer (cron, `hermes chat -q`, webhook and API sessions) follow the existing `approvals.cron_mode`, `single_query_mode` and `unattended_mode` settings, so by default they deny.

### 2. `/sandbox` for grants made ahead of time

- `/sandbox allow <path>` adds a folder to the current session before any command needs it;
- `/sandbox` lists the session's writable set;
- `/sandbox revoke <path>` removes an entry.

A workspace the user selects in Desktop or the TUI joins the session's writable set the same way, since the user chose it.

### Guards

Granted folders pass the same checks as `binds` today: refusal of the Hermes home and hidden paths, and ancestor pins for hidden paths inside a writable folder. The plugin already builds a fresh bwrap argv for every command (only the tracked cwd varies today), so session grants can join that argv per command.

## Core dependency

Hermes core already holds the approval machinery this needs (`tools/approval.py`: once/session/always choices, session approvals, the permanent allowlist, gateway approval transport). What it lacks is a documented way for a terminal environment plugin to request an approval during `execute()`. Plugins can ask the user a question only from a slash-command handler (`ask_choice`). Part 1 therefore needs either a small core hook for backend-initiated approvals or a plugin that calls private approval internals; the hook seems the cleaner path. Part 2 fits inside the plugin.

## Open questions

- Should session grants survive a session resume?
- Should a grant of `$HOME` follow the existing home-as-cwd rule (non-dot entries writable, dot entries read-only or hidden)?
- When file tools run through the sandbox (`HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ=0`, or later the `uses_host_filesystem` hook from NousResearch/hermes-agent#143756), the same grants should cover `write_file` and `patch`, and a write outside the set could raise the same prompt. Related: NousResearch/hermes-agent#132488.

## Context

Based on the README and `sandbox.py` at `e4e4039` (plugin 1.2.1) and Hermes core at `bf0203a`, against Hermes 0.22.5. This is a design request from reading the source; I have not run the plugin yet.

title: ha_call_service reports "already in state <old_state>" for radio devices even though the call succeeds
body:
# Bug: ha_call_service reports "already in state <old_state>" for radio devices even though the call succeeds

**Plugin:** homeassistant v2.0.1 (official catalog) — `tools.py`, `_async_call_service` / `_parse_service_response`

## Symptom

Calling `light.turn_on` / `switch.turn_off` (etc.) on a physical radio device (Zigbee/WiFi plug or bulb) returns:

```
{"success": true, "service": "switch.turn_off", "affected_entities": [],
 "note": "switch.foo was already in state 'on' — nothing to change."}
```

…while the call actually succeeds and the device changes state. The note reports the **pre-call** state and claims the intent was already satisfied.

## Root cause (verified)

1. `POST /api/services/<domain>/<service>` returns `[]` for radio devices: the entity state flips only when the device confirms, typically **150–300 ms after the call returns**. Verified with direct REST polling (state unchanged at +150 ms, new state at +300 ms; reproduced 3× on/off/on). HA's "empty response = no-op" behavior holds only for instant software entities (helpers, templates).
2. `_parse_service_response` maps the empty list to `success: False, "affected no entities"`.
3. The refinement block in `_async_call_service` (the `# Exists in the right domain: the state was already as requested` branch) fetches the state — still the pre-call value due to the lag above — and concludes "already as requested" **without ever comparing the observed state to the requested one**, then prints the observed (old) state in the note.

True no-ops (turn_on on an already-on entity) print the same text, so the bug is invisible for instant entities and misleading exactly where it matters.

## Repro

1. `switch.turn_off` on `switch.foo` in state `on`
2. → note: "was already in state 'on' — nothing to change", `affected_entities: []`
3. `ha_get_state` moments later: `off`

## Impact

Actions always work; only the receipt lies. An agent trusting the note may conclude the command failed, was unnecessary, or retry needlessly.

## Suggested fix

In the empty-response path: derive the requested state from the service name (`turn_on`→`on`, `turn_off`→`off`); report a true no-op only when observed == requested; otherwise poll `/api/states/<id>` briefly (~1.5 s) for the device confirm and report the real transition (populating `affected_entities`); emit an actionable error only when a `turn_on`/`turn_off` leaves the state unchanged after the window.

Happy to send a PR.

title: Claude: consume app-owned multi-subscription CLI directory inventory
body:
## Owner decision

James: “The login should not live inside the agent. The login should live inside the connection apps.”

Companion to oscarhenrycollins/claude-connection#4, wizard-agent-service#204 and wizard-app-manager#265. The former standalone repository was archived during this port, so this contribution is based on **current official-plugins main**, retaining its login-identity, effort, cache, cancellation and usage improvements. The legacy Wizard-pinned fork proposal remains at humanitylabs-org/hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#1; it is not a substitute for updating the canonical provider.

## Contract

An explicitly granted Claude config directory can contain the app's `accounts.json` inventory. Choose isolated official-CLI subdirectories by opaque ID; never copy, return or separately refresh provider tokens. Missing inventories retain the existing singleton contract. Explicit empty/malformed/duplicate/escaping inventories fail closed, not onto the user's host login. An unrelated OAuth-token override or conflicting plugin config-directory setting is denied.

Inference rotates between calls. A definitive auth/quota rejection cools that directory for the **next** Hermes retry; this adapter never replays a native POST or a partial streamed answer. Setup, usage and model discovery use the same explicit inventory boundary. A nonsecret `wizard.app-owned-claude/1` provider marker lets the dashboard verify that this agent actually supports the granted folder instead of falsely reporting a successful local login as an agent connection.

Onboarding opens the **Claude connection app** to sign in, not `hermes auth`. Existing agent-owned pools are untouched. Migration requires app re-sign-in or an explicitly stopped-owner handover; no automatic credential copy is proposed.

## Verification / rollout

New offline inventory regressions cover two directories, legacy compatibility, empty/invalid inventories, traversal/symlink rejection, next-request cooldown, immutable child environment, unrelated overrides, and setup/usage/discovery directory settings. Native amd64 worker suite and stock-Hermes consumer proof are being run; keep draft until those results are attached. No release pins, image locks or owner live services changed.

Reuse:
- transport: REUSE the current official native Claude CLI transport, relay, model catalogue and subprocess lifecycle.
- grant: EXTEND the existing explicit config-directory contract with connection-app inventory selection.
- UI: NEW none; no gateway, token store, refresh owner or native-request replay mechanism.

title: camofox: browser_snapshot/browser_click fail with "No browser session" after a successful browser_navigate (Hermes v0.22.5)
body:
## Symptom

`browser_navigate` succeeds and returns a real page snapshot, but every following camofox call fails:

```json
{"error": "No browser session. Call browser_navigate first.", "success": false}
```

so `browser_snapshot` / `browser_click` / `browser_type` / `browser_scroll` are unusable — navigate is the only working tool.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `v0.22.5+1722.g9976f48` (2026.9.24), profile `default`, TUI
- camofox plugin `1.0.0` (official catalog, `190593f4`), installing to `<hermes-data>/plugins/camofox`
- camofox-browser `1.18.1`, Camoufox Firefox 152, `CAMOFOX_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9377`, no `CAMOFOX_API_KEY`
- config: `browser.cloud_provider: local`, `browser.use_gateway: false`, `browser.camofox.managed_persistence: false`

## Reproduction

1. `hermes plugins install camofox && hermes plugins enable camofox`
2. Call `browser_navigate("https://httpbin.org/html")` — succeeds, returns the Moby-Dick snapshot.
3. Call `browser_snapshot()` — fails with `No browser session`.

Server journal for 5 identical navigations issued as 5 separate tool calls:

```
session created  userId=hermes_1ecd277543
session created  userId=hermes_2f1c89e59d
session created  userId=hermes_78b2d175a0
session created  userId=hermes_4e80ee197e
session created  userId=hermes_f91b0d0df3
(all with sessionKey "task_local-510cf6e3c4")
```

Five calls, five different random userIds, identical sessionKey — i.e. `camofox_client._sessions` is empty on every invocation, so `get_session()` mints a fresh ephemeral identity each time and `_adopt_existing_tab()` can never find the earlier tab.

Two facts that constrain the cause:
- The plugin's `on_session_end` hook does fire (Hermes `agent/turn_finalizer.py`), but zero `DELETE /sessions/<userId>` requests reach the server from tool calls, so the hook is not tearing sessions down.
- `discover_plugins()` is **not** re-running per turn: `hermes_cli/plugins.py` returns early when `self._discovered and not force`, and both call sites (`agent/system_prompt.py`, `agent/prompt_builder.py`) pass `force=False`. So "the plugin module is re-executed on every prompt build" is not the explanation, even though it would look that way.

We could not identify the mechanism from the plugin side. The question for this repo: **is a plugin allowed to rely on module-level state between tool calls at all in Hermes v0.22.x?** If not, `_sessions` should not be the source of truth for tab identity.

## Workaround that works (local patch, verified)

In `camofox_client.get_session()`, make the ephemeral identity reproducible per task instead of per call, and let adoption run:

```python
digest = (uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_URL,
                     f"camofox-task:{get_camofox_state_dir()}:{task_id}").hex[:10]
          if task_id else uuid.uuid4().hex[:10])
identity = {"user_id": f"hermes_{digest}", "session_key": f"task_{key[1][:16]}"}
managed, adopt = False, (bool(task_id) and
                         _flag("CAMOFOX_ADOPT_EXISTING_TAB", camofox_cfg, "adopt_existing_tab"))
```

with `browser.camofox.adopt_existing_tab: true`. After that, `navigate -> snapshot -> type -> click -> snapshot` works across separate tool calls under one stable userId, and a second `navigate` correctly moves the page.

Note: `browser.camofox.managed_persistence: true` also makes the flow work, but it gives every task the same profile-scoped userId (`get_camofox_identity()` = `uuid5` over the state dir), so one cookie jar is reloaded into every task by `plugins/persistence/index.js`'s `session:creating` hook — cross-task cookie bleed. That is why the patch keeps the ephemeral branch isolated per task.

## Ask

Either (a) document that plugin tool handlers must not hold state between calls and make the session map durable (disk) inside the plugin, or (b) fix the runtime so plugin module state survives between tool calls. Happy to send the local patch as a PR if the direction is agreed.

title: [memory-wiki] plugin API starves the gateway event loop on large histories — gateway watchdog kills the whole gateway (exit 75)
body:
## Summary

Opening the Memory Wiki page fires plugin API requests (`/overview`, `/days`) that scan the profile's whole session history in pure Python, with no cache. On a sizable `state.db` this turns into minutes of GIL-bound CPU inside the gateway process; the asyncio event loop starves until the gateway's own shutdown watchdog kills the entire gateway (exit 75).

## Environment

- Hermes 0.22.5 (main channel, build `c5d9f2025e`), Linux x86_64, 2 CPU cores
- `memory-wiki` v1.1.0 (official catalog, pin `54afaf50`)
- History size: `state.db` 358 MB, 735 sessions, 47,613 messages

## Reproduction

1. Install and enable `memory-wiki`
2. Open the Memory Wiki page (the frontend calls `/overview`; the Daily logs tab calls `/days`)
3. On a large history the request runs for minutes; about 3 minutes after opening the page the gateway exits

## Observed

Gateway log, in order:

```
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s)
CRITICAL gateway.shutdown_watchdog: Gateway event loop missed 3 consecutive liveness probes; dumping all thread stacks and exiting with code 75 so the service supervisor can restart it.
```

The thread dump shows an AnyIO worker stuck here:

```
plugin_api.py  get_days -> _with_db
memory_wiki_core.py  build_daily_logs -> extract_subject_candidates -> _extract_from_text
```

The UI then reports "Memory Wiki unavailable — Could not read this profile's memory history": the user-visible error is just the gateway dying mid-request. Because nothing is cached, every retry repeats the full scan and can kill the gateway again.

## Root cause notes

- `build_daily_logs` loads up to `limit_days * 25` sessions (1,500 here) × every message × ~7 regex passes per message (`_PATH_RE`, `_QUOTED_PHRASE_RE`, `_SLASH_COMMAND_RE`, `_TITLE_CASE_PHRASE_RE`, `_CAMEL_CASE_RE`, `_PACKAGE_RE`, `_REPO_STYLE_RE`) and only slices the result to `limit_days` at the very end. Filtering sessions by date *before* extraction would cut the work by orders of magnitude.
- Message contents are scanned unbounded; real histories contain huge tool outputs and base64 blobs.
- The work runs GIL-bound in the gateway process, so it doesn't just slow the page — it starves the event loop and takes the whole agent down.

#49 (subject-index cache + moving aggregation off the event loop) would fix this too; filing separately because the impact here is a full gateway crash, not just slow search.

Happy to test a fix.

title: advanced-delegation: save and switch named sets of model routes (presets)
body:
## Summary

advanced-delegation lets me define named model routes (`fast`, `balanced`, `deep`, `second-opinion`), but there is no way to save a whole set of routes and switch between sets. I'd like named route presets, for example one that pins every route to my Claude subscription and one that pins every route to my OpenAI Codex subscription, switchable in one step.

## Current behavior

- `hermes delegation config` edits one route at a time. Moving four routes from one provider to another means re-picking provider, model, reasoning effort and service tier for each route.
- `/delegation <mode>` switches between Default, Model routes and Profile routes. It does not switch between sets of model routes.
- The routes live in a single list at `delegation.backends.model_map.options`, so there is nowhere to keep an alternate set.

## Proposed behavior

- Save the current routes as a named preset, with the default route included, e.g. `hermes delegation preset save claude`.
- List, show and apply presets from the CLI, e.g. `hermes delegation preset use codex`.
- Add a slash form, e.g. `/delegation preset codex`. It should follow the existing save-for-next-session rule, with `--now` as the opt-in to apply it to the current chat.
- Optionally mark the active preset in `hermes delegation config`.

## Why

People with more than one provider subscription often want to switch every route at once. Examples are running out of quota on one provider, or wanting a different provider for a given task. The same route names (fast / balanced / deep / second-opinion) then point at a different provider's models. Right now the only options are re-entering every route by hand or hand-editing config.

## Related

hermes-agent #79169 asks for named model presets for the main and auxiliary models. This request is the delegation-route equivalent, and the two could share a preset format.

title: feat(advanced-delegation): save and switch named route presets
body:
## Summary

Closes #217.

Adds named model-route presets to Advanced Delegation, including the storage/API needed by the Desktop Subagents preset selector.

- Save/list/show/use/rename/delete complete route sets, including the default and all route fields.
- `hermes delegation preset ...` commands, with explicit `save --force` for replacement and redacted `show` output.
- `/delegation preset NAME [--now]`, plus a bare preset picker/listing. Apply-now uses the host facade so the request reaches the owning chat process.
- Profile-scoped, authenticated `/api/plugins/advanced-delegation/presets` GET/POST API. Responses contain names and the active marker only; credential snapshots never cross this API.
- Active-preset display detects manual edits. Registry mutations use current transactional state, and unavailable providers in unrelated saved presets no longer block listing/deletion.
- Runtime snapshot projection excludes inactive preset libraries from durable session pins.

## Desktop / core dependency

The requested dropdown belongs to the existing Hermes Agent settings page. Companion issue: **NousResearch/hermes-agent#145841**. Companion PR: **https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145845** supplies the Subagents controls and pins runtime route settings with the session schema, including same-name model changes and durable resume.

**Merge/release coordination:** the plugin alone supplies the CLI/slash/API but does not add the Desktop control. Older cores can read saved route values in existing chats even while retaining the previous tool schema; the README and slash reply disclose this limitation. Ship the paired core change for strict next-session isolation. After merge, the official catalog pin must be advanced through the normal release process.

## How to test

With this plugin enabled in a disposable profile:

1. Configure routes with `hermes delegation config`, then run `hermes delegation preset save first`.
2. Change a route model/default, save `second`, then run `hermes delegation preset use first`. `config --show` must show the original routes/default and active preset.
3. Exercise `preset list`, `show`, `rename first renamed`, and `delete renamed`. `show` must mask credentials; deleting a snapshot must not delete current routes. An existing-name save must refuse unless `--force` is given.
4. With companion core PR #145845, select presets in Subagents settings. Existing chats retain their routes until explicit `/delegation preset second --now`; new chats use the saved preset. Save/rename/delete must refresh through the authenticated API.
5. Load the web dashboard and confirm the hidden registration bundle loads without plugin errors.

```bash
cd advanced-delegation
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=/path/to/hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=/path/to/hermes-agent python -m pytest -q
node --test tests/test_dashboard_packaging.cjs
hermes plugins validate .
```

Local platform: macOS. Cross-platform GitHub checks require maintainer approval.

## Verification

- Full plugin suite against baseline core: **312 passed, 4 compatibility skips**.
- Full plugin suite against companion core: **313 passed, 3 compatibility skips**.
- Dashboard bundle execution tests: **2 passed**, included through the existing `evals/ci.sh` CI hook.
- Regression tests proved RED on the base implementation; review findings received targeted failing tests before fixes.
- Real plugin discovery, isolated-host slash dispatch/rebuild, authenticated HTTP mounting, default/work profile isolation, snapshot payload refusal, credential masking, stale-provider recovery and mutation interleavings covered.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate advanced-delegation`: **passed**. The newly introduced private lock and dashboard-scope imports have been removed; existing editor/provider imports still produce validator warnings.
- Uses documented public `update_user_config` when present, otherwise the original public guarded config-writer path. Existing mode/route/profile editing works on baseline cores. No fallback after a transaction error.
- The hidden dashboard manifest now ships its declared registration bundle; no missing default `dist/index.js` asset.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

No changes to unrelated plugins. No running installation or live user configuration is required for these tests.

title: xchat: conversation-key handshake wraps a superseded identity version
body:
## Plugin

`xchat` 0.1.0

## What happened, and what did you expect?

I expected `hermes send -t xchat:<recipient-id> "…"` to open an encrypted conversation with an account that had never been messaged before. The handshake was refused on the first attempt, and on every attempt after it:

```
hermes send: xchat: conversation-key handshake failed: X API HTTP 400:
{"detail":"One or more parameters to your request was invalid.","errors":[{"message":"Invalid identity key: one or more participant keys do not use the latest public key version."}],"title":"Invalid Request","type":"https://api.x.com/2/problems/invalid-request"}
```

`hermes xchat status` reported every credential present and registered, and nothing in `~/.hermes/logs/` named the cause — apart from that single line, the failure is silent.

The trigger is a recipient account that has registered **more than one** X Chat identity. The API returns all of them, oldest first:

```
GET /2/users/<recipient-id>/public_keys
count: 3
  1787584059885   original device
  1793107625688   registered by an earlier client
  1793191919524   device re-initialised encrypted DMs
```

The cause is the record selection in `_initiate_conversation` (`xchat/adapter.py`):

```python
records = await api.get_public_keys(uid)
...
rec = records[0]
```

`records[0]` is the **oldest** identity, and its `public_key` / `public_key_version` are wrapped into the conversation key. X refuses any participant key that is not the account's latest, so the conversation key never seeds.

The visible consequence is misleading. Because the recipient's client cannot establish encryption, its X app labels the thread **Unencrypted** and sends a plain DM instead — a surface this adapter does not read. From the outside it looks as though the bot is ignoring you: no reply, no error in the conversation, nothing in the logs beyond that one 400.

Single-identity accounts are unaffected, which is why this stays hidden until an account rotates or re-initialises its keys.

Fix: select the numerically greatest `public_key_version` rather than the first record, comparing as integers — the versions are millisecond timestamps whose string length can vary, which is the caution the X Chat troubleshooting guide gives for exactly this comparison. I have a patch with a test for it and will attach it as a PR.

## Versions

```
hermes version: v0.22.5+2.gfef9acf
hermes plugins list: xchat 0.1.0 (enabled, catalogue pin f98c0999), chatxdk 0.4.1
Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.9
```

Still present on `main` @ `e4e4039`: `xchat/adapter.py` reads `rec = records[0]` at the time of filing.

## Logs

```
$ hermes send -t xchat:<recipient-id> "test"
hermes send: xchat: conversation-key handshake failed: X API HTTP 400: {…"Invalid identity key: one or more participant keys do not use the latest public key version."…}

$ curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.x.com/2/chat/conversations
{"data":[],"meta":{"result_count":0,"has_message_requests":false}}
```

Test receipt for the patch: `xchat/tests/` → **56 passed** on the patched tree; the new test fails on the unpatched base with `AssertionError: assert '1787584059885' == '1793191919524'`, i.e. the old rule picked the oldest identity, precisely the one X rejects.

One note on the form: the bug template's Plugin dropdown offers only `homeassistant` and `spotify`, so this could not be filed through the web form.

title: fix(xchat): wrap the newest identity version in the conversation-key handshake
body:
## Summary

`_initiate_conversation` selected a participant's identity with `records[0]`, the first record returned by `GET /2/users/{id}/public_keys` — the **oldest** identity the account ever registered. X refuses a conversation key built on anything but the account's latest version, so any recipient that had registered a second identity could never be messaged:

```
400 Invalid identity key: one or more participant keys do not use the latest public key version.
```

This selects the numerically greatest `public_key_version` instead. They are millisecond timestamps whose string length can vary, so the comparison is done as integers — the caution the X Chat troubleshooting guide gives for exactly this comparison.

## Reproduction

Against a recipient whose account had three registered identities (oldest first):

```
GET /2/users/<id>/public_keys
  1787584059885   original device
  1793107625688   registered by an earlier client
  1793191919524   device re-initialised encrypted DMs
```

`hermes send -t xchat:<id> "…"` failed every time with the 400 above, while `hermes xchat status` reported every credential green. Because the conversation key never seeds, the recipient's client falls back to an unencrypted thread — which this adapter does not read — so the user-visible symptom is silence rather than an error.

Single-identity accounts are unaffected, which is why the defect hides until an account rotates or re-initialises its keys.

## Tests

`xchat/tests/` on this branch: **56 passed**.

The new test, `test_handshake_wraps_the_newest_identity_version`, fails on the unpatched base — the control that shows the old rule was the broken one:

```
E   AssertionError: assert '1787584059885' == '1793191919524'
```

## Related

- #173 and #191 cover the inbound side — a rotated identity's signing key never reaching the SDK, so signature verification fails. Different surface: this PR changes only the outbound handshake's key selection and does not touch `_register_signing_keys`.
- A recipient that has already registered more than one identity hits this defect first, before any inbound traffic exists, so the two are complementary rather than duplicates.

Closes #219.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] eager_input_streaming (#156) returns invalid tool-call JSON with stop_reason tool_use; turn fails error_max_turns
body:
## What happens

Since #156 (`db36218`), the relay sets `eager_input_streaming` on every tool. The API does not validate streamed tool arguments. On a long real conversation, Opus 5.5 returns a complete `tool_use` whose arguments are not valid JSON. The stop reason is `tool_use`, not `max_tokens`, so the reply was not cut off.

The relay's `Capture` then drops the call at `message_stop`. Native answers the call locally with a parse error, `--max-turns 1` stops the follow-up turn, and the step raises:

```
RuntimeError: Native request failed: error_max_turns
```

The same input fails the same way on every retry, so the turn fails after all retries.

## Repro

I replayed one saved failed request: 122 messages, 16 tools, about 300K input tokens, `claude-opus-5-5`, effort `high`, adaptive thinking. Environment: macOS, Claude Code 2.1.284, plugin at `main` as of `33907ef`, per-call path. Each arm ran on the same saved request. I cannot share the request, because it holds a private conversation.

- **Flag on (current main), 3 runs:** 3 of 3 raised `Native request failed: error_max_turns`. Each capture had `stop_reason: tool_use`, about 1,250 output tokens, and one unparsed call. In one run I logged the parse error: a `tool_call` argument of 3,032 characters failed with `Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 3031 (char 3030)`. The JSON breaks two characters before its end, where a closing bracket is missing.
- **Flag off (`stream_tool_input` not applied), 3 runs:** 3 of 3 returned a valid `tool_call` with finish `tool_calls`.
- **Flag on, with #171 applied, 2 runs:** 2 of 2 returned without an error, but without the tool call. One returned an empty reply. The other returned one sentence. In this conversation, the dropped call carried the agent's task-completion report.

## Why #171 is not enough

#171 (for #164) handles a call cut off at `max_tokens`. Here the stop reason is `tool_use`, so the model meant to make the call. #171 turns the error into a reply with the call silently dropped. The agent loses a tool call that it intended to make.

## Field data

On two machines, `error_max_turns` failures that survived every retry started the day after we installed a build with #156. Before that, a retry always recovered from this error.

## Possible directions

- Make `eager_input_streaming` opt-in, or skip it for requests above a context size.
- When a call with `stop_reason: tool_use` fails to parse, return a retryable error, or repair the arguments only when the repair is unambiguous. Do not drop the call silently.

As a local workaround, we stopped calling `stream_tool_input` in the relay. Our Hermes stall timeout is 900 seconds, so the long-argument stall that #156 fixed does not affect us.

Related: #156, #164, #171, #113.

title: rea: forward engine-location env vars to the MCP server (Ghidra/JDK, Kuna, TShark, sigrok, WABT)
body:
# PR draft — NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins

**Title:** `rea: forward engine-location env vars to the MCP server (Ghidra/JDK, Kuna, TShark, sigrok, WABT)`

## Body

### Problem

`mcp.json` forwards only `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON`. Hermes spawns stdio MCP
children with a whitelisted environment (`_build_safe_env`: PATH/HOME/TMPDIR
+ Windows location vars + `XDG_*` + secret-source names + the server's own
`env` block), so every engine REA locates via an environment variable is
invisible to the server — including the flagship one. A fresh install with
Ghidra configured per REA's docs fails at the first `open_binary`:

```
provider_unavailable / not_configured:
  "GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is not set"
  java_probe_failure: "java.exe: Owned Windows process requires an
                       absolute executable path [java.exe] (Win32 87)"
```

(`JAVA_HOME` filtered ⇒ REA falls back to bare `java.exe`, which its owned
process launcher rejects on Windows.)

The README's documented workaround is a same-name `mcp_servers.rea` override.
That works but is a footgun we hit end-to-end:

- native config wins the name outright — the override **replaces** the
  plugin's pinned server, so `rea-agents` updates silently stop landing;
- a merely **disabled** (`enabled: false`) user entry still squats the name,
  and the plugin's server is never spawned, with no log line;
- the override must duplicate the pinned launch command verbatim and drifts
  on every version bump.

### Change

Forward the engine-location vars with the same optional-forwarding
`${VAR}` idiom already used for `REA_PWNTOOLS_PYTHON`: an entry rendered
from one whole unset `${VAR}` is dropped (never passed literally), so this
is a **no-op for users who set nothing** and needs no new config surface —
set the var in `~/.hermes/.env` (or the environment the gateway starts
from) and it reaches the server.

- `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME`, `REA_ANALYSIS_PROVIDER` — Ghidra/JDK
  discovery (the default native provider most users start with)
- `REA_KUNA_COMMAND`, `REA_TSHARK_COMMAND`, `REA_CAPINFOS_COMMAND`,
  `REA_SIGROK_COMMAND`, `REA_WABT_BIN_DIRECTORY` — the vars the README
  currently tells users to shuttle through a config override

README: replace the "add them to a same-name `mcp_servers.rea` override"
paragraph with the `.env` recipe; keep the override path documented as the
per-machine pin, noting it shadows the pinned server and must be version-
bumped by hand.

### Tested

Windows 11 x64, Hermes v0.22.5+canary, `rea-agents@6.7.0`, Ghidra 12.1.4,
Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1. With the three Ghidra/JDK vars in the server's `env`
block (locally patched copy of this file):

- `open_binary` → `pe` / `x86_64` / SHA256 reported
- `binary_overview` → 11 segments, 236 procedures, 232 strings,
  provider `ghidra 12.1.4`, Evidence ID issued
- `close_binary` → clean

Without them (current published `mcp.json`), the same probe fails with the
diagnostic quoted above. JSON validated; unset vars render as absent.

title: [accent-picker] Accent Picker+ — durable accent, palette slot editing, live drag, gamut fix
body:
A reimagined build of the official **accent-picker** desktop plugin (original by @Teknium), keeping its OKLCH field, swatches and command structure, and turning the authoring-only picker into a full user-facing theme editor.

## Changes and why

### 1. Full square chroma/lightness field
`oklchToSrgb255` returns `null` outside sRGB, and the field painted those pixels transparent — for saturated hues a wedge of the panel vanished (screenshot-verified). Out-of-gamut pixels are now gamut-clipped per row against `maxChroma(l, hue)`, keeping hue/lightness and always filling the square.

### 2. Durable accent — 'Save as theme'
The original treats the accent as scratch state by design, so every pick was lost on restart. *Save as theme* re-derives the palette with the SDK's `retintTheme` and installs it as a user theme — written through `window.hermesDesktop.uiPreferences` (the host bridge) because a bare `localStorage.setItem` on the shared `hermes-desktop-user-themes-v1` key is clobbered by the ui-preferences sync's next `adopt()`.

### 3. Colors tab — every palette slot
Background, sidebar, card, popover, border, input, etc. are editable with the same OKLCH field, targeting the palette `paletteFor(seed, resolvedMode)` actually paints. Edits apply **live while dragging** (throttled to ~8 fps).

### 4. Reset / Revert / Restore
Per-slot *Reset to default* and *Revert edit*, a *Restore base theme* button, and an *Accent+: revert the last color edit* palette command. Undo history capped at 25 entries.

## Verification

Tested against the packaged desktop build by driving the UI over CDP: gamut-clipped field renders fully opaque; slot edits paint and persist (survives an app restart); reset/restore return to the base theme; no console errors.

`src/` still holds the original TSX and will be synced in a follow-up — the tested artifact is `desktop/plugin.js`, which is what ships.

Credit for the original plugin and design: **Teknium / Nous Research**. MIT.

title: ElevenLabs Music: songs, lyrics, edits, stems and video scores (new official plugin)
body:
Adds **ElevenLabs Music**, a new official plugin: describe a song (or paste lyrics) and Hermes writes, generates and sends the track. It can then redo a section, extend or loop the song, split it into stems, or score a video. It is separate from ElevenLabs Sound Effects and uses the same `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`.

## Infographic

![ElevenLabs Music infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab03c80/7WbHMhHZC2E-S2qo21qLi_nsOyQZ72.png)

## Demo

[▶ Demo video (2:19, 1440p60, with sound)](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/demo.mp4): request a song → card plays with the sung word highlighted → Extend by 30 s across the seam → Split into stems (vocals, drums) → WAV download → music library. [Clean version without captions](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/demo-nocaptions.mp4) (2:12). Recorded in a real Hermes Desktop with a real model and real ElevenLabs; every moment music plays runs at 1.0x.

## What users get

| Tool | What it does | Billed |
|---|---|---|
| `elevenlabs_music_compose` | Song or instrumental from a prompt, 3 s to 10 min | by length |
| `elevenlabs_music_draft_plan` | ElevenLabs writes a composition plan (sections, lyrics, styles, durations) | free |
| `elevenlabs_music_compose_plan` | Generate from a plan: exact lyrics and structure, plus edits of stored songs (keep slices, regenerate parts, extend, loop, condition on a reference) | by length |
| `elevenlabs_music_upload` | Store the user's own song so plans can edit or sample it | like a generation |
| `elevenlabs_music_stems` | 2 stems (vocals, accompaniment) or 6 (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other) | by length |
| `elevenlabs_music_from_video` | Music timed to 1-10 videos, optionally with sound effects | by length |
| `elevenlabs_music_finetunes` | Finetune ids you can use (your own, your workspace's, ElevenLabs-curated styles) | free |
| `elevenlabs_music_job` | Check on or wait for a generation still running | free |

- **Every surface:** tools return `MEDIA:` lines. Files go to `<HERMES_HOME>/cache/generated/audio/`, with one record per track in the plugin's per-profile data dir.
- **Chat apps:** billed calls run as background jobs. Locally the tool waits inline (~5 min). On Telegram, Discord, Slack and other chat apps it waits only `chat_app_wait_seconds` (default 20). After that it returns a job id and the agent sets a background timer, sends one "started" message and delivers the song when it is done. A "still running?" check never sets a second timer and never starts the song again.
- **Desktop (opt-in half):** an inline music card through the tool-media renderer seam. It has title, genres, waveform seek, play/loop, the sung word highlighted, full lyrics, Download (original, or MP3/WAV/OGG/FLAC via ffmpeg), Reveal, and Next (variations, instrumental, other model, extend 30 s, redo a section, stems). There is also a music library tab.
- Ships the `elevenlabs-music` skill: a prompting guide from ElevenLabs' docs, plan-chunk recipes for edit/extend/loop, and how to deliver on each surface.
- **Billing safety:**
  - Every argument is validated before any billed request, and settings outside their choices are refused.
  - A failure after ElevenLabs has answered says it may already be billed and not to retry.
  - A song that is already stored is never uploaded (and billed) again.

## Live evidence (real model: Claude Sonnet 4.6 via OpenRouter; real ElevenLabs API)

**CLI** (`hermes chat -q`, plugin installed `file://…#elevenlabs-music` into a scratch home): "Make me a 10 second upbeat ukulele instrumental jingle for a coffee shop." → one `elevenlabs_music_compose` call (3.7 s); the reply carried the `MEDIA:` line. ffprobe reads 10.03 s, and the `tracks.jsonl` row was written.

**Telegram** (real `hermes gateway run` + the in-repo Telegram stand-in; ground truth = stand-in calls + read-only `state.db`):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| 30 s song, background path | One "started" message → `terminal(sleep …, background, notify)` → turn ends → wake → `elevenlabs_music_job` → one `sendAudio` (30.04 s mp3) |
| "is it done?" mid-job (ElevenLabs held 45 s by a local proxy) | `job(wait 0)` → "not yet", **no second timer**; the original timer delivered exactly one `sendAudio`; exactly one POST to `/v1/music/detailed` |
| Done before the check | Delivered on the check; the later wake answered "already delivered", with no re-send |
| 6 s chime | Delivered in the same turn, no timer |

Generation count = request count in every run (`tracks.jsonl`, `jobs/`, proxy log). Final head re-run: one "started" message (`sendMessage` mid=2), wake, one `sendAudio` 20.04 s. ElevenLabs generated 6-30 s songs in 3-5 s, so with the default 20 s wait most short songs arrive inline even in chat.

**Desktop** (sandboxed Hermes Desktop built from core `780d5a3`, real composer turns, vision-checked):

| | |
|---|---|
| Music card | ![card](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/1-card.png) |
| Playing, sung word highlighted ([video](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/playback.mp4)) | ![playing](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/2-playing.png) |

| Download menu (picking WAV produced a 20.04 s 16-bit PCM file) | ![download](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/4-download.png) |
| Next menu with cost labels | ![next](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/5-next.png) |
| "Split into stems" → six stem cards | ![stems](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/teknium1/23394ba8779891869b3da51be4422670/raw/6-stems.png) |

The live passes and the demo recording found 7 defects, all fixed on this branch:
- **Desktop:** lyrics were unreadable on the chat code-block background; the Next menu opened over the sidebar.
- **Chat apps:**
  - the mid-job check repeated the "set a timer" instruction;
  - the "started" reply went out as two messages;
  - the time estimate was 4x too high;
  - a plan section without styles was refused although the schema says the first section's set the song (now inherited);
  - an overdue job stayed at "15 s left".

The independent review's findings are fixed too (post-billing wording, double upload, v1 songs offered for editing, long-song WAV/FLAC cap, Desktop decoded-audio memory, and smaller ones).

**Not covered live:** the Reveal button and library row buttons; the greyed-out WAV/FLAC rows on long songs (logic covered by the node test); natively slow 10-min generations; Discord/Slack (the same code path as Telegram, keyed on the session platform); a gateway restart in the middle of a job (covered by the "interrupted, may have billed" path, not exercised live). Spend for all live passes: 11 short billed generations (10-30 s each) plus 2 stem splits.

## Tests

- **`pytest elevenlabs-music/tests` (26):** the plugin is loaded by core's real `PluginManager` from a temp `HERMES_HOME`, and its tools are dispatched through the real registry against a loopback stand-in that enforces the OpenAPI request schema. Covered:
  - compose and the library record;
  - chat-app job, mid-job check and wake;
  - refusals before any billing;
  - stem ZIP unpacking, including a path-traversal entry, and the 48 kHz format mapping;
  - the job thread's profile scope;
  - no re-upload of a stored song, and the billed wording after a failure;
  - settings refusals;
  - Desktop routes, including the hard-link refusal.
- **`npm test`** for the Desktop helpers.
- **`hermes plugins validate elevenlabs-music`** passes.
