title: feat(xchat): pace polling to the account's 24-hour call budget
body:
## Problem

X caps user-context calls at **1,000 per 24 hours per account** (`x-user-limit-24hour-*`), separately from the per-endpoint 15-minute window. The poll loop spends one call per cycle on conversation discovery just to ask whether anything arrived, so `XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL` alone cannot keep the channel alive:

- Short interval → the allowance is spent overnight and the adapter sits at `[xchat] rate limited — sleeping 900s`, with the channel dark until the window resets. Observed on a live install: `x-user-limit-24hour-remaining: 0` while the 15-minute window still showed 98 of 100 remaining.
- Long interval → the budget survives, but replies are minutes late, which is the wrong trade for a chat surface.

The limit is per account and cannot be raised by configuration.

**How this was observed.** A dedicated X account used solely for the agent, on a
long-running headless gateway under a service manager, polling continuously for
weeks — the shape in which a 24-hour allowance is genuinely spent. On shipped
defaults (`XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL` 10s) the discovery call alone is 8,640 calls a
day, so the account goes dark after 2.8 hours of idling; at 30s it is 2,880
(8.3 hours), at 60s 1,440 (16.7 hours), at 300s 288. No single interval is both
responsive and affordable, which is why pacing has to adapt rather than be tuned.


## What this changes

- **Two intervals.** Poll at `XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL_ACTIVE` (default 15s) for `XCHAT_ACTIVE_WINDOW` seconds (default 600) after any traffic — an inbound message reaching `_dispatch_inbound`, or any outbound send through `_record_sent`. Outside that window, poll at the existing `XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL` (default unchanged).
- **A budget floor.** A token bucket refilled at the allowance's mean rate (`XCHAT_DAILY_CALL_BUDGET`, default 900 calls/24h; capacity one third of the allowance) charges one token per cycle and one per events read. Once it empties the loop never polls faster than the idle interval, so a chatty afternoon cannot drain the account and strand the channel. A rolling bucket is used rather than a calendar-day counter because X's window is rolling — a day counter drifts out of phase with it.
- **One startup line** recording the effective pacing, so the running configuration is auditable from the log rather than inferred.

No new dependencies. Defaults preserve the current idle cadence; the only behavioural change without configuring anything is that polling accelerates for ten minutes after traffic and is capped by the bucket.

## Tests

Six new tests in `xchat/tests/test_xchat_adapter.py` covering config and env mapping, idle→active→expiry boundaries, outbound send opening the window, the exhausted-budget floor, and refill at the allowance rate.

```
with the patch:  62 passed
unpatched base:   6 failed  (AttributeError: _next_poll_interval / _charge_calls absent)
```

The base run is the RED half of the pair: the new tests reference methods that do not exist, so they fail for the right reason.

## Notes for review

- No linked issue: the bug form's Plugin dropdown lists only `homeassistant` and `spotify`, so there is no route to file an xchat issue through it (also noted in #219).
- Live receipt is the startup line, which records the effective pacing rather than leaving it to be inferred:

  ```
  [xchat] pacing: idle=300s, active=15s for 600s after traffic, budget=900 calls/24h
  ```

  The idle→active→expiry transition itself is covered by tests rather than by a
  log: the measurement account's 24-hour window was already exhausted when this
  was deployed, so the fast interval could not be exercised until the window
  reset. I can add the log excerpt once it has been.
- A follow-up worth considering separately is X's `GET /2/activity/stream` (`chat.received`), which would replace polling entirely with one persistent connection. That is a larger change — stream lifecycle, reconnect, decryption — and is deliberately not in this PR.

title: fix(xchat): keep polling when the conversation list is throttled
body:
### Why

The plugin learns which conversations to read by listing them, then reading each
conversation's events. Those two endpoints are metered **separately**:

| Endpoint | Header seen live |
|---|---|
| `GET /2/chat/conversations` | `x-user-limit-24hour-limit: 1000`, remaining `0` |
| `GET /2/chat/conversations/{id}/events` | `x-user-limit-24hour-limit: 10000`, remaining `9990` |

A `429` from the list therefore ends the entire poll cycle and sleeps for up to
fifteen minutes — even though the events endpoint is answering normally. On a
live account the sequence was: list `429`, three seconds later events `200`. The
channel went deaf for the rest of the day, with nothing in the log beyond
`rate limited — sleeping 900s`.

Polling cost makes this reachable on shipped defaults. `XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL`
defaults to 10s, so the discovery call alone is 8,640 a day: the whole 1,000-call
allowance is spent after **2.8 hours** of idling. At 30s it is 2,880 (8.3 hours),
at 60s 1,440, at 300s 288. The events read is the cheaper half — it is metered on
its own, larger allowance — which is precisely why the list `429` should not end
the cycle.

**How this was observed.** A dedicated X account used solely for the agent, on a
long-running headless gateway under a service manager, polling continuously for
weeks — the shape in which a 24-hour allowance is genuinely spent. On shipped
defaults (`XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL` 10s) the discovery call alone is 8,640 calls a
day, so the account goes dark after 2.8 hours of idling; at 30s it is 2,880
(8.3 hours), at 60s 1,440 (16.7 hours), at 300s 288. No single interval is both
responsive and affordable, which is why pacing has to adapt rather than be tuned.


### What

* Conversation ids are persisted to `~/.hermes/xchat/conversations.json`
  (mode 600) whenever discovery widens the set, and are also recovered from the
  existing cursor state — so a restart that happens *during* a throttle still
  knows what to poll.
* `_discover_or_degrade()` replaces the direct list call in the poll loop: on
  `429` it polls the known conversations directly (no head ids, so the cursor
  check inside `_poll_conversation` keeps each read to one page), and retries
  discovery only when the throttle is due to lift — capped at 30 minutes —
  rather than spending a refused request every cycle.
* With no known conversations the throttle still surfaces as an error, so a
  genuinely empty install does not silently poll nothing.

### Tests

Four new tests, 59 passing:

* a throttled list degrades to the known conversation set and does not re-try
  discovery before the throttle lifts;
* with no known conversations the throttle raises;
* known ids persist across a restart, file at mode 600;
* known ids are recovered from the cursor state alone.

Evidence for the degrade path against the live API, from the installed plugin:

```
WARNING [xchat] conversation list throttled — polling 1 known conversation(s) directly for the next 1800s
```

after which the backlog was read and answered on the events endpoint while the
list was still `429`.

### Notes for the reviewer

* This is self-contained: it touches only the polling path and adds no new
  dependency, transport or config key. Pre-existing behaviour is unchanged
  whenever the list answers.
* CI will show zero check-runs until a maintainer approves the workflow run for
  a first-time contributor's fork; the local receipt above is all the evidence
  there is in the meantime.

title: xchat: inbound is poll-limited, and stops entirely when the account's 1,000-call daily budget empties
body:
### What happens

The xchat plugin learns about new messages by polling: `GET /2/chat/conversations`
for the list, then `GET /2/chat/conversations/{id}/events` per conversation. Two
consequences, both observed on a live account this week.

**1. Latency is the poll interval.** At a 30-second interval, a reply takes up to
30 seconds; at the interval needed to stay inside budget, minutes.

**2. The read path dies for the day when the budget empties.** X meters
user-context calls per account: `x-user-limit-24hour-limit: 1000`, and two calls
per tick at 30 seconds is ~5,760 a day. Once spent, every list read answers `429`
with `x-user-limit-24hour-remaining: 0` until the window rolls over — 10 hours, in
our case. The adapter is connected, the token is valid, and nothing arrives.

Worse, the list and events endpoints are metered *separately*
(`x-user-limit-24hour-limit` 1000 vs 10000, measured), and the poll treats a list
`429` as the end of the cycle — so a list throttle stops inbound even while the
events endpoint would answer. (That half is fixed in a separate PR: conversation
ids persist and a throttled list degrades to polling known conversations.)

### Why polling is the wrong transport here

X already pushes these events. With an Activity API subscription on the account,
`GET /2/activity/stream` delivers `chat.received` over one long-lived connection,
with the same payload shape the events endpoint returns: `encoded_event` plus,
when the conversation key rotated with the message, an inline
`conversation_key_change_event`. Probed on a live account:

* `POST /2/activity/subscriptions` `{"event_type":"chat.received","filter":{"user_id":"<bot>"}}` created with the **user** token (id returned; `chat.sent` likewise);
* `GET /2/activity/stream` with the **app bearer** — first attempt `503 connection_issue: ProvisioningSubscription`, then `200` after ~75 s and held open;
* two messages arrived and decrypted on the stream, both `verified: true`, including the inline key rotation;
* `backfill_minutes` is refused at this tier (`403/400 ... not authorized to use backfill_minutes parameter`), so a reconnect cannot replay the gap.

That last point matters: **the stream does not remove polling, it demotes it**. A
slow cursor poll is still needed for cold starts, reconnects and transport
failure, and it is the only backstop for a missed key rotation.

### What we would like to contribute

Measured on this box, working end to end, in three separable pieces:

1. **Transport** (~250 lines, `stream.py` + adapter wiring): subscription
   reconciliation (list with the app bearer, create missing with the user token),
   one long-lived request, one JSON object per line, `503 ProvisioningSubscription`
   treated as transient, reconnect backoff 5 s→300 s, `401/403` reported rather
   than retried. Dispatch reuses the existing `_dispatch_inbound()`; dedupe goes
   into the existing `_seen_event_ids` under the payload id so the poll cannot
   double-answer. Polling falls to a slow backstop interval while the stream is
   connected. Off unless a Bearer token is configured.
2. **Conversation-key durability** (~150 lines, stands alone): keys persist to
   `~/.hermes/xchat/conversation_keys.json` (mode 600) and load at connect, and a
   failed decrypt rebuilds the conversation's key set from its event history once
   and retries. Without this, a streamed message whose rotation predates the
   restart fails with `no matching key found` and is dropped — a bug that affects
   the polling path today as well.
3. **List-throttle fallback** (~140 lines, stands alone): proposed as its own PR,
   since it fixes polling whether or not a stream ever lands.

Hooks for the adaptive-pacing work are in #226; the backstop interval would use
the same helper.

### The question

Before we send (1): **would you rather have one PR for the stream transport, or a
transport-only PR with the key-durability work kept separate?** Our preference is
separate, on the grounds that (2) is a bug fix in its own right and (3) needs no
transport at all. Ready to send whichever shape you prefer.

Two related threads we do not want to duplicate: #191 (draft; a KeyChange
refreshing its sender's public-key roster — we can hang the key-durability work
off that design if you would rather), and #220 (identity-key handshake).

title: bubblewrap: terminal(background=true) reports "Background process started" but the job dies with the sandbox
body:
*I'm Opus 5.5, running on Hermes Agent, posting on behalf of @mgr-nick (who reviewed this text).*

### Plugin

bubblewrap

### What happened, and what did you expect?

On a profile with `terminal.backend: bubblewrap`, a background terminal call looks successful but the job never
runs to completion. Live test on a helper agent (2026-10-29):

1. `terminal(command="sleep 2; echo done > bgtest.txt", background=true)` returned
   `{"output": "Background process started", "session_id": "proc_8d74ed30220f", "pid": 3, "exit_code": 0, "error": null, ...}`
   (plus the usual hint to poll or use `notify_on_complete`).
2. After `sleep 5` in a normal call, `ls -la bgtest.txt` → `No such file or directory`.

`pid 3` is a PID inside the per-command sandbox's PID namespace, and the job dies when that command's sandbox ends.
The plugin's own prompt section already says "Background processes are not available on this backend: each command's
sandbox ends with it", so this is expected behaviour, but the tool result contradicts it: the model sees a successful
start with a session id it can poll, and a model that trusts tool results over the system prompt will wait for, or
report on, a job that never ran.

**Expected:** with this backend, `background=true` should fail clearly (e.g. an error such as "background processes
are not supported by the bubblewrap backend; run it in the foreground, or use a backend that keeps processes"), or
run the job in a sandbox that outlives the call. Either way the result shouldn't report a live process.

(Core's hermes-agent#142560, merged 2026-10-22 and included in this version, makes failed background launches on
non-local backends report real failures, but here the launch itself succeeds inside the short-lived sandbox.)

### Versions

Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (`bf0203a794`, stable); bubblewrap plugin 1.2.1; bubblewrap 0.12.0; Debian 13
(GCP VM). Our setup puts a small wrapper ahead of `bwrap` that runs each sandboxed command in its own systemd scope
with a memory cap; the plugin's prompt text indicates the same outcome without it.

### Logs

The tool result quoted above.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] cache_read still freezes at the system+tools mark on 0.3.3 (20048e6); every tool round re-writes the history
body:
### What happened, and what did you expect?

On 0.3.3 (`20048e6`), `cache_read` freezes at the system+tools mark from the second request on, and every tool round re-writes the whole message history to the cache. This is the same signature as #38, which was reported fixed on 0.3.3 (`4bc79c7`), but here it reproduces on a fresh install of the current pin.

It matters at scale: on our gateway over one 5-hour window, Hermes sent 414 subscription requests with 57.4M input tokens, of which 48.8M were cache writes (14–21% cache reads). Long delegate loops reach ~170K tokens per request with only ~20.7K read from cache each call. That drains the 5-hour plan limit far faster than Claude Code sessions on the same machine, which read 95% from cache in the same window.

Expected: from call #2 on, `cache_read` tracks the previous call's total, as in the #38 confirmation.

**Minimal reproduction** (one user turn, four sequential tool calls, Claude Code env vars removed so #150 does not apply):

```sh
env -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID ... \
  hermes chat --oneshot -m claude-sonnet-5 \
    --provider claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental -t terminal \
    -q 'Run these as four separate terminal tool calls, one at a time: (1) `wc -l ~/.hermes/gateway-starts.log` (2) `date` (3) `uname -r` (4) `nproc`. Then reply with the outputs in one line.'
```

The same freeze shows in all three variants I tried, so it does not depend on the Claude Code version or on thinking:

| Variant | `cache_read` per call | `cache_creation` per call |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code 2.1.312 (default) | 10187 on every call | 702 → 838 → 940 → 1034 → 1117 |
| Claude Code 2.1.293 via `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` | 10187 on every call | 702 → 837 → 939 → 1033 → 1116 |
| 2.1.312 with `--reasoning none` | 10187 from call #2 on | 822 → 924 → 1018 → 1101 |

The write is always the whole message history, never the increment, so the entry each call writes at its message breakpoint is never read by the next call.

The offline wire eval passes on 2.1.312: `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` reports 22 requests and 19/19 `prefix_receipts` with `old_prefix_sha256 == replayed_prefix_sha256`. So the bytes through the previous breakpoint replay identically under the loopback peer, but the live API still does not hit. Whatever breaks the cache is something the eval does not exercise.

`claude_code_telemetry` is `false` for these runs. I have not tried it with telemetry on.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.5 (2026.9.24) · stable · local bf0203a794a0, install method git
claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental 0.3.3, catalog pin 20048e6e2c1c48d6023e73ae6951595f58352b20
Claude Code 2.1.312 (also reproduced with 2.1.293)
Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.11
Subscription login; models claude-sonnet-5 and claude-opus-5-5[1m] both affected
```

### Logs

`agent.log`, default variant (2.1.312), one session:

```text
API call #1: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=10891 cache=10187/10891 (94%) write=702
API call #2: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=11027 cache=10187/11027 (92%) write=838
API call #3: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=11129 cache=10187/11129 (92%) write=940
API call #4: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=11223 cache=10187/11223 (91%) write=1034
API call #5: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=11306 cache=10187/11306 (90%) write=1117
```

A long delegate session on the previous pin (`885ba10`) showed the same freeze at a larger size (`cache=20748/...` on every call, `write` growing from ~149K):

```text
API call #40: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=169880 out=332 cache=20748/169880 (12%) write=149130
API call #41: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=170313 out=386 cache=20748/170313 (12%) write=149563
API call #42: model=claude-sonnet-5 in=170810 out=485 cache=20748/170810 (12%) write=150060
```

title: fix(homeassistant): don't report a device that confirms late as already in state (#213)
body:
Fixes #213.

## Problem

With a physical device (Zigbee/Wi-Fi plug, bulb, lock), `POST /api/services/<domain>/<service>` returns `[]` before the device confirms. The state flips 150–300 ms later. The no-op branch in `_async_call_service` read the state once, still the pre-call value, and for a `switch.turn_off` that was working it returned:

> `success: true` … "switch.plug was already in state 'on' — nothing to change."

It never compared the observed state with the requested one. `toggle`, `lock.lock` and `cover.set_cover_position` got the same claim.

## Fix

- **Compare the observed state with the state the service asks for.** This covers `turn_on`, `turn_off`, `lock`/`unlock`/`open`, `open_cover`/`close_cover` and `open_valve`/`close_valve`. For `turn_on`, any active state counts, so a media player reporting `idle` or a thermostat on `heat` is satisfied. `toggle` always asks for a change.
- **True no-ops are unchanged.** They still answer from one state read, with the same note as before.
- **Otherwise, wait for the device to confirm.** The state is re-read for up to 1.5 s (0.25 + 0.5 + 0.75 s).
  - A confirmed transition returns success with the new state in `affected_entities`.
  - A move to `unavailable`/`unknown` doesn't count as confirmed.
  - A state that never moves becomes an error saying the device may be offline or slow to confirm, and to check with `ha_get_state` before retrying. That way a `toggle` isn't sent twice.
- **Services that name no target state** get a neutral note ("accepted; Home Assistant reported no state change for … (state 'open')") instead of the no-op claim.
- **The `ha_call_service` description** now lists the new error case.

## Tests

Nine new tests in `TestCallServiceVerification`:
- late confirmation
- a device that never confirms
- a true no-op that answers without waiting
- an `idle` media player
- toggle
- a lock passing through `locking`
- a service with no target state
- a drop to `unavailable`
- a failed re-check

Seven of them fail on current `main` with the bug's own message, for example `lock.door was already in state 'unlocked' — nothing to change.` The other two pin the existing no-op behaviour.

With the fix, the plugin suite passes against current Hermes core on Linux, macOS and Windows:
- Linux and Windows: 144 passed, 2 skipped
- macOS: 145 passed, 1 skipped

`hermes plugins validate homeassistant` also passes. All of this ran the same way as this repo's CI: Python 3.14, uv with core's overrides.

#231 also references #213. This PR waits for the device's confirmation, as the issue suggests, adds tests, and changes nothing else.

title: camofox: retry the cold-start tab create once, transparently
body:
## Problem (repro'd on a live routed-worker estate)

After camofox-browser's idle shutdown (`BROWSER_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, browser exits once the session map empties), the **first** `POST /tabs` pays for launching Camoufox *and* restoring the persisted storage state:

- server log (harbor.camofox, quiet host): `launching camoufox` 11:51:07Z → `restoring persisted storage state` (884 KB, managed userId) 11:51:08Z → `session created` 11:51:16Z — **8.2 s** cold, vs **0.4–0.7 s** warm.
- under concurrent load the same path measured **25.2 s / 29.7 s** (server log 10:22:37Z / 10:59:22Z) against the server's own 30 s tab-create route budget (`tabCreateRequestTimeoutMs`, camofox-browser `server.js`) — the server answers **500 `tab create timed out after 30000ms` while the coalesced build is still finishing**; a caller with a smaller `browser.command_timeout` instead sees a client-side `ReadTimeout`.
- the coalesced build completes **just after** the failure, so an immediate second `POST /tabs` answers 200 in ~1 s (measured 1177 ms at 10:59:32Z; and live at 11:51:16Z both in-flight requests — 9693 ms and 4681 ms — returned 200 off one build at the same instant).

Every Hermes deployment behind the camofox backend eats this flake on the first browser call after idle; the agent sees an opaque 500 and (if lucky) retries at the LLM level.

## Fix

`create_tab()` in `camofox_client.py`: one transparent retry of `POST /tabs` when the first attempt fails with **5xx or a client Timeout**, with the retry given a raised per-call budget `max(browser.command_timeout, 60)` so it can wait out an in-flight cold build. Wired into `ensure_tab` (the only `POST /tabs` call site). No other route, no config surface, no retry storm — a second failure keeps the existing raise-for-status semantics, and 4xx is never retried.

## Tests

`tests/test_camofox_tab_create_retry.py` — 5 cases against the in-process `FakeCamofox` over real `requests` calls:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| cold 500 → retry → tab created (exactly 2 POSTs) | PASS (red on base) |
| persistent 500 → raises, exactly first+retry (no storm) | PASS (red on base) |
| client `ReadTimeout` → retried with raised budget ≥ 60 s | PASS (red on base) |
| 4xx → not retried (1 POST) | PASS (green on base too — locks existing semantics) |
| warm create → unchanged single POST | PASS (green on base too) |

Full plugin suite: **93 passed, 1 skipped**.

## Not in this PR

The root-cause side belongs to camofox-browser itself (a slow-`newContext`-aware budget, or answering 202 `starting` and letting the client poll, would make any client retry unnecessary) — I've noted it upstream there. This PR removes the flake class for every Hermes deployment at the client source regardless of server version.

title: Fix Home Assistant device event cooldown and state descriptions
body:
Title: Fix Home Assistant device event cooldown and state descriptions

## Summary
- Start per-entity cooldown only after an event produces a message, so no-op events cannot suppress the next meaningful transition.
- Preserve actual unknown/unavailable transitions for switches, lights, fans and binary sensors instead of describing them as off or cleared.
- Describe attribute-only climate changes to current temperature, target temperature and target temperature range while ignoring unrelated attribute changes.

## Verification
- Added 22 synthetic regression cases; before the production fix: 17 failed, 5 passed.
- Complete Home Assistant suite: 158 passed, 1 skipped using an isolated test home and the current installed Hermes core checkout with isolated aiohttp/pytest dependencies.
- git diff --check passed.

## Scope
Only the Home Assistant adapter and synthetic device-event regression tests are changed. No configuration, captured device data, backups, or unrelated changes are included.

title: [homeassistant] ha_call_service reports "was already in state … — nothing to change" for calls that did change the state
body:
### Plugin

homeassistant

### What happened, and what did you expect?

# `ha_call_service` reports "was already in state … — nothing to change" for calls that did change the state
**Plugin:** homeassistant v2.0.1 (`NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins`, `homeassistant/`)
**Hermes:** 0.21.x · **HA:** 2026.10.4 · **Entities:** MQTT / zigbee2mqtt (Hue Go E27)
## Summary
A `light.turn_on` on an `off` light returns `success: true` with `affected_entities: []` and the note
`"light.philips_hue_go was already in state 'off' — nothing to change."` — while the light actually
turned **on** at the requested brightness. The mirror case is identical: `light.turn_off` on an `on`
light reports `"was already in state 'on' — nothing to change"` and the light goes **off**.
The note is not merely cosmetic: it tells the model the intent was already satisfied, so a caller that
trusts the tool's verdict draws the opposite conclusion from reality. Only a follow-up `ha_get_state`
reveals what happened.
## Reproduction (observed 2026-10-31, 13:54:29Z and 13:54:57Z)
```
ha_call_service(domain="light", service="turn_on", entity_id="light.philips_hue_go",
                data='{"brightness": 51}')
# -> success: true, affected_entities: [], note: "… was already in state 'off' — nothing to change."
ha_get_state("light.philips_hue_go")
# -> state: "on", brightness: 51, last_changed: 13:54:29.178Z
ha_call_service(domain="light", service="turn_off", entity_id="light.philips_hue_go")
# -> success: true, affected_entities: [], note: "… was already in state 'on' — nothing to change."
ha_get_state("light.philips_hue_go")
# -> state: "off", brightness: null, last_changed: 13:54:57.077Z
```
## Cause
`_async_call_service()` (tools.py, ~line 611) treats an empty `affected_entities` list as "nothing
changed", then does an immediate `GET /api/states/{entity_id}` to decide *why* (missing entity / wrong
domain / already in the requested state). For MQTT-backed entities the state update arrives
**after** the service call returns, so that GET reads the **pre-call** state — and the code
interprets it as "already as requested" (tools.py, ~line 654-657):
```python
# Exists in the right domain: the state was already as requested — intent satisfied.
out["success"] = True
del out["error"]
out["note"] = f"{entity_id} was already in state '{state['state']}' — nothing to change."
```
Any async/optimistic entity (MQTT, Zigbee2MQTT, cloud integrations, Z-Wave) hits this race; it is not
specific to this instance.
## Suggested fix
Before concluding "already in state", check the read state against the service's intent — and when it
*contradicts* it, do not claim a no-op:
```python
_INTENT = {("light", "turn_on"): "on", ("light", "turn_off"): "off",
           ("switch", "turn_on"): "on", ("switch", "turn_off"): "off"}
want = _INTENT.get((domain, service))
if want is not None and state["state"] != want:
    # call accepted, state not propagated yet — poll briefly, then report honestly
    for _ in range(5):
        await asyncio.sleep(0.2)
        state = await _api_json("GET", f"/api/states/{entity_id}", 10)
        if state["state"] == want:
            break
    if state["state"] != want:
        out["note"] = (f"{entity_id} state is '{state['state']}' right after "
                       f"{domain}.{service} — call accepted, propagation not observed yet.")
        return out
out["note"] = ...  # only now the genuine "already in state" case
```
Minimum viable change: never emit `"already in state X — nothing to change"` when `X` is the state the
call was supposed to leave.
## Impact
Every state-changing call on an async entity returns a note that contradicts reality; an agent that
trusts it either reports the wrong outcome to the user or skips a needed retry. Verified twice in a row
on two opposite services, so it is deterministic for this entity class.


### Versions

```text
Hermes: 0.21.x · HA: 2026.10.4
```

### Logs

```text

```

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Fable loses the prompt cache
body:
### Plugin

homeassistant

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Hello!

I'm Ethan, at least this bit of text is hand written by a human (me).    I've been using the claude subscription-directsdk with great success. However' I've noticed when using fable I was getting some cache misses unexpectedly.   I had fable/opus investigate and they reproduced the issue, implemented a fix locally, and prepared the following report for you.

Now for some disclaimers.  I have verified i am no longer getting cache misses but I haven't put the time in to go deep and evaluate if this is the right approach to solving the problem.   My apologies if this turns out to be invalid or otherwise mistaken.

A second disclaimer is I am actually not running the sdk within hermes.  Instead I am using it from pi with a ts to python adapter.  That said the cache misses are at a part of the stack where it seems unlikely to be specific to this unusual aspect of my setup. 

Here's the AI generated summary of the issue.  Everything below this line generated by opus 5.5

## AI Generated Bug Report

### What happened, and what did you expect?

On `claude-fable-5-1`, the cached prefix breaks at `messages[1]`, the
environment message, whenever the conversation switches between a user turn
and a tool-result step, in either direction. The request at each such switch
reads only the system prompt and tools from cache and writes the whole
conversation again. The other routes in `model_catalog` keep `messages[1]`
stable on the same install: Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Opus 4.8
and Sonnet 5.

Expected: `messages[1]` is byte-identical on every request of a conversation,
as it is on Opus.

**Cause.** Claude Code 2.1.311 ("native" below) adds a per-model "batching
reminder": feature `tengu_toasty_thimble`, env `CLAUDE_CODE_TOASTY_THIMBLE`,
on by default for Fable only. On tool-result steps, native sends it in the
same trailing `role: system` message as the date line:

```json
{"role": "system", "content": [
  {"type": "text", "text": "Today's date is 2026-10-30."},
  {"type": "text", "text": "First privately list what you need next; then request every item that doesn't depend on another's result in this one response."}
]}
```

`stable_request_context` moves the date line into `messages[1]` only when the
trailing message is a string or a single block (`content[0] if len(content) == 1`). The two kinds of request therefore produce two different
`messages[1]`:

* **User turn.** The date is alone, so it moves, and `messages[1]` ends with
  `\n\nToday's date is …`.
* **Tool-result step.** The date has the reminder beside it, so nothing moves,
  and `messages[1]` lacks the date.

**Reproduction (offline, no credentials).** `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py`
already catches this when pointed at Fable. As shipped, it runs only against
`claude-sonnet-5`, where it passes because that route sends neither the
reminder nor a bare date line. Against Fable:

```text
$ python3 evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py /path/to/claude --model claude-fable-5-1
AssertionError: cached prefix changed at round 1: a7373b2f… != efd4b120…
```

**Fix.** We patched the relay to do the reverse of the current move and keep
per-request text out of `messages[1]` entirely:

* When native ends the environment message with `\n\n` and the date line, the
  relay strips that line and sends it as the first block of the trailing
  system message, adding that message when there is none.
* Otherwise the trailing message native sends is left as is.

Later requests replay `messages[1]` but never the trailing message, so
`messages[1]` no longer depends on what native puts there: the date alone, the
date beside a reminder, or a reminder Anthropic turns on remotely, through
client data, for any model pattern. It also stops a long session from
re-writing its history when the date changes at midnight. Sonnet 5 already
gets this layout today: its date arrives as a `<system-reminder>` block the
relay never moves.

The change to `admission.py`, against `e4e40398` (this code is unchanged on
`main` since):

```diff
--- a/claude-subscription-directsdk/admission.py
+++ b/claude-subscription-directsdk/admission.py
@@ -162,20 +162,22 @@
     return True
 
 
-# The only trailing system text the relay moves: native 2.1.299's date line, exactly as its opening request ends the
-# environment message. Any other trailing text stays put, since moving text that varies per request into the
-# environment message would change the prefix from message 1 on every request.
+# The only environment text the relay moves: native 2.1.299's date line, exactly as its opening request ends the
+# environment message. Later requests send it in their trailing system message, alone or (2.1.311 on Fable) ahead
+# of a per-step nudge, so it moves out of the environment message, which every later request replays, never in.
 _DATE_LINE = re.compile(r"Today's date is \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.")
 
 
 def stable_request_context(payload, queried):
     """Keep native's per-request context in the prefix later per-call requests replay.
 
-    Native splits today's date out of the environment into a trailing system message
-    and prepends reminders to the newest user frame. Neither position recurs when
-    signed thinking is replayed (#40), and new user turns lose their cache prefix (#36).
-    Append that date line (no other trailing text) after two newlines to the first system
-    message, keeping a string a string; drop only plain text before the whole queried frame,
+    Native ends the environment message with today's date on some requests and sends the
+    date in a trailing system message on others, and prepends reminders to the newest user
+    frame. The environment message then differs between requests, the reminders do not recur
+    when signed thinking is replayed (#40), and new user turns lose their cache prefix (#36).
+    Move that date line (no other text) from the end of the first system message to the front
+    of the trailing one, adding one when there is none, so the environment message carries
+    nothing per-request; drop only plain text before the whole queried frame,
     found exactly once, on later user turns, which native already omits from tool-result steps. Removed cache markers move with setdefault, never multiply.
     Warm sessions skip this transform at the relay. Assistant text/thinking, tool-result-only
     turns, opening-turn reminders and top-level system/tools are never touched.
@@ -195,26 +197,22 @@
         if queried is not None and (not isinstance(queried, list) or any(not isinstance(b, dict) for b in queried)):
             return payload
         changed = False
-        last = messages[-1] if messages else {}
-        env = next((m for m in messages[:-1] if m.get('role') == 'system'), None)
-        content = last.get('content')
-        tail = {'type': 'text', 'text': content} if isinstance(content, str) else (
-            content[0] if isinstance(content, list) and len(content) == 1 else {})
-        if last.get('role') == 'system' and env is not None and tail.get('type') == 'text' \
-                and _DATE_LINE.fullmatch(tail.get('text', '')):
-            original, line = env['content'], '\n\n' + tail['text']
-            target = {'type': 'text', 'text': original} if isinstance(original, str) else (original[-1] if original else {})
-            if target.get('type') == 'text' and not target['text'].endswith(tail['text']):
-                if isinstance(original, str):
-                    env['content'] = original + line
-                else:
-                    target['text'] += line
-                mark = tail.get('cache_control', last.get('cache_control'))
-                messages.pop()
-                previous = messages[-1]['content']
-                if mark is not None and isinstance(previous, list) and previous:
-                    previous[-1].setdefault('cache_control', mark)
-                changed = True
+        env = next((m for m in messages if m.get('role') == 'system'), {})
+        original = env.get('content')
+        target = {'type': 'text', 'text': original} if isinstance(original, str) else (original[-1] if original else {})
+        kept, _, line = target.get('text', '').rpartition('\n\n') if target.get('type') == 'text' else ('', '', '')
+        if kept and _DATE_LINE.fullmatch(line):
+            if isinstance(original, str):
+                env['content'] = kept
+            else:
+                target['text'] = kept
+            date, last = {'type': 'text', 'text': line}, messages[-1]
+            if last is not env and last.get('role') == 'system':
+                tail = last['content']
+                last['content'] = [date] + ([{'type': 'text', 'text': tail}] if isinstance(tail, str) else tail)
+            else:
+                messages.append({'role': 'system', 'content': [date]})
+            changed = True
         newest = next((m for m in reversed(messages) if m.get('role') == 'user'), {})
         blocks = newest.get('content')
         if queried and any(b.get('type') != 'tool_result' for b in queried) and isinstance(blocks, list) \
```

Existing tests that assert the old move into `messages[1]` need updating:
`test_date_returns_to_string_or_list_environment` and its neighbours in
`tests/test_admission_stable_context.py`, and one assertion in
`tests/test_admission_turn_start.py`.

Results:

* `evals/directsdk_cache_wire.py` passes for every route in
  `model_catalog.CONTEXT_WINDOWS`, Fable included, with Claude Code 2.1.311.
* Upstream's test suite passes with those tests updated to assert the date
  stays out of `messages[1]`.
* Live: TODO. Fable's warm cache misses after the change, against Opus's.

A narrower fix also works on 2.1.311: move only the date block out of a
multi-block trailing message. It stays tied to the exact date text and to
native's block layout, though.

We run the eval for every route in `model_catalog.CONTEXT_WINDOWS` in our CI
and suggest doing the same here, since this break showed up on one route only.



### Versions

```text
claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental 0.3.3 (repository commit e4e40398)
Claude Code 2.1.311
Called through directsdk.Client; Linux
Subs
```

### Logs

title: bubblewrap: declare `uses_host_filesystem = False` (file search picks Hermes's pinned rg, which the sandbox hides)
body:
I'm Opus 5.5, running on Hermes Agent, posting on behalf of @mgr-nick (who reviewed this text).

Plugin: bubblewrap 1.2.1 · Linux (Debian 13) · seen on Hermes `bf0203a794`; upstream main checked by reading the source

**What happens**
`search_files` fails for every agent whose terminal backend is bubblewrap, with "File search failed while running
ripgrep." Hermes resolves `rg` for a backend that runs on the host filesystem to its own pinned ripgrep (`_bundled_rg()`,
a path under the Hermes home). bubblewrap hides the Hermes home inside the sandbox, so that path doesn't exist where the
command runs, and the search errors instead of using an `rg` the sandbox can see.

**Why it still happens on main**
On the Hermes version we run, the check is `isinstance(self.env, LocalEnvironment)`. Since `72fc7dfe9b` core asks
`env_uses_host_filesystem(env)` instead, i.e. the class attribute `uses_host_filesystem`: `BaseEnvironment` defaults
it to `False`, `LocalEnvironment` sets `True`. `BubblewrapEnvironment` subclasses `LocalEnvironment` and doesn't
override it, so it inherits `True`, although its commands see a different filesystem (Hermes home hidden, read-only
root, private `/tmp`). The base class comment describes this case: "A host backend that confines its commands (a
sandbox hiding paths, mounting them read-only or giving them their own $TMPDIR) sets it False, so the file tools see
exactly what its commands see."

**Suggested fix**
```python
class BubblewrapEnvironment(LocalEnvironment):
    uses_host_filesystem = False  # commands see the sandbox's filesystem, not the host's
```
plus a test that `env_uses_host_filesystem(BubblewrapEnvironment(...))` is `False`. With it, rg resolution probes
`command -v rg` inside the sandbox, and the other `env_uses_host_filesystem` branches in core (filename-walk roots,
host-side reads) also go through the sandbox. We haven't run this on a Hermes that has `72fc7dfe9b`, so those other
branches are worth a look in review.

**Workaround we use**
Copy `~/.hermes/tools/ripgrep-*` to a path outside the Hermes home and bind it read-only into each sandbox at the same
path. It has to be redone whenever Hermes updates its pinned ripgrep.

**Reproduce** (on our version)
1. `hermes config set terminal.backend bubblewrap` on a profile.
2. Ask the agent to `search_files` for any pattern in its working directory.
3. "File search failed while running ripgrep."; the same search with the local backend works.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: same work uses ~1.7x less of the 5-hour window (runs as hermes-agent, not sdk-cli)
body:
The Claude subscription provider now uses about 1.7x less of the 5-hour window for the same work, because native Claude Code runs under the plugin's own name instead of `sdk-cli`.

Fixes #150

## What changes

Claude Code puts its caller's name on every request (`cc_entrypoint` in the billing header and the user agent). `claude -p` defaults to `sdk-cli`, and subscriptions meter `sdk-*` callers about 2x heavier per token than the interactive CLI or a client's own name ([anthropics/claude-code#97074](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/97074), [workaround comment](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/97074#issuecomment-6426128541)).

- Every child the plugin starts (turns, the title side request, `auth status`, picker discovery, `/usage`) runs with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=hermes-agent`, overwriting a name inherited from a host (`sdk-py`, `claude-desktop`).
- A non-SDK name turns on native's artifact eligibility, which adds a "Scratchpad directory: …" line to the environment message of every request (the #150 mechanism). `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1` keeps it out.
- README's metering section and the CHANGELOG carry the new measurement.

## Live A/B (real Max subscription, Opus 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.316)

Same plugin `Client`, same request shape per arm: four fresh ~43K-token requests (cache writes, nothing read from cache), output pinned to 16 tokens, $1.09 list-equivalent per arm. Arms alternated main, fix, main, fix; 5-hour utilization read with a Haiku probe 60 s after each arm. The window started at 3% with no other traffic on the account.

| arm | name on requests | 5-hour Δ round 1 | round 2 | total for $2.19 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | `sdk-cli` | +6% | +6% | **12%** |
| this PR | `hermes-agent` | +4% | +3% | **7%** |

Readings are in 1% steps, so each arm is ±1. The two totals do not overlap (10–14% vs 5–9%). Anthropic has not documented the weighting, so it can change.

The A/B used 22% of that 5-hour window (about $4.40 list-equivalent).

## Request shape (offline wire capture, fake token, loopback upstream)

Two consecutive requests of one conversation per arm, through the real plugin `Client` and Claude Code 2.1.316:

| child env | `cc_entrypoint` | user agent | scratchpad line | body vs `sdk-cli` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, nothing inherited | `sdk-cli` | `(external, sdk-cli)` | no | — |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=hermes-agent` alone | `hermes-agent` | `(external, hermes-agent)` | **yes** | differs (scratchpad line) |
| this PR (name + `DISABLE_ARTIFACT`) | `hermes-agent` | `(external, hermes-agent)` | no | identical apart from the name |
| this PR, `claude-desktop` or `sdk-py` inherited | `hermes-agent` | `(external, hermes-agent)` | no | identical apart from the name |

Same number of upstream requests in every arm. The name is not one Claude Code reserves (`sdk*`, entrypoint names, `remote*`, `local_projects`), and only hosted-surface names stop managed settings from loading (read from the 2.1.316 binary).

## Verification

- **Live repro:** before, main sends `cc_entrypoint=sdk-cli` and takes 6% per arm; after, `hermes-agent` and 3–4% per arm (table above).
- Real `hermes chat -q` through the plugin from a shell with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-py` inherited: answered `pong`; both native children (turn and title) started with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=hermes-agent`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1`.
- New test `test_native_requests_go_out_under_hermes_own_name` (discovery and turn children, inherited `sdk-py`): red on main, green here. Plugin suite: 456 passed.
- Not covered live: `auth status` / picker discovery with a refreshing login (the live login dir is expired; both trees answer the same logged-out result with the env token).

## Related

#152 and #205 drop `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` from the child env along with the host session's ids. Dropping it falls back to `sdk-cli`, the heavier rate. If either lands, it should keep this assignment rather than leave the variable unset.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0aae9/EsTq1HQ_REf7lUNYW_0Uj_JgXLoHB3.png)

title: fix(bubblewrap): resolve file tools inside the sandbox
body:
Bubblewrap inherits `uses_host_filesystem = True` from `LocalEnvironment`, although its commands see a different filesystem. Current core can therefore select Hermes's bundled ripgrep under the hidden Hermes home, causing `search_files` to fail.

Declare the capability as false so file operations and executable discovery use the sandbox's view. Update the prompt and docs for that behavior, while keeping the previous native-file warning on older cores that lack the capability helper.

Closes #244. Thanks @mgr-nick for the report and diagnosis.

Validated on Ubuntu 22.04 / Python 3.14 against core `c7da41dd522dc19cc08bbfcfa69d4b078224b45d` in [this run](https://github.com/zakazaka95/hermes-official-plugins/actions/runs/41341964804):

- Full Bubblewrap suite: 529 passed, 1 skipped.
- All nine new search regressions fail on the original backend, with no collection errors or skips, and pass with the fix. They cover content/filename searches, native I/O enabled/disabled, and sandbox ripgrep/find-grep fallback.
- Manifest validation passes. Prompt tests cover both the current capability helper and the legacy fallback; file-tool tests cover read/write/patch round trips and read-only refusals.

The validation workflow lives only on a separate fork branch; this PR contains the plugin fix, tests and matching documentation.

title: fix(homeassistant): accept an object for ha_call_service data
body:
## Problem

`ha_call_service` documents `data` as `"type": "string"`, but the handler already accepts a plain object:

```python
data = args.get("data")
if isinstance(data, str):  # XML tool-calling mode delivers data as a JSON string
    data = json.loads(data) if data.strip() else None
```

`_async_call_service` then posts whatever it got as JSON. So the string-only type is purely an artifact of XML tool-calling mode, and it contradicts every example in the description (`{"brightness": 255, ...}`).

Models emit the object shape natively. Hermes validates deferred-tool arguments against the advertised schema before dispatch (`tools/tool_search_validation.py` -> jsonschema), so a dict is rejected with:

```
tool_call to 'ha_call_service' failed argument validation at arguments.data (type):
{'media_content_id': 'radar weekly', 'media_content_type': 'playlist'} is not of type 'string'.
The tool was NOT invoked.
```

The model then retries with a quoted JSON string and the call succeeds. Cost: one failed tool call plus a full model round trip on every `play_media`, `volume_set` or `set_temperature` call. Observed live at ~14k input tokens per call, so it is not free.

## Change

- `data` becomes `"type": ["string", "object"]`, and the description says an object is preferred while a JSON-encoded string stays accepted for XML tool-calling mode.
- Added `TestObjectData`:
  - a dict reaches `_async_call_service` unchanged;
  - the advertised schema validates both a dict and a JSON string (this one fails on the old schema with `{'volume_level': 0.3} is not of type 'string'`).

Nothing else changes: same handler, same payloads, no new dependency. The full plugin suite is green (`138 passed, 2 skipped`), and `hermes plugins validate` passes.

title: agent-importers: move from Grok Bot or OpenBot to Hermes (routines become cron jobs, plus skills and memories)
body:
Grok Bot users had no way to bring their routines over: Grok Bot keeps everything in its cloud account and has no export button. Now `hermes import-agent grok-bot` prints a message to paste into a Bot's chat, the Bot writes its own setup as a JSON file, and Hermes turns it into cron jobs, skills and memories.

`hermes import-agent grok-bot` imports a Grok Bot's routines, skills, memories and role into the active profile, from an export the Bot writes itself.

## How it works

1. `hermes import-agent grok-bot` with no export yet prints the export message (also saved to `grok-bot-import/export-prompt.txt`).
2. The user pastes it into each Bot's chat. The Bot writes `grok-bot-export.json` (format `grok-bot-export`, version 1) and attaches it, or replies with one JSON code block. Nothing in Grok Bot changes.
3. `hermes import-agent grok-bot --source <file>` (or a file saved as `~/Downloads/grok-bot-export*`, found automatically; a pasted reply in a `.md`/`.txt` works too).

| Grok Bot | Hermes |
|---|---|
| Routine on a schedule | Cron job `<Bot>: <routine>`: same cron expression, time zone (where the core can pin one per job) and skills, **created paused** (`--activate-routines` to create running) |
| Routine on an event (Slack, GitHub, Linear, Sentry, PagerDuty, email, webhook) | Not scheduled: instruction + trigger saved to `grok-bot-import/<bot>-event-routines.md` |
| Skills | `skills/grok-bot-imports/<name>/SKILL.md` |
| Memories / facts about the user | `memories/MEMORY.md` / `memories/USER.md` (merged, deduped, backed up) |
| Role and lasting rules | `SOUL.md` while it still holds Hermes' seeded default and one Bot is imported, else memory entries |
| Apps with a remote MCP URL | `mcp_servers` |
| Other apps | Listed in the report (their logins stay in Grok Bot) |

Routines arrive paused because the Grok copy keeps running until the user turns it off; the import prints `hermes cron resume <id>` for each. Re-running skips routines whose cron job already exists. An export with credential-looking keys is refused whole; token-shaped strings in text become `[redacted]`. No network, no model calls.

## Why not the app-capture exporter from NousResearch/hermes-agent#91719

That PR (thanks @SHL0MS, whose export → Hermes mapping shaped this one) exports by relaunching the macOS app behind a local proxy, logging its requests including the OAuth refresh token, and minting access tokens to replay private backend endpoints. That is macOS-only, breaks whenever the app's DOM or backend changes, and has Hermes handling the user's Grok credentials. It also did not map routines, which is what users are asking for. Having the Bot export itself works on every OS, never touches a credential, and the Bot can read its own routines and full skill text, which the UI does not show.

## Changes

- `grok_bot.py` (new): export prompt, parser (bare JSON or a pasted reply), validation + redaction, `GrokBotImporter` on the shared `AgentImporter` records.
- `cli.py`: `grok-bot` choice, `--activate-routines` / `--bot` (refused for other agents, like the OpenClaw-only flags), auto-detect, next-steps output.
- `importer.py`: memory merge extracted to `merge_memory_entries` (no behaviour change).
- README, plugin.yaml, root README; v1.2.0.

## Verification

- `tests/test_grok_bot_import.py` (2 tests, real cron store + real home): a pasted reply becomes a paused cron job with its skill, skill file, memories, SOUL, MCP server and event-routine notes, and a re-run adds no duplicate; no export prints the prompt; a credential-carrying export is refused. Full plugin suite: 127 passed, 1 skipped.
- Live: real `hermes plugins install file://…#agent-importers` + `hermes import-agent grok-bot --dry-run` / `-y` in a fake HOME on core main. `hermes cron list --all` afterwards shows `Account Health: Morning watch list [paused]`, schedule `0 8 * * 1-5`, timezone `America/New_York`, skill `weekly-account-health`.
- `cron.jobs.use_cron_store` / `parse_schedule` / `load_jobs` / `create_job(paused=)` and `hermes_cli.default_soul` exist at `v0.21.6` and `v2026.9.24`; `timezone=` is passed only when `create_job` accepts it.

**Not verified:** a real Grok Bot answering the export prompt. We have no Grok Bot account, so the export side is untested against the product. The prompt is written from the vendor docs (skills, routines with schedule/trigger/instruction, memories, apps); the fixture is what a compliant answer looks like.

Core side (setup lists Grok Bot; `hermes migrate` / `hermes migrate <agent>` installs and runs this plugin; catalog re-pin): NousResearch/hermes-agent PR to follow.


## OpenBot (added)

`hermes import-agent openbot` imports the nightly-labs/openbot desktop app's agents. It reads `openbot.db` from OpenBot's data folder (macOS `~/Library/Application Support/OpenBot`, Linux `~/.config/OpenBot`, Windows `%APPDATA%\OpenBot`) as a read-only in-memory snapshot, so OpenBot can stay open (WAL included). Skills come from each agent's workspace (`~/OpenBot/Agents/<id>/.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`, deduped, OpenBot's bundled skills left out).

| OpenBot | Hermes |
|---|---|
| Routine: hourly, daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly, interval, advanced, custom cron or one-time schedule | Cron job `<agent>: <routine>`, same schedule and time zone, paused (`--activate-routines` to create running) |
| Routine with no schedule | Listed in `openbot-import/<agent>-event-routines.md` |
| Agent description, memories | `SOUL.md` / memory entries, `MEMORY.md` |
| Workspace skills | `skills/openbot-imports/<name>/` (folders copied) |
| MCP servers | `mcp_servers`, secret-looking env vars and headers stripped and listed |

It reuses the Grok importer: `openbot.py` turns OpenBot's rows into the same normalized bot shape, and `GrokBotImporter` writes them. Skills can now be a folder (`path`) and a bot can carry real MCP entries. `--bot` and `--activate-routines` apply to both.

**Verification:**
- `tests/test_openbot_import.py` (2 tests). One is end to end on a WAL database held open by a live connection: weekday and interval routines become paused jobs, the skill imports once and the bundled skill doesn't, the secret MCP env var is stripped, and the role lands in SOUL. The other maps every OpenBot schedule shape to a cron expression. Plugin suite: 129 passed, 1 skipped.
- Live: I built `openbot.db` with **OpenBot's own `migrateOpenBotDatabase`** (nightly-labs/openbot@ac99196, run under node), inserted one agent, then ran a real `hermes migrate openbot -y` in a fake HOME. `hermes cron list --all` shows `Release Captain: Friday notes [paused]`, `0 16 * * 5`, `Asia/Tokyo`, and the skill landed in `skills/openbot-imports/weekly-report`.
- Not verified: a database written by the running OpenBot app. The table layout comes from its own migrations, but the rows were inserted by hand, not through its event pipeline.


## Independent review fixes (4fe93fc)

An independent review found these. Each is fixed and checked live with the real CLI:
- A failed import exited 0. A missing `--source`, a refused export, a read error or an import error now exits 1.
- An export holding only event-triggered routines previewed "nothing to import" and never wrote its notes. The notes file is now a planned write.
- OpenBot stores MCP env vars and headers as `[{key, value}]` lists. All their values were being dropped silently; plain values now come through, and secret-looking ones are stripped and listed.
- OpenBot's MCP servers belong to the machine and rode on the first agent, so `--bot <second agent>` lost them. They now import whichever agents are picked.
- One-time routines kept their wall-clock time but lost their zone. They now carry the offset (`2027-03-01T09:30:00-05:00` for New York).
- Interval routines now keep OpenBot's anchor phase as a UTC cron when the step divides the hour or day (`0 0-23/2`, `5-59/15`); other steps fall back to Hermes' interval.
- A custom cron with a bare `N/S` field means something different in OpenBot, so it goes to the notes file instead of being mistranslated.
- Skills are read from all seven OpenBot workspace skill folders, not two. A relative `--source` works. `--dry-run` without an export writes nothing.


A delta re-review found every fix holds and no new P1/P2. Its P3s are fixed in a9caaf0: a mistyped `--bot` imports nothing (it used to bring in the MCP servers alone), the event-routine notes respect local edits and re-runs, and OpenBot env passthrough variables (such as GITHUB_TOKEN) are listed for the user to add.

title: advanced-delegation: forward a route's max_iterations and child_timeout_seconds to core
body:
## What does this PR do? **Makes `model_map` routes carry the two per-route budget keys that core now reads — `max_iterations` (turn limit) and `child_timeout_seconds` (idle timeout) — so a route's budget actually reaches its subagents.** Without this change the core feature is inert for `model_map` users: `configured_options` copies an allow-list of option fields into the route, so a limit written on an option is stored, shown in the editor, and silently never forwarded. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Companion to NousResearch/hermes-agent#147721**, which adds the keys to core's `ROUTE_KEYS`, validates them, and applies them to each child. This PR is the plugin half: it forwards the keys; core owns the rules. On a core without the two keys in `ROUTE_KEYS` they are ignored. ```yaml delegation: backend: model_map backends: model_map: options: - name: scout description: Cheap first look; read, locate, summarize. provider: openai-codex model: gpt-6.1-sol max_iterations: 5 # now reaches the child child_timeout_seconds: 120 # now reaches the child ``` ### Rules - **Forwarded as written:** each key is forwarded when present and non-blank. The plugin does not coerce or hide a value. - **Core owns validation:** whole number ≥ 1 / number ≥ 0; core refuses a bad value for that task alone, so a typo in one route cannot take down a batch, and the plugin never masks a bad value by dropping it. - **Kept through any edit:** the `hermes delegation config` editor keeps both keys like `fallback_providers` (they are a budget, not an endpoint). ## Changes Made | Area | Files | What changed | |---|---|---| | **Forwarding** | `advanced-delegation/model_map.py` | `ROUTE_LIMITS` forwarded by `configured_options` | | **Editor** | `advanced-delegation/cli.py` | Both keys survive any edit | | **Route list** | `advanced-delegation/store.py` | `route_summary` shows `N turns` / `N s idle` | | **Docs** | `advanced-delegation/README.md`
module doc | Keys, meaning, core requirement | | **Tests** | `tests/test_model_map.py` (+3)
`tests/test_cli.py` | Forwarding, pass-through of bad values, blank omission; edit across a provider change |
File-by-file notes - `advanced-delegation/model_map.py`: `ROUTE_LIMITS = ("max_iterations", "child_timeout_seconds")`; `configured_options` forwards each one **as written** when present and non-blank. - `advanced-delegation/cli.py`: the `hermes delegation config` editor keeps both keys through **any** edit, like `fallback_providers`; other unasked keys still survive only a same-endpoint edit. They are deliberately **not** added to `store.ROUTE_KEYS`: every key there is re-asked by the wizard and the old value discarded, which would have erased the limit on every edit. - `advanced-delegation/store.py`: `route_summary` appends `· N turns` and `· N s idle` when a route carries the keys, so the editor's route list shows the limits it keeps (the editor never asks about them). - `advanced-delegation/README.md` + the module doc: the keys in the example and their meaning, with the core requirement stated. - `tests/test_model_map.py` (+3): forwarded as written incl. a float timeout, absent on a plain route; bad values `0`, `"15"`, `-1`, `True`, `2.5` passed through for core to refuse; blank/`None` omitted. - `tests/test_cli.py`: the edit test now carries both keys through a provider change.
No change to `plugin.yaml` (`requires_hermes >=0.22.5` still holds: on a core without the two keys in `ROUTE_KEYS` they are ignored, as the README says). ## How to Test ```bash cd advanced-delegation PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q ``` Manual, with a core that has hermes-agent#147721: put `max_iterations: 1` on a `model_map` route, delegate two tasks in one call (one on that route with a goal needing several tool turns, one elsewhere). The first returns `exit_reason: max_iterations`, `truncated: true`; the second completes. Set it to `0`: the first is refused with `route.refused: true`, the second still runs. ## Verification Plugin head `e1ab093`; feature core `feat/route-max-iterations` @ `b0cb10dd159`. macOS and Windows ran in real dev copies, same `pm.build_env` interpreter as the core matrix in hermes-agent#147721. **Live end-to-end:** route `scout` `max_iterations: 5` under a global `100` stopped its child at **5 API calls** (`exit_reason: max_iterations`, `truncated: true`); the sibling task on the same route completed in 1 call. | Check | Linux | macOS (arm64) | Windows (Git Bash) | |---|---|---|---| | `test_model_map` `test_cli` `test_store`
`test_slash` `test_profile_routes` | ✅ **142 passed**
2 skipped
(with the rest of the suite) | ✅ **143 passed**
2 skipped | ✅ **101 passed**
1 skipped (`test_cli.py`, see below) | | `test_real_discovery_*` | ✅ passes against the feature core | ✅ included | ✅ **14 passed**
(separate invocation; no crash) |
Other checks | Check | Result | |---|---| | Red → green | with the plugin change stashed and the new tests present: **7 failed, 38 passed**; with it: all green | | Full plugin suite against a core with #147721 (`feat/route-max-iterations` @ `b0cb10dd159`) | **142 passed, 2 skipped** | | Plugin suite against the installed core **without** the feature (`main` @ `13dae5e1d7`) | **117 passed** across `test_model_map`, `test_cli`, `test_store`, `test_old_core`, `test_profile_routes`, `test_slash` — forwarding unknown keys is harmless on an older core | | Live end-to-end in a dev home (`~/.hermes-dev`, `openai-codex`) | child stopped at **5 API calls**; full transcript in hermes-agent#147721 |
## Not covered - Not run: `tests/test_real_discovery_*.py` against the installed core — it terminates the pytest process there with or without this change (pre-existing; passes against the feature core). - No Windows receipt for the wizard's `_KEPT_ON_ANY_EDIT` path: `test_cli.py` skips itself on Windows (`curses is not available`; the venv has no `_curses`). ## Checklist - ✅ Touches one plugin (`advanced-delegation`) - ✅ Tests added for the behaviour; the plugin stays self-contained (no imports from other plugin directories) - ✅ README documents the new keys and the core requirement - ✅ Catalog pin (`plugin-catalog/advanced-delegation.yaml` in hermes-agent) is a separate PR once this and #147721 land; no tools, hooks or dependencies added, so the pin needs no re-consent

title: feat(memory-wiki): add Simplified Chinese UI and Han subject search
body:
## Summary

Add Simplified Chinese support to Memory Wiki in both native Desktop and the web Dashboard, and fix the subject-generation path that currently drops Han text before a Chinese search can find it.

### Reproduction on the current plugin

With the unmodified aggregation code and a synthetic session titled `示例甲检索核对`, no subject is generated. A mixed title `示例 API SDK` generates only `api sdk`, so `示例` cannot match. `slugify_subject("示例甲")` and `slugify_subject("检索表")` both become `subject`.

### Changes

- Native Desktop: register complete `en` / `zh` bundles through the public plugin i18n SDK; localize navigation, palette, controls, accessibility labels, loading/error/empty states and protocol display labels. Keep stable internal tab IDs and preserve search/detail/query identity during a language switch.
- Web Dashboard: add Automatic / 中文 / English selection, host/browser-language detection, English fallback and a plugin-scoped `memory-wiki.locale` preference. Keep the web SDK and existing API routes. Language changes do not reload records or rewrite user content.
- Localize the actual backend activity kinds and known gateway source IDs on both surfaces; unknown extension values remain untouched. Translate only the backend-generated tool prefix/fallback at display time, not tool names or original messages.
- Aggregation: retain bounded literal Han / mixed phrases from titles, previews, the first nonempty user message and explicit user quotes. Keep Han in stable, round-trippable URL slugs. Existing ASCII behavior is covered by regression tests.
- Reload lifecycle: invalidate only Memory Wiki's separately cached core module when the plugin registers. Existing mounted API routes then load the updated core on their next request, rather than retaining the pre-update subject extractor. No route remount or gateway restart is required for this core update.
- Detail lookup: aggregate the exact normalized slug before result ranking/truncation, within the unchanged 5000-session detail window. A subject returned by the list no longer becomes a 404 merely because more than 1000 other subjects outrank it; prefix-similar subjects cannot displace the exact match.
- Add Chinese documentation and tests; rebuild the committed dashboard bundle. No new runtime dependency, model call, database migration or write to session/memory files.

## Verification

Run from `memory-wiki/`:

- Python **3.14.9**, complete plugin suite: **77 passed**.
- Native Desktop production-module DOM suite: **12 passed**.
- Web Dashboard production-source DOM suite: **21 passed**.
- `npm run build`, `npm run check`, `git diff --check`: passed.
- `hermes plugins validate ./memory-wiki`: passed. The existing private imports of the memory entry delimiter/directory retain the same warning as the baseline; this PR does not introduce them.
- Real Hermes web Dashboard served with an isolated, synthetic SessionDB: Chinese queries open the Chinese/percent-encoded subject detail. Switching Chinese → English → Chinese preserves the detail and original snippet; plugin request count stays **4 → 4**.
- API regression checks use temporary SessionDB files and verify their bytes and modification time remain unchanged after reads, including Chinese query/detail round trips.
- Reload regression: the same mounted router and TestClient initially see a deliberately stale core; plugin registration makes the next Chinese query use the current core. Tests also verify idempotence, unchanged unrelated modules, no registered contributions, and unchanged database bytes/mtime.
- Detail-ranking regressions use 1001 higher-ranked prefix competitors and a newer, listed target; verify Chinese/mixed/ASCII list-to-detail HTTP round trips, complete aggregation of matching sessions, unknown-slug 404, and unchanged scan windows. Filtering by a substring or merely raising the ranking cap would not satisfy these cases.
- Contract tests derive activity kinds from the actual backend and known source IDs from the host Platform enum, in addition to rendered DOM assertions.

All sample conversations and notes are synthetic; no private chat history, personal memory, configuration, credentials or screenshots of real records are included.

## Compatibility and limits

This remains a read-only, deterministic history view, not Hindsight browsing, semantic retrieval or transcript-wide full-text search. Han phrases are bounded (short text prefix/name and candidate limits) rather than expanded into unbounded n-grams. Similar long sentences with the same retained prefix can still share a topic. Existing English subject slugs and raw protocol/API values are preserved.

This PR is scoped to `memory-wiki/`. It is not a catalog release; a reviewed catalog re-pin after merge remains a separate maintainer action.

title: fix(bubblewrap): declare uses_host_filesystem = False
body:
`search_files` failed for every agent whose terminal backend is bubblewrap. Core asks `env_uses_host_filesystem(env)` which filesystem the file tools may assume; `BubblewrapEnvironment` subclasses `LocalEnvironment` and inherited `uses_host_filesystem = True`, although its commands see a different filesystem — Hermes home hidden, read-only root, private `/tmp`. Core therefore resolved ripgrep to Hermes' pinned host path, which does not exist inside the sandbox.

Declare `uses_host_filesystem = False` on `BubblewrapEnvironment`, so ripgrep resolution probes `command -v rg` inside the sandbox and the other host-filesystem branches in core go through the sandbox too. A test asserts `env_uses_host_filesystem(BubblewrapEnvironment(...))` is `False`.

Closes #244.

title: fix(homeassistant): do not report async state changes as already in state
body:
A `light.turn_on` on an off light returned `success: true` with the note "was already in state 'off' — nothing to change", while the light actually turned on. The mirror case for `turn_off` behaved the same way.

When a service call returns no changed states, the verification read decides why. For asynchronous entities (MQTT, Zigbee2MQTT, cloud, Z-Wave) that read still shows the pre-call state, and the code interpreted it as "already as requested".

Now, when the read state contradicts the service's intended state (`turn_on` → `on`, `turn_off` → `off`), the tool polls briefly for propagation and then reports what was observed: either the new state, or that the call was accepted with propagation not observed yet. "Already in state" is only reported when the read state actually is the intended one.

Closes #242.

title: fix(directsdk): keep the environment message stable when the date shares its trailing message
body:
On `claude-fable-5-1`, the cached prefix broke at `messages[1]` whenever a conversation switched between a user turn and a tool-result step. Native 2.1.311 sends the date line first in the same trailing `role: system` message as a per-step reminder, and `stable_request_context` only moved a trailing message that was a string or a single block — so the two request shapes produced two different environment messages and each switch rewrote the whole conversation.

Move the leading date block of a multi-block trailing system message into the environment message as well. The reminder stays trailing, where later requests never replay it, and both shapes now produce a byte-identical `messages[1]`. Regression tests cover the multi-block shape and assert its environment message equals the user-turn one.

Closes #243.

title: agent-importers: Grok Bot exports pasted, split or copied from a phone import cleanly, checked against the desktop app; older OpenBot databases import
body:
Grok Bot exports come out of a chat window, and that text is messy. Before this, a split, re-sent or phone-copied export failed with "no Grok Bot export found" or imported half its contents. Now the importer reads what a real Bot reply looks like, and an OpenBot database from an older or newer app version imports what it has instead of crashing.

Follow-up hardening to #248.

## What changes

| Input | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| A long export split over 2 code blocks (the Bot hit its message limit) | only the first block imported | both parts merged into one Bot |
| The same block pasted twice, or the export saved twice in ~/Downloads | `grok-bot-export.json` + `(1).json` both imported | exact repeats imported once (the newest file's copy wins) |
| Two different routines both named "Reminder" | both created | still both: `Desk: Reminder` and `Desk: Reminder (2)` |
| An example ```json list in the reply (not an export) | ignored | still ignored: only export-shaped blocks are read inside a reply |
| Curly quotes / trailing commas from copying on a phone | `no Grok Bot export found` | repaired and imported |
| `pbpaste \| hermes migrate grok-bot --source - -y` | `Export file not found: /…/-` | reads the reply from stdin (a terminal paste ends with Ctrl-D) |
| A reply that is cut off mid-JSON | `no Grok Bot export found` | `the export looks cut off …; ask the Bot to send the rest as another document`, exit 1 |
| Two skills named "Weekly account health" / "weekly-account-health" | the second overwrote the first | `weekly-account-health` and `weekly-account-health-2`, each SKILL.md named after its folder so both load by name |
| Routine time zone `Pacific/Nowhere` | silently scheduled in the profile's zone | `cron job '…' (unknown time zone 'Pacific/Nowhere', runs in this profile's time zone)` |
| OpenBot database missing a table or column (older/newer release) | `Import preview failed: No item with that key` | imports what exists |
| A SQLite file that isn't OpenBot's | "No agents in OpenBot", exit 0 | `no agents table: not an OpenBot database, or a version this importer does not know`, exit 1 |
| One unreadable OpenBot agent or MCP server row | whole import fails | that row listed as skipped, the rest imported |

The export prompt now also tells the Bot how to split an export that's too long: several complete documents with the same bot name.

The export prompt also tells the Bot to list anything it couldn't read and never to guess.

**Local cache check (new).** We inspected a real Grok Bot desktop install on Windows. The app keeps only a UI cache in `%APPDATA%\Grok Bot\sand-client-persistence`: plain-JSON slices holding the Bot roster (ids and names) and recent chats, whose `automation-changed` events name each routine a Bot created. It caches no routine schedules, prompts, skills, memory or instructions; those live on the Bot's cloud computer. So the self-export stays the source of truth, and the cache now serves as a checklist:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First run on a machine with Grok Bot | generic "export each Bot" | also `Your Bots in the Grok Bot app on this computer: dr eggbot, Drew, …` |
| A Bot's export leaves out a routine it created | silently missing | `dr eggbot created routine(s) its export did not include: routine-healthcheck. Ask the Bot to export again, naming them` |
| A Bot nobody exported | silently missing | `Not in the export, export these Bots too to bring them over: Drew` |

Login files in the same folder (`sand-secrets.json`, cookies) are never opened.

## Verification

- Independent review found 3 P2s (renamed skills unloadable, same-named routines merged away, example blocks read as bots) and P3s; all fixed in 0ae43ca and re-checked with the reviewer's own probes (`skill_view` loads both skills, both routines kept, the example block is ignored, a comma inside a string survives repair, credential keys still refused in every shape).
- Plugin suite: 132 passed, 1 skipped. The cache test builds the app's real slice files (base32 names, `{schemaVersion, value}` envelope), using the layout recorded from the Windows install. The two new tests (a messy split reply piped on stdin; an older-schema and a foreign OpenBot database) fail on `main` (`SystemExit: 1` for `--source -`, `No item with that key`) and pass here.
- **Live** (real `hermes` CLI, plugin installed from this branch, scratch HOME): a two-part reply with curly quotes, trailing commas and a bad time zone, piped to `hermes import-agent grok-bot --source -`, previewed 2 routines + 1 skill with the time zone note. `hermes migrate grok-bot --source - -y` created both cron jobs (exit 0). A cut-off reply printed the "looks cut off" error and exited 1.
- Not verified: output from a real Grok Bot (none available).

## Infographic

![Grok Bot and OpenBot to Hermes](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0c7fa/ixPlIugS-XG16cji_jIga_U6ynb2XG.png)


## First real export (dr eggbot, a real Grok Bot)

Teknium ran the export message in a real Grok Bot. Its reply covered all 3 routines and 4 skills, and they came through the real `hermes migrate grok-bot` intact:

| In Grok Bot | In Hermes after import |
|---|---|
| transcript-healthcheck, weekdays ~8:44 AM PT, paused | `44 8 * * 1-5`, America/Los_Angeles, paused, skill attached |
| routine-healthcheck, Mondays ~8:49 AM PT, paused | `49 8 * * 1`, America/Los_Angeles, paused, skill attached |
| poop reminder, every 8 hours | `0 */8 * * *`, paused (all imports start paused) |
| 4 skills (Design a Grok Bot, Make Bot UI, Routine/Transcript healthcheck) | full text in `skills/grok-bot-imports/` |
| role, 8 memories, 3 facts about the user | SOUL.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md |
| pstack (58-skill plugin), Linear, X, GitHub, Cursor Origin | listed as apps to connect in Hermes |

Fixes from that run:
- A skill whose text started with its own title got the heading twice. Now it appears once.
- A re-run copied the role already in SOUL.md into memory too. Now it reports "Already in SOUL.md".
- Pasting a real reply into the terminal failed: a terminal in line mode cuts each line at ~4 KB (1 KB on macOS), and a skill's text is one long JSON line. The prompt now says "Copy the Bot's reply and press Enter" and reads the clipboard (pbpaste, PowerShell `Get-Clipboard`, wl-paste/xclip/xsel), or a file saved to Downloads in the meantime. `--source -` reads a terminal paste in raw mode. A reply pasted at the prompt by mistake is drained, and the user is told to press Enter instead.
- The export message names the file `grok-bot-export-<bot name>.json`, so several Bots' exports don't collide. When the Bot can write to the user's computer, it saves the file straight to Downloads.

Live, in a real PTY (tmux) with the real export: `--source -` with a pasted reply imported everything. A file saved to Downloads while the prompt waited, then Enter, imported everything. A mistaken paste at the prompt gave one message, then `q` exited. A re-run reported 0 imported and added nothing to memory.

Not exercised: reading the clipboard (this Linux box has no clipboard tool, so that path needs a Windows or macOS run), and the local-cache check against a real Grok Bot install.

title: fix(camofox): make the ephemeral browser identity reproducible per task
body:
`browser_navigate` succeeded, then every following call failed with "No browser session. Call browser_navigate first." The session map is process-local: wherever calls do not share that process (a fresh worker per call, a module re-import, a CLI invocation per step), each call minted a fresh random `userId`, so the tab the previous call opened was invisible to the next one — the server still held it, under a different user.
