Derive the ephemeral `userId` from `(state dir, task_id)` instead of `uuid4`, so every call in the same task resolves to the same browser user, and allow tab adoption for that reproducible identity (with `browser.camofox.adopt_existing_tab: true` / `CAMOFOX_ADOPT_EXISTING_TAB=1`). Unkeyed calls keep a random id, so they never collapse onto one shared profile, and the ephemeral branch stays isolated per task — unlike managed persistence, which shares one profile-scoped identity and cookie jar across tasks.

Closes #215.

title: fix(directsdk): make eager tool-input streaming opt-in
body:
Since the relay began setting `eager_input_streaming` on every tool, complete `tool_use` replies whose streamed arguments are not valid JSON fail the turn with `error_max_turns` — deterministically, on every retry. The API does not validate streamed tool arguments, so a call the model meant to make is lost; the same input succeeds with the flag off. Reports cover both long Opus conversations and short Sonnet ones, so a context-size gate would not cover it.

Gate the flag behind `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_EAGER_INPUT_STREAMING` (declared in `plugin.yaml` `optional_env`). It stays available for the long-write stall case it was added for, and a value native already set still wins.

Closes #221.

title: feat(directsdk): explicit upstream opt-in for organizational gateways
body:
An organization routing model traffic through an internal gateway (access control, user attribution, observability, policy) while preserving the native subscription OAuth bearer had no supported path: DirectSDK correctly rejects an inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, and the Admission relay then always used `https://api.anthropic.com`.

Add `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_UPSTREAM` as the one explicit opt-in for selecting a trusted organizational gateway, declared in `plugin.yaml` `optional_env`. The generic guard is unchanged and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is never read as an upstream, so an accidentally inherited value still cannot redirect native credentials. The value is validated by `Admission` as before: HTTPS (loopback HTTP only for fixtures), no userinfo, query, or fragment. Gateway-specific authentication stays separate, e.g. through `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, and the native `Authorization` header stays the only bearer forwarded.

## Rebased onto current main

This branch was opened on 2026-11-02 and had not been touched since, so its CI result was nine days
stale. It is now rebased onto current `main`, where the picker handshake had been rewritten
(first-party direct) in the meantime, so the one-line upstream change is re-applied to that code
rather than to the older function it originally patched.

The plugin's relay fixtures named their peer through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, which the relay no longer
reads as an upstream, so they now name it through the plugin's own variable. The refusal tests (an
inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `gateway.example.com`) and the fake native's reads of the
plugin-injected relay URL are unchanged.

## Testing

`claude-subscription-directsdk`: 505 passed, 15 skipped against current `hermes-agent` core. The one
remaining failure (`test_blocked_stdin_has_deadline_and_cancellation[True]`, a 0.53 s vs 0.3 s timing
bound) fails identically on `origin/main`, so it is not this PR.

title: fix(directsdk): /usage shows plan limits with claude_code_telemetry off
body:
With `claude_code_telemetry: false`, `/usage` (and any `fetch_account_usage` caller) always comes back empty: the plugin sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` on the usage probe too, and the CLI skips its `get_usage` fetch under that flag (`rate_limits: null`). The current code already names this as the reason, so the behaviour is known; this PR makes the quiet setting stop blinding `/usage` instead.

The probe is the one place where the user explicitly asked for a network read: it is zero-inference and runs behind the unused admission gate. So for this spawn only:

- `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` is dropped
- `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` and `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING` stay on, as do `ALWAYS_QUIET`
- a flag the user exported in Hermes' own environment is kept (as `apply_traffic_policy` promises), and the reason now names that variable

Checked on Claude Code 2.1.301 with a real subscription login: quiet set as before → `rate_limits: null`; same set without the one flag → `five_hour` / `seven_day` windows returned.

Tests: `test_quiet_mode_says_why_limits_are_missing` becomes `test_quiet_mode_still_fetches_limits` (asserts the flag is absent, the other two are set, the gate is used), plus `test_a_user_exported_quiet_flag_is_kept_and_named`. `tests/test_directsdk_account_usage.py` passes. Locally two unrelated tests fail with and without this change against my older core (`test_host_streaming.py::test_profile_routes_through_host_streaming`, and `test_refusal_after_a_tool_call_reaches_the_user` hangs), so CI is the real check for the rest.

title: feat(accent-picker): persist chosen accent as user theme
body:
## What
The Accent Picker currently treats the chosen colour as scratch state only: it uses `setAccentOverride`, which is explicitly non-persisted and cleared on plugin dispose/reload. This means the accent reverts to the theme default every time Hermes restarts or the session changes.

## Fix
Switch the picker from `setAccentOverride` to the existing `persistAccent` helper, which installs the retinted palette as a real user theme instead of a transient override. Reset paths (button + palette command) also clear through `persistAccent(null)`.

## Follow-up
This plugin-side change requires the matching SDK export in hermes-agent (see the linked PR). Once both land, the accent survives reloads and restarts without extra user action.

title: Feature: unified backend — combine model_map and profile_routes in one delegate_task call
body:
## Problem

The plugin enforces one backend at a time: `model_map` or `profile_routes`. That breaks down the moment you have two providers with different auth.

I have one provider on an API key (several models) and another on OAuth (a Docker-contained profile). I want cheap lookups on the first provider's small model, research on its long-context model, and coding on the second provider's frontier model in a contained profile, all from the same session, routed per subtask.

Today I can't. `model_map` covers the first provider's models but can't reach the second (different auth). `profile_routes` covers the second provider but locks each profile to one model, so I'd need throwaway profiles just to switch models on a single key.

## Use case

```python
delegate_task(tasks=[
  {"goal": "summarize this", "option": "cheap"},      # small model on provider A
  {"goal": "research this", "option": "research"},     # long-context model on provider A
  {"goal": "refactor this", "option": "code"},         # frontier model on provider B (Docker)
])
```

## Proposal

Let a `model_map` route resolve to a profile instead of just a model+provider. Or let both `option` and `profile` coexist on `delegate_task`. Either way, one config spans providers and profiles.

## Alternatives considered

- Create a lightweight profile per model on provider A. Works but is config bloat for models sharing one key.
- Switch backends per session. Not possible; backend loads at session start.

## Context

Plugin SHA: e404b68. Hermes 0.22.5. Related: PR #136 (design decision 2.2), [hermes-agent #144070](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/144070) (separate selector model for routing).

title: langfuse: default environment to active profile name
body:
Under a multiplexed gateway, every profile's traces land under `environment="default"`. The plugin defaults `environment` to the empty string, and the Langfuse SDK falls back to `"default"` for empty values. All profiles end up in one bucket in the Langfuse UI.

`_default_environment()` calls `get_active_profile_name()`, which reads the `HERMES_HOME` override set by the gateway's `_profile_runtime_scope`. It runs at client construction time (first LLM call), so it works for resumed sessions too. An `on_session_start`-based approach does not work because that hook only fires for new sessions, not resumed ones.

The `"custom"` return value (unrecognized `HERMES_HOME`) is treated as unset, since bucketing under `"custom"` is worse than letting the SDK default to `"default"`.

An explicit `HERMES_LANGFUSE_ENV` / `LANGFUSE_ENV` secret still takes precedence, so operators who set a custom environment tag are unaffected.

Tested on a multiplexed gateway with 9 profiles. Before: all traces under `environment=default`. After: traces tagged with the profile name (`new-regolo`, `parents`, etc.).

title: memory-wiki: include hidden sessions; bucket day logs by message date
body:
Two gaps that show up when a profile uses long-lived chats (e.g. a per-profile Bot Chat that receives new messages every day):

1. **Hidden sessions never appear.** `_load_memory_sessions` calls `list_sessions_rich` without `include_hidden`, so hidden sessions are absent from Subjects, Daily logs and Recent sessions. Now passes `include_hidden=True` (archived stays excluded), with a `TypeError` fallback for hosts whose `list_sessions_rich` predates the kwarg.
2. **Daily logs bucket a whole session under its start date.** A session active for weeks shows all its activity on day one and nothing after. `build_daily_logs` now groups each session's messages by message timestamp; the session is listed under every day it had activity, with that day's messages, subjects and work items only. Single-day sessions produce the same output as before.

Tests: added cases for a hidden session, a two-day session, and an unchanged single-day session. README notes the behaviour.

Checked against real profiles (up to ~3.3k sessions / 2.8 GB `state.db`): a day page loads in 0.2–2.8 s and the overview in 0.5–5 s.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] feat(directsdk): list the account's own models; pin Mythos 5.1 as access-gated
body:
## Summary

- **The picker lists the account's own models.** Claude Code serves an account's model catalog only when it talks to Anthropic directly. Behind any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, the discovery relay included, it logs `[servedCatalog] off (not_first_party)` and answers a generic list. So an account entitled to Mythos 5.1 never saw it, and older models the account still runs (Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Fable 5) were missing too. The `initialize` handshake now runs without the relay. It writes only `initialize` and no user turn, so it sends no Messages request. An inherited auth or backend override (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry) keeps the handshake behind the relay.
- **Mythos 5.1 is pinned as an access-gated route.** It's available only to organizations Anthropic verifies ([Mythos 5.1](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/mythos-5-1/overview): 1M context, thinking adaptive and always on). It gets its window, thinking policy and capabilities like any pinned route, but a new `ACCESS_GATED` set keeps it out of `fallback_models` and out of the rows discovery appends from the catalog. Only an account whose own picker offers it sees it. `AGENTS.md`'s model checklist now covers gated models, so pinning can't reveal one to everyone.
- **The Fable usage-credits note follows Anthropic's plan rule for Fable 5 and 5.1** ([Fable on your plan](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964)): shown on Pro, not on Max or Ultra (it was shown on Ultra). On Team and Enterprise it reads `usage credits on standard seats`, because the handshake names the plan, not the seat tier, and premium seats include Fable.
- **Labels follow the served catalog's shape** (the model is in `displayName`; `description` is a tagline) as well as the generic one.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Account entitled to Mythos | not listed; typed id runs at 200K, no vision, reasoning-off 400s once then retries | listed as `claude-mythos-5-1[1m]` "Mythos 5.1", 1M, vision, reasoning-off sends `effort: low` |
| Account without Mythos | not listed | not listed (pinned, but never appended or in the fallback list) |
| CLI missing, logged out, or handshake failed | pinned catalog | pinned catalog without gated routes |
| Inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` / API key / cloud backend | generic list via relay | unchanged: generic list via relay |
| Fable 5.1 on Ultra | `usage credits` | no note |
| Fable 5 on Pro (now listed) | not listed | `usage credits` |

## Request accounting

Without the relay nothing counts the handshake's upstream calls, so first-party rows report `upstream_requests: None` (unobserved) instead of a counted zero. The relayed path still counts. On Claude Code 2.1.316 the handshake's debug log shows only its bootstrap, MCP-directory and telemetry fetches. The request path is unchanged and stays behind the admission relay.

## Test plan

- [x] `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=~/.hermes/hermes-agent python -m pytest -q`: 463 passed, 9 subtests passed (Linux).
- [x] New tests fail on `main` and pass here: an entitled account sees Mythos from the served picker; an account without it does not, though the route is pinned; the fallback list excludes it; an inherited base URL keeps discovery behind the relay and counted; the Fable rule across Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise, including a served Fable 5 row with no billing text.
- [x] Live on Claude Code 2.1.316 (Ultra account): the picker lists `claude-mythos-5-1[1m]` "Mythos 5.1" with no `unpinned` note; native reports `contextWindow: 1000000` for that route behind the relay; a reasoning-off Mythos request sends `effort: low` and completes with one upstream request.
- [x] Live Hermes agent turn with the branch plugin installed into a temporary `HERMES_HOME`: `claude-mythos-5-1[1m]` with reasoning off, one image and one `read_file` call. It streamed, answered correctly (file contents plus both shapes), took 2 API calls, and hit no thinking-disable 400.
- [ ] macOS and Windows: not run locally; CI covers them.
- [ ] Team or Enterprise account wording: not checked against a real account.

## Notes

- Mythos's minimum Claude Code version isn't documented; the README says it is qualified on 2.1.316.
- Hermes core's `_MANDATORY_THINKING_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS` gets the matching `claude-mythos` entry in NousResearch/hermes-agent#148127.
- After merge, the catalog pin in `NousResearch/hermes-agent:plugin-catalog/claude-subscription-directsdk.yaml` needs to move to the new SHA (AGENTS.md "Pin bump").


## Review follow-ups

BearHuddleston's review, addressed in new commits:
- `7bc684b` fix(directsdk): treat the whole Mythos family as mandatory-thinking. `claude-mythos-5` no longer receives `thinking: disabled`; the entry matches core's `claude-mythos` (NousResearch/hermes-agent#148127), and the reasoning-off test covers Mythos 5.
- `0ae4af3` fix(directsdk): keep the version in a generic-list 1M row's label. `Opus (1M context)` no longer counts as versioned, so the label falls back to `Opus 5.5 with 1M context`; a one-row test pins it.

Plugin suite on the new head: 464 passed, 9 subtests passed (Linux). Each new test fails on its parent commit.

## Infographic

![your-accounts-models](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab0e521/IoU1-cq0lTvKt2YoCoytt_ub1BgZTI.png)

title: [agent-importers] Grok Bot: imported routines run, but their output lands nowhere the user looks
body:
### Plugin

agent-importers (Grok Bot importer)

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Context: a first-run test of the Grok Bot path (#248, #254, NousResearch/hermes-agent#147724) on a fresh install. The import itself went well (routines became paused jobs, skills and memories came over). This is about what happens right after.

A Grok Bot user's first question after the import is "do my routines still work?". Imported routines are created with `deliver: local`. Resumed and run, a routine succeeds silently: the result is written to `~/.hermes/cron/output/<id>/<date>.md`, and nothing shows up in the chat, in Bot Chat or on a configured messaging platform. In Grok Bot the result shows up in the Bot's conversation, so the user concludes the routine did not run.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Run `hermes setup` and import a Grok Bot export that has one scheduled routine.
2. `hermes cron resume <id>` (the id the import printed).
3. `hermes cron run <id>`. Output: `Ran now: succeeded.`
4. `hermes cron list`. Output: `Deliver: local`.

**Expected:** the first result of an imported routine is visible where the user already talks to the agent.

**Actual:** the result exists only as a markdown file under `cron/output/`. The import summary says "Results land in Hermes' cron output".

**Root cause**
- [`grok_bot.py` L598-L607](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L598-L607): `_create_job_kwargs` never sets `deliver`.
- [`cron/jobs.py` L1864-L1865](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/40b566502a84e24ed97afdc7ea5056968e071472/cron/jobs.py#L1864-L1865): `create_job` falls back to `"local"` when there is no origin.
- [`cli.py` L337-L339](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/cli.py#L337-L339): the summary message.

Related core proposal: NousResearch/hermes-agent#89752 (`cron.default_delivery`).

**Proposed fix**
When the target profile has a home channel or a Bot Chat, create imported jobs with that delivery (`bot-chat` under Bot Mode, otherwise the first configured home channel) and show it in the preview. Otherwise keep `local`, but print the output path and a one-line `hermes cron edit <id> --deliver ...` per job.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] In a profile with a Telegram home channel, an imported routine, resumed and run with `hermes cron run`, delivers its result to Telegram.
- [ ] The preview row says where each routine will deliver.
- [ ] With no delivery target available, the summary prints the output folder for each job.
- [ ] Test: importing into a home with `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL` set produces jobs whose `deliver` is not `local`.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.6 (f0d94882), fresh install on a clean HOME
agent-importers 1.2.1 (471acd3, the current catalog pin and main of this repo)
macOS 26.6 (arm64)
```

### Logs

```text
$ hermes cron run <id>
Ran now: succeeded.
$ hermes cron list
  Deliver: local
```

### Related

#265, #266 (same first-run test), NousResearch/hermes-agent#148134 (setup clears the import results, including the resume lines).

title: [agent-importers] Grok Bot: several Bots merge into one agent, and the per-profile path prints a resume command that fails
body:
### Plugin

agent-importers (Grok Bot importer)

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Grok Bot users often have several Bots, and the docs say "Repeat per Bot, into the profile that should own its work" ([import-from-other-agents.md L77](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/40b566502a84e24ed97afdc7ea5056968e071472/website/docs/user-guide/import-from-other-agents.md?plain=1#L77)). In a first-run test, both easy paths went wrong:
- With 2 exports in `~/Downloads`, `hermes setup` imports both into `default`. Because there is more than one Bot, neither role is written to SOUL.md; both become memory entries of the same agent ("Grok Bot Ava: You are Ava..." and "Grok Bot Scout: You are Scout... Stay silent otherwise").
- The per-profile path prints `hermes cron resume <id>` without `-p <profile>`, and that command fails as printed.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Put `grok-bot-export-ava.json` and `grok-bot-export-scout.md` in `~/Downloads`. Run `hermes setup`, answer Yes, then confirm. Read `memories/MEMORY.md`.
2. `hermes profile create scout`, then `hermes -p scout migrate grok-bot --source ~/Downloads/grok-bot-export-scout.md -y`.
3. Run the printed `hermes cron resume <id>`. Output: `Job with ID or name '<id>' not found`.
4. `hermes -p scout chat -q hi --oneshot`. Output: `No API key found for provider 'openrouter'` (the profile was created without `--clone`, which the import flow does not mention).

**Expected:** each Bot keeps its own identity, and every command the import prints works as printed.

**Root cause**
- [`grok_bot.py` L342](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L342) (`single=len(bots) == 1`) and [L401-L426](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L401-L426): the role goes to memory as soon as two Bots are imported.
- [`hermes_cli/setup_agent_import.py` L157-L163](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/40b566502a84e24ed97afdc7ea5056968e071472/hermes_cli/setup_agent_import.py#L157-L163) (hermes-agent): the setup child always runs on `--profile default`.
- [`cli.py` L336](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/cli.py#L336): the resume hint has no profile selector.

**Proposed fix**
- When an import holds more than one Bot, setup and `hermes migrate grok-bot` offer "one profile per Bot (recommended)", create the profiles (credentials inherited or copied as `hermes profile create --clone` does) and import each Bot into its own profile.
- Printed commands carry `-p <profile>` when the target is not the default profile.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Importing 2 Bots from setup with the default answer gives 2 profiles, each with its role in SOUL.md and only its own routines.
- [ ] Every printed `hermes cron resume` works when pasted as is.
- [ ] Each created profile answers a one-shot chat without extra setup.
- [ ] A single-Bot import is unchanged.

Related: NousResearch/hermes-agent#91719 (the earlier proposal that imported into Bot Mode profiles; superseded by NousResearch/hermes-agent#147724, which credits it).

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.6 (f0d94882), fresh install on a clean HOME
agent-importers 1.2.1 (471acd3, the current catalog pin and main of this repo)
macOS 26.6 (arm64)
```

### Logs

```text
$ hermes cron resume <id>
Job with ID or name '<id>' not found
$ hermes -p scout chat -q hi --oneshot
No API key found for provider 'openrouter'
```

### Related

#264, #266 (same first-run test), NousResearch/hermes-agent#148134 (setup clears the import results, including these resume lines).

title: [agent-importers] Grok Bot: tell the agent what was imported, and count routines that still need a schedule
body:
### Plugin

agent-importers (Grok Bot importer)

### What happened, and what did you expect?

After a Grok Bot import, the agent does not know an import happened:
- Asked "which routines did I have?", it offers to set them up, although they already exist as paused jobs, so a yes would create duplicates.
- Asked to "recreate the routines the import left out", it lists `skills/grok-bot-imports/` and never finds `grok-bot-import/<bot>-event-routines.md`. In the same turn it paused a routine the user had just resumed.

Separately, a scheduled routine whose time is only in words (`schedule_cron: ""`, `schedule_text: "Every month on the 15th at 9:00 AM"`) is silently filed in that notes file under "routines that run on an event". It appears neither under "Would import" nor under "Skipped", and the summary counts only the jobs it created.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Import an export with 2 scheduled routines with cron expressions, 1 email-triggered routine and 1 scheduled routine with only `schedule_text` set to "Every month on the 15th at 9:00 AM".
2. The summary lists the 2 paused jobs (`2 routine(s) were created PAUSED ...`) and has no line about the 4th routine.
3. `hermes chat -q "Which routines did I have in Grok Bot?"`. The agent proposes to create them.
4. `hermes chat -q "Recreate the routines the import could not create"`. The agent finds nothing to recreate.

**Expected:** the agent can tell what was imported and what still needs work, and every routine in the export is accounted for in the summary.

**Root cause**
- [`grok_bot.py` L381-L393](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L381-L393): no import record the agent can read.
- [L499-L502](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L499-L502) and [L581-L595](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L581-L595): a schedule routine whose time does not parse goes to `unscheduled`, the same bucket as event routines.
- [L530-L557](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/471acd3b4d0d5c12f6f0f6b42db4a2f52a912dba/agent-importers/grok_bot.py#L530-L557): the notes file is written, but nothing references it.

**Proposed fix**
- One memory entry per import: date, Bot, job ids (paused), the notes file path, and "do not recreate these".
- Scheduled-but-unparsed routines get their own "needs a schedule" heading and a summary line ("1 routine needs its schedule set: VAT reminder").

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Right after an import, "which routines did I have?" names the existing paused jobs and creates nothing.
- [ ] "Recreate what the import left out" reads the notes file.
- [ ] Every routine in the export appears in the preview as imported, skipped with a reason, or needs attention; none is silent.
- [ ] Test covering a `schedule_text`-only routine.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.6 (f0d94882), fresh install on a clean HOME
agent-importers 1.2.1 (471acd3, the current catalog pin and main of this repo)
macOS 26.6 (arm64)
```

### Logs

```text
2 routine(s) were created PAUSED so they don't run twice. ...
(no line for the 4th routine; it is only in grok-bot-import/<bot>-event-routines.md,
 under "routines that run on an event")
```

### Related

#264, #265 (same first-run test).

title: bubblewrap 1.3.0: file tools run inside the sandbox (requires Hermes 0.22.6)
body:
Bubblewrap's file tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`) now run inside the sandbox. Until now they went through Hermes' host fast path, so they could read hidden paths and write outside the sandbox's writable set. That also broke `search_files`: it picked Hermes' own ripgrep, which lives under the hidden Hermes home.

- `BubblewrapEnvironment.uses_host_filesystem = False`, the core capability that hermes-agent#143756 added and v0.22.6 ships (`git show v0.22.6:tools/environments/local.py` / `base.py` both carry it). This salvages @zakazaka95's #246 with the commit and authorship kept. #251 by @salch-cred made the same one-line flip and gets a co-author credit.
- `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.6"`, version 1.3.0. With that floor the old-core prompt branch is dead code, so the `HERMES_NATIVE_FILE_READ` advice and the "file tools run on the host" note are gone from the prompt note and the READMEs. The plugin README has a per-tool table showing that each tool runs in the sandbox.
- New real-bwrap test: with no env override, `write_file` to a path outside the writable set is refused with `Read-only file system`. It is red on main's `sandbox.py` and green here.

Local: 528 passed, 1 skipped. Run against hermes-agent v0.22.6 with real bwrap and a clean env (TMPDIR outside the Hermes home). Install scanner reads `safe` on v0.22.6 and on core main.

Closes #244.

title: advanced-delegation: forward a route's escalate_reasoning and escalate_ceiling to core
body:
## What does this PR do? **Makes `model_map` routes carry core's two per-route reasoning-escalation keys, `escalate_reasoning` and `escalate_ceiling`, so a route that asks for escalation gets it.** Today `configured_options` copies an allow-list of option fields into the route, so these keys are saved by the route editor and web API but never reach core, and the core feature does nothing for `model_map` users. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Companion to NousResearch/hermes-agent#148143**, which adds the keys to core's `ROUTE_KEYS`, validates them and runs the retry ladder. This PR is the plugin half: it forwards the keys and core owns the rules. A core without the keys in `ROUTE_KEYS` drops them without a warning. > [!WARNING] > **Stacked on #249** (route `max_iterations` / `child_timeout_seconds`). Merge #249 first. Until then GitHub also shows #249's commits here; this PR's own change is the one commit `c67f8d0`. ```yaml delegation: backend: model_map backends: model_map: options: - name: coder description: Write and fix code. provider: openai-codex model: gpt-6.1-terra reasoning_effort: low escalate_reasoning: true # now reaches the child escalate_ceiling: xhigh # now reaches the child ``` ### Rules - **Both keys or nothing:** core escalates only when a route sets `escalate_reasoning: true` and an `escalate_ceiling`. Either key alone leaves escalation off. - **Forwarded as written:** each key is forwarded when present and non-blank. Blank or `None` counts as absent, the same as the limits. Strings are only trimmed (`"XHigh "` → `"XHigh"`); nothing else is coerced: a `bool` stays a `bool` and a `str` stays a `str`. - **Core owns validation:** the ceiling must be on the ladder `none` · `minimal` · `low` · `medium` · `high` · `xhigh` · `max` · `ultra`. Core refuses a bad value for that task only, and the plugin does not hide a bad value by dropping it. - **Kept, not asked:** `hermes delegation config` keeps both keys through any edit but does not ask about them. Change them in the desktop route editor, the web API or `config.yaml`. - **Untouched:** `profile_routes`. Profile routes ignore both keys. ## Changes Made All paths are under `advanced-delegation/`. | Area | Files | What changed | |---|---|---| | **Forwarding** | `model_map.py` | `ROUTE_ESCALATION` forwarded by `configured_options` | | **Editor** | `cli.py` | Both keys survive any edit | | **Route list** | `store.py` | `route_summary` shows `escalates to ` | | **Docs** | `README.md`
module doc | Keys, ladder, both-keys rule, core requirement | | **Tests** | `tests/test_model_map.py` (+5, 8 cases)
`tests/test_cli.py` | Forwarding, exact types, pass-through, blank omission, list label; edit across a provider change |
File-by-file notes - `advanced-delegation/model_map.py`: `ROUTE_ESCALATION = ("escalate_reasoning", "escalate_ceiling")`. `configured_options` forwards it next to `ROUTE_LIMITS` through the same present-and-non-blank check. - `advanced-delegation/cli.py`: `_KEPT_ON_ANY_EDIT` gains both keys, so they survive any edit, like `fallback_providers` and the limits. They are not in `store.ROUTE_KEYS` on purpose, because the wizard re-asks those keys and discards the old value. - `advanced-delegation/store.py`: `route_summary` adds `· escalates to ` only when `escalate_reasoning is True` and the ceiling is non-blank, which matches when core escalates. The label shows in `--show` and in the interactive route list. - `advanced-delegation/README.md` + the module doc: both keys in the example, the ladder, the both-keys rule, profile routes ignoring them, and older cores dropping unknown route keys. The README also says that the CLI editor keeps the keys but does not edit them. - `tests/test_model_map.py`: the keys are forwarded with exact types (`type(...) is bool` / `str`) and are absent on a plain route. Bad values `"yes"`, `1`, `False` and `"galaxy"` pass through unchanged with their types. A disabled pair (`false` + `xhigh`) is forwarded as written. `None` / whitespace are omitted. The `route_summary` label appears only for the enabling pair. - `tests/test_cli.py`: the edit test now carries both keys through a provider change.
No change to `plugin.yaml` or `profile_routes`. ## How to Test ```bash cd advanced-delegation export HERMES_AGENT_REPO=$CORE PYTHONPATH=$CORE $CORE/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider ``` Manual, with a core that has hermes-agent#148143: give one `model_map` route `reasoning_effort: low`, `escalate_reasoning: true`, `escalate_ceiling: high`, and a turn limit too tight to finish at `low`. Give a second route the same setup without the escalation keys. Delegate one task to each. The first result's `attempts` climbs `low → medium → high`. The second has no `attempts` and stops after one try. ## Verification Plugin head `c67f8d0` (on #249's head `e1ab093`); Linux, each core's own `.venv`. **Live end-to-end** (core `4e4c133d9fa` + this plugin, dev home, `openai-codex` `gpt-6.1-terra`): the escalating route **retried `low → medium → high` and completed at the ceiling**. The control route ran once, stopped at `max_iterations`, and did not retry. ```json "attempts": [{"effort": "low", "exit_reason": "max_iterations"}, {"effort": "medium", "exit_reason": "max_iterations"}, {"effort": "high", "exit_reason": "completed"}] ``` | Check | Linux | macOS | Windows | |---|---|---|---| | Full plugin suite vs feature core
`feat/route-reasoning-escalation` @ `4e4c133d9fa` | ✅ **151 passed**
2 skipped | not run | not run | | Full plugin suite vs #249's core
`route-limits` @ `9f779382670` (no escalation keys) | ✅ **151 passed**
2 skipped | not run | not run | | Live end-to-end (shared with the core PR) | ✅ low → medium → high | not run | not run |
Logs and skips Both runs print the same lines: ```text SKIPPED [1] tests/test_slash_core.py:112: core with set_global_backend(apply_now=) SKIPPED [1] tests/test_slash_host.py:72: core with set_global_backend(apply_now=) 151 passed, 2 skipped, 70 warnings ``` Both skips come from an existing guard. The two tests need a core whose `set_global_backend` takes `apply_now=`, and neither core in this stack has that parameter, so the tests skip. This PR does not touch them. The suite also passes against #249's core, which shows that forwarding the keys is harmless on a core that does not read them.
**Review:** two stages (spec, then a review from a different model family). Approved. Minor items folded into `c67f8d0`: the README says the keys are route-only, the README notes that the CLI editor does not edit them, and the tests assert exact types. ## Not covered - macOS and Windows: not run. This is a pure-Python plugin change with no OS-specific path. The core PR ran its OS matrix. - The CLI editor does not ask about the two keys (by design). Use the desktop route editor, the web API or `config.yaml`. ## Checklist - ✅ Touches one plugin (`advanced-delegation`) - ✅ Tests added for the behaviour; the plugin stays self-contained (no imports from other plugin directories) - ✅ README documents the new keys and the core requirement - ✅ Catalog pin (`plugin-catalog/advanced-delegation.yaml` in hermes-agent) will be a separate PR after this, #249 and hermes-agent#148143 land. No tools, hooks or dependencies are added, so the pin needs no re-consent.

title: feat(unreal-engine): Unreal Editor MCP server and skill as an official plugin
body:
Unreal Engine becomes an official plugin: one install gives Hermes the Unreal Editor's MCP server and the unreal-mcp workflow skill. **Merge before** the hermes-agent PR that removes the built-in MCP catalog (`optional-mcps/` and `hermes mcp install`). After that PR, this plugin is how users get the Unreal server. ## Before Hermes core shipped two separate pieces for Unreal: - an entry in its built-in MCP catalog. `hermes mcp install unreal-engine` wrote `mcp_servers.unreal-engine` (`http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`) to config.yaml; - an optional skill, `optional-skills/creative/unreal-mcp`, installed on its own. Hermes is deleting the catalog. Local servers, and servers that come with a skill, move to plugins. ## After `hermes plugins install unreal-engine` installs a portable package (Agent Plugins v1: `plugin.json` + `mcp.json` + `skills/`, no Python): ```mermaid flowchart LR P[unreal-engine plugin] --> M["mcp.json: server unreal-engine
http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"] P --> S[skills/unreal-mcp] M --> E[Unreal Editor 5.8+
Unreal MCP plugin] ``` - The server is registered for every session while the plugin is enabled. config.yaml is not changed. - The skill is the hermes-agent optional skill with these changes: it says the plugin provides the server, it uses the tool names Hermes actually registers (`mcp__unreal_engine__*`, not `mcp_unreal_engine_*`), and it explains how to change the URL or timeout with a config.yaml entry of the same name. It no longer mentions `hermes mcp install`/`configure` or the catalog. - Card art in `assets/unreal-engine.jpg`, plus a README table cell. ## Why the server is named `unreal-engine` Hermes gives a plugin's MCP server exactly the name in its `mcp.json`. When config.yaml has a server with the same name, the config entry wins and the plugin's entry is skipped with a warning (`tools/mcp_tool_config.py::_portable_mcp_servers`). | User's config.yaml | Server named `unreal-engine` (this PR) | Server named anything else | |---|---|---| | No Unreal entry | Plugin's server, `127.0.0.1:8000` | Plugin's server | | Old catalog entry `mcp_servers.unreal-engine` | **One server: the user's entry** (their port, tool filter, timeout); log line `Portable MCP server 'unreal-engine' conflicts with native config; skipping` | Two servers, so every Unreal tool appears twice | ## Compatibility | Hermes | What happens | |---|---| | 0.21.6 and newer | Loads. Plugin servers keep their `mcp.json` names, so an existing `mcp_servers.unreal-engine` wins. Verified on v0.21.6 and current main. | | Older than 0.21.6 | The catalog entry's `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"` refuses an install by name: `unreal-engine needs Hermes >=0.21.6; this is .` (`plugin.json` has no version field. An install by path or URL on such a core would prefix the server name and could duplicate a catalog entry.) | | Cores that still ship the MCP catalog | `hermes mcp install unreal-engine` still works there. If a user runs it too, its config entry replaces the plugin's entry: one server. | ## Live verification Core: hermes-agent main at `a58549f51a` plus tag v0.21.6. Each run used a temp `HERMES_HOME` under the repo's `.scratch/`. The plugin was installed from a local `file://` copy of this branch with `hermes plugins install #unreal-engine --enable --force`. | Check | Result | |---|---| | `hermes plugins validate ./unreal-engine` | Passed. Scan caution `sudo_usage` is the skill's `sudo xcode-select` line for macOS setup | | Fresh home: loaded MCP config (`_load_mcp_config`) | `unreal-engine → http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp`, `strict_redirect_headers: true` | | Fresh home: session-start discovery, no editor running | `Failed to connect to MCP server 'unreal-engine': ... [Errno 111] Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 8000)`; 0 tools, session continues | | Home with old catalog entry (port 8123, tool filter) | One server, the user's entry: `url: http://127.0.0.1:8123/mcp`, `tools.include` kept; conflict warning logged | | Same, server renamed `unreal` (counterfactual) | Two servers resolved, `unreal-engine` and `unreal` | | Old catalog entry on v0.21.6 | One server, the user's entry | Not run: a real Unreal Editor (no editor on the test machine), so the tool list and skill recipes were not run end to end in this PR. The skill text comes from the hermes-agent optional skill, which recorded editor-verified behaviour. ## Follow-ups - hermes-agent: after this merges, open `plugin-catalog/unreal-engine.yaml` pinned to the upstream merge commit (`tier: official`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"`). A draft is ready. - hermes-agent: once that catalog entry is live, remove `optional-skills/creative/unreal-mcp` so the skill has one source. - README table: whichever of this PR and the n8n plugin PR merges second needs a one-row rebase (both replace the "More on the way" row).

title: feat(n8n): n8n MCP server setup as an official plugin
body:
n8n becomes an official plugin: `hermes n8n setup` asks for your instance's MCP Server URL and adds n8n's official MCP server to Hermes, with OAuth sign-in and no API key. **Merge before** the hermes-agent PR that removes the built-in MCP catalog. After that PR, this plugin is how users add n8n. ## Before Hermes core's built-in MCP catalog had an `n8n-official` entry. `hermes mcp install n8n-official` asked for the URL and wrote: ```yaml mcp_servers: n8n-official: url: https:///mcp-server/http auth: oauth enabled: true ``` Hermes is deleting the catalog. n8n's MCP server has a different URL for every user (self-hosted or n8n Cloud), so a hosted connector does not fit it. ## After ```mermaid flowchart LR I[hermes plugins install n8n] --> S["hermes n8n setup
asks for the URL"] S --> C["config.yaml
mcp_servers.n8n-official
url + auth: oauth"] C --> L["hermes mcp login n8n-official
(Hermes MCP OAuth)"] L --> T[n8n tools in the next session] ``` - A native plugin (`plugin.yaml` + `register(ctx)`) with one CLI command, `hermes n8n setup [--url URL]`. It registers no model tools; the tools come from n8n's server. - `setup` writes the same entry the catalog wrote, through `hermes_cli.config.load_config()` / `save_config()` (the pair `hermes mcp add` uses). From then on it is an ordinary MCP server: `hermes mcp login/test/configure/remove n8n-official` all work. - An existing `n8n-official` entry is kept as it is. `--url` replaces only its URL. - The URL must be http(s) with a host. A URL that does not end in `/mcp-server/http` gets a note but is still used. - `after-install.md` prints the two commands, plus card art and a README table cell. ## Why a setup command and not a bundled server | Path | Per-user URL? | Core change? | |---|---|---| | Portable `mcp.json` (`streamable-http`) | No. Agent Plugins v1 forbids expanding a remote URL: `${N8N_MCP_SERVER_URL}` fails `_validate_remote_url` (scheme check) | None, but it cannot work | | `ctx` API that registers an MCP server from a native plugin | Would work | There is no such API. Needs one | | Plugin writes `mcp_servers.n8n-official` once, through the public config writer | Yes | **None** (this PR) | Trade-off: disabling or uninstalling the plugin leaves the server entry in config.yaml. The README says so and gives `hermes mcp remove n8n-official`. Setup needs a terminal once; a user who only runs the desktop app has no in-app setup form for this plugin. ## Compatibility | Hermes | What happens | |---|---| | 0.21.6 and newer | Loads (`requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"`). The suite passes on v0.21.6 and current main. | | Older than 0.21.6 | Install by catalog name is refused: `n8n needs Hermes >=0.21.6; this is .` Discovery also skips the plugin cleanly on the version gate. | | Users with the catalog's `n8n-official` entry | Nothing to do. `setup` keeps their entry, including tool choices. | | Users of the retired stdio bridge (`mcp_servers.n8n`) | Untouched; a different name. | ## Live verification Core: hermes-agent main at `a58549f51a` plus tag v0.21.6. Each run used a temp `HERMES_HOME` under the repo's `.scratch/`. The plugin was installed from a local `file://` copy of this branch. | Check | Result | |---|---| | `hermes plugins validate ./n8n` | Passed. Security scan safe, no private core imports | | Plugin suite (5 tests: real `PluginManager` discovery in a temp home, the registered `hermes n8n` parser, result read back through `tools.mcp_tool_config._load_mcp_config`) | 5 passed on main and on v0.21.6 | | Install from a local path + `echo \| hermes n8n setup` | config.yaml gains `n8n-official: {url, auth: oauth, enabled: true}`; Hermes' MCP loader resolves it | | `hermes n8n setup` again | `'n8n-official' is already in config.yaml (...); keeping it.` | | OAuth path for that entry (forced-interactive probe, `.invalid` host) | `tools.mcp_oauth_manager.get_or_build_provider('n8n-official', ...)` returns `HermesMCPOAuthProvider`, then the connection fails on DNS as expected | Not run: a real n8n instance and a completed browser sign-in. ## Follow-ups - hermes-agent: after this merges, open `plugin-catalog/n8n.yaml` pinned to the upstream merge commit (`tier: official`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"`). A draft is ready. - Core: an API that lets a native plugin register an MCP server from user settings would let this plugin drop the config write, so disable/uninstall would also remove the server. - README table: whichever of this PR and the Unreal Engine plugin PR merges second needs a one-row rebase (both replace the "More on the way" row).

title: fix(agent-importers): deliver imported routines to the profile home channel
body:
Imported Grok Bot routines were created without `deliver`, so cron fell back to `local`: a resumed routine succeeded silently into `~/.hermes/cron/output/<id>/` and the user — coming from Grok Bot, where results show in the Bot's conversation — concluded it never ran.

The importer now resolves the target profile's first configured home channel (`<PLATFORM>_HOME_CHANNEL` in the process env or the profile's `.env`, or a `home_channel` in its config) and creates the job with that delivery. The preview row says where each routine will deliver; with no target available the job stays `local` and the summary prints each job's output folder plus its `hermes cron edit <id> --deliver ...` hint instead of the generic line.

Acceptance test included: importing into a home with `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL` set produces jobs whose `deliver` is `telegram`, not `local`.

Closes #264.

title: fix(agent-importers): record the import and count routines that need a schedule
body:
After a Grok Bot import, the agent didn't know an import had happened: asked "which routines did I have?", it offered to set them up again (duplicates), and "recreate what was left out" never found the notes file. Separately, a scheduled routine whose time is only in words (`schedule_text: "Every month on the 15th at 9:00 AM"`) was silently filed under "routines that run on an event" — counted neither as imported nor skipped.

- One memory entry per import: date, Bot, the created job names/ids (paused), the notes file, and "do not recreate these routines — they already exist as cron jobs".
- Schedule-triggered routines whose time doesn't parse get their own `# Routines that need a schedule` heading in the notes file and a counted summary line (`1 routine(s) need a schedule set: VAT reminder`), so every routine in the export is accounted for.

Test covers the `schedule_text`-only routine end to end.

Closes #266.

title: feat(advanced-delegation): model_map options may resolve to a profile
body:
The backend enforced one routing style at a time: a `model_map` option could only name a model+provider, so reaching a second provider with different auth (e.g. an OAuth profile contained in Docker) meant throwaway profiles just to switch models on one key.

Core's route keys already accept `profile` — this passes it through. A `model_map` option may now name a `profile` (optionally with a `model` override) and resolves to that profile route: the profile's own credentials, containment and defaults apply. Plain model options are unchanged, and an entry with `profile` no longer needs `provider`/`model`.

So one config spans both worlds:

```yaml
options:
  - {name: cheap, description: "Small model on provider A", provider: A, model: small}
  - {name: code, description: "Frontier model on provider B (contained)", profile: coder}
```

Closes #260.

title: fix(agent-importers): print cron hints for the profile the import targeted
body:
The import's next-steps block printed `hermes cron resume <id>` with no profile selector. The jobs were created in the target profile, so pasting that line into a shell on the default profile answers `Job with ID or name '<id>' not found` — the exact failure in #265's per-profile path.

The hint now resolves the profile from the import's target home and prints `hermes -p <profile> cron resume <id>` for named profiles (the `--deliver` hint gets the same treatment); the default profile keeps the bare form.

Test: importing into `profiles/scout` prints `hermes -p scout cron resume`.

Refs #265 (the multi-Bot merge and setup-side parts of that issue are core/setup concerns, not this CLI hint).

title: REA plugin: gateway drops additional --args, causing MCP connection to fail
body:
### What happens

The [REA plugin](https://github.com/reacommunity/rea) is listed in the Hermes catalog with `command: npx` and `args: ["--mcp", "rea-agents@6.7.0"]`. When Hermes tries to connect this MCP server via stdio, only `npx rea` runs instead of `npx rea-agents@6.7.0 --mcp`, causing immediate disconnect.

### Plugin manifest excerpt

```yaml
name: rea
subdir: rea
# command/args come from the catalog entry:
#   command: npx
#   args:
#     - --mcp
#     - rea-agents@6.7.0
```

This manifest matches the pattern used by other working MCP servers. The individual args are correctly separated (not concatenated into a single string).

### Root cause (confirmed)

The bug is in the Hermes gateway — not in this plugin's manifest. See: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/148496

The gateway appears to either collapse all args into a single shell-invoked string or drop arguments beyond index 0 when spawning stdio subprocesses. This affects any MCP server that needs more than one arg (e.g., version pinning + flags).

### Workaround tried

Putting everything into one `--args` value also fails — npx interprets it as a single package name. Global install (`sudo npm i -g`) works but requires root and isn't ideal.

### Environment

- Hermes version: latest (desktop app)
- OS: macOS
- Plugin tier: official
- Node.js: `/usr/local/bin/npx 10.9.3`

title: fix(importers): merge memory entries against the live memory_char_limit
body:
Fixes #148472 (reported there with reproduction details).

## What

- Replaces the hardcoded `MEMORY_CHAR_LIMIT = 20_000` with `_memory_char_limit()`, which resolves the budget the memory tool actually enforces (`memory.memory_char_limit` via `get_builtin_memory_config`) and falls back to the store's own default (2200) — never 20_000.
- The config is read through the raw, seed-free path and handed to `get_builtin_memory_config` explicitly: the zero-arg form loads config, which materializes a missing home (SOUL.md, dirs) — a write even under `--dry-run` (this broke 2 dry-run tests before the explicit call).
- `overflowed_entries` stats plumbing is unchanged; with the limit right it now surfaces what really overflows.

## Why

A merge against the larger hardcoded budget writes a store that exceeds what `MemoryStore` accepts; the memory tool then refuses every operation on the imported home — including the consolidation that would fix it.

## Tests

New `TestLiveMemoryCharLimit` in `agent-importers/tests/test_agent_import.py`:
1. Entries past the configured limit are counted as `overflowed_entries` and left out of the written store, which stays within budget.
2. The resolver honors the live config value and falls back to 2200 when config/core is unavailable.

Full plugin suite: 132 passed, 3 skipped (pre-existing), 0 failed.

title: fix(xchat): keep polling known conversations when the list budget is spent
body:
Two halves of the read-path death in #228, without the streaming transport (that stays a separate, larger change):

1. **Ids only in memory.** The conversation list and events endpoints carry separate daily budgets (1,000 vs 10,000 measured). A restart while the list budget is spent left the adapter connected, token valid, with zero conversations to poll. Discovered ids now persist to `xchat/conversations.json` (same atomic tmp+replace pattern as cursors) and seed the poll set at startup.

2. **One throttle stops everything.** A list-side `429` propagated out of the poll loop and slept the whole cycle. It now skips discovery for that cycle and polls the known conversations; only an events-side throttle reaches the rate-limit sleep.

Tests cover persistence across an adapter rebuild and the degraded cycle.

Refs #228.

title: fix(xchat): persist verified conversation keys and rebuild on decrypt failure
body:
Conversation keys learned from a KeyChange lived only in memory. After a restart, the next message under a rotated key failed decrypt until the KeyChange event paged in again — and that event may sit behind the cursor, so the message was dropped with the cursor advanced past it.

- The verified key cache persists to `xchat/conversation_keys.json` (base64, mode 600, same atomic tmp+replace pattern as cursors/sent-ids) and loads at startup.
- A `decrypt_one` failure now rebuilds keys from the event itself (`_absorb_key_batch`, which also persists) and retries once before dropping the message.

Test: keys absorbed from a KeyChange are present in a fresh adapter over the same home.

Refs #228 (the streaming transport itself remains the larger separate change).

title: fix(agent-importers): say plainly when several Bots merge into one profile
body:
From #265: with two exports in `~/Downloads`, setup imports both Bots into `default`. Because there is more than one Bot, neither role is written to SOUL.md — both become memory entries of the same agent, silently. The user finds two Bot personalities inside one agent with no explanation of what happened or what to do instead.

The import report now carries an explicit entry for that case: it names the Bots, states that their roles became memory entries of a single agent (not separate identities), and points at the documented per-profile path — `hermes profile create <name> --clone`, then `hermes -p <name> import-agent grok-bot --bot <Bot>` per export.

The identity model itself (offering profile-per-Bot inside setup) spans setup/core; this makes the current behavior impossible to miss.

Refs #265.

title: fix(xchat): run conversation discovery on its own cadence
body:
From #228's budget math: the poll loop spent one conversation-list read per cycle. The list endpoint is billed per call against a separate 1,000/day budget (events: 10,000), so at the default 30 s interval the list budget empties in ~8 hours — after which inbound dies for the rest of the window even though events would still answer.

Discovery now runs at startup and then at most every `max(600s, 20 poll cycles)`; between discoveries every known conversation is polled directly (an idle events page returns no resources, so that stays cheap). New conversations are picked up on the next discovery pass instead of within one poll cycle — the trade the budget imposes, and the same direction as the persisted-ids/degrade work in #277.

Refs #228.

title: fix(directsdk): record native rate_limit_event instead of dropping it
body:
Claude Code emits a `rate_limit_event` stream message whose `rate_limit_info` carries `rateLimitType`, `overageStatus` and `isUsingOverage` — the subscription-window signal #43's quota policy needs. The receive loop only handled `assistant`, `result` and `stream_event`, so the event was discarded.

It is now summarized secret-free into `native_admission.rate_limit` (`window`, `overage_status`, `using_overage`). Paid use is flagged only when actually in use: `overageStatus: "allowed"` alone means *permitted*, and the subscription windows (`five_hour`, `seven_day`, `seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`, `seven_day_overage_included`) are not paid use — the pitfalls called out in #43's design data.

No behavior change for the turn itself; this lands the signal the opt-in guard can later consume.

Refs #43.

title: feat(directsdk): opt-in guard against paid extra usage
body:
Opt-in quota guard for #43's design question: once a call reports the subscription is on paid extra usage, refuse later calls with a billing-style error (402) until that window resets, so Hermes takes its fallback instead of silently spending.

- `block_extra_usage` setting (default off), read per spawn like `claude_code_telemetry`.
- The marker is written from the native `rate_limit_event` summary landed in the previous PR: paid use is `isUsingOverage` true or the `overage` window type only; `overageStatus: "allowed"` alone means permitted, and the subscription windows are never paid use.
- No marker (no signal ever seen) never blocks — missing data is not evidence.
- Conservative expiry: 5 h for `five_hour`, 7 days otherwise (the event carries no reset time).

Refs #43.

title: fix(xchat): select latest identity key instead of oldest
body:
`_initiate_conversation` selected `records[0]`, which is the oldest public key when a recipient has rotated identities; X rejects any participant key that is not the account's latest, so the conversation key never seeds.

Select the record with the greatest `public_key_version` instead, comparing as integers (versions are millisecond timestamps whose string length can vary).

Closes #219.

title: fix(directsdk): cut tool call at max_tokens still yields finish length
body:
A tool call cut off mid-argument is dropped at `message_stop` (its input becomes an unparsed entry in `admission.capture.unparsed`). The per-call path still failed with `error_max_turns` because:

- `_fast_eligible` only treated `error_max_turns` as fast-eligible when a `tool_use` block survived in the capture.
- The boundary check required `bool(calls)`, which is false when every call was dropped.

Treat a turn whose calls were all dropped (unparsed non-empty) the same way at both checks, so the answer reaches Hermes with `finish_reason == "length"` and no tool calls, as intended.

Closes #164.

title: fix(camofox): do not report navigation success the server never confirmed
body:
## Problem

`browser_navigate` can report a successful navigation that the Camofox server never completed. Two false-success paths:

1. **Blank-tab fabrication.** When `_navigate_tab` has to create a fresh tab, it returns a synthesized `{"ok": True, "url": <requested>}` instead of the server's own `POST /tabs` payload. A blank tab (or a redirect the server actually landed on) is reported as the requested URL with `success: True`.
2. **`ok:false` ignored.** `browser_navigate` always sets `success: True` without reading the server's `ok: false` (e.g. a Google block/captcha page), so a blocked navigation looks like a success.

## Repro (against the camofox-browser REST server)

With a Camofox server running:

- `POST /tabs` returns `{"tabId": "t", "url": ""}` (blank landing) → `browser_navigate` still returned `{"success": true, "url": "<requested>"}`.
- `POST /tabs/<id>/navigate` returns `{"ok": false, "googleBlocked": true, ...}` → `browser_navigate` still returned `{"success": true}`.

## Fix

- `ensure_tab` now returns `(session, created)` where `created` is the server's own `POST /tabs` payload (which navigates the new tab and reports the landed URL); no fabricated success.
- The fresh-tab path in `_navigate_tab` returns the server's landed URL plus `tab_created: true`.
- `browser_navigate` reads `ok`, treats a blank landing after a real page request as a failure, and on `ok: false` names the cause in `result["error"]` (including `googleBlocked`).

## Tests

`TestNavigateReliability` in `camofox/tests/test_camofox_tools.py` (2 cases). Both are red on current `main` (they reproduce the two false-success reports) and green with this change.

title: fix(directsdk): retain request IDs on incomplete upstream responses
body:
## Summary

When an upstream response ends before a complete message arrives, DirectSDK captures Anthropic's request ID but drops it from the exception. An HTTP 200 followed by a connection reset therefore leaves the saved error without the ID needed to investigate that request.

Pass the captured ID into `ClaudeAPIError` and include it in the existing error text and a `request_id` attribute. Accept only `req_` IDs with ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, up to 128 characters total. Missing or malformed values are omitted. No additional headers, prompts or response content are logged, and retry admission and status classification stay unchanged.

Add real loopback regressions for HTTP 200 followed by EOF or a TCP reset after the relay has consumed partial SSE. Cover both client modes, both response-header names, header precedence, missing/unsafe/overlong IDs, content privacy and the single-upstream-request boundary. Update the plugin documentation.

This improves diagnostics for future failures. It does not repair the connection that reset or recover IDs from older unrecorded failures.

## Validation

Native Windows, Python 3.14.3. Dependencies installed using the repository CI recipe and current Hermes core at `b7736eca98c`. Each file ran in a separate process with an isolated home, a synthetic Python native client and local HTTP peers. No real Claude Code model calls or inherited credentials.

- Red on unchanged plugin main `1b9102c7c4211b9622680fe6e2b78246634cbc1d`: four real-reset cases and four truncated-stream cases fail because the request ID is absent from the error text.
- All 34 added request-ID regression cases pass on the fix.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_directsdk_admission.py -q`: **55 passed, 1 failed**. The failure is the unchanged `test_contentless_refusal_is_a_terminal_content_filter[details0-The request was declined.]`, raising `Incomplete native response`. Its isolated rerun passed on both unchanged main and the candidate. A complete baseline run of this file also passed, 32 tests. This is recorded as a flaky result with unresolved cause, not a clean file pass or a proven pre-existing failure.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_directsdk_errors.py -q`: **23 passed**.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_directsdk_headers.py -q`: **5 passed, 9 subtests passed**.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate <plugin>`: **passed**, with existing private-core-import and in-process-isolation advisories. None of those imports changed.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

The current repository workflow has no separate lint, formatter or static/type-check job. The full plugin suite and Linux/macOS execution are left to repository CI under the workstation's focused-test limit.

## Checklist

- [x] Read `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- [x] Change is confined to one plugin.
- [x] Added offline behavioral regressions and demonstrated the missing-ID failure before the fix.
- [x] Validated the plugin manifest against current core.
- [x] Documented the validation caveat and delivery limits.

The catalog pin must move after merge before catalog-installed copies receive the fix.

title: feat(hermes-security): add the Security plugin
body:
Adds **Security** (`hermes-security/`) as an official plugin: local repository security review for Hermes Agent. Imported from [unsupportedpastels/hermes-security-scanner-plugin](https://github.com/unsupportedpastels/hermes-security-scanner-plugin) at `6ef674d`, where it was developed. After this merges, the monorepo copy is the maintained one.

## Summary

- **What it does.** The agent builds a threat model, splits the repository into chunks of about 4,000 lines, and reviews them with up to 10 parallel subagents. It checks each candidate against the code and traces whether an attacker can reach it. Rejected and inconclusive candidates stay in the report, and coverage gaps are listed. Standard, deep and diff (changed code only) modes.
- **Optional confirmation.** With **Run tests to confirm findings** turned on, the agent writes small reproductions and runs them in a temporary copy of the repository. A finding counts as "Confirmed by test" only with a passing test and a matching negative control. Testing a running app needs a per-scan grant from `/security authorize-validation` or the Desktop page: one exact origin, one hour, 200 requests. Agent tools cannot grant it.
- **Surfaces.** 9 tools in the `security` toolset, 7 namespaced skills (`hermes-security:security-audit` and others), the `/security` slash command, `hermes security-review` and `python -m hermes_security` CLIs, a dashboard API, and a Hermes Desktop **Security** page (opt-in, like every Desktop plugin). Exports to Markdown, JSON, CSV and SARIF.
- **Resuming.** The `on_session_end`, `subagent_start` and `subagent_stop` hooks track scan progress and reviewers that ended without saving. With `allow_gateway_injection` turned on, the plugin queues one "Continue security scan" message per stalled turn, capped at 3 with no progress, and never after Stop.
- **Monorepo changes to the imported tree.** `plugin.yaml` gains `label`, `author: NousResearch` and `homepage`. `pyproject.toml` lists Nous Research as author. The README uses the shared card, links back to this repo and installs with `hermes plugins install hermes-security`. The card is `assets/hermes-security.jpg` (1200×600). The plugin is added to the top-level README table, and a CODEOWNERS line is added for `/hermes-security/`.

## Fixes found by this repo's CI

The plugin's own repo never ran macOS or Windows CI, and running it here turned up two product bugs and some test assumptions. All are fixed in this PR:

- **macOS: timed-out tests lost their output.** After a timeout the runner kills the process group a second time during cleanup. By then the group leader is an unreaped zombie, and macOS answers `killpg` with `EPERM` where Linux answers `ESRCH`. Only `ProcessLookupError` was ignored, so on macOS every timed-out or truncated test reported "command could not start". `PermissionError` is now ignored there too, with a regression test.
- **Windows: data-folder permissions were re-applied on every write for the built-in Administrator.** Windows prints that account's SID as the SDDL alias `LA`. The plugin's "already private" check compared against the full SID, so it never matched. The alias is now normalized before comparing.
- **Tests:** fixtures are read as UTF-8 (Windows defaults to cp1252). Tests only assert a non-UTF-8 file name where the filesystem allows one (APFS doesn't). The process-group test polls `kill(pid, 0)` where there is no `/proc`. A live timing field is ignored when comparing two reads of a running scan.

## License

This plugin stays **Apache-2.0**, with its own `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Parts are adapted from Apache-2.0 source (Copyright 2025 OpenAI), and `UPSTREAM_PROVENANCE.json` records each adapted file. Those files can't be relicensed as MIT. It's the first non-MIT plugin in the repo, so please confirm that's acceptable.

## Security and privacy (catalog disclosure)

- **Network:**
  - **osv-scanner download:** the first scan downloads a pinned osv-scanner release from GitHub, about 55 MB, refused unless its SHA-256 matches the pin, and stores it in the plugin data folder.
  - **Dependency lookups:** package names and versions go to api.osv.dev (and api.deps.dev for manifests without a lockfile). Declared runtime versions are checked against endoflife.date.
  - **Turning it off:** `HERMES_SECURITY_DEPENDENCY_CHECK=off`, or `HERMES_SECURITY_OSV_SCANNER` pointing at an admin-installed binary.
- **Local execution:** only with **Run tests to confirm findings** turned on. Tests run as the user in a temporary copy, with credential-looking environment variables removed. That's not a sandbox, and the README says so.
- **Untrusted input:** repository text is treated as data, never as instructions. Git hooks and filters never run. Secrets are stored only as type, location and a one-way fingerprint.
- **Storage:** everything stays in the profile's plugin data folder. Nothing is uploaded to a hosted service. The configured model provider receives the code under review.
- **Hermes APIs:** only documented plugin APIs. `hermes plugins validate` passes with no private-import, core-override or desktop-surface warnings. No Python dependencies (stdlib only; the dashboard API uses Hermes's own FastAPI).

## Test plan

- [x] `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=<hermes-agent main> PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent main> python -m pytest -q` in `hermes-security/` on Linux, Python 3.14, with current hermes-agent `main` installed via uv using core's overrides (as CI does): 655 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed
- [x] `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate hermes-security` against hermes-agent `main`: passed, no warnings
- [x] `node --test tests/e2e/*.mjs` (Desktop workbench contract): 51 passed
- [x] This PR's CI: `hermes-security` passes on Linux, macOS and Windows (all 64 checks green)

## After merge

Release is a separate hermes-agent PR adding `plugin-catalog/hermes-security.yaml`. It pins the merged SHA with `subdir: hermes-security`, `tier: official`, the card image at that SHA, the 9 tools and 3 hooks, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.5"`, and the disclosure above. Everything the plugin calls exists in Hermes 0.21.5 except `agent.delegation_backends.list_backends` (0.22.5). That call is guarded, so on older Hermes the Desktop Subagents picker just stays hidden.

## Infographic

![security-goes-official](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1058a/jcduLug7jOvNkRwq9Dcjg_rnx1DLs7.png)

title: [bubblewrap] home_default_deny: hide every unlisted home entry, not only dot entries
body:
Right now, the sandbox hides unlisted dot entries of HOME, but every other entry stays visible.
This adds a setting home_default_deny that can hide everything (and only show what is explicitly allowed):

- dot (default): today's behaviour.
- all: every unlisted top-level entry of HOME is hidden, and home_allow also takes top-level
  names.
  
```sh
hermes config set plugins.entries.bubblewrap.settings.home_default_deny all
hermes config set plugins.entries.bubblewrap.settings.home_allow '["server", "bin"]'
```

Four commits, each green on its own. Overlaps with #138 (a hide denylist); happy to rebase if it
lands first. Version left at 1.3.0 for you to bump.

title: feat(advanced-delegation): model_map options may resolve to a profile
body:
## What this does

`model_map` could only name a model and provider. If you wanted to reach a second provider with different auth (OAuth profile in Docker, say), you had to switch the whole backend to `profile_routes` and lose per-task model routing.

This lets a `model_map` option name a `profile` instead. The subagent runs as that profile: its own model, credentials, Docker volumes, skills. One config, both kinds of routes.

```yaml
options:
  - {name: cheap,   description: "Lookups",     provider: openrouter, model: gemini-3-flash}
  - {name: frontier, description: "Docker-contained", profile: openai}
```

## Why not just allow profile + model override

Core's `_profile_route()` loads the profile config and uses `model.default`. It does not read a `model` field from the route dict. So a `profile` + `model` combination would silently drop the model override at the core layer.

We reject the combination early in the plugin instead. If someone later wants model override within a profile route, that needs a core change to `_profile_route()`, not just a plugin change.

## What changed

- `model_map.py`: `ROUTE_FIELDS` includes `profile`. `_entry_problem()` accepts profile-only entries, rejects entries with both profile and model/provider. `route_task()` returns `{"profile": name, "label": chosen}` for profile routes.
- `store.py`: `ROUTE_KEYS` includes `profile`. `validate_route()` accepts profile-only entries (no model/provider/tier needed), rejects mixed entries. `route_summary()` shows `profile: name`. CLI display works.
- `tests/test_model_map.py`: 4 new tests (profile route dispatch, mixed entry rejected, mixed config with both types, profile route as default).
- `tests/test_store.py`: 4 new tests (validate accepts profile-only, rejects mixed, route_summary shows profile, describe shows profile route).
- `README.md`: documented the `profile` field with example.

## Relation to #273

#273 does the `model_map.py` part in fewer lines but leaves `store.py` untouched. `validate_route()` there would reject profile routes as missing a model, and `route_summary()` / `hermes delegation config --show` would not display them. #273 also allows `profile` + `model` together, but core's `_profile_route()` silently drops the model.

This PR patches all four files and has 8 tests covering both the plugin and store layers. Tested live: a `delegate_task(option: "contained-research")` call spawned a subagent on a Docker-contained OpenAI profile from a Regolo parent session.

Closes #260.

title: fix(agent-importers): pin the cron resume hint to the imported profile
body:
Fixes #265 (the per-profile resume hint half)

## What this changes

Importing a Grok Bot or OpenBot into a named profile printed
`hermes cron resume <id>` without a `-p` selector, so the hint failed when
pasted from any other profile — the resume ran against the caller's cron
store and reported `Job with ID or name '<id>' not found`.

`_print_routine_next_steps()` now pins the hint to the profile the import
targeted, using core's `hermes_constants.profile_cli_selector()` — the same
helper `hermes_cli/auth.py` and `doctor_state.py` use for their
copy-pasteable guidance. The default profile keeps the bare
`hermes cron resume` form, so single-profile behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

- New end-to-end test `test_the_resume_hint_is_pasteable_from_a_named_profile`
  (RED first: reproduced the missing `-p`; GREEN after the fix). It mirrors
  the issue's repro: the profile home is created explicitly, the import runs,
  and the output must contain `hermes -p scout cron resume` with no bare
  `hermes cron resume` form left.
- Full `agent-importers` suite: 133 passed, 1 skipped (baseline was
  132 passed, 1 skipped — the only delta is the new test).
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate ./agent-importers` → passed.

## Scope

Touches only `agent-importers`. The multi-Bot half of #265 (several Bots
merging into one agent / "one profile per Bot") is a design decision — I
would like to follow the maintainer's direction on it before coding, as
asked in the issue comment.

title: Allow for non-localhost entries in camofox_vault.py:secret_transport_ok()
body:
Camofox was recently moved out of core ( https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/161 ), and with it [camofox_vault.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/main/camofox/camofox_vault.py) was created.

This file/feature restricts valid camofox urls to a specific protocol and/or endpoint check in `secret_transport_ok` as follows:

```python
_LOOPBACK_HOSTS = ("localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1")

...

def secret_transport_ok(url: str) -> bool:
    """A credential may go to this Camofox URL: HTTPS, or plain HTTP only on loopback; no userinfo."""
    parts = urlsplit(url)
    if parts.username or parts.password or parts.query or parts.fragment:
        return False
    return parts.scheme == "https" or (parts.scheme == "http" and parts.hostname in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS)
```

**The problem:** This loopback-only approach restricts docker-based deployments unnecessarily. In order to run camofox on its own docker container, I need to create a faux-local network connection in its `docker-compose.yml` entry using:

```yml
  browser:
    image: ghcr.io/redf0x1/camofox-browser:latest
    container_name: browser

    environment:
      CAMOFOX_HOST: "0.0.0.0"
      CAMOFOX_PORT: "9377"
      CAMOFOX_AUTH_MODE: "disabled"

....

    # Share the primary node's network so it will appear as localhost to it
    network_mode: service:hermes
```

This approach **does** work, however it is also brittle. When the hermes container is updated/rebuilt (ie: replaced), or restarted this local network approach breaks, and requires a manual reboot of the `browser` container too to reconnect it to the correct network reference.

**The ask:** Allow for a config-driven property to inject an alternative allowed hostname (ie: the docker container name of the camofox browser container) so that it can also be used over http.

title: fix(camofox): gate plain-HTTP vault fills behind an explicit opt-in
body:
Fixes #291

## What this changes

`secret_transport_ok()` decides whether `browser_vault` may send a credential-bearing
script to the Camofox server: HTTPS to any host, or plain HTTP to loopback only. A Docker
deployment that runs Camofox in its own container can never satisfy that, so users resort
to `network_mode: service:hermes` to make the container look like localhost — which breaks
whenever the Hermes container is replaced.

This adds an explicit opt-in: `CAMOFOX_ALLOW_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=true` (or
`browser.camofox.allow_insecure_transport: true` in config.yaml) admits plain HTTP to any
host for operators who knowingly serve Camofox over an unencrypted container network. The
knob is declared in the plugin manifest so setup surfaces it. Everything else is unchanged:
HTTPS stays accepted, the loopback rule stays by default, and userinfo, query, fragment and
redirects keep being refused.

## Testing

- New test `test_secret_scripts_allow_plain_http_only_when_explicitly_opted_in`: pins the
  unchanged default (a container hostname under `CAMOFOX_URL` is still refused without the
  opt-in), the opt-in behavior (path allowed as on loopback; query, fragment, userinfo
  refused; any host admitted), turning the flag back off, and the config-key fallback.
  (RED on the previous revision, GREEN after.)
- Full `camofox` suite: **97 passed**.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate ./camofox` → passed.
- README's vault-fill paragraph documents the knob as the Docker alternative.

## Scope

Touches only `camofox` (vault guard + manifest + README). Default behavior is byte-for-byte
what it was on main; the knob is strictly additive.

title: fix(langfuse): scope trace state and shutdown to the active profile
body:
## What breaks

The SDK client is already cached per Hermes home (`_LANGFUSE_CLIENT_BY_HOME`), but the live trace state is process-global and keyed only by task/session/thread plus turn/request ids. In a process that serves more than one profile (home selected through the context-local home override), the same ids in two profiles collide:

- the second profile reuses the first profile's root span, so its turn is traced into the other profile's project;
- `_state_for_turn()` matches the `:turn:<id>` suffix in any profile, so subagent hooks can attach to the wrong profile's trace;
- `on_session_finalize()` with an empty `session_id` closes every profile's open traces, and at `reason="shutdown"` shuts the client down while the profile still has live traces, or shuts it down twice.

## Reproduction

Two profile homes in one process, the same `session_id` and `turn_id` in both, then `on_pre_llm_request` under each home override: `main` opens one root span for both, and finalizing one profile with `session_id=""` ends the other profile's trace. The new tests encode each case.

## Changes

- Trace-state keys carry the active home as a `profile:<home key>:` namespace, matching the client cache. Unprefixed (legacy) keys keep working.
- Turn lookup and session finalization only touch the active profile's state.
- A client is shut down only when its profile has no live traces left, and at most once (tracked in a `WeakSet`, not by `id()`, which a later client could reuse).
- The namespace never leaves the process. It contains the home path, so a turn without a session id exports its scope key without it, as before. A test pins this.

No SDK, manifest, hook or dependency changes; telemetry stays fail-open.

## Tests

Run as CI does (Python 3.14, core installed through uv with core's `override-dependencies`, `pytest` + `pytest-asyncio`, the plugin's own dependencies):

- `tests/test_langfuse_multiprofile_lifecycle.py` against `main`'s plugin: 8 failed (assertion failures, no collection errors), 1 passed (the export test, since `main` has no namespace to leak).
- The same file on this branch: 9 passed.
