- Full suite from `langfuse/` (`HERMES_AGENT_REPO=../../hermes-agent PYTHONPATH=../../hermes-agent python -m pytest -q`): 174 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 6 test files.
- `python -m hermes_cli.main plugins validate langfuse`: Validation passed.
- `ruff check` (default rules): no new diagnostics in `__init__.py` (2 before, 2 after), none in the new test file.

Only Linux was run locally; the Linux/macOS/Windows matrix is CI's.

## Release

Per CONTRIBUTING.md, merging does not ship this: the catalog pin `sha:` in hermes-agent's `plugin-catalog/langfuse.yaml` moves in a separate PR once this lands.

title: fix(directsdk): strip inherited ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the native env instead of failing the turn
body:
## Problem

Closes #157.

While `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set for Hermes' own `anthropic` provider (a normal setup: one Hermes serving both the API-key route and the subscription route from the model picker), **every** turn on `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` fails before Claude Code starts:

```
ValueError: OAuth provider refuses conflicting native auth/backend overrides: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
```

The conflict check (`directsdk.py`, `_run`) treats any inherited key as a hard error, so the two providers cannot coexist in the same environment — the key has to be removed from `.env` and the gateway restarted before a single subscription turn can run.

## Repro (live, hosted Hermes Cloud instance)

- Hermes gateway with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `$HERMES_HOME/.env` (used by the `anthropic` provider), plugin 0.3.4 pinned @ 83f0a89
- `claude` CLI 2.1.318 installed and logged in (`claude auth status` → `loggedIn: true`)
- One turn on the subscription provider → the `ValueError` above; Hermes retries, falls back, and the turn silently bills another provider

## Fix

The provider never forwards such overrides, so instead of failing the turn it **removes the conflicting keys from the child env** before spawning native:

- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY`
- `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` (when truthy)

Hermes' own client path keeps its key; native keeps the subscription OAuth login; each provider bills what it was configured with. The explicit `env=` path is unchanged and still never guesses.

The same change was validated live on the hosted instance where the repro was taken: with the key stripped at spawn, a real subscription turn completed through the provider (`model: sonnet`, `billing_provider: claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`, no fallback).

## Tests

- The old test asserted the hard error (`assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "OAuth")`); it now asserts the contract the fix establishes: a probe `Popen` captures the spawn env, and the child env must not contain `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` while the turn proceeds (`tests/test_directsdk.py`).
- Full `tests/test_directsdk.py` passes (6/6) plus `test_admission_one_shot.py` + `test_admission_restoration.py` (49) against a hermes-agent checkout (`HERMES_AGENT_REPO` sibling, per CONTRIBUTING).
- `hermes plugins validate .` passes.

Note: I could not run the full plugin suite on this hosted instance (some admission tests spawn real loopback relays and hang in this sandboxed environment); the changed paths are covered by the runs above.

title: [advanced-delegation] Support delegating tasks to profiles on other machines using native Hermes peers/Runs
body:
## Problem and use case

I use Hermes profiles on more than one machine. I would like `delegate_task` to assign a bounded task to an explicitly configured profile on another machine and bring the result back to the originating conversation, without manually composing a peer CLI command or introducing a separate orchestration service.

For example, a coordinator on one host could delegate a repository check to a coding profile on a second host, where the checkout and required tools already exist. Merely changing the model's `base_url` does not move the agent's tools or files to that host.

## Current behavior

Advanced Delegation's `profile_routes` backend selects a local profile. Its editor uses `list_profile_names()`, the provider returns a `profile` route, and core resolves that name through local `profile_exists()` / `get_profile_dir()`.

Hermes already documents direct gateway peers (`hermes peer dm`, `run`, `status`, `stop`), the Runs API, and profile-prefixed API routing. The missing capability is integration with `delegate_task`, not a new network transport.

## Requested behavior

- Configure an allowlist of named remote profile destinations, alongside descriptions the model can use to choose the right destination. Host addresses and credentials should not become free-form model arguments.
- Execute on the destination machine under the authorized target profile. Do not simulate this by copying the remote profile's model/tool credentials to the coordinator.
- Return a result attributable to the selected destination and remote run, preserving the existing local/model-route behavior for existing configurations.
- Refuse unavailable or unauthorized destinations explicitly; do not silently execute the same task locally or under a different profile.
- Prefer the existing peer/Runs primitives rather than a new SSH wrapper, custom remote daemon, or Desktop relay dependency.

## Lifecycle and security contract to settle

The current delegation-provider seam selects routes; core owns spawning, isolation, concurrency, background completion, stop, and result assembly. It does not currently expose a remote executor merely by accepting another route key. This may require a coordinated core extension; the plugin should not bypass the lifecycle contract.

For a first version, I would prefer a separate task-scoped remote execution rather than silently injecting delegated work into an unrelated persistent Bot Chat. Please clarify which existing Runs/session primitive fits this ownership model, and whether a core proposal should own that part.

The contract should state how parent depth/concurrency/budgets, destination tools/policy and interactive approvals apply. Authentication must be scoped to the actual destination profile. A network timeout after submission must not trigger an untracked duplicate execution. Stop should distinguish a cancellation request from confirmed termination, including when the peer is unreachable.

## Acceptance examples

1. Two gateways: an allowlisted remote profile completes a harmless tool task on its own host; the parent receives the result and destination/run identity. No remote model/tool credentials are copied to the caller.
2. Unknown destination, wrong-profile authentication, and offline peer refuse safely with no local fallback.
3. After a submission/response disconnect, reconciliation uses native admission/run identity instead of blindly resubmitting the task.
4. Parent cancellation or peer disconnection reports the actual known remote state; it never claims stopped solely because the local request ended.
5. Existing local profile routes and model routes continue to work. The remote capability should be composable with mixed routing rather than impose another mutually exclusive choice.

## Related work and evidence

- #260 and PRs #273 / #289 concern model/profile unification; they do not add execution on another machine. This request is complementary, not a replacement.
- Plugin code inspected at `83f0a896b3518c7131181838e340c9a80c79524d`: [profile_routes.py](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/83f0a896b3518c7131181838e340c9a80c79524d/advanced-delegation/profile_routes.py), [CLI profile picker](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/83f0a896b3518c7131181838e340c9a80c79524d/advanced-delegation/cli.py#L307-L314).
- [Core route resolution](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8e7cf55eb673ab4ee5a35cd41faf35592eb70bd6/tools/delegate_tool_routes.py).
- Official docs: [peers](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/bot-mode#bot-initiated-dms-across-machines-hermes-peer), [Runs/API routing](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/api-server), [delegation provider contract](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/delegation-provider-plugin).

This proposal is based on documentation/source inspection, not a cross-machine implementation or E2E test. It does not request public exposure of gateways, automatic peer discovery, credentials migration, or a model override inside a profile route.

**Next maintainer decision:** Is remote execution in scope for Advanced Delegation, with a minimal native core executor extension if required, and which session/lifecycle contract should a focused implementation preserve?

title: DirectSDK 0.3.4: full Hermes turns intermittently hit extra-usage 400 while minimal requests succeed
body:
# DirectSDK 0.3.4: intermittent full Hermes Opus 5.5 extra-usage 400

## Environment
- Hermes gateway on Windows 11; installed provider `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.4; Claude Code CLI 2.1.318 (also reproduced on 2.1.292); logged in with claude.ai/firstParty; no Anthropic API key or paid extra-usage authorization used in this investigation.
- In live Telegram and Desktop turns, provider attempts `claude-opus-5-5`; gateway falls back to Codex only after upstream 400.
- Anthropic response: `Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage, not your plan limits. Add more at claude.ai/settings/usage and keep going.`

## Timing matters
- Gateway log records successful **full** DirectSDK Opus turns before failures, including 2026-11-04 17:48:30 (329,018 input tokens), 17:48:51 (332,141), and 17:51:12 (332,470) in the same session later rejected at 17:53:19.
- After a gap, a different full session successfully completed nine Opus turns 20:20:29–20:23:43, with 256,272–286,668 input tokens; more full turns failed at 20:25 and 20:51. This is not a simple 'all full prompts fail' or 1M/200K incompatibility.
- A post-upgrade Telegram `test claude` turn failed at 20:51:28 with upstream 400; first request ID `req_011CgjBRGpb3EeF1mPVNMSud`; plugin then denied a native retry with HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED; fallback was `openai-codex/gpt-6-sol`.

## Local controls and November 5 differential
- Official `claude -p` with Opus 5.5 succeeds on the same host and login (`claude -p 'Reply with OK only.' --model sonnet --max-turns 1` returned OK on Nov 5).
- Invoking installed `directsdk.Client.create` directly succeeds with Opus 5.5 on: simple prompt; 54 tiny messages; system+tool; a 65K-token synthetic system prompt; and a 76K-token synthetic request with 24 inert tools, streaming/reasoning medium/max_tokens 4096. These controls do not prove they are billed to the same allowance as full gateway traffic.
- On Nov 5 with the same installed plugin and CLI, `hermes chat --provider claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental -m claude-opus-5-5 --ignore-rules -q 'Reply with OK only.' -Q --max-turns 1 --run-budget 35` succeeded **on DirectSDK** (log: 24,498 input tokens, no fallback). With standard Hermes rules enabled, equivalent short queries on `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and `claude-opus-5-5` all returned the extra-usage HTTP 400 then silently answered OK via Codex fallback. One Opus 5.5 example: `req_011Cgk6KyZJEUcKxfrcf12Rh` at 08:25 PT. This narrows the current distinction to the standard Hermes request shape/rules, but is not proof which field caused Anthropic's billing classification, especially given yesterday's full successful turns.
- The live Telegram turn at 08:27:52 PT failed with the same 400 (`req_011Cgk6XNdBfVigfj4FGfsUg`) and fell back. The installed catalog 0.3.4 has an update available; current catalog head `83f0a89` is titled 'retain request IDs on incomplete upstream responses', not a confirmed fix for this symptom. No package or gateway changes were made.
- `claude -p '/usage'` reports weekly all-model 40% used and reset Nov 7, 6pm Pacific; it did not provide a five-hour figure. No extra-usage charges were verified.

## Question
Why does a normal Hermes request get Anthropic's extra-usage rejection when an otherwise comparable `--ignore-rules` request succeeds on the same plan/model? Could this also depend on time-window/account eligibility, given yesterday's successful full turns followed by failures? Please correlate the request IDs and advise a supported diagnostic or fix. We do not want to enable paid credits, alter caller identity or change prompts to evade billing policy.

Please do not request raw conversation content or credentials in a public thread; we can supply additional redacted structural metadata privately if needed.

title: advanced-delegation 1.0.0: route editor crashes on Hermes 0.22.7 (require_readable_config_before_write returns None)
body:
## Summary

On Hermes **v0.22.7** the plugin installs and its read path works (`hermes delegation config --show`), but **every write path** (`save_routes`, `set_mode` — i.e. the route editor and `/delegation` mode switching) crashes with `AttributeError`.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.7 (2026.9.24), commit `b200f5bc60e3`, git install
- Python 3.14.9, Linux (Debian 13)
- Plugin installed from the catalog: `hermes plugins install advanced-delegation --enable`
  - version 1.0.0, catalog pin `e404b6816b20237a82f6fbe2749b5a576cf75dba`
  - `plugin.yaml` → `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.5"` (satisfied)

## Steps to reproduce

```bash
hermes plugins install advanced-delegation --enable
hermes delegation config          # pick Model routes, add a route, save
```

Any attempt to save the mode or the routes raises:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/ismail/.hermes/plugins/advanced-delegation/store.py", line 119, in save_routes
    _save_list("model_map", "options", options, default)
  File "/home/ismail/.hermes/plugins/advanced-delegation/store.py", line 115, in _save_list
    _write(mutate)
  File "/home/ismail/.hermes/plugins/advanced-delegation/store.py", line 83, in _write
    section = data.get("delegation")
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'
```

## Cause

`store._write()` uses the return value of the write guard as the config document:

```python
path = get_config_path()
data = require_readable_config_before_write(path)   # <-- returns None on 0.22.7
section = data.get("delegation")
```

In `hermes_cli.config`, `require_readable_config_before_write()` is a **guard** — it raises when the existing file cannot be read and otherwise returns `None`. It does not return the config dict.

## Suggested fix

Call the guard for its side effect, then load the raw config (this is also what `set_config_value` does):

```python
from hermes_cli.config import atomic_config_write, get_config_path, read_raw_config, require_readable_config_before_write

if is_managed():
    raise RuntimeError(format_managed_message("change delegation settings"))
path = get_config_path()
require_readable_config_before_write(path)
data = read_raw_config()
```

Going through `save_config(raw, strip_defaults=True)` is equivalent if you prefer core's normalizer.

## Workaround (routing itself works)

Writing `delegation.backends.model_map` with `read_raw_config()` → `save_config()` produces a working setup: `hermes delegation config --show` then prints the routes, and a spawned subagent runs on the configured route. So the bug is confined to the plugin's writer, not to the delegation backend.

Happy to test a patch on 0.22.7 if useful.

title: fix(hermes-security): make right-clicking a scan row open Open and Delete (0.1.1)
body:
## ELI5

On the Security page, right-clicking a scan in the list did nothing. Now it opens a menu with **Open** and **Delete**, so you no longer have to open the scan first to find Delete. A scan that is still running can't be deleted from the menu until you stop it. Separately, long values in the page's dropdowns now stay on one line and end in "…" instead of wrapping or spilling out of the box.

## Summary

- **Right-click menu on scan rows.** Each row in the Scans list opens a context menu with **Open** and **Delete**. Delete calls the existing `deleteScan`, so it asks for the same confirmation as Delete in the scan detail and refreshes the list. If the deleted scan was selected, the selection clears.
- **Running scans can't be deleted from the menu.** The item is disabled and reads "Delete (stop the scan first)" while the scan is `created`, `running`, `awaiting_analysis` or `finalizing`, so its agent never writes into a deleted scan.
- **Older Desktop builds keep working.** If the host SDK doesn't provide `ContextMenu`, `ContextMenuTrigger`, `ContextMenuContent` and `ContextMenuItem`, the row renders as the plain button it was before. Delete is still available in the scan detail.
- **Dropdown ellipsis fix.** The Radix select value doesn't keep the `className` the trigger passes to it, so the `.hs-select-value` rule never matched. The rule now also targets the `[data-slot=select-value]` span Radix keeps.
- **Version 0.1.1.** The plugin, package and dashboard versions move together, and scan manifests now record the package version instead of a hard-coded `0.1.0`.

| Situation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Right-click a finished scan | Nothing happens | Menu with Open and Delete |
| Right-click a running scan | No menu | Menu, with Delete disabled |
| Desktop without the shared ContextMenu | Plain row | Plain row (unchanged) |
| Long dropdown value | Wraps or overflows | One line, ends in "…" |

## Test plan

title: feat(advanced-delegation): per-route OpenAI Daybreak for model routes
body:
## ELI5

OpenAI's Daybreak program (the same models with reduced refusals for security work) could only be reached by subagents through an old alias model. Now any model route can turn Daybreak on for itself, on the real model such as Sol 6 or Luna 6, so you can keep a normal `sol` route and a separate `daybreak` route side by side. Hermes still only sends Daybreak from your own chats, on models your OpenAI account lists for it; anything else is refused with a clear error instead of quietly running without it.

## Summary

- **New route key `daybreak: true`** on `model_map` routes. A routed task gets `request_overrides.extra_body.access_programs.cyber: daybreak_blue`, the field core sends when the main chat's Daybreak switch is on. It is the route's own opt-in, independent of `agent.daybreak`.
- **Core's Daybreak rules are checked on every spawn**, and a task that breaks one is refused with a `DelegationRouteError` (never run on the plain model):
  - provider must be `openai-codex`;
  - the account's Codex catalog must list Daybreak for the model (`agent.codex_service_tiers.daybreak_offered`, the Desktop switch's gate);
  - the delegating session must be the owner's CLI, TUI or Desktop chat (`agent.session_source.DAYBREAK_SOURCES`).
- **Config validation:** a `daybreak` that is not a boolean, or `true` off `openai-codex`, skips the route with one warning, like other malformed routes.
- **`hermes delegation config`** offers a Daybreak switch only where the catalog lists it, validates it before saving, and drops it with a note when the model changes to one without it. `--show` marks Daybreak routes.
- **Settings-editor declaration:** the backend declares `route_keys = ("daybreak",)`. A core whose Desktop route editor reads that declaration offers and keeps the key; older cores never read the property.
- Version 1.0.0 → 1.1.0.

```yaml
- name: daybreak
  description: "Sol with reduced guardrails: security work."
  provider: openai-codex
  model: gpt-6-sol        # the real base model, not a *-daybreak-* alias
  daybreak: true
```

## Compatibility

| Core | This plugin | Result |
|---|---|---|
| any | 1.0.0 | unchanged: `daybreak` is not a route key |
| current `main` | 1.1.0 | works from YAML and `hermes delegation config`; the current Desktop route editor drops unknown keys on save, so the README says to set Daybreak routes outside Desktop there |
| core with the editor change (companion hermes-agent PR) | 1.1.0 | Desktop shows the Daybreak control only because this backend declares the key, and keeps it on save |

## Security

Daybreak is the approved account's own access. The plugin reuses core's surface gate and catalog check instead of its own lists, and fails closed when core lacks Daybreak support (the import fails, the task is refused). Only the route name and description reach the model; `daybreak` and the request field never appear in the `delegate_task` schema (tested).

## Test plan

- [x] Plugin suite against `NousResearch/hermes-agent` `main` on Python 3.14 (the CI setup): `156 passed, 2 skipped`
- [x] Same suite against the companion core branch: `156 passed, 2 skipped`
- [x] `hermes plugins doctor .`: manifest 1.1.0, discovery/import/registration OK
- [x] Live on a ChatGPT/Codex account: routes on `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna` with `daybreak: true` resolved through core's credential resolver, built a child agent whose request body carried `access_programs: {"cyber": "daybreak_blue"}`, and both got a normal reply from Codex; the plain route on the same account carried no access program
- [x] Live refusals: a `telegram` session source and a model the catalog does not list (`gpt-6.1-sol`) were both refused with the messages above


## Screenshots

**How it works**, rendered from captured output of a live run: the route config, `hermes delegation config --show` (excerpt), the request body each route sent to Codex, and the two refusals.

![Daybreak model routes: config, route list, live request, refusals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unsupportedpastels/hermes-official-plugins/eea4586cee107b89e6257a86480134c69cc215ef/daybreak-how-it-works.png)

**Desktop route editor** with the companion core change (NousResearch/hermes-agent#149677): the Daybreak control appears because this plugin declares the `daybreak` route key, and only for models the account's catalog lists.

title: [homeassistant] When an entity changes twice within one second, the agent only gets the first change
body:
### Plugin

homeassistant

### What happened, and what did you expect?

When an entity changes state twice within one second, the agent only gets the first change. A Matter lock does this on every lock and unlock: it reports `locking`, then `locked` about 80 ms later.

You only see this with a short cooldown, because the default `cooldown_seconds: 30` drops the second change anyway. With `cooldown_seconds: 0`, lock a Matter lock from Home Assistant. The agent gets "changed from 'unlocked' to 'locking'" and never "locked", so it thinks the lock is still locking.

The adapter builds the message id from the entity id and the current time in whole seconds:

```python
message_id=f"ha_{entity_id}_{int(now)}"
```

So both changes get the same id. The gateway accepts one message per id and refuses the second with `admission_conflict`. The error also stops the WebSocket listener. It reconnects after 5 s, and changes in those 5 s never arrive.

I expected every change to reach the agent. Fix and tests: #301.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.22.7 (Docker image), homeassistant plugin 2.0.1 (same adapter.py on main), Home Assistant 2026.11.0, Linux
```

### Logs

Home Assistant recorded `locking` at 10:13:17.856 and `locked` at 10:13:17.939.

```text
10:13:18,070 INFO gateway.run: inbound message: platform=homeassistant ... msg="[Home Assistant] Matter Back Door (lock.matter_back_door): changed from 'unlocke..."
10:13:18,554 WARNING hermes_plugins.homeassistant.adapter: [Homeassistant] WebSocket error: admission_conflict
10:13:18,558 INFO hermes_plugins.homeassistant.adapter: [Homeassistant] Reconnecting in 5s...
10:13:23,575 INFO hermes_plugins.homeassistant.adapter: [Homeassistant] Reconnected
```

title: fix(homeassistant): deliver both changes when an entity changes twice within one second
body:
Fixes #300.

## What this does

When an entity changed state twice within one second, for example a lock going from `locking` to `locked`, the agent only got the first change. Both changes had the same message id, built from the current second, so the gateway refused the second one and the listener reconnected. Now the id uses the event's `time_fired`, and both changes reach the agent.

## Why `time_fired`

Home Assistant puts `time_fired` on every event it sends over the WebSocket, as an ISO timestamp with microseconds. The adapter subscribes only to `state_changed` events, and Home Assistant builds each event message from [`Event._as_dict`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.11.0/homeassistant/core.py#L1459-L1471), which always sets `"time_fired": self.time_fired.isoformat()` (via [`json_fragment`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.11.0/homeassistant/core.py#L1500-L1502) and [`websocket_api/messages.py`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/2026.11.0/homeassistant/components/websocket_api/messages.py#L153)). So the adapter reads it directly, with no fallback. The same event keeps the same id, so the gateway still recognises it if it arrives twice.

## Changes

- `homeassistant/adapter.py`: one line, the message id.
- `homeassistant/tests/test_homeassistant_adapter.py`: `_make_event` gives events a `time_fired`, as Home Assistant does; a new test checks that two changes 81 ms apart get different ids. It fails on `main`.

## Testing

```
cd homeassistant
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=/opt/hermes PYTHONPATH=/opt/hermes python -m pytest -q
215 passed, 2 skipped
```

Run inside the hermes-agent v0.22.7 Docker image, where core is installed at `/opt/hermes`, on this branch rebased onto current `main`. I also checked it live with a Matter lock in Home Assistant and `cooldown_seconds: 0`: the agent now gets both `unlocking` and `unlocked`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(advanced-delegation): store._write must read config after the guard returns None
body:
On Hermes 0.22.7, `require_readable_config_before_write()` is a guard that raises when the existing file cannot be read and otherwise returns `None`. `_write()` used its return value as the config document, so every write path (`save_routes`, `set_mode`) crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`.

Call the guard for its side effect, then load the raw config with `read_raw_config()` (the same pattern `set_config_value` uses). All 117 tests pass.

title: fix(advanced-delegation): Daybreak routes run from the owner's gateway-hosted chats
body:
## ELI5

A model route marked `daybreak: true` was refused in your own Desktop or Webapp chat when the gateway hosted it. Hermes now reports which gateway chats are yours, and the route accepts those chats while shared rooms, connected agents and messaging chats stay refused.

## Summary

- `_daybreak_route` uses the core's verdict on the turn's chat (`agent.session_source.turn_daybreak_surface()`, from the chat's launch policy; core side NousResearch/hermes-agent#149846):
  - `True` (the owner's own gateway-hosted Desktop, Webapp or TUI chat, or a `/bg` task from one) allows the route;
  - `False` (a hosted room, an A2A peer, or a `/bg` task from one of those) refuses it, whatever the session source says;
  - `None` (nothing judged the turn: classic CLI, the TUI backend, cores without the helper) falls back to the session source, as before.
- A `/bg` task binds no session, so its source reads as `cli`. Without the `False` refusal, it passed from any chat.
- A cron job binds an empty platform, which also read as `cli` and passed, though the README says cron is refused. `HERMES_CRON_SESSION` now marks the source as `cron`, and cron is refused.
- README: the Daybreak rules name hosted rooms and A2A peers as refused, and explain the gateway-hosted case.

| Turn | Verdict | Session source | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Owner's gateway chat | true | `local` | refused | allowed |
| Hosted room or A2A peer | false | `local` | refused | refused |
| `/bg` from a non-owner chat | false | `cli` | allowed | refused |
| `/bg` from the owner's chat | true | `cli` | allowed | allowed |
| Classic CLI or TUI backend | none | `cli`/`tui` | allowed | allowed |
| Cron job | none | empty, read as `cli` | allowed | refused |

## Tests

- `test_the_gateways_verdict_decides_and_a_refusal_beats_the_session_source`: the table's first five rows, with a bound agent carrying each verdict. On a core without the helper, each row expects what the session source alone gives.
- `test_a_cron_job_is_refused_though_it_binds_no_platform`.
- Against the core branch: 163 passed, 2 skipped. Against a core without the helper: 163 passed, 2 skipped.

title: mcp-serve: --tools advertises the ten browser_* tools removed in Hermes 0.23.0
body:
## What

`mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py` still advertises the ten `browser_*` tools that were **removed** in
Hermes 0.23.0 (hermes-agent#143146): `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`,
`browser_press`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_back`, `browser_get_images`,
`browser_console`, `browser_vision`.

Browser automation is now a single tool, `browser_exec` (defined in
`tools/browser_use_cli.py`), and the plugin still lists the deleted names in:

- `mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py` — `EXPOSED_TOOLS` tuple (12 names) and `_URL_ARGS["browser_navigate"]`
- `mcp-serve/README.md` — the "`--tools` exposes" tool list
- `mcp-serve/cli.py` — the `--tools` help string ("web, browser, vision, ...")
- `mcp-serve/plugin.yaml` — the same description line

## Why it matters

`available_tool_specs()` skips any name that is not in the definitions dict, so the deleted names
never appear in `tools/list`, while the README and `--help` claim browser support works. Any
client prompt (or skill) that keeps calling the old names fails at run time.

## Suggested fix

Drop the `browser_*` entries from `EXPOSED_TOOLS` and `_URL_ARGS`, and update `README.md`,
`cli.py --help`, and `plugin.yaml`.

I would **not** substitute `browser_exec` here: it runs model-written Python on the host
(`tools/browser_use_cli.py`), which is the same reason `terminal`, the file tools and the kanban
tools stay out. Browser automation stays on the Hermes side.

```diff
--- a/mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py
+++ b/mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py
@@ EXPOSED_TOOLS: tuple[str, ...] = (
     "web_search", "web_extract",
-    "browser_navigate", "browser_click", "browser_type", "browser_press", "browser_snapshot", "browser_scroll",
-    "browser_back", "browser_get_images", "browser_console", "browser_vision",
+    # No browser tool on purpose: ``browser_exec`` runs model-written Python on this
+    # host, the same reason ``terminal`` and the file tools stay out. The ten
+    # pre-0.23 ``browser_*`` tools no longer exist in core.
     "vision_analyze", "image_generate", "skill_view", "skills_list", "text_to_speech",
 )
@@
-_URL_ARGS: dict[str, tuple[str, bool]] = {
-    "browser_navigate": ("url", False), "web_extract": ("urls", False), "vision_analyze": ("image_url", True),
-}
+_URL_ARGS: dict[str, tuple[str, bool]] = {
+    "web_extract": ("urls", False), "vision_analyze": ("image_url", True),
+}
```

## Verified locally (Hermes v0.23.0)

- `hermes mcp-serve --tools` exposed set = 10 bridge tools + `web_search`, `web_extract`,
  `vision_analyze`, `image_generate`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `text_to_speech`
- initialize + tools/list over stdio OK; `channels_list` returns real data
- `pytest tests/test_hermes_tools.py` → 10 passed (browser_navigate parametrization replaced
  with web_extract URL-scheme cases; fixture schema gains a `urls: array` property)

Related: #197 (vision_analyze local-path guard) — same file, worth a combined look.

title: fix(homeassistant): a trailing newline or extra target no longer bypasses the service and entity policy
body:
`ha_call_service` now validates the whole domain/service name (`fullmatch`), so a trailing line feed can no longer slip a blocked domain such as `shell_command` past the blocklist, and a custom `script.<name>` service is checked against the entity allow/deny lists even when the payload also names other entities. The same full-match rule now applies to `entity_id` in `ha_get_state` and `ha_call_service`, so a trailing LF cannot dodge an exact denylist entry either.

Salvages #178 by @arsiktech (their commit is cherry-picked unchanged, authorship kept).

What I changed on top: `_ENTITY_ID_RE.match` → `fullmatch` at both entity_id checks (the sibling of the service-name bug: `lock.front_door\n` missed a `lock.front_door` deny entry and the LF is dropped from the request URL), plus 2 regression tests (4 cases); the LF cases fail on the PR's own head.

Tests: homeassistant suite 172 passed, 2 skipped. The PR's original 14 new cases fail on main; the 2 LF entity cases fail without the follow-up commit.

title: fix(directsdk): the logged-out error names the CLI and login dir the spawn used
body:
When Claude Code reports no usable login, the `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` error now names the `claude` binary the plugin ran and the login directory that spawn used. A gateway or service that resolves a different CLI or login than the shell where `claude auth login` ran then shows that in the error itself.

Salvages #188 by @salch-cred (their commit is cherry-picked, authorship kept). Refs #47; does not fix it (that root cause is core's provider-profile lookup on the bot surface).

What I changed on top:
- The login dir now comes from the child's own environment (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else the child's `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` + `.claude`). The original used Hermes' `Path.home()`, which is wrong whenever the spawn's HOME differs (supervised gateways, explicit `Client(env=...)`), which is exactly the case #47 needs to diagnose.
- The test now pins the exact values (`cli: <resolved binary>`, `login: <child HOME>/.claude`) instead of only the labels; it fails on the original commit.
- CHANGELOG `### Fixed` entry.

Tests: claude-subscription-directsdk suite 498 passed.

title: perf(directsdk): tool-less requests skip the inert MCP helper
body:
A request with no tools no longer starts the inert MCP helper or writes its `tools.json`, so titles, summaries and other tool-less calls skip a Python start (~0.6 s) and one MCP handshake each. `--strict-mcp-config` still gets `{"mcpServers": {}}`, so native cannot pick up ambient servers, and tool-carrying requests are unchanged.

Salvages #190 by @creditlabsonarc-rgb (their commit is cherry-picked unchanged, authorship kept). Refs #42 (partial: the warm-process/pool items stay open).

What I changed: nothing in the code. I cherry-picked it onto current `main`, where it now applies without the earlier CHANGELOG conflict, and opened it as a regular PR because the original is a draft.

Tests: the new `tests/test_directsdk_mcp_skip.py` no-tools case fails on main and passes here; claude-subscription-directsdk suite 500 passed on this branch.

title: hermes-security: scan-create test no longer fails at random on fast runners
body:
One hermes-security test fails at random on fast CI runners and turns unrelated PRs red. It now accepts both answers the server can legitimately give at that moment.

`test_standalone_health_and_real_scan` asserted that the `POST /scans` answer still says `created`. The route starts the background inventory before it builds the response, and on macOS CI that thread can finish a one-file repo first, so the answer already says `awaiting_analysis`. The test's real check, the status after the thread joins, is unchanged.

It turned xchat #153 and mcp-serve #198 red on `hermes-security · macos-latest` (`AssertionError: assert 'awaiting_analysis' == 'created'`); neither PR touches this plugin.

Test-only change; `tests/plugin/test_workbench_api.py` passes locally.

title: hermes-security: two more Workbench tests no longer fail at random
body:
Two more hermes-security tests fail at random, the same way #308's did. They now wait for the scan's background setup to finish before acting on it.

A Workbench start answers immediately and finishes the inventory and dependency check on a background thread. These two tests acted on the scan while that thread was still writing to it:

| Test | How it failed |
|---|---|
| `test_scan_actions_policy_and_events` | Its read-back saw `dependenciesPending` flip between two reads. This is what turned #158 red on `hermes-security · windows-latest`. |
| `test_tests_allowed_scan_runs_local_controls_from_dashboard_and_agent` | It submitted work against a plan that wasn't finished yet (`$.snapshotDigest: expected string`). This failed on every run on a loaded Linux host, `main` included. |

Both now wait on the scan's background thread first, as `test_standalone_health_and_real_scan` already does. In real use the agent's next step stays `wait` until that thread is done, so this changes only the tests.

**Evidence:** on the same machine, `test_workbench_api.py` on `main` gives 1 failed, 48 passed on every run. With this change it gives 49 passed on 3 runs out of 3.

title: fix(mcp-serve): drop the ten browser_* tools removed in Hermes 0.23.0
body:
`mcp-serve/hermes_tools.py` still advertised the ten `browser_*` tools removed in Hermes 0.23.0 (hermes-agent#143146). `available_tool_specs()` skips unknown names so they never appeared in `tools/list`, but README, `--help` and `plugin.yaml` claimed browser support.

Drop the `browser_*` entries from `EXPOSED_TOOLS` and `_URL_ARGS`, and update README.md, cli.py, plugin.yaml and tests. All 10 tests pass.

Closes #304.

title: fix(meshy): overlapping saves of one task no longer 500 on Windows
body:
Two overlapping saves of one Meshy task (a double click, two windows) could fail on Windows with `500: could not write the file (Access is denied)`. Now the task sidecar `.meshy-task` is written once per folder under a lock, and later saves leave a correct sidecar alone.

**Root cause:** `_save_format` (`meshy/dashboard/plugin_api.py`, the `_write_new(folder / _TASK_SIDECAR, ...)` call) replaced the sidecar on every save outside any lock, so two threads `os.replace`d staging files onto the same name at once, which Windows denies with WinError 5 (no handle leak: the staging fd is closed by its `with` before the rename).

**Evidence**
- Failure: main push run, job 127798707353: `PermissionError: [WinError 5] ... .meshy-task.<hex>.part -> ...\.meshy-task` at `plugin_api.py:932` from `_save_format` line 1005, in `test_save_downloads_a_file_once_and_a_retry_finishes_failed_companions` (two concurrent `save` calls).
- New test `test_concurrent_saves_publish_the_task_sidecar_once` counts renames onto the sidecar across two concurrent saves plus a third: red on base (3 renames), green with the fix (1). Full meshy suite: 121 passed on Linux.
- `meshy · windows-latest` on this head (run 42191975316): 4/4 green (first run + 3 reruns: jobs 127805997576, 127808139370, 127810525645, 127811787637).

title: fix(homeassistant): do not report async state changes as already in state (#242)
body:
Fixes #242.

When Home Assistant returns an empty `changed_states` list for a service call, the adapter previously assumed the entity was already in the requested state. For async devices (e.g. Matter locks) HA returns an empty list because the state has not settled yet, so the adapter reported "was already in state" even though the call actually changed the state.

Now the adapter only reports "already in state" when the current state matches what the service would set (turn_on -> on, turn_off -> off, etc.). Otherwise it reports the call was accepted and the state may still be settling.

All 97 homeassistant tests pass.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Multiplexed gateway: profile's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ignored, and an inherited token overrides claude_config_dir
body:
**Plugin:** claude-subscription-directsdk (v0.3.4, `main`)

## What happened

On a multiplexed gateway (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`) the plugin cannot keep two profiles on two different Claude accounts. Two related gaps, both left after #34 / #59 (which added the per-profile `claude_config_dir`):

1. **A served profile's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` never reaches Claude Code.** The plugin spawns `claude` with `env=dict(os.environ)`. Multiplexing deliberately does not load a served profile's `.env` into `os.environ` (it is bound per turn as the secret scope), so a token set in `~/.hermes/profiles/<name>/.env` is ignored. The child gets whatever token the gateway process itself has.
2. **`claude_config_dir` is silently ineffective whenever the gateway process has a token.** Claude Code prefers an env `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` over the login in `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. Verified:
   - `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<empty dir> CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=<any valid token> claude auth status` → `authMethod: oauth_token`
   - same without the token → `loggedIn: false`

   So a profile that sets `claude_config_dir` still runs on the gateway's token, i.e. on another profile's account and quota.

## Measured

Gateway with profile `default` (token in its `.env`, so in the process env) and a second served profile with its own token in its `.env` and `claude_config_dir` set. I pointed `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` at a wrapper that logs only a SHA-256 prefix of the token the child receives, then ran one cron turn per profile:

- Second profile's turn received the **default profile's** token hash, not its own.
- Setting `claude_config_dir` for it changed nothing (the env token still won).

Impact: in a multiplexed setup that serves a restricted or shared-use profile next to a personal one, the restricted profile silently consumes the personal account. Isolation between profiles' Claude accounts is not achievable through the plugin's settings.

## Expected

- A profile's own `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (from the secret scope) is what its Claude Code child gets.
- If a profile selects a login directory (`claude_config_dir`) and has no token of its own, an inherited token from the gateway process must not override that selection.
- Single-profile installs and an explicit `Client(env=...)` behave exactly as today.

## Proposed fix

Small helper applied wherever the child env is built (right after `apply_config_dir`): resolve the token through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` (plugin catalog rule 11), set it on the child env only; else drop the inherited token when `claude_config_dir` is set; otherwise leave env alone. PR follows.

## Versions

claude-subscription-directsdk 0.3.4 (`main` at e7a218f), Hermes Agent current `main`, Claude Code CLI on Linux.

title: fix(claude-subscription-directsdk): per-profile OAuth token under multiplexing
body:
Fixes #313.

## Problem
On a multiplexed gateway, a served profile's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (in its own `.env`) never reaches its Claude Code child, because multiplexing does not load profile `.env` into `os.environ`. And a profile that sets `claude_config_dir` (#59) still runs on the gateway process's token, because Claude Code prefers an env token over the config-dir login. Details and measurements in #313.

## Change
- `directsdk_setup.apply_profile_credential(env)` (one helper):
  1. profile token from `agent.secret_scope.get_secret` (lazy import; `ImportError` / `UnscopedSecretError` / any error = no profile token) is set on the **child env only**;
  2. else, if the profile's `claude_config_dir` setting is non-empty, an inherited `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is removed from the child env so the selected login is used;
  3. else env is untouched.
- Called after `apply_config_dir` in the native spawn (`directsdk.py`, skipped for an explicit `Client(env=...)`) and in the setup/discovery child env (`_child_env`).
- `os.environ` is never modified; the token is never logged.
- No change for single-profile installs (`get_secret` returns the same value the child already inherited).

## Tests
`tests/test_directsdk_profile_credential.py` (20 tests): profile token wins over ambient; ambient token dropped when `claude_config_dir` is set and no profile token; env untouched otherwise; `ImportError`/`UnscopedSecretError` tolerated; `os.environ` never mutated; token value never appears in output; explicit `Client(env=...)` untouched; spawn and setup/discovery paths. With the helper turned into a no-op, 9 of the 20 fail, so they do catch the bug.

Full suite on my machine: 527 passed, 3 failed + 1 crash in `test_directsdk_setup` / `test_directsdk_vision` / `test_directsdk_admission::test_refusal_after_a_tool_call_*`. The same ones fail identically on `main` without this change (local core/dependency mismatch on my side); CI is the reference. `hermes plugins validate .` passes.

## Notes
- No `plugin.yaml` version bump: earlier fix-only changes did not bump it.
- A pin bump in hermes-agent's `plugin-catalog` follows after merge, per AGENTS.md.
- The bug itself was measured on a live multiplexed gateway (see #313). This patch is covered by the unit tests above; I have not yet run it end-to-end on that gateway.

title: fix(directsdk): answer native session-title side request locally before admission gate (#39)
body:
Fixes #39.

On a fresh conversation, Claude Code sends a session-title side request next to the first turn. The relay admits exactly one upstream request per call, so whichever request arrived first kept the admission. When the title won, the relay treated its tiny title response as the turn's assistant message and denied the real turn.

Fix: `admission.py::is_title_request()` recognises that shape (no tools, `output_config.format.type == "json_schema"`, schema properties exactly `{title}`). `Handler.do_POST` now reads the body before touching the gate and answers a recognised title request with 400 (`HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_TITLE`) without setting `gate.used`, so native catches the error and returns no title, and the real turn keeps its admission.

A body read failure now answers 400 instead of landing inside the forwarding try; Content-Length is optional.

title: fix(rea): restore 1000s per-server timeout now that Hermes supports per-server deadlines (#91)
body:
Fixes #91.

#90 dropped `extensions.com.nousresearch.hermes.servers.rea.timeout: 1000` from rea/plugin.json because Hermes v0.22.2's loader refused the whole package with "server declaration 'rea' has unknown keys ['timeout']".

Hermes now supports per-server tool-call timeouts via `mcp_servers.<name>.timeout` (tools/mcp_tool_common.py::_resolve_tool_timeout). This restores the 1000s deadline so large-binary Ghidra queries do not time out under the default 300s.

title: fix(directsdk): normalize native system context to a stable shape across requests (#38)
body:
Fixes #38.

Native rewrites its injected `role: system` message at messages[1] between request 1 and 2: on the first request it packs all reminders (including the date line) into one list block; on later requests it splits the date into a trailing system message and leaves messages[1] as a plain string. This shape change invalidates the cache prefix and freezes cache_read at request 1 mark.

Now stable_request_context normalizes messages[1] to the later shape on every request: list -> string, with the date line split into a trailing system message when present. All 29 stable-context tests pass.

title: perf(memory-wiki): per-session cache so refreshes skip rescanning unchanged sessions (#49)
body:
Closes #49.

Every dashboard request currently re-reads every recent session's messages and
re-runs the deterministic extractors over the full history — tens of seconds per
refresh on large profiles (80–90 s at ~500 MB / 47k messages here, 41–71 s at
1.79 GB per @liiopp in #49). #234 moved that work off the event loop, but the
work itself is the same on every request, even though nothing changed between
them.

### What this does

The per-session extraction only depends on that session's own row and messages,
so this memoizes it as one JSON "unit" per session, keyed under a fingerprint of
the cheap sessions-table fields the gateway already bumps atomically on every
append / rewrite / rewind (`message_count`, `tool_call_count`,
`transcript_revision`, `last_active`, plus title/preview/source/started_at):

- warm requests re-assemble the aggregates from units without reading messages;
- a write to one session invalidates exactly that session's unit — unrelated
  activity elsewhere never resets the cache (this is what kills the mtime-stamp
  approach from the earlier prototype in #49: on an active install some session
  is written every few seconds);
- units keep only what the aggregation can actually surface: snippets are
  capped at the per-slug top 5 `_finalize_subject` sorts down to, and the
  "no snippets" fallback snippet is stored once per unit instead of once per
  empty slug (a single session can have hundreds of those) — the aggregation
  materializes it back on delivery, so payloads stay identical while units
  stay 3–4x smaller;
- units persist to an atomic sidecar JSON under
  `HERMES_HOME/cache/memory-wiki/` (profile-scoped), so warm state survives
  gateway restarts; the store is bounded by unit count (2000) and serialized
  size (64 MB) with least-recently-active eviction;
- one process-wide lock lets concurrent cold requests share the same build, and
  each `HERMES_HOME` owns its own cache instance;
- `MEMORY_WIKI_CACHE=off` restores the uncached path, and `cache=None` (the
  default for every core function) keeps byte-identical legacy behavior — the
  aggregation code over units is the same code path the uncached branch uses.

### Numbers (copy of a real ~574 MB profile, 780 sessions, 29.5k messages)

Measured end-to-end on a cold process, asserting payload equality at every step:

- pre-PR main: ~76 s per overview request
- this branch, uncached (`cache=None`): ~88–91 s — payload asserted byte-equal
  to pre-PR main on the real profile, not just in unit tests
- cached, cold (first view): ~65 s
- cached, warm (repeat view, including after a restart): ~5–6 s
- cached after the gateway wrote to one session: ~7 s (only that session re-scanned)

Correctness: the cached payload is identical to the uncached one (asserted in
tests and on the real-profile benchmark); all tests that run in CI pass.

### Tests

New `tests/test_memory_wiki_cache.py` (9 tests): fingerprint sensitivity per
field, no rescan on warm requests, single-session invalidation on write, parity
with the uncached path (including from a reloaded sidecar), corrupt sidecar
recovery, count- and byte-bound eviction (including the one-giant-unit case),
and the env off-switch / profile scoping.
`conftest.py` gains a `memory_wiki_cache` fixture alongside the existing core
one.
