title: fix(camofox): allow a config-named host to receive a vault secret over plain HTTP (#291)
body:
Fixes #291.

## What this does

`secret_transport_ok()` in `camofox/camofox_vault.py` only allowed a credential-bearing script to a Camofox over HTTPS, or over plain HTTP on loopback. A self-hosted Camofox in its own container is reached by container name over plain HTTP (`http://camofox:9377`), so `browser_vault` refused to fill a saved login there.

The rule is now: HTTPS always; plain HTTP on loopback; plain HTTP on a host the operator named in the profile's own config.

## Changes

- `camofox/camofox_vault.py`: new `_allowed_plain_hosts()` reads `CAMOFOX_ALLOWED_PLAIN_HTTP_HOSTS` (comma-separated) or `browser.camofox.allowed_plain_http_hosts` (list or comma-separated string). `secret_transport_ok()` accepts a plain-HTTP URL whose host is on that list.
- The allowlist does not loosen anything else: userinfo, query and fragment are refused on every host, every other host still needs HTTPS or loopback, and the comparison is case-insensitive.
- `camofox/tests/test_camofox_vault_transport.py`: 10 new tests (the existing `test_camofox_vault.py` needs the `agent.browser_page_backend` seam, which this core does not have, so the transport decision is exercised on its own).
- `camofox/README.md`: the new setting is documented next to the vault section.

The env var wins over the config key, like the other `CAMOFOX_*` settings.

## Testing

```
cd camofox
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=... PYTHONPATH=... pytest tests -q
104 passed, 2 skipped
```

title: fix(directsdk): make Claude Code caller configurable per profile
body:
Full Hermes requests on our Claude Enterprise account fail with the plugin's hard-coded `hermes-agent` caller, while the same prompt completes with `sdk-cli`. Add a per-profile choice so users can select the caller without maintaining a source patch. **Refs #296**; follows the configuration suggestion in [this comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/issues/296#issuecomment-6691636040).

### Change

- Add `claude_code_entrypoint` to the plugin settings UI and CLI, restricted to `hermes-agent` and `sdk-cli`. Keep `hermes-agent` as the default.
- Read the active profile's setting at every native spawn: inference, auth status, model discovery and `/usage`. A reused client honors profile switches and later configuration edits without modifying the parent environment.
- Reject invalid values before spawning the CLI, including during login probes, rather than reporting a misleading login failure.
- Preserve artifact/title suppression and the existing transport, credentials and request admission behavior. Document that the entrypoint variable is internal and that account eligibility/usage metering are not guaranteed by either choice.

```sh
hermes config set plugins.entries.claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental.settings.claude_code_entrypoint sdk-cli
```

### Live reproduction behind this change

On November 6, 2026, using Hermes 0.22.7, DirectSDK 0.3.4 at catalog revision `e7a218f2`, Claude Code 2.1.311, Linux ARM64 and an Enterprise login:

| Caller | Full Hermes result |
| --- | --- |
| `hermes-agent` | HTTP 400 before tool execution; CLI exit 1; no fallback. |
| `sdk-cli` | The identical prompt executed a real terminal command and returned its output; two DirectSDK/Opus calls, CLI exit 0, no fallback. |

Both runs used `claude-opus-5-5[1m]` through the running gateway with normal rules, memory and tools enabled. The successful control had 39,098 input tokens on its first call and 39,224 on the tool-result continuation. We changed only the caller constant and refreshed the gateway between runs, then restored `sdk-cli`. These were fresh diagnostic conversations, not a byte-for-byte replay of private history. This production comparison used the existing local constant patch; the new configuration path is covered by the tests below.

The rejected request was `req_011CgnKvJwqBjFoYMM8NYLXV` (2026-11-06 20:44:45 UTC):

> Third-party apps now draw from extra usage, not plan limits. Ask your workspace admin to add more and keep going.

This adds a reproducible Enterprise data point to #296. It does not establish that every report in that issue has the same cause, that all Enterprise accounts behave this way, or which allowance a successful request consumes.

### Validation

- New regression tests fail on the unmodified upstream implementation (15 failed, 4 passed before the change).
- Full plugin suite on Python 3.14.5 against Hermes core `6b21d056`: **536 passed, 9 subtests passed**, including 22 new cases.
- `hermes plugins validate`: passed, including the settings schema and security scan. Existing private-core-import advisory remains.
- Real Claude Code 2.1.292 loopback admission/cache-wire evaluations: **passed with both the default caller and an explicit per-profile `sdk-cli` setting**. These run without account credentials or paid inference.

No catalog pin or release version is changed in this PR.

title: va-claims: VA Benefits plugin
body:
Adds the VA Benefits plugin (`va-claims`) as an official plugin.

**What it does:** files and tracks VA disability claims (21-526EZ) the way 38 CFR Parts 3/4, 14 and 38 USC 5107/5901-5905 actually work, plus a tracker for every other VA benefit (Post-9/11 GI Bill, VA health enrollment, CHAMPVA, SGLI/VGLI, pension, VR&E). Live claim status via the VA Lighthouse Benefits Claims API (sandbox or production), intent-to-file with the 12-month effective-date clock, deadline countdowns, and a Hermes Desktop VA Benefits page.

**Privacy:** local-first. The veteran's ICN is the only personal value that leaves the machine, and only to api.va.gov.

**MCP:** ships `mcp_server.py`, a stdio MCP shim exposing the same seven tools for non-Hermes clients.

**Checks:**
- `hermes plugins validate ./va-claims` — passed (clean scan, no collisions, SDK-only desktop surface)
- `python -m pytest va-claims` against a hermes-agent checkout — 6 passed (registration wiring, local-first tools, credential hints); the MCP test skips when `mcp` is absent
- card at `assets/va-claims.jpg`, README banner + top-level table cell added

Previously submitted to the plugin catalog as NousResearch/hermes-agent#150234; moving it here per the official-plugins contribution path. The catalog entry can then point at this repo.

title: fix(xchat): serialize writes to the shared sent-message-id file
body:
## Summary

`xchat/adapter.py::_remember_sent` records the ids of messages Hermes sends through the X Chat self-chat, so the poll loop can tell Hermes' own messages from ones the owner typed. It is a read-modify-write over a single shared JSON file (`sent_message_ids.json`), and the docstring explicitly says the gateway and out-of-process senders (cron, `hermes send`) share that file.

Two concurrent writers both read the list, both append their own id, and the second `tmp.replace(path)` overwrites the first's id — the first writer's id is lost. The temp file name was also fixed (`.json.tmp`), so two processes writing at the same time could even fight over the same temp file (truncated writes, Windows sharing violations). A lost id means a message Hermes sent is later treated as "typed by the owner", so the adapter answers its own message — a visible self-reply loop.

## Fix

- Serialize the read-modify-write with an exclusive lock file (`sent_message_ids.lock`) using `msvcrt.locking` on Windows / `fcntl.flock` on Unix, so concurrent writers no longer lose each other's ids.
- Give each writer a unique temp file name (`uuid.uuid4().hex`) so two processes never share a temp file.
- Retry the `Path.replace` a few times on `OSError` (Windows sharing violations) and clean up the file descriptor on every path.
- `_load_sent_ids` already swallows `OSError`/`ValueError`.

## Testing

Added `test_remember_sent_survives_concurrent_writers`: 20 threads each record 5 distinct ids; asserts none are lost. All 61 xchat tests pass.

title: fix(agent-importers): include -p <profile> in the printed cron resume command
body:
Fixes part of #265 (the per-profile path prints a resume command that fails as printed).

## Summary

When a Grok Bot / OpenBot import runs inside a non-default profile (`hermes -p scout migrate grok-bot ...`), the paused routines are created in that profile's cron store, but the printed follow-up command was always:

```
hermes cron resume <id>    # <destination>
```

without the `-p <profile>` flag, so running it as printed fails with "Job with ID or name '<id>' not found" (it looks in the default profile).

## Fix

`_print_routine_next_steps` now resolves the active profile from `get_hermes_home()` via `profile_name_for_home` and prefixes the printed command with `-p <profile>` when it is not `default`. The default profile keeps the original, flag-less form.

## Testing

`agent-importers/tests/test_grok_bot_import.py` (4 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change; verified they also fail on `main` before my edit).

title: fix(camofox): vault fills bypass ALL_PROXY too; scrub registered vault values at the tool boundary
body:
## What

Two hardening fixes on the Camofox `browser_vault` path:

- **ALL_PROXY bypass.** The secret-bearing `evaluate` POST passes `proxies={"http": None, "https": None}`. requests merges environment proxies and then drops `None`-valued keys, so an `ALL_PROXY`/`all_proxy` in the environment still routes the fill script (which carries the saved password) through the proxy, past the loopback/HTTPS check. Now `{"http": "", "https": "", "all": ""}`; an empty string survives the merge and means "no proxy".
- **Tool-boundary scrub.** `_dumps` and `_fail` pass every tool result through a new `policy.scrub_vault_values`, which runs core's `redact_registered_vault_values` over every string in the payload. That covers page-controlled fields such as a title or navigate URL that echo a filled value. If core exposes `redact_registered_vault_number`, JS Number-coerced numeric secrets are scrubbed too; otherwise numbers are left unchanged.

## Tests

`camofox/tests/test_vault_secret_hygiene.py`:
- plaintext non-loopback secret evaluate sends nothing
- secret evaluate never follows a redirect
- ambiguous authority is refused
- no environment proxy (`HTTP_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `ALL_PROXY`, `all_proxy`) carries a secret script
- snapshot and navigate output scrub registered vault values
- numeric coercion cases (skipped when core lacks the optional helper)

Against hermes-agent `v0.23.0`: **113 passed, 10 skipped**. Without the proxy change, the `ALL_PROXY`/`all_proxy` cases fail.

Independent of #292 and #320 (they change the plain-HTTP transport gate; no overlapping lines). No new tools, hooks or dependencies. Catalog pin bump (`plugin-catalog/camofox.yaml`) can follow on hermes-agent after merge, per CONTRIBUTING.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Tool-call arguments do not stream to Hermes, so "Preparing a tool…" never shows
body:
## What happens

Tool-call arguments reach Hermes only after the whole reply ends. While the model writes a large `write_file` or `patch` call, Hermes receives nothing it can show, so:

- Hermes never emits `tool.generating`, and the "Preparing a tool…" label never appears in the TUI, desktop or other frontends.
- All tool calls of a reply arrive together in the final chunk, after a pause the user cannot explain.

## Why

Claude Code already streams the arguments. With `--include-partial-messages` it emits `content_block_delta` events with `input_json_delta` pieces as the model writes them. In one measurement (macOS, Claude Code 2.1.304), a single tool call arrived as 86 pieces over 1.8 s.

The plugin drops those pieces:

- [`directsdk.py:974-979`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L974-L979) turns every non-text delta, `input_json_delta` included, into an empty heartbeat chunk. The heartbeat keeps the stale detector quiet (#113), but carries no arguments.
- [`directsdk.py:1076`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L1076) sends every tool call, with complete arguments, in the last chunk.

Hermes core now streams this provider (`supports_streaming`, NousResearch/hermes-agent#142905), and its chat-completions stream parser already accepts `tool_calls` argument deltas.

## Proposed change

Forward the pieces as OpenAI-style `tool_calls` deltas:

- On `content_block_start` with a `tool_use` block, emit a delta with the call's `index`, `id` and mapped Hermes `function.name`, and empty `arguments`.
- On each `input_json_delta`, emit a delta with the same `index` and the `partial_json` text as `arguments`.
- Keep the final chunk's tool calls for the response object, but do not send their arguments again in the stream. Hermes joins argument deltas, so a second copy breaks the JSON.
- Keep the existing behaviour for a refused turn ([`directsdk.py:1057-1066`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L1057-L1066) drops a cut-off call). This needs care: a call already streamed to Hermes cannot be taken back, so a refusal after partial arguments must still end with no tool calls in the final message.

Estimated size: about 25 lines in `directsdk.py`.

## Interaction with #221 and #256

- The API sends argument pieces as they are written only when the relay sets `eager_input_streaming` ([`admission.py:407`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/admission.py#L407), #156).
- #221 reports invalid tool JSON with that flag, and #256 makes it opt-in.
- If #256 lands, the API holds each argument until it is complete, and this change mostly helps users who turn the flag back on. Both changes can land independently.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] json_object structured output fails on every call: declare unsupported_response_formats
body:
## What happens

Every Hermes call that asks this provider for schema-less JSON (`response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`) fails, and it fails the same way on every attempt.

## Why

- Hermes' plugin LLM helper sends `json_object` when a plugin asks for JSON without a schema ([`agent/plugin_llm.py:450`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/agent/plugin_llm.py#L450)).
- The plugin accepts only `json_schema` and raises `ValueError('Only json_schema structured output is supported')` ([`directsdk.py:317-324`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L317-L324)).
- Hermes retries without `response_format` only when the error looks like a structured-output rejection ([`agent/auxiliary_client.py:3326`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/agent/auxiliary_client.py#L3326)). That check looks for `response_format`, `output_config` or a vendor parameter name in the message. The plugin's message names none of them, so no fallback runs.

## Proposed change

Declare the unsupported format on the provider profile:

```python
unsupported_response_formats=('json_object',),
```

Hermes reads this field ([`providers/base.py:245`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/providers/base.py#L245)) and drops the format before the first request, so the call runs on prompt instructions alone. The DeepSeek provider uses the same field for the opposite case ([`plugins/model-providers/deepseek/__init__.py:61`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/plugins/model-providers/deepseek/__init__.py#L61)).

The profile is built in `__init__.py`, so `profile.unsupported_response_formats = ('json_object',)` after construction (the same way `supports_streaming` is set) also keeps the plugin loadable on older hosts.

An alternative is to map `json_object` to `json_schema` with `{"type": "object"}`. Declaring it unsupported is smaller and matches what Hermes already does for other providers.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Errors raised before Claude Code starts are classified unknown and retried
body:
## What happens

Errors the plugin raises before it starts Claude Code are retried by Hermes, although no retry can change the result. The retries send no request and cost nothing, but they delay the error the user needs to see.

## Why

The request path raises plain `ValueError` for input it cannot send, before any process starts:

- unsupported request parameters or `extra_body` fields ([`directsdk.py:263-286`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L263-L286))
- an unsupported `response_format` ([`directsdk.py:317-324`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L317-L324))
- a missing model, or a timeout that is not a positive number ([`directsdk.py:764-791`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L764-L791))
- a conflicting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry override in the environment ([`directsdk.py:806-809`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L806-L809))

These errors carry no `status_code`, and `classify_api_error` handles only the cancel case ([`__init__.py:162-168`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/__init__.py#L162-L168)). Hermes then classifies them as `unknown`, which means "retry with backoff" ([`agent/error_classifier.py:67`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/agent/error_classifier.py#L67)).

## Proposed change

Return a non-retryable verdict from `classify_api_error` for these errors, for example `{'reason': 'format_error', 'retryable': False, 'should_fallback': False}`. To avoid matching unrelated `ValueError`s from deeper in Hermes, raise a plugin-owned subclass (for example `class RequestRejected(ValueError)`) at these sites and classify by that class, by name, as #77 does for its two classes.

## Related

- #77 handles the other two pre-request failures, `ClaudeCodeMissing` (status 503) and `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` (status 401), which today are retried or fall back to another provider. It needs NousResearch/hermes-agent#137928 to take effect, and fixes the case reported in NousResearch/hermes-agent#132337.
- This issue covers only the `ValueError` sites above, which #77 does not touch.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] No limit on concurrent native processes: a subagent fan-out starts one claude per call at once
body:
## What happens

The plugin starts one Claude Code process per model call and puts no limit on how many run at once.

- Hermes runs up to 10 subagents in parallel by default ([`delegation.max_concurrent_children: 10`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/a8b0bc15053c1d71fb2bfea39007847c9e1c5673/hermes_cli/config_defaults.py#L1359)), and child agents use the parent's provider.
- A fan-out can therefore start 10 `claude` processes plus 10 inert MCP helper processes on one subscription at the same moment.
- Auxiliary calls (titles, compression) start their own processes on top of that.

Each process uses about 250 MB of memory on macOS, and all of them draw on the same subscription limits at once.

## Why it matters for rate limits

- The plugin turns off Claude Code's own retries (`CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES='0'`, [`directsdk.py:818`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L818)) so Hermes owns retry policy.
- A plan or session limit comes back to Hermes as status 429 ([`NATIVE_ERROR_STATUS`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L69-L75)), and Hermes backs off per call.
- With 10 concurrent callers, every caller hits the limit, backs off and retries independently, so the burst repeats.

## Proposed change

An opt-in per-host cap on concurrent native requests, for example a plugin setting `max_concurrent_requests` (default unlimited, or a small number such as 4). Requests above the cap wait for a slot inside `Client._create` before they spawn, and the wait counts against the request timeout. A file lock or a counter in the plugin's cache directory makes the cap hold across Hermes processes (gateway, TUI and cron on one machine).

## Related

- #281 records Claude Code's `rate_limit_event`. A cap could later use that signal to shrink itself while a limit is active.
- #43 and #282 cover quota reserve and the extra-usage guard. Neither limits concurrency.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] claude processes outlive a SIGKILLed Hermes until their requests finish
body:
## What happens

When the Hermes process is killed with SIGKILL (an OOM kill, `kill -9`, a crashed desktop backend), its running `claude` processes keep running until their requests end. Each one can keep generating, and spending the subscription allowance, for minutes after nobody can read the answer.

## Why

- Each native process starts in its own session (`start_new_session=True`, [`directsdk.py:397-401`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L397-L401)), so a signal to Hermes' process group does not reach it. This is deliberate: it lets the plugin kill the whole tree on cancel.
- Cleanup runs from the request's `finally` block and an `atexit` hook ([`directsdk.py:441-448`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L441-L448)). SIGKILL runs neither.
- The plugin closes the child's stdin after the history replay ([`directsdk.py:944`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk.py#L944)), so the child never sees its parent go away. When its stdout pipe breaks, the request is usually already finished upstream.

#89 (closed) fixed cancellation and cleanup paths while Hermes is alive. It did not cover a hard kill.

## Proposed change

Two options, smallest first:

1. **Sweep on next start.** Record each spawned process group id with its parent pid in a small file under the plugin's cache directory. On the next spawn, signal any group whose recorded parent pid is no longer alive. This reaps leftovers on the next request instead of immediately, and needs no extra process.
2. **Parent watch.** Keep one end of a pipe open in the child (for example passed as an extra fd to a short wrapper) and kill the group when it reads EOF. This reaps immediately but adds a wrapper around the native launch, including the Windows `cmd.exe` shim.

Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` would also work there, but it has no macOS or Windows equivalent, so it cannot be the only mechanism.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Default claude_code_telemetry to off once /usage works without it?
body:
## Question

Should `claude_code_telemetry` default to off once `/usage` works without it?

## Cost of the current default

With the setting on (the default, [`directsdk_setup.py:114-140`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk_setup.py#L114-L140)), each native process does its telemetry and feature-flag work before it sends the model request. Measured on macOS with Claude Code 2.1.304, median of 3 runs, time from spawn until Claude Code sends its request:

| Setting | Time to request |
|---|---|
| telemetry on (default) | 0.77 s |
| telemetry off | 0.31 s |

The plugin starts one process per model call, and one Hermes turn makes one call per tool round, so the difference applies to every step of every turn.

## Why the default is on today

Turning the setting on by default was deliberate (hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#111). With it off:

1. `/usage` returns nothing, because Claude Code skips its usage fetch when nonessential traffic is off ([`directsdk_setup.py:330-332`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/blob/13b2c1c9c8204bf333df240b2aacf98c3e6250b7/claude-subscription-directsdk/directsdk_setup.py#L330-L332)).
2. The model picker lists fewer models: Claude Code's own picker shrinks, and the plugin's union with its pinned table (hermes-plugin-claude-subscription-directsdk#109) shows only the pinned models.

## What would change the answer

#258 removes cost 1: the usage probe drops only the nonessential-traffic flag for its own spawn. If it lands, the remaining cost of an off default is cost 2, models that Claude Code offers but the pinned table does not list yet.

Options:

- Keep the default on (current behaviour).
- Default to off after #258 lands, and keep the pinned table current when new models ship.
- Default to off for the request path only, and keep telemetry on for model discovery and `/usage` probes.

title: fix(advanced-delegation): load config after the read guard in _write
body:
Fixes #297.

## Summary

On Hermes 0.22.7 `hermes_cli.config.require_readable_config_before_write()` is a **guard**: it raises when the existing file cannot be read and otherwise returns `None`. It does not return the config dict. `store._write()` used its return value as the config document, so every write path (`save_routes`, `set_mode`, i.e. the route editor and `/delegation` mode switching) crashed with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`.

## Fix

Call the guard for its side effect, then load the raw config with `read_raw_config()` (with a fallback to `load_config()` on cores where `read_raw_config` is unavailable), matching what `set_config_value` does. This keeps the comment-preserving `atomic_config_write` round-trip intact.

## Testing

`advanced-delegation/tests/test_store.py` (4 errors are pre-existing: the test fixture monkeypatches `agent.codex_service_tiers.daybreak_offered`, which this hermes-agent checkout does not expose; verified they also fail on `main` before my edit).

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Hide Claude Code startup with a warm native process per conversation
body:
## What I'd like

A way to avoid starting a fresh `claude` process for every model call. Ideally there would be an opt-in setting that keeps a native process ready for the next request, so a turn doesn't pay Claude Code's startup on every tool round.

## Why

On my gateway, a normal Hermes turn makes 3 to 10 model calls, and each call spawns its own `claude -p` process plus the inert MCP helper. I measured the fixed cost on the same host:

| Step | Time per call |
|---|---|
| `claude -p` start until its `system/init` event (stdin closed, so no 3 s stdin wait) | 0.70–0.81 s |
| Inert MCP helper start + handshake (from your 0.3.1 changelog) | ~0.6 s |
| Waiting on native exit after `result` | ~0.55 s on 0.3.3; already removed in 0.3.4, thank you |

So even on 0.3.4, about **1.3 s per call** goes to startup. That's **4–13 s per turn** before the model does any work. For a short call, that's a large share: on 0.3.3 my median latency for calls under 40K tokens with short replies was 4.85 s; on 0.3.4 a 27.5K-token Opus call took 2.7 s. The network isn't the bottleneck (7 ms RTT to api.anthropic.com).

## A possible design: a warm spare, not a long-lived session

I understand why each request is its own process: a clean replay of Hermes-owned history, Hermes-owned compaction, and no native state carried between requests. A warm spare keeps all of that.

- After a request finishes (or when the client is created), pre-spawn **one** native process for the same profile, model, effort, system prompt and tool-manifest fingerprint. Let it finish Node startup and the MCP handshake, then wait on stdin for the stream-json frames.
- On the next request, if the fingerprint matches, write the frames to the spare; if it doesn't, kill the spare and spawn fresh, exactly as today. Within one conversation, the system prompt and tools usually stay the same between tool rounds, so most calls would hit.
- Each process still serves exactly one request, so replay, admission and cleanup semantics don't change.
- Bound it: one spare per conversation (or per profile), killed after N seconds idle, and never kept across a profile, auth or config change.

I can see one wrinkle: the admission relay and `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` are set per request at spawn. The spare would need its relay route created ahead of time, or a way to bind the route when the request arrives. You know that code far better than I do, so if a different shape fits better (for example, a long-lived process speaking a multi-request protocol), that would be just as welcome.

A setting such as the following would let operators opt in:

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental:
      settings:
        warm_native: true      # default false
        warm_idle_seconds: 120
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent `main` @ 9ffa7dff (updated Nov 7, 2026), Linux x86_64, 8 vCPU / 31 GB, systemd user gateway (Telegram + Desktop)
- Plugin `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` 0.3.4 (official plugins @ e7a218f2), updated from 0.3.3
- Claude Code CLI 2.1.293, Claude Max subscription
- Main model `claude-opus-5-5`, reasoning effort high

Thanks for the plugin. 0.3.4 already made a visible difference here.

title: fix(blender): enforce camera track-to framing, add solid backdrop rules, and harden Windows bridge launch
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses common rendering failure modes when generating 3D models or still renders via the Blender MCP server, and updates the documentation and reference material for modern Blender releases (4.x / 5.x):

- **Camera Framing Invariant**: Require and enforce `TRACK_TO` constraints targeting the subject or scene origin `(0, 0, 0)` rather than guessing arbitrary Euler angles, preventing cameras from pointing into empty space or cropping objects.
- **Lighting & Backdrop Rules**: Document 3-point studio lighting guidelines to prevent dark/unlit renders, and caution against `scene.render.film_transparent = True` when delivering renders to messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, Slack) where transparent alpha channels render as solid white or inverted blocks.
- **Modern Blender API Guidelines (4.x / 5.x)**: Document modern `bpy` API shifts (`scene.render.image_settings.file_format`, `bpy.ops.object.camera_add()`, removed `rot_euler` parameter in torus primitives, and Principled BSDF input conventions).
- **Windows Detached Bridge Launch**: Note shell quoting pitfalls in POSIX/Git bash on Windows (`cmd /c start` triggering UNC path popups or hangs).
- **Golden Procedural Donut Recipe**: Provide a verified, self-contained reference recipe with smooth shading, icing layer, scattered sprinkles, 3-point lighting, and dynamic output paths.

## Testing & Verification
- Validated scene generation, camera tracking, and headless rendering with Blender 5.x.
- Audited diff with automated SAST checks for secret and credential safety (zero hardcoded personal paths or credentials).

title: fix(mcp-serve): drop removed browser_* tools (#304)
body:
Fixes #304.

## Summary

`mcp-serve` still advertised the ten `browser_*` tools removed in Hermes 0.23.0.
Drop them from `EXPOSED_TOOLS` and `_URL_ARGS`, and update README, cli.py --help
and plugin.yaml.

## Testing

Import of hermes_tools verified.

title: fix(directsdk): declare json_object unsupported; classify pre-start errors (#327 #328)
body:
Fixes #327 and #328.

## Summary

- Declare `unsupported_response_formats=("json_object",)` on the profile so Hermes does not send
  schema-less JSON requests the plugin cannot handle (it only supports json_schema).
- Classify pre-start `ValueError`/`TypeError` (unsupported params, missing model, bad timeout, ...)
  as `format_error` in `classify_api_error` so Hermes does not retry deterministic input errors.

## Scope

This branch now carries **only** this fix — one commit on current `main`. It previously carried the
mcp-serve browser-tool removal (#310) and the advanced-delegation config-write guard as well; both
have their own PR, and the mcp-serve copy in particular was a stale variant that left the plugin's
own test asserting the removed tool list, which is why the `mcp-serve` CI job was red here.

## Testing

- The plugin's own test followed the second change: it asserted that a `ValueError` is left
  unclassified (`is None`), which is what the pre-start errors used to be. It now asserts the
  `format_error` verdict, and covers `TypeError` too.
- `claude-subscription-directsdk`: 505 passed, 15 skipped against current `hermes-agent` core. The
  one remaining failure (`test_blocked_stdin_has_deadline_and_cancellation[True]`, a 0.53 s vs 0.3 s
  timing bound) fails identically on `origin/main`, so it is not this PR.

title: fix(directsdk): default claude_code_telemetry to off (#331)
body:
Fixes #331.

## Summary

Default `claude_code_telemetry` to off, since `/usage` works without it (#258).

Claude Code sends its usage telemetry and fetches its feature flags. The feature flags are what
unlock newer and older models in the account's model picker, so turning them off can shrink the
picker from every model the account runs to each family's current one (#86). The default is now
off: the plugin starts the CLI with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC`, `DISABLE_TELEMETRY`
and `DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING` set, and the pinned model table fills the picker in. A user who wants
the flags back turns the setting on.

## What follows the default

The setting is read in every surface that mentions it, so the default had to follow:

- `plugin.yaml`: the config-schema default is `false`, so the plugin's settings UI shows the switch
  as off rather than on.
- `directsdk_setup.telemetry_enabled()`: the default is off.
- The usage probe names the reason the limits are missing: with nonessential traffic off the CLI
  answers `rate_limits: null`, so `/usage` says the fetch was skipped rather than that no plan
  limits were returned.
- `README`: the setting is documented as off by default, and the CLI command is corrected to turn it
  **on**.

## Testing

The plugin's own tests followed the default, and are updated with it:

- `test_directsdk_telemetry.py`: the default now asserts the quiet flags reach the child on both the
  setup probe and a turn, and an explicit `"true"` restores the feature flags (the old
  "explicit true matches the default" no longer holds).
- `test_directsdk_config_dir.py`: an unreadable config means the setting is NOT set, so the default
  (off) applies.
- `test_directsdk_account_usage.py`: the no-limits reply now names the telemetry-off reason, and a
  new test covers the telemetry-on path that still reports "Claude Code returned no plan limits".
- `claude-subscription-directsdk`: 505 passed, 15 skipped against current `hermes-agent` core. The
  one remaining failure (`test_blocked_stdin_has_deadline_and_cancellation[True]`, a 0.53 s vs 0.3 s
  timing bound) fails identically on `origin/main`, so it is not this PR.

## Scope

This branch now carries **only** this fix — one commit on current `main`. It previously carried the
mcp-serve browser-tool removal (#310) and the advanced-delegation config-write guard as well; both
have their own PR, and the mcp-serve copy in particular was a stale variant that left the plugin's
own test asserting the removed tool list, which is why the `mcp-serve` CI job was red here.

title: fix(directsdk): disable eager_input_streaming to avoid invalid tool JSON (#221)
body:
Fixes #221.

## Summary

Stop setting `eager_input_streaming` on tools: the API does not validate streamed tool
arguments, so a complete `tool_use` can carry invalid JSON and break the turn.

title: fix(rea): forward GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR from the environment (#116)
body:
Fixes #116.

## Summary

Forward `GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR` from the user's environment into REA's MCP server env,
now safe after hermes-agent drops unset `${VAR}` entries.

title: fix(directsdk): search common Windows install locations for claude (#47)
body:
Fixes #47.

## Summary

On Windows, `_install_prefixes` skipped system locations entirely, so a `claude` binary
installed under Program Files (or npm's global bin) was never found on the bot/gateway
surface where PATH is minimal. Add the common Windows install locations to the search.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: surface the request id and category of safeguard refusals
body:
### Problem

When the Anthropic safeguards refuse a request, the plugin knows the upstream request id (`admission.request_id`, read from the `request-id` response header in `admission.py`) and the refusal category (`stop_details.category`), but neither reaches the user or the logs. Hermes' notice only says "Cyber safeguards flagged this message".

Anthropic's false-positive report form (https://claude.com/form/cyber-block-false-positive-report-cvp-rejection-appeal) asks for the request id, so users of this provider currently cannot file a useful report. In the Claude Code UI there is also a thumbs-down button for blocked replies; through Hermes (e.g. Telegram) there is no equivalent.

### Proposal

- Log one line per refusal (time, model, request id, category) at WARNING level, or to a small `refusals.log`.
- Pass the request id and category into the refusal text Hermes shows (for example a trailing `Request ID: req_...`), so the user can copy it straight into the report form.

I run a local patch that appends `{"time","model","request_id","category"}` to `~/.hermes/logs/refusals.log` right after `native_admission` is built in `directsdk.py`; happy to open a PR if that shape is acceptable.

title: fix(claude-subscription-directsdk): map mcp__<tool> (dropped server segment) to the offered tool
body:
Native Claude Code sometimes names a tool `mcp__<tool>` (drops only the server segment of `mcp__hermes__<tool>`). `directsdk.py` handles the full prefix and the bare name (#62) but not this form, so core's `_repair_tool_call` repairs it and logs `Auto-repaired tool name: mcp__tool_call -> tool_call` on every such call. In one install that was 105 lines (tool_call 75, tool_search 11, hindsight_recall 10, hindsight_retain 8, tool_describe 4), no failures: cosmetic.

Fix: 4 lines in the tool_use loop, after the bare-name branch: map `mcp__<tool>` to `PREFIX + <tool>` when `<tool>` is an offered name. Replayed history keeps the offered name.

Test: `test_server_segment_slip_maps_to_the_tool_and_replays_with_the_offered_name` (clone of the #62 bare-name test). `python -m unittest tests.test_directsdk`: 7/7 pass with the fix, the new test fails without it. Based on 13b2c1c.

title: X Chat installation blocked on native Windows ARM64: no compatible chatxdk==0.4.1 build
body:
### Problem
Installing the official `xchat` plugin fails when Hermes tries to enable it because its pinned dependency, `chatxdk==0.4.1`, has no compatible wheel for my environment.

### Environment
- Windows 11 on ARM64 (Snapdragon X Elite)
- Hermes running natively on ARM64 (verified using its active Python executable)
- Python 3.14.9
- Plugin reviewed pin shown in the catalog: `e7a218f2`

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open the Hermes Desktop plugin catalog.
2. Install the official `xchat` plugin.
3. Enabling the plugin fails during dependency resolution.

### Error
Relevant excerpt from the installation error (line breaks added for readability):

```text
enable refused: Plugin 'xchat' conflicts with the dependencies pinned by Hermes core or
an enabled plugin, so it was not admitted. Resolver: uv lock exited 1: error: No solution
found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.14'
and platform_machine == 'ARM64' and sys_platform == 'win32')
```

The resolver then reports that `chatxdk==0.4.1` has no compatible wheels for that combination and concludes that the workspace requirements are unsatisfiable.

### Expected behaviour
The plugin should support native Windows ARM64, or the catalog should clearly identify this platform as unsupported before installation.

### Request
Could you confirm whether native Windows ARM64 support is planned, and whether this requires an upstream `chatxdk` build or a dependency change in the plugin?

I want to keep Hermes running natively rather than switch to x64 emulation. The plugin has been uninstalled for now.

title: fix(hermes-security): don't show a scan as paused while its workers are running
body:
## ELI5

A security scan could say "Paused — could not continue automatically" even while it was working and finding things. That happened when the chat turned down the plugin's automatic "keep going" message: the plugin called the scan paused without checking whether its helpers were still running. Their results come back to the chat and keep the scan going, so it wasn't paused. Now it only says paused when nothing is running and the scan really is stuck.

## Summary

- At the end of each chat turn, the auto-continue hook tries to queue a "Continue security scan" message. When the host refuses it, the hook set the scan's reason to `paused: could not continue automatically`.
- It did that even when workers dispatched for the scan were still running. Their results come back into the parent chat and drive its next turn, so the scan was not stalled. Every accepted result counts as progress and clears the label, and the next turn end sets it again, so the label flipped on and off the whole time the scan ran.
- Now, when the inject is refused and `next_step` reports live workers (`running > 0`, which already excludes stale and already-accepted dispatches), the hook returns `workers-running`, doesn't record a pause event or `offAt`, and clears a stale `PAUSED_OFF` reason.
- A refused continue with no workers running still pauses the scan exactly as before. The `CAP` stuck guard, the user-interrupt guard and the one-queued-continue guard are unchanged.

| Situation at turn end | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Continue delivered | scheduled | scheduled (unchanged) |
| Refused, workers running | `paused: could not continue automatically` + `autoresume.paused` event | no pause; stale paused reason cleared |
| Refused, nothing running | paused | paused (unchanged) |

## Test plan

- [x] New `test_injection_refused_while_workers_run_is_not_a_pause`: one worker running, step still `dispatch`, inject refused across two turns → reason stays `None`, no `autoresume.paused` event, guard count unchanged; after the worker stops, a refused continue pauses again. It failed before the fix and passes after.
- [x] Full `hermes-security` suite: 649 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed.




## Infographic

![running-means-running](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b59e/aZYredeXlk-rR5j-nS_v4_alomo8wU.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): start each scan in its own chat
body:
## ELI5

Starting a new security scan on a repo you'd scanned before put the new scan into the old scan's chat instead of opening a fresh one. That happened because every scan's chat for the same repo got the same name, and Hermes treats a chat name like an address: asking for a new chat with a name that's already taken reopens the existing one. Each scan's chat now carries a short piece of the scan's ID in its name, so every new scan opens its own new chat.

## Summary

- The workbench's **New scan** creates the scan's chat with `session.create` and the title `Security scan · <repo>`.
- Chat titles are unique per profile, and a titled `session.create` resolves an existing chat holding that title before minting a new one. So the second and later scans of a repo were linked to, and run in, the first scan's chat.
- The title is now `Security scan · <repo> · <first 6 hex of the scan id>` (for example `Security scan · hermes-mobile · 669d51`), built by a new exported `scanChatTitle(id, path)`. Each scan gets its own chat, and the suffix matches the scan id shown in the workbench.
- Nothing else changes: **Open chat** and **Continue scan** still use the chat linked to that scan, and the chat-draft fallback for backends that can't create sessions is unchanged.

| Action | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| First scan of a repo | new chat `Security scan · repo` | new chat `Security scan · repo · <id>` |
| Later scan of the same repo | reopened the first scan's chat | new chat for that scan |
| Open chat / Continue scan | scan's linked chat | scan's linked chat (unchanged) |

## Known gap (out of scope)

**Fix in chat** on a finding uses the title `Fix: <finding title>`, so fixing the same finding again reopens the earlier fix chat. That may be the behavior people want, so this PR leaves it alone.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/e2e/test_security_workbench.mjs`: the New scan → `session.create` assertions now expect the per-scan title, and a new check confirms two scans of the same repo get different titles (`node --test tests/e2e/*.mjs`: 53 pass, 0 fail).
- [x] Full Python suite: 648 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- [ ] Not exercised live in Desktop yet: the plugin a running Desktop backend has loaded only changes after a restart.

## Infographic

![a-fresh-chat-every-scan](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b5c9/Gt2k9-hF8p8nXxcmATtKU_AyyDyVYq.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): summarize workers and repeated gaps in report.md
body:
## ELI5

A finished security report had hundreds of lines nobody can use: one line per behind-the-scenes helper saying it finished ("Review worker att_…: accepted"), and one line per security checklist item that wasn't checked off, all saying the same thing. The report now says each of those once, as a count ("Review workers: 165 accepted", "149 ASVS controls are unknown: …"), and points to the data file that still has every detail.

## Summary

- **Review workers:** `report.md` printed one bullet per review worker with its attempt ID and status. A real scan of a mobile app repo produced 165 of these, all `accepted`, sitting right after the OWASP table. They're now one line in the Coverage section, for example `Review workers: 120 accepted, 1 rejected, 1 missing. coverage.json lists each one.`
- **Limitations:** every open OWASP lane or ASVS control was its own bullet. The same scan had 152 nearly identical lines like `ASVS control V1.1.1 is unknown: no explicit control coverage unit.` Gaps with the same kind, state and reason now collapse to one line with a count. Several `Worker packet … has no accepted result.` gaps collapse the same way. A gap that appears only once, such as an unsupported file with its specific reason, stays exactly as written.
- **Incomplete banner:** it said `154 coverage gaps are listed under Limitations`. That count no longer matches the grouped list, so it now says `The coverage gaps are listed under Limitations.` A single gap is still quoted in the banner.
- **Unchanged:** `coverage.json` (every worker and every gap), the scan's `partial`/`complete` status, findings, SARIF, CSV and JSON exports. Reports already sealed are not rewritten.

| Report part | Before (real scan) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Worker list | 165 `- Review worker att_…: accepted` bullets | `Review workers: 165 accepted. coverage.json lists each one.` |
| ASVS gaps under Limitations | 152 bullets | 2 bullets (149 with one reason, 3 with another) |
| Other gaps | 2 file-specific bullets | the same 2 bullets |
| Whole `report.md` | 4,535 lines | 4,057 lines; the rest is the 30 findings |

## Test plan

- [x] New `test_markdown_summarizes_workers_and_repeated_gaps`: 122 workers with mixed statuses become one count line with no attempt IDs; 40 identical ASVS gaps and 3 packet gaps each become one line; one-off gaps keep their text; a single worker gets no "lists each one" pointer.
- [x] Re-rendered the real scan's sealed `coverage.json`/`findings.json` with the new renderer and compared it with its sealed `report.md` (numbers in the table above).
- [x] Full Python suite: 649 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed. JS workbench suite: 53 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] `UPSTREAM_PROVENANCE.json`: `markdown.py` is adapted from upstream and pinned by hash; the pin is updated, and the new `test_provenance_pins_match_the_shipped_files` fails CI on any stale pin (the old test checked only the hash format).

## Infographic

![a-shorter-report](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b64c/gShi3DcB2S4xo40kL3vdl_XMsm0nng.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): lay report.md out for a human reader
body:
## ELI5

A finished security report was hard to read: you had to scroll through thousands of lines to see what was found, how bad each problem was and how to fix it, and the report was full of internal IDs and code-style labels. Now it opens with a table of every finding that links to each one, puts related problems next to each other, and shows how bad each one is and how to fix it before the detailed proof. The internal noise is gone, and the full details are still in the data files next to the report.

> Stacked on #346: this branch contains its two commits (`caabe7b`, `73eb6a9`). Merge #346 first, or review only the last commit (`6405b40`) here.

## Summary

**Find things fast**
- **Header:** the repository name and short commit (`NousResearch/hermes-mobile`, Commit `8c20dd6` · Standard scan · 2026-11-09) instead of the plugin's clone path and a 40-character hash. A local folder scan also shows its path.
- **Summary table** right after the banner: number, severity, linked title, `file:line`, and the first sentence of the fix. Each finding has an `#finding-N` anchor.
- **Grouped by weakness type**, decided by the finding's first mapped CWE: memory and resource exhaustion, sign-in/sessions/credentials, access control, sensitive data exposure, links/URLs/outbound requests, injection, code and dependency integrity, and other. The worst group comes first, the worst finding first within each group, and findings are numbered in reading order.

**Each finding reads top-down**
- Under the title: severity, location, evidence state and validation status.
- Then the summary, **Fix**, and regression tests, before root cause, attack path and evidence.
- Assumptions, existing controls, counter-evidence and proof gaps used to be four separate sections. They're now one **What could make this wrong** list (`Assumes:`, `Existing control:`, `Not verified:`), with exact duplicates removed.
- Code fences carry a language (`swift`, `kotlin`, `python`, ...) for highlighting. Excerpts over 30 lines keep 12 lines at each end and name the left-out line range. The median excerpt is about 10 lines, so this touches only very long ones.
- Empty taxonomy fields (`ASVS: .` on every finding) are dropped, and CWE/OWASP move to one closing `Classification:` line.
- The dependency finding no longer repeats generic attack steps; it points to the **Dependency check** table.

**Less noise, plainer words**
- The incomplete banner says what was reviewed and what's still open, for example `Reviewed 2,838 of 2,840 files and 10 of 10 OWASP Top 10 categories. Still open: 152 ASVS checklist controls with no recorded review; 2 files not fully reviewed.`
- Coverage, the dependency table and OWASP move after the findings. OWASP rows read `Reviewed by 118 workers. Latest note: ...` instead of listing worker IDs. Exclusions read `.git — Git metadata` instead of `git\_metadata`. Times read `2026-11-09 00:20 to 01:07 UTC`. Open units are listed once, under Limitations, with `file:` prefixes and state names made plain.
- Dependency finding summary: "1 package ... **has** 2 published advisories" (was "have").

**Unchanged:** `findings.json`, `coverage.json`, `scan-manifest.json`, SARIF/CSV/JSON exports, severity and completeness decisions, and the code-fence escaping. A fence is still longer than any backtick run in the excerpt, now with a language tag. Already sealed reports are not rewritten.

## Before / after on a real scan (30 findings, mobile app repo)

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Find a finding | scroll; titles only as headings | summary table with links |
| Order | severity only | weakness group, then severity |
| Fix position | last section of each finding | right after the summary |
| Uncertainty sections | 4 per finding | 1 per finding |
| Code highlighting | none | language-tagged fences |
| Worker IDs in OWASP table | 5 per row | none |
| Length | 4,057 lines (after #346) | 3,821 lines |

The length drops only modestly, because most of the report is the 30 findings' real content (about 1,440 lines of quoted code). The gain is in ordering and scanability, not size.

## Test plan

- [x] New `test_markdown_is_laid_out_for_a_reader`: header from a clone path, banner counts, summary table and anchors, a manifest location without a fake line number, group order and numbering, fix-before-proof order, the merged caveats list, no empty ASVS, a language-tagged fence, a 40-line excerpt trimmed with the exact left-out range, the dependency entry pointing to its table, plain exclusion labels, OWASP rows without worker IDs, and section order.
- [x] Existing tests updated only where the format intentionally changed: fence assertions now include the language tag (the escaping property is unchanged), `Proof gaps` → `Not verified:`, the grouped-gap wording, and the scan-time format.
- [x] Full Python suite: 651 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed. JS workbench suite: 53 pass, 0 fail. `markdown.py` provenance pin updated.
- [x] Re-rendered the sealed hermes-mobile scan with the new renderer and read the output.

## Infographic

![a-report-built-for-humans](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b690/hON9rXWh_yO5oBWH9j9SJ_SDIJqxCE.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): ASVS controls no longer decide whether a scan is complete
body:
## ELI5

Every security scan said "incomplete", even when it had read every file and checked every OWASP category. That's because the plugin also counted a 152-item checklist (ASVS) that no reviewer is ever asked to fill in. Now a scan is complete when every file and all ten OWASP categories are done, and the report says how many checklist items were checked, as information only.

> Stacked on #347 (which is stacked on #346). Merge those first, or review only the last commit here.

## Summary

- `mandatory_gaps` now returns only unclosed OWASP lanes, and the coverage builder and finalize check skip submitted `asvs:` units. No review packet assigns ASVS controls; the planner only assigns files and lanes. So every applicable control stayed `unknown`, and every scan ended `partial`. A real mobile-app scan reviewed 2,838 of 2,840 files and all 10 OWASP categories, and was still marked incomplete with 152 ASVS gaps.
- The ASVS ledger is unchanged in `coverage.json` (`standards.asvs.controls`). The new `asvs_summary()` counts applicable controls by state, plus how many relate to reported findings.
- The report's Coverage section gets one informational line, for example `ASVS 5.0.0 checklist (informational; it does not decide completeness): 0 of 152 applicable controls recorded as reviewed (152 not yet reviewed). 3 controls relate to reported findings. coverage.json lists each control.`
- The audit skill, `references/artifact-contract.md` and the README say the same. Workers record an `asvs:` unit only when they actually checked that control.
- **Still incomplete when it should be:** unreviewed or unsupported files, unclosed OWASP lanes, missing worker results and a failed dependency check all still mark a scan partial. On the mobile scan, the two minified `novnc.js` bundles marked unsupported keep it partial, which is correct.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_unreviewed_asvs_controls_alone_never_make_a_scan_incomplete`: all lanes closed with ASVS untouched gives no mandatory gaps, and `asvs_summary` counts the unknown and finding-mapped controls.
- [x] `test_explicit_closures_and_evidence` now asserts a deferred ASVS control is counted, not a gap.
- [x] `test_asvs_is_reported_as_an_informational_count`: the exact report line, including singular/plural.
- [x] `test_open_asvs_units_never_make_a_reviewed_scan_partial` (full scan path) and `test_finalize_ignores_open_asvs_units`: submitted `asvs:` units that are deferred, failed or unknown keep their state in the ledger but add no gap, in both the coverage builder and the finalize check. Both fail without the change.
- [x] Full Python suite: 655 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed. Provenance pins updated (skill, contract, `markdown.py`, `finalize.py`).



## Infographic

![complete-when-its-done](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1b76a/vrb_PuwfPxaE4M-sQQeZe_27AZat8p.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): say how to turn on automatic continue when the host refuses it
body:
## ELI5

The security plugin can keep a scan going by itself, but only if you've switched that on once. Without it, scans just stopped and said "could not continue automatically", with no hint how to fix that. Now the scan page shows the exact command to switch it on, next to a Continue button.

## Summary

- The host refuses a plugin's injected turn unless `plugins.entries.hermes-security.allow_gateway_injection` is `true`. In a live Desktop session, the log showed that refusal on every turn end (`inject_message: gateway injection denied for plugin hermes-security; set plugins.entries.hermes-security.allow_gateway_injection: true`). The workbench only showed `Paused — could not continue automatically`, and the activity event blamed "the chat is closed or automatic continue is turned off".
- The scan view now shows a notice for that pause: it says automatic continue is off or the chat is closed, gives `hermes config set plugins.entries.hermes-security.allow_gateway_injection true` and "restart Hermes", and has a **Continue** button. It replaces the generic chat-activity line for that state only. The "needs attention" and stall notices are unchanged.
- The `autoresume.paused` event names the same setting.
- The README already documented the opt-in, so it's unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] The workbench e2e stalled-scan test renders the `could not continue automatically` pause and checks the notice text, the exact command (`AUTO_CONTINUE_SETTING`), and that the stall text isn't shown at the same time. JS suite: 53 pass.
- [x] Full Python suite: 648 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed.

title: fix(hermes-security): packages installed only for development count as low
body:
## ELI5

The dependency check rated a testing tool (pytest) the same as code that ships in the app, so a problem in a tool only developers run became one of the scan's two most serious findings. The plugin now reads the lockfile to see which packages are only for development, labels them "development only" and counts them as low.

## Summary

- osv-scanner reports no dependency groups for `uv.lock`, so `summarize` couldn't tell dev packages from shipped ones. The new `dependencies.dev_only_packages(path, read)` reads the lockfile itself:
  - **`uv.lock`:** names reachable only from the project's `dev-dependencies` groups and never from its `dependencies` or `optional-dependencies` (extras can ship). A name on both paths ships. Local packages that another local package lists only as a dev dependency (a workspace test-helpers member) are dev tools, not shipped roots, so what they pull in is dev-only too. If that would leave no roots, every local package counts as shipped.
  - **`package-lock.json`:** entries marked `"dev": true` with no shipped entry of the same name. `devOptional` counts as shipped.
  - **Anything else, or a lockfile that doesn't say** (no project package in a `uv.lock`): every package counts as shipped.
- Leads for those names carry `devOnly: true`. The aggregate dependency finding counts them as low, names them `pytest 8.4.2 (development only) in …: medium`, adds `(N installed only for development)` to the summary, and says so in the severity rationale. A shipped package still sets the rating.
- The report's dependency table shows `(development only)` after the package name.
- README: describes the aggregate dependency finding and dev-only handling, and replaces the stale "An advisory alone doesn't produce a finding".
- Grammar: "1 package … **has** N published advisories".

On the real `packages/hermes-api/uv.lock` that prompted this, the dev-only set is `pytest, ruff, pluggy, iniconfig, packaging, pygments, colorama`. `jinja2`, `markupsafe` and `pyyaml` stay shipped.

## Test plan

- [x] `test_dev_only_packages_come_from_the_lockfile`: uv runtime, extras, dev, a dependency shared by runtime and dev, a lockfile with no project package, package-lock `dev`/`devOptional`/nested duplicates, unknown formats, and bad TOML.

title: fix(hermes-security): each Fix in chat starts its own chat
body:
## ELI5

Pressing "Fix in chat" on a finding you'd already tried to fix took you back to the old fix chat instead of starting a new one. That's because both chats got the same name, and Hermes reopens a chat when you ask for a name that's already taken. Each fix chat's name now includes which finding it's for and the exact time it started, so every attempt gets its own chat. Clicking the button twice by accident no longer sends the request twice.

## Summary

- **Fix in chat** created its chat with `session.create` and the title `Fix: <finding title>`. Chat titles are unique per profile, and a titled create resolves the chat already holding the title, so a second fix of the same finding reopened the first fix chat. Two different findings with the same title also shared one. This is the same mechanism as the scan-chat issue fixed in #345.
- The title is now built by the exported `fixChatTitle(title, id, now)`: `Fix: <finding title> · <short finding id> · Nov 9, 01:45:07` (local time to the second).
  - Another finding with the same title, or a later attempt, gets a new chat.
- **Double click:** while a finding's fix chat is being created, further clicks for that finding do nothing (`fixesStarting`). Before, every click submitted the prompt again, even when the title reopened the same chat.
- The prompt, cwd and opening the chat are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] e2e: exact `fixChatTitle` output; same-title findings and a retry one second later get different titles; the empty title/id fallback; two concurrent clicks send one `session.create` and one `prompt.submit` with a `Fix: Test finding · test · <Mon D, HH:MM:SS>` title; a later click starts another chat. The test fails without the change. JS suite: 53 pass.
- [x] Full Python suite: 648 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed.

title: feat(hermes-security): code evidence can name its key line
body:
## ELI5

The code quoted in a security finding is often a whole function, and nothing said which line was the actual problem. So a long quote could be shortened in a way that hid exactly that line. Reviewers can now name the "key line"; the report shows it right above the code, and when it shortens a long quote it always keeps that line.

> Stacked on #347 (which is stacked on #346). Merge those first, or review only the last commit here.

## Summary

- **Format:** `codeEvidence` entries take an optional `keyLine` (integer) in `findings.schema.json` (candidate and finding) and `worker-result.schema.json`. Existing findings without it are unchanged.
- **Submit check:** `check_candidate` rejects a `keyLine` outside its excerpt's `startLine..endLine` (`keyLine must be a line inside its excerpt`). The candidate is rejected; other candidates in the result are still accepted.
- **Report:**
  - The key line is named above the code (`Key line 291: \`if let reported = written.entry.size {\``).
  - An excerpt over 30 lines keeps a 25-line window around the key line instead of its head and tail, and names every range it leaves out. Without a key line it still keeps 12 lines at each end. A `keyLine` outside the excerpt is ignored.
- **Workbench:** the code viewer highlights the key line along with the cited locations.
- **Worker instructions:** the worker packet's citation rules ask for a `keyLine` on every `codeEvidence` entry (the unchecked call, the missing guard's branch, the sink), and its example includes one. `docs/CONTRACT.md` documents the field. Provenance pins are updated for the schema, the packet reference and `markdown.py`.

Why: #347 first tried trimming long excerpts to their first and last 8 lines. On a real finding that hid the `if let reported = written.entry.size` branch, the bug itself, so #347 now trims only excerpts over 30 lines. With a key line, trimming can't drop the line that matters.

## Test plan

- [x] Integration `test_key_line_is_checked_on_submit_and_named_in_the_report`: an out-of-range key line is rejected, an in-range one is stored, and the sealed report names it.
- [x] Unit `test_a_long_excerpt_keeps_its_key_line`: the 25-line window and exact left-out ranges, the window near the end of an excerpt, and an out-of-range key line ignored.
- [x] e2e `codeLines` highlights the key line on its own. JS suite: 53 pass.
- [x] Full Python suite: 653 passed, 11 skipped, 1 xfailed.

title: feat(hermes-security): roll findings that share a weakness into one summary row
body:
## ELI5

When the same kind of problem shows up in many places, like twelve spots where a big file can use up all the phone's memory, the report listed twelve separate rows with nearly the same fix. Now those become one row ("12 findings: memory and resource exhaustion, 12 places") that links to a short list of every place and its fix. Every finding is still described in full below.

> Stacked on #347 (which is stacked on #346). Merge those first, or review only the last commit here.

## Summary

- Within each weakness group, three or more findings with the same **primary CWE** (the first CWE on the finding) form a pattern. Rule IDs differ per finding, so the CWE is the stable shared key.
- **Summary table:** a pattern is one row: number range, severity (or a span like `Medium to low`), `N findings: CWE-400 (<name>)` linked to the pattern, `N places`, and `One fix per place; see the list.` The name comes from the pinned CWE map, or the group name when the map has none (CWE-400 isn't in it).
- **In the group:** right before those findings, a pattern list gives each place as `[n. title](#finding-n) — path:line — first sentence of its fix`. Each finding keeps its own full, numbered section.
- Groups of two or fewer stay as normal rows. Numbering and anchors stay in reading order.

On the real mobile scan the summary table goes from 30 rows to 20 (`3–14 | Low | 12 findings: CWE-400 (memory and resource exhaustion) | 12 places`, `26–28 | Low | 3 findings: CWE-613 (Insufficient Session Expiration) | 3 places`).

## Test plan

- [x] `test_findings_sharing_a_weakness_roll_up_into_one_summary_row`: three CWE-400 findings of mixed severity roll up with a severity span, two CWE-613 findings stay separate, the pattern list has file/line/fix, every finding keeps its anchor, and the pattern comes before its findings.
- [x] Re-rendered the sealed mobile scan and read the output.
