title: feat(details-summary): add the Details Summary plugin
body:
Adds `details-summary`, an official plugin that makes every PR Hermes opens start with one to three plain sentences. The full agent-written description goes under a collapsed `
Claude Opus 5.5 Medium` row.

Claude Opus 5.5 Medium ## The problem Agents write PR descriptions that are accurate and long. Reviewers skim past them. Simon Willison's [details-summary post](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Nov/9/details-summary/) proposes a fix: a short opener a human picked, then the full agent text inside `
model + effort`. GitHub Markdown supports the fold natively. ## What the plugin does | Part | Seam | Effect | |---|---|---| | Prompt section | `ctx.register_system_prompt_section` | Every new session gets the body shape, the summary label for its own model and effort (`Claude Opus 5.5 Medium`), and opener rules: 1–3 sentences, 60 words or fewer, 25 per sentence, plain words, no "This PR". | | Enforcement | `pre_tool_call` hook returning `block` | Reads the body of `gh pr create`, `gh pr edit`, `gh api …/pulls` and tools named like `create_pull_request`. A body without the fold, with a long or filler-heavy opener, a generic summary label, or no blank line after `` is refused with the exact problems and the rules. | | CLI | `ctx.register_cli_command` | `hermes details-summary check ` and `hermes details-summary prompt`. | A body the hook cannot read is refused: `$(...)`, `--fill`, stdin, or a body file written in the same command (the hook runs before the command). The refusal tells the model to write the file first and pass `--body-file`. Comments, issues and other `gh` calls pass through. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[model writes body file] --> B[gh pr create --body-file] B --> C{pre_tool_call hook} C -->|shape ok| D[GitHub] C -->|problems| E[block: list of problems + opener rules] E --> A ``` ## Decision to check The summary label puts the model name in the PR body. That is AI attribution, which some repos ban. Here it is deliberate (the whole point of the post is to label the agent-written part), and it only appears in the ``. A user who does not want it should not install the plugin. ## Not in this PR - The catalog entry in hermes-agent (`plugin-catalog/details-summary.yaml`, pinned to this merge commit). That follows once this merges. - PRs opened outside Hermes (web UI, other agents). The README says to run `hermes details-summary check` in a CI job for those. ## Live verification Hermes `v0.23.0+209`, `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` at medium, a fresh profile, plugin installed with `hermes plugins install` from the standalone repo this was ported from: | Ask | Result | |---|---| | "Open a PR for this branch and write a proper description" (plugin not mentioned) | [demo PR](https://github.com/alt-glitch/details-summary-demo/pull/1) on the first try: 26-word opener, `Claude Opus 5.5 Medium` fold | | Replace the body with "This PR introduces a comprehensive enhancement" | `gh pr edit` blocked, nothing sent; the agent reported both reasons and did not retry another way | | Put a `## Summary` heading with bullets on top | the agent saw the rule, asked first, then put the heading inside the fold | This PR's own body was checked with `hermes details-summary check` before it was opened. Locally against hermes-agent `origin/main` `109fd8161a`: 31 tests pass, and `plugins validate` and `plugins doctor --ci` pass on a clean clone. The real-discovery test copies the plugin into a temp home instead of symlinking, so it runs on the Windows lane too.

title: fix(directsdk): telemetry off, full /usage, own login per profile
body:
The Claude subscription plugin (DirectSDK) now keeps Claude Code's telemetry off by default, shows the whole Claude account on `/usage`, runs each profile on its own Claude login, and adds per-profile settings for paid extra usage and an organization gateway. Closes #331, #313, #43, #46, and the plugin side of NousResearch/hermes-agent#146288.

## Before

Plugin 0.3.5, the version on `main`:
- Claude Code sent telemetry unless the user turned the `claude_code_telemetry` setting off, and turning it off cost the picker most of its models and `/usage` its limits.
- `/usage` showed the plan windows and dropped the rest of the account answer.
- In a gateway serving several profiles, a profile with no Claude login of its own ran on the login of the profile the gateway was started for.
- Paid extra usage went unnoticed: the plugin dropped Claude Code's rate-limit event.
- An organization could not route the Claude login through its own gateway, proxy or TLS-inspecting CA.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[turn on a served profile] --> L{own Claude login?}
  L -->|no| G[the launch profile's login and allowance]
  R[Claude Code rate_limit_event] --> X[dropped]
```

## After

Plugin 0.4.0:
- Telemetry is off by default. The model picker's start-up request and the usage probe still fetch what they need, so the picker stays complete and `/usage` keeps its limits.
- A served profile uses its own token or its own `claude_config_dir`. With neither, the turn is refused before Claude Code starts, and the message names both ways to give the profile a login.
- `extra_usage` (`allow`, `notify` default, `ask`, `stop`) acts on the rate-limit event and, in a fresh process, on one zero-inference usage check. State is in memory only.
- `upstream_url`, `upstream_proxy`, `upstream_ca_file` are one explicit opt-in. Only Messages requests go to the gateway; Claude Code's own account calls take the same proxy and CA. A bad value refuses and never falls back to the direct route.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  T[turn on a served profile] --> L{own token or claude_config_dir?}
  L -->|yes| O[runs on that login]
  L -->|no| F[refused before Claude Code starts]
  R[Claude Code rate_limit_event] --> P{extra_usage}
  P -->|notify| W[one warning per window]
  P -->|ask or stop| S[next request refused until allowed or reset]
```

## What the user sees

| Situation | Before (0.3.5) | After (0.4.0) |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh install | Claude Code telemetry on | off; the picker still lists every model the account has |
| `hermes usage` | session, week and per-model windows | the same windows plus extra usage, credits spent and this week's share per surface |
| A served profile with no Claude login of its own | answers on the launch profile's login | refused with "This profile has no Claude login of its own" and both ways to add one |
| The account starts drawing paid extra usage | nothing | `notify`: one warning per window. `ask`/`stop`: the next request is refused before it is billed, naming the reset time and the `hermes config set` line |
| The "Third-party apps now draw from your extra usage" 400 | an unknown error, then a silent fallback to another provider | a billing stop that says why; no fallback |
| An org gateway, proxy or CA | not supported | three settings; an invalid value refuses the turn, `/usage` and the picker |
| `hermes status` on Windows | WinError 32 traceback and a `claude.exe` left running | the probe child is killed and waited for, also at interpreter exit |
| A stale `.oauth_refresh.lock` left by a crashed Claude Code | every request fails until it is deleted by hand | an empty lock past Claude Code's 60 s window is removed before the next spawn |
| An API-key or cloud login at setup | reported as logged in; the first turn bills the API | setup says which login Claude Code would use and how to switch |

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (hermes usage) | After (hermes usage) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/35515432-7e07-4a3d-8bff-39c75684c003) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f1d9a720-98cd-4569-9c50-bc8bb58db052) |

The same account and Claude Code; the after rows are the detail `get_usage` already returned.

| Before (served profile with no login of its own) | After (served profile with no login of its own) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/160e2def-3a2c-4b26-80d3-29e4fcbfec28) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/de3a537b-4024-4b14-8e6b-ae7464732642) |

A profile with no Claude token or config directory of its own, served by the shared gateway. Before, it answered on the launch profile's login.

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Not in this PR

- A mid-session notice for `notify`: the warning goes to the log. Core has no provider-to-UI notice seam yet.
- The caller name Claude Code reports stays `hermes-agent` (unchanged on purpose).
- The Windows run of the `hermes status` fix: covered on Linux with a real child on a daemon thread at interpreter exit.

## Live verification

| Check | Before (0.3.5 on `main`) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes -p <scratch> usage`, real Claude Code 2.1.319, zero inference | 3 windows | 3 windows plus `Extra usage: off`, `Usage credits spent: 0.00 USD`, `This week by surface` |
| `hermes -p <served profile> chat -q`, a profile with no login of its own, served by the shared gateway | answered `ok` on the launch profile's login | refused with the login hint; Claude Code never started |
| Offline evals `directsdk_admission`, `directsdk_cache_wire` on Claude Code 2.1.319 and the CI pin 2.1.292 | pass | pass |

Gateway wire check, on real Claude Code 2.1.319 and 2.1.292 behind a loopback gateway and a recording CONNECT proxy:
- `get_usage` and the picker's `initialize` request send nothing to the base URL.
- A turn sends only `POST /v1/messages` to the gateway.
- With only the plugin settings set, every direct call went through the proxy.

Not verified live: a real `isUsingOverage: true` event (no account here is past its limit) and the Team/Enterprise 400.

Salvaged by cherry-pick with authorship kept: #258 (@ephyria-k), #314 (@kalfian), #281 (@salch-cred), #27 (@grantjayy), #28 (@100yenadmin); #25 the lock reap only, with Co-authored-by. Superseded: #337, #282, #257, #130, #23.

## Follow-ups

- A core seam for provider notices, so `notify` can show in the chat.
- Close #337, #282, #257, #130, #23 as superseded when this merges.

## Next PR

#360 (tool calls stream as written) is stacked on this branch and moves to `main` when this merges.

title: accent-picker: persist accent choice across restarts (ctx.storage + ctx.files + register-time restore)
body:
The Accent Picker shipped with setAccentOverride, which is deliberately scratch-only — the color resets on every launch. This PR makes the picker persist the chosen accent across restarts.

Changes:

src/plugin.tsx: restore the persisted accent at register() time (so it applies on startup, not only when the popover opens); pass ctx through to the trigger; remove the onDispose handler that cleared the override on unload (which previously clobbered the saved value); update description.
src/picker.tsx: accept ctx as a prop; persist via both ctx.storage (fast, sync) and ctx.files (disk, robust against Electron webview localStorage loss); restore on mount from both; switch from setAccentOverride to $accentOverride.set to avoid normalization drift.
desktop/plugin.js: rebuilt.
Persistence strategy: two-tier — ctx.storage for immediate sync reads, ctx.files (plugin data folder) as the durable disk layer. Restore runs at plugin load so the color is active before the UI renders.

Testing: manually verified accent survives a full Hermes restart and applies on startup without opening the picker.

title: [hermes-security] Test harness keeps ambient credentials: SSH agent, kubeconfig and cloud profiles survive _test_env
body:
## Summary

`validation/runner.py` builds the environment for repository-controlled test commands with a **name-keyword** filter, and documents the result as "minus credentials". Variables whose *names* don't contain one of the keywords pass through, so code executed by the test-confirmation harness inherits the operator's ambient credential **paths** and agent sockets, not just `PATH`.

## Evidence (v0.1.2, commit `85e835c3`)

`hermes_security/validation/runner.py:77-83`

```python
_SECRET_NAME=('TOKEN','SECRET','PASSWORD','PASSWD','API_KEY','APIKEY','ACCESS_KEY','PRIVATE_KEY','CREDENTIAL','SESSION_KEY')

def _test_env(cwd):
    """Run like the user's own shell (PATH, toolchains, HOME) minus credentials."""
    env={k:v for k,v in os.environ.items() if not any(s in k.upper() for s in _SECRET_NAME)}
    env.update(TMPDIR=str(cwd),TEMP=str(cwd),TMP=str(cwd))
    return env
```

Consumed at `:90` (`subprocess.Popen(..., env=env, ...)`) and `:126` (`_win32.spawn_in_job(..., env=env, ...)`).

Variables that survive and matter:

- `HOME` → `~/.aws`, `~/.kube`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.docker/config.json`, `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`
- `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` → repository code can ask the running agent to sign with loaded keys
- `KUBECONFIG`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `GNUPGHOME`

`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` *are* stripped (they match `ACCESS_KEY` / `SECRET`), which makes the docstring look right in the common case while the file-path and socket routes stay open.

## How it is reached

`hermes_security/service.py:761-764` makes the scan's tests switch the only gate:

```python
if level == 'local-safe' and scan['safety_level'] == 'static':
    raise PolicyDenied('this scan was started without permission to run tests; start a new scan with tests allowed')
```

Nothing downstream re-checks the environment: `validation/policy.py:93-96` validates the argv shape of a local-command plan and never touches `env`.

## Impact

Medium. A scan started with tests allowed can run a repository-supplied command with the operator's SSH agent, kubeconfig and cloud profile selectors, reaching systems outside the disposable copy. Allowing tests is consent to execute the code, not to hand over ambient credentials — and both the helper's docstring and the marketplace disclosure ("credential-looking environment variables removed") currently promise more than the code does.

## Suggested fix

One shared boundary, both platforms:

```python
_CREDENTIAL_NAMES=('SSH_AUTH_SOCK','SSH_ASKPASS','KUBECONFIG','AWS_PROFILE',
                   'AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE','GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS',
                   'AZURE_CONFIG_DIR','DOCKER_CONFIG','GNUPGHOME','NETRC')

def _test_env(cwd):
    env = {k:v for k,v in os.environ.items()
           if not any(s in k.upper() for s in _SECRET_NAME) and k not in _CREDENTIAL_NAMES}
    home = cwd/'_home'; home.mkdir(exist_ok=True)   # throwaway HOME inside the copy
    env.update(TMPDIR=str(cwd), TEMP=str(cwd), TMP=str(cwd),
               HOME=str(home), XDG_CONFIG_HOME=str(home/'.config'))
    return env
```

If a cold toolchain cache (npm/cargo/pip) makes a throwaway `HOME` too slow, point `HOME` at a per-scan cache directory under the plugin data folder instead — the property that matters is that no operator dotfiles or sockets are reachable. A strict allow-list (`PATH`, locale, toolchain roots) is the larger, cleaner change but needs a compatibility pass over the stacks the harness supports.

## Regression controls

- A `["sh","-c","env"]` plan's output shows no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `KUBECONFIG` or `AWS_PROFILE`, and `HOME` is not the operator's.
- A repository script that opens `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` fails against the harness environment.
- An ordinary `pytest` / `npm test` in the disposable copy still passes.

## Environment

hermes-security 0.1.2 (`85e835c3`, latest at time of filing) · Hermes Agent 0.23.0 · macOS 27.0.1 · Python 3.14.9.

Found by hermes-security's own standard scan of its installed source (16 packets, 20 candidates, 5 independent validators). Everything here is static analysis: no repository code was executed and no test was run.

title: fix(directsdk): stream tool calls as Claude writes them
body:
**Merges after #357; stacked on it.**

Tool calls now reach Hermes as Claude writes them, so a long `write_file` shows "Preparing write_file…" instead of a bare spinner, and a broken or cut-off tool call is retried instead of failing the turn. Closes #164, #221, #326, #327, #328, #341.

## Before

On #357's head, the relay held each tool call until Claude finished writing it:
- A large `write_file` showed only the thinking spinner until the whole call was written: 30 s for a 1,500-word file.
- A call whose streamed arguments were invalid JSON, or cut off at `max_tokens`, was dropped. Claude Code then failed the turn with `error_max_turns`, and each retry failed the same way.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[Claude writes a tool call] --> H[relay holds it until complete]
  H --> S[Hermes shows a spinner]
  H -->|arguments do not parse| D[call dropped, turn fails]
```

## After

The relay passes each tool call on as Claude streams it:
- Hermes sees the tool name as soon as Claude starts the call, then the arguments as they are written.
- A call whose arguments do not parse comes back with finish `length` and its raw arguments. Hermes never runs a call from a `length` reply; it retries.
- After invalid JSON, that conversation's next requests ask the API to buffer and validate tool input. A cut-off call keeps streaming.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[Claude writes a tool call] --> P[name, then argument deltas, as written]
  P --> U[Hermes shows Preparing write_file]
  P -->|arguments do not parse| L[finish length, never run, retried]
```

## What the user sees

| Situation | Before (#357 head) | After |
|---|---|---|
| A long `write_file` call | the thinking spinner until the call is written (30 s for 1,500 words) | "Preparing write_file…" from the moment the call starts |
| Invalid JSON in a tool call (#221) | the turn fails; every retry fails the same way | the call is not run; the next request answers |
| A tool call cut at `max_tokens` (#164) | `Native request failed: error_max_turns` | the call is not run; Hermes retries with more room |
| A refusal | the reason, no request id | one log line with model, request id and category; the refusal text ends with `(request_id=req_...)` for Anthropic's false-positive form (#341) |
| `response_format: json_object` on an auxiliary call (#327) | `ValueError` on every call | dropped by core before the request |
| A request refused before Claude Code starts (#328) | retried as an unknown error | not retried; fallback allowed |
| A tool id from another provider (`terminal:42`) | sent to Anthropic unchanged and rejected | a stable `toolu_hermes_<hash>` id, paired with its result |
| Claude names a tool `mcp__<tool>` | core repairs it and logs a line per call | mapped to the offered tool |

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| Before (15 s into a long write_file call) | After (15 s into a long write_file call) |
|:---:|:---:|
| ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8ac2b3ac-f5f9-4b19-acf4-2b29841d1e66) | ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc87a2a0-d054-4cba-92c8-66de76720024) |

The interactive CLI on the same prompt. The after row reads "wriie_file" because the capture's tmux counts the width of the ✍️ emoji differently from the CLI; in a terminal it reads "write_file".

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Not in this PR

- Telling core the native output cap, so a `length` retry does not shrink `max_tokens`: no plugin seam yet.
- The burst of text after a tool result (P#33): it comes from the API, not the plugin; tracked there.

## Live verification

| Check | Before (#357 head) | After (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive `hermes -p <scratch>`, "write a 1,500-word guide in one write_file call", real Claude Code 2.1.319, Sonnet 5.5 | 30 s of "deliberating..." with no tool row, then the edit | "Preparing write_file…" from 9 s until the edit at 53 s |
| Offline evals on Claude Code 2.1.319 and the CI pin 2.1.292 | pass | pass; invalid streamed JSON answers finish `length` with 1 upstream request; a refusal answers `content_filter` with 1 upstream request |
| Cache wire eval, 25 requests | Claude Code's environment message changed between requests 1 and 2 (the stable-context tests fail with this fix reverted) | the same on every request |

Both shots are the same moment, 15 s after the prompt was sent. The two runs wrote files of different length (37.7 s and 53.5 s turns), so only the 15 s frame is a like-for-like comparison.

Cherry-picked with authorship: #21 (@efron), #342 (@mwe-ai), #336 (@kanederkson, the relevant commit), #171 (@salch-cred, the `_fast_eligible` hunk and its tests). Superseded: #256, #338 (both turned eager streaming off, which brought back multi-second silent gaps).

## Follow-ups

- A core seam for the native output cap.

## Next PR

#361 (one Claude Code process per Hermes agent) is stacked on this branch and moves here when this merges.

title: feat(directsdk): one Claude Code process per agent
body:
**Merges after #360; stacked on it. Draft: the maintainer declined this direction before (see Decision to check).**

Each Hermes agent now keeps one Claude Code process for its whole conversation instead of starting a new one and replaying the history on every model call. Upstream requests are byte-identical to the per-call path, so cost and caching do not change; the gain is latency per tool round.

## Before

With #360, every model call starts a new Claude Code process:
- Each call replays the whole conversation into the new process before the request goes out.
- That local replay costs 0.5 s per tool round at the start of a conversation and 1.0 s at 100 rounds (real CLI, scripted upstream).
- A 4-step tool loop starts 4 processes.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S1[step 1] --> P1[new Claude Code, replay 1 turn]
  S2[step 2] --> P2[new Claude Code, replay 2 turns]
  S3[step 3] --> P3[new Claude Code, replay 3 turns]
```

## After

The process belongs to the client Hermes already keeps per agent:
- Each step sends only the new tool results into the kept process: about 0.035 s locally, flat with history length.
- The relay checks that every request extends the previous one. Anything else (an edited or compacted history, a `/steer` row, a change of model, system, tools, effort or output cap) restarts into a new process with the per-call bytes.
- Auxiliary calls (titles, summaries), calls without tools, a second concurrent call and calls past `max_sessions` (default 4) run per-call.
- The process ends on cancel, close, an hour idle, or when Hermes dies, even by SIGKILL.
- Hermes' tools are served inside the plugin over Claude Code's control protocol, so the inert MCP helper process is deleted.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S1[step 1] --> K[one kept Claude Code]
  S2[step 2] -->|new tool results only| K
  S3[step 3] -->|new tool results only| K
  E[edited history] -->|refused before upstream| R[restart, per-call bytes]
```

## What the user sees

| Situation | Before (#360) | After |
|---|---|---|
| A tool loop on one agent | a new Claude Code per model call | one Claude Code for the conversation |
| Local cost of a tool round (offline, 0 to 100 replayed rounds) | 0.50 to 1.00 s | 0.035 to 0.039 s |
| Memory | one short-lived process per call | about 200 to 240 MB RSS per kept process, at most `max_sessions` (4) per Hermes process |
| Upstream requests and cache reads | per-call bytes | the same bytes |
| `session_mode: false` | n/a | the per-call path, exactly as before |
| Windows | a fresh working directory per process, so Claude Code's first message changed on every restart | one shared working directory per user in the user's own temp |

## Verdict

Pending the long-session bench.

## Decision to check

This direction was declined three times (#29, #79 and #101, all opt-in): the surface and the control-protocol coupling were judged too large for a gain per-call mostly recovers. What differs here:
- Byte-identical requests, so no cost or cache claim; the case is latency only.
- Smaller: net +387 product lines against #101's +782, no process pool, and the helper process deleted.
- Default on (a ruling for this stack); flip `session_mode` in `plugin.yaml` for opt-in.

Still true: the coupling to Claude Code's control protocol (the tool-use id key is Claude Code's own), and more memory per process than #79 estimated.

## Not in this PR

- macOS and Windows runs of session mode; Linux only.
- A tool parked for minutes, and the subscription meter's view of a kept process.

## Live verification

| Check | Per-call (`session_mode: false`) | Kept (this head) |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes -p <scratch> chat -Q -q`, read three files one call at a time, then sum: 4 model steps on Sonnet 5.5, Claude Code 2.1.319, through the shared gateway | 5 `claude` processes: one per step, plus the title call | 2: one kept for all 4 steps, plus the title call; the kept one exited with the chat |
| Both answered | "The sum is 42" | "The sum is 42" |
| Seconds between model calls 1 to 4 (Hermes' log) | 2.18, 1.90, 1.77 | 1.70, 1.67, 1.57 |
| Offline evals on 2.1.319 and the CI pin 2.1.292 | pass | pass |

Claude Code processes started for the chat, sampled every 0.2 s (seconds from the command start):

```mermaid
gantt
  title Claude Code processes per chat
  dateFormat ss.SSS
  axisFormat %S s
  section per-call
  title call   :24.310, 25.460
  step 1       :24.310, 26.350
  step 2       :27.260, 28.590
  step 3       :29.040, 30.600
  step 4       :31.040, 32.380
  section kept
  title call   :02.900, 04.450
  steps 1 to 4 :02.900, 10.180
```

In the per-call run Hermes took 24 s to start before the turn began (its log shows no turn until then); that start-up is not part of the comparison. One run per mode, so the step times are an example, not a measurement. An earlier A/B on a real claude.ai login (12 calls) ran tool rounds in 1.5 to 2.2 s kept against 2.0 s per call, with the same cache reads per step (0, 836, 901, 967 tokens).

## Follow-ups

- The long-session bench (verdict above).
- macOS and Windows runs.

title: fix(singularity): bind child environments and preserve restart-safe artifacts
body:
# fix(singularity): bind child environments and preserve restart-safe artifacts

## Summary

Companion to https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/94878. Keep this PR **draft and dependency-blocked** until the core boundary API lands.

- Build the local Apptainer/Singularity client environment for the captured profile owner, including owner-bound registry authentication for image construction. Pass registry credentials through the child environment rather than adding them to image-build arguments.
- Select persistent overlays by durable owner, image identity and task, not a per-interpreter scope generation. Retain single-profile legacy-overlay behavior and do not adopt unowned legacy state across multiplexed profiles. Remove the process-exit sweep that would delete persistent overlays.
- Stop an instance with its start-time control environment even when cleanup runs under a foreign/stale caller scope. Retain the instance handle after a failed stop so cleanup can retry.
- Refuse core versions that lack the required boundary API rather than silently falling back to the old behavior.

## Local evidence

Source: `4d6dcb23063613865abda1fa641be401dd6dea79` against core `c179f7aadadbd2693a8438c772c6e66129c96838` (core incorporates pinned main `6933155eafe49da75c8c632722adb57caaff197d`).

- Seven plugin/core conformance files: **53 passed, 0 failed**. These are local canonical-runner results, not hosted CI or native Apptainer certification.
- The restart regression uses separate interpreter processes: a marker survives with the same image; changed image contents select a new overlay. Stop-failure/retry and foreign/stale caller cases are covered with a stubbed backend executable.
- `hermes plugins validate ./singularity` passes against that core. It still reports pre-existing private-core import warnings for the default image, shared process/task-path helpers, and credential/skills mount helpers. This PR does not claim a warning-free or universally compatible plugin. The newly used child-environment builder is explicitly documented in the companion core API declaration; other private names are not promoted to public APIs.

## Landing and release order

1. Land core #94878 and its profile-boundary API.
2. Review and land this companion separately; do not infer compatibility solely from the older broad `requires_hermes` floor. The runtime API guard remains required.
3. Propose a separate catalog pin using the **actual official merged plugin commit** and a core release requirement that really contains the API. Preserve the existing catalog repository and `subdir: singularity`.

This PR does not change the catalog pin or installed copies. Native Docker/Apptainer behavior, Windows/macOS, hosted CI, production multi-tenant behavior, and installed/live runtime activation are not certified by these local tests. No merge or runtime activation is requested by this submission.

title: feat(advanced-delegation): add model-routing skill
body:
## Summary

Adds one bundled skill to the `advanced-delegation` plugin, `model-routing` (loads as
`advanced-delegation:model-routing`). It is a procedure for splitting big work into subagent tasks
and sending each one to the cheapest of the user's own `model_map` routes that reliably passes it:
plan -> contract -> parallel dispatch with non-overlapping owned files -> verify with real tests ->
record the outcome -> escalate only on model-caused failures -> final review on the strongest route.

A stdlib helper (`skills/model-routing/scripts/route_ledger.py`) keeps a local outcome ledger and
turns it into route suggestions:

- `sync-routes` reads the user's routes in config order (cheapest -> strongest) with
  `hermes config get delegation.backends.model_map.options --json`, falling back to parsing
  `hermes delegation config --show` on cores without `config get`; `--from FILE` reads saved output.
  It stores only names, descriptions and `provider:model@effort[+tier][+daybreak]` (no keys; any
  `user:pass@` is stripped from a `base_url`) in `routes.json`. Malformed routes are skipped with a
  warning on both paths; all `hermes` calls share a 200-second budget, and a missing or hung
  `hermes` exits 2 with a one-line error.
- `suggest` maps difficulty 1-5 onto any ladder length (position `(d-1)*(n-1)/4`, exact halves round
  toward the cheaper route); high risk floors at the middle route and moves one up from there.
  A model-caused failure promotes similar tasks one route; 3 straight first-try passes allow a trial
  one route down; a route re-pointed to another model voids its old model failures.
- `add` validates `--route` against the synced ladder; `stats`, `classes`, `ladder` report.

## Why it belongs in this plugin

The skill only makes sense with Model routes mode: its ladder *is* the plugin's `model_map` config,
and it drives `delegate_task`'s `option` parameter that this plugin adds. Shipping it with the plugin
keeps it in step with the config format (a test parses `store.describe()` output directly).

## What it adds

- `skills/model-routing/` (SKILL.md, references/workflow.md, scripts/route_ledger.py), registered with
  `ctx.register_skill()` as the last registration in `register()`, after the delegation providers,
  the slash command and the CLI command, so it never appears on an old core where the plugin is
  inactive. The call is wrapped in `try/except Exception` with a warning: a skill failure never
  disables the delegation modes. SKILL.md calls the helper as
  `python "${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/route_ledger.py"`; core substitutes `${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}` for
  plugin skills too (`tools/skills_tool_plugin.py` -> `agent/skill_preprocessing.py`).
- No tools, hooks, middleware or dependencies. The script writes only its ledger and `routes.json`
  under `<HERMES_HOME>/plugin-data/advanced-delegation/` (Hermes's per-plugin data folder; override
  the ledger file with `ADVANCED_DELEGATION_LEDGER`).
- README section "Model routing skill"; `plugin.yaml` description mentions the skill.
- Version 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0. `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.22.5` (`ctx.register_skill` with
  `description=` exists in 0.22.5).

## Tests

`tests/test_model_routing_skill.py` (stdlib + pytest, no network, `hermes` faked): frontmatter and
section standards, no machine-local paths or model names in the skill, script portability (stdlib,
UTF-8, no POSIX-only calls), ladder mapping on 1/2/3/4/5/7 routes, risk floor, promotion, trial
demotion, model-change invalidation, route validation, missing-ladder error, both sync sources and
the fallback, malformed-route warnings, tier/daybreak fingerprints, base_url credential stripping,
UTF-8/UTF-16 BOM `--from` files, clean errors for a missing or hung `hermes`, malformed ledger rows,
and registration (unit, old core, real `PluginManager`, a failing `register_skill`).

```
cd advanced-delegation
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=<hermes-agent> PYTHONPATH=<hermes-agent> python -m pytest -q
198 passed, 3 skipped            # baseline before this change: 145 passed, 3 skipped
hermes plugins validate ./advanced-delegation
Validation passed.               # security scan: safe
```

Platforms tested: Windows 11 (Python 3.11, Hermes v0.23.0 checkout). CI covers Linux/macOS/Windows.

## Release note

Merging does not ship it: releasing needs a maintainer to re-pin `plugin-catalog/advanced-delegation.yaml`
on hermes-agent to the merge commit. The pin adds no tools, hooks or dependencies, so it should not
ask users to consent again.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: pin Fable 5.2 (fable alias) and Mythos 5.2 (access-gated)
body:
## What

Anthropic released **Claude Fable 5.2** (`claude-fable-5-2`) and **Claude Mythos 5.2** (`claude-mythos-5-2`) on November 9, 2026. This pins both, following the "Adding a Claude model" checklist in `AGENTS.md`.

- `model_catalog.py`
  - `claude-fable-5-2` pinned at 1M. Claude Code's `fable` alias now resolves to Fable 5.2 ([model config](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config#work-with-fable)), so the plugin alias follows it. `claude-fable-5-1` stays pinned for anyone who selected it by ID.
  - `claude-mythos-5-2` pinned at 1M and added to `ACCESS_GATED`. It shares Fable 5.2's specs but is limited to verified organizations ([Fable 5.2 overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/fable-5-2/overview)), so it is listed only when the account's own picker offers it.
  - Thinking: both models document adaptive thinking as always on. The existing `claude-fable` / `claude-mythos` prefixes in `MANDATORY_THINKING` already cover them, matching core's `_MANDATORY_THINKING_CLAUDE_SUBSTRINGS`. No change was needed in this plugin or in core.
- `directsdk_setup.py`: the Fable usage-credits note now includes Fable 5.2. Anthropic's plan article says all three Fable models work the same way: included on Max, Ultra and premium seats, usage credits on Pro and standard seats ([support article](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964)).
- `README.md`: Requirements and the route table name Fable 5.2's minimum Claude Code version (2.1.321) and both new routes.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry; `plugin.yaml` 0.3.4 → 0.3.5.

Fable 5.2 also rejects forced tool use and sampling parameters. The transport already accepts only `tool_choice: auto` and strips `temperature`/`top_p` for every model, so nothing changes there.

## Tests

- `tests/test_directsdk_models.py`: `EXPECTED`/`GATED` rows for both routes; argv checks for `fable`, `fable-5.2`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-mythos-5-2`, `mythos-5.2`; adaptive display parametrization.
- `tests/test_directsdk_reasoning_off.py`: reasoning-off asks for `effort: low` on both new routes.
- `tests/test_directsdk_setup.py`: a served Fable 5.2 row gets the plan-rule note and the `Fable 5.2` label.

Run with `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=~/.hermes/hermes-agent`, one file at a time: every file passes. `test_directsdk_admission.py` exits partway through with no summary line, and does exactly the same on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout, so that predates this change.

## Live checks (Claude Code 2.1.321, Max account)

- Discovery handshake (`initialize` only, no user turn): `claude-fable-5-2[1m]` is listed as `Fable 5.2` with a 1,000,000 window, and `fable` maps to `claude-fable-5-2[1m]`. Mythos 5.2 is not offered to this account, so it is correctly absent.
- Two real requests, `fable` and `claude-fable-5-2`, each returned the exact sentinel reply with `finish_reason: stop`.

## Not done

- Mythos 5.2 was not exercised live: no verified-organization account was available.
- Fable 5.2 was not exercised on a Pro account.
- The `hermes-agent` catalog pin bump will follow after merge.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Text written before a tool call is often missing: the turn arrives as thinking, thinking, tool_use with no text block
body:
**Setup:** Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (stable), plugin claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental 0.3.3, Claude Code 2.1.302, model claude-opus-5-5[1m], Desktop app (remote backend), Linux (Mint 22.3).

**What happens:** when the model writes a reply and then calls a tool in the same response (typically `clarify`), the text often never reaches Hermes. The stored assistant message has empty `content`; its `reasoning_details` carrier holds the native turn as `thinking, thinking, tool_use` (or `thinking, tool_use`) with no `text` block. The response's `output_tokens` (about 1,900 in one case, of which the tool arguments were about 600) show that the text was generated. Short lines before a tool call sometimes arrive (`thinking, text, tool_use`), and text-only final replies always arrive (313 of 313 from 1 to 8 Nov).

**How often:** for assistant messages that call `clarify`, the number with no text block, out of all such messages, per day:

- 16 to 29 Oct: 2 of 49
- 30 Oct: 7 of 32
- 1 Nov: 13 of 42
- 2 Nov: 27 of 59
- 4 Nov: 30 of 61
- 5 Nov: 30 of 68
- 8 Nov: 31 of 52
- 9 Nov, one Desktop session: 99 assistant messages with a tool call, 4 with a visible text block.

Neither the plugin nor Claude Code changed on this server in that period (both installed 18 Oct), so the change looks upstream: model, service or native.

**Effect:** the user sees a question with no report, or is asked to review a document that never appeared. Progress notes written before tool calls are lost the same way.

**Where it is lost:** the relay capture (`admission.py`, `_block_start` and `_block_delta`) records every streamed content block, and the carrier shows no text block at all. So the text seems to be missing from the upstream stream itself, or folded into the second thinking block (thinking display is omitted here, so the thinking text is empty and cannot be inspected).

**Workaround on our side:** a `pre_tool_call` hook refuses a `clarify` call whose own message carries no visible text and asks the model to rewrite. Because the rewrite is lost the same way, it often ends with the text sent alone and the question not asked (17 refusals across sessions on 9 Nov).

**Questions:** can you reproduce it? Is a second thinking block with no text between it and the tool call expected from native, or is a text block being dropped? Is there a setting (for example thinking display, or interleaved thinking) that keeps the text block?

title: feat(directsdk): cap concurrent Claude Code processes
body:
**Merges after #360; stacked on it.**

A subagent fan-out no longer starts one Claude Code process per call all at once: at most `max_concurrent` (default 4) run at the same time in one Hermes process, and the rest wait their turn. Closes #329.

## Before

The plugin started a new `claude` process for every model call and never limited how many ran at once:
- `delegate_task` runs up to 10 children in parallel by default, and each child uses the parent's provider.
- Each child's call started its own `claude` (about 220 MB here) at the same moment, plus auxiliary calls such as titles and compression.
- All of them draw on one subscription, and the plugin turns off Claude Code's own retries, so a burst that hits a plan limit fails for every caller at once.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[delegate_task, 6 children] --> C1[claude]
  F --> C2[claude]
  F --> C3[claude]
  F --> C4[claude]
  F --> C5[claude]
  F --> C6[claude]
```

## After

Every call takes a place in one pool before its `claude` starts and gives it back when that process exits:
- At most `max_concurrent` processes run at once in the Hermes process, across subagents, auxiliary calls and every profile one gateway serves.
- A call past the limit waits in arrival order within its own request timeout. It is never failed or sent to a fallback provider.
- An interrupt ends a waiting call at once, without starting Claude Code. A process that crashes gives its place back.
- `/usage`, the model picker and the login check take no place: they send no model request and finish in seconds.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  F[delegate_task, 6 children] --> P{free place?}
  P -->|4 places| R[claude runs]
  P -->|full| W[wait in order, within the call's timeout]
  R -->|process exits| P
  W --> P
```

## What the user sees

| Situation | Before (#360 head) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `delegate_task` with 6 children | 7 `claude` processes at once (1.4 GB) | at most 4 (0.9 GB); the reply comes about 1 s later |
| A 10-child fan-out (the core default) | 11 processes at once on one subscription | 4 at a time, in about 3 rounds |
| A call waits more than 2 s | not possible | the CLI shows its usual spinner; the log gets one warning a minute naming `max_concurrent` |
| Interrupt while a call waits | not possible | the call ends at once; no Claude Code process starts |
| `/usage` during a fan-out | answers | answers, without waiting for a place |

<!-- before-and-after:start -->
| `claude` processes alive during one 6-child fan-out, before and after |
|:---:|
| ![Preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c9b83df-07c0-4e05-9ba9-1c23212f7455) |

`ps` samples every 0.5 s from the live runs in Live verification. Red is #360's head (peak 7), teal is this head (peak 4, the dashed line). The dotted lines mark when the final reply appeared.

<!-- before-and-after:end -->

## Not in this PR

- One limit across Hermes processes (a separate cron or TUI process gets its own pool): needs a file lock; here every CLI and TUI turn runs in the one host gateway.
- A wait line on Hermes' status bar: a model provider has no way to write one, so the wait goes to the log only.
- Shrinking the limit while Claude Code reports a rate limit (#281's signal): a follow-up once that event is used for policy.

## Live verification

| Check | Before (#360 head plugin code) | After (this head, `max_concurrent` 4) |
|---|---|---|
| Interactive `hermes -p <scratch copy of the Claude profile> chat`, one `delegate_task` of 6 children that each reply "OK", real Claude Code 2.1.319, Sonnet 5.5; `ps` every 0.5 s | peak 7 `claude` processes, 1427 MB | peak 4, 883 MB; 3 children waited 2.2 to 2.4 s each |
| Enter to the final reply | 13.2 s | 14.2 s |
| Model calls, rate-limit errors | 9 calls, none | 9 calls, none |
| Offline evals on Claude Code 2.1.319 and the CI pin 2.1.292 | pass | pass |

The chart above plots those `ps` samples. Six one-word calls are far below the plan's request rate, so this run shows the limit holding, not a rate limit being avoided. The two runs used the same scratch profile copy and login; the before run's plugin code is #360's head.

## Follow-ups

- #361 (one process per agent) is rebased onto this next. Its kept processes take places from this pool too. `max_sessions` becomes a sub-limit that leaves one place for single calls, and a queued call ends the least recently used idle session instead of waiting.

title: fix(hermes-security): "Same as my chats" starts the scan on that model
body:
## ELI5

When you start a security scan and leave the model on "Same as my chats", the form shows the model of the chat you have open. The scan was labeled with that model, but the scan's own chat quietly ran on your profile's default model instead, so the two could differ. Now the scan runs on the model the option names. Scans already started keep the model they were started on; start a new scan to get the right one.

## Summary

- **Bug:** with "Same as my chats (X)" selected, the New scan form recorded X on the scan but created the scan's chat without any model. The chat then used the profile's default model. When the open chat was on a different model than the profile default, the scan page showed one model while the scan's chat ran on another.
- **Fix:** the scan's chat is created on the model the option names. The provider is sent only when it is certain: the current provider if it lists that model, otherwise the only provider that lists it; if neither holds, the model is sent alone.
- Picking a model explicitly, and the subagent route picker, behave as before.

| Model field | Scan records | Scan's chat ran on (before) | Scan's chat runs on (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same as my chats (X), profile default is X | X | X | X |
| Same as my chats (X), profile default is Y | X | Y | X |
| Explicit pick Z | Z | Z | Z |

## Summary

Keep deployment-security questions visible even when every source file has been read. Existing deployment-area reviewers now trace public and private ingress separately, including image-provided management listeners and access to shared data. - Add optional structured deployment coverage units through existing worker/checkpoint contracts. Workers record missing facts; the parent must explicitly resolve or defer them before sealing. Deferral finishes with partial coverage rather than spawning repeat workers.

- Show deployment evidence and unresolved limitations in the Workbench and Markdown report. File-count wording says “All in-scope files read,” not that every review obligation is complete.
- Preserve explicitly subsumed duplicate reports without labeling them false positives.

title: fix(hermes-security): require a verdict on possible duplicates before finalizing
body:
> #369 has merged. This branch is rebuilt on `main` and carries only its own two commits, `172fe36` and `c41f8d1` (the same changes as before the rebuild; `git range-diff` shows both unchanged).

## ELI5

When several reviewers in one scan found the same bug, the report listed it several times, sometimes once as high and again as medium. The scan already noticed some of these look-alikes but never made anyone decide, so they shipped as separate findings. Now the scan stops before finishing and asks a checker to say, for each look-alike pair, "same bug" or "two different bugs", and it will not finish until every pair has an answer.

## Summary

- **Finds more of the look-alikes.** Two findings are paired when the locations that define the bug overlap in one file: each finding's first location plus every location marked as the root control or the sink. Before, only the first locations were compared.
- **Asks for a verdict.** Once every candidate has been checked, the scan's next step is `validate` again, this time listing the open pairs (`kind: duplicate`). No new step name, tool, hook or table.
- **Two one-field verdicts on a candidate's `provenance`.** `duplicateOf` (one candidate id: "same bug as that one, keep that one") and `distinctFrom` (a list: "checked against these, a different bug"). `subsumes` still works and is still the way to carry the other finding's locations over.
- **Finalize waits.** `security_scan_finalize` refuses while a pair has no verdict, in the same place and style as the deployment-evidence refusal in #369. Nothing is written or sealed when it refuses.
- **Nothing merges on its own.** Overlap only flags a pair. Only an explicit verdict merges two findings.

## Before and after

| Situation | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Two reports of one bug that lead with different files but share the sink or root control | Not flagged; sealed as two findings | Flagged as one pair |
| A flagged pair nobody adjudicated | Sealed as two findings; the pair was only listed in the finalize result | `next` asks for a verdict; finalize refuses until it has one |
| Validator decides "same bug" | Had to resubmit the survivor with the other's locations and `subsumes` | Resubmits either one with `duplicateOf`; the survivor keeps its own locations and severity |
| Validator decides "different bugs" | No way to record it | `distinctFrom`; the pair is no longer flagged |
| `duplicateOf` naming itself, an unknown or rejected candidate (also one a survivor subsumed), or forming a cycle | n/a | Ignored; the pair stays open; nothing raises |
| Reviewed files changed after the scan started, pairs still open | Sealed partial | Unchanged: sealed partial, now with the open pairs named as a gap |
| Sealed findings | No verdict fields | Unchanged: neither new field reaches a sealed finding |

### Trade-offs

**What gets better**

- One finding per bug, with one severity, when a validator says two reports are the same.
- A "different bugs" decision is recorded once instead of being re-argued.

**What costs more**

- An extra validator round when pairs are open. Measured on the sealed findings of one real, large scan (60 findings with locations), where 17 pairs are the same bug reported twice (13 judged by re-reading the code, 4 low-severity pairs and the 6 "different" pairs judged from the findings' own text):

  | Rule | Pairs flagged | Same bug | Different bugs |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | First location only (before) | 3 | 3 | 0 |
  | First + root control + sink (this PR) | 18 | 12 | 6 |
  | Root control or sink against any location (not chosen) | 34 | 17 | 17 |
  | Every location regardless of role (not chosen) | 44 | 17 | 27 |

  In that scan a validator delegate took 136 to 205 seconds for 6 to 9 candidates. Pair verdicts are an estimate from that pace, not a measurement: about three more validator delegates, one extra round of a few minutes in the rolling pool.
- Finalize can now refuse. A scan stopped early with overlapping live candidates needs a verdict on each pair before it can be sealed, even as partial. The parent can give those verdicts itself through a validator-role result when delegation is unavailable. One exception: when reviewed files changed after the scan started, results are no longer accepted, so finalize seals a partial report as it did before, with the open pairs listed as a gap and in `possibleDuplicates`.

**Unchanged**

- Existing worker results stay valid; both fields are optional.
- Step names, tool names, the findings schema, the sealed bundle format and the reducer's conservation check.
- `possibleDuplicates` keeps its shape in `summary` and stays in the finalize result (empty there unless a changed target sealed with pairs open).
- Rejected candidates are never absorbed through `duplicateOf` and never become a survivor.

## Known gaps (out of scope)

- **Some duplicates are still missed.** In the scan measured above, 5 of the 17 same-bug pairs are not flagged: the two reports share a location, but one of them labelled it a wrapper or entry point instead of the root control or sink. Catching them doubles the pairs sent to validators (34, half of them different bugs), so this PR keeps the narrower rule.
- **No override.** There is no way to seal with a pair deliberately left open while the target is unchanged.
- **A validator can answer the wrong way.** Marking the duplicate `rejected` closes the pair, but the report then counts it as "not an issue" instead of a duplicate. The worker text says to leave the evidence state unchanged; nothing enforces it.
- **A validator that answers without either field** leaves the pair open, so the step repeats. Nothing bounds this: each accepted result counts as progress, so the automatic-continue limit never trips. The parent ends it by recording the verdict itself.
- **A "different" verdict is stored against the two original ids.** If one of them is later merged into another finding, that survivor can pair with the other side again and need a fresh verdict.
- **Running pairs** are recognized only when one live validator dispatch names both ids in its goal, as candidates are today.
- **Detection compares every pair of live candidates.** Fine at the sizes seen (tens to low hundreds); not measured on a scan with thousands of candidates.

## Verification

- Full plugin Python suite on Python 3.14 against core `main`: **733 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed** (699 on `main` at `1313994`, plus 34 new: 31 unit, 3 integration). No existing test was changed.
- New tests fail on the base for the stated reason: detection returns `[]` instead of the pair; the integration tests get `chains` where `validate` is expected. The three `derive` tests fail on the pure base with a `TypeError` for the new keyword, so they were also run with the keyword accepted and the new block disabled, giving `chains` instead of `validate` / `wait`.
- Integration tests go through `submit_worker_result` → `next_step` → `finalize` on a real store: `duplicateOf` seals one finding listing both source candidates; `distinctFrom` seals two; the sealed bundle verifies and carries none of the three verdict fields.
- An independent review of `172fe36` found two defects before publication, both fixed with regression tests in `c41f8d1` (that second commit was checked by rerunning the suites, not by a second independent review): a scan whose target changed could neither record a verdict nor be sealed, and a `duplicateOf` naming a rejected candidate was honored when a survivor had subsumed that candidate.
- Workbench Node suites: **45 passed** and **10 passed** (no desktop or dashboard file changed).
- `hermes plugins validate` passed; doctor registered **9 tools and 3 hooks**.
- Adapted-file provenance refreshed for the two pinned files this edits (`skills/security-audit/SKILL.md`, `references/worker-packet.md`); `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limits

Deterministic tests only. Whether validator models actually use the two fields when asked was **NOT RUN**: no live scan and no model evaluation was performed on this branch. Existing sealed scans are not rewritten; their `summary` may list more possible duplicates than before because detection is wider.

## Infographic

![one-bug-one-finding](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1df84/uxtIAUTpJH5QtbkwMk2Rk_322x1xXv.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): a later not-applicable no longer undoes a reviewed lane
body:
> #369 has merged. This branch is rebuilt on `main` and carries only its own commit, `e86b402` (the same change as before the rebuild; `git range-diff` shows it unchanged).

## ELI5

Every reviewer in a scan ticks off ten security categories for its own files. A reviewer that only looked at a data file would truthfully tick "does not apply" for a category, and that single tick replaced the "reviewed" recorded by everyone who had checked real code. If the scan had a finding in that category, the report then called the category contradictory and marked the whole scan incomplete. A "does not apply to my files" tick now leaves a reviewed category alone.

## Summary

Each worker reports the ten OWASP lanes for the files in its own packet, but the store keeps one row per lane and, among the closed states, the last writer won. A later `not_applicable` replaced `reviewed`, the ledger saw a finding mapped to a not-applicable lane, turned the lane `unknown` ("finding contradicts not_applicable lane"), and the scan sealed as `partial`.

For `lane:` units written by worker submissions:

- `not_applicable` arriving after `reviewed` leaves the stored row untouched: state, note and the list of reviews that closed it.
- `reviewed` arriving after `not_applicable` replaces it (as before) and starts the list of reviews afresh with the reviewer, so the stored lane is the same in either order.
- The worker's report is still written to the activity log in both cases.

| Submissions for one lane | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| reviewed, then not applicable | `not_applicable`; with a mapped finding: `unknown`, scan `partial` | `reviewed` |
| not applicable, then reviewed | `reviewed`, list of reviews includes the not-applicable worker | `reviewed`, list of reviews names only the reviewer |
| every worker says not applicable | `not_applicable`; with a mapped finding: `unknown` | unchanged |
| parent checkpoint sets not applicable on a reviewed lane | `not_applicable` | unchanged |

**Unchanged:** file, ASVS and deployment units; the open states and the rule that a closed unit is never downgraded to an open one; parent checkpoints (the parent's own disposition still replaces); the ledger rule that a finding mapped to an all-not-applicable lane is a contradiction. No schema, report-format, tool or worker-instruction change, and no migration.

## Known gaps (out of scope)

- A parent checkpoint that copies a data-only worker's "not applicable" onto a reviewed lane still reproduces the old result through that path. That is the parent's explicit disposition and is kept on purpose.
- ASVS control units have the same order dependence. They are informational and never make a scan partial.
- The activity entry for a kept lane looks like any other coverage update; nothing marks the row as unchanged.
- Worker instructions do not yet say that a lane state covers only the worker's own packet. That is wording in a provenance-pinned reference and is left for a follow-up.

## Verification

- Full plugin Python suite on Python 3.14 against core `main`: **709 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed** (699 on `main` at `1313994`, plus 10 new cases: 8 store-level, 2 through the service). No existing test was changed.
- New tests fail on the base for the stated reason: the store test gets `not_applicable` where `reviewed` is expected, and the service test gets lane state `unknown`. The assertion on the list of reviews for the not-applicable-then-reviewed order was tightened after that base run, so that one case was not run against the base in its final form.
- The control cases pin what must not change: a `file:` unit with the same sequence, an all-not-applicable lane with a mapped finding (the contradiction gap is still reported), and a parent checkpoint.
- Workbench Node suites: **45 passed** and **10 passed** (no desktop or dashboard file changed).
- `hermes plugins validate` passed; doctor registered **9 tools and 3 hooks**. No provenance-pinned file is edited; `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limits

Deterministic tests only; no live scan was run on this branch. Existing sealed scans are not rewritten.

## Infographic

![lane-reviews-stick](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1df89/zvk43NUSzoI--J1NTzjsQ_0yPVS3PD.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): let an undecided duplicate pair seal as partial
body:
> #369 and #371 have merged. This branch is rebuilt on `main` and carries only its own three commits: `74cda70` (`fix(hermes-security): let an undecided duplicate pair seal as partial`), `e3c20e0` (`fix(hermes-security): an explicit resume restarts automatic continue`) and `d22f9c7` (`fix(hermes-security): resume keeps a queued continue on record`). The first two are unchanged by the rebuild (`git range-diff` shows `=`).

## ELI5

When a scan finds two reports that look like the same bug, it asks a checker to say "same bug" or "two different bugs" before it will finish. Two things could go wrong. If the checker honestly could not tell, the only way to finish was to pick an answer anyway. And if the checker kept replying without picking, the scan kept asking forever. Now the checker can answer "could not decide": the scan finishes, marked incomplete, with that pair listed. And if three automatic retries in a row bring no answer, the scan pauses and asks for attention.

## Summary

- **A third verdict, `provenance.maybeDuplicateOf`.** A list of candidate ids: "checked against these; the code read could not settle whether it is the same bug". The pair stays listed, marked `verdict: "undecided"`, but is not asked about again and no longer stops `security_scan_finalize`. The scan seals as `partial` and counts the pair in a coverage gap.
- **A later real verdict wins.** `distinctFrom` on either side, or a `duplicateOf` that merges, replaces "undecided".
- **The automatic-continue limit now works in this step.** While pairs wait for a verdict, the step's progress key is derived from the set of open pairs instead of the latest event. It changes only when a pair is settled, dropped or added, so the existing limit (three continues without progress) pauses the scan when validators keep answering without a verdict.

- **Resume always restarts automatic continue.** Resuming a scan (the Workbench button, or cancel then resume) now lifts the automatic-continue hold itself (the no-progress count and the user-stop mark), in every step, instead of relying on the event it writes. A continue that is still queued stays on record, so a second one is not sent.

No new step name, tool, tool parameter, hook, store table or migration. `recovery.py` is not changed.

## Before and after

| Situation | Before (#371) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validator cannot tell whether two reports are one bug | Must answer "same" or "different" anyway, or the scan cannot finish | Answers `maybeDuplicateOf`; the scan finishes `partial` with the pair in a gap |
| Scan stopped early with an open pair, target unchanged | Cannot be sealed, even as partial | Sealed as partial once the pair is marked undecided |
| Undecided pair, then a validator records `distinctFrom` | n/a | The pair is closed; no gap for it |
| Validator keeps answering with no verdict, automatic continue on | Rescheduled without limit: each saved result counted as progress | Paused as "needs attention" after three continues with no pair settled |
| A verdict is recorded while paused | n/a | The count resets and the scan continues |
| The user resumes a scan that is paused or was stopped in this step | Continues (the resume event counted as progress) | Continues (resume lifts the hold) |
| No pairs open | unchanged | unchanged: every other step keeps the event-based key |

### Trade-offs

**What gets better**

- A scan can always be finished honestly: an unsettled pair becomes a named gap instead of a forced verdict.
- A validator loop ends after three automatic continues instead of running until someone notices.

**What costs more**

- **A lazy "undecided" is possible.** A validator can mark every pair undecided to finish quickly. The cost is visible: the scan is `partial`, the gap counts the pairs, and `summary` and the finalize result name each one.
- **During the duplicate step, only a settled pair counts as progress.** A turn the user stopped, or a "needs attention" pause, in that step is now lifted only by a verdict, a rejected or merged candidate, or a new pair. Before, any saved result or checkpoint lifted it. Resuming the scan still lifts it, and so does asking the agent to continue.

**Unchanged**

- Existing worker results stay valid; the field is optional and never reaches a sealed finding.
- `possibleDuplicates` keeps its shape; an undecided entry gains one key, `verdict`.
- Detection, `duplicateOf` resolution, the changed-target exception, the gap sentence and the refusal message.

## Known gaps (out of scope)

- A `maybeDuplicateOf` that names an unknown or non-overlapping candidate is stored and ignored, as `distinctFrom` already is.
- The gap sentence counts the open pairs without naming them; the names are in `summary` and the finalize result.
- The parent agent can still loop on its own turns (without automatic continue) if it keeps dispatching validators that give no verdict. The limit covers automatic continues only, as it does for every other step.
- A scan already in the duplicate step when the plugin updates gets one count reset, when its stored numeric key meets the new one.

## Verification

- Full plugin Python suite on Python 3.14 against core `main`: **763 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed** (745 on `main` at `a2e6a5e`, plus 18 new cases: 8 unit, 10 integration). No existing test was changed.
- New tests fail on the base for the stated reason: the reducer has no `undecided` result; the duplicate step's key was the event key passed in (`7 == 99`); the schema refuses the field; and the limit test gets `scheduled` where `capped` is expected, because the base scheduled a fourth continue after three answers with no verdict. The precedence test passes on the base (the base ignores the unknown field), so it is a guard, not regression proof.
- The limit test drives the real `recovery.continue_scan` with real validator submissions, clears each queued continue through the real `security_scan_get` handler, and checks that a real verdict resets the count.
- The undecided test goes through `submit_worker_result` → `next_step` → `finalize` on a real store: status `partial`, the gap sentence for one pair, two findings sealed, the bundle verifies, and no sealed finding or retained row carries any of the four verdict fields.
- An independent review of `74cda70` found one defect before publication: with the pair-based key, a scan that was paused or user-stopped in the duplicate step stayed held after an explicit resume. `e3c20e0` fixes it with four regression cases (paused and stopped, each with and without a cancel first), which fail on `74cda70` with `capped` or `stopped-by-user` where `scheduled` is expected. That second commit was checked by rerunning the suites, not by a second independent review.
- A second independent review, of `e3c20e0` alone, found one defect: resume cleared the whole guard, so resuming from the dashboard while a continue was still queued in the chat sent a second one. `d22f9c7` fixes it with two regression cases (with and without a cancel first), which fail on `e3c20e0` with `'scheduled' == 'already-queued'`. `d22f9c7` itself was tested, not independently reviewed.
- Workbench Node suites: **45 passed** and **10 passed** (no desktop or dashboard file changed; neither reads `progressKey` or `possibleDuplicates`).
- `hermes plugins validate` passed; doctor registered **9 tools and 3 hooks**.
- Adapted-file provenance refreshed for the two pinned files this edits (`skills/security-audit/SKILL.md`, `references/worker-packet.md`); `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limits

Deterministic tests only. Whether validator models use the third answer sparingly was **NOT RUN**: no live scan and no model evaluation was performed on this branch.

## Infographic

![the-third-answer](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1eba8/7uXaa3VDP2sS3DYvFzyZV_kyESpwbn.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): test commands no longer inherit credential pointers
body:
## ELI5

When you allow a scan to run tests, it runs the repository's own commands as you, in a temporary copy. Before running them it removed passwords and keys from the environment, but it left in the settings that tell tools where your credentials live: your SSH agent, your Kubernetes config, your cloud profile, your database address. A test command could use those against real systems. Those settings are now removed too. Your home folder is still readable, so this is still not a sandbox, and the README now says that plainly.

## Summary

Refs #359. Reported by @skhdev-dotcom.

- **Removed from the test environment as well:** `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `SSH_ASKPASS`, `GIT_ASKPASS`, `GNUPGHOME`, `GPG_AGENT_INFO`, `KUBECONFIG`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE`, `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`, `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `NETRC`, `PGPASSFILE`, `PGSERVICEFILE` and `DATABASE_URL`, matched whatever their case. One function builds the environment for both the POSIX and the Windows runner, so both get it.
- **Wording corrected.** The helper's docstring said "minus credentials"; it and the README now say the filter is name keywords plus a fixed list of names, that any other variable passes through, and that files under `HOME` stay readable.

| Variable in the user's shell | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Name contains `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `API_KEY`, `ACCESS_KEY`, `CREDENTIAL`, ... | removed | removed |
| `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `KUBECONFIG`, `AWS_PROFILE`, `DATABASE_URL` and the others listed above | passed to the test command | removed |
| `PATH`, `HOME`, toolchain and locale variables | passed | passed |
| Files under `HOME` (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.kube`) | readable | readable (unchanged) |

### Trade-offs

**What gets better**

- A repository's test command no longer picks up the SSH agent, a Kubernetes context, a cloud profile or a database address by default. This matters most on macOS and Windows, where the test's network is not isolated; on Linux with `unshare` the network is already off.

**What costs more**

- A test suite that needs one of these variables now fails or skips inside the harness, and its finding stays "not confirmed by test" instead of confirmed. The likeliest case is a suite that reads `DATABASE_URL` for a local test database.

**Unchanged**

- `HOME` and toolchain caches, so cargo, npm, gradle and pip keep working with the network off.
- Everything else about the harness: the temporary copy, the limits, the paired controls, who may allow tests.

## What this does not do (and why)

- **It does not hide files under `HOME`.** Code running as the user can open `~/.ssh` or `~/.aws` by path. The issue suggests a throwaway `HOME`; that would not stop a read by absolute path, and it would break toolchain caches that the harness relies on when the network is off. Closing this needs a real filesystem sandbox, which is a separate change.
- **`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` and `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`**, named in the issue, were already removed: both names contain `CREDENTIAL`.
- **It is a deny-list.** A pointer variable not on the list still passes. A strict allow-list is the cleaner design and needs a compatibility pass over the supported stacks first.
- **The catalog entry's disclosure** ("credential-looking environment variables removed; that is not a sandbox") stays true and is not changed here.

## Verification

- Full plugin Python suite on Python 3.14 against core `main`: **672 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed** (670 on the base commit `ab348e1`, plus 2 new tests). No existing test was changed.
- The new tests fail on the base for the stated reason. A real command run through `run_local` reports which of the listed names exist in its own environment: on the base it reports all sixteen plus the two harmless ones, and now only the two harmless ones (`HS_TEST_HARMLESS`, `PATH`). The same run shows `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` was already removed before this change. A second test covers lower- and mixed-case names.
- An independent review of the first commit found no runtime problem and one wording issue: the README and docstring still read as if every credential pointer is removed. The second commit (`docs(hermes-security): say the test environment filter is a fixed list`) fixes that wording.
- Workbench Node suites: **44 passed** and **10 passed** (no desktop or dashboard file changed).
- `hermes plugins validate` passed; doctor registered **9 tools and 3 hooks**. No provenance-pinned file is edited; `git diff --check` is clean.

## Limits

Run locally on Linux only; macOS and Windows are covered by this repository's CI. No live scan was run on this branch.

## Infographic

![trimmed-test-environment](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab1ebf6/yX64FZ9bWtqn7ujM0y0Pv_SMYenRaE.png)

title: fix(hermes-security): bump to 0.1.3
body:
## ELI5

This gives the Security plugin a new version number, 0.1.3, so Hermes can tell the copy with today's fixes apart from the old one. Nothing changes in how it works; the fixes themselves are in the PRs listed below.

> All six have merged; this branch is rebuilt on `main` and carries only the bump commit. The core catalog pin (`plugin-catalog/hermes-security.yaml` in hermes-agent) then moves to the merge commit of this PR.

## Summary

- 0.1.2 → 0.1.3 in all five places the version lives, the same set the 0.1.2 bump touched: `plugin.yaml`, `pyproject.toml`, `hermes_security/__init__.py` (which scan manifests stamp as `producer.version`), `dashboard/manifest.json`, and the manifest test.
- A patch release, covering:
