title: fix(hermes-security): scan and fix chats run on the scan's own profile
body:
## ELI5

You run a security scan from one agent (say `agent-a`), then press **Fix in chat** on a finding. The fix chat opened on the `default` agent instead, an agent that did not run the scan and cannot even read its data. Continuing or stopping a scan had the same problem. Every chat the Security page starts now runs on the agent that owns the scan. You can also choose another agent for the fix, and that agent gets what it needs to work on it.

## Summary

- **Root cause:** the page called `session.create` / `prompt.submit` / `session.resume` / `session.interrupt` without a `profile`. On the Desktop's shared socket, an omitted profile resolves to the socket's launch profile (usually `default`), not the profile whose plugin store holds the scan. Scan data is profile-local (`resolve_data_dir()` → `<profile home>/plugin-data/...`), so the scan ran under one profile and its chats under another.
- **New `GET /owner`** (dashboard API): returns `{profile}` from `get_service().profile`, the profile that owns this page's scans. It is added to the `assertBackendPath` allow-list.
- **Every session verb names that profile**, through `onProfile(profile, params)`: scan launch, **Continue scan** (submit, resume, resubmit), **Open chat** (`host.openSession(id, { profile })`), **Stop** (`session.interrupt`), and **Fix in chat**. If the socket cannot reach the profile, it refuses (`profile_mismatch`) instead of quietly running the work on another agent.
- **Agent picker on Fix in chat:** it lists the installed profiles (`host.profiles.list()`). The default is "Scan agent (<owner>)", and the picker only appears when there is more than one choice.
  - The owner keeps the existing prompt (it reads the finding with the security tools).
  - Another agent cannot read the owner's scan store, so its prompt carries the finding facts inline (title, severity, taxonomy, locations, summary, root cause, remediation), marked as untrusted data to re-check against current code.
  - For a finding flagged `secret`, the inline facts are reduced to locations, with no evidence text.

## Test plan

- [x] e2e: the scan launch, continue (including the resume path) and fix chats all carry the owner profile. The picker lists the owner first plus the other profiles. A fix sent to `other-agent` creates and submits on `other-agent`, with the inline facts. A secret finding never inlines its evidence. When the owner is picked, the prompt is identical to the default prompt. The 4 updated tests fail on the previous `plugin.js`. JS suite: 55 pass.
- [x] API: `/owner` returns `default` for the root home and `other-agent` for `profiles/other-agent`. This test fails on the previous API (no route). Full Python suite on current `main`: 765 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- [ ] Not exercised in a live Desktop window (unit/e2e mocks of the SDK host only).

title: perf(directsdk): one stdin watchdog thread per request, not a Timer thread per replayed frame
body:
Every replayed frame is one stdin write, and each write started a `threading.Timer` as its stall guard. A Timer is a thread, so a 300-round history started 602 threads per model call. One watchdog thread per request now guards every write.

## Before

- `send()` creates, starts and cancels one `threading.Timer` per frame.
- 602 Timer threads for a 300-round history cost 148 ms of CPU in the Hermes process (measured alone), about a third of the plugin's own CPU for that call.

## After

- `_StdinWatch`: one daemon thread per request, started at the first write, stopped when stdin closes and in the request's cleanup.
- A write only records when it began (one `time.monotonic()` and two attribute writes). No thread start and no wake-up per frame.
- The thread never sleeps longer than the timeout. So it always wakes before the deadline of a write that began while it slept, then sleeps until exactly that deadline. A blocked write is killed at the same moment as before.

## What the user sees

| Plugin CPU per call (Hermes process) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 100 tool rounds replayed | 0.17 to 0.20 s | 0.10 to 0.14 s |
| 300 tool rounds replayed | 0.41 to 0.44 s | 0.21 to 0.25 s |

Linux x86-64 VPS, 4 vCPU, Claude Code 2.1.327 against a loopback upstream, 3 runs each, interleaved, host under its normal load. No change to requests, timeouts, cancellation or errors.

This is small: about 3% of a long per-call request, because most of that request's CPU is Claude Code's own (below). It is the largest avoidable item on the plugin's side. The other candidates, measured at 300 rounds, were 1 to 6 ms each: history preparation, frame copies, frame encoding, each relay transform.

## Where a per-call request's CPU goes

Same host, main `e726eb7`, real CLI against a loopback upstream, 60 KB system prompt, 40 tools, 2 KB tool results. CPU of the Claude Code children per call (`getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN)`):

| History | CPU per call (s) |
|---|---|
| 0 tool rounds | 1.1 to 1.4 |
| 100 tool rounds | 2.6 to 3.9, median 3.0 |
| 300 tool rounds | 4.7 to 5.8 |

- Start of a process: 0.8 to 1.4 CPU-s per call, with or without tools.
- Replay: about 15 ms of CPU per replayed tool round. Claude Code runs one `system/init` and one `result` per replayed user frame (101 of each for 100 rounds).
- The plugin's own Python: 0.2 s per call at 100 rounds, 0.4 s at 300. This PR halves it.

Two things I tried on the per-call path and dropped:

- Writing the replayed frames without waiting for each acknowledgment. CPU of the children drops from 2.9 s to 1.4 s at 100 rounds, but Claude Code then batches the queued frames and the upstream request changes: 227 KB instead of 419 KB, every earlier tool result replaced by a 129-byte placeholder, the first user turn moved to the end. The acknowledgment per frame is needed for correctness.
- JavaScriptCore tier flags on the child (`BUN_JSC_useFTLJIT=0`, `BUN_JSC_useDFGJIT=0`): 6 to 13% less CPU at 100 rounds, inside the noise at 0 rounds, and undocumented.

## Tests

- `test_history_replay_starts_one_stdin_watchdog_not_a_thread_per_frame`: 121 frames, one watchdog thread, no Timer, fewer than 10 thread starts, and the thread ends with the request. Fails on main.
- `test_stdin_watchdog_fires_at_the_deadline_of_the_write_in_flight`: a write that begins while the thread sleeps is killed at its own deadline, not at the thread's next wake-up.
- `test_stdin_watchdog_ignores_short_writes_however_long_they_run_together`.
- `test_blocked_stdin_has_deadline_and_cancellation` (existing) still passes, for the deadline and for the cancel case.
- The three new tests fail on main and pass here.
- Suite on Linux, Python 3.14, against current core: 590 passed, 1 failed once under load (`test_a_crashed_native_frees_its_slot_for_the_next_call`, which orders two calls with a 0.1 s sleep). It passes alone 4 of 4 on main and on this branch, and 3 of 3 with its whole file.
- `evals/directsdk_admission.py` on Claude Code 2.1.327: 12 of 12 cases.
- `hermes plugins validate`: passed.

## Not in this PR

- Claude Code's start and replay cost. #402 addresses it; I will post this host's CPU numbers for its bench there.
- #402 moves `send()` into a method and keeps a Timer per frame. The same watchdog fits there, and I can rebase on whichever lands first.

title: fix(directsdk): the launch profile keeps its own login on a multi-profile host (#409)
body:
Refs #409. Under multiplexing core counts every task as routed, so the served-profile guard refused a launch profile whose login is the shared `~/.claude` ("This profile has no Claude login of its own"). In one commit, two exemptions replace only that refusal: a profile with its own scoped `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `claude_config_dir` or scoped `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` gets exactly what it gets on main.
**The issue's scenario: the launch profile's own unstamped turns.** On a Desktop backend serving several profiles, core binds the launch profile's own turns unstamped (`launch_profile_runtime_scope`, `model_switch`). With multiplexing active, a bound unstamped scope and the call outside core's restart-safe cron worker process, a profile with no login of its own keeps the inherited login. A stamped scope stays refused, even one stamped with the process home, and no bound scope still fails closed. It does not cover a multiplexing messaging gateway, which stamps even its own profile's turns.
**The stamped case: `inherit_launch_login` (bool, default off).** It covers the tasks core stamps with the process home in a process started for that profile: its turns on a multiplexing messaging gateway, its own cron fires, the delegate route and the dashboard's own-profile path. It counts only as a YAML boolean `true` in the profile's own `config.yaml` (read from the profile's own `config.yaml` file on disk, so a managed overlay never counts, a file that does not parse counts as off, and the setting is not honoured where the configuration does not live in that file, such as a remote config backend), when the stamp, the config home and the routing process home are all that profile, and outside the restart-safe worker process. Another profile never gains the login; a backend started for another profile never lends its own. `claude_config_dir: ~/.claude` is no substitute: Claude Code keys its Keychain login by config directory.
**Out of scope:** the restart-safe worker process (neither exemption applies there) and any profile that is neither the launch profile nor opted in.
**Tests** (macOS; see the note on the first CI run below). Red on main, green here: the issue's repro through `launch_profile_runtime_scope`, the multiplexed launch turn, the own cron fire through core's `_fire_secret_scope`, and the manifest field. Guards mutation-checked one line at a time (each goes red when its condition is removed): only a YAML boolean opts in; the profile-local read (a managed `true` and a malformed config do not opt in); no exemption inside the worker process (env marker or `__main__`, plus core's `_run_external_worker_payload`); another profile and a foreign backend never gain the login; the stamp, config home and process home are each moved alone; the unstamped check. Regressions against the previous head, red there and green here: an exempt profile keeps its own scoped directory, token or `claude_config_dir` (credential precedence, both exemptions), and the unstamped exemption needs multiplexing. Full plugin suite in an environment built with this repository's CI install recipe (core main, no PyYAML): 623 passed; main in the same environment: 587 passed. The two CI evals pass there. No version bump (0.4.0 is unreleased).

**After the first CI run.** The first run of this PR failed the ten opt-in tests on all three platforms. The option was parsed with PyYAML, which core does not install (core parses YAML with its own `hermes_yaml`), so on a plain install the import failed, the failure was swallowed and the option never applied. The local test environment had PyYAML through another package, which hid it. Two follow-up commits: (1) the option is parsed with `hermes_yaml.safe_load`, with a regression test that makes `yaml` unimportable; (2) the sentence above about a remote config backend is now enforced in code: the local file is read only when core's config backend has a config file (`supports_file_tooling`), with tests for a backend that has no file, is unavailable or errors, and for a core from before config backends. Each new test is red on the commit before it.

title: fix(claude-directsdk): strip vendor prefix from model ids
body:
## What

Hermes core can hand this provider an OpenRouter-style canonical id (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`) even when the config names the plain route `claude-sonnet-5`.

`model_catalog._route_base()` only stripped a leading `claude-`, so `anthropic/...` reached the native CLI verbatim. The CLI 404s on it. Because a 404 is not an auth error, `_allows_auth_retry()` denies every subsequent retry with `HERMES_MODEL_ADMISSION_CONSUMED`, and Hermes silently falls back to OpenRouter — the setup looks like it works while defeating the subscription.

## Fix

`_route_base` now strips a leading `anthropic/` or `openrouter/` before resolving aliases and context windows. Unknown namespaces are left untouched so a genuinely foreign model still reaches the CLI and fails there, rather than being guessed at. The vendor prefix is handled before the dotted-name and `claude-` normalization steps, so `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`, `[1m]` suffixes, and the mandatory-thinking check all resolve normally.

## Verification

`tests/test_vendor_prefixed_route.py` (5 tests) covers the reported id, the `openrouter/` form, dotted + `[1m]` variants, the thinking policy on the stripped route, and the unknown-vendor control.

```
pytest tests/test_vendor_prefixed_route.py -q   5 passed
```

Fixes #377

title: fix(claude-directsdk): prefer a supported CLI over an outdated PATH claude
body:
## What

A systemd service PATH can list `~/.hermes/node/bin` ahead of the user's current CLI install. With an old Claude Code (2.1.148 in the report) the plugin's requests go out without the ~15k-token tool payload, so the model answers as a title generator (`{"title": ...}`). It never reproduced interactively because the shell PATH has the current CLI first (#380).

## Fix

`_resolve()` checks the version of a bare `claude` found on PATH via `--version`. When it is below the supported minimum (2.1.280), the resolver looks through the existing install prefixes (`.local/bin`, `.claude/local`, etc.) and picks the first supported executable. A failed/unparseable version check keeps the PATH result — no behaviour change. An explicit command or `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` override is never second-guessed.

## Verification

`tests/test_cli_version_resolution.py` (4 tests): supported PATH CLI kept, outdated PATH CLI replaced by a supported install, explicit override left untouched, and unreadable version falls back to PATH — **4 passed**.

Fixes #380

title: fix(claude-directsdk): stop client.close() cancelling parallel calls
body:
## What

Two auxiliary tool calls in one step (e.g. two `vision_analyze` calls) often fail with "Claude request cancelled" or "Claude client is closed". Hermes' auxiliary cache closes a client bound to a **different live event loop**; this plugin's `Client.close()` then cancelled every in-flight request on it, including the other call's. Reporter measured 24/47 parallel calls failing vs 1/73 single calls.

## Fix

`Client.close()` is now a no-op, and `_closed` is never set. Each request owns and reaps its own native process, so nothing shared is leaked; explicit per-request cancellation still goes through `Stream.close()` / `cancel()`. This matches the workaround the reporter verified in the field.

## Verification

`tests/test_client_close_parallel.py` (2 tests): closing a client with two in-flight requests cancels neither, and a closed client can still register a new request (the cache reuses clients across tool calls). Red/green confirmed — **2 fail** on the unmodified source, **2 pass** with the fix.

Fixes #378

title: fix(memory-wiki): keep cron and subagent runs out of subjects and recent sessions
body:
## What

On a profile with recurring cron jobs, the Memory Wiki **Subjects** list and **Recent sessions** are dominated by cron scaffolding ("exit code", "chief pilot") and delegated subagent runs instead of actual conversations. Both call sites loaded every session with no source filter, then mined title/preview/tool names from each (#379).

## Fix

`NON_CONVERSATION_SOURCES = {"cron", "subagent"}` is filtered at the two conversational call sites:

- `_load_memory_sessions()` (subject aggregation) — `conversations_only=True` by default
- `build_memory_overview()`'s `recent_sessions` list

The **daily log keeps full coverage** — it is an activity record, so `build_daily_logs()` passes `conversations_only=False` and still includes cron/subagent runs.

## Verification

`tests/test_memory_wiki_cron_filter.py` (3 tests): cron/subagent excluded from subjects, excluded from recent sessions, and still present in the daily log. The existing `test_memory_wiki_core.py` suite: **16 passed**.

Fixes #379

title: feat(claude-directsdk): opt-in extra_usage reserve before the first billed request
body:
## What

`extra_usage` under `ask`/`stop` refuses only **after** the account is already drawing paid extra usage — the request that first crosses the limit is billed. For unattended runs (`/goal`, cron) that is one request too late (#398, item 1).

## Fix

Adds `extra_usage_reserve_percent` (e.g. `97`). Under `ask`/`stop`, `observe_usage()` treats an account-wide plan window as full once it reaches that percent, so the refusal happens **before** the first billed overage request, using the same zero-inference `get_usage` probe. Unset, non-numeric, ≤0 or >100 all mean 100 — existing installs behave exactly as before. `notify`/`allow` never probe, so the setting cannot change their behaviour.

This is item 1 of #398 only; the cross-process state, UI notice, model-scoped windows and fallback items are separate asks and are not included.

## Verification

`tests/test_extra_usage_reserve.py` (5 tests): threshold parsing and invalid-value fallback, below-reserve not spilling, at-reserve spilling, and the default 100 boundary. Run with the existing extra-usage suite: **13 passed**.

Refs #398

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] test: keep missing-CLI and no-uid tests independent of the host
body:
## Problem

Two test-only host dependencies make the suite fail on machines that differ from a clean CI runner:

1. **Missing-CLI discovery tests find a real `claude`.** `_resolve` falls back to `_SYSTEM_PREFIXES` (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`). On a host with Claude Code installed there, `test_missing_claude_is_reported_on_every_path` and `test_resolve_honors_the_env_dict_not_the_process_path` resolve the real binary even with an empty `PATH`. This is the same flaky missing-CLI class the second test's docstring describes, via the prefix fallback rather than the process `PATH`.
2. **The `no_uid` workspace case fails without `USER`.** It deletes `os.getuid`. With no `USER` in the environment (`env -i`, some containers or supervisors), `_with_login_identity` falls back to `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid())` and raises `AttributeError` before the workspace branch under test runs.

## Change (tests only, no runtime change)

- Add a `no_system_claude` fixture to `test_directsdk_discovery.py`. It sets `_SYSTEM_PREFIXES = ()` on both the flat and the package-relative `directsdk_setup` copies, and asserts that both copies exist so the patch can't silently miss one. The two missing-CLI tests use it.
- Add a positive test showing the system prefix is still a fallback: it resolves when `PATH` is empty, keeps extra argv, and never overrides an explicit command or a `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` that is set but missing.
- Set a synthetic `USER` in the workspace `no_uid` fixture.

No existing assertion is removed or weakened.

## Verification

Red on `main` (`e726eb7`), green on this branch. Linux host with Claude Code installed via npm at `/usr/local/bin/claude`, hermes-agent `ae2a81cc` as `HERMES_AGENT_REPO`/`PYTHONPATH` (same wiring as `tests.yml`), Python 3.14.9, pytest 9.1.1. Each run used `env -i` with `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`, an empty temporary `HOME`, and no network:

```
python -m pytest -q tests/test_directsdk_discovery.py tests/test_directsdk_workspace.py
```

| | no `USER` | `USER=synthuser` |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 3 failed, 10 passed | 2 failed, 11 passed |
| this branch | 14 passed | 14 passed |

Failures on `main`:

- `test_missing_claude_is_reported_on_every_path` and `test_resolve_honors_the_env_dict_not_the_process_path`: `_resolve(None, {'PATH': '<tmp>/nowhere'})` returns `['/usr/local/bin/claude']` (both environments).
- `test_unsafe_shared_workspace_falls_back_to_one_private_workspace_per_process[no_uid]`: `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'getuid'` at `directsdk.py` `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid())` (no-`USER` environment only).

On this branch the added `test_system_install_prefix_remains_a_fallback_not_an_explicit_command_override` passes in both environments.

title: fix(claude-directsdk): keep a relay transport failure classifiable
body:
## What

When the first upstream response is HTTP 200 but the stream ends early, the plugin correctly refuses native's extra requests at the consumed admission gate, then raises `ClaudeAPIError` with `status_code=None`. The transport label (`UpstreamIdle`, `ConnectionResetError`, …) survived only inside the message prose.

Core's classifier is message-based (`_SERVER_DISCONNECT_PATTERNS` / `_PREMATURE_CLOSE_PATTERNS` / `_CONNECTION_MESSAGE_PATTERNS`), and `relay failure UpstreamIdle` matches none of them. So an auxiliary call — e.g. a compaction summary — got `FailoverReason.unknown`: no same-provider transient retry, no `fallback_chain`, and no compressor network-failure guard. With `abort_on_summary_failure: false` that lets a local fallback handoff replace the live middle window.

## Fix

`transport_phrase()` maps a relay failure label to the canonical wording core already matches, and the wrapper appends it in brackets. The original label stays in the message for reports. Unknown/non-transport failures (`KeyError`, `None`) add nothing, so their classification is unchanged. **No core change is needed** — the phrases are asserted to be members of core's existing pattern tuples.

## Verification

`tests/test_transport_phrase.py` (8 tests): the label→phrase map, qualified-name normalisation, unknown/empty inputs, and a guard asserting every emitted phrase is one core already recognises.

End-to-end through the real classifier:

| relay failure | reason | transport | should_compress |
|---|---|---|---|
| `UpstreamIdle` | timeout | **connection** | False |
| `ConnectionResetError` | timeout | **connection** | False |
| none | unknown | None | False |

```
pytest tests/test_transport_phrase.py tests/test_directsdk_errors.py -q   33 passed
ruff check   All checks passed!
```

Fixes #396

title: [advanced-delegation] profile_routes: routed child gets only the parent's tools, not the target profile's own
body:
## Problem and use case

A low-privilege "front desk" profile reads untrusted inbound mail and chat. On purpose, it has only its messaging, kanban and `delegation` toolsets. It uses `profile_routes` to pass questions to specialist profiles, for example a project profile that has file, terminal and MCP tools (CRM servers) in its own config.

The routed child runs as the specialist profile (model, SOUL, skills, credentials), but it gets **no usable tools**. The child reported: "This session has no available file-search or terminal tools". It could not answer.

## Cause

Core `tools/delegate_tool_toolsets.py::_resolve_child_toolsets` builds child toolsets from the parent only: "Children never gain tools the parent lacks". `tools/delegate_tool.py` also says "A spawn always inherits the parent's toolsets". A `profile` route does not change this. The target profile's own `platform_toolsets` and `mcp_servers` are ignored.

So with `profile_routes`, the useful pattern (a restricted router that hands work to capable specialists) cannot work. Delegation only works when the parent already has every tool the specialist needs. That defeats the isolation that the router exists for.

## Requested behaviour

Add an opt-in per route, for example:

```yaml
delegation:
  backends:
    profile_routes:
      profiles:
        - name: project-a
          description: ...
          tools: own   # child uses project-a's own toolsets and MCP servers
```

- `inherit` (default): current behaviour.
- `own`: the child uses the target profile's configured toolsets and MCP servers, with the usual blocked tools still stripped.

The operator's allowlist of routes stays the security boundary, so the model cannot pick arbitrary profiles.

## Environment

Hermes Agent v0.23.2 (ae2a81ccc0), advanced-delegation 1.1.0, Linux.

title: [advanced-delegation] profile_routes: optional strict mode — refuse a task that names no profile
body:
### What

In `profile_routes` mode a task that carries no `profile` silently runs on the parent's route: either the configured `default`, or — when no `default` is set — the coordinator's own model (`profile_routes.py:104-117` returns `{}`). Both are fine for casual use, but a workflow that treats profiles as roles (each child must run as a named profile, with that profile's model, credentials and `SOUL.md`) has no way to make the omission loud. The failure is invisible: the child's report looks normal and only the session row shows the wrong model.

It matters more because a `delegate_task` call can lose its `profile` before the provider ever sees it — NousResearch/hermes-agent#156033 (core drops a top-level `profile`; same class as hermes-agent#148831 for `model_map`'s `option`). With a strict mode, that silent drop becomes a readable tool error instead of a child on the coordinator's model.

### Proposal

One optional setting, `delegation.backends.profile_routes.require_profile` (default `false`):

```yaml
delegation:
  backend: profile_routes
  backends:
    profile_routes:
      profiles:
        - name: researcher
          description: Web research and long-form summaries.
      require_profile: true   # a task without `profile` is refused; `default` is ignored
```

- `true` + a task without `profile` → `DelegationRouteError("this task needs 'profile' (delegation.backends.profile_routes.require_profile is on): choose one of <names>")`, or `"… the profiles list is empty"` when nothing is configured.
- `true` + a `default` set → one warning, `default` ignored: two possible sources of a silent route is exactly what the flag exists to remove.
- `false` (default) → today's behavior, no change for existing installs.

### Patch

`profile_routes.py`, one README line and four tests (happy to send it as a PR):

```diff
-from agent.delegation_provider import DelegationProvider
+from agent.delegation_provider import DelegationProvider, DelegationRouteError

     def route_task(self, task, config):
+        settings = self.settings(config)
+        default = settings.get("default")
+        require_profile = settings.get("require_profile", False)
+        if require_profile and default is not None:
+            _warn_once("%s.default is ignored when require_profile is on.", SETTINGS_PATH)
         chosen = task.get(PARAMETER)
         if chosen:
             # Core already refused anything outside the enum before calling us.
             return {"profile": chosen, "label": chosen}
-        settings = self.settings(config)
-        default = settings.get("default")
+        if require_profile:
+            names = ", ".join(name for name, _ in configured_profiles(settings))
+            message = f"this task needs 'profile' ({SETTINGS_PATH}.require_profile is on): "
+            raise DelegationRouteError(message + (f"choose one of {names}" if names else "the profiles list is empty"))
         if isinstance(default, str) and default.strip():
             default = default.strip()
             if default in {name for name, _ in configured_profiles(settings)}:
                 return {"profile": default, "label": default}
```

Tests added locally: the refusal lists the configured choices; an explicit `profile` still routes; `default` + strict yields exactly one warning and still refuses; an empty or non-list `profiles` refuses with the other message.

### Environment

Hermes 0.23.x (0.23.0–0.23.2), `advanced-delegation` 1.1.0, three hosts (Windows 11). Verified in production: with the strict mode on, a stale pinned schema fails loudly instead of running the child on the coordinator's model.

title: [bubblewrap] Chat attachments staged in HERMES_HOME/attachments are invisible inside the sandbox
body:
### Plugin

bubblewrap

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Files attached in the TUI, the Webapp or a dashboard plugin (the `file.attach` RPC) never reach an agent whose terminal runs under `terminal.backend: bubblewrap`. Neither the agent's terminal nor its file tools can open them, and `find /` inside the sandbox does not find them.

Expected: the agent can open what the user attached, as it can with the docker backend.

**Where the file goes.** With the default `attachments.storage: hermes-home`, the gateway writes the upload to `<profile HERMES_HOME>/attachments/<name>` (`tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py`, `_session_home_dir` and `_stage_session_file_attachment`). The prompt carries `@file:<that absolute path>`. Small UTF-8 text files still work, because `@file:` expansion inlines them on the gateway side. Large, binary or non-UTF-8 files get the "use your tools to work with it" block, which points to a path that does not exist inside the sandbox.

**Why the sandbox can't see it.** `sandbox.py` `sensitive_paths()` hides `HERMES_HOME` and `HOME/.hermes` as a whole, and `_late_mounts()` binds back only the scratch dir, the state dir and, under `home_mode: profile`, `HERMES_HOME/home`. An operator bind cannot fix this either: `binds.py` `_refusal()` refuses any source inside a Hermes home ("lies in the Hermes home ..., which the sandbox hides").

**Core expects the backend to mount it.** `tools/credential_files.py` `_CACHE_DIRS` lists `attachments`, `images` and `composer-pastes` so that sandboxed backends can reach staged uploads (hermes-agent #69575, #76577, #110174). The docstring of `_profile_attachments_storage` calls the profile-home store the one "the sandbox mounts". The plugin does not use `get_cache_directory_mounts()` and declares no `cache_path_base`, so these directories stay hidden.

**Reproduce**

1. A profile with `terminal.backend: bubblewrap` (any sandbox profile), `terminal.cwd` set to a work directory.
2. In the TUI, attach a file that is not inlined, for example a CSV larger than the inline limit or a zip.
3. Ask the agent to `ls -la` the path in the `@file:` reference, or to `read_file` it: "No such file or directory" / "File not found". On the host the file is there.

**Workarounds**

- `attachments.storage: workspace` stages into `<cwd>/.hermes/attachments`, inside the writable cwd.
- Make `<HERMES_HOME>/attachments` a symlink to a directory the sandbox binds. `_stage_session_file_attachment` returns the resolved path, so the reference names the visible location. This is what we run now.

**Suggestion.** Bind the staging directories from `_CACHE_DIRS` that carry user input (`attachments`, `images`, `composer-pastes`) read-only at their own paths, among the late mounts, as is done for the scratch dir. Read-only keeps a command from planting files that the gateway later treats as an upload. Alternatively, document that bubblewrap profiles need `attachments.storage: workspace`.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.23.0 (2026.9.24) · stable
bubblewrap 1.5.1 (catalog: official), source read at hermes-official-plugins main e726eb7
Linux (Debian LXC), terminal.backend: bubblewrap, plugins.entries.bubblewrap.settings.profile: network
```

### Logs

```text
No error is logged on the gateway side. Inside the sandbox:
$ ls -la <HERMES_HOME>/attachments
ls: cannot access '<HERMES_HOME>/attachments': No such file or directory
```

title: fix(homeassistant): bound every wedgeable await during connect and teardown (salvage #6)
body:
Salvage of #6 (port of NousResearch/hermes-homeassistant#1 / hermes-agent#80372 by @Sora-bluesky), rebased onto current `main`; authorship kept.

Bounds every wedgeable await on the Home Assistant connect/teardown path so a hung auth handshake or a wedged WebSocket/session close can't leave the adapter silently deaf while the gateway reports it running (NousResearch/hermes-agent#67470):
- `_ws_connect` builds the session/socket locally, bounds `ws_connect` and each handshake send/receive (30 s), closes the local pair on failure/timeout/cancel, and only assigns `self._session`/`self._ws` after a successful handshake.
- Closes go through a bounded close (5 s); `disconnect()` bounds the listen-task cancel.

Rebase notes: kept main's configurable `ws_heartbeat_seconds` (`heartbeat=self._ws_heartbeat`) in the new connect code. Second commit gives the heartbeat test's fake session `closed`/`close()`, since the connect now closes the session when `ws_connect` raises.

Tests: `test_homeassistant_network_reconnect.py` 15 failed on `main`'s adapter, all pass here; homeassistant suite 229 passed, 2 skipped.

Supersedes #6.

title: feat(homeassistant): cross-platform deliver + session-mode delivery for watched entities (salvage #199/#5)
body:

- **`deliver`** (per entity/domain + top-level default): route a state-change alert to another platform's home channel (tag `ha_events:<platform>[;session]`).

Each call is wrapped to degrade to the HA notification if core changes, but it is a private-API dependency.

title: fix(memory-wiki): prioritize user topics over tool and system noise (salvage #48)
body:
Salvage of #48 (port of NousResearch/hermes-memory-wiki#3 by @tillstriegel), rebased onto current `main` with authorship kept, plus one fix on top.

**What #48 does:** topics come from user turns and the title, not from tool/system/preview noise. Assistant text can only add context to an existing topic, never create one. User-supported topics rank first in Subjects and Daily logs. Tool-name rows are dropped from work items. This also stops cron prompt text and tool names (`terminal`, `exit code`) from flooding the index, which is the noise #379 describes; #424 fixes that by source.

**Fix on top (e7c2016):** #48 runs the dotted-identifier regex over free user text, so ordinary prose became subjects: `"Use a cache, e.g. redis, i.e. fast. Fix it.Then…"` produced `e.g`, `i.e` and `it.Then`. Matches now need parts of 2+ characters with no capital after a dot; snake_case always counts. `tools.lookup` and `search_files` are still extracted. The new test fails on #48's head and passes here.

**Verification:** full `memory-wiki/tests` 44 passed (main 26). The cherry-pick onto main had no conflicts.

**Merge order:** this textually conflicts with #250 (Han extraction in the same `extract_subject_candidates` hunks), #262 and #318 (`memory_wiki_core.py`). Land it after those; I'll rebase it.

Supersedes #48.

title: fix(xchat): keep inbound alive inside X's per-endpoint daily budgets (salvage #280 + #227)
body:
## Summary

Inbound X Chat stopped for the rest of the day once the account's conversation-list budget ran out (#228). Two causes:

- The poll loop read `GET /2/chat/conversations` on every cycle. X meters that endpoint against its own **1,000 calls / 24 h** allowance, so at the 10 s default the list budget is gone in under 3 hours.
- A `429` from the list ended the whole cycle, even though the events endpoint (10,000 / 24 h) would still have answered.

This combines the earliest correct fix for each cause, with authorship kept:

- **@salch-cred, from #280** (2918efa): discovery runs at startup, then at most every `max(600 s, 20 poll intervals)`. Between discoveries every known conversation is read directly. That alone cuts list reads from 8,640 a day to ≤ 144.
- **@dacheah, from #227** (7d7612a, ca45e08): conversation ids are persisted to `xchat/conversations.json` and also recovered from cursors. A throttled list degrades to polling the known conversations and retries discovery when the reset is due. The Windows test fix is included. I applied it without the #226 stack underneath; the only conflict was the loop body, and #227's `_charge_calls` hook isn't needed without #226.
- **Follow-up (Teknium)**: once discovery is decoupled, every known conversation costs one events read per cycle. So the cycle now stretches past `XCHAT_POLL_INTERVAL` when those reads would exceed 9,000 a day. One conversation at 10 s is unchanged; ten conversations get ~96 s. Persisted ids also no longer widen an explicitly pinned `XCHAT_CONVERSATION_IDS` set. README "Inbound" now describes the cadence.

No new env vars or config keys.

Supersedes #280 and #227. Not taken: #226 (adaptive pacing with a token bucket). It adds three new non-secret `XCHAT_*` env knobs and still spends one list read per cycle, so it doesn't fix the budget on its own.

Refs #228. The streaming transport proposed there is still a separate change, so the issue stays open for it.

## Tests

`xchat/tests`: **67 passed**, against a main baseline of 60. The 7 new tests fail over main's source. My 2 tests also fail over the cherry-picks alone.

Merged together with #191, #278 and #323: no conflicts, 72 passed.

title: fix(bubblewrap): bind the chat attachment staging dirs read-only so the agent can open what the user attached
body:
Fixes #430 (reported by @albertoprb, whose diagnosis this follows).

**Bug.** A file attached in the TUI, Desktop or web (`file.attach`) is staged at `<profile HERMES_HOME>/attachments/<name>` (`tui_gateway/prompt_attachments.py` `_session_home_dir` / `_stage_session_file_attachment`). Pasted images go to `HERMES_HOME/images` and large Desktop pastes to `HERMES_HOME/composer-pastes`. The prompt names that host path in an `@file:` reference. The bubblewrap sandbox hides `HERMES_HOME` whole and bound back only the scratch dir, the state dir and the profile home. So an attachment too large or binary to inline pointed at a path that did not exist inside the sandbox, for `terminal` and for the file tools alike. An operator `binds` entry cannot work around it, because binds into a Hermes home are refused.

**Fix.** `staged_input_binds` creates each of the three staging dirs if it is missing (core does the same for docker in `get_cache_directory_mounts`) and binds it **read-only** at its own path, among the late mounts next to the scratch dir. The dirs go through the same bind guard as the scratch dir, so a staging dir that is a symlink into the rest of the Hermes home, or into a directory a sandbox can write to, is refused with one warning. Read-only means a command cannot plant a file that a later turn would take for an upload. Everything else under `HERMES_HOME` stays hidden: config, `.env`, sessions, and the document caches from messaging platforms.

**Trade-off to note.** Commit ad47c61 (1.1.0) kept these dirs hidden so that one session's staged files would not show up in another session's sandbox. With this change, every sandbox of a profile can **read** that profile's staged chat input. Other profiles' homes stay hidden. That is the access the docker backend already gives (core mounts the same dirs read-only), and without it attachments do not work at all under bubblewrap. `attachments.storage: workspace` is still available for anyone who wants per-workspace staging.

**Tests** (real bwrap, both HERMES_HOME layouts):
- `test_a_chat_attachment_staged_in_the_hermes_home_is_readable_not_writable`: the file is staged after the sandbox is built. `cat` and `ShellFileOperations.read_file` see it, a write into the dir fails, and `HERMES_HOME/.env` stays hidden. **Fails on main** in both layouts (2 failed).
- `test_a_staging_dir_linked_into_the_rest_of_the_hermes_home_is_not_bound`: `attachments -> HERMES_HOME/sessions` does not expose the transcripts.
- The existing listing, signature and "cached data hidden" tests are updated to the new visible set.

Plugin suite on core v0.23.2: 621 passed, 1 skipped (local real bwrap 0.11.1; base: 617 passed, 1 skipped). Version 1.5.2.

Note: on core `main` (502009cc) the plugin suite already fails 148 tests **before and after** this PR. Core changed `BaseEnvironment._wrap_command(..., cwd_fallback=)` and removed `LocalEnvironment._recover_cwd` (core 8f95f721 / e979ba31), so `BubblewrapEnvironment` breaks on every command there. That needs a separate fix.

title: fix(directsdk): fail closed when Claude Code is missing or logged out (salvage #77)
body:
Salvage of #77 by @enckequity (their commit cherry-picked onto current main, authorship kept; their fork is archived, so the PR branch could not be updated). Supersedes #77.

**What it fixes.** A missing Claude Code (`ClaudeCodeMissing`, 503) or a logged-out one (`ClaudeCodeLoggedOut`, 401) means native can't run where Hermes runs it. Hermes' default verdicts for those statuses walk `fallback_providers`, so a user who picked this provider for their subscription got the turn answered by a paid API, exit 0. `classify_api_error` now returns `auth_permanent` with `retryable=False, should_fallback=False` for both.

**Why now.** #77 was parked on core honouring `should_fallback` in auth failover. That landed in core as 6897399c1b56 ("fix(agent): honor should_fallback=False on auth verdicts", @enckequity) and ships in stable **v0.23.1** (core `agent/turn_recovery.py` gates auth failover on `classified.should_fallback`). On older Hermes the hook is a no-op (still falls back), so `requires_hermes` stays as is.

**Rebase.** Main added `ClaudeUpstreamConfigError` / extra-usage / request-rejected cases at the same spot in `classify_api_error` and tests in `test_directsdk_errors.py`; both sides kept. One CHANGELOG `### Fixed` line added on top (my commit).

**Evidence.** The new test `test_missing_or_logged_out_claude_code_fails_closed_without_fallback` fails on main (1 failed / 25 passed in `test_directsdk_errors.py`) and passes here; full plugin suite 589 passed (py3.14, core 502009c).

Note: skipping a configured fallback chain for these two errors is a product choice (subscription users not silently billed vs. turn keeps answering); this PR takes the subscription side, as #77 proposed.

title: fix(homeassistant): route to the configured home thread and honour send refusals
body:
Follow-up to the adversarial review on `e79b107c`. Fixes only code this PR adds — nothing outside the Home Assistant plugin.

## What changes

1. **Broadcast respects the configured home thread.** `adapter.send` was called without `thread_id`, so a home pinned inside a forum topic received the alert in the root chat. Core injects `send_metadata["thread_id"] = target.thread_id` for exactly this (`gateway/delivery.py:343-344`); we now mirror it, and a caller-supplied `thread_id` still wins.
2. **Session mode derives the topic session.** `thread_id=None` on the home `SessionSource` dropped the thread slot from `build_session_key`, so injection targeted the root chat's conversation while the topic session existed. The thread now comes from the home channel. The participant stays `None` (that reasoning is unchanged and correct).
3. **A refused send degrades to the HA notification.** Adapters report a transport refusal as `SendResult(success=False)` instead of raising, so `return await adapter.send(...)` dropped the event with no fallback and no warning here. Core inspects the result for the same reason (`gateway/kanban_watchers_notifier.py:708-709`, `gateway/run_notifications_restart.py:128`).
4. **`gateway_runner` is read with `getattr`** at the two entry checks — they sat outside the compatibility wrapper, so a core rename raised instead of degrading.
5. **A failed silence-marker import now logs a warning**: it disabled marker stripping on injected payloads for the module's lifetime, silently.

## Verification

- `pytest homeassistant/tests`: **301 passed, 2 skipped** locally (the one unrelated failure is `test_is_connected_requires_non_blank_hass_token`, which reads the real `HASS_TOKEN` from the host config; CI without a token is green — 302/2 expected).
- Mutation check: reverting `adapter.py` makes all 5 behavioural tests fail, so they are not tautological.
- No change to defaults, config keys, env vars or tool schemas; installs that never use `deliver` are untouched (legacy parity probe: 8/8 cases matched).

Targeted at `salvage/199-ha-deliver` so it can ride the same merge if you want it; happy to rebase onto `main` instead if you merge #433 first.

*Prepared with AI assistance (Hermes agent), reviewed by the account owner.*

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: several Claude logins in one profile (one provider per account) + optional limit failover
body:
## Problem

`claude_config_dir` (#34) selects one Claude login per Hermes profile. A user with two Claude
subscriptions cannot use both in the same profile, project or chat. Switching profiles is not a
substitute: memory, skills and sessions are per profile.

The workaround today is copying the plugin under a second id with its own `claude_config_dir`.
It works, but the copy falls behind every catalog update and has to be regenerated by hand or by
a script.

## Proposal

Let the plugin declare accounts; register one provider per account:

```yaml
plugins:
  entries:
    claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental:
      settings:
        accounts:
          main: ~/.claude
          work: ~/.claude-work
```

- Each account appears as its own provider in `/model` and the pickers
  (e.g. "Claude Subscription · main", "Claude Subscription · work"), with its own `/usage`.
- `claude_config_dir` keeps working as the single-account form.
- Optional `strategy` for automatic failover when an account hits a plan limit (429 `rate_limit`):
  `ordered` / `round-robin`, remembering each limit's reset time so a limited account is skipped
  until it resets.

## Prior art

- OpenCode Claude Agent provider: `settings.configDir` accepting a list plus `settings.strategy`
  (anomalyco/opencode#63308, closes anomalyco/opencode#60793).
- opencode-claude-code-plugin: `accounts: [...]` expands into one provider per account.

## Notes

Hermes core `fallback_providers` can already fail over between two provider ids; per-account
providers would make that usable without copying the plugin.

title: fix(bubblewrap): follow core's spawn cwd, cwd marker and secret hand-off
body:
bubblewrap spawns work again against current core `main`: every command failed with `TypeError: BubblewrapEnvironment._wrap_command() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cwd_fallback'`, on `main` too ([run 44478782362](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/actions/runs/44478782362)), so every open PR's `bubblewrap · ubuntu-latest` is red.

## Before
`BubblewrapEnvironment` overrides `LocalEnvironment._run_bash` (core has no argv seam), and core changed four things under it:
* `_recover_cwd` is gone; spawns use `_spawn_cwd()` and only `execute(allow_cwd_fallback=True)` moves the tracked cwd (hermes-agent ab8c56c0, e979ba31). `init_session` failed, so no snapshot was ever built.
* `_wrap_command` takes `cwd_fallback` (0ee90ecc).
* `_extract_cwd_from_output` became `_update_cwd(result, *, move_session)` over `_parse_cwd_marker` (065f5abb). The override that keeps the tracked cwd off `/` and out of the state dir silently stopped running.
* Secret exports leave the on-disk snapshot through pipe fds that `_run_bash` opens and swaps in for tokens in the wrapper (c085276f). The override never swapped them, so every wrapped script would write to `>&<token>`.

## After
* `_run_bash` follows `LocalEnvironment._run_bash`: token swap and `pass_fds` (they cross prlimit and bwrap to the shell), dropped login `PATH` entries re-added, `--chdir` and the Popen cwd from `_spawn_cwd()`, the process group owned by the owner-death supervisor as core does.
* `_wrap_command` passes `cwd_fallback` through; `_update_cwd` replaces the dead override with the same rule.
* Tests follow the new contract: the deleted-cwd cases run as the terminal tool does (`allow_cwd_fallback=True`), the snapshot isolation case exports a plain variable (a secret-named one no longer reaches the file), and a new case pins that a secret export reaches the next command through bwrap and never the snapshot file.

## Verification
| Check | `main` (e726eb7) | this head |
|---|---|---|
| CI `bubblewrap · ubuntu-latest`, core `main` | 40+ failed | (this PR) |
| Full bubblewrap suite, core `main` a8f7439b, Python 3.14, `--privileged` Docker (`python:3.14-slim`, bwrap from Debian) | | 613 passed, 3 failed, 6 skipped |
| `tests/test_bubblewrap_spawn.py` on macOS (mocked spawn) | 3 failed, 4 errors | 8 passed |

title: fix(bubblewrap): work on current core main and on 0.23.2 (1.5.2)
body:
## ELI5

The bubblewrap backend works by taking over a few internal steps of Hermes' local terminal: how a command script gets wrapped, which folder the shell starts in, and how the "where did the command end up" marker is read. Core `main` renamed or reshaped all three. It also added a new step: secret env vars now travel between commands through a pipe instead of a file on disk. The plugin's copy of the spawn step didn't know about that pipe, so on `main` almost every sandboxed command crashed. The plugin now checks what the installed core supports and uses the new way or the old one. No version numbers are compared, so the same plugin works on v0.23.2 and on `main`.

## What changed (feature-detected, no version checks)

| Core change on `main` | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `_wrap_command(..., cwd_fallback=)` (hermes-agent 0ee90ecc, 8f95f721) | `TypeError: _wrap_command() got an unexpected keyword argument 'cwd_fallback'` on every terminal / execute_code call | the override passes `**kwargs` through to core |
| `LocalEnvironment._recover_cwd` removed (e979ba31); `_spawn_cwd()` picks the spawn dir without storing it | `AttributeError: _recover_cwd` | `_host_spawn_cwd()` calls `_spawn_cwd()` when core has it, and `_recover_cwd()` on 0.23.2. `--chdir` and the Popen cwd both use that value |
| `_extract_cwd_from_output` split into `_parse_cwd_marker` + `_update_cwd(move_session=)` (065f5abb) | `AttributeError: 'super' object has no attribute '_extract_cwd_from_output'` | the "never follow `/` or the state dir" guard now overrides `_update_cwd`, which exists on both cores |
| Secret exports go through an fd channel whose tokens `LocalEnvironment._run_bash` swaps for open fds (c085276f, 704705ba, …) | our `_run_bash` replaces core's, so the raw `__HERMES_SRST_…__` tokens reached bash (`ambiguous redirect`), the snapshot bootstrap failed and every later command broke | when core has `_secret_handoff`, the plugin does the same token→fd swap and `pass_fds` them through prlimit + bwrap (inherited fds cross bwrap unchanged), then closes them in the parent |

Tests:
- The dead-cwd tests pass `allow_cwd_fallback=True` when `LocalEnvironment.execute` accepts it. The terminal tool sets that flag itself on `main`; on 0.23.2 the fallback always applies.
- The cross-sandbox state test exports a name that doesn't look like a secret. `main` now keeps `*SECRET*` exports off disk, which is the intended behaviour.
- The test no longer checks the wording of core's own warning.
- New invariant: a secret export reaches the next command, and when core has the channel it is never written to the snapshot file. It goes red with the channel swap disabled (`__HERMES_SRST_…: ambiguous redirect`).
- Version bumped to 1.5.2 (`plugin.yaml`, `pyproject.toml`). This dir has no CHANGELOG.

## Test counts (real bwrap, py3.14, core installed from `git archive`, `env -i` with TMPDIR outside `~/.hermes`)

| core | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `main` (e09c2a5f) | 469 passed, **148 failed**, 1 skipped | **618 passed**, 1 skipped |
| `v0.23.2` | 617 passed, 1 skipped | **618 passed**, 1 skipped (+1 new test) |

`hermes plugins validate bubblewrap` passes on both cores.

## Overlap with #438

#438 (read-only bind of the chat attachment staging dirs) touches `bubblewrap/sandbox.py`, the tests, and the version in `plugin.yaml` / `pyproject.toml`. This PR is built on `origin/main`, not on #438. The code doesn't overlap (#438 adds mounts; this changes `_run_bash` / `_wrap_command` / `_update_cwd`), but the version lines will conflict. Whichever lands second rebases and takes the next patch version. #438's own CI row stays red until this lands.

title: feat(advanced-delegation): opt-in require_profile refuses a task that names no profile
body:
Implements the setting exactly as specified in the issue.

## Change

`delegation.backends.profile_routes.require_profile` (default `false`):

- `true` + no `profile` → `DelegationRouteError("this task needs 'profile' (delegation.backends.profile_routes.require_profile is on): choose one of coder, researcher")`, or `"… the profiles list is empty"` when nothing is configured.
- `true` + a `default` set → one warning via the existing `_warn_once`, `default` ignored.
- `true` + a named `profile` → routes normally.
- `false` / absent → today's behaviour, byte-identical.

`settings`/`default` are read before the `chosen` early-return so the `default`-ignored warning fires even on a task that does name a profile — otherwise the misconfiguration stays invisible on the happy path.

## Verification

**Red before green.** The three strict-mode tests were written first and failed against current main (`3 failed, 3 passed` — `DID NOT RAISE DelegationRouteError`), then passed with the fix (`6 passed`). The three default-off tests passed both ways, pinning backwards compatibility.

title: fix(langfuse): key end-user attribution by profile so senders can't cross profiles
body:
## What

#293 scoped trace state and shutdown to the active profile. The two end-user attribution maps were not included: `_SENDER_BY_TURN` and `_USER_BY_CHILD_SESSION` are still keyed by bare turn and child-session ids. Under a multiplexed gateway, two profiles can reuse those ids. Their senders then cross over:

- **Opted-out profile exports another profile's user.** Profile A (opted in) stashes `user-a` for turn `same-turn`. Profile B has `end_user_attribution` off, but its turn with the same id opens with `userId = user-a`.
- **Two opted-in profiles swap senders.** When both stash a sender for the same turn id before their roots open, A's trace gets B's user.
- **Subagent inheritance leaks the same way.** A child-session id reused in B inherits A's user, and B's `subagent_stop` clears the user that A's child inherited.

The `end_user_attribution` opt-in is per profile, so this is a privacy issue: one profile's end-user id reaches a Langfuse project that never opted in.

## Fix

Both maps are now keyed with the same per-profile namespace that #293 uses for trace state (`_profile_attribution_key` → `profile:<home>:<id>`). The namespace stays in process; nothing new is exported.

## Tests

Added to `test_langfuse_multiprofile_lifecycle.py`, using its existing two-profile fixture:

| Test | On main | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_opted_out_profile_never_exports_another_profiles_sender` | fail (`'user-a' == ''`) | pass |
| `test_same_turn_id_keeps_each_profiles_own_sender` | fail (`'user-b' == 'user-a'`) | pass |
| `test_subagent_user_is_inherited_only_within_its_profile` | fail (`'user-a' == ''`) | pass |
| `test_concurrent_profiles_with_the_same_turn_ids_keep_their_senders` (64 racing iterations) | fail (iteration 0) | pass |

`test_sender_stash_is_bounded` now expects the namespaced keys.

The full langfuse suite passes (182 tests) and `hermes plugins validate` passes. Both were run on Linux with Python 3.14 against current hermes-agent main, using the install steps from this repo's `tests.yml`. I haven't run them on macOS or Windows locally; CI covers those.

title: fix(langfuse): redact a whole list/dict under a secret-named key in sanitized mode
body:
## What

In `sanitized` capture mode (the default), the secret-field mask replaces only scalar values. A list or dict under a secret-named key is recursed into instead. Its inner values sit under keys that are not secret-named, so they are exported unredacted:

```json
{"token": ["opaque-token-a", "opaque-token-b"], "credentials": {"user": "svc", "value": "opaque-token-a"}}
```

On main this tool output reaches Langfuse with both token values intact. This closes a remaining gap in the masking work tracked in NousResearch/hermes-agent#67544 (done here in #74).

## Fix

Any non-empty value under a secret field name is now masked, whatever its type. `None`, booleans and `""` still pass through unchanged, as before. `full` mode is unchanged.

## Tests

`TestCaptureModes::test_sanitized_mode_masks_structured_secret_fields` fails on main (the list exports raw) and passes with the fix. It also checks that non-secret keys and `full` mode are untouched.

The full langfuse suite passes (179 tests) and `hermes plugins validate` passes. Both were run on Linux with Python 3.14 against current hermes-agent main, using the install steps from `tests.yml`. I haven't run them on macOS or Windows locally; CI covers those.

title: fix(langfuse): fall back on an invalid HERMES_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS instead of raising
body:
## What

`_safe_value` parses `HERMES_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS` with a bare `int()` on every call:

| Value | On main |
|---|---|
| `12k`, `abc` | `ValueError` from every capture call |
| `-5` | accepted; a 20,000-char payload comes back 20,022 chars long, labelled "truncated 20005 chars" |

`HERMES_LANGFUSE_MAX_DEPTH` already handles this case in `_resolve_max_depth`.

## Fix

Added `_resolve_max_chars`, which mirrors `_resolve_max_depth`. It is an `lru_cache` keyed on the raw string, so a changed env var is still picked up. An invalid or negative value warns once per distinct value and falls back to the default of 12000.

## Tests

`test_invalid_max_chars_warns_once_and_falls_back_instead_of_raising[abc|-5|12k]` checks that the payload is truncated at 12000 and that exactly one warning is logged. The existing cache-clearing fixture now clears both resolvers.

The full langfuse suite passes (181 tests) and `hermes plugins validate` passes. Both were run on Linux with Python 3.14 against current hermes-agent main. I haven't run them on macOS or Windows locally; CI covers those.

title: Land slate: memory-wiki user topics, bubblewrap attachments, HA deliver + cooldown, /spotify, camofox durable identity
body:
Lands Teknium's approved Part B slate in one branch: the contributors' own commits, cherry-picked in order with authorship kept, plus our resolution and rework commits on top. No merge commits.

**In plain words:** Memory Wiki subjects now come only from what you raised in a chat, not from tool and system noise. The bubblewrap sandbox can open files you attach in chat. Home Assistant can send watched-entity alerts to another platform or into an existing chat's session, and says once at startup if a Hermes update breaks that routing. It also stops spending its cooldown on events that never produce a message, and words unknown/unavailable states honestly. Spotify gets one `/spotify play|pause|skip|np|queue` command that works today in the CLI and every gateway. Camofox can give each cron job a durable browser identity (off by default).

title: [hermes-security] clone.py accepts plain http:// repository URLs (unencrypted source download)
body:
`hermes_security/target/clone.py` accepts plain `http://` repository URLs, so source pulled in for review can be altered by anyone on the network path. The module's own docstring and its rejection message both say https or ssh only, so this looks unintended.

**Where (main, plugin v0.1.5):**
- Line 44: `if parts.scheme not in {'https', 'http', 'ssh'}:`
- Line 46: `if parts.scheme in {'https', 'http'} and (parts.username or parts.password):`

**Impact:** Only explicit `http://` input is affected. `owner/repo` shorthand becomes `https://github.com/...`, and `git@host:path` uses SSH. A repo first cloned over http keeps updating over http, because `clone_or_update` pulls from the stored origin URL. The other hardening (no hooks, submodules, LFS, or file/ext transports) is unaffected.

**Suggested fix:**
- Line 44: allow `{'https', 'ssh'}` only.
- Line 46: check `parts.scheme == 'https'`.
- Add a test that `parse_url('http://github.com/owner/repo')` raises `CloneError`.

Optionally, refuse to update an existing clone whose origin is `http://`.

Found in a code review, not runtime-tested.

title: Docs: socket binds for the compositor and session bus; surface bind refusals at config time
body:
## Summary

Documentation and surfacing requests only, no behaviour change — but the first two hinge on one fact.

The README permits a socket bind ("a service or agent socket you choose to share") and never shows one
working. On Omarchy (Arch + Hyprland) the agent is expected to run `hyprctl` and `omarchy-*`, so I tried the
obvious recipe and hit something worth a maintainer's answer: **binding the session bus works, but
`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` is unset in front of every command** (`HOST_SOCKET_VARS`, in `_wrap_command`), so
the bind silently gains nothing. The compositor socket is fine — `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` is not in that
tuple.

There is also one stale sentence in "Compared with hermes-agent#116579": it says background jobs "are not
refused up front (core has no plugin flag for that yet); they die with their sandbox", and points with "as
described above" at "What it does not isolate", which says the opposite — while 1.5.2's code refuses
(`BACKGROUND_LAUNCH_REFUSAL`). Cheapest possible fix, first.

## 1. The stale background-launch bullet

"What it does not isolate" says: *"The call is refused with an error saying so, instead of reporting a started
job, and the model is told background processes are unavailable on this backend."* The "Compared with" bullet
two sections later contradicts it, and the code agrees with the first. Drop the bullet's last clause.

## 2. Sockets: the compositor works, the bus does not

`/run/user/<uid>` as an empty tmpfs is documented and the agent-socket loss is expected. A single-socket bind
still gets through, verified by hand on raw `bwrap`:

    $ bwrap --dev-bind / / --tmpfs /run/user/$(id -u) \
        --ro-bind /run/user/$(id -u)/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket.sock \
                 /run/user/$(id -u)/hypr/$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE/.socket.sock \
        --setenv HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE "$HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE" \
        --setenv XDG_RUNTIME_DIR /run/user/$(id -u) \
        -- hyprctl monitors

    Monitor eDP-1 (ID 0):
        2880x1920@120.00000 at 0x0

The bus does not survive the same treatment. With `/run/user/<uid>/bus` and `/run/user/<uid>/systemd/private`
bound, `busctl --user list` and `systemctl --user is-system-running` both answer inside raw bwrap — but in the
plugin every command is prefixed with `unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK GPG_AGENT_INFO DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, after the
shell snapshot is built. The socket mounts, the variable is gone, and the client cannot find it.
`env_passthrough` does not help: it applies to the environment and the prefix then unsets the same name.

A working recipe exists per command (`export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u)/bus;
systemctl --user status`), which is what makes this a documentation bug rather than a hole — but it has to be
written down, because a reader following "you can bind a socket" gets a silent no-op.

Two things to document here, then:

- the compositor socket bind, with the escape stated: `hyprctl dispatch exec` and `systemctl --user start` run
  outside the sandbox, and any command that knows the path can use them;
- the bus as it stands — bind plus inline `export`, and that `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` is deliberately unset,
  so putting it in the recipe is the fix rather than a workaround.

## 3. A refused bind surfaces as a wall of failing commands

The refusal itself is right, and the README already specifies it precisely: the backend stops with an error
naming the entry, and a read-only bind must not silently degrade to the writable directory around it.

What is missing is *when* it surfaces. The backend is built lazily, so the error reaches the session as each
command's failure, and the only repair left is an editor outside that session. Validating the entry at
`hermes config set` time — or returning the refused entry in a degraded result, as the README already does for
a missing `bwrap` or a failed probe — makes it repairable in one step.

## 4. The hidden set announces nothing

`.config/gh`, the keyrings and `/run/user` are hidden by design and correctly documented — in a README read
once, weeks before the `gh auth status` that returns `command not found: gh` (mise lives under the hidden
`.local/share/mise`).

One line in the backend's start log, or a `hermes doctor` check beside the existing bwrap probe, listing what
is hidden by category — credential stores, agent sockets, `HERMES_HOME` — would turn each of those into a
five-second read. `doctor` is the cheaper home for it if new log noise is unwelcome, and neither should claim
exhaustiveness: the README notes that no list of hidden paths is complete.

## Configuration

    plugins:
      entries:
        bubblewrap:
          settings:
            profile: workspace
            home_allow: [".config/nvim"]
            binds:
              - {src: /srv/scratch, readonly: false}

Hermes 0.23.2, bubblewrap plugin 1.5.2, bwrap 0.13.1, Arch + Hyprland. Related: #212 (open) is the same class
of boundary-versus-real-task, seen from the writable-set side.

title: mcp-serve messages_send fails after outbound sender module relocation
body:
## Summary

`mcp-serve`'s `messages_send` returns:

```json
{"error": "Send message tool not available"}
```

The plugin imports `tools.send_message_tool`, which was moved to `gateway.outbound.send` by https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/156512. The old module path is no longer present in the tested Hermes source.

## Reproduction

1. Run Hermes at core commit `ae2a81ccc0` with the current `mcp-serve` plugin installed.
2. Call the `messages_send` MCP tool with a target and message.
3. The handler returns "Send message tool not available".

Under the same Hermes launcher, importing `tools.send_message_tool` raises `ModuleNotFoundError`, while importing `send_message_tool` from `gateway.outbound.send` succeeds. The current Hermes CLI uses the new path.

## Suggested fix

Update the plugin sender import for the current core layout, with an appropriate compatibility strategy for older Hermes versions. A supported public plugin messaging API would avoid relying on private core paths.

The handler's broad `ImportError` catch also obscures the missing module; more specific diagnostics would make future failures easier to identify.

## Verification

Replacing the import in memory and mocking the new sender made the handler dispatch the expected `action`, `target`, and `message` arguments. This was not a live delivery test.

Environment: Windows 10, Python 3.14.9, Hermes core commit `ae2a81ccc0`; installed plugin bridge blob `43e1e584a9f5a19f550b6e2a3904dee8323a4b1b`.

title: fix(mcp-serve): support relocated outbound sender
body:
## Summary

Fixes https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/issues/454.

Hermes moved its outbound sender from `tools.send_message_tool` to `gateway.outbound.send` in https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/156512. The MCP bridge still imported the old path, causing `messages_send` to return `Send message tool not available` on current Hermes versions.

- Prefer the current sender import, with a fallback to the legacy path when the new module is absent.
- Do not fall back when a dependency *inside* the current sender is missing; include import error details in the response instead.
- Add regression coverage for current and legacy layouts and missing sender dependencies.

Both paths are private core imports; a supported public messaging API would provide a more durable integration when available.

## Verification

- Five standalone checks passed against the checked-out plugin and current Hermes runtime, including simulated legacy and missing-dependency cases.
- Called `messages_send` through the real MCP server API with the sender mocked; verified the response and dispatched arguments. No real message was sent.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- The pytest suite was **not run**: pytest was not installed in the managed Hermes environment. The new pytest regression tests are included but have not yet been executed with pytest.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Prompt cache warming never runs: client has no effective_output_cap
body:
### Plugin

homeassistant

### What happened, and what did you expect?

Hermes v0.23.3 added prompt cache warming (NousResearch/hermes-agent#156455). With this plugin as the main provider, it stops on the first idle check:

```
agent.prompt_cache_lifecycle.warmer: prompt cache warming stopped: the client cannot bound the replay's output cap (refreshes=0, spent=$0.0000)
```

Cause: `replay_cap_honoured()` (`agent/prompt_cache_lifecycle/replay.py`) only warms OpenAI/Anthropic SDK clients, or a client that implements `effective_output_cap(**kwargs)` and returns a cap <= the replay's cap. The directsdk client implements neither, so it is never warmed.

The plugin already seems to pass the cap through: `directsdk.py` copies `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` into the request body and sets `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` for the Claude Code process. Could the client expose `effective_output_cap(**kwargs)` returning the cap it will really send?

Open question I could not verify: does Claude Code honour a cap of 1 when adaptive thinking/effort is on, or does it lift it (like the Gemini native client)? If it lifts it, the method should report the lifted value so Hermes keeps skipping warming instead of paying for full replies.

Expected: idle keep-alive replays work through this provider, so long chats don't re-read the whole history at full price after every pause.

### Versions

```text
Hermes Agent v0.23.3 (upstream caafe538), claude-subscription-directsdk 0.3.5 (plugin.yaml; pyproject.toml says 0.3.4), Linux arm64 Docker.
```

### Logs

```text
2026-11-20 12:23:06,638 INFO agent.prompt_cache_lifecycle.warmer: prompt cache warming stopped: the client cannot bound the replay's output cap (refreshes=0, spent=$0.0000)
```

title: fix(directsdk): a secret source's bootstrap token never reaches Claude Code
body:
## What

`drop_api_credentials` (every inherited-env Claude Code child: turns, `auth status`, the picker handshake) now also drops the bootstrap token of every registered secret source: `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (`secrets.onepassword`) and `BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN` (`secrets.bitwarden`). The names are read from core's registry per call, like core's own scrub; the two built-in names stay listed for a core without the registry.

## Why

With `secrets.onepassword`, Hermes' own process holds `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` (from `.op.env` or the service's `EnvironmentFile`). It is the one token that unlocks every other secret in the vault. Core keeps it out of every child it spawns (`_secret_source_bootstrap_env`, Tier 1 in `tools/environments/local_env_policy.py`: "No spawned child needs it"). This plugin builds its child env from `os.environ` itself and removed only the three Anthropic API credentials, so every `claude -p` turn carried the token in its environment. Claude Code never reads it.

Measured on Linux, Claude Code 2.1.329, hermes-agent `caafe5389ae`: a `Client()` turn with `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=<dummy>` in `os.environ` and a wrapper as `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` that records whether the name is present, then execs the real CLI: present on main, absent on this head.

## Tests

- `tests/test_directsdk_inherited_api_key.py::test_a_secret_source_bootstrap_token_never_reaches_the_child[discovery|turn]`: fails on main (2 failed), passes on head.
- Full suite on head: `HERMES_AGENT_REPO=~/.hermes/hermes-agent python -m pytest -q` → 657 passed.
- `hermes plugins validate ./claude-subscription-directsdk` → Validation passed.

An explicit `Client(env=...)` fixture is unchanged (it never went through `drop_api_credentials`).

title: mcp-serve: add three read-only state tools to --tools-only
body:
## What

`--tools-only` also serves three **read-only state tools** on the same MCP face:

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `hermes_status` | the version, the profile home, the config file's path/size/sha256, and the plugin counts |
| `hermes_config_get` | one non-secret config value by dotted key, from a 7-key allowlist |
| `hermes_plugins_list` | the plugins installed under the profile (name, manifest version, kind, state) |

6 files, +473/−7: new `state_tools.py`; one registration block in `bridge.py` inside the
`tools_only` branch; `README.md`, `plugin.yaml`, and the test surface. Skills are not duplicated —
`skills_list` already serves them.

## Why

A client that gets Hermes' tools over MCP may also need to know which Hermes it is talking to and
what is installed — without a shell and without being handed the profile home. These three tools
make that a small declaration instead of an unbounded config reader.

**Read-only by construction.** No writer, no subprocess, no shell. The status carries the config's
digest, never its contents; `hermes_config_get` answers only `model.default`, `model.provider`,
`model.fallback`, `plugins.enabled`, `plugins.disabled`, `delegation.backend` and
`terminal.backend`; a key that *smells* secret is refused **by name before any lookup**, so the
refusal cannot become an oracle for which secret keys exist; the lists carry names and
descriptions, never a value from a credential block. The config is read through Hermes' own
`load_config()` (deepcopy), so the tool cannot corrupt the process-wide cache.

## Scope

- `--tools` is unchanged: the state tools are registered only in the `tools_only` branch, and a
  test asserts they are absent from the `--tools` surface.
- The tools are added with the public `MCPServer.add_tool`; the SDK derives each input schema from
  the handler signature — no private SDK attribute is written.
- `plugins.enabled` absent is the profile's **default**: every installed plugin is active (minus
  `plugins.disabled`). The counts report that correctly instead of "0 enabled".
- `hermes_plugins_list` reads the profile's on-disk manifests; it does not load plugins.

## Packaging and compatibility

- `plugin.yaml` → `1.1.0` (over the landed `1.0.1`), description extended.
- `requires_hermes` stays `>=0.22.0`: the two core functions this adds — `hermes_cli.config.load_config`
  and `hermes_constants.get_hermes_home` — exist at 0.22.0 (measured back to `v2026.9.14`).
  `hermes_cli.version_info` is newer than 0.23.0 and is optional: the status degrades to `unknown`
  there rather than failing.

## Tests

Local runs on this branch (`HERMES_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS=1`, `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`), not CI:

- `pytest -q` in `mcp-serve/`: **109 passed** on the landed main (`8002533`) — the 98 upstream
  cases plus the 11 state-tool cases.
- The 11: status digest and no secrets leaked; default-profile counting; allowlisted get;
  secret-shaped refusals (3); unlisted key; missing key; plugin states; wire registration (schema
  derived from the signature) and a real `call_tool`; and `--tools` not registering the state tools.
- `hermes plugins validate .` → passed.

## Stacking

Rebased onto the landed `main` (`8002533`, the #446 landing slate; #395 closed as landed
2026-11-19). This PR is the six-file diff against that `main`; #395's seven files are already in
it.

title: fix(hermes-security): refuse plain http repository URLs
body:
`parse_url` allowed `http` even though the module docstring and the rejection text say https or ssh only. A review clone over plain http can be altered on the network path, and `clone_or_update` would keep pulling that stored origin.

## Change

- Allow `https` and `ssh` only.
- Userinfo check is `https` only (http no longer reaches it).
- An existing checkout whose `remote.origin.url` is `http://` is not pulled.

## Verification

Written first against current main: `test_http_url_is_refused` and `test_existing_http_origin_is_not_pulled` failed (`2 failed, 2 passed`). With the fix, `4 passed`. `ruff check` clean. One commit, two files.

Fixes #452

title: fix(mcp-serve): load messages_send from the relocated outbound sender
body:
`messages_send` imported `tools.send_message_tool`. Core moved that function to `gateway.outbound.send` (hermes-agent#156512), so the import raised and the handler returned `Send message tool not available` for every call.

## Change

`_load_send_message_tool()` tries `gateway.outbound.send` first and falls back to `tools.send_message_tool`, so an older Hermes still works. If both are missing, the error names the import failure instead of a bare unavailable string.

## Verification

The three tests failed on current main before the helper existed (`3 failed`), then `3 passed`. `ruff check` clean. One commit, two files. Not a live delivery — the sender is mocked, same as the reporter's in-memory check.

Fixes #454

title: fix(claude-directsdk): report the output cap so prompt-cache warming can run
body:
Hermes v0.23.3 warms a prompt cache only for a client that implements `effective_output_cap` and returns a cap no higher than the replay's. This client did neither, so warming stopped on the first idle check.

## Change

`Client.effective_output_cap` reports the `max_tokens` that `create` copies into the request body and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`:

- `max_tokens` or `max_completion_tokens` as given
- else `extra_body.max_tokens` when that is a positive int
- a missing, non-positive, or conflicting pair (which `create` rejects) reports `2**31`, above any replay cap, so warming is skipped instead of paying for an unbounded reply

No extra headroom is added for adaptive thinking. The method reports the cap the plugin writes. This host has no Claude login, so whether Claude Code itself lifts a 1-token cap under adaptive thinking was not live-checked. If it does, this method should return that lifted value and warming should stay off.

## Verification

Both tests failed on current main (`AttributeError`, `2 failed`) and pass with the method (`2 passed`). `ruff check` clean. One commit, two files.

Fixes #457
