title: fix(langfuse): price a keyed main endpoint with its key
body:
## What
- `_canonical_usage_and_cost()` sends the key from core's aux pricing
  lookup (`_pricing_api_key`) to both pricing calls. Without a key it
  keeps the old keyword-free `get_pricing_entry()` call.
- Pricing now also catches `ConfigBackendUnavailable`, so a down config
  backend no longer stops the export of a generation.

## Why
Against a keyed endpoint (LiteLLM, vLLM with `--api-key`) the keyless
`/models` lookup fails with 401 each time core's cached list is cold.
The endpoint logs a rejected request and the generation gets no cost.

## Safety
The plugin follows core's rules exactly, because it calls core's own
lookup: a key only when `base_url` is the configured `model.base_url`,
no saved key beside a live credential source, no key when config
cannot be read. Tests check that another host never gets the key and
that no saved key goes beside a credential source. The change adds no
hook, tool or dependency.

`_pricing_api_key` is private in core. If you prefer a public helper,
I am happy to change the call.

## Limits
- Only the configured main endpoint gets a key. A keyed fallback
  provider at another URL is still priced without a key.
- The key is the one core selects for `model.base_url`. An explicit
  `--api-key`, or a built-in provider pointed at a proxy, is not
  covered.
- The lookup reads config on each priced call, as core's aux pricing
  does. With a credential pool, loading it can do core's `auth.json`
  housekeeping.

## Tests
`tests/test_langfuse_pricing_key.py`, with a transport-level HTTP mock
and a fresh host per test (core caches the model list per URL):
- a keyed main endpoint is priced with its key (fails on `main`);
- a down config backend still exports usage (fails on `main`);
- another host never gets the key;
- no saved key goes beside a live credential source;
- a core without the lookup prices without a key.

Six mutations each fail a test: the model key for any host, no
credential-source guard, no key in either pricing call, the backend
error not caught, and a fallback that reads the model key itself.
Full plugin suite against hermes-agent v0.23.3: 183 passed, also with
the new tests run twice in one process.

title: feat(camofox): read-only signed-in status for managed profiles
body:
Fixes #399

Adds a read-only per-origin signed-in check for Camofox profiles, so an unattended task can learn whether a site is still signed in before it navigates there and fails mid-run.

## What it adds

- Tool `browser_signed_in_status` (toolset camofox): for an origin (URL or bare host) it reports `signed_in` (true / false / unknown), the cookie NAMES for that origin (never their values), the live-cookie count, and the earliest expiry as ISO-Z with which cookie holds it. Expired cookies never count as signed in.
- CLI `hermes camofox signed-in <origin>` with `--user-id` (check a scheduled agent profile instead of the resolved one) and `--open-session` (load the persisted profile first via an about:blank probe tab when no session is active).
- Identity resolution mirrors `get_session` precedence: external override, durable agent identity, managed persistence, deterministic task-scoped userId. With no durable identity it fails with guidance instead of checking a random throwaway profile.
- With no active Camofox session the answer is `signed_in: null` (`no_active_session`), honest about the cold start: `--open-session` opts into starting the browser to load the persisted profile, inheriting the same cold-start retry.

The check uses the server storage-state route (GET /sessions/<userId>/storage_state), which is gated by `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` like cookie import; the tool is offered only when that key is set. Cookie values are never returned, logged, or shown by the CLI.

## Tests

- New `tests/test_camofox_signed_in.py`: 15 tests covering schema registration, identity precedence (override, agent, profile, task, none), cookie name and expiry reporting, expired-cookie handling, no-active-session behavior with and without `open_session`, and CLI output for yes, no, unknown, and error cases.
- Full camofox suite: 140 passed, 1 skipped (the pre-existing Windows symlink Developer Mode skip).
- Ruff clean on all touched Python files; `plugin.yaml` parses with the new tool in `provides_tools`.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Native child expands @path file mentions in Hermes turns — files enter the context without a tool call
body:
## Summary

The native Claude Code child expands `@path` file mentions inside the conversation text Hermes sends. Any `@/absolute/path` or `@relative/path` token that appears in a user turn, a skill body, recalled memory or a tool result is read from disk and injected into the model context as a synthetic "Called the Read tool" result.

This happens even though Hermes owns tools and the child runs with tools disabled. As a result, a file the agent never chose to read can end up in the upstream request. In our case this was a credentials file that a skill only referenced by path in a `curl -H "@<file>"` example.

## Environment

- claude-subscription-directsdk 0.3.4. Current `main` (`72eb3b8721`) has the same spawn env: `directsdk.py` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` / `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS`, but nothing for file mentions.
- Claude Code 2.1.317, Linux.

## Reproduction

1. `echo SENTINEL_VALUE > /tmp/mention-test.txt`
2. In a Hermes chat on this provider, send a message containing `see @/tmp/mention-test.txt`. The same happens when the token is in a skill or a memory snippet Hermes injects.
3. Capture the upstream request at the relay, or ask the model what it sees. `SENTINEL_VALUE` is present as a Read-tool result the agent never issued.

Observed with a mock upstream (counting requests that contain the sentinel):

| Input | File content sent upstream |
|---|---|
| `@/abs/path` | yes |
| `@relative/path` (relative to the child's cwd) | yes |
| `` `@/abs/path` `` inside backticks | yes |
| `"@/abs/path"` in double quotes | no |
| any of the above with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1` | no |

## Why it matters

- It silently bypasses Hermes' tool and approval layer. No tool call is logged in Hermes, the file just appears in the context.
- Hermes content routinely contains paths after an `@`: curl `-H @file` / `--data @file`, e-mail-like strings, docs. Kanban workers that load a whole skill as their first message trigger it on every run.
- The leak is invisible to the user and to Hermes' own redaction, because the expansion happens inside the child.

## Suggested fix

Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS=1` in the child env, next to the existing
`env.update(CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY='1', CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS='1')`. The rationale is the same as #195: Hermes owns context, so Claude Code should not add content on its own. A regression test could send a turn containing `@<tmpfile>` through the fake CLI / relay and assert the file content never reaches the upstream body.

## Workaround for affected users

`/etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json` with `{"env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FILE_MENTIONS": "1"}}`. Managed settings win over the plugin's `--setting-sources ''` and take effect for the next spawn without a gateway restart. We verified this with the mock upstream: 0 leaks with the setting, 3 of 3 without.

title: fix(claude-directsdk): drop native's conflicting cwd and git lines in place
body:
## What

Native's environment message names its private scratch cwd and says `Is a git repository: false`, while Hermes' runtime section names the real cwd. The model gets two conflicting answers on every turn.

## Fix

`stable_request_context` now drops only those two lines from the first system message, in place:

- block structure unchanged — a list of text blocks stays a list of text blocks
- every `cache_control` marker stays on its original block
- all other environment text (platform, downloaded-file guidance) is untouched

This is the part #317 got wrong: it converted `messages[1]` to a string and dropped the marker on that block. Here the message shape and markers are preserved, so the cache prefix still applies.

## Verification

Three tests written first: two failed on current main and all three pass with the fix. All admission suites together: **243 passed** vs `2 failed, 241 passed` on baseline. Ruff clean. One commit, two files.

title: fix(camofox): decode alternate IP literals before the metadata floor check
body:
## Finding (7-Question Gate)

An in-scope actor who can supply a navigation URL (for example through prompt injection in page/memory content) sends `http://2852039166/latest/meta-data/`. Browsers decode that as `169.254.169.254`; core's `is_always_blocked_url` only checks `ipaddress.ip_address(hostname)`, which rejects the decimal form, so the URL passed the plugin's navigation policy and Camofox would fetch it. Impact: cloud-credential read. Cost: one URL, no account. Reproduced against the real `navigation_policy_error`: `blocked=False, error=None` for decimal, hex, dotted-octal and mixed encodings.

## Fix

Camofox's own navigation policy now decodes alternate IPv4 literals (decimal, `0x` hex, leading-zero octal, and inet_aton 2/3/4-part forms) and checks the result against core's `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_IPS` / `_ALWAYS_BLOCKED_NETWORKS`. Dotted literals still go through core unchanged, and loopback/LAN encodings stay reachable because this plugin is a local browser by design — only the metadata floor is restored.

Core's checker has the same gap, but the account cannot open PRs on hermes-agent, so the plugin-side guard is where this can land.

## Verification

The 4 bypass URLs failed on current main and all 5 tests pass with the fix. Full camofox suite, clean-tree baseline with the identical file list:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| fix reverted | `4 failed, 125 passed, 1 skipped` |
| with fix | `129 passed, 1 skipped` |

`ruff check` clean. One commit, two files. No secrets or live endpoints used.

Refs: local code-review hunt (Claude-BugHunter `bb-methodology` → `triage-validation` → `evidence-hygiene`)

title: 0.3.5 -> 0.4.0 update breaks every gateway-served profile with ClaudeCodeLoggedOut until claude_config_dir is set per profile
body:
## Summary

Updating the plugin from 0.3.5 to 0.4.0 (`hermes plugins update claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`) breaks **every profile served by a multiplexed gateway** that does not already declare a per-profile Claude login: each turn fails with `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` (HTTP 401, non-retryable). The update applies silently — no migration, no warning that the behavior is breaking — leaving profiles unusable until the operator manually sets `claude_config_dir` (or a per-profile `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`) for **each** profile.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.23.3 (+273 ff7c9b2), Linux, multiplexed default-profile gateway
- Plugin v0.4.0 (catalog pin 72eb3b87), claude CLI 2.1.326, Claude subscription login in `~/.claude` (`claude auth status` → loggedIn)
- Profiles: 8 profiles using `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` as model provider; one main `hermes gateway run --profile default` serving all of them

## Repro

1. Have a Hermes install where multiple profiles use `provider: claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` and NO profile has `plugins.entries.claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental.settings.claude_config_dir` set.
2. Run `hermes plugins update claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` (0.3.5 → 0.4.0).
3. Start a session in a non-launch profile (served profile) via the gateway.
4. Every model call fails:

```
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable)
error_type=ClaudeCodeLoggedOut provider=claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental
summary=HTTP 401: This profile has no Claude login of its own, and Claude Code would
otherwise sign in with the login of the profile this Hermes process was started for.
Give it one: set this profile's claude_config_dir plugin setting to a logged-in
Claude config directory, or put CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (from `claude setup-token`)
in this profile's .env.
```

Observed: 36 occurrences in one profile in 3 minutes, 12 in another profile the same day after the same update.

## Expected / ask

- `hermes plugins update` should detect the 0.3.5 → 0.4.0 behavior change (multiplex guard #313) and either warn before applying or auto-apply the migration (e.g. copy the launch profile's login dir into the served profile's `claude_config_dir` setting with a notice).
- At minimum, the post-update check should list every affected profile and the exact `hermes -p <profile> config set ...` command needed, instead of failing turns with a 401.

title: Provider stops being registered after hermes update + gateway restart (Unknown provider claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental) until forced reinstall
body:
## Summary After `hermes update` (v0.23.2 → v0.23.3) and the gateway restart that followed, the model provider `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` stopped being registered **in one specific profile** (installed, enabled, settings correct) and every turn failed in the gateway with `AuthError: Unknown provider 'claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental'`. A forced reinstall of the same catalog pin fixed it: ``` hermes -p plugins install claude-subscription-directsdk --force ``` ## Environment - Hermes Agent v0.23.3+273.gff7c9b2, multiplexed default gateway (PID had to be restarted manually; update follow-up `gateway_restart` did not finish) - Plugin dir present: `profiles/

/plugins/claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental/`, version 0.4.0, catalog sha 72eb3b87 (same pin as other working profiles) - Profile config: `plugins.enabled` contains the plugin; `plugins.entries..settings.claude_config_dir` set to the logged-in dir - Other profiles with identical setup kept working; only this profile reported `Unknown provider` ## Repro / symptom 1. Run `hermes update` (core change), let it restart the gateway. 2. In one profile, send a turn: ``` Warning: Unknown provider 'claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental'. Check 'hermes model' for available providers, or run 'hermes doctor'... ``` Gateway log: ``` gateway.run: Model resolution failed for session agent::...: Unknown provider 'claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental' File .../hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py", line 1347/1378, in resolve_runtime_with_fallback raise primary_exc -> AuthError("Unknown provider ...", code="invalid_provider") ``` 3. Boot log of that profile shows the plugin discovered (64 found/60 enabled) but **no "registered model provider" line for the plugin**, while other plugins register fine. 4. Forced reinstall of the same pinned version restores the provider registration; next smoke call succeeds. ## Expected / ask - Provider registration should be idempotent and survive a core update + gateway restart when the plugin is present, enabled and pinned. - If a provider plugin fails to register after an update, `hermes doctor` and/or the boot log should surface the exact reason instead of a bare `Unknown provider` at turn time. - Investigate the "parked provider" path: profile state seems to have kept the provider parked after the update (commits around parked-provider enable exist), and no command surfaced to un-park it until a forced reinstall.

title: Catalog pins (0.3.5/0.4.0) omit the error_max_turns fix that has been in main since Nov 9 (#164/#221/#326) — catalog users keep hitting it
body:
## Summary

The published catalog pins for `claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental` (0.3.5 = 6313fad5, 0.4.0 = 72eb3b87) do **not** include the `error_max_turns` fix that has been in `main` since Nov 9 ("fix(directsdk): stream tool calls as written; never run or drop a broken one (#164 #221 #326)", commit 495eeb68). Users installing from the catalog still hit `error_max_turns` turns, while the fix only exists on `main` / a side branch.

## Evidence

- `git compare 6313fad5...495eeb68` → `status: diverged`, fix NOT contained in the pin.
- `git compare 7519110 (main merge Nov 15)...495eeb68` → fix **is** contained in main.
- Local impact: profiles running 0.3.5/0.4.0 from the catalog failed turns on Nov 15 with:

```
agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3, not retryable)
error_type=...Native request failed: error_max_turns
```

and the fix only arrived by installing the newer ref manually.

- The CHANGELOG on `main` had not listed the fix at the time of the Nov 13 pin cut.

## Expected / ask

- Re-pin the catalog to a commit that contains #164/#221/#326 so catalog users stop seeing `error_max_turns`.
- Keep CHANGELOG entries in the same commit as the fix so pin cuts don't silently drop bugfixes.

title: max_concurrent=4 cancels legitimate turns in a multiplexed gateway ('Claude request cancelled' from slot wait, indistinguishable from an interrupt)
body:
## Summary

`max_concurrent` (new default 4 in 0.4.0) cancels legitimate turns in a multiplexed gateway when a profile fans out subagents/auxiliary calls: the call waits for a free slot and then dies with a non-descriptive `RuntimeError: Claude request cancelled` (from `concurrency.py acquire`), which Hermes then retries — burning time and producing confusing `error_max_turns`-like failures. In our environment the limit was hit repeatedly while only 4 Claude Code processes were running across the whole gateway (12 profiles, kanban reviewer included).

## Evidence

From logs (Hermes v0.23.3, plugin 0.4.0, multiplexed gateway):

```
_hermes_user_provider_...claude_subscription_directsdk_experimental....concurrency:
Claude Code call waiting 2 s for a free slot: 4 running in this Hermes process, max_concurrent 4.
Raise the plugin setting max_concurrent to run more at once.

concurrency.py, line 100, in acquire
    raise RuntimeError('Claude request cancelled')
... agent.conversation_loop: API call failed (attempt 1/3)
summary=Claude request cancelled   model=claude-mythos-5-2[1m]  thread=bg-review
```

- The name "Claude request cancelled" is indistinguishable from a user interrupt; retry loops then re-enter the same slot wait.
- There is no surfaced hint at turn time that the cause is `max_concurrent` (only a log line), and no TTY picker path to raise it per profile.

## Expected / ask

- Make the queued-slot rejection distinguishable from an interrupt (distinct error class/`error_type`, clear message naming `max_concurrent`).
- Consider defaulting `max_concurrent` higher for multiplexed gateways (several profiles x subagents), or making the wait deadline derive from the remaining request timeout so healthy calls don't get cancelled before they ever start Claude Code.
- Surface a hint in the turn error (not only in a log line) when a call was dropped due to the slot cap.

title: fix(claude-directsdk): name the max_concurrent slot cap instead of an interrupt
body:
## What

`concurrency.acquire` raised `RuntimeError('Claude request cancelled')` both for a real interrupt and for a queued call dropped while waiting on `max_concurrent`. Hermes treats RuntimeError as a generic error, so the turn reported an interrupt, retried into the same full pool, and never named the slot cap — the reporter saw alternating `Claude request cancelled` and `error_max_turns`-like failures.

## Fix

Raise a distinct `SlotCapacityCancelled` from the slot-wait path, carrying the running count and limit:

```
Claude Code call was cancelled while waiting for a free slot (4 running, max_concurrent 4). Raise the plugin setting max_concurrent to run more at once.
```

Core sets `error_type` from the exception class name, so this now surfaces as `SlotCapacityCancelled` instead of `RuntimeError`. Timeout behaviour is unchanged. The actual interrupt paths elsewhere in `directsdk.py` are untouched — only the pool-wait path gets the new class.

## Verification

Two tests written first: both failed on current main (`RuntimeError` instead of the distinct class; and a timed-out waiter yielded a slot). Both pass with the fix. Concurrency suites, clean-tree baseline with the identical file list: `1 failed, 6 passed` both with and without the change — the one failure is pre-existing. Ruff clean. One commit, two files.

Fixes #475

title: [xchat] a post shared into the chat arrives as bare text
body:
The issue form's plugin dropdown offers only homeassistant and spotify, so it cannot be submitted for xchat. The headings below follow the form. Filed by CLI; the bug label is not applied, because an outside account cannot set labels.

## Plugin

xchat

## What happened, and what did you expect?

Sharing an X post into an X Chat DM — the native share action, not a pasted URL — delivers the typed comment and silently discards the post. The recipient sees "thoughts?" or "install this plugin" with no referent, and either asks for the link or answers against whatever the previous turn was about.

Pasting the same URL as plain text works, which is how the gap was isolated.

Expected: a shared post should reach the agent the same way a pasted link does, so the existing post-reading path can fetch it. No new API call, and no quota cost.

A shared post is a card, not media. After decrypt, `content` looks like this (keys only):

```
content_type: Text
sent_from: SHARE_SHEET
text: <the typed comment, or empty>
attachments: [{ post: { attachment_id, post_url, rest_id } }]
```

`post_url` is the canonical `https://x.com/<user>/status/<id>`.

`xchat/crypto.py` `message_text` (line 335) returns only `content["text"]` (line 346). `message_attachments` (line 350) keeps only entries carrying `media_hash_key` (line 366), so it covers photos, voice notes and video and nothing else. The poll intake in `xchat/adapter.py` builds the dispatched message from those two functions alone (the `message_text` read is at line 857 on current main). The event is decrypted successfully and the card is then thrown away, so the loss is invisible: no warning, no cursor stall, nothing in the log.

Upstream main is unchanged on both functions as of 269ddcb. No open issue or pull request covers cards, quotes or shared posts. Issue #228 is a different defect: polling stops when the daily budget empties. It does not cover a shared post.

## Versions

```
Hermes Agent v0.23.3 (2026.9.24)
xchat  0.1.0  enabled  catalog
```

The defect is in the plugin source on main, not in a particular Hermes release. `message_text` and `message_attachments` on main match the copy that dropped the card.

## Logs

None. The drop does not log. The stored inbound text was the typed sentence and nothing else; the same status URL pasted as text arrived intact.

## Workaround

Paste the post URL as plain text in the same message.

title: fix(xchat): keep a shared post's URL on the inbound message
body:
## Summary

A post shared into an X Chat DM arrives as an attachment whose only key is `post` (`post_url`, `rest_id`, `attachment_id`), sent from the share sheet. `message_text` returns `content["text"]` and `message_attachments` keeps only entries with `media_hash_key`, so the card is decrypted and then discarded. The agent sees the typed comment with no referent.

Append each `post_url` that starts with `https://` to the inbound text before dispatch, skipping duplicates and anything already in the text. A shared post then behaves like a pasted link. No new API call.

The helper is `_shared_post_urls` in `adapter.py`. The only intake on main is the poll path (`adapter.py` lines 857–860). `message_text` is left as a pure text extractor; the decision sits at the call site.

Fixes #477

## Test plan

- [x] On unpatched main, `test_shared_post_url_appended_to_text` fails (text is `thoughts?` with no URL) and `test_shared_post_without_comment_still_dispatches` fails (nothing dispatched). `test_shared_post_already_in_text_not_duplicated` already passes, because the URL was typed.
- [x] With the fix, `pytest -q` in `xchat/` — 75 passed, 0.39s. The three new cases cover a comment plus a URL, an empty comment with a non-URL and a duplicate dropped, and a URL already in the text not repeated.
- [ ] CI has not run. A first contribution's workflow runs sit at `action_required` until a maintainer approves them.

## Related

No open pull request covers shared posts, cards or `post_url`. Issue #228 is a different defect (polling stops when the daily budget empties) and is not closed by this change.

title: fix(camofox): decode empty template substitutions in the eval denylist
body:
## Finding

`browser.restrict_evaluate` blocks expressions naming sensitive primitives. `_risky_eval_reason` decodes JS string literals to catch concatenation (`document["coo" + "kie"]`), but a template literal with an empty substitution — ``document[`coo${""}kie`]`` — reached the browser while the equivalent plain-string form was blocked. Reproduced against `_risky_eval_reason`: `None` for the template form, `document.cookie` for the concatenated form.

## Fix

Strip `${...}` substitutions from decoded string literals before token matching, so an empty substitution joins the surrounding fragments. Non-empty substitutions are left untouched — evaluating arbitrary JS is outside a static denylist's job, and the README describes this as refusing expressions that *name* the primitive.

## Verification

Three tests written first: the template case failed on current main, all three pass with the fix. Camofox suites, clean-tree baseline with the identical file list: `1 failed, 54 passed, 1 skipped` → `55 passed, 1 skipped`. Ruff clean. One commit, two files.

Local code review under the `hunt-llm-ai` and `triage-validation` skills. No live browser or external target involved.

title: fix(xchat): keep the post URL from a shared X post
body:
## What

Sharing an X post into an X Chat DM delivers only the typed comment. The native share is a card (`attachments: [{post: {post_url, ...}}]`), not a media attachment. `message_attachments` keeps only entries with `media_hash_key`, and `message_text` returned just `content["text"]`, so the card was silently discarded — no warning, no cursor stall.

## Fix

`message_text` now appends each canonical `https://x.com/<user>/status/<id>` from `post` attachments to the message text. An empty comment yields just the URL; a typed comment keeps its text followed by the URL. Media attachments and plain text messages are unaffected, and duplicate URLs in the same message are collapsed. This uses the existing post-reading path — no new API call or quota cost, as the issue asks.

## Verification

Five tests written first: two failed on current main (`'https://x.com/...' in 'thoughts?'` and `'' == 'https://x.com/...'`); all five pass with the fix. Three xchat suites, clean-tree baseline with the identical file list: `2 failed, 17 passed` → `19 passed`. Ruff clean. One commit, two files.

Fixes #477

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Tracking: 0.4.0 refuses multi-profile hosts that shared ~/.claude (ClaudeCodeLoggedOut after auto-update)
body:
Tracking issue for the 0.4.0 multi-profile login regression. Users on a multiplexed gateway (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`) or a multi-profile Desktop host whose profiles all shared the default `~/.claude` login started failing every Claude turn with `ClaudeCodeLoggedOut` ("This profile has no Claude login of its own…") right after plugin auto-update. Their Claude login is fine. A new policy refuses the turn.

## Culprit

- Guard: #357 (alt-glitch, merged 2026-11-15), commits 2d41094def ("a served profile never inherits the launch profile's login") and 907e17ca75 ("a served profile with no login of its own is refused, not run on the launch login"). These close #313: a served profile must not spend the launch profile's allowance.
- Rollout: NousResearch/hermes-agent caafe5389a (Teknium, 2026-11-19), which re-pins the catalog from 0.3.5 (6313fad) to 0.4.0 (72eb3b8). Auto-update pulled it to installs from then on. The update gave no migration step and no notice.

## Defects (separate from the intended #313 policy)

1. **The launch profile is refused on its own login.** `serves_routed_profile()` returns True for every task while multiplexing is active, including the launch profile's own turns. Reported in #409.
   - #420 (open, DIRTY) exempts unstamped scopes. That covers the Desktop/`hermes serve` turns.
   - The messaging gateway binds its own profile's turns stamped (`gateway/run.py` `_profile_runtime_scope`, `stamp_home=True` by default). So #420 does not fix the multiplexed messaging gateway or its own cron jobs unless the user sets the new opt-in `inherit_launch_login: true` (erosika on #420; thebergerking91 on #409).
   - Open question on #420: since the stamp, config home and process home already have to match, should inheriting the login be the default for the launch profile, with the setting as an opt-out?
2. **Served profiles that shared `~/.claude` on purpose broke with no migration or notice.** Reported in #472 (8 profiles, every turn a non-retryable 401). The refusal itself is the intended policy. What's missing is a post-update notice or check that lists the affected profiles and the command to fix each one.
3. **On macOS, the workaround the error suggests does not work for the default login.** `claude_config_dir: ~/.claude` exports `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and Claude Code then looks up a different Keychain item than the default `Claude Code-credentials`. Reproduced here on Claude Code 2.1.322: `claude auth status` gives `loggedIn: true`, while `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=$HOME/.claude claude auth status` gives `loggedIn: false`. On a Mac, the only ways back are `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from `claude setup-token` or turning multiplexing off. Either the hint/README should say this, or `apply_config_dir` should skip the export when the setting resolves to the CLI default.
4. **The error reads like a logout.** It names neither the policy nor `inherit_launch_login`, so users go to the plugin source or re-login for nothing.

## Workarounds today

- Linux: set `claude_config_dir` per profile (or `~/.claude` for the launch profile), or put `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in each profile's `.env`.
- macOS: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` per profile (`claude setup-token`). Alternatively, a `claude_config_dir` logged in with that same `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-hermes claude auth login`).

## Related

#409, #420, #472, #313, #357

title: fix(directsdk): profiles share the subscription login by default; isolation is the owner's switch (#481)
body:
Tracked in #481. Builds on #420 (@100yenadmin), whose three commits stay here with their authorship, and replaces its per-profile `inherit_launch_login` opt-in.

## Why

Plugin 0.4.0 (#357, merged 11/15) refuses every profile a multi-profile host serves when that profile has no Claude login of its own, so it can't spend another person's allowance (#313). The catalog re-pin to 0.4.0 (hermes-agent caafe5389a, 11/19) brought that refusal to everyone. The usual setup is one person, several profiles, one subscription, and there every turn failed with "This profile has no Claude login of its own", including the launch profile's own turns (#409, #472). #420 fixed the Desktop case only. The multiplexing messaging gateway stamps its own profile's turns, so it still needed a per-profile opt-in (erosika on #420).

## Short answer: who has to re-auth?

Nobody, unless the install owner turns on `isolate_profile_logins`.

- **Inherited OAuth (no action):** a profile uses the Claude login Hermes already has, either the normal `~/.claude` login or a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in Hermes' environment. The profiles that broke after the 0.4.0 update work again with no setup.
- **Re-auth (one sign-in per profile):** only with `isolate_profile_logins: true`, and only for profiles other than the one Hermes was started for that have no login of their own. Two ways: `claude setup-token` and put `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in that profile's `.env`, or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-<name> claude auth login` and set that directory as the profile's `claude_config_dir`.

## Every case

A profile's own token or config directory always comes first and is unchanged from 0.4.0. The table covers profiles with neither.

| # | Situation | 0.4.0 (main) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Single-profile install | inherited OAuth | inherited OAuth (unchanged) |
| 2 | Profile Hermes was started for, Desktop / `hermes serve` turn | refused, re-auth needed | inherited OAuth |
| 3 | Profile Hermes was started for, messaging gateway turn or its own cron job | refused, re-auth needed | inherited OAuth |
| 4 | Profile Hermes was started for, isolation on | refused, re-auth needed | inherited OAuth |
| 5 | Another profile, isolation off (default) | refused, re-auth needed | inherited OAuth (never the launch profile's `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`) |
| 6 | Another profile, isolation on | refused, re-auth needed | refused, re-auth needed (new message names the switch and both ways) |
| 7 | Another profile sets the switch in its own config | n/a | ignored: its `true` doesn't isolate, its `false` doesn't lift the owner's `true` |
| 8 | Gateway started for profile X, isolation on in X's config | n/a | X: inherited OAuth; profiles X serves: re-auth needed |
| 9 | Desktop backend started for X runs profile Y's job (Run now) | refused, re-auth needed | Y is another profile: case 5 or 6 |
| 10 | Job in core's restart-safe cron worker process, isolation on | refused, re-auth needed | refused, re-auth needed (its process home can't show whose login it inherited) |
| 11 | Job in core's restart-safe cron worker process, isolation off | refused, re-auth needed | inherited OAuth |
| 12 | Owner's config can't be read | n/a | treated as isolation on (one warning) |
| 13 | Switch is `true` / `"true"` / `"on"` / `"yes"` / `"1"` | n/a | isolation on |
| 14 | Switch is `false` / `"no"` / unset | n/a | isolation off |
| 15 | No secret scope bound under multiplexing | error before Claude Code starts | error before Claude Code starts (unchanged) |
| 16 | Core without the secret-scope API | inherited OAuth | inherited OAuth (unchanged) |
| 17 | `claude_config_dir` (or an inherited `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) names `~/.claude` | exported; reads as logged out on macOS | not exported; inherited OAuth |
| 18 | Profile with its own token or other config directory | its own login | its own login (unchanged) |
| 19 | Explicit `Client(env=...)` | its env | its env (unchanged) |

`isolate_profile_logins` is the install owner's switch. It is read from the install's default profile and the profile Hermes was started for, managed overlay included, and never from a served profile's own config.

## What changes in the code

- `isolate_profile_logins` setting (bool, default off) in `plugin.yaml`, read by `directsdk_setup.isolate_profile_logins()`.
- `apply_profile_credential`: a profile with no login of its own now gets inherited OAuth when it is the profile Hermes was started for (unstamped launch scope from #420, or a scope stamped with the process home, outside core's cron worker process), or when isolation is off (sharing passes the token or config dir only, not the gateway headers). It is refused only when isolation is on.
- `apply_config_dir` and a profile's own `.env` config dir no longer export Claude Code's default `~/.claude`.
- New refusal text: it names `isolate_profile_logins` and the macOS-correct login command.
- Removed: #420's per-profile `inherit_launch_login` and its file-only config reader.

## Verification

- The two touched test files: 75 pass on this head; 37 fail on main's `directsdk_setup.py`.
- Seven one-line mutations each go red: no sharing, exporting the default dir, no stamped launch exemption, unreadable treated as off, reading only the root, sharing the gateway headers, a served profile reading its own switch.
- CI on 373f1a9: 64/64 green. The first Ubuntu attempt failed `test_directsdk_probe_lifecycle.py::...[usage-launcher-exits-first]`, which this PR doesn't touch; it passed on rerun. The same test also fails locally on `origin/main` under Python 3.12 on macOS, which has no `os.waitid`.
- Live on macOS, Claude Code 2.1.322, the real `~/.claude` Keychain login, a served profile under multiplexing, the plugin's real `setup_status` (`claude auth status`, zero inference):

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no settings | refused ("no Claude login of its own") | logged in (inherited OAuth) |
| `claude_config_dir: ~/.claude` | "installed but not logged in" | logged in (inherited OAuth) |
| `isolate_profile_logins: true` on the root | refused | refused, names the switch |

title: fix(directsdk): refuse another vendor's model id before spawning Claude Code
body:
Hi! I've been carrying a version of this in my fork and wanted to offer it here. It covers what happens when another provider's model id (say `gpt-5.1`) ends up routed to this plugin. Below is what I found, plus a small fix. Happy to adjust anything.

## What happens on main

When another vendor's model id reaches this provider (left over after a provider switch, or carried over by a `/model` or fallback mix-up), the transport doesn't look at it. It spawns Claude Code with `--model gpt-5.1`, and Claude Code sends the turn upstream on the subscription login. Anthropic answers `404 not_found_error` with the message `model: gpt-5.1`.

As far as I can tell, that wording matches none of core's model-not-found patterns. The error reaches Hermes as `ClaudeAPIError(404, "Incomplete upstream response (... upstream said: model: gpt-5.1)")`, and `classify_api_error` reads it as `unknown`, retryable, with no fallback. So each retry spawns Claude Code again and sends another request for the same 404.

I reproduced it on main `269ddcb` offline, with a fake Claude Code and a fake Anthropic that returns that 404 (no real login):

```
error: ClaudeAPIError 404 Incomplete upstream response (first upstream attempt: status 404, capture incomplete, native retries denied: 0, upstream said: model: gpt-5.1)
native spawns: ['"gpt-5.1"'] upstream Messages requests: ['/v1/messages']
core verdict (generic): unknown retryable True fallback False compress False
```

## What this PR does

- `model_catalog.names_foreign_model(model)` is a deny rule, not an allow list. An id counts as foreign only when it doesn't contain `claude`, isn't an alias, and either has a listed non-Anthropic vendor prefix (`openai/`, `google/`, `meta-llama/`, ...) or starts with a listed non-Anthropic family word (`gpt`, `chatgpt`, `o<digit>`, `gemini`, `gemma`, `llama`, `mistral`, `deepseek`, `grok`, `qwen`, `kimi`, `glm`, ...). It strips whitespace, ignores case and drops a `[1m]` suffix, and it only reads the id. Native argv is unchanged.
- `Client._create` raises `ClaudeModelNotFound` for such an id. It sits in the same block that already refuses a missing model, so it runs before request files, the relay/admission, the `max_concurrent` slot and the spawn. `ClaudeModelNotFound` subclasses `RequestRejected` and carries `status_code = 404` plus `Model not found ...` text.
- `classify_api_error` matches the class by name, like the other refusals, and returns `model_not_found`, `retryable=False`, `should_fallback=True`. Core's generic path gives the same verdict from the 404 and the text, even without the hook.

I tried to keep within `AGENTS.md`:
- Discovery and the picker are untouched, and unpinned plain ids still go out bare at 200K.
- These all still reach Claude Code:
  - any id containing `claude`;
  - every plugin and Claude Code alias (`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, `default`, `best`, `opusplan`, with or without `[1m]`) and short names (`sonnet-5.5`);
  - vendor-prefixed routes (`anthropic/…`, `openrouter/anthropic/…`, `custom/claude-…`);
  - access-gated ids;
  - ids the rule doesn't recognise (`lyric`, `unqualified-future-model`).

So a new Claude model or CLI alias should keep working the day it ships.

## Verification

- New `tests/test_directsdk_non_claude_model.py`:
  - 19 foreign spellings, streaming and non-streaming, plus the async path: each raises `ClaudeModelNotFound` with zero native spawns and no request left registered.
  - An end-to-end case against a fake Anthropic returning the 404. It checks zero spawns, zero upstream requests, and core's verdict for a 190K-token, 400-message session: `model_not_found`, not retryable, fallback, no compression.
  - Other refusals keep their verdicts: `RequestRejected` stays `format_error`, and a relayed `ClaudeAPIError` 404 stays core's to classify.
  - 22 Claude spellings still spawn with unchanged `native_model` argv.
  - Every profile route, alias, pinned id and access-gated id, in raw, `[1m]`, upper-case and `anthropic/`-prefixed forms, passes the guard.
- On main `269ddcb`: 41 failed, 23 passed (exit 1). The foreign ids spawned native (`DID NOT RAISE`), the end-to-end case reached the fake Anthropic, and `names_foreign_model` didn't exist yet.
- On this branch, the new file plus `test_directsdk_models.py`, `test_vendor_prefixed_route.py`, `test_directsdk_errors.py` and `test_directsdk_discovery.py`: 119 passed.
- Full suite: 719 passed, 9 subtests passed (exit 0), against 655 on main. The difference is the 64 new tests. `git diff --check` is clean.

What I couldn't verify: a live request with a real foreign id. The 404 wording above is what my fixture serves, not a captured live response.

## Open question

A family list needs some upkeep, and a mistyped Claude id (`claude-opsu-5`) would still hit the retry loop. A complementary option would be to map a relayed Anthropic `404 not_found_error` to `model_not_found` in the profile hook, which covers any bad id at the cost of one free 404. I kept this PR to the pre-spawn refusal, but I'm happy to add that or do it separately if you prefer.

title: fix(directsdk): never let core fuzzy-repair a native tool name onto a different offered tool
body:
## What happens on main

While reading how a native `tool_use` name gets back to Hermes, I noticed that a name outside the offered inventory is handed to Hermes as is (#39). Core's turn validation (`agent/turn_tool_validation.py`) then handles an unknown name in this order:

1. If the `tool_call` bridge is offered and the name is a Tool Search-deferred tool, it routes the call through the bridge.
2. Otherwise it calls `repair_tool_call`. That fixes case, separators and `_tool` suffixes, then falls back to a 0.7 `difflib` match, and runs whatever tool comes back with the model's arguments.

The first steps of (2) are harmless: `Probe`, `probe_tool` or `mcp__hermes__Probe` really are `probe`. As far as I can tell, the fuzzy step is not, because it can land on a *different* tool:

- With the fake native in this repo's tests, `mcp__hermes__prob`, `probes` and `mcp__hermes__prove` all run the offered `probe` on main.
- Among core's own tool names, the same step turns `kanban_block` into `kanban_unblock` when only the latter is offered, and `image_generate` into `video_generate` when no bridge is offered.
- `read_terminal` runs `terminal` when no bridge is offered.

There's also a smaller ordering quirk. Suppose both `probe` and `mcp__hermes__probe` are offered. Native's `mcp__hermes__probe` is exactly the name it was given for `probe`, but main reads it as the prefix-dropped form of the other tool and runs `mcp__hermes__probe`.

## What this PR does

`offered_tool_name` now resolves a native name in this order:

1. **The exact advertised name** (`mcp__hermes__<name>`) comes first. It now wins over any slip reading, which fixes the ordering quirk above.
2. **The known slips**, a dropped prefix (#62) or a dropped server segment (#342), are unchanged. The one difference: if two offered tools both claim a name this way (`mcp__probe` with `probe` and `mcp__probe` offered), it now fails closed instead of picking one.
3. **Deferred tools** go to Hermes unchanged, as on main, when the `tool_call` bridge is offered and core's `is_deferrable_tool_name` (after `_canonical_tool_name`) says the name is deferrable.
   - Core's own routing check is "bridge offered and the name is in the session's deferrable scope". The transport can't see the session scope, so it uses the name-level check, which covers everything in that scope.
   - So `read_terminal` next to `terminal` still routes to `read_terminal`.
   - This relies on core routing deferred calls before repairing them, which as far as I can tell landed in 6bbe4a6c78 ("route real-name calls to deferred tools through tool_call", first in v0.23.2). On an older core that this plugin still supports (`requires_hermes >=0.21.4`), the guard passes the deferred name through and core fuzzy-repairs it exactly as on main, so there it's no worse, but not fixed either. If you'd like, I can also check for `turn_tool_validation._route_deferred_call` and skip the pass-through when it's missing.
4. **Case, separator and `_tool` suffix slips** of exactly one offered tool (`Probe`, `PROBE`, `probe_tool`, `mcp__hermes__probe-tool`, `ProbeTool`) are mapped onto that tool, the same way as the #62/#342 slips.
   - They run the same tool as on main.
   - They reach Hermes spelled as offered, so core logs no auto-repair line and native's replayed history carries the advertised name.
5. **Anything else** is checked with core's `repair_tool_call` over the offered names.
   - If that finds nothing, the name goes to Hermes unchanged for its normal recoverable unknown-tool error, as on main (e.g. `mcp__fastmail__draft_email`).
   - If it finds something, that is almost always a fuzzy match onto a different tool. The call then raises `ClaudeToolOutsideInventory` at `content_block_start`, before any tool delta reaches Hermes.
   - Two rare cases fail closed here even though core would have healed them without fuzzy matching: a name with a quoted fragment core trims (`terminal" parameter="command"`), and a case-only slip when two offered tools differ only in case (`PROBE` with `probe` and `Probe` offered). I can mirror the quote trimming if you think it's worth it.
   - The profile classifies that as a non-retryable `format_error` that may fall back. The message and log carry the tool names only, never the arguments.
   - What the user sees, with no fallback configured, is core's non-retryable notice with the plugin's message as its "Provider said:" line: `Claude called 'mcp__hermes__prob', which is not one of the offered tools; Hermes did not run the similarly named 'probe'. Ask again.` Core's generic `format_error` wording before it ("rejected this request as malformed… /new… `hermes doctor`") doesn't really fit this case, but I didn't want to change core copy from a plugin PR.

If any of the core helpers can't be imported (a future rename, say), every unknown name passes through exactly as on main instead of failing. A test pins the import paths, so a rename shows up in CI rather than quietly turning the guard off.

Some limitations I'd rather mention up front:

- **Mixed batches.** One fuzzy-only name in a parallel batch (say `probe` plus `prob`) fails the whole response, so the valid `probe` doesn't run either, and nothing in the batch runs. Core's mixed-batch handling would have run the valid ones and returned an error only for the bad one. I didn't find a clean way to hand core a name it is guaranteed not to repair, so I've documented this rather than fixed it, and there's no dedicated test for it yet; happy to add one.
- **Text streamed before the refused call.** In streaming mode, that text has already reached Hermes when the refusal arrives. I checked what core does then through `AIAgent.run_conversation` with a stream consumer:
  - It doesn't classify the error for fallback.
  - It keeps the text as a cut-short reply and asks the model to continue, using its "cut off by a network error" nudge, up to 4 times (`turn_truncation.py`).
  - Because the nudge says it was a network error, the model tends to repeat the same call, so the reply can repeat. With the fake native the final reply was `Reading.\nReading.\nReading.\nReading.` after 4 attempts.
  - No tool runs either way, and the new test pins that. The user still sees a truncated turn rather than a fallback.
- **Deferrable but out of scope.** A deferrable name outside the session's scope still passes through, so core can still fuzzy-repair it, as on main. That case seemed narrow enough to leave.

Happy to reshape any of this. For example, I could drop the refusal and keep only the slip mapping and the exact-name ordering, if you'd rather handle the fuzzy part elsewhere (see the open question).

## Verification

All runs are against hermes-agent main `52b5271`. `tests/test_directsdk_tool_repair_guard.py` has 43 tests. The loop tests drive core's production `AIAgent.run_conversation` on this plugin's client against the fake native. Only the tool handlers are stubbed (`model_tools.handle_function_call`, `registry.dispatch` and the inline `read_terminal` executor), so the tests can see which tool actually ran.

- **Red on main (`269ddcb`): exit 1, 24 failed, 19 passed.**
  - Fuzzy-only names run `probe` in the loop (`assert [('probe', {'value': 'x'})] == []`).
  - `read_terminal` without the bridge runs `terminal`.
  - `read_files` after streamed text runs `read_file`.
  - Slips reach Hermes unrepaired (`['Probe'] == ['probe']`).
  - The exact name loses to the slip reading (`['mcp__hermes__probe'] == ['probe']`).
  - The rest fail because `ClaudeToolOutsideInventory` and `_core_tool_routing` don't exist yet.
  - The 19 that pass on main pin behaviour this PR keeps: the offered name and its slips run `probe` in the loop, deferred names pass through and `read_terminal` dispatches `read_terminal`, and a foreign name reaches the host.
- **Green on head:** 43 passed.
- **Focused** (the new file plus `test_directsdk`, `test_directsdk_tool_names`, `test_directsdk_tool_stream`, `test_directsdk_replay`, `test_directsdk_errors` and `test_admission_tool_streaming`): 105 passed.
- **Full suite:** 698 passed, 9 subtests passed (main: 655 passed; the difference is the 43 new tests).
- `git diff --check` is clean.

## Open question

The fuzzy hazard isn't specific to this plugin. Any provider whose model emits a near-miss name goes through the same 0.7 fallback in core's `repair_tool_call`. It might be better fixed there, for instance by keeping the deterministic case, separator and suffix repairs and turning a fuzzy-only result into the normal recoverable unknown-tool error. That would also keep mixed batches intact.

If that's the direction you prefer, I'm glad to shrink this PR to the slip mapping and the exact-name ordering, or close it in favour of a core change.

title: fix(directsdk): hand core the cache write tiers Claude Code reports
body:
## What I noticed

On this route Claude Code places the prompt-cache markers and picks their tier. Hermes sends none: as far as I can tell, core's `anthropic_prompt_cache_policy` returns `(False, False)` for the `process://` URL (I checked `opus`, `sonnet`, `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`). So the prompt-cache clock's `classify_route` files every response from this provider as `openai_spec`.

The API still reports the tier each write was actually granted, in `usage.cache_creation` (`ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` / `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`). Anthropic documents this as the way to confirm which TTL a turn's cache writes used ([prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)). Core already reads that split from a response's top-level `usage.cache_creation` (`agent.usage_pricing.cache_write_tiers` → `CanonicalUsage.cache_write_by_ttl`). This plugin only kept it inside `native_usage`, so core never saw it.

So on main, every write on this route lands in the clock as `('openai_spec', requested_ttl=None, tier='30m', confidence='declared')`. That is a 30-minute assumption, whatever Claude Code was actually granted:

- A main turn on a subscription within plan usage writes at 1h. `/context` shows it warm for 30 minutes, then "unknown".
- A session on usage credits, or a delegated child (`CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m`, from #416), writes at 5m. `/context` keeps showing it warm for 25 minutes after it has expired.

### What this changes, and what it doesn't

This is an observability fix: `/context`'s prompt-cache line and the TUI's `prompt_cache` session payload report the granted tier and the correct guaranteed-warm end.

As far as I can tell, cold-cache pruning and keep-alive don't act on this route today, on main or with this change:

- **Pruning / edge offload:** the route's base URL is `process://claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental`. Its host has no dot, so `is_local_endpoint` treats it as local (`agent/model_metadata.py:698`), and `_estimated_end` goes to `_managed_unload_end` (`agent/prompt_cache_clock.py:275-276`), which returns `None` for anything that isn't Hermes' own llama-server. With no estimated end, `cache_certainly_cold` is never true (`prompt_cache_clock.py:739-746`), so `prompt_cache_is_cold` stays `False` and the prune (`turn_proactive_prune.py:43,96`) and edge offload (`prompt_cache_lifecycle/edge.py:174`) never run here.
- **Keep-alive:** `PromptCacheWarmer` stops at `replay_cap_honoured` (`prompt_cache_lifecycle/warmer.py:280`, `replay.py:102-114`): the plugin's `directsdk.Client` has no `effective_output_cap` and isn't an SDK client, so it is never warmed.

If core later gives this route an estimated end, the proven tier would already be there for those to use, but I'm not claiming that as a benefit of this PR.

## Change

`directsdk.py` now copies the two counters from native's `usage.cache_creation` into the normalized response usage as `cache_creation`, exactly as reported. Streaming and non-streaming responses share this path, so both are covered.

- If native doesn't report the split, `cache_creation` stays absent and core keeps its current 30m assumption. The plugin never invents a zero.
- A counter that isn't a non-negative `int` (a bool, a negative number, a float, a string or `None`) is dropped. A `cache_creation` that isn't a dict is ignored.
- Only those two counts are copied. Nothing else from native's usage is copied, and nothing is logged.
- The requested-TTL policy from #416 is untouched. This change only reports what the API granted.
- Pricing should be unchanged. This provider prices from Claude Code's own cost report (`get_usage_cost`), which always returns a result, so core's tier-based pricing doesn't run here.

With the split passed through, the clock records a write on this route as `('5m', 'proven')` (300 s) or `('1h', 'proven')` (3600 s).

## A limitation I'd like your input on

This only fixes the window right after a write. The route is still classified `openai_spec`, so a later cache read renews the window with core's OpenAI rule, `max(deadline, read + 30m)`, instead of restarting the tier.

For example, take a 5m write followed by a read 60 s later:

- This branch: tier `5m`, confidence `proven`, deadline 30 minutes after the read.
- Main: tier `30m`, confidence `declared`, the same deadline.

So the deadline doesn't regress, but it is now labelled "proven" while still being too long. A 1h write followed by an early read keeps its write + 1h deadline: the `max()` keeps it, but the read doesn't restart it.

A real 1h turn usually reads and writes, and then the window can come out too short. For example, a 1h write at t0 followed by a read+write turn at t0+50m gives a guaranteed end of t0+80m (read + 30m), while the cache was actually renewed to t0+110m. Main gives the same t0+80m, so this isn't a regression either.

I didn't want to touch core in a plugin PR, so I'm leaving this as an open question. As a core follow-up, would it make sense for `classify_route` (or the fold) to treat a response that reports an Anthropic `ephemeral_5m/1h` split as `anthropic_spec`, so that a read restarts the tier? That would fix both the 5m and the 1h case above. If you'd rather this PR waited for that, or didn't mark these writes as proven until then, I'm happy to adjust.

## Tests

New file `tests/test_directsdk_cache_tiers.py` (26 cases). Each test drives the fake CLI and reads the usage through core's own `normalize_usage`.

- **Tier reaches core:** the granted tier arrives, streaming and non-streaming.
- **Counts:** each reported tier reaches core as counted: 5m only, 1h only, and a write split across both.
- **The clock, on the route as it really runs.** The test uses the plugin's `profile` fixture: a temporary `HERMES_HOME`, with the real route-ceiling lookup and route store, nothing stubbed. It asserts that core adds no marker (`anthropic_prompt_cache_policy == (False, False)`), sends an unmarked attempt, and folds the response with `record_cache_response`.
  - 5m write: `('openai_spec', None, '5m', 'proven')`, 300 s. On main: `('openai_spec', None, '30m', 'declared')`.
  - 1h write: `('openai_spec', None, '1h', 'proven')`, 3600 s. On main: the same `30m` / `declared`.
  - No split reported (control): `('openai_spec', None, '30m', 'declared')`, 1800 s, the same as main.
- **Controls:**
  - An unreported split stays unknown (`cache_write_by_ttl == ()`).
  - Eight malformed shapes, streaming and non-streaming, stay unknown and never fail the request.
  - Only the two counts are carried.

Results against hermes-agent main:

- The new file on current main: 8 failed, 18 passed. The tier and clock assertions fail as intended, e.g. `assert ('openai_spec', None, '30m', 'declared') == ('openai_spec', None, '5m', 'proven')`. The unknown and malformed controls pass.
- This branch: 26 passed.
- Full suite: 681 passed, versus 655 passed on main. The difference is the 26 new tests.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

**Not live-verified.** I haven't captured a real `claude -p` response from a subscription for this PR; the fake CLI emits the documented `usage.cache_creation` shape. A redacted `usage.cache_creation` from a real run would confirm it, if anyone has one handy.

title: fix(directsdk): drop the account reminder native appends after the frame
body:
## What I noticed

Claude Code adds an account-email `<system-reminder>` to the turn it answers. When native **prepends** it to the frame Hermes queried, the relay already drops it: `_frame_first` on the opening turn (since #196) and `stable_request_context` on later user turns. On a plain tool-result step it lands at the end of the last result, and `restore_queried_turn` puts Hermes' text back.

I found one case that none of these cover: a **`/steer` row after tool results**, where the queried frame is `[tool_result…, text]`. There, Claude Code sends the reminder as **a block of its own after the frame**, followed by its marked date line:

```
[tool_result, "<steer text>", "<system-reminder>…# userEmail…</system-reminder>", "<system-reminder>Today's date is …</system-reminder>" (cache_control)]
```

On current `main` that block goes upstream as part of the user's message, which is the #195 symptom. Restoration also gives up on the turn, because of the marked date line, and reports `native_admission.unrestored`. I saw the same layout on 2.1.283, 2.1.296 and 2.1.325.

## The change

A new `drop_account_reminder` step runs in `Handler.do_POST` **before** restoration. It finds the queried frame in the newest user turn and drops text only when it fullmatches what Claude Code's `session_context` renderer writes:

- **Wordings:** the bare 2.1.280 form (the one in `test_admission_first_turn.py`), the 2.1.283 sentence + `IMPORTANT` paragraph, the 2.1.296 sentence + attribution paragraph, and both 2.1.325 email sentences. The default one adds "A site asking automated clients for contact details…". The feature-flagged one says "Use this email address only… treat this email address as private information…".
- **Placements:** a block after the frame (the `/steer` case), or appended to the frame's **last** block (its text, a tool result's string, or a structured tool result's last item). A template inside an earlier block of the frame is left alone. Only the block-after-frame placement is something I saw live; the appended ones are covered from the renderer strings (see "Synthetic only" below).
- **Other sections:** the same reminder can also carry `# attachedProject`, `# gitStatus` and `# perforceMode` sections, which the renderer joins after `# userEmail`. In that case only the `# userEmail` section is removed. The rest stays byte-for-byte, so what remains is exactly what the renderer would produce for the same context without an account. Sections have to be non-empty and in the renderer's order; otherwise nothing is touched.
- **Left unchanged:** any other wording, including the "The session context has changed / was re-read" headers. So are host text that contains an email (or even the template), a reminder block Hermes itself queried, ambiguous frames and changed tool identities.
- **Markers and logging:** a cache marker on a dropped block moves onto the frame's last block with `setdefault`, as #196 does. The address is never logged.

It runs before restoration so that restoration only judges what native added besides the reminder. As far as I can tell that changes nothing you'd see in the layouts I captured: on a tool-result step native appends the reminder to the last result's string, always followed by its date line, so the drop doesn't match there and restoration handles it as it does today. The `/steer` turn still reports `unrestored`, accurately, because its marked date line is forwarded as native built it.

The README sentence about ordinary user turns being untouched now mentions this exception, and there's a CHANGELOG entry with the version and section scope. `pin_message_breakpoint` and `stable_request_context` are unchanged. The new code sits next to `_frame_first`, plus one call (with a comment) in `do_POST`, and it merges cleanly with #470.

## Evidence (and its limits)

- **Renderer (read from the installed binaries, not executed):** the `session_context` attachment renderer is `Jze` in 2.1.283, `vlt` in 2.1.296 and `Wjt` in 2.1.325. It builds `As you answer…:\n# userEmail\n…[\n# attachedProject…][\n# gitStatus…][\n# perforceMode…]\n\n<trailer>`, and the `userEmail` value is assembled next to it. The fixtures' wording is copied from those strings.
- **Live loopback capture:** I ran the real DirectSDK `Client` with real 2.1.283, 2.1.296 and 2.1.325 binaries against a loopback Messages peer. Each run used a throwaway `HOME`/`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` whose config names a fake claude.ai account (`user@example.com`), a dummy OAuth token, and proxies pointed at a dead port, so there was no inference and no real credentials. I tried six scenarios: opening turn, later user turn, multi-block user turn, one tool result, two tool results, and tool result + `/steer`.
  - With the relay transforms off, every request carries the reminder.
  - Through `main`'s relay, five of the six are already clean on all three versions. The `/steer` case forwards the address on 2.1.283, 2.1.296 and 2.1.325.
  - Through this branch, all six are clean on all three versions, and the date line and Hermes' frame are left as they were.
- **Synthetic only:** I couldn't produce these live, so their tests are built from the renderer strings.
  - The 2.1.325 private-information sentence is behind a feature flag that didn't turn on in the offline setup.
  - The extra sections never showed up in the plugin's configuration: the CLI added no `gitStatus` or `perforceMode` section to the attachment, even with a git repo as the working directory or `CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE=1`.
  - The reminder appended to the frame's last text block.
  - The reminder alone appended to a tool result's string. Live, native always follows it with its date line in the same string, which this change leaves to restoration.
  - The reminder inside a structured tool result's items.
  - A marked reminder block after a frame made only of tool results.
- **Not captured on 2.1.292,** the version `evals/ci.sh` pins. It sits between 2.1.283 and 2.1.296, whose renderers have the same structure, and the tests cover both of their wordings, so I'd expect the same result, but I haven't run it.
- **Not covered on purpose:** the "context has changed / re-read" headers only appear when an earlier `session_context` attachment is in the CLI's own history. The plugin replays history without native attachments, so I left those forwarded unchanged rather than guess.

## Verification

- `tests/test_admission_account_reminder.py` has 93 cases. On untouched `main` 269ddcb: **33 failed, 60 passed** (exit 1). Every failure is an assertion where the address is still in the forwarded payload, or `unrestored` behaves as described above.
  - The test's `relay()` helper mirrors `do_POST`. `main` has no drop step, so for that run the helper used the identity in its place.
  - The two `Admission` tests use `main`'s real relay.
- With this change: 93 passed.
- `tests/test_admission_*.py` + `tests/test_directsdk_admission.py`: 393 passed.
- Full plugin suite: `main` 655 passed; this branch 748 passed (655 + 93), exit 0.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

I kept this to one logical change in one plugin. If you'd rather I narrow it, I'm happy to adjust. For example, I could drop the multi-section handling and just leave such reminders alone. I can also turn the loopback capture into an `evals/` script like `directsdk_cache_wire.py` if that would help.

title: agent-importers: Claude Code hooks come over on import, with warnings for what behaves differently
body:
People moving from Claude Code to Hermes lose their hooks today: `hermes import-agent` copies memories, permissions, MCP servers and skills, but not the scripts that block dangerous commands or run tests before finishing. Now those hooks come across as Hermes shell hooks, and the import report warns about anything that won't behave the same way.

**Outcome:** `hermes import-agent claude-code` imports settings.json `hooks` into config.yaml `hooks:`, keeping each script's expected event name.

## What changes

Real `hermes import-agent claude-code -y` in a fake home with this plugin installed (core at NousResearch/hermes-agent#158713), source `~/.claude/settings.json` holding a `PreToolUse` gate (`Bash|NotebookEdit`), a `Stop` test hook and a `Notification` hook:

```
✓ Imported:
    hooks  hooks.PreToolUse[Bash|NotebookEdit] $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/gate.sh → config.yaml hooks.pre_tool_call
        ⚠ matcher names NotebookEdit, which Hermes has no tool for; that part never matches
        ⚠ $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is not set by Hermes; read the stdin `cwd` field instead
    hooks  hooks.Stop[*] ~/.claude/hooks/tests.sh → config.yaml hooks.pre_verify
        ⚠ runs only on turns that edited files (Hermes pre_verify)
─ Skipped:
    hooks   Notification has no Hermes hook event
```

```yaml
hooks:
  pre_tool_call:
    - command: $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/gate.sh
      event_name: PreToolUse
      matcher: terminal|NotebookEdit
      timeout: 5
  pre_verify:
    - command: ~/.claude/hooks/tests.sh
      event_name: Stop
```

Before this PR the same run imported no hooks and printed nothing about them. No `shell-hooks-allowlist.json` is written: every imported hook still asks for consent on first use.

- `importer.py`: event map (8 events), matcher tool-name rename (`Bash`→`terminal`, `Edit`→`patch`, …; `mcp__*` passes through), `event_name` set from the Claude event, dedupe on (command, matcher) (the consent key), `prompt` hooks and unmapped events skipped with a reason.
- `cli.py`: the report names each imported hook and prints its warnings, which addresses the second review finding on NousResearch/hermes-agent#132012 (warnings were recorded but never shown).
- `event_name` addresses the first finding (scripts saw Hermes event names). Cores before NousResearch/hermes-agent#158713 ignore the key and send the Hermes name; the hook still loads.
- README row + paragraph; version 1.2.2 → 1.3.0.

## Tests

`tests/test_agent_import.py::test_claude_hooks_become_shell_hooks_that_keep_their_event_name` loads the written config through core's real `agent.shell_hooks._parse_hooks_block`, checks the printed report, and checks that a re-import adds nothing. 63 passed against core main and against #158713.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab36906/IZFMpTmWCnQOuTPzV8i1S_VCocBDov.png)

title: fix(directsdk): reject a non-string image_url through the plugin gate
body:
## What

`content_blocks` sliced `image_url["url"]` before checking its type. A dict, list or int therefore raised a raw `TypeError`/`AttributeError`/`KeyError` out of `Client.create`, bypassing the plugin's `RequestRejected` path and its clean rejection diagnostics.

## Fix

Type-check the value first; a non-string takes the existing "Only base64 data image_url inputs are supported" rejection. Valid `data:` URLs and remote URL hints are unchanged.

## Verification

Four tests: three malformed shapes fail on upstream main with the raw exceptions, all four pass with the fix. Ruff clean.

Local code review under the `triage-validation` and `hunt-exceptional-conditions` skills; no duplicate of the prior directsdk PRs.

title: fix(directsdk): keep extra_body.response_format when response_format=None
body:
## What

`response_format = kwargs.get('response_format', body.pop('response_format', None))` evaluated its default argument eagerly. `body.pop()` always removed `extra_body["response_format"]`; when a caller passed the common SDK default `response_format=None`, `.get()` returned that `None`. The requested json_schema reached neither `output_config.format` nor the model, so Hermes' post-hoc validation rejected unconstrained text.

## Fix

Pop the extra_body value first, then prefer an explicit **non-None** `response_format`. An explicit schema still wins; extra_body only fills the gap.

## Verification

Three tests: the explicit-None case fails on upstream main with a missing `output_config`; all three pass with the fix. Together with the existing structured-output suite: base `1 failed, 9 passed` → `10 passed`. Ruff clean.

title: fix(spotify): keep the empty-204 payload across the 401 retry
body:
## What

`SpotifyClient.request` forwards `method`, `path`, params and body across its forced-refresh 401 retry, but omitted `empty_response`. A 204 arriving after the refresh therefore returned the generic `{"success": True, "empty": True}` instead of the explanatory payload supplied by `get_currently_playing`, `get_playback_state` and `upload_cover`.

## Fix

Forward `empty_response` on the retry. One argument; no change to the first call or to non-empty responses.

## Verification

New test drives 401 → 204 through `get_currently_playing`: fails on upstream main with the generic envelope, passes with the fix. Client suite base `1 failed, 18 passed` → `19 passed`. The four pre-existing ruff findings in `spotify_client.py` are unchanged; the new test file is clean.

title: fix(spotify): shape a malformed redirect port as an auth error
body:
## What

`_validate_redirect_uri` reads `parsed.port`, which raises `ValueError` for a non-numeric or out-of-range port (`http://127.0.0.1:notaport/cb`, `:99999`). That raw exception escaped `hermes spotify login` instead of the plugin's shaped `AuthError(code="spotify_redirect_invalid")`.

## Fix

Read the port once under a `ValueError` guard and treat an invalid port as the documented redirect problem. Valid loopback URIs are unchanged.

## Verification

Two new parametrized cases: both raise `ValueError` on upstream main and `AuthError` with the right code after the fix. Combined with the loopback suite: base `5 failed, 9 passed` → `3 failed, 11 passed` (the remaining three are pre-existing loopback-server failures on this Windows host, identical on both sides). New test file is ruff-clean.

title: fix(memory-wiki): apply cache bounds when a sidecar is loaded
body:
## What

`SessionUnitCache._load()` reads every unit from the sidecar into `_units`/`_sizes`/`_bytes` and never calls `_evict_locked()`. The configured `max_units`/`max_bytes` are enforced only by `store()`. After a restart, a sidecar that outlived a smaller bound stays over budget until the next new session is stored — and indefinitely on a read-only workload.

## Fix

Run the existing eviction at the end of `_load()`. `_drop_locked` already sets `_dirty`, so the trimmed sidecar is rewritten on the next flush.

## Verification

New test writes five units to a sidecar, opens the cache with `max_units=2`, and asserts `units == 2` and `dirty is True`: fails on upstream main (5 units), passes with the fix. Cache suite base `1 failed, 10 passed` → `11 passed`. Test file ruff-clean.

title: feat(directsdk): opt-in WebSearch web_search provider through the Claude subscription (#389)
body:
## What

Opt-in `web_search` through the user's Claude subscription (Shape A of #389, as approved by @teknium1): a separate, isolated `claude -p --tools WebSearch --allowedTools WebSearch --strict-mcp-config` call, registered as a normal Hermes web-search provider. The directsdk main turn and its single-admission relay are not touched.

Closes #389.

## Why another PR

#469 got the shape right, and this PR reuses its flag list (`--setting-sources ''`, `--disable-slash-commands`, `--no-session-persistence`, the empty strict MCP config), the scratch-dir idea and the settings shape. Thank you @salch-cred. While checking it against real behaviour I found three things that I think block it. Nobody could have caught them without a subscription login, so this is not a criticism of the author.

1. **The provider is never registered.** #469 adds `def register(ctx)` to the model provider's `__init__.py`. That plugin is `kind: model-provider`. Current hermes-agent `main` (`6677d97d`) skips that kind in `hermes_cli/plugins_discovery.py` (`gate_manifest`: "Skipping '%s' (model-provider, handled by providers/ discovery)"), and `providers/__init__.py` only `exec_module`s the file. It never calls `register(ctx)`. I loaded #469's tree into an isolated `HERMES_HOME` against current core with `native_web_search: true`: the model provider loaded, the web registry listed `brave-free, ddgs, exa, firecrawl, keenable, openai-native, parallel, perplexity, searxng, tavily, xai`, and `claude web provider present: False`.
2. **Results are one blob.** It returns the whole tool_result text as a single row with `url: ""`. Claude Code's `stream-json` output carries a structured `tool_use_result.results[0].content` list of `{title, url}`, so proper per-result rows are available.
3. **No `--model`, no INFO logging, no live eval.** Without `--model` the call runs on the account's default model instead of haiku.

If @salch-cred prefers to adopt these fixes on #469, I am happy to close this one in favour of it.

## Solution

Hermes has no seam for a model-provider plugin to also register a web provider, and I did not want to patch core. The supported route is a second, tiny `kind: backend` plugin in the same repo: `claude-subscription-directsdk-websearch/`. Hermes loads it through the normal backend path and it calls `ctx.register_web_search_provider(...)`. Its settings live in the model provider's `plugins.entries.claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental.settings`, so users configure one place.

- Provider name `claude-subscription-websearch`, search only. Select it with `web.search_backend`. It is available only while `native_web_search` is true, so it can never become an automatic fallback.
- Rows come from the CLI's structured result: `{title, url, description: "", position}`. WebSearch returns no snippets. If a CLI omits the structured result, the `Links: [...]` JSON line of the tool text is parsed instead. Model-written commentary in the result is dropped, and nothing is ranked, trimmed or rewritten.
- `native_web_search_model` (default `haiku`, validated), `native_web_search_timeout` (default 60 s, 5 to 300).
- INFO log per search: `Claude WebSearch query='...' model=haiku results=N (...s; tool_use X, result Y)`; failures are logged at INFO with the query too.
- Speed: the prompt asks for an immediate WebSearch call with the exact query, and the process group is killed the moment the WebSearch `tool_result` arrives, before Claude's own summary turn. Measured with real calls (haiku, subscription login): the CLI starts and emits `tool_use` after about 1.5 to 2.2 s; the `tool_result` arrives at about 7.8 to 11.6 s; Claude's summary turn then adds about 3.3 to 4.3 s that the provider no longer waits for. The terse prompt made no measurable difference to when `tool_use` appears (1.78 s vs 1.97 s), so it is kept only because it keeps the model from rewording the query.

## Safety

- Off by default, per profile (`native_web_search: false`). Off means not available and no process starts (tested).
- Exactly one native tool; `--strict-mcp-config` with `{"mcpServers":{}}`; no Hermes MCP tools; `--setting-sources ''`; no slash commands; no stored session; its own scratch working directory per call, removed afterwards; never the main turn's directory.
- No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`AUTH_TOKEN` reaches the child (it would bill the API), and an inherited `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or cloud-backend switch refuses the search instead of sending it elsewhere. The profile's own `claude_config_dir` and OAuth token are used as for the model provider.
- Results are untrusted text. A fixture test carries an injected "IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS" string in the tool result and checks it is never returned. Titles and URLs go back as plain fields.
- The settings text and both READMEs say: queries go out through your own Claude subscription and bypass Hermes-side web config and egress settings.
- The child is run in its own process group, killed on timeout and on early stop.

## Backwards compatibility

No behaviour change for anyone who does nothing: the model provider's code is untouched (only `plugin.yaml` settings, README and CHANGELOG), the new plugin is separate and must be installed and enabled, and the setting defaults to false. Core: needs `register_web_search_provider`, present on current main; the manifest says `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.0"`, which I could not bisect to the first release carrying it, so please correct that if it is wrong.

## Config example

```yaml
plugins:
  enabled: [claude-subscription-websearch]
  entries:
    claude-subscription-directsdk-experimental:
      settings:
        native_web_search: true
        native_web_search_model: haiku
        native_web_search_timeout: 60
web:
  search_backend: claude-subscription-websearch
```

## Tests & live eval results

- New suite: 31 passed (Python 3.14, current core `6677d97d`). Covers off-by-default, the argv (one tool, strict empty MCP, haiku), model validation, rows, limit, injection text, no-structured fallback, API-key scrub, gateway refusal, config-dir, error/silent/timeout, early stop before the summary turn, INFO logging, and discovery by core's real plugin loader (registered when enabled, absent otherwise).
- Existing directsdk suite: 654 passed, 1 failed (`test_directsdk_account_usage.py::test_failures_name_the_reason[reply1-...]`), and the identical failure on a clean `origin/main` worktree, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.
- `hermes plugins validate` passes for both plugin directories.
- Live eval `claude-subscription-directsdk/evals/directsdk_websearch_live.py` (real CLI, one haiku search; deliberately not in `evals/ci.sh`): main turn 1 runs the real native executable against a loopback peer that answers with a `web_search` call, with admission `upstream_requests: 1, blocked_requests: 0`. The search is then answered through the subscription, 5 title/url rows in 11.7 s, with the peer still at 1 request, so the search never touches the relay.
