Main turn 2 replays the result, again exactly one upstream request (2 in total for two main turns). The rows are checked to appear in the second request.
- Re-run before opening this PR (query "Debussy Marche ecossaise Earl of Ross"): 5 rows in 10.3 s (`tool_use 2.07, result 10.28`), main turn 1 and main turn 2 each `upstream_requests: 1`, peer total 2.
- End to end through core's own `tools.web_tools.web_search_tool` in an isolated `HERMES_HOME` with `web.search_backend` set: `Web search via claude-subscription-websearch ...`, 4 rows, 7.8 s.

Sample rows: `{"title": "Web Search Provider Plugins", "url": "https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/web-search-provider-plugin", "description": "", "position": 1}`

## Files changed

- `claude-subscription-directsdk-websearch/` (new plugin): `plugin.yaml`, `__init__.py` (`register`), `native_search.py` (provider), `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `conftest.py`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `tests/` (fake CLI fixture, hits fixture, 2 test files).
- `claude-subscription-directsdk/plugin.yaml`: the three `native_web_search*` settings with the egress disclosure.
- `claude-subscription-directsdk/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`: the section and the entry.
- `claude-subscription-directsdk/evals/directsdk_websearch_live.py`: the live eval.

Catalog note: the new plugin needs its own `plugin-catalog/` entry and a top-level README row and 1200x600 card (`assets/`) per CONTRIBUTING; I have not added the card.

title: fix(mcp-serve): clear the wakeup before checking the queue
body:
## What

`EventBridge.wait_for_event` checked `_matching()` and only then called `self._new_event.clear()`. An event enqueued in that window sets the `Event`, which `clear()` immediately erases; the following `wait()` then sleeps until its timeout. With a short `events_wait` timeout the loop exits and returns `None` while the event sits in the queue — a classic check-then-clear lost wakeup.

## Fix

Clear before the queue check. A wakeup after the check still makes `wait()` return immediately, and the next iteration observes the event.

## Verification

Deterministic test: a `threading.Event` subclass whose `clear()` enqueues an event before clearing (models the interleaving exactly). Fails on upstream main (`assert None is not None`), passes with the fix. Test file ruff-clean; the 35 setup errors in `test_bridge.py` are this host's missing `HERMES_AGENT_REPO` checkout and are identical on both sides.

title: fix(model-map): fall back when a named option was removed from config
body:
## What

`task_parameters` advertises the `option` enum from config at session build, while `route_task` re-reads live settings at task time and indexed `options[chosen]` directly ("Core already refused a chosen value outside the enum"). A config edit that removes or renames an option between session build and task dispatch leaves a still-valid enum value with no entry, raising `KeyError` instead of the documented default/parent fallback.

## Fix

If `chosen` is no longer in the live options, warn once and return `{}` (the parent route), mirroring the existing invalid-`default` handling immediately above.

## Verification

New test builds the enum from `fast`+`deep`, removes `deep` from config, and routes a task naming `deep`: fails on upstream main (`KeyError: 'deep'`), returns `{}` with the fix. model_map suite base `1 failed, 45 passed` → `46 passed`. Ruff clean.

title: fix(agent-importers): never delete a skill before its copy succeeds
body:
## What

`import_skills`'s copy callback called `shutil.rmtree(destination)` and then `shutil.copytree(...)` with no staging or rollback. A failed copy (disk full, unreadable source, symlink loop) destroyed the previously imported skill, and `apply()` does not catch the exception, so the whole import aborted with no per-item `error` record — unlike the memory path, which snapshots first and records an error string.

## Fix

Copy into a sibling staging directory, move the old tree aside only after a complete copy, swap staging into place, and restore the previous tree if the swap fails. Return an error string so `apply()` records `status: error` and the run continues.

## Verification

New test imports a skill, adds a local marker, makes `shutil.copytree` raise, and re-imports with `overwrite=True`: on upstream main the marker is destroyed and the run raises `OSError`; with the fix the marker survives and an `error` item is recorded. Suite base `1 failed, 59 passed, 3 skipped` → `60 passed, 3 skipped`. Ruff clean.

title: Create SECURITY.md for security policy
body: Added a security policy outlining supported versions and vulnerability reporting.

title: fix(directsdk): tolerate PID reaping in _wait_gone
body:
## Summary

The `claude-subscription-directsdk · ubuntu-latest` check on PR #478 failed in `Contract::test_fail_closed_and_cancellation` with `psutil.NoSuchProcess` (run `44870661193`, job `136744236485`, PID 3160). `_wait_gone` calls `pid_exists(pid)` and `Process(pid).status()` as two separate operations, so a PID reaped in between raises instead of being treated as gone. macOS and Windows passed for the same plugin on the same commit, and #478 changes only xchat.

Move the liveness check into a small `alive()` predicate that catches `NoSuchProcess`, using the same guard as the existing `_alive` helper in `tests/test_directsdk_probe_lifecycle.py`. `psutil.AccessDenied` still propagates. Two regression tests pin both verdicts: a PID that disappears in the window counts as gone, a live one still counts as alive.

## Verification

- On the unpatched helper, `test_pid_reaped_between_checks_counts_as_gone` fails with `psutil.NoSuchProcess` at the original `tests/test_directsdk.py:73`; the live-process control passes.
- With the fix, locally (Python 3.11.16, psutil 7.2.2): 2 new tests pass, 9 in the touched file pass, full plugin suite reports 657 passed with 9 subtests passed. The earlier CI run collected 655 tests (654 passed, 1 failed); the two new tests account for 657.
- Independent review: PASS, one file changed, +30/-1, tests only. Mutation checks removing the guard and forcing `alive()` to always true or always false each fail a named test. An `any` to `all` mutation survives the suite — a pre-existing gap in multi-PID coverage, not introduced by this change.
- Not run: CI on this head, and Python 3.14.10 as used by CI (local runs used 3.11.16).

## Related

No open PR or issue covers this defect; searched `NoSuchProcess` and `test_fail_closed_and_cancellation`. This does not overlap PR #478 or issue #477.

title: [claude-subscription-directsdk] Opt-in rotation across several Claude logins in one profile when a plan limit is reached
body:
## Request

Opt-in support for **several Claude logins in one profile**, used in order: when the active login reaches its plan limit (session or weekly window), the next request goes to the next login, instead of the request being refused until the reset.

Hermes already does this for other providers through [credential pools](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-pools) (for example several ChatGPT/Codex logins with `fill_first`). For Claude subscriptions, the only pooled route today is the `anthropic` OAuth credential, which the docs describe as requiring extra usage credits, so it draws paid usage rather than the plan allowance.

## Current behaviour (plugin 0.4.0)

- One login per profile: `claude_config_dir` or the profile's `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (#34, #313, #357).
- At a plan limit the request stops with the reset time and does not fall back (`_plan_limit()`, `should_fallback: False`), because the next provider in the chain may be paid API usage. That reason is sound and this request keeps it: no switch to another provider, only to another subscription login the user explicitly listed.
- Switching login today means switching Hermes profile by hand.

## Possible shape

- A per-profile list, for example `claude_config_dirs: [dir1, dir2]`. Empty by default, so nothing changes for existing installs.
- Each entry is a normal, separately logged-in official CLI directory, selected exactly like `claude_config_dir`. The plugin still never reads, copies or refreshes tokens.
- When the active login reports a plan limit, it is cooled until its `resetsAt`, and the next request uses the next login. The current request is not replayed. When every login is limited, the existing refusal stays as it is.
- `extra_usage` (`notify` / `ask` / `stop`) applies per login, as it does today.
- `/usage` shows each login's windows.

## Relation to #214

#214 included rotation between several subscription directories. It was closed because it depended on one external app's inventory format, and the closing comment pointed to `claude_config_dir`. This request is the generic version: a plain list of official CLI directories, with no external app contract.

## Terms question

Anthropic's [Claude Code legal page](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance#acceptable-use) says advertised limits "assume ordinary, individual usage", and the [Usage Policy](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup) forbids bypassing product restrictions. Holding several personal subscriptions is not prohibited as such, but moving on to another login after a limit may be read as a grey area.

If you consider this outside what the official plugin should carry for that reason, a short statement here would also help: it gives users a clear answer instead of third-party switchers.

## Environment

- claude-subscription-directsdk 0.4.0
- Hermes Agent `9d1199d1` (git install)
- Claude Code 2.1.330, Linux

title: fix(homeassistant): report WebSocket connection status to Hermes Desktop
body:
## What users see

Hermes Desktop can show “Restart required” for Home Assistant even after the gateway authenticates the WebSocket and subscribes to events. The gateway logs a successful connection, but the adapter only sets its in-memory running flag. Desktop looks up the platform in the gateway runtime status and has no entry for it.

## Change

Use the core adapter lifecycle helpers to publish successful connection and shutdown. While the listener recovers a dropped WebSocket, publish `retrying` and return to `connected` once the handshake and event subscription succeed. The existing gateway status publisher routes each update to the adapter’s profile. A stop during reconnect prevents the listener from marking itself connected again.

## Verification

- Reproduced the missing initial status against the unmodified adapter. All three new regression tests failed on that revision.
- Ran the Home Assistant plugin suite locally with an isolated Hermes home.
- Validated the plugin manifest with Hermes. No Desktop or core changes are required.

title: fix(camofox): do not cache a missing VNC URL from a health probe
body:
## What

`check_camofox_available()` cached the result of `_vnc_url_from_health()` on every 200 response — including `None`. `get_vnc_url()` treats key presence as authoritative and never probes again, so a Camofox server that answers healthy before VNC is enabled (or restarts with VNC later) is permanently recorded as having no VNC. `browser_navigate` hints and `hermes camofox status` never show the live link.

## Fix

Only write the cache when the health response actually carries a VNC URL. An absent VNC URL means "not yet", not "never".

## Verification

New test: health without `vncPort`, then health with `vncPort=6080`; fails on upstream main (still `None`), passes with the fix (`http://camofox.local:6080`). Client suite base `1 failed, 2 passed` → `3 passed`. Test file ruff-clean.

title: fix(camofox): honour auxiliary.camofox_vision's own settings
body:
## What

`browser_vision` passes the registered `camofox_vision` task to `llm.complete` with explicit `timeout`/`temperature` read only from `auxiliary.vision`. Core resolves `camofox_vision` with `inherit_from: vision`, so a user's `auxiliary.camofox_vision.timeout`/`temperature` block is dead configuration: explicit values win over task config.

## Fix

Read the `camofox_vision` block, merge it over its `inherit_from` parent, then pass the effective values. The legacy `auxiliary.vision`-only configuration still behaves exactly as before.

## Verification

New test sets `vision: {timeout: 45, temperature: 1}` and `camofox_vision: {inherit_from: vision, timeout: 7, temperature: 0.9}`; on upstream main the LLM receives 45.0/1.0, with the fix it receives 7.0/0.9. Ruff clean. The one failure in the combined tools suite is pre-existing on both sides.

title: fix(camofox): apply the credential transport gate to cookie import
body:
## What

`browser_import_cookies` and `check_cookie_import_available` gate only on `CAMOFOX_URL` plus `CAMOFOX_API_KEY`. The other credential-bearing path (`browser_vault`) already refuses credentials on plain HTTP to non-loopback hosts via `secret_transport_ok`. Cookie import sends live session cookies and `Authorization: Bearer …` with no such check, defeating the plugin's transport policy.

## Fix

Call the existing `secret_transport_ok()` in both the check and the import path. HTTPS and loopback HTTP still work; the documented `browser.camofox.allow_insecure_transport: true` opt-in is honoured, as in the vault path.

## Verification

New test with a non-loopback `http://` URL and an API key: on upstream main the check reports available and the POST goes out; with the fix the check is false, the import returns a clear failure, and no request is made. Cookie + vault suites base `1 failed, 23 passed` → `24 passed`. Ruff clean.

title: fix(directsdk): reject boolean extra_usage_reserve_percent
body:
## What

`reserve_percent()` called `float(value)` with no type guard. YAML parses an unquoted `true` as a bool, and `float(True) == 1.0` satisfies `0 < percent <= 100`. A one-character config typo silently turned into a 1% reserve, refusing every request as soon as the plan window reached 1% — with no indication of the wrong setting.

## Fix

Treat booleans as invalid, taking the documented fallback (`100`, no early stop). The numeric-string and numeric paths are unchanged.

## Verification

Extended `test_default_threshold_is_100` with `True` and `False`: fails on upstream main (`1.0 != 100.0`), passes with the fix. Reserve suite base `1 failed, 6 passed` → `7 passed`. Source file is ruff-clean; the test module's two pre-existing lambda-assignment findings are unchanged.

title: fix(directsdk): accept a numeric epoch in resets_at
body:
## What

`observe_usage()` passes each full window's `resets_at` through `_parse()`, which only accepts `datetime` or `str`. Core's sibling parser (`agent/account_usage.py::_parse_dt`) and this module's own `_epoch()` both accept numeric epochs, so a numeric reset was silently dropped: the refusal message omitted the real reset and the cached stop expired after 15 minutes instead of at the plan reset.

## Fix

Route numeric `int`/`float` values through the existing `_epoch()` helper, which already handles seconds and milliseconds. ISO strings and datetimes are unchanged.

## Verification

New test compares ISO, seconds-epoch and milliseconds-epoch forms of the same instant: numeric cases fail on upstream main (`None`), all three pass with the fix. Reserve + epoch suites base `1 failed, 7 passed` → `8 passed`. Ruff clean.

title: fix(spotify): treat cursor 0 in recently_played as present
body:
## What

`_handle_spotify_playback` checked `if after and before:` to reject dual cursors on `recently_played`. An explicit epoch `0` is falsy, so `{after: 0, before: 2}` bypassed the error and both cursors were sent to Spotify, making the request ambiguous. Epoch 0 is a legal cursor value.

## Fix

The check is now `after is not None and before is not None`, so 0 behaves like any other epoch. Truthy cursors and the single-cursor paths are unchanged.

## Verification

New case in `test_recently_played_cursors`: `after=0, before=2` must error — fails on upstream main (no error), passes with the fix. Suite base `1 failed, 24 passed` → `25 passed`. Ruff: 9 pre-existing findings on this module, unchanged by the diff.

title: fix(homeassistant): back off a failing instance-timezone read
body:
## What

`_instance_timezone()` caches a successful `/api/config` for an hour (`_TZ_TTL`) but retried a failed one on every call. The sibling registry cache in the same module already honours a failure TTL (`_REGISTRY_FAILURE_TTL`) so that "a stalled or refusing HA costs one timeout per window, not one per call" — the timezone path had no equivalent.

On an instance where `/api/config` stalls or is refused, every `ha_get_state` paid the full 10 s timeout before returning the same empty fallback.

## Fix

Record `failed_at` on the failure path and return the cached fallback while it is within `_TZ_FAILURE_TTL` (60 s, matching the registry backoff). A success still overwrites the entry immediately, and the per-instance `url` keying is unchanged.

## Verification

New `test_a_failing_config_read_is_not_retried_on_every_call`: two state reads against a failing `/api/config` must hit it once. Fails on upstream main (`2 == 1`), passes with the fix. HA tool suite: base `3 failed, 118 passed` → `2 failed, 119 passed`; the two remaining `TestObjectData` failures are pre-existing and unrelated. Ruff clean.

title: fix(agent-importers): keep an absolute-source backup path shallow
body:
`backup_existing()` computed `Path(*path.parts[1:])`, which drops only the drive anchor, so an absolute source was mirrored in full under `backups/`:

```
backups/Users/<name>/AppData/Local/.../config.yaml
```

Every level of the source tree became a level of the backup path. Real migrations ran past Windows' 260-character limit and `ensure_parent()` raised `WinError 206`, aborting the migration before any file was written.

Back up the last two parts plus a short digest of the full path instead. The tree stays shallow and two same-named files from different directories still get separate destinations.

Test: `agent-importers/tests/test_openclaw_backup_paths.py`

- on `main`: `2 failed, 1 passed`
- with this change: `3 passed`
- full `agent-importers` suite: `3 failed, 137 passed, 5 skipped` (the 3 are pre-existing and unchanged)
- `ruff check` clean

title: weixin: move the Weixin (personal WeChat) platform from hermes-agent core (history kept)
body:
## What this does, in plain words

Weixin (personal WeChat over Tencent's iLink Bot API) leaves Hermes core and becomes the official `weixin` plugin here, imported with its full history (147 commits). The catalog marks it `default: true`, so every Hermes home gets it installed and enabled; it stays idle until someone logs in with `hermes gateway setup` → Weixin.

**Existing Weixin users:** nothing to do. `hermes update` or the next gateway start installs this plugin once. Same platform name `weixin`, same `WEIXIN_*` env vars, same `platforms.weixin` keys, same QR-login files under `weixin/accounts/`.
**New users:** the plugin is already there; the QR login in `hermes gateway setup` works as before.

## Slate (merge order)

1. NousResearch/hermes-agent core removal + migration row: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159644
2. **This PR**: the plugin.
3. NousResearch/hermes-agent data-only catalog entry `plugin-catalog/weixin.yaml` (`hold`, gets re-pinned to this PR's merge sha): https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159643

On a core that still bundles Weixin, `register()` does nothing (same guard as homeassistant/yuanbao), so the plugin is safe to merge before or after the core PR. `plugins validate` passes on main.

## Changes

- **Import (`778c804`):** `git filter-repo` of hermes-agent `plugins/platforms/weixin/` (and its earlier home `gateway/platforms/weixin.py`) plus `tests/gateway/test_weixin*.py` into `weixin/`, merged with `--allow-unrelated-histories`. Authors kept.
- **Packaging (`b1adec5`):**
  - manifest `name: weixin` (core's was `weixin-platform`), version 2.0.0, `homepage`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.22.3"`; `pyproject.toml` with `aiohttp` and `cryptography`.
  - `Platform("weixin")` is resolved at call time in the adapter and the env bridge (`gateway_env.py` builds its `EnvCred` row when the gateway runs it). Core has no `WEIXIN` member once the core PR lands.
  - Core's `platform.weixin.voice_as_attachment` string is carried in `_i18n.py` for all 17 languages core shipped it in.
  - Every send goes through the native standalone sender (`StandaloneSendPolicy(all_sends=True)`), which keeps core's old routing where Weixin went first and no other plugin's import could block it.
  - Send-only homes (`8c4a7e1`): the policy sets `sends_while_disabled`, so a home with `WEIXIN_*` creds and `platforms.weixin.enabled: false` still delivers through `send_message` and cron, as core's outbound special case did. The field is passed only when the running core's `StandaloneSendPolicy` has it (core PR #159644 adds it).
  - Placeholder tokens (`8c4a7e1`): core's startup refusal is kept. An enabled Weixin whose `WEIXIN_TOKEN` is under 4 characters or a placeholder shape is turned off, with core's error text.
  - The QR-login setup wizard uses only the public setup helpers (`hermes_cli.cli_output`, `hermes_cli.setup`, `hermes_cli.gateway_setup_wizard`, `hermes_cli.config`). It no longer goes through the private `hermes_cli.gateway` facade. It reaches `hermes gateway setup` through the generic `PlatformEntry.setup_fn` seam, with no core special case.
  - Tests: `tests/conftest.py` modelled on homeassistant's, plus `test_plugin_packaging.py` (registry entry, env bridge on a core without `Platform.WEIXIN`, yaml disable beats env creds, a fresh home does not enable Weixin, i18n, the setup QR flow writing core's `WEIXIN_*` names, the inert guard).
  - Card `assets/weixin.jpg` (1200x600), README cell, `weixin/README.md`.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Plugin suite against the core PR head (weixin dir and `Platform.WEIXIN` gone) | 73 passed |
| Plugin suite against core main / v0.23.4 (core still bundles it; registry-pinning tests skip) | 67 passed, 6 skipped / 67 passed, 6 skipped |
| `hermes plugins validate weixin` (core PR head and main) | Validation passed |
| `scan_plugin` on core main and v0.23.4 | `safe` on both |

`plugins validate` still warns about six private core imports (`gateway.platform_env.EnvCred`/`strip_slash`, `gateway.platforms.send_targets.*`, `agent.ssl_verify.certifi_bundle_path`, the `plugins.platforms` guard). Core's own bundled adapters use the same seams, and none of them has a published equivalent yet.

### Live probe (real `gateway run --force`, fake HOME, own PIDs; the install is cloned from this branch at `b1adec5`)

| Leg | Result |
|---|---|
| base core + creds | core adapter `Connected … base=http://127.0.0.1:9`, poll refused |
| core PR, first start | plugin installed once from the catalog; the plugin's adapter connects (refused) in the same start |
| second start | no second clone; connects again |
| fresh home, plugin installed by `install_defaults`, no creds | zero weixin warnings |
| multiplex, creds only in `profiles/b` | installed into b only, `✓ weixin connected (profile: b)` |

The full table is in the core PR.

## NOT_COVERED

- Tencent's iLink backend itself: every connect goes to a closed loopback port.

title: feat(wecom): WeCom (Enterprise WeChat) as an official plugin, formerly core
body:
## What this does, in plain words

WeCom (Enterprise WeChat) leaves Hermes core and lands here as the official `wecom` plugin. One plugin registers both WeCom platforms, `wecom` (AI Bot over the WeCom WebSocket) and `wecom_callback` (self-built apps over an HTTP callback), and it is installed by default on every home.

**Existing users:** nothing to do. `hermes update` or the next agent/gateway start sees the home used WeCom and installs this plugin once. Env vars (`WECOM_*`, `WECOM_CALLBACK_*`), `platforms.wecom` / `platforms.wecom_callback` config and `WECOM_HOME_CHANNEL` stay the same. **New users:** the catalog entry is `default: true`, so every home gets it installed and enabled once. With no WeCom credentials it registers both platforms, enables neither and binds no port.

## Changes
- History import: `plugins/platforms/wecom/**`, the older `gateway/platforms/wecom*.py`, and the adapter tests, via `git filter-repo` (commit fc6a4f5 merges it).
- One packaging commit (2a51b65):
  - `plugin.yaml` `name: wecom` (was `wecom-platform`), `homepage`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.23.2"`.
  - `pyproject.toml` lists aiohttp, httpx, defusedxml and cryptography. defusedxml comes from here now: core drops its `wecom` extra.
  - `register.py` with an inert guard (`core_ships_wecom()`), so on a core that still bundles WeCom the plugin registers nothing.
  - `Platform("wecom")` / `Platform("wecom_callback")` are resolved at call time, and imports are package-relative.
  - The env bridge goes through `env_enablement_fn`. Core's `EnvCred` rows needed an enum member at import.
  - New core fields are passed only when the running core has them: `listen_port=("port", 8645)` and `StandaloneSendPolicy(media_via_adapter=True)`.
  - Local `_i18n.py` carries core's 6 `platform.wecom.media.*` strings in all 17 languages.
- Tests: `tests/conftest.py` (homeassistant/yuanbao style) and `test_plugin_packaging.py`. Core's stream-consumer test stays in core.
- Card `assets/wecom.jpg` (1200x600) and a README cell.

## Verification
- Plugin suite against a core tree with `plugins/platforms/wecom` deleted and both enum members removed: **96 passed**. Against release v0.23.4 (still ships WeCom, so the plugin is inert): **93 passed, 3 skipped**.
- `hermes plugins validate wecom/`: OK on both trees. `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin`: **safe** on both.
- Live migration probe (run from the core PR's tree):

| # | Leg | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | base tree, `WECOM_BOT_ID`+`WECOM_SECRET` in `.env` | core adapter created, `Connecting to wecom...`, refused at a closed loopback port (baseline) |
| 2 | head, first start, same creds | `wecom` plugin installed once from the catalog at `2a51b65` + notice; the plugin's adapter connects (refused) in the SAME start |
| 3 | head, second start | no second clone (dir mtime, `installed_at`, config md5 unchanged); adapter connects again |
| 4 | head, fresh home | nothing installed, zero WARNING+ lines matching `wecom`, nothing listening on 8645 |
| 5 | head, creds + `_left_core_installed: [wecom]`, plugin removed | not reinstalled |
| 6 | head, catalog without `wecom` | "cannot find in the plugin catalog yet" |
| 7 | head, callback creds only (`WECOM_CALLBACK_*`, custom port) | installed once with the "WeCom callback" notice; `wecom_callback` binds the configured port (`ss` shows it) |
| 8 | head, multiplex, creds only in `profiles/b/.env` | installed into `profiles/b/plugins/wecom` only; the plugin adapter is created for profile b |
| 9 | `default_plugins.install_defaults(home)` with a fixture catalog marking `wecom` default | fresh home: installed + enabled once, `_default_plugins_installed: [wecom]`; second call no-op; after `hermes plugins remove wecom` not reinstalled; a home the left-core migration already installed into: no second install (one dir, both markers) |

Real `gateway run --force` processes (own PIDs, killed after ~45 s) with a fake `HOME` + `HERMES_HOME` + `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` + `HERMES_GATEWAY_LOCK_DIR`; `WECOM_WEBSOCKET_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:9`. The md5 of the real `~/.hermes/config.yaml` was equal before and after.

## The slate (merge order)
1. Core removal: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159649
2. Plugin: NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-official-plugins/pull/510 (this PR)
3. Catalog entry `plugin-catalog/wecom.yaml` https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159647, `hold` until re-pinned to the merged plugin sha

## NOT_COVERED
- The two new core fields (`listen_port`, `media_via_adapter`) are not in main yet. Until the core PR lands, the plugin drops them and behaves as before: the optional-kwarg filter, covered by a test.
- The probe's callback leg made one real token request to qyapi.weixin.qq.com (invalid corp id). The callback adapter has no URL override.
- The WeCom servers themselves: every bot connect goes to a closed loopback port.

title: feat: google-meet and teams-pipeline (moved out of Hermes core)
body:
Google Meet and the Teams meeting pipeline leave Hermes core and live here as two opt-in official plugins, `google-meet` and `teams-pipeline`. Their history comes with them, and homes that had them enabled get them installed automatically.

Slate (merge order): this PR → catalog PR NousResearch/hermes-agent#159652 → core removal PR NousResearch/hermes-agent#159653.

## What changes
- **Existing user:** nothing to do. A profile whose `plugins.enabled` had `google_meet` / `teams_pipeline` gets the catalog plugin installed and enabled on `hermes update` or the next agent/gateway start. The tool names, `hermes meet`, `hermes teams-pipeline`, `HERMES_MEET_*` / `MSGRAPH_*` env vars, config keys and store files are all unchanged.
- **New user:** `hermes plugins install google-meet` / `hermes plugins install teams-pipeline`.

## Contents
- `git filter-repo` import of `plugins/google_meet`, `plugins/teams_pipeline` and their tests, with history (101 commits), merged with `--allow-unrelated-histories`.
- One packaging commit:
  - manifests renamed to the catalog names (`homepage`, `manifest_version: 2`, `requires_hermes >=0.21.7`), deps in `pyproject.toml` (playwright/websockets pinned exactly as core's removed `google-meet` extra had them; httpx);
  - relative imports, plus test conftests on the langfuse alias pattern;
  - card art and README cells.
- **Inert on cores that still bundle them:** each `register()` returns early when `plugins/<old key>/plugin.yaml` exists under core's `plugins.__path__`, so only one copy registers. Both directions are tested.
- **teams-pipeline binds itself:** core no longer wires it by name. It calls `ctx.register_platform_handler("msgraph_webhook", …)`. The factory runs inside `msgraph_webhook.connect()`, which runs in the owning profile's scope for multiplex secondaries. It reads `load_gateway_config()` there and keeps the runtime on the adapter, so a reconnect reuses it (tested). Teams summary delivery passes its own Graph client factory to core's `TeamsSummaryWriter`.
- **google-meet bot subprocess:** spawned with the plugin dir mounted as a package, because an installed plugin is not importable as `plugins.google_meet`. `hermes meet install` now checks the Python deps (they come with the plugin install) and still installs Chromium and the audio tools.

## Tests / validation
- Run against a core tree with both bundled dirs deleted (the core PR's tree): google-meet **36 passed**, teams-pipeline **40 passed**. `hermes plugins validate` passes for both.
- Expected warnings: private-import notes (`plugins.platforms.teams.summary_writer`, `agent.auxiliary_client`, `hermes_cli.browser_runtime`, …, all carried over from core), and `register_platform_handler` being in-process only.
- `scan_plugin`: **safe** for both on core main and on `v2026.9.24`. Prose that matched `sudo_usage` was reworded; the actual `apt-get` command is unchanged.

## Since opening
- Windows CI: the google-meet conftest ignored every test on win32, so pytest exited 5 ("no tests ran"). It now honours `@pytest.mark.platforms` the way core does, so the suite runs on Windows as it did in core.
- `teams-pipeline` logs `Teams pipeline runtime bound to msgraph webhook ingress` (the line core logged).
- **Fix found by the live multi-profile probe:** Graph credentials (`GraphCredentials.from_env`, the `validate` CLI) were read from `os.environ`; they now go through `agent.secret_scope.get_secret`, so a multiplexed secondary profile uses its own `MSGRAPH_*`. The regression test is red without the fix.
- The live migration probe table is in NousResearch/hermes-agent#159653.

## NOT_COVERED
- No live Meet join or live Graph tenant run.
- The `graph_client_factory` kwarg exists only in core with NousResearch/hermes-agent#159653. Before that lands, enabling Teams Graph delivery from the plugin on an older core raises `TypeError`. The plugin is inert there anyway while core still bundles the pipeline.

title: fix(xchat): retry the sent-id lock instead of writing unlocked
body:
`_remember_sent` shares `sent_message_ids.json` between the gateway and out-of-process senders (cron, `hermes send`) and serializes the read-modify-write with a lock file. When the lock could not be taken it carried on and wrote **unlocked** anyway.

On Windows that branch is not rare. `msvcrt.locking(LK_LOCK)` blocks for about 9 s and then raises `EDEADLK`, so a contended lock looks like a failure rather than a wait. Two writers that both timed out then did an unlocked read-modify-write and one of them lost its id. Measured on this branch: 100 record attempts, **10 lock failures, ids lost**.

A lost id is not cosmetic: the poll loop no longer recognises the message as Hermes' own and answers it, so the self-chat replies to itself.

Retry the lock (`SENT_ID_LOCK_ATTEMPTS = 4`, 50/100/150 ms apart) instead of trading it for an unlocked write, and keep the unlocked write only as a last resort after the retries are exhausted.

Test: `xchat/tests/test_xchat_adapter.py`

- `test_a_lock_timeout_retries_instead_of_writing_unlocked` fails on `main`, passes here
- `test_a_permanently_unavailable_lock_still_records_the_id` pins the last-resort path
- the pre-existing flaky `test_remember_sent_survives_concurrent_writers` now passes: **56 passed**
- `ruff check` clean

title: fix(memory-wiki): enforce the cache bounds when loading the sidecar
body:
`store()` runs every ingested unit through `_evict_locked()`; `_load()` appended them raw and never checked the bounds. A sidecar written by a run with larger bounds — an older default, or a different profile's config — therefore reloaded **unbounded**, so a cache configured narrow still held, and re-serialized on every flush, everything a previous run had written. The count and byte limits only held for units stored in the current process lifetime.

Ingest through the same `_evict_locked()` the store path uses. Eviction is least-recently-active first, so the newest units survive.

Measured on this branch, loading a 20-unit sidecar into a `max_units=5` cache: `{'units': 20, 'bytes': 9150}` — 4× the bound. After the fix the same load settles at the bound and `s-19` survives while `s-0` is dropped.

Test: `memory-wiki/tests/test_memory_wiki_cache.py`

- `test_a_sidecar_written_under_a_bigger_bound_reloads_within_the_current_one` — fails on `main`
- `test_a_sidecar_written_under_a_bigger_byte_bound_reloads_within_the_current_one` — fails on `main` (6560 bytes into a 4096-byte ceiling)

Base: `2 failed, 10 deselected`. With the fix: `12 passed`. `ruff check` clean.

title: claude-subscription-directsdk: Claude Code child inherits Hermes-internal secrets and config-declared key_env values
body:
**What happens**

The DirectSDK provider builds the Claude Code child's environment from `os.environ` minus `API_CREDENTIAL_ENV` (`directsdk.py`, the spawn path around `_with_login_identity(_with_windows_essentials(dict(... os.environ)))`). Hermes loads the launch profile's `.env` into `os.environ`. So any other credential in that file reaches every Claude Code child the plugin starts, on every profile a multiplexed gateway serves. That includes a custom fallback endpoint's `key_env` (for example `fallback_providers: [{provider: custom, base_url: https://api.anthropic.com, key_env: HERMES_CUSTOM_X_API_KEY}]`), `HERMES_CUSTOM_*_API_KEY` and `GATEWAY_RELAY_*` secrets.

Hermes' own spawn paths already strip these names: `tools/environments/local_env_policy.py` (`_is_hermes_internal_secret`, `_home_declared_key_env`, `_ALWAYS_STRIP_KEYS`). The plugin's child skips that policy.

Claude Code runs with `--tools ''`, so a model turn can't read the value today. But the value still sits in a process that doesn't need it, and the plugin's own docs say only the login belongs to the CLI.

**Expected**

Scrub the child environment with the same rules as Hermes subprocesses: Tier-1 always-strip keys, Hermes-internal secret names, and the bound profile's config-declared key_env names. Keep what Claude Code needs (its login, PATH, HOME, proxy and CA settings, and the plugin's own flags).

**Workaround**

Set `CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_COMMAND` to a wrapper that runs `env -u NAME` before it execs the pinned CLI.

Seen on plugin 0.4.0 with Hermes v0.23.3 (caafe538).

title: fix(agent-importers): report a cut-off Grok Bot export as cut off
body:
`parse_export()` narrows the reply to the first `{` .. last `}` before checking whether the reply
was truncated:

```python
if not blocks and "{" in text:
    candidates.append(text[text.index("{"):text.rindex("}") + 1])
```

`str.rindex("}")` raises `ValueError: substring not found` when the closing brace never arrived, so a
cut-off reply never reaches the `ExportFormatError("the export looks cut off ...")` written for it.
`ExportFormatError` subclasses `ValueError`, so the caller cannot distinguish the two by type and
displays the raw `substring not found` instead of the actionable message.

Cut-off replies are routine: a Grok Bot splits a long export across several messages, and the
docstring documents that path.

Fix: require both braces before slicing, so the truncation check below is reachable.

Test: `agent-importers/tests/test_grok_bot_truncated_export.py` (3 tests).

- base: `3 failed` — all at `grok_bot.py:167`, `ValueError: substring not found`
- with fix: `15 passed` (`test_grok_bot_import.py` included)
- `ruff check`: clean

title: feat(hermes-mobile-app-connector): one official plugin for mobile push and device access
body:
## ELI5

The Hermes Agent phone apps used to carry two small server plugins and copy them onto your Hermes install themselves: one sends notifications to your phone, the other lets the agent use your phone's calendar, reminders, health data, contacts, location and alarms. This adds them to the official plugin collection as one plugin, Hermes Mobile, so Hermes installs and updates it like any other official plugin instead of the app doing it. Once the apps are updated, they pair with one request over the connection they already have, with no files uploaded and no restart. On a Hermes with no phone paired, the plugin stays quiet: no warnings, no network calls, and no phone tools offered to the agent.

## Summary

- **One plugin, `hermes-mobile-app-connector` 2.0.0** (label "Hermes Mobile"), replacing the two app-bundled plugins (push notifications and device access). It registers the `push` gateway platform, the notification hooks, the 16 `mobile_*` tools and one dashboard API. The catalog name `hermes-mobile` already belongs to an unrelated community plugin, hence the longer name.
- **Pairing in one call.** `POST /api/plugins/hermes-mobile-app-connector/pair` takes the relay URL and creates or adopts the install key. It stores both in the plugin's own data and returns what the app needs (install key, install id, preview key). Notifications, device wakes and `deliver: push` work right away, with no gateway restart.
- **Official surfaces only.** The plugin's non-test code imports no core name off the published plugin API:
  - session data goes through the published storage interface;
  - cron goes through `cron.plugin_api`;
  - session facts come from `ctx` accessors.

  The poll of the `hermes serve` request registry is deleted; the gateway's `on_session_prompt` hooks cover those prompts.
- **Safe on homes that never pair a phone.** The relay settings are optional, the device tools are offered only once a phone is paired, and hooks a release does not fire are not registered. This PR does not make the plugin a default install.
- Written by Flo (@flrn-st). The first commit imports the two plugins file for file (current tree only), so `git diff a4d5cbd HEAD` shows everything the port changed.

## Pairing

| Call | Does | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /pair` `{"relay_url", "install_key"?}` | Validates the relay URL: https, or http to localhost only. Uses the key already configured, else adopts the one sent, else creates one. Stores the URL and key in `plugin-data/hermes-mobile-push/pairing.json`, mode 0600, written atomically. | `install_key`, `install_id`, `preview_key`, `relay_url`, `source`, `notifications_ready` |
| `GET /pair` | Status only | `paired`, `install_id`, `relay_url`, `source`, `notifications_ready`; never a key |
| `DELETE /pair` | Removes only the stored `pairing.json` | the `GET` shape |

- **No silent key changes.** Values the operator configured always win: environment variables or secrets (`"source": "environment"`), or `platforms.push` in `config.yaml` (`"source": "config"`). The call stores only what the operator did not configure, so with both values configured it writes nothing, and with only the key configured it stores just the relay URL. Sending a key that differs from the one in use returns 409, because other paired phones depend on it.
- **No secrets in errors or status.**
  - A malformed request gets a 400 that names the bad field, never its value.
  - A relay URL with `user:password@` in it is refused.
  - Responses show the relay URL as scheme, host and path only.
- **Same auth, same profiles.** The routes use the dashboard's existing sign-in and the same `profile` parameter as the device routes. With two profiles set up differently, `?profile=` read and wrote the named profile's settings, not those of the profile the dashboard runs under.

**Why no gateway restart or core change is needed.** The plugin reads the effective relay settings at the moment it sends, and core already handles the rest. Each case below was run on hermes-agent main, through core's own plugin-API mount, against a local recording relay:
- **Notifications:** turn hooks read the settings on every call. Right after `POST /pair`, a turn's notification reached the relay and decrypted with the returned preview key.
- **The push platform:** `load_gateway_config()` re-checks plugin platforms on every load. It reported `push` off before pairing, on after, and off again after `DELETE /pair`.
- **`deliver: push` from cron with no push adapter running:** core's outbound send falls back to the plugin's standalone sender. A send through `gateway.outbound` returned `success: true` at the relay.
- **A gateway whose push adapter is already connected:** after a re-pair to another relay URL, its next send went to the new URL. After `DELETE /pair` it sent nothing and reported push not configured.

## What changed from the app-bundled plugins

| Area | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Packaging | Two plugins, `hermes-mobile-push` and `hermes-mobile-device-access` | One plugin, `hermes-mobile-app-connector`; code in `push/` and `device/` |
| Pairing | The app uploaded the plugin, wrote env vars into every profile, restarted gateways, read the preview key file | One `POST /pair`; no upload, no restart |
| Dashboard routes | `/api/plugins/hermes-mobile-push/...`, `/api/plugins/hermes-mobile-device-access/...` | `/api/plugins/hermes-mobile-app-connector/...`; paths below the prefix and response shapes unchanged, plus `/pair` |
| Stored data | `plugin-data/hermes-mobile-push/`, `plugin-data/hermes-mobile-device-access/` | Same folders, so paired phones keep working |
| Relay settings | Required env vars of the push plugin | Optional; env/secrets first, then the stored pairing; push stays disconnected without both |
| Device tools | 15 of 16 offered with no phone paired | None until a phone is paired; all 16 once a paired phone supports reminder edits and has granted them |
| Session reads and writes | `SessionDB` and a raw `sqlite3` read of `state.db` | `persistence_assembly` / `persistence.conversation`; delivery transcripts are written with the same `open_persistence(profile_scope())` call core's own delivery mirror uses |
| `hermes serve` prompts | Polled the sidecar's open requests | Deleted; `on_session_prompt` / `on_session_prompt_settled` on a Hermes that fires them |
| Cron delivery check | Read cron's job store and private delivery helpers | `ctx.cron_delivery_platforms()` |
| Device follow-ups | Private cron create and register calls | `cron.plugin_api.ensure_named_job` |
| Minimum Hermes | 0.21.5 | 0.23.3, the first release with the storage interface |

## Newer seams on older releases

The cron, session-fact and silence-helper seams came from NousResearch/hermes-agent#159657 (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/159657), merged after v0.23.3. The plugin feature-detects each one. On a release without them the feature is off and nothing raises; there is no fallback to a private name:

- **Cron delivery check:** a cron job that already delivers to `push` is not recognized, so its run can notify as well as deliver.
- **Device follow-ups:** a device request that outlives the tool's 20-second wait gets no automatic follow-up reply; `mobile_request_result` still returns its result.
- **Session facts:** the accessors for detached forks, delegated children and the session source are missing, so turns are not filtered by them.

The silence helpers exist on v0.23.3 already, unpublished, and keep working there.

## Behavior differences to know

- **Cron delivery answers now come from cron's own resolver.** An unconfigured bare `push`, an unresolvable `push:<target>` or a missing `bot-chat:<profile>` now count as "not delivered to push", so the run is eligible to notify. Mid-run, the answer follows the firing run's own job settings. Outside a cron run the notification's job name falls back to "Scheduled task".
- **Silent-sessions route:** it reads through the storage interface and matches the sources core writes exactly (`cron`, `webhook`, `msgraph_webhook`). A session whose source a user overrode to another label (`scheduled`, `cron:<id>`) is no longer listed. At the 1,000-session cap the newest-first window follows the store's last-activity order. A comparison over one store of 1,000 sessions returned the same 500 silent ids as the old query, at about 106 ms against 17 ms.
- **A briefly locked device store:** if another connection holds the device store exclusively past the check's short wait, the availability check counts the phone as possibly paired rather than hiding its tools.

## Security and privacy

- **No secrets in the tree.** The relay URL and install key come from each profile's settings or the stored pairing at runtime, and the preview key is generated per home on first load.
- **The pairing response carries secret material** (install key and preview key), only to the dashboard's signed-in client. The app already read the same values through the dashboard's file API.
- **Nothing new crosses the network.**
  - Notifications go to the configured relay with encrypted previews.
  - A device wake sends the relay an empty JSON object (`{}`) with the install key as the bearer.
  - Device data travels only between the phone and Hermes, over the phone's own connection.

## Test plan

Suites at head a17fd38, in a scratch home on Ubuntu 24.04.4: Python 3.14.9 for the two runs against Hermes, Python 3.11 for the stubbed run:

- [x] Against hermes-agent main 2506f5b0a4d3, which includes NousResearch/hermes-agent#159657: 366 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] Against v0.23.3, the declared minimum: 355 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] With no Hermes importable (stubbed mode): 335 passed, 29 skipped, 0 failed.
- [x] The CI job's own setup on Python 3.14 (hermes-agent main installed with its overrides, plus the plugin's `cryptography` pin): 364 passed, 4 skipped. Two of the skips are the openapi schema tests, which need `jsonschema`, not a dependency of the plugin or of core.
- [x] `hermes plugins validate` against main: `Validation passed.`, no private core imports.
- [x] Hermes' own plugin discovery in a scratch home with the plugin enabled and nothing configured, on main and on v0.23.3, compared with the plugin disabled (run before the `/pair` commit):
  - no added warnings and no added network attempts;
  - 0 device tools offered;
  - `push` registered but not connected;
  - new files: `plugin-data/hermes-mobile-push/preview_key` and its `preview_key.lock`, which the old push plugin also created.
- [x] The pairing runs above, against main (and the re-pair runs against v0.23.3 too).
- [x] For installs configured only with environment variables or secrets, every place that reads the relay settings gives the same answer as before this PR. Covered combinations: empty, URL only, key only, both, scoped secret, config extras over env, mixed, a refused http URL, and values with trailing spaces.
- [ ] Not run: macOS and Windows (CI covers both), a real phone, a real relay.

## Known gaps

- **Old copies alongside the new plugin.** Homes that already have the two app-bundled plugins keep them next to this one until the app or the catalog removes them; they register the same platform and tools.
- **The apps need an update.** They still upload the old plugins and call the old route prefixes. The update switches them to `POST /pair` and the new prefix. `POST /pair` is the server side of that flow; no shipped app calls it yet.
- **Hooks don't read `platforms.push` values.** An install that sets its relay values only in `platforms.push` sends deliveries with them, but its turn hooks, like the old plugin's, read environment, secrets and the stored pairing only.

## Follow-ups

- **hermes-agent catalog entry** `plugin-catalog/hermes-mobile-app-connector.yaml` pinned to this PR's merge commit:
  - opt-in for now, `default: true` later;
  - in the same PR, add `hermes-mobile-push` and `hermes-mobile-device-access` to `plugin-catalog/removed.yaml` by name, so old copies stop loading.
- **App update:**
  - stop bundling and uploading the plugins;
  - install `hermes-mobile-app-connector` from the catalog when it is missing;
  - pair with `POST /pair`.

## Review

An independent review covered the branch through `734c599` and then the `/pair` and rename commits through `2ee1b42`. Its findings are fixed in `9a40875`, `c7c0892`, `d6d27bc` and `3f98cd1`. Those four commits, plus two CI fixes to the tests (`0840165` loads YAML through core's `ruamel.yaml`, since CI has no PyYAML; `a17fd38` checks POSIX file modes and `flock` only off Windows), were checked by rerunning the review's reproductions and the suites above, not by a further review pass.

## Infographic

![Hermes Mobile plugin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unsupportedpastels/hermes-official-plugins/a17fd3856584879e10aa7c20797a85284a213f3c/assets/hermes-mobile-app-connector.jpg)

title: feishu: Feishu / Lark platform and feishu_doc / feishu_drive tools leave Hermes core (official, opt-in)
body:
Moves the Feishu / Lark messaging platform and its `feishu_doc` / `feishu_drive` tools out of hermes-agent core and into this repo as the `feishu` plugin. Hermes installs it automatically for homes that used Feishu, and nothing an existing setup depends on gets renamed.

It is an **official, opt-in** plugin: maintained by Nous Research in this repo, catalog `tier: official`, not installed by default on new homes (`hermes plugins install feishu`). This replaces NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#109 (same history, same code), re-homed here because Feishu is one of the most-connected platforms and should not carry a "not supported" label.

**Existing user:** `hermes update` or the next start installs this plugin with the same env vars, config and tools. **New user:** nothing is installed until you run `hermes plugins install feishu`.

Core removal PR: NousResearch/hermes-agent — branch `laneb/feishu-labs` (PR NousResearch/hermes-agent#159651; adds the LEFT_CORE row that installs this plugin for homes that used Feishu). Catalog PR: `plugin-catalog/feishu.yaml` (NousResearch/hermes-agent#159650, `hold`, `tier: official`, no `default`). Replaces labs PR NousResearch/hermes-labs-plugins#109.

**Merge order: core → this → catalog.** `hermes plugins validate` is **expected red on hermes-agent main** until the core PR lands, because main still has `feishu_doc_read` and the four `feishu_drive_*` tools built in (the "built-in tool collisions" check). Against a core without Feishu it passes (see below).

## What moved

| From hermes-agent | To |
|---|---|
| `plugins/platforms/feishu/` (and older `gateway/platforms/feishu*.py`; `gateway/platforms/feishu.py` → `adapter.py`) | `feishu/` |
| `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py`, `tools/feishu_drive_tool.py` | `feishu/feishu_doc_tool.py`, `feishu/feishu_drive_tool.py` |
| `tools/feishu_lark.py` | `feishu/lark_client.py` (renamed in the packaging commit) |
| `tests/gateway/*feishu*`, `tests/plugins/platforms/feishu/*`, `tests/tools/test_feishu_tools.py` | `feishu/tests/` |

History is kept. `git filter-repo` covered all 48 paths Feishu has had in core, up to `85e4be32560f`: 317 commits by 76 authors, with commit-message issue refs rewritten to `NousResearch/hermes-agent#N`. The imported tree is byte-identical to core at that sha (checked file by file with `cmp`). It merges in with `--allow-unrelated-histories` as `7289484` (the same imported history as labs #109). The packaging is one commit on top, `0a2389f` (labs #109's packaging with this repo's conventions: official wording and homepage, README card, official card art), plus `2dcf0c2`, the Feishu cases of core's shared approval suites.

None of the names existing installs rely on change: platform `feishu`, toolsets `feishu_doc` / `feishu_drive`, tools `feishu_doc_read` / `feishu_drive_list_comments` / `feishu_drive_list_comment_replies` / `feishu_drive_reply_comment` / `feishu_drive_add_comment`, every `FEISHU_*` env var, the `platforms.feishu` config keys, `FEISHU_HOME_CHANNEL`, and `feishu_comment_rules.json` / `feishu_comment_pairing.json`. Core's composite `hermes-feishu` toolset goes away with core.

## Packaging

- **Manifest:** `name: feishu`, label "Feishu / Lark", homepage `hermes-official-plugins/tree/main/feishu`, `kind: platform`, `provides_tools` = the 5 tool names. `requires_env` / `optional_env` are exactly what core had. In `pyproject.toml`: `lark-oapi>=1.7.5,<2` and `qrcode>=7.4.2,<8` (core's `feishu` extra pinned `==1.7.5` / `==7.4.2`).
- **`register.py`:** calls `ctx.register_platform` with everything core's `register()` passed: `allow_update_command=True`, `max_message_length=8000`, `display_tier="medium"`, the dashboard card, `SEND_ENTRY_KWARGS`, AUTHZ, `apply_yaml_config_fn`, the standalone sender, the setup flow and `ensure_deps_fn`.
  - Fields newer than some cores are passed only when the running core's `PlatformEntry` has them (`_OPTIONAL_ENTRY_KWARGS` / `_supported_entry_fields()`). That covers the new fields from the core PR: `binds_port_fn` (true only when `connection_mode` is `webhook`), `listen_port=("webhook_port", 8765)`, `thread_reply_anchor=True` and `opus_voice=True`.
  - The two tool modules then register through `ctx.register_tool`, not `tools.registry.register`, with the same names, schemas and `check_fn`.
- **Inert on cores that still bundle Feishu.** `core_ships_feishu()` works like yuanbao's guard. It looks for `plugins/platforms/feishu` or `tools/feishu_doc_tool.py` with `PathFinder`, searching only those packages' own `__path__`, so a leftover `__pycache__` does not count. When it finds core's copy, the plugin logs one INFO line and registers nothing.
- **`Platform.FEISHU` becomes `Platform("feishu")` at call time.** The env bridge moves from the import-time `EnvCred(Platform.FEISHU, …)` row to `env_enablement_fn` with the same keys: `app_id` / `app_secret`, `domain` (default `feishu`), `connection_mode` (default `websocket`), optional `encrypt_key` / `verification_token`, and the home channel from `FEISHU_HOME_CHANNEL` (+`_NAME`, `_THREAD_ID`).
- **`platform_hint`:** `adapter_hint.py` is core's file byte-for-byte (477 chars, tested).
- **Private imports `validate` flagged are replaced:**
  - `agent.i18n.t` → a local `_i18n.py` with core's 22 `platform.feishu.*` strings in all 17 languages, plus the shared card strings the adapter uses (`gateway.clarify.expired|hint_multi|option_line`, `gateway.exec_approval.action_deny|action_once|smart_deny_line|header|reason_label`, `platform.shared.approval_expired`). The language choice is the same as core's.
  - `pm.extras.available("feishu")` / `pm.ensure_import("feishu")` → an `importlib.util.find_spec("lark_oapi")` check, since the deps come from the plugin's `pyproject.toml` at install time. `pm.install_hint` in the QR tip → "reinstall the plugin".
  - `hermes_cli.setup_platforms.declines_reconfigure` → the same gate built from the public `hermes_cli.config.get_env_value` / `hermes_cli.setup.prompt_yes_no`.
  - `tools.feishu_lark` → plugin-local `lark_client.py`. Every `plugins.platforms.feishu.*` import is relative now.
- **Still flagged by validate (warning), with no public seam yet:**
  - `gateway.status_scoped_locks.release_scoped_lock`
  - `utils.env_float` / `env_int` / `file_cache_version`
  - `agent.async_utils.safe_schedule_threadsafe`
  - `gateway.platforms.shared_ingress.bind_listener`
  - `tools.clarify_gateway` (module import; its names are public)
  - `gateway.platforms.send_targets.StandaloneSendPolicy` / `regex_groups_parser`
  - The comment-reply agent run in `feishu_comment.py`: `gateway.run._load_gateway_config` / `_resolve_gateway_model` / `_resolve_runtime_agent_kwargs`, `hermes_cli.models.get_default_model_for_provider`, `run_agent.AIAgent`, `agent.conversation_compression_checkpoint.checkpoint_required_from_config`, `tui_gateway.launch_profile_policy.async_launch_profile_scope_if_multiplexed`
- **Tests:** core's suite is ported with import paths rewritten.
  - `tests/conftest.py` is modelled on homeassistant's (plus the inert-core skip): a `feishu_plugin` package alias, the real `PlatformEntry` registered up front, the root collected as a plain `Dir`, and an autouse temp `HERMES_HOME` with `FEISHU_*` cleared. `plugin_registry`-marked tests are skipped when core still bundles Feishu.
  - It also carries core's session fixture `_bind_lark_sdk_globals_when_installed`.
  - Helpers the tests imported from core's tree were copied in: `feishu_helpers.py`, `approval_helpers.write_approvers` and `dead_profile_home.py`.
  - New `test_plugin_packaging.py` covers both toolsets, the entry fields (new fields only when core has them, `binds_port_fn` truth table), hint bytes, the env seed, the env bridge through the real `load_gateway_config`, the localized strings (17 languages, same keys) and the inert guard.
  - Two core tests asserted on `pm` calls that no longer exist (`ensure_import`, `install_hint`). They now assert the find_spec check and the plugin's own QR tip. Three `asyncio.get_event_loop()` calls became `asyncio.run`, because core's conftest supplied a loop that this conftest does not.
- **README:** official header (like homeassistant's) and setup copied from core's `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/feishu.md` (the comment-rules CLI is now `python -m feishu.feishu_comment_rules`). Card: `assets/feishu.jpg` (1200×600, "OFFICIAL PLUGIN" in the house style), a root README card, and Feishu / Lark added to "Already used one of these?".

## Parity: same env, same `platforms.feishu`

Two homes load real `load_gateway_config()` from the same env. Base is core main with the bundled plugin. Head is a core tree with `plugins/platforms/feishu`, `tools/feishu_*.py` and `Platform.FEISHU` removed, with this plugin installed in `HERMES_HOME/plugins/feishu` and enabled. They produce an identical `platforms.feishu` (enabled flag, `extra`, home channel) for each env:

| Env | Result (both cores) |
|---|---|
| all 9 keys (`APP_ID`, `APP_SECRET`, `DOMAIN=lark`, `CONNECTION_MODE=webhook`, `ENCRYPT_KEY`, `VERIFICATION_TOKEN`, `HOME_CHANNEL`, `_NAME`, `_THREAD_ID`) | enabled, 6 extras, home `[oc_home, Ops, th1]`, equal |
| `APP_ID` + `APP_SECRET` only | enabled, `domain=feishu`, `connection_mode=websocket`, no home, equal |
| `APP_ID` only | not configured on either, equal |

## Results at import time (labs #109, core `85e4be3`)

| Check | Core without Feishu (main minus `plugins/platforms/feishu`, `tools/feishu_*.py`, `Platform.FEISHU`) | hermes-agent main `85e4be3` (still bundles Feishu) |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest -q` in `feishu/` | **265 passed** | **264 passed, 1 skipped** (the `plugin_registry` test; the plugin is inert) |
| `hermes plugins validate feishu` | **Validation passed** (no collisions, scan safe, private-import warning above) | **Validation failed (expected):** built-in tool collisions on the 5 feishu tools |
| `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin` | — | main: **safe**; release `v0.23.4`: **safe** |

The "core without Feishu" tree is a `git archive` of main with those paths deleted, `FEISHU = "feishu"` dropped from the enum, and the three remaining `Platform.FEISHU` references in `gateway/run.py` / `gateway/run_turn.py` neutralised, because the core branch was not pushed yet when this ran. Re-run it against the core PR head before merging.

Not ported: open core PRs touching Feishu. They stay in hermes-agent for now.



## Results on this branch (`2dcf0c2`)

| Check | Core PR head `0353d1b` (Feishu removed) | hermes-agent main (still bundles Feishu) |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m pytest -q` in `feishu/` | **271 passed** | **270 passed, 1 skipped** (`plugin_registry`; plugin inert) |
| `hermes plugins validate feishu` | **Validation passed** | **Validation failed (expected):** built-in tool collisions on the 5 feishu tools |
| `tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin` | — | main: **safe**; release `v2026.9.24`: **safe** |

The CI `feishu` jobs here run against hermes-agent main, so they stop at validate (expected red) until NousResearch/hermes-agent#159651 lands. The shared-approval test's long command no longer ends in a pipe-to-shell string (it tripped the install scanner's `high` rule; the test only needs a long command).
